danh_muc.ten: Rice, Sticky Rice, Noodles & Savory Cakes

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a family-style seafood dish that combines Thai flavors: a rich curry coating plump crab meat, featuring the fragrant aroma of crab roe and the smooth taste of coconut milk. Crab is rich in high-quality protein and many micronutrients, helping to boost physical strength. The process is clear—just pay attention to pan-searing to retain the crab roe and finally turning off the heat to toss the sauce. It is quite friendly for those with some cooking experience, usually taking about 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
1 meat crab (about 300 g) * x number of servings
15 g curry cube (one small cube) * x number of servings
200 g onion * x number of servings
100 ml coconut milk * x number of servings
5 cloves garlic * x number of servings
cac_buoc: Open the crab shell, cut the crab in half, and use the back of a knife to gently crack the claws. Dip the cut surfaces and claws into tapioca starch, but do not use too much. Sprinkle 5 g of tapioca starch into the top shell to cover the crab roe, and set aside.
Finely chop the onion and set aside.
Mince the garlic and set aside.
Boil a kettle of water and keep it ready.
Heat a pan with about 20 ml of cooking oil; wait 10 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Place the crab cut-side down into the pan, fry for 20 seconds—this step is mainly to seal the roe and meat. Then flip and fry each side for 10 seconds. Once fried, remove the crab and set aside.
Place the top shell in the pan, use a spoon to pour hot oil over it, and pan-sear to seal the roe inside. After 20 seconds, remove and set aside.
Without washing the pan, add another 10 ml of oil. Use high heat until the oil is shimmering and slightly smoking, then add the minced garlic and onion; stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the curry cube to the pan and stir until melted (10 seconds), then add the fried crab and toss well.
Pour in 300 ml of boiling water, cover, and simmer for 3 minutes.
After simmering, pour in the coconut milk and egg white, then turn off the heat. After turning off the heat, stir constantly until the sauce thickens.
Serve.

mon_an.ten: Sizzling Eel Strips (Xiang You Shan Si)
mon_an.mo_ta: Sizzling Eel Strips is a classic home-style dish from the Shanghai-Jiangzhe region. The eel strips are fresh, tender, smooth, and crispy, with a strong garlic aroma and a slightly sweet sauce. Pouring hot lard over the top creates an irresistible fragrance that pairs perfectly with rice. Eel is rich in high-quality protein and DHA, providing abundant nutrition. This dish requires certain knife skills and heat control; the difficulty is moderate, and beginners may need extra practice. From preparation to serving, it usually takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Cut the eel into three sections and then julienne into thin strips.
Mix with 0.5 g ground pepper and 3 g cooking wine, then add 5 g sesame oil to marinate.
Heat the pan and swirl with oil.
Add vegetable oil and heat until 60% hot (medium-high).
Add half of the minced garlic and all the minced ginger; toss a few times.
Add the eel strips and stir-fry vigorously over medium-high heat for 30 seconds.
Drizzle 10 g of cooking wine around the edge of the pan and toss a few times.
Add the light soy sauce and stir-fry evenly.
Add the oyster sauce and dark soy sauce; toss a few times.
Add the salt, white sugar, and 3 g ground pepper; stir-fry evenly.
Mix the starch with water to make a slurry, pour it into the pan, and reduce the sauce until thickened.
Transfer to a plate and sprinkle with minced garlic and chopped scallions.
Heat another pan, add the lard, heat until 70% hot, and pour it over the eel strips.

mon_an.mo_ta: This dish is spicy, numbing, fresh, and fragrant, with tender and juicy meat. It is a classic Sichuan-Hunan style snack that is clean and practical to make at home. Crawfish are rich in high-quality protein and micronutrients, but the sauce is high in oil and salt, so it is best enjoyed occasionally. Handling live crawfish and various spices presents a challenge for beginners; however, not removing the vein can significantly reduce the difficulty. From preparation to serving takes about 45 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Oil = 70 ml (3 times the usual amount for stir-frying)
The following amounts are for 2 cân (1 kg) of crawfish; adjust proportionally.
cac_buoc: Scrub the crawfish clean, devein them, cut the scallion into 2 cm sections, and mince the ginger and garlic.
Heat the oil until slightly hot, then add the bay leaves, star anise, cinnamon, green Sichuan peppercorns, Sichuan peppercorns, and bullet chilies.
Once the spices are fragrant, add the scallion, ginger, and garlic.
After the aromatics are fragrant, add the Pixian bean paste and soybean paste; stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add the crawfish and stir-fry until they change color.
Pour in the beer; once it boils, add the light soy sauce and salt.
Cook the crawfish until fully done, then serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: A quick, fresh, and attractive seafood dish. After pan-searing, Argentine red shrimp have tender white meat with a deep sweetness and a fragrant, crispy shell. They are rich in iodine, phosphorus, astaxanthin, and other micronutrients that help boost immunity, protect the heart, and reduce cholesterol. The difficulty is moderate, requiring control over the heat and flipping technique, but the steps are clear enough for beginners to succeed. It is expected to take about 20 minutes.
cac_buoc: Thaw the Argentine red shrimp; it is best to move them from the freezer to the fridge 1 day in advance to thaw naturally, preserving the best flavor and quality. You can buy pre-butterflied and deveined shrimp to save time.
Wash the thawed shrimp and pat them dry; it is essential to remove all moisture, using paper towels if necessary.
Slice the ginger, dice the onion, wash the cilantro, separate the leaves from the stems, chop the leaves, and mince the garlic.
Heat a pan over high heat. Once hot, pour in two tablespoons of olive oil. When the oil is hot, add the ginger slices, diced onion, and cilantro stems to sauté.
After about 1 minute, remove the ginger, onion, and cilantro stems and discard them.
Adjust to medium-high heat and add the shrimp to begin searing. Ensure each shrimp has full contact with the pan. Sear for about 20 minutes, while brushing a layer of oil onto each shrimp.
When the bottom shell is slightly golden brown, flip them over and sprinkle with minced garlic. Shake the pan gently to cook evenly.
About 1 minute later, pour in 20 ml of white wine.
Fry for another minute, then reduce to medium-low heat and sprinkle evenly with a layer of salt and black pepper.
Add a drop of light soy sauce onto each shrimp.
Sprinkle with cilantro leaves and transfer to a plate.
Garnish with a lemon slice on the side and serve.

mon_an.ten: Microwave Steamed Black Cod with Ginger and Scallions
mon_an.mo_ta: Cooking fish in the microwave with ginger and scallions enhances its freshness, finished with a drizzle of fragrant hot oil. This is a home-style steamed fish dish with silky meat and a savory-fresh taste, based on an improved Cantonese method. Black cod is rich in high-quality protein and omega-3 fatty acids, which are beneficial for the heart and brain. The operation is not too complex, but requires a feel for the timing and oil temperature, making it more suitable for those with some kitchen experience. From preparation to table takes only about twenty minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Black cod, skin-on, 2 fillets, 450 g (the star of this recipe; all seasonings can be adjusted proportionally to the actual weight of the cod)
cac_buoc: Place each fish fillet into a Ziploc bag, placing the skin-side down on a plate.
Take 25 g of julienned scallion whites and 10 g of peeled julienned ginger, mix them, divide into two halves, and place them on the fish fillets inside the bags.
Pour 2.5 mL of cooking wine into each bag.
Seal the Ziploc bags and place them in the microwave. Cook on medium power (800 watts) until the *fish flesh is opaque and flakes easily* (about 3.5-5 minutes), then remove the fish from the bags.
Discard the scallions and ginger.
Mix 25 mL of soy sauce and 2 mL of sesame oil, then drizzle evenly over the two fillets.
Take 10 g of finely julienned scallion greens and 3 g of peeled julienned ginger, mix them, and divide into two portions to sprinkle over the fillets.
Heat 50 mL of peanut oil in a small pot to 190 ℃.
Drizzle the hot oil over the fish fillets with the scallion greens and serve immediately.

mon_an.ten: Spicy Boiled Basa Fish (Shui Zhu Yu)
mon_an.mo_ta: Shui Zhu Yu is a classic Sichuan dish that is spicy, numbing, fresh, and fragrant, with silky smooth fish meat. Basa fish is rich in high-quality protein and low in fat, and when paired with seasonal vegetables, it provides balanced nutrition. The method is of medium difficulty and slightly challenging for beginners, but following the steps will lead to success. Estimated cooking time is about 2 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Vegetables (e.g., sliced potatoes/bean sprouts/cauliflower/lettuce/...) can be varied; suggested total weight 300 g to 500 g
40 g red oil chili bean paste (add 10 to 20 g more if you want more red oil and spice)
The amounts below are suitable for 3 to 5 people.
cac_buoc: Preparation: If using frozen basa, let it thaw naturally at room temperature for 5 hours before slicing.
Slicing: Slice the basa into thin pieces, about 5 cm long and 3 cm wide.
Marinating: Place the sliced basa into a large stainless steel bowl.
Add 30 g bean paste, 3 g salt, 10 ml vine pepper oil, and 3 g white pepper powder.
Mix well by hand, then add 5 ml rapeseed oil to seal in the flavors.
Let it sit at room temperature for at least 30 minutes to marinate.
Prepare vegetables: Mince the garlic. Take 300 g cauliflower and 200 g lettuce; wash both.
Blanch and stir-fry vegetables: Blanch the cauliflower in boiling water and set aside; wash and drain the lettuce, then stir-fry until cooked and set aside (no oil needed).
Sauté bean paste: Heat a pan with 20 ml rapeseed oil, add 10 g bean paste, 10 g fermented black beans (optional), and minced garlic; sauté slowly over medium heat.

Poach fish slices: Add 150 ml hot water; once it boils, add the marinated fish slices. Gently stir to separate the slices in the water, then add 2 g salt and 2 g sugar to season (adjust salt to taste at this point). Once the water boils again, it is ready to be served.
Plating: First, place the cooked vegetables into a large bowl, then ladle the hot fish slices over the vegetables. Pour the remaining hot broth from the pan over the top and it's done!

mon_an.ten: Oil-Braised King Prawns (You Men Da Xia)
mon_an.mo_ta: This classic Lu cuisine dish uses a harmonious sweet and savory sauce to coat whole prawns, resulting in a glossy red finish and firm, chewy meat. Prawns are rich in high-quality protein and astaxanthin while being low in fat, making them a nutritious ingredient that doesn't add much burden. The process involves making scallion oil, trimming the prawns, braising, and reducing the sauce, requiring some control over heat and seasoning. It is best suited for cooks with some experience; the entire process takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cooking wine, salt, rock sugar, vegetable oil
cac_buoc: Trim the rostrum of the prawns to the base, cut off the antennae and legs, remove the sand bag (stomach), butterfly the back to remove the vein, wash, and set aside.
Prepare the aromatic oil.

When the oil is 30% hot, add the Sichuan peppercorns. Once the oil is hot, turn off the heat and add the scallions and ginger (try not to let the oil change color). When the scallions are slightly golden, strain the oil (excess scallion oil can be saved for noodles).
Add the oil to the pan, arrange the prawns neatly, and when both sides change color, gently press the prawn heads.
Add minced ginger (finely diced).
Add 30 g Shaoxing wine.
Add two small bowls of water.
Add 3 g salt.
Add 10 g rock sugar.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then turn to low heat, cover, and simmer (do not add more broth or open the lid during this time).
When the shells are glossy and the prawns are curled, they are ready; arrange the prawns on a plate.
Reduce the sauce (strain and pour back into the pot to thicken, then add the scallion oil) until only 1/4 of the liquid remains.
Drizzle the sauce over the prawns.
Complete.
Enjoy! ✅

mon_an.mo_ta: This Sichuan-style grilled fish is spicy, numbing, fresh, and fragrant, with meat that is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. The vegetables soak up the special sauce, making it a perfect dish to eat with rice. Grass carp is rich in high-quality protein, and when combined with various vegetables, it offers balanced nutrition. The method looks complex, but following the steps is not actually difficult, making it suitable for beginners who want to challenge themselves with a main course. From preparation to table takes about one hour.
cac_buoc: Butterfly the grass carp (usually 3 cân) from the back, making several scores along the back down to the sides, but do not cut through to the belly, otherwise it won't hold its shape.
You can pour hot water over the fish to wash off the slime or use a brush under running water until it no longer feels slippery.
Place the fish in a container, add cooking wine, 10 g white pepper powder, and 5 g salt; rub well and marinate for twenty minutes to absorb the flavor.
Cut half a scallion stalk into sections, halve the garlic cloves, and place them in a container with the star anise, bay leaves, and cinnamon.
Cut the dried chilies in half and place them in a container with the lantern chilies.
Cut the celery into small sections.
Blanch the bean sprouts.
Blanch the yuba and cut into strips.
Julienne the onion.
Grill the fish.
If you have an oven, grease the baking tray, place the fish skin-side down, and grill until both sides are golden, then sprinkle with cumin powder.

If you don't have an oven, heat a pan with oil, sprinkle 2 g of salt on both sides of the pan, and fry the grass carp. Do not flip immediately; wait for one side to set before flipping. Fry until both sides are golden, sprinkle with cumin powder, remove, and set aside on a plate.
Pour 20 ml of cooking oil into the pot. When hot, add the scallion, garlic, star anise, and bay leaves to sauté until fragrant.
Add half a packet of hot pot base and 15-20 g of bean paste; stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add 5 g white sugar, 10 g salt, and 5 ml light soy sauce to season. Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients and bring to a boil.
Add the celery, bean sprouts, and yuba strips in order; no need to cook through, just blanch them briefly, then layer the julienned onion on top and place the grilled fish on top.
Add the dried chilies, lantern chilies, and green Sichuan peppercorns.
Heat oil in another pot until hot, then pour it over the chilies to release the aroma.
Finally, sprinkle with roasted peanuts, chopped scallions, white sesame seeds, and cilantro.
Cook for 5-6 minutes, and the delicious dish is complete.

mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed oysters are a pure and original coastal home-style dish. The oyster meat is tender and juicy, carrying the light salty fragrance of the sea, while minced garlic and ginger strips stimulate a delicate sweetness. Oysters are rich in high-quality protein and zinc, helping to boost immunity. The operation is not complex, but opening the hot lid and handling the shells requires a bit of care; beginners can also complete it successfully. From scrubbing to serving, it takes about twenty minutes.
cac_buoc: Use a brush to scrub the oysters clean (a toothbrush can be used if you don't have a scrub brush).
Add water to the steamer, place the steaming rack inside, arrange the 6 oysters flat on the rack, and steam at 50% power for 3 minutes.

Using a wet towel in your right hand, open the hot lid. Remove the top half of each shell and discard. Place the oysters with the curved side down and the flat side up. Place 1 ginger strip and 10 g of minced garlic on each oyster.
Close the lid and steam at 100% power for 3.5 minutes.
Turn off the heat, use a towel to open the lid, and add 5 ml of soy sauce to each oyster.
Transfer to a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed sea bass is a classic Cantonese steamed dish. The fish meat is silky, tender, and crisp, with a light and fresh flavor that preserves the original taste of the sea bass. Sea bass is rich in high-quality protein and DHA, making it nutritious and easy to digest. This dish is simple to prepare and very beginner-friendly, taking only about thirty minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 10-15 ml seasoned soy sauce for seafood
cac_buoc: Slice the ginger into slices and strips. Cut the white parts of the scallions into sections and julienne the green parts; soak the green strips in cold water and set aside.

After cleaning the sea bass, pat it dry with paper towels. Score both sides of the fish, use salt to wash off any remaining slime, then rub 10 g of salt all over the inside and outside of the fish. Marinate for over 10 minutes.
Alternative cutting and plating method: After cutting, you can stand the sea bass upright to steam; it cooks more evenly and is easier to eat without needing to flip it.
(Illustration)

Stuff the ginger and scallion whites into the fish belly, and sprinkle more ginger and scallion whites over the body (using half of the prepared amount). Use chopsticks on the steaming plate to keep the fish off the bottom of the dish while steaming.
Heat the water until you can feel the warmth, then place the fish inside.
Steam over high heat for 10 minutes.
Once steamed, transfer to a clean plate and discard the ginger and scallions from the fish.
Drizzle 15 ml of seasoned soy sauce for seafood over the fish.
Sprinkle the fresh julienned ginger and scallions over the fish. Heat 10 ml of oil in a pot until hot, then pour the hot oil over the fish and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Poached shrimp is a classic, quick Cantonese dish where the shrimp remains sweet, fresh, and tender, preserving its natural flavor. Shrimp is rich in high-quality protein and minerals, paired with a dipping sauce that is appetizing without being greasy. The method is simple and forgiving, making it very beginner-friendly; it takes only about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Shrimp 250 g * x number of servings (1-2 servings recommended)
cac_buoc: Cut the onion into small pieces, slice the ginger, and spread them evenly in the pan.
Rinse the live shrimp (deveining and trimming the legs and antennae are optional), drain well, and layer them over the onion and ginger slices in the pan.
Pour the cooking wine into the pot, cover with a lid, cook over medium heat for 1 minute, then low heat for 5 minutes, and turn off the heat to let it sit for 5 minutes.
While waiting for the shrimp, prepare the dipping sauce:
Finely chop the scallion and mince the garlic. Combine them with soy sauce, sesame seeds, and aromatic vinegar in a bowl, then stir.
Heat the oil until hot and pour it over the dipping sauce.
Remove the shrimp from the pot and serve on a clean plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Sweet and Sour Carp is a classic Lu cuisine dish, crispy on the outside and tender on the inside with a balanced sweet and sour taste. The golden-fried fish is drizzled with a glossy red sauce, making it very appealing. The fish meat is rich in high-quality protein and minerals, making it easy to digest. This dish is not very beginner-friendly, with a medium difficulty level or higher, requiring skills in scoring, coating, and heat control. It takes about 1 hour from preparation to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: This dish is only for 3 or more people (fish that are too large or too small are not suitable), so no calculation formula is needed; it is especially suitable for family gatherings like New Year's Eve dinner.
cac_buoc: Clean the fish thoroughly, ensuring no scales or foreign objects remain.

Position the fish with the head facing left and the belly facing down. Hold the knife in your right hand. Make a vertical cut 1 cm deep, press firmly, then slice horizontally to the left for 3-4 cm. Gently make a slit in the middle of each slice.
Place the fish in a basin, then slice the ginger and cut the onion into sections (rough cuts are fine, mainly to remove the fishy smell).
Squeeze the juice from the onion and ginger into the basin with all your strength.
Add 20 g of salt and 25 g of cooking wine, then "bathe" the carp, rubbing it evenly.
(Illustration)
(The longer you marinate, the less fishy the smell; 30+ minutes recommended.)
Find a clean basin, add 100 g flour, 200 g starch, 180 g water, and 5 g salt. Mix by hand until the batter is thick and stretchy, then crack in an egg and mix again.
Wait for 30 minutes.
Place the fish on a cutting board and use a dry towel to pat the skin dry (this helps the batter stick better).
Wash the basin and wipe it dry with a towel.
Heat about 1 L of oil in a pot until it reaches 70% heat, about 200-240 °C.

Hold the fish by the tail, dip the head into the bottom of the pot, and use a ladle to pour hot oil over the body. Once the batter sets, slowly release the fish into the pot. Use a spatula to gently lift the head and place a slotted spoon underneath to prevent the bottom from burning.
Prepare a serving plate next to the stove.

Use the spatula to gently push from the body and use both tools to flip the fish. Fry for another two minutes, then use the same method (slotted spoon supporting the head, spatula supporting the body) to transfer the fish to the plate.
Pour the oil from the pot into the dry basin, set aside, and wash the pot.
In a small bowl, mix 50 g water, 40 g tomato paste, 20 g white sugar, and 10 g white vinegar.
Prepare another small bowl with 10 g starch and 10 g water to make a starch slurry.
Heat the pot over high heat, pour in the prepared sauce, bring to a boil, then turn to low heat.
Pour in the starch slurry while stirring constantly. Turn off the heat after 20 seconds.
Use a spoon to drizzle the sweet and sour sauce evenly over the fish. Garnish with cilantro or chopped scallions. The Sweet and Sour Carp is ready.
The sweet and sour sauce here is cooked to a slightly thick consistency......

mon_an.mo_ta: Chinese Braised Fish is a classic home-style dish with a savory, fresh, and slightly sweet flavor. The fish is tender and well-seasoned, making it a favorite Chinese braised dish. Fish is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids, providing easy-to-absorb nutrition. It requires handling raw fish and frying, with several steps that may be challenging for beginners, but following the recipe will lead to success. It takes about 40 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish: Beginners are recommended to start with a medium-sized crucian carp; score the fish first so it cooks easily (otherwise the back may stay raw)
Ginger strips: Take regular old ginger, cut 2-3 slices, and julienne them
3-4 cloves of garlic, crushed, minced, or sliced
10 g salt; if the chilies are very spicy, use a bit more
1-2 bird's eye chilies (optional); based on experience, use 2 at most, otherwise it will be painfully spicy.
MSG to taste; do not use too much, 5 g is enough.
5 g oyster sauce is enough, same rule as MSG
cac_buoc: Note that these ingredients are based on experience; except for cilantro, using too much of the others is not necessarily better.
Oyster sauce
Scallions
Cilantro
Bird's eye chili
MSG (or chicken powder)
Prepare the ginger and garlic, mince them.
Chop the dried chilies and combine with the ginger and garlic.
Add 30-50 ml of oil and wait for the pan to get hot...
Add the fish (pat it dry first to avoid oil splatters), then shake the pan and fry the fish with hot oil. Be sure to use low heat during this process.
Flip the fish and repeat the frying process on the other side.
Add the ginger, garlic, and chilies; sauté until fragrant.
Pour in the cooking wine (use a generous amount). Be careful as this will create a lot of smoke.
Add the vinegar (add more if you like vinegar).
Then add the sugar and soy sauce (dark soy sauce).
Add cold water until it just covers the fish. Turn to medium heat, cover with a lid, flip the fish after 1 minute, and cover again.
After 3-4 minutes, add the salt, bird's eye chilies, and oyster sauce (MSG, chicken powder, etc.). Cover again, then flip the fish once more.
When the sauce reduces to just below the dorsal fin (or when there isn't much sauce left), turn to low heat. Add the cilantro and chopped scallions, cover for 20 seconds, then turn off the heat.
Serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Fish Head is a classic home-style braised dish. The fish head is rich in gelatin, the meat is tender, and the sauce is savory, fresh, and slightly spicy—perfect with rice. Fish head is rich in high-quality protein, lecithin, and unsaturated fatty acids, which are beneficial for skin and brain health. Because it involves handling raw fish and chopping bone, the difficulty is high; it is not recommended for absolute beginners to try alone. The entire process (including marinating) takes about 2–2.5 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: If possible, try to prepare a separate kitchen knife. Supermarkets or markets have cheap ones with thicker blades; a blade thickness of 5-7 mm is best.
Oil, salt, chicken powder, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, aged vinegar, black pepper powder, cooking wine
Note: Fish heads sold at the market are usually of two types: Silver Carp or Bighead Carp. The former is cheaper, while the latter is slightly more expensive but tastes better!
Note: This recipe is for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Wash the scallions, ginger, garlic, cilantro, and beauty chili separately.
Briefly rinse the dried chilies and star anise.
Cut the scallions in half. Cut the white parts into 4 cm sections. Cut the green parts into sections, then split each section into four.
Slice the ginger into 3 mm thick slices.
Crush the garlic.
Remove the roots from two sprigs of cilantro and chop into 1.5 cm pieces.
Cut the beauty chili into 3 mm thick rounds.
Cut the dried chilies into four pieces.
Note: "Fish body" mentioned below refers to the meat attached when buying the fish head.
Scrape the scales off the fish head and clean any remaining internal organs.
Chop off the fins and clean the gills.
Chop the jaw area where the head meets the body, cut the body into chunks, and chop the head into four or six pieces.
Note: Handling fish is difficult to explain in words; you can search for videos on how to process a fish head.
Rinse the chopped fish head thoroughly, especially any blood remaining on the pieces.
Place the cleaned fish in a basin. Add 5 g salt, 10 g light soy sauce, and 10 g cooking wine. Add the chopped green scallions and 1/3 of the ginger slices. Mix well and let sit for 1-2 hours.
Add 30 ml of oil and wait for the pan to get hot...
Once the oil is hot, turn to low heat.
If you don't understand why, refer to the sautéing and frying lessons.
Add the ginger slices and sauté slowly until most of the moisture is gone and they turn golden brown.
Add the scallion sections and sauté until they turn slightly white.
Add the minced garlic, star anise, and dried chilies; sauté for 5 seconds.
Add the marinated fish head to the pot and stir-fry for 2-3 minutes.
Pour in 500 ml of water. Add 2 g salt, 3 g chicken powder, 5 g light soy sauce, 3 g dark soy sauce, 5 g cooking wine, 2 g black pepper powder, and 3 g aged vinegar.
Add two sprigs of cilantro to the pot and cover with a lid.
Turn to high heat and bring to a boil.
Turn to medium heat and simmer slowly to let the flavors penetrate.
When the sauce has reduced by half, open the lid.
Turn to high heat to reduce the sauce. When only 1/3 of the sauce remains, turn off the heat and transfer to a small basin.
Note: Drizzle the sauce from the pot evenly over the fish head. You can place the cooked cilantro at the bottom of the basin for a better presentation.
Place fresh cilantro on top of the fish head, then place the beauty chili rounds on top of the cilantro.
The fragrant and flavorful Braised Fish Head is ready!

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Carp is a home-style Lu cuisine dish where the fish is fried then stewed. It has a slightly chewy skin, tender meat, and a savory-sweet sauce enriched by pork belly. It is rich in high-quality protein and minerals like calcium and phosphorus. Frying the fish and balancing the seasonings requires patience, but the steps are clear enough for beginners to follow. The process takes about 1 hour from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Note: The fish mentioned below refers to fish that has been basic-cleaned by the seller (scaled and gutted).
Wash the scallions, ginger, garlic, and dried chilies separately.
Cut the white parts of the scallions into 4 cm sections, then split each section into four.
Slice the ginger into 3 mm thick slices.
Mince one clove of garlic; cut the remaining cloves in half.
Cut the dried chilies into four pieces.
Slice the pork belly into 4 cm * 4 cm pieces.
Wash the fish.
Score the thick part of the fish's back with diagonal cuts to help it absorb flavor.

Pour plenty of oil into the pot and heat until 70% hot (just starting to smoke). Fry the fish for 1 minute until the skin is slightly firm, then remove and set aside (do not move the fish immediately after adding; wait for it to fry before flipping). Pour out the frying oil, leaving a little in the pot.
Heat the remaining oil, add the pork belly, and sauté until fragrant.
Add the dried chilies, scallions, ginger, and garlic halves; sauté for 1 minute.
Return the fried fish to the pot.
Pour the following along the sides of the pot:
50 ml cooking wine
50 ml aged vinegar
50 ml seasoned soy sauce (Weijixian)
20 ml dark soy sauce for color
5 ml oyster sauce for umami
5 g salt (one spoonful)
50 g white sugar
Add enough water to cover the fish.
Turn to medium heat and bring to a boil.
Turn to low heat and simmer slowly to let the flavors penetrate.
After 15 minutes, open the lid and remove the scallions, ginger, garlic, and dried chilies from the pot.
Turn to high heat to reduce the sauce. When only 1/4 of the sauce remains, sprinkle with minced garlic, turn off the heat, and serve.
The Braised Carp is ready!

mon_an.mo_ta: This dish features a rich savory sauce, sweet and slightly spicy crab meat, soft potatoes, and chewy rice cakes. It is a perfect main dish for gatherings, especially when the sauce is mixed with rice. It is rich in high-quality protein and micronutrients. The method has some difficulty, requiring handling live crab and controlling heat and seasoning ratios, which can be challenging for beginners. The process takes about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 3-4 people.
20 g garlic (add 10 g more if using shrimp)
15 g seafood sauce (substitute: 12 g oyster sauce + 3 g white sugar)
15 g soybean paste (substitute: 12 ml light soy sauce + 2 ml dark soy sauce + 1 g white sugar)
10 g sweet bean sauce (substitute: 5.5 g white sugar + 4 ml light soy sauce + 0.5 ml dark soy sauce)
2 g white pepper powder (add 1 g more if using shrimp)
200 ml beer (add 50-100 ml more if using shrimp)
800 ml water (add 200 ml more if using shrimp)
30-50 ml cooking oil (add 10 ml more if using shrimp; 500 ml needed if deep-frying)
cac_buoc: Cut the potatoes into 3 cm cubes, bell peppers into 4 cm diamond shapes, onion into 3 cm wide wedges, and rice cakes into 1 cm thick slices.
Chop the crab into 50-80 g pieces, coat with a thin layer of starch, fry in 180 °C oil for 1 minute, then remove.
Add oil to the pot, sauté the garlic, ginger, and dried chilies. Add all the pastes and rock sugar, sauté over low heat until the oil turns red, being careful not to burn the bottom.
Add the crab, potatoes, beer, and water. Bring to a boil, then turn to low heat and simmer for 12 minutes.
Add the rice cakes and bell peppers. Turn to high heat to reduce the sauce until it coats the ingredients. Finally, sprinkle with white pepper powder.

mon_an.ten: Giant River Prawns with Butter and Mustard
mon_an.mo_ta: This dish highlights the magical combination of butter and mustard. The shrimp meat is firm yet tender, and the sauce is rich, spicy, and fragrant, making it a modern seafood favorite. Shrimp is rich in high-quality protein and micronutrients. The difficulty is moderate; as long as you prepare the ingredients and control the heat, beginners can succeed. It takes about 30 minutes from processing the shrimp to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 15 g to 30 g cooking wine, rum, or beer
5 sprigs of cilantro, cut into sections
5 cloves of garlic, minced into a paste
cac_buoc: Use scissors to trim the sharp spines on the head and tail, the antennae, and the legs of the prawns. Butterfly the back and remove the vein.
Mix the mustard sauce in advance: combine soy sauce, oyster sauce, mustard, salt, and sugar. Stir well!
Wash the cilantro and cut into sections; set aside.
Drain the prawns. Add oil to the pan and add the prawns directly. Fry over medium heat until the surface is golden brown, then remove.
Add the minced garlic to the remaining oil. Sauté over high heat until white smoke rises and the garlic is fragrant. Add the prawns and butter, letting the prawns absorb the buttery aroma.
Pour in the prepared sauce, bring to a boil over high heat, and toss the prawns. Once the sauce thickens, add the alcohol (30 g for cooking wine or beer; only 15 g for rum to get a deep aroma).
Wait for the sauce to thicken slightly, add the cilantro, toss twice, and serve.

mon_an.ten: Steamed Mandarin Fish with Scallion Oil
mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed Mandarin Fish with Scallion Oil is a home-style steamed dish with a strong scallion aroma and tender meat. It has a light, fresh Chinese flavor profile suitable for many regions. Mandarin fish is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids; through careful deodorizing, it retains its freshness and nutrition. The method is very beginner-friendly with a high success rate. It takes about 45 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Example for 2 servings. In practice, since the texture and freshness change with the size of the fish, it is recommended to choose a 2-serving size for the best flavor.
10 g seasoned soy sauce for steamed fish
Steaming plate (flat enough to fit the fish)
cac_buoc: Buy a pre-cleaned fish from the market (if cleaning yourself, do not keep the internal organs). Scrape off all scales from the body.
Use paper towels to wipe away blood from the spine and the black membrane inside the belly (blood affects flavor, and the membrane is the source of fishy odors).
Use a knife to scrape the fish skin several times to remove slime for further deodorizing, then rinse the fish inside and out with clean water.

Lay the fish flat on the board and pat dry with paper towels. With the head to the left and tail to the right, make vertical cuts every 3 cm starting from the gills, deep enough to reach the spine. Repeat on the other side.
Place the fish in a basin, ensuring there is no excess water.
Take a 50 g piece of ginger (egg-sized), peel, wash, and slice into 3 mm thick slices.
Wash the bird's eye chilies, remove stems, and cut into 2 mm rounds (or 1 mm wide strips).
Wash the scallion, remove roots, and cut into 3 cm sections. If the scallion is thick, split it down the middle.
Add 8 g salt and 25 g cooking wine to the basin. Wear disposable gloves and massage the fish for 1 minute, ensuring every part is coated.
After massaging, tuck a ginger slice into each cut on the body and place 3 slices inside the belly. Marinate for 10 minutes (do not marinate too long or the freshness will decrease).
While marinating, add 5 L of water to the steamer pot and bring to a boil.
After marinating, the fish will release liquid. Discard the liquid, cooking wine, and ginger slices used for marinating. Rinse the fish inside and out, then pat dry with paper towels.
Place the fish on the steaming plate and re-insert fresh ginger slices into the cuts and the belly.
Place the plate in the steamer, cover, and steam over medium heat for 20 minutes.
Steam will condense into fish juices on the plate; do not discard this after cooking, as it is the essence of the fresh flavor.
Use the gripper to remove the plate. Drizzle 10 g of seasoned soy sauce over and around the fish.
Evenly sprinkle the scallion sections and bird's eye chilies over the fish.
Pour 15 g of vegetable oil into an iron wok and heat slowly over medium-low heat for 5 minutes. Do not use high heat or the oil will evaporate too quickly.
Slowly drizzle the hot oil over the fish. The deliciously fresh Steamed Mandarin Fish is ready!

mon_an.ten: Braised Sea Cucumber with Scallions (Cong Shao Hai Shen)
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic Lu cuisine home-style seafood dish, characterized by a strong scallion aroma and tender, chewy sea cucumber that has absorbed the flavors of a glossy, savory-sweet sauce. Sea cucumber is rich in collagen and micronutrients, making it excellent for health. The overall cooking difficulty is not high, but you must set aside time to properly rehydrate the dried sea cucumber. The actual braising takes about 30 minutes, and beginners can easily succeed by following the steps.
cac_buoc: Cut the scallion whites into 1 cm sections and set aside.
Cut the sea cucumber into 1 cm sections and set aside.
In a small bowl, combine 20 g oyster sauce, 10 g light soy sauce, and 2 g white sugar; stir well.
In another bowl, mix starch and water to make a starch slurry for thickening.
Heat the pan and add 20-25 ml of cooking oil. Wait 10 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Add the scallion whites and turn to *low heat*, being careful not to burn them. Fry for about 3-5 minutes.
Use chopsticks to remove the scallions and set them aside on a plate.
Pour in the prepared sauce, sauté until fragrant, and wait for 1-2 minutes.
Add the cut sea cucumber and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add 100 ml of water, turn to medium-low heat, and wait for 5 minutes.
When the sauce in the pot is almost gone, pour in the starch slurry and return the fried scallions to the pot.
Once the sauce has *thickened into a glaze*, turn off the heat and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: This famous traditional Cantonese dish stands out for its fresh, fragrant, and tender texture. The shrimp is sweet and snappy, complemented by a bold garlic aroma. Sea shrimp is rich in high-quality protein, calcium, selenium, and other micronutrients, while the minced garlic helps with sterilization and appetite. The method is very simple, involving just a few steps: processing the shrimp, spreading the sauce, steaming, and drizzling with oil. It takes about 15 minutes in total.
cac_buoc: Use a knife to butterfly the shrimp from the head down to 1 cm above the tail.
Spread the minced garlic sauce in the middle of the shrimp body and place them on a plate.
Add hot water to the pot, place the plate inside, and steam over high heat for 3 minutes.
Heat the oil until hot, pour it over the shrimp, and drizzle with light soy sauce.

mon_an.mo_ta: Garlic butter shrimp is a classic Western-style seafood dish featuring tender, crispy shrimp coated in a rich garlic and butter sauce with a hint of lemon. High in quality protein and energized by butter, it is perfect for a quick nutritional boost. The recipe is simple, using common ingredients that are easy for beginners to master, taking about twenty minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 1-2 people.
cac_buoc: Remove the heads and shells from the shrimp while keeping the tails intact, devein with a toothpick, wash thoroughly, and pat dry with paper towels.
Mince the garlic and set aside.
Heat the skillet over medium heat and add 10 ml of olive oil.
When the oil is hot, add the shrimp and sear each side for 1-1.5 minutes until they change color, then remove and set aside.
Add the butter to the same pan; once melted, add the minced garlic and sauté over low heat until fragrant (about 30 seconds).
If using white wine, add it now and cook until the alcohol evaporates (about 1 minute).
Return the shrimp to the pan and toss well with the garlic butter sauce (about 1 minute).
Squeeze in the lemon juice, toss quickly, and immediately turn off the heat.
Arrange on a plate and drizzle with the remaining sauce from the pan.

mon_an.mo_ta: This traditional home-style dish from Fuzhou, Fujian, features clams enveloped in a crispy-on-the-outside, soft-on-the-inside fried egg, carrying the savory aroma of onions and soy sauce. Clams are rich in high-quality protein, zinc, iron, and other trace elements, providing balanced nutrition when combined with eggs. The difficulty is moderate, requiring some heat control during frying, but the steps are straightforward. It takes about 30 minutes to bring to the table.
cac_buoc: Bring water to a boil, add the clams, boil for 2 minutes, then remove and discard the shells; place the clam meat in a large bowl.
Add the onion, light soy sauce, cooking wine, chicken powder, and starch to the bowl and mix thoroughly.
Crack 2 eggs into the bowl and continue to whisk.
Heat oil in a pan, pour in the clam mixture, fry until one side is golden brown, then flip and continue frying the other side.

mon_an.mo_ta: This dish captures the seasonal savory-fresh flavors of Pinghu, Zhejiang in autumn. The smooth crab roe is coated in savory bean paste, the meat is sweet and delicate, and the sauce is perfect for mixing with rice. It is rich in high-quality protein and trace elements. The difficulty is moderate, suitable for beginners with some basic skills, taking about 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Scrub the crabs clean, then cut them in half on a cutting board.
Add rapeseed oil to the pot, sauté the minced ginger and bean paste until fragrant, then add the rock sugar and stir until melted and small bubbles appear; scoop out the mixture.
Spread a layer of the paste on a plate, then arrange the crabs neatly on top with the cut side facing down.
Add some green onion segments and ginger slices; it is recommended to crack an egg or spread the ground pork at the bottom of the plate.
Place in a steamer and steam for 10-12 minutes.

mon_an.mo_ta: Yangshuo Beer Fish is a famous local specialty from Yangshuo, Guangxi. It uses fresh Li River fish fried with the scales on and braised in beer instead of water. The scales become crispy and fragrant, the meat stays tender, and the beer aroma blends with the light acidity of tomatoes for a unique, bold flavor. The fish is rich in protein and minerals, while the tomatoes and peppers provide vitamins and stimulate the appetite. Medium difficulty, slightly challenging for beginners, but following the steps ensures success. Ready in about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 sword-bone fish or carp (about 750 g, do not descale)
cac_buoc: Clean the fish by removing the innards but keeping the scales; butterfly it from the belly (keeping the back connected). Marinate with 15 ml cooking wine, ginger slices, and 3 g salt for 15 minutes.
Cut the tomatoes and bell peppers into bite-sized pieces, crush the garlic, slice the ginger, and cut the green onions into segments (separating the white parts from the green leaves).

Rub the bottom of the pan with a ginger slice, heat the pan, then pour in 30 ml of cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add the fish (skin side down) and fry until both sides are golden and the scales are crispy; remove and set aside.
Leave the base oil in the pan, then sauté the white parts of the green onions, ginger slices, and garlic cloves until fragrant.
Add 15 g of Guilin chili sauce and stir-fry until the red oil is released.
Add the tomato pieces and sauté until they soften and release their juices.
Pour in the entire bottle of beer, add 15 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml dark soy sauce, 5 g white sugar, and 5 g salt; stir well.
Add the fried fish, bring to a boil over high heat, then turn down to medium-low, cover, and simmer for 15-20 minutes.
Open the lid, add the bell pepper pieces, and continue to cook for 3-5 minutes.
Turn to high heat to reduce the sauce until thickened, sprinkle with green onion leaves, and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: This pan-seared fish is a flavorful home-style river fish dish. After marinating and air-drying, the fish becomes firm and fragrant, seared until the skin is golden and crispy while the meat remains delicate and savory with a hint of spice and sweetness from bean paste and green chilies. It is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids. Requires 2-4 days of marinating and drying; cooking time is about half an hour. Frying the fish requires patience and heat control, which may be challenging for beginners, but the aromatic result is exceptionally good with rice.
cac_buoc: Butterfly the fish from the back (ask the fishmonger to do this; do not cut the belly), then wash thoroughly.
Rub salt evenly over the fish, pour in about 80 ml of cooking wine and 20 g of minced ginger, then place in the refrigerator to marinate for 1-2 days.
Remove the marinated fish and hang it to air-dry until semi-dry (about 1-2 days, depending on temperature and sunlight).
Before cooking, rinse the fish with clean water and pat dry (to prevent oil splattering).
Heat the pan over high heat, then quickly switch to low heat. Add oil and swirl to coat the entire surface. Slide the fish into the pan along the side (fry the back side first).
Once the fish is in the pan (and after flipping), do not move it immediately (the skin tears easily); fry for about 30 seconds, then try shaking the pan gently.
Fry the back side for about 1 minute, flip and fry for 1-2 minutes until both sides are golden brown.
Once both sides are seared, push the fish to the side of the pan to make room to sauté the bean paste until fragrant, then add the ginger and garlic.
Once the aromatics are fragrant, add the cooking wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and pour in hot water until it is level with or slightly below the fish.
Adjust to medium-high heat and cook for 5-10 minutes, then add the green bell pepper segments, white sugar, chicken powder, thirteen-spice powder, and aged vinegar.
Reduce to low heat for 2-5 minutes, add the green onions and cilantro, then serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Carp with Napa Cabbage is a fragrant and savory home-style stew. The fish is tender and flavorful, while the napa cabbage becomes sweet and absorbs the delicious broth, representing a typical Northern Chinese flavor. Carp is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids, while napa cabbage provides fiber and vitamins for balanced nutrition. The process involves frying and stewing, which requires some skill but is not overly complex. Suitable for those with basic kitchen experience; takes about 40 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: adjust seasonings based on the size of the fish.
13 baby napa cabbage leaves (can add more as they shrink)
cac_buoc: Wash the carp and score the skin (make several diagonal cuts on both sides to help it absorb flavor).
Wash the baby napa cabbage and set aside on a plate.
Add oil to the pot; once hot, add a little salt, ginger, garlic, Pixian bean paste, cinnamon, and star anise, and sauté until fragrant.
Place the fish in the pan to fry (3 minutes), flipping every 30 seconds.
Add water (enough to almost cover the fish), then add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and the baby napa cabbage.
Stew over high heat for 15-20 minutes; when the liquid has mostly reduced, add salt and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Bighead Carp with Tofu is a home-style braised dish where the tender fish meat is deeply flavored and the tofu absorbs the rich, savory, and slightly spicy broth. Fish is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids, while tofu provides plant-based protein and calcium. The difficulty is moderate; frying the fish requires patience to prevent sticking, but the steps are clear enough for beginners. Takes about 40 minutes from start to finish.
cac_buoc: Clean and score the fish, then marinate with ginger slices and cooking wine for 5-10 minutes.
Cut the firm tofu into pieces and soak in water; set aside.
Add oil to the pan; you can add a pinch of salt to prevent the fish from sticking. Pat the marinated fish dry with paper towels, place it in the pan, and fry both sides.
Once both sides are seared, push the fish to the side of the pan to make room to sauté the green onion, ginger, garlic, dried chilies, bay leaves, and star anise until fragrant.
Once the aromatics are fragrant, add the cooking wine, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, rock sugar, and cinnamon, then pour in the hot water until it is level with or slightly below the fish.
Bring to a boil over high heat, add the firm tofu (placing it against the sides of the pan), add salt, and switch to low heat.
Braise over low heat for 10-15 minutes, then turn to high heat to reduce the sauce before serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: Pan-seared butter shrimp is a rich home-style seafood dish with tender and snappy shrimp meat. Fresh shrimp are high in quality protein and minerals like calcium and zinc, while butter adds a creamy aroma and energy. The method is relatively simple, requiring only patience in prepping the fresh shrimp, making it beginner-friendly. Total time is about one hour.
cac_buoc: Remove the heads of the fresh shrimp and pull out the veins (if this is difficult, you can remove them after butterflying in the next step). Use scissors or a knife to butterfly the back of the shrimp, then pat dry and set aside.
Prepare the sauce: combine the light soy sauce, rice wine, white sugar, and salt in a small bowl and stir well.
Heat the pan over medium-high heat, add the cooking oil, and wait 10 seconds for the oil to get hot.
Add all the shrimp to the pan, grind the black pepper over them, and toss.
Once the shrimp change color, add the butter. When the butter is completely melted, pour in the prepared sauce and continue to toss.
Toss over high heat for 15 seconds to reduce the sauce, then serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: An ultra-fast breakfast: slightly crispy toasted bread sandwiched with sweet jam. It is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, easy to carry, and a typical Western-style snack. It primarily provides carbohydrates and sugar for a quick morning energy boost. There is almost no barrier to entry, making it perfect for busy people who aren't skilled at cooking. Takes only about 2 minutes from start to finish, requires no stove, and involves almost no cleanup.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Enough jam to cover one side of the bread
cac_buoc: Place the bread in the toaster.
Select the browning level; the bread will pop up automatically when finished.
After two minutes, the toast is done and pops up.
Take out one slice, spread it generously with jam, and cover with the other slice.
Wrap in a paper towel to eat on the go or eat before heading out.
Done in two minutes—fast, simple, and delicious. Perfect for busy programmers. Minimal time, no waste, and no dishes to wash.

mon_an.mo_ta: A sunny-side up egg is a quick home-style breakfast made in the microwave. It has a soft texture with set whites and a slightly runny yolk—a classic fast-cooking dish. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and various vitamins, making them easy to digest. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly. Using a microwave with power settings takes only 3 minutes; for those without, it only takes a few minutes of repeated heating.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Use the conditions above to calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
Amount of salt: 1 g per egg.
Amount of oil: 5 ml per egg.
cac_buoc: Prepare a small bowl, pour in the calculated amount of oil, sprinkle with salt, and mix well. Tilt the bowl to coat the surface with oil.
Take an egg and crack it into the small bowl.
Pierce the surface of the yolk: make 5 small holes with a toothpick or 1 hole with a chopstick.
Place in the microwave and cook on medium power for 3 minutes.
(For microwaves without power control) Prepare a small bowl, pour in the oil, sprinkle with salt, and mix well. Tilt the bowl to coat the surface.
Place in the microwave for 1 minute.
If the egg has not set into a solid mass, continue to microwave in 30-second increments.

mon_an.mo_ta: This egg is prepared using a scientific circulating boiling method, resulting in a fluffy yolk, evenly set white, and distinct layers of flavor. This method retains more nutrients, with a polyphenol content 23% higher than traditional boiling, and is rich in protein. The difficulty level is quite high, requiring precise temperature control and multiple transfers; estimated time is about 35 minutes.
cac_buoc: Prepare two pots of water: Pot A maintained at boiling (100 °C) and Pot B maintained at warm (30 °C).
Use a slotted spoon to place the egg into Pot A and start the timer.
Transfer the egg to the other pot exactly every 2 minutes.
Repeat the transfer process for a total of 16 times (total time 32 minutes).
After the final transfer, let it sit in Pot B for 30 seconds.
Immediately place in ice water (0 °C) to stop the cooking process (hold for 30 seconds).
When peeling, start from the air cell at the blunt end and peel the membrane along the vertical axis.

mon_an.mo_ta: Microwave sunny-side up eggs are a convenient and quick home-cooked dish, featuring soft whites, jammy yolks, and a hint of sesame oil aroma. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and lecithin. The method is extremely simple, easy for beginners to master, taking only about 2 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for one person's breakfast.
cac_buoc: Crack the eggs into a small bowl and use chopsticks to poke 2 holes in each yolk to prevent splattering in the microwave.
Pour room-temperature drinking water into the bowl.
Add the salt to the bowl.
Finally, add the sesame oil.
Place the bowl with all ingredients into the microwave and cook on high power for 80 seconds.
When the time is up, use oven mitts to remove the finished dish.

mon_an.mo_ta: A smooth steamed egg dish made quickly in the microwave with a pudding-like texture, perfect for a quick family meal. Rich in high-quality protein and easy to digest, it is ideal for breakfast or a light snack. Very simple to make, even for beginners, the entire process takes about 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A few drops of sesame oil (for serving)
Use the conditions above to calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
Warm water or broth 100-120 ml (1.0-1.2 times the volume of beaten eggs)
Plastic wrap or a microwave-safe lid
cac_buoc: Beat the eggs, add warm water/broth, salt, and light soy sauce; stir gently until well combined, trying not to create bubbles.
Strain the egg mixture through a sieve into a heat-resistant bowl; if there are air bubbles on the surface, poke them gently with a toothpick.
Cover with plastic wrap and poke 8-10 small holes, or use a microwave-safe lid (leaving a small gap).
Place in the microwave and cook:
700W: 1 minute 30 seconds → depending on the situation, cook for another 20-30 seconds until the surface is just set.
600W: about 1 minute 40 seconds – 2 minutes 10 seconds.
800W: about 1 minute 10 seconds – 1 minute 40 seconds.
After cooking, remove and let it rest for 1 minute to allow residual heat to fully cook the center.
Drizzle with sesame oil and sprinkle with scallions before serving.
Different power levels and containers will affect the time; it is recommended to test with short intervals the first time to find the optimal setting for your device.

mon_an.mo_ta: A quick microwave version of a sponge cake that is fluffy, sweet, and fragrant—a family dessert that even absolute beginners can easily make. Based on eggs and flour, combined with butter for energy and a rich aroma, and sugar for a quick energy boost; adding nuts or fruit increases fiber and vitamins. With just a few ingredients and a high-power microwave, it's done in a minute. From preparation to enjoyment, it can take as little as 2 minutes, with beginners finishing in about 20 minutes.
cac_buoc: Add the following ingredients, ensuring they do not exceed 3/4 of the container's capacity.
Scoop an amount of butter about half the size of an egg into the container and microwave for 15 seconds to melt.
Melt or mash the chocolate/banana into granules or a paste.
Crack an egg into the container and whisk until well combined.
Add 15 g white (or brown) sugar (those who like it sweeter can add more) (see note 4).
Add 1 g salt (if subsequent flavor ingredients contain salt, adjust accordingly).
Add 2.5 g baking powder.
Add 15 g flour (the gluten content does not significantly affect the result).
Add any flavor ingredients you like! (Dry ingredients like nuts and cookies are not added at this stage).
Stir until it reaches a thick yogurt-like consistency with no dry flour visible.
Top with your choice of dry ingredients (excluding powdered mixes).
Give yourself a pat on the back 🥰
Microwave on high for 1 minute (until the cake rises and sets).
Remove the cup (it will be very hot!), take a photo for social media, and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Italian Sausage Shakshuka is a rich and fresh Mediterranean-style dish featuring poached eggs nestled in a sweet and savory tomato meat sauce, served with crispy bread for dipping. The main ingredients provide high-quality protein, while tomatoes, bell peppers, and onions offer vitamins and fiber. It is not difficult to make; just pay attention to the heat when poaching the eggs. The entire process takes about 30 minutes to reach the table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
Barilla Napoletana pasta sauce: 1 jar (400 g, provides the base flavor of tomato, onion, and herbs)
Bread (suggested: Sourdough, Ciabatta, or thick-cut sandwich bread)
cac_buoc: Remove the Italian pork sausage casings and set aside; finely dice the onion; thinly slice the bell pepper.
Add 10 ml - 15 ml olive oil to a wide skillet and heat over medium heat.
Add the prepared sausage or meat; sauté until the edges are golden and crispy (if using raw sausage, use a spoon to break it into small pieces as it browns).
Add the diced onion and sliced bell pepper to the skillet with the meat; continue to sauté for 4 - 5 minutes until the vegetables are soft and the onions are translucent.
Pour in the Barilla Napoletana sauce and stir well. Adjust to medium-low heat and maintain a simmer for 2 - 3 minutes. (If the sauce looks too thick, add 15 ml of water).
Use the back of a spoon to make 3 - 4 small "wells" in the sauce.
Carefully crack an egg into each well.

Cover the skillet and use the steam to cook the whites. Wait 3 - 5 minutes. Note: Check frequently. When the whites are opaque and set, but the yolks still jiggle slightly when the pan is shaken (runny state), this step is complete.
Turn off the heat. Depending on preference, sprinkle with grated Parmesan, fresh parsley, or red pepper flakes.
Bring the whole skillet to the table and serve with crusty bread to dip into the yolks and sauce.

mon_an.mo_ta: Shou Zhuo Bing is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with distinct layers, making it a favorite homemade flour-based dish. The crust is made from a semi-cooked dough that is chewy and pliable, combined with eggs and vegetables for balanced nutrition. The method is beginner-friendly, taking about 40 minutes from kneading to pan-frying, making it perfect for busy mornings.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 1-2 people.
cac_buoc: Place the flour in a bowl, add boiling water and stir into shaggy clumps, then add cold water and knead into a smooth dough; cover with a damp cloth and rest for 20 minutes.
Divide the dough into portions of about 100 g each, roll into balls, and then roll out into thin sheets.
Brush oil evenly over the surface, sprinkle with salt, roll into a spiral shape, and rest for 10 minutes.
Roll the dough out again into a thin pancake with even thickness.
Add oil to a hot pan and fry over low heat until both sides are golden and puffy.
Once the pancake is fried, layer it with a fried egg, lettuce, ham, cheese, etc., then roll it up and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: A traditional Chinese sweet congee that is fragrant, soft, and sticky. Cooking glutinous rice with red dates and longan creates a naturally sweet flavor that warms the body and stomach. It is believed to nourish the blood, calm the mind, improve memory, and benefit the heart and spleen. The method is very approachable for beginners, taking about 70 minutes from preparation until the aroma fills the house.
cac_buoc: Shell the longans, rinse twice with clean water, and soak in a bowl for 10 minutes.
Rinse the red dates twice with clean water and soak in a bowl for 10 minutes.
Place the glutinous rice in a rice cooker, wash twice with clean water, then add 2000 ml of water.
Add the longans and red dates to the rice cooker.
Turn on the rice cooking mode; the congee will be ready after 1 hour.

mon_an.mo_ta: Boiled corn is a quick family dish that is sweet and tender. Boiling fresh corn with its husks preserves its original flavor, while adding salt and sugar enhances the sweetness. Rich in fiber, vitamins, and starch, it provides a satisfying sense of fullness. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Choose to add sugar or not according to taste (optional).
Pot large enough to hold the corn
Water to cover the corn by about half a knuckle
When boiling corn, start with a light brine of about 2 g salt per 50 ml water.
cac_buoc: Peel the outer husks of the fresh corn, keeping some of the inner husks in the pot.
Pour in water to cover the corn by about half a knuckle, then add salt and sugar.
Once the water boils, turn to low heat, cover, and continue to cook for 15-20 minutes; it is fine to cook the corn a bit longer.
Once cooked, drain the water, let cool, and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Onsen Tamago originated in Japan; the whites are a semi-liquid custard while the yolks are warm and creamy—a delicate texture that is the complete opposite of a standard soft-boiled egg. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein, lecithin, and various vitamins, providing comprehensive nutrition. Preparation requires a thermometer to control the water temperature at 70 °C; while it demands temperature precision, the steps are simple. With a patient 30-minute wait, it's done. Served with kombu soy sauce and scallions, it is a fresh and light snack.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Kombu soy sauce (a low-sodium Japanese soy sauce used to season onsen eggs)
Quantity: 1 egg, adjust based on your appetite and pot size.
cac_buoc: Pour tap water into a pot, ensuring the water level is about 3 cm above the eggs; insert the thermometer into the water.
Turn on the stove or induction cooktop, gradually adjusting the power or flame so the water temperature stays at 70 °C.
Place the eggs in the pot. The eggs must not overlap; they should all sit on the bottom with enough room to move slightly.
Maintain the current temperature for 25 minutes.
Prepare a cup of ice water.
Remove the eggs and immediately place them in the ice water; wait for 3 minutes.
Crack the egg into a small bowl to finish.
If using a manual thermometer (non-electric), the probe must be submerged at least 6 cm; if using an electronic thermometer, there are no special requirements.
A thicker pot can be used for easier temperature control.
While 70 °C for 25 minutes is sufficient to kill Salmonella, it is still recommended to consume in moderation or use pasteurized eggs certified for raw consumption.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a simple home-style egg dish that can be easily made using a standard electric cooker. The yolks remain runny and creamy with a rich flavor. Each egg provides about 6 g of high-quality protein, making it especially suitable for fitness enthusiasts. The process is straightforward; just master the heating and resting times. Even beginners can do it quickly, with the whole process taking about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 or more eggs (as many as your electric cooker can hold)
Cold water to cover the eggs by about 2 cm
cac_buoc: Place the eggs in the electric cooker. The eggs must not overlap; they should all sit on the bottom with enough room to move slightly.
Pour in cold water to cover the eggs by about 2 cm.
With the lid open, use maximum power to heat until the water boils (about 85-95 degrees, simmering, no need for a rolling boil).
Turn off the heat, cover the lid, and let the eggs sit.
For a runny yolk, let them sit for 6 minutes.
If you want the yolks to be fully cooked and powdery, let them sit for 10 minutes.
Drain the water and rinse the eggs with cold water for about 1 minute before peeling and serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: Pan-fried dumplings (potstickers) are a staple home-style dish featuring a golden, crispy bottom and a tender, juicy filling, commonly found on Northern Chinese dining tables. Made from frozen dumplings, they are rich in starch and protein, making for a simple and quick meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Sesame seeds, scallions (chopped), or other garnishes
1 pack of dumplings (choose according to appetite, approx. 10 - 15 pieces)
cac_buoc: Prepare a pan (a non-stick pan works best).
Add 10 ml - 15 ml of cooking oil.
Turn on the heat and add the dumplings (try to spread them evenly without overlapping).
Immediately pour in fresh water until it reaches about 1/2 the height of the dumplings.
Cover the pan (the heat should be on high at this point).
Wait for 8 - 10 minutes.
When only about 2 mm of water remains in the pan, turn the heat to medium and begin frying.
Once the water has completely evaporated, shake the pan to ensure the dumplings brown evenly.
Sprinkle with black sesame seeds and scallions, then cover for another 10 seconds.
After 1 - 2 minutes, lift a dumpling to check the bottom; if a golden crispy crust has formed, remove from the pan immediately.

mon_an.mo_ta: Oatmeal egg pancakes are a nutritious and quick breakfast with a soft texture, featuring the grain aroma of oats and the richness of eggs and milk in a simple home-style fashion. High in protein, starch, and fiber, they provide ample energy, making them especially suitable for fitness enthusiasts and busy work mornings. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about ten minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 2 eggs (can also use 2 egg whites and 1 yolk)
50 g plain dry oats (approximately the volume of one egg)
Optional: 50 g vegetables, such as spinach
A handful of finely chopped vegetables
cac_buoc: Mix the milk with the dry oats and stir until the mixture thickens.
Beat the eggs until well combined and uniform in color.
Pour the beaten eggs into the oat and milk mixture, and continue stirring until thick and even.
Add a layer of butter to the pan and coat evenly.
Pour the mixture into the pan and spread it into a pancake shape.
Cook over low heat for two to three minutes. If adding vegetables, stir the chopped greens in during the cooking process.
Flip the pancake and continue cooking for another two minutes.
Remove from the pan and serve for breakfast with the remaining milk.

mon_an.mo_ta: A convenient and nutritious breakfast rich in protein and fiber, skillfully combining the smoothness of milk, the grain aroma of oats, and the soft-crisp texture of a fried egg. It is warm, easy to digest, and provides a long-lasting feeling of fullness. The process is direct and extremely beginner-friendly, taking about three minutes to complete. Serve with fruits and vegetables for a more refreshing meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Use the conditions above to calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
cac_buoc: Pour the milk into a breakfast cup (cold milk is fine).
Prepare 200 ml of water; if using filtered water, add the oats directly. Otherwise, bring the water to a boil before adding the oats.
After the water has boiled for 2 minutes, the oats are cooked.
Drain the cooked oats and add them to the milk (try not to pour the cooking water into the milk as it affects the flavor).
Alternatively, use instant oats.
Pour the milk into the container with instant oats and stir.
Place the mixture in the microwave.
Microwave on medium power for 4 minutes.
Heat a pan and add a thin layer of oil. Once the oil is hot, fry the egg for 20 seconds per side; consider seasoning with a base (3 g salt and pepper, optional).
Turn off the heat and serve on a plate.
The basic cooking takes 3 minutes; the finished dish is served at room temperature and is very easy to eat, usually taking only 2 minutes to finish.
🥑 Even better when served with fruits, vegetables, or soda crackers.

mon_an.mo_ta: Air fryer toast is an extremely simple and quick staple dish, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with a pure wheat aroma, making it particularly suitable for fat-loss diets. Rich in fiber and plant protein, it provides a lasting feeling of fullness. There are no barriers to making this; simply place the bread slices in the air fryer. It is extremely beginner-friendly, taking only about five minutes from preparation to completion.
cac_buoc: Take two slices of bread (whole wheat bread is recommended).
Place the bread slices upright in the air fryer.
Toast at 200 °C for 5 minutes.
Remove and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a soft, fluffy, and delicious American home-style egg dish. Adding milk makes the eggs creamy and smooth with a cotton-like texture, rich in high-quality protein and calcium. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 20 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 10 g whole milk or heavy cream
cac_buoc: Crack the eggs into a large bowl, add salt, and beat until frothy. Let sit for 15 minutes.
Cut the butter into small pieces and add to the pan. Pour in the beaten eggs and turn on low heat, stirring constantly.
As soon as the butter melts, quickly scramble the eggs into a smooth consistency. Turn off the heat just before the eggs are fully set.
Add the milk and stir for 15 seconds until the scrambled eggs are moist and silky, then serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: This simplified version of a Scotch egg features a crispy outer layer and a soft, runny yolk inside, blending the richness of cheese with the smoky flavor of bacon. It is a creative snack inspired by British cuisine. The egg provides high-quality protein, the cheese adds calcium, and the scallion pancake wrap meets the energy needs of a full meal. The process is not complicated and easy for beginners, taking about 20 to 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1-2 portions of scallion pancake dough (depending on egg size)
cac_buoc: Place the egg in a pot of cold water. Once the water boils, cook for 3 minutes, then remove.
Transfer the egg to an ice bath; this makes peeling faster and keeps the egg intact.
Wrap a slice of cheese around the egg.
Wrap a slice of bacon around the cheese-covered egg.
Trim the ends of the scallion pancake dough and wrap it around the egg into a rectangular shape.
Place in a pan when the oil reaches medium-high heat (oil surface shimmers, light blue smoke appears, and bubbles form around a chopstick inserted into the oil). Fry until golden brown.
Alternatively, cook in an air fryer at 160 °C for 15 minutes.
Slice and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This traditional snack is infused with a deep tea aroma, savory and easy to eat. Rich in high-quality protein, it is a nutritious and quick breakfast choice. The steps are clear and the difficulty is moderate. Beginners should pay attention to the heat and spice ratios. It takes about 30 minutes to complete, and one batch is enough for 2-3 people, making it perfect for a relaxed weekend preparation.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Use the conditions above to calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
cac_buoc: Boil the eggs starting from cold water on high heat for about 8 minutes (depending on your stove).
Remove the eggs and rinse under cold water.
Gently tap the eggs against each other so that every shell has cracks.
Place the eggs back in the pot and add the star anise, bay leaves, cinnamon, fennel seeds, rock sugar, black tea, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and salt.
Add enough water to completely submerge the eggs.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 15 minutes.
After simmering for 15 minutes, remove the whole spices. Let the eggs soak in the liquid for a while longer for better flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a standout home-style dish known for its pudding-like smoothness and delicate, fresh flavor. Enjoyed across many regions, it is often affectionately called "egg cake" in the North. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and lecithin, making this a convenient choice for daily nutrition. Simply master the egg-to-water ratio and the secret of slow steaming on low heat. It is very beginner-friendly, taking about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat until smooth.
In a separate container, prepare warm water (20-30°C) at 1.5 times the volume of the beaten eggs (use half an eggshell to measure 0.5 parts water). Dissolve the salt in the water.
Pour the salt water into the beaten eggs and stir in one direction (clockwise or counter-clockwise). Scoop off any surface bubbles; for a smoother texture, strain the mixture through a sieve.
Cover the bowl with aluminum foil (or a plate) and place it in a steamer pot with about 3 cm of water.
Bring to a boil over medium heat, then turn to the lowest heat setting and steam for 4 minutes.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a traditional Northern flour-based dish, soft, fluffy, and delicious with a subtle wheat aroma. Using frozen flower rolls (Hua Juan) for steaming allows for a quick supplement of starch and fiber. The method is extremely simple and easy for beginners to master. The entire process takes only half an hour, making it an ideal quick breakfast.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 5 frozen flower rolls (Hua Juan) (3 pieces for a smaller portion) (available at supermarkets or grocery apps)
cac_buoc: Remove 5 flower rolls from the packaging.
Arrange the rolls flat on a plate, trying not to overlap them.
Pour 400 ml of water into the pot, place the steamer rack inside, set the plate of rolls on the rack, and cover the pot.
Turn the heat to high and bring the water to a boil.
Reduce to medium heat and steam for 15 minutes.
Open the lid and gently feel the surface temperature of a roll. If not hot enough, cover and steam longer; if ready, turn off the heat and remove.
Remove the plate and let cool to about 50 °C before serving.

mon_an.ten: Pan-fried Sticky Rice Cakes with Egg
mon_an.mo_ta: A simple and quick snack with a slightly crispy exterior and a chewy, soft interior, wrapped in the aroma of egg and a hint of sweetness. This is a classic Southern home-style flavor. The sticky rice cakes provide plenty of starch while the eggs add protein; it is high in energy and very filling. The process is extremely simple and easy for beginners to master, taking only about ten minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 10 g brown sugar (recommended range 8 g - 15 g)
cac_buoc: Cut the sticky rice cakes into small rectangular pieces for easier frying.
Crack an egg into a bowl and beat well, then add 2 g of salt.
Dip each piece of sticky rice cake into the beaten egg, coating both sides evenly.
Pour 10 ml of vegetable oil into a pan, add the coated cake pieces, and fry slowly over low heat until softened.
Slowly pour the remaining beaten egg over the surface of the cakes.
Use chopsticks or a spatula to flip the cakes, frying back and forth until golden brown, then serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This Western-style breakfast sandwich features water-packed tuna mixed with mayonnaise and Russian-style pickle brine for a fresh, slightly tangy, and smooth flavor. Combined with crispy toasted bread, it is particularly filling. Rich in high-quality protein and Omega-3, it provides a quick energy boost. It is very simple to make—just mix the sauce and use a sandwich maker; even beginners can finish it in 5 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Russian-style pickle brine 10-15 mL (adjust to taste)
cac_buoc: Add the tuna, mayonnaise, and Russian-style pickle brine to a bowl and stir with a spoon, ensuring the tuna is finely mashed and the sauce reaches a pasty consistency; set aside
Place 1 slice of bread onto the sandwich maker
Spread the prepared tuna mixture onto the bread, 10-15 ml is recommended
Top with the remaining square bread slice, press the sandwich maker down, and turn it on
Wait for the machine to stop heating, then serve on a plate

mon_an.mo_ta: A Korean soft-boiled egg side dish with a rich sweet and spicy flavor. The sauce coats the whites, while the inside remains soft and smooth with a slightly spicy aftertaste. Eggs provide high-quality protein and lecithin, making them nutritious and filling. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly; the process from boiling the eggs to chilling them for flavor takes about an hour and a half.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. Below is the sauce amount for one portion, enough to marinate 5 - 8 eggs.
Soy sauce (or light soy sauce) 4 tbsp
cac_buoc: Bring a pot of water to a boil, then add the eggs and boil for 7 minutes (to achieve the perfect soft-boiled state).
While the eggs are boiling, prepare the sauce: add 4 tbsp soy sauce, 4 tbsp water, 2 tbsp mirin, and 2 tbsp white sugar to a small pot.
Bring the sauce to a boil to evaporate the alcohol in the mirin, then turn off the heat and let it cool; set aside.
Add the sliced chilies to the cooled sauce.
Remove the boiled eggs, place them in ice water to cool, and then peel them.
Place the peeled eggs into the prepared sauce, drizzle 5 ml of sesame oil over the surface, and sprinkle with scallions.
Place in the refrigerator to chill for 1 - 2 hours to allow the eggs to fully absorb the flavors.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a quick and simple Western-style snack featuring bread filled with smooth egg salad and savory bacon, offering a soft texture with a fragrant charred aroma. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein, which, combined with bacon and butter, provides a quick energy boost. The process is very beginner-friendly and takes only about 10 minutes to complete.
cac_buoc: Trim the four crusts off the bread and set aside
Hard-boil the egg and mash it finely
Mix the egg, mayonnaise, salt, and black pepper
Add butter to a pan and fry the bacon until cooked
Assemble the sandwich by placing the prepared egg salad and bacon between the two slices of bread
Cut the square sandwich into triangles and serve on a plate

mon_an.mo_ta: A fragrant Shaanxi-style spicy condiment with glossy red oil, blended with the aroma of sesame and garlic—spicy but not harsh, with a long-lasting aftertaste. Chilies are rich in vitamin C and capsaicin, which help stimulate the palate and warm the body.
