Mastering the oil temperature can be a bit challenging for beginners, but following each step correctly will lead to success. It takes about 10 minutes and is the highlight for mixed dishes and noodles.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Peanut oil 150 ml (can be replaced with rapeseed oil)
White vinegar 5 ml (about one small iron spoon)
Other spices: star anise (1), Sichuan peppercorns (20-50 seeds depending on taste), bay leaves (2-3 leaves), angelica dahurica (2-3 slices), sliced ginger (thumb-thick) (optional)
cac_buoc: Take 2 small garlic cloves and peel them
Use a cutting board to mince the garlic and bird's eye chili
Take a bowl and pour the peanut oil in
When the oil is hot, add the other spices and scallions, wait until the spices are charred, then remove and discard them
Take an iron pot, pour the oil from the bowl in and heat for 2 minutes (if using rapeseed oil, heat until smoking)
The bowl is now empty
Add the dried chili flakes, white sesame, minced garlic, bird's eye chili, salt, five-spice powder, and black cardamom to the empty bowl to make the "spice base"
Turn off the heat and let the oil cool down to about 210 °C
Pour the hot oil from the pot into the bowl and stir well with a spoon (you can pour more into a similar spice bowl at 165 °C and mix them together to increase the spiciness)
After pouring the hot oil and stirring gently, add the white vinegar; the oil will sizzle again. Continue stirring; the white vinegar helps enhance the aroma
When the chili oil has cooled to a warm temperature, add the sugar and MSG; the sugar helps mellow the spiciness and prevents choking

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an ingredient used in Chinese pastry dishes, commonly used for flatbreads (la bing) to help create distinct layers that are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside. It mainly provides starch and fat for energy. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 3 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: All-purpose flour = (number of cakes to be made ÷ 0.13) g
Salt = (number of cakes to be made ÷ 2) g
Oil = (number of cakes to be made × 10 ml)
cac_buoc: Add the flour to a small bowl and add salt
Pour in hot oil at 200 degrees
Use chopsticks to stir into a thick paste until no flour lumps remain.

mon_an.mo_ta: This versatile seasoning sauce is intensely spicy and fragrant with a perfectly savory taste, capturing the essence of street food. It primarily provides fats and aromatic compounds from spices to stimulate the appetite. The method is very simple and stress-free for beginners, taking only about 10 minutes.
cac_buoc: Place all ingredients into a container and mix well.
Heat oil in a pot, using enough oil to completely submerge the ingredients in the container.
Drizzle the hot oil in three stages, 1/3 each time, stirring while pouring.
Finally, add 10 ml sesame oil, 10 ml soy sauce, 10 ml Sichuan pepper oil, and 10 ml oyster sauce.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Caramel Color (Simple Version)
mon_an.mo_ta: Caramel color is a key technique for coloring Chinese braised dishes; when the heat is controlled correctly, it yields a glossy red color and a characteristic caramel aroma. The main ingredient is sugar, providing energy, but it is primarily used to balance the color and flavor of the dish. This simple version requires some heat control; beginners may need extra practice to avoid bitterness or a weak sweet taste. Total time is about ten minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Sugar: 50 g (about 15 single-crystal rock sugar cubes, or granulated white sugar of the same weight. Standard ratio: 50 g sugar for 1000 g meat, can be adjusted by 10 g to taste)
Rock sugar: produces the most vibrant and glossy red caramel color; must be melted with oil and water, otherwise it melts very slowly
Granulated white sugar: must be melted with oil and water, otherwise it melts very slowly
Powdered sugar: can be melted without adding water
Do not use high heat when making caramel color!!! Induction cookers may not provide enough heat; too much heat causes bitterness, too little heat results in a weak sweetness
cac_buoc: ⚠️ Warning and preparation:

The final step of making caramel color (adding water/adding spices) is a continuous operation and requires a very fast reaction. Once the caramel reaches the critical point, hesitating for just a few seconds will make it bitter.
Requirement: Before turning on the stove, you must have 400 ml of boiling water and all prepared scallions, ginger, and garlic placed next to the stove, ensuring you can reach them in 1 second.
Turn on the stove, pour 100 ml of boiling water into the pot
Next, pour 100 ml of oil into the pot as soon as possible after the previous step; you can use medium or high heat at this stage, or high heat if in a hurry
Add the rock sugar (if the pieces are too large, crush them beforehand; the smaller the better)
Adjust to medium heat
Start stirring
Must stir continuously without stopping; when it turns brown, reduce to low heat
It will continue to thin out, turning a dark tea color, then a soy-red color with small bubbles; prepare to execute "Method 1" or "Method 2" below
The small bubbles will gradually disappear, followed by large bubbles; when the large bubbles appear, the caramel color is complete

Quickly proceed to the next step at this moment (whichever method you choose, you must be prepared and act very fast! Otherwise, the heat will be too high and the caramel will turn bitter), choosing based on the cuisine style and personal taste
Method 1: You can directly add 400 ml of boiling water to lower the temperature

Method 2 (Advanced seasoning): When the sugar water turns jujube red and many dense small bubbles appear, quickly add the prepared scallions, ginger, garlic, Sichuan peppercorns, etc., and stir-fry. Once fragrant (within 5-10 seconds), immediately pour in 400 ml of boiling water to lower the temperature and stop the reaction. (*Note: if the subsequent recipe requires searing meat for color, add the meat to stir-fry at this step first, and finally add the water.*)

mon_an.mo_ta: This sauce is pleasantly sweet and sour, serving as the classic flavor base for sweet and sour dishes in Chinese cuisine. The preparation is simple with an easy-to-remember ratio, making it beginner-friendly. It takes about 10 minutes from preparation to completion. Sugar provides energy, while the vinegar helps open the palate and cut through richness, instantly making home-cooked dishes more flavorful.
cac_buoc: Stir all the seasonings together according to the ratio in a small bowl
After preparing the main dish according to its specific recipe, pour the mixed sweet and sour sauce into the pot
Depending on the dish, cook for 5-10 minutes
Use high heat to reduce the sauce until thickened, which helps enhance the richness, aroma, and gloss of the dish

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a homemade sweet and tart jam with a deep fruity aroma, perfect for spreading on bread. Strawberries are rich in vitamin C, though the sugar content during cooking is quite high and can be adjusted to taste. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly, taking about two hours from preparation to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: White sugar 400 g (can be reduced to 200 g for a lower-sugar diet)
cac_buoc: Wash the strawberries and remove the leafy hulls
Chop the strawberries and place them in a suitable bowl
Pour the white sugar into the bowl and mix well with the strawberries
Cover the bowl with plastic wrap and let it sit for 1 hour
Pour the strawberry and sugar mixture into a non-stick pot and bring to a boil over high heat
Once boiling, lower the heat and stir continuously until the jam thickens, then turn off the heat
Wait for the strawberry jam to cool, then transfer it into a prepared airtight jar

mon_an.mo_ta: Scallion oil is a homemade aromatic oil that enhances fragrance and freshness, featuring a bold scallion scent and the complex umami of dried shrimp. It is perfect for mixing into fillings, salads, or drizzling over hot dishes. It primarily provides energy from fats, while the scallions, ginger, and other aromatics contain plant compounds that help remove fishy odors and stimulate the appetite. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, usually taking about 30 minutes for both preparation and simmering.
cac_buoc: Soak the dried shrimp in 50-degree warm water with 10 ml of cooking wine to remove any fishy smell; soak for 10 minutes then drain
Wash the scallions and cilantro, cut into 5 cm lengths, and pat the surface dry
Thinly slice the onion, blanch in a pot of hot water for 5 minutes, then drain
Peel and slice the ginger
Pour all the oil into a pot, add all the prepared ingredients above, and fry over medium-low heat for 20 minutes

mon_an.mo_ta: Garlic soy sauce is a household dipping sauce with a strong garlic aroma, savory, fragrant, and rich. It is often used to enhance the flavor of poached chicken, dumplings, and more. Garlic and sesame provide antibacterial benefits and supplement unsaturated fatty acids, respectively. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly, with the entire process taking only about 5 minutes.
cac_buoc: Crush the garlic.
Pour the soy sauce into the dipping dish.
Heat a pan, add the peanut oil, and once the oil is very hot, add the crushed garlic and fry for half a minute.
After half a minute, turn off the heat, pour the hot oil into the dipping dish, stir with chopsticks, and it's done.

mon_an.mo_ta: A homemade beverage syrup made by mixing white granulated sugar with water at a 1:1 ratio until completely dissolved. It is convenient for controlling the sweetness of cold drinks and serves as a base recipe for various beverages. Rich in carbohydrates, it helps replenish energy quickly. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly, taking only a few minutes, and it can be stored in the refrigerator for one week.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Suggested ratio => sugar: water = 1 : 1, for easy sugar control; for example, if you want to use 15 g of sugar, measure 30 g of syrup
Jar with a tight lid (high borosilicate glass bottles are recommended as they are affordable)
cac_buoc: Add the weighed white granulated sugar and drinking water into the jar and mix well.
Close the lid and place it in the refrigerator.

mon_an.mo_ta: Sugar-crusted fried taro is a traditional Chaozhou snack that is crispy on the outside and chewy on the inside, sweet, fragrant, and delicious. It is often served as an afternoon tea treat. Lipu taro is rich in fiber, potassium, and various vitamins, providing a long-lasting feeling of fullness. It is not difficult to make but requires mastering the heat when cooking the sugar, making it suitable for beginners with some basic skills. The entire process takes about 20 minutes.
cac_buoc: Cut the taro into long strips (cut them slightly thick so they don't break easily when stir-frying).
Pour enough oil to submerge the taro, wait for the oil to get hot (it's ready when small bubbles form around a chopstick inserted into the oil).
Add the taro to the oil and fry until the pieces float; they should be slightly golden and easily pierced with a chopstick.
Set aside the frying oil for later use; it can be used for any future stir-frying or cooking.
The next key step: add sugar (30 g) and water (15 g) at a 2 : 1 ratio, and simmer until small bubbles form without changing color.
Add the chopped green onions and fried taro, turn off the heat and toss well; as the temperature drops, the sugar will crystallize.
Serve on a plate and enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: This dessert combines the rich flavor of coffee with the light sweetness of coconut milk, featuring a smooth, pudding-like texture with multiple layers of flavor. Whipping cream and coconut milk provide quality fats and plant-based nutrition, offering a satisfying treat. The method is very friendly, requiring only mixing and heating without complex techniques, ensuring success even for beginners. Excluding refrigeration time, the actual preparation takes about 1 hour, with a total of about 4 hours including setting time.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 250 ml Coconut Palm brand coconut milk (Yēshù)
35 ml espresso (fruity coffee beans are personally not recommended)
50 ml coconut water (Vita Coco is suggested, or use fresh coconut water if available)
(For garnish, you can add some blueberries and/or coffee powder)
cac_buoc: Mix the measured whipping cream, Coconut Palm coconut milk, espresso, and coconut water; set aside.
Heat the liquid mixture for 1 minute until the temperature reaches 50-60 degrees.
(Optional) If you prefer it sweeter, add sugar.
Add the gelatin, stir until dissolved, and cook for 1 minute.
(Optional) Pass the mixture through a strainer (this step makes the coconut milk jelly smoother).
Pour into molds.
(Optional) Skim off any bubbles on the surface. This step makes the jelly taste better and look more appealing.
Place in the refrigerator and wait for 3 hours to set.

mon_an.mo_ta: Oreo ice cream has a smooth texture, with a milky aroma blended with the sweet crunch of Oreos. Using pure animal-based whipping cream makes the overall taste light and not greasy. It primarily provides energy, containing fats and carbohydrates, making it a perfect small dessert to cool down. The process is quite simple, involving processing the cookie filling and whipping the cream; beginners just need a little patience. Preparation takes about half an hour, followed by freezing for over 4 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A container with a capacity over 600 ml, small diameter (must fit the electric mixer), and deep (if using ice cream molds, a container with a spout is better for pouring)
Small knife (or a tool to remove the cream filling)
cac_buoc: Twist the Oreos open and remove the cream filling; set aside.
Crush the Oreo cookies; half should be a fine powder and the other half should be small chunks no larger than 0.5 cm; set aside (you can buy "Oreo crumbs" online to save time and effort ^-^).
Pour all the cream into the deep container and add the prepared sugar.
Start the electric mixer at high speed and whip until the cream holds its shape on the beaters (0.5 cm - 1 cm) rather than dripping off like a liquid (partial dripping is normal).
Once whipped, add the Oreo crumbs to the cream and stir well until the Oreos reach the bottom.
Optional: pour the mixture into ice cream molds.
Place in the freezer (-18 degrees) for over 4 hours before serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: This introductory baking dessert has a smooth, soft flavor and a texture as light as a cloud, making it a classic staple in Western baking. The main ingredients, eggs and milk, provide quality protein and calcium for rich nutrition. The process has high requirements for whipping, mixing, and baking temperature, which can be challenging, but beginners can succeed by patiently following the steps. It usually takes 1.5 to 2 hours from preparation to coming out of the oven.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Oven (a rice cooker can be a substitute, but often fails due to the inner pot material)
Hand mixer (electric is best; manual whisking is exhausting and has a higher failure rate) or chopsticks (highly discouraged)
Anodized aluminum mold (never use a non-stick mold; common sizes are 6-inch or 8-inch)
The standard measurement for each serving is 1 egg (normal medium size, about 50 g).
Ingredients | 1 serving (standard) | 6-inch mold (3 servings) | 8-inch mold (5 servings)
cac_buoc: Take fresh eggs out of the refrigerator.
Prepare two bowls and wipe them dry to hold the egg whites and egg yolks separately.
The bowl for egg whites can have a little water but must be completely free of any oil; the bowl for egg yolks must not have any water droplets.
Crack the eggs, using your hands or an egg separator, to separate the whites and yolks into the two bowls.
During separation, the yolk must not break, and the whites must not contain any yolk, otherwise it will seriously affect the whipping process. (The chalaza can go into the whites without issue).
(Note: when not using a stand mixer, the bowl for whites is also the whipping bowl; to avoid overflow, the whites should not exceed 1/8 of the container's volume).
Prepare a new empty bowl and add all the cooking oil and milk from the recipe.
Use a whisk to mix quickly by hand until the oil and water are completely combined into a milky white suspension (emulsification complete).

Sift all the cake flour from the recipe into the emulsified mixture. Use a spatula to mix in a "Z-motion" until no dry flour is visible (the batter may look slightly coarse at this stage, which is normal).
Add all the separated egg yolks into the bowl and continue using the spatula to mix in a "Z-motion".
The batter will now become very smooth and won't easily develop gluten. Set aside.
Prepare the remaining 3/4 of the white sugar. Divide it into three equal parts.
Add lemon juice or white vinegar to the egg whites (optional).
Use the mixer at medium speed to whip the whites until *coarse bubbles* form, then add the first portion of sugar.
Use the mixer at high speed to whip the whites until *fine bubbles* form, then add the second portion of sugar.
Use the mixer at high speed to whip the whites to "soft peaks", then add the third portion of sugar.
Visual cue: lift the mixer head; the egg cream should pull into a long, curved peak (often called a "large hook"). This state is suitable for cake rolls.
Use the mixer at low-medium speed to whip the whites to "stiff peaks".

Visual cue: lift the mixer head; the egg cream should form small, short, straight, and firm peaks (often called "small straight peaks"); if you turn the bowl upside down, the egg cream should stick firmly to the bottom and not slide at all. This is the standard state needed for chiffon cake.
The egg whites have now reached the required level of whipping.
(You can refer to the attached link images to judge the state of the egg whites.)
The mixer should be kept close to the bottom of the bowl to avoid the top being whipped while the bottom remains liquid.
Briefly stir the egg yolk mixture a few times.
Use a spatula to take 1/3 of the whipped egg whites and add them to the yolk mixture.
Use a "folding" technique to avoid deflating the bubbles.
The folding technique is:
First, hold the spatula in your right hand and insert it from the center of the bowl to the bottom of the batter.
Sweep toward the 8 o'clock position until you touch the side of the bowl, then scoop the batter up into the air, move toward the center, and drop it back in.
Use your left hand to rotate the bowl from 9 o'clock to 7 o'clock (exactly 60 degrees) to complete one cycle.
The speed should be about twice per second.
This method comes from the book "Mr. Kojima's Cake Classes." Simply put, fold it like you are stir-frying vegetables.
Pour the mixture of 1/3 egg whites and yolk batter into the remaining 2/3 egg whites, and continue to fold until uniform.
Pour the cake batter into the mold and tap it a few times to remove large air bubbles.

Total baking time: 30-35 minutes for a 6-inch cake, 50 minutes for an 8-inch cake. Adjust flexibly according to your oven's characteristics, usually not exceeding ± 5 minutes. (You can watch the oven during the last few minutes).
Preheat and bake with top heat at 150 °C and bottom heat at 160 °C; it takes about 10 minutes to reach the set temperature.
After preheating, place the mold on the lower rack of the oven.
Choose a variable temperature baking mode, divided into two stages.
Stage one oven settings: top heat 150 °C, bottom heat 160 °C;
The first 3/5 of the total baking time is the first baking stage.
Stage two settings: top heat 160 °C, bottom heat 170 °C;
The remaining 2/5 of the total baking time is the second baking stage. Simply adjust the oven temperature to switch.
Once baked, remove from the oven.
This can be hot, so be sure to use a towel or oven mitts.

Air fryers have very strong hot air circulation and are very close to the heating element; using oven temperatures directly will burn the top while leaving the inside raw. Strictly follow these cooling and covering steps:
Preheating: set the air fryer to 130 °C and preheat for 5 minutes.

Insert and cover: place the mold with the batter into the air fryer. Immediately cover the mold with a layer of aluminum foil (shiny side up, matte side touching the food), pinching the edges tightly to prevent the hot wind from blowing it away.
First baking stage: set to 130 °C and bake for 35 minutes.
Second browning stage: open the air fryer and remove the foil. Increase the temperature to 150 °C and continue baking for 10–15 minutes.
Doneness check: the top of the cake should be puffed up and golden brown. Insert a toothpick into the center; if it comes out clean without wet batter, it is fully baked.
The steps for releasing steam and inverting the mold after removal are exactly the same as the oven version.
(Optional) Drop the mold from a height to release the internal hot steam.
Invert the mold for 10 minutes to let the cake cool.
Do not unmold the cake before it has cooled, as it will ruin the structure.
Unmold and enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: This traditional Italian dessert requires no oven. It features a smooth, light cheese mixture and coffee-soaked ladyfingers, making it a perfect introductory dessert. It is rich in protein and calcium, but since the sugar and calorie content are quite high, it should be enjoyed occasionally. The operation is simple and very friendly for baking beginners, requiring only about half an hour of active work, followed by four hours of refrigeration to set.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A container for the finished product (a Lock&Lock glass box is used here)
Hand mixer (those with strong arms can also whisk by hand)
cac_buoc: Separate the egg yolks and egg whites.
Add 10 g of white granulated sugar to the bowl of egg whites and whip to soft peaks.
Add 40 g of white granulated sugar to the egg yolks in three additions, stirring well each time.
Add the mascarpone cheese to the egg yolks in three additions, stirring well.
Finally, add the rum to the egg yolk mixture and stir well.
Fold the whipped egg whites into the egg yolk and cheese mixture in three additions.
Dip both sides of the ladyfingers into the coffee and layer them flat in the container.
Alternate two layers of the cheese mixture and two layers of ladyfingers in the container (adjust this based on your preference and the height of the container).
Place in the refrigerator to chill for four hours (if you are impatient, you can take it out earlier).
Take it out, sift cocoa powder over the surface, and it's ready to enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a homemade honey bread that requires no mixer. It is fluffy, sweet, and fragrant with a slightly crispy bottom. The surface is brushed with honey water and sprinkled with sesame seeds, exuding a rustic sweet aroma. The main ingredients are bread flour, milk, eggs, and butter, providing ample carbohydrates, protein, and calcium, making it a reliable choice for breakfast or a snack. The method is simple, entirely hand-mixed, with flexible proofing times—you can even leave it in the fridge overnight and bake it the next day, making it very beginner-friendly. The process takes about 3 hours, mostly waiting for the dough to rise, with very little actual labor.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The ingredient quantities below are for one rectangular baking tray (10 x 15 inches) + one square baking tray (9 x 9 inches) + parchment paper. It is recommended to reduce the amount as needed; for breakfast, this amount lasts about two weeks (stored in the fridge). Refrigerated bread will harden; microwave for 10-20 seconds to soften.
cac_buoc: Make the dough: mix the flour, milk (recommended to warm to 40°, I use the microwave for 15-20 seconds), yeast, egg, sugar, and salt together.
Stir the dough to combine the ingredients into a mass.
Add the butter and mix.
Continue stirring + hand-kneading until well combined.
Begin proofing: cover the container with plastic wrap and leave at room temperature (10-20°) for 1-2 hours; a slightly longer time won't have a major impact.
Once the dough has clearly fermented and doubled in size, you can start dividing it; at this point, the dough is no longer too sticky.
Divide the dough: ideally 60 g per portion (for aesthetics), or adjust the size to your preference.
Roll each small dough ball into a tongue shape with a rolling pin, then roll it up and let it rest for another 10 minutes.
Roll into a tongue shape again, roll it up, and cut in half from the middle (one becomes two).

Roll into a tongue shape again, roll it up, and cut in half from the middle (two become four). (You can repeat the rolling/folding a few more times depending on your time, just keep the portion size consistent).
Line the baking tray with parchment paper and pour in some peanut oil; dip the bottom of each rolled portion in water then flour and place in the tray.
Proof again (covered with plastic wrap); this step can be done in the refrigerator to bake the next day.
Brush with egg wash.
Bake in the oven at 180° (355°F) for 18-20 minutes.
Remove from the oven, brush with honey water, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

mon_an.mo_ta: Fried milk is a dessert with a crispy shell and a soft, tender interior. Making it is not difficult, but the milk mixture must be heated sufficiently and chilled to set, otherwise it will easily melt when cutting and frying. The actual operation takes about 30 minutes, with at least 2 hours required for refrigeration.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 40 g cake flour or all-purpose flour
A square heatproof container, about 20 cm x 15 cm
The quantities below make about 12 pieces of fried milk, suitable for 3-4 people.
700 ml cooking oil, actual consumption will be less than this
cac_buoc: Take 80 ml of the milk, mix it with the cornstarch, and stir until no lumps remain.
Pour the remaining 170 ml of milk and the white sugar into a pot, heat over low heat and stir constantly until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Stir the cornstarch mixture again, slowly pour it into the pot while stirring constantly.
Keep the heat low and stir continuously for about 3-5 minutes until the milk mixture thickens and a trail drawn across the bottom of the pot holds for 3 seconds.
Brush about 2 ml of oil onto the inner walls of the heatproof container, pour in the milk mixture and smooth the surface to a thickness of about 2 cm.
Once the milk mixture cools to room temperature, cover it tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 hours; it is ready when the surface is not sticky to the touch and the mass does not flow.
Remove the set milk block from the mold and cut into strips about 6 cm x 2 cm x 2 cm, totaling about 12 strips.
Place the flour, beaten egg, and breadcrumbs into 3 separate containers.
Coat each milk strip evenly in flour, then the beaten egg, and finally the breadcrumbs, ensuring all sides are fully covered.
Pour 700 ml of oil into a pot and heat over medium heat to 165-175 ℃; if you don't have a thermometer, test with a few breadcrumbs—they should float within 2 seconds and bubble continuously.
Fry the milk strips in 2-3 batches, frying each batch for 60-90 seconds; flip them 1-2 times during the process for even cooking.
When the surface is evenly golden brown, remove the strips and place them on kitchen paper towels to drain for about 2 minutes before eating.

mon_an.mo_ta: Basque cheesecake is a rich and smooth dessert with a fragrant burnt surface and a moist, soft interior, a classic flavor from the Basque region of Spain. The main ingredients are cream cheese and eggs, providing quality protein and calcium. The process is very simple and easy for beginners to master. It takes only about 30 minutes from preparation to coming out of the oven, but it is recommended to refrigerate overnight before eating, for a total time of about 8 hours or more.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cream cheese: 212 g (this is the weight of one block, which is convenient; the original recipe calls for 250 g)
Chocolate: 38 g (only tried melting regular chocolate; add it during the whipping cream step and stir well)
The ingredient quantities below are for a 7-inch round mold; the original recipe uses a 6-inch round mold.
cac_buoc: Soften the cream cheese in the microwave for 10 seconds + 10 seconds.
Add the white granulated sugar to the cream cheese and use a mixer to beat until smooth.
Add the 2 whole eggs + 1 egg yolk and stir well.
Add the whipping cream and stir well.
Add the cake flour and stir well.
Bake in the oven at 220° (425°F) for 20-25 minutes (I usually bake for 20 or 22 minutes).
Let it cool, then place in the refrigerator, preferably overnight.

mon_an.mo_ta: Baked egg tarts are a classic Chinese dessert with a crispy crust and a smooth, milky filling. Rich in protein, calcium, and vitamins, they provide a great energy boost. The process is very simple and beginner-friendly; furthermore, the semi-finished tarts can be frozen for later use. From preparation to oven takes about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: This recipe makes enough for one full pack of tart shells; prepared tarts can be frozen directly
Tart shells, any brand, about 30 pieces per pack
200 ml milk, regular bagged milk is fine
450 ml heavy cream, available at bakeries or supermarkets
80 g white granulated sugar, regular is fine, fine sugar is better for dissolving
Whisking tool, including but not limited to chopsticks or a whisk
cac_buoc: Place a bowl on the electronic scale and weigh 450 g of heavy cream (assuming a density of 1)
Add 80 g white granulated sugar (medium sweetness, adjust to taste, recommended range 60-100 g)
Add 200 g milk (assuming a density of 1)
Add 8 egg yolks; set aside the whites for other uses
Whisk all ingredients until the sugar is completely dissolved
Strain the mixture through a sieve to remove egg membranes, shells, undissolved sugar, and cream lumps
Preheat the oven to 220°C (about 10 minutes); remember to remove the baking tray
Arrange the tart shells evenly on the baking tray, spaced 0.5 cm apart
Pour the strained mixture into the shells until 0.5 cm from the rim; do not overfill
At this stage, the prepared tarts are ready; they can be flash-frozen for over 12 hours for storage
Place the tarts in the oven and bake at 200°C for 25 minutes
Once baked, they are ready to serve

mon_an.mo_ta: Margaret cookies are crumbly and crisp with a rich buttery aroma, a classic Western bite-sized dessert. Primarily made from egg yolks, butter, and flour, they are high in carbohydrates and fats for a quick energy boost. Moderate difficulty, taking about 45 minutes from preparation to oven, making them easy for beginners.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: As this dessert is high in calories, determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for one person.
cac_buoc: Melt the butter over a water bath; mash the egg yolk and set aside
Add sugar, salt, and the mashed egg yolk to the melted butter and whisk well
Add the low-gluten flour and cornstarch, then knead into a dough
Divide the dough into small pieces of about 8 g each, then roll into balls
Use your thumb to gently press down on each ball to create cracks
Preheat the oven to 150°C, place the dough balls inside, and bake for 20 minutes
Allow to cool slightly before serving

mon_an.mo_ta: Red grapefruit cake is a refreshing dessert easily made in an air fryer, combining the tart citrus notes of red grapefruit pulp with a soft cake texture, perfect for a single-serving afternoon tea. Eggs and flour provide protein and starch, while red grapefruit is rich in vitamin C. Medium difficulty; the key is whisking the batter multiple times until it is a smooth, pale yellow mixture without lumps. Beginners just need patience to follow the steps. From preparation to serving takes about 35 minutes, perfect for a quick freshly baked treat.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One portion is a meal for one person; for more people, increase proportionally. This example uses an 18 cm diameter foil tray; if using a larger tray, please increase ingredients proportionally.
cac_buoc: Crack 2 eggs into the foil tray and add 20 g red grapefruit pulp
Pour 15 ml oil into the foil tray and shake to coat the bottom evenly
Add 10 g sugar, 40 g flour, and 40 ml water to the tray
Stir clockwise with chopsticks until it forms a smooth, pale yellow batter
Add the remaining 5 g sugar, 40 g flour, and 40 ml water to the tray
Continue stirring with chopsticks until it forms a smooth, pale yellow batter
Place the foil tray in the air fryer basket and bake at 180°C for 15 minutes
Open the air fryer, carefully remove the tray, and flip the cake using chopsticks or a spoon
Continue baking at 180°C for 8 minutes
Remove and serve

mon_an.mo_ta: Gajar Halwa is a well-known Indian winter dessert where grated carrots are slow-simmered with milk until thickened, then blended with ghee and nuts for a smooth, sweet, and fragrant finish with a golden-red color. Rich in carotene, calcium, and healthy fats, it is warming and nutritious. The process is simple but requires some patience; the whole process takes about 45 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 3-4 people.
80 g sugar (adjust between 60 g-100 g to taste)
cac_buoc: Peel the carrots and use a grater to shred them finely
Add 20 g ghee (half the amount) to a heavy-bottomed pot and melt over medium heat
Add the grated carrots and sauté for 3-5 minutes until *the carrots soften and become fragrant*
Pour in 500 ml whole milk and stir well
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low to maintain a *slow simmer*
Stir continuously for 25-30 minutes until *the milk is almost completely absorbed by the carrots and evaporated* (this is the key step; be patient and stir constantly to avoid burning the bottom)
When almost no liquid remains in the pot, add 80 g sugar and stir well
The mixture will release liquid again after adding sugar; continue to sauté over medium-low heat for 5-8 minutes until *the liquid evaporates again*
Add the remaining 20 g ghee and 3 g cardamom powder, then sauté for 2 minutes
In a separate small pan, use a little ghee to fry the cashews, sliced almonds, and raisins separately until *golden brown* (about 1 minute); note that raisins will puff up
Mix half of the fried nuts and raisins into the carrot pudding
Serve on a plate and sprinkle the remaining nuts and raisins on top for garnish

mon_an.mo_ta: Taro Cream Mochi features a soft, elastic outer skin with a smooth, sweet taro mash and light cream filling. This multi-layered dessert is a creative homemade Chinese treat. Taro and purple sweet potato provide fiber and anthocyanins, while milk and cream add calcium for balanced nutrition. No oven is required, and the simple steps are very beginner-friendly. The entire process takes about two hours to create a homemade snack that children will love.
cac_buoc: Cut the taro into pieces and boil over high heat until soft (about 40 minutes), then place in the blender
Add 30 g milk and 25 g heavy cream, then blend into a puree
Add 3 g purple sweet potato powder and 18 g white granulated sugar, then continue blending into a smooth taro mash

In another bowl, combine glutinous rice flour B, 22 g cornstarch, 135 g milk, and 50 g white granulated sugar; mix well and strain once, cover with plastic wrap, poke small holes, and steam over medium heat for half an hour
While steaming, add glutinous rice flour A to a pan and stir-fry over low heat until slightly yellow (toasted) to use as dusting flour
While the steamed milk-flour mixture (jelly-like) is still hot, add 30 g butter and knead until fully absorbed, then refrigerate for one hour
In another bowl, combine 120 g heavy cream and 8 g white granulated sugar; whip until stiff peaks form and transfer to a piping bag

Take the chilled dough out, knead for 5 minutes, and divide into 30 g pieces; dust with 2 g of the toasted flour, roll into circles, pipe 5 g of cream, place 30 g of taro mash on top, and wrap like a bun (trim excess dough if needed)
Once wrapped, dust evenly with another 2 g of toasted flour
Repeat the above two steps until all ingredients are used

mon_an.mo_ta: English scones are a classic afternoon tea treat, crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with a rich milky egg aroma. They are best served with jam or cream. Primarily made from flour, butter, eggs, and heavy cream, they are rich in carbohydrates and protein for a quick energy boost. The process is quite simple; as long as you master basic kneading techniques, even beginners can handle it. Takes about one hour from preparation to oven.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 4-6 people.
cac_buoc: Whisk the egg; weigh 30 g of the beaten egg into a clean bowl, then add all the heavy cream and cream cheese and mix well. If the cheese is too hard, warm it over a water bath to about 40°C before mixing.
In a clean bowl, mix the low-gluten flour, salt, sugar, and baking powder until combined
Cut the butter into small pieces, add to the mixture above, and rub in with your fingers until it reaches a coarse cornmeal texture
Pour the egg-milk mixture from step one into the butter-flour mixture and stir until just combined. Fold and press into a uniform dough.
Place the dough on a cutting board, roll it out to a thickness of 1.5 cm, and use a knife or cutter to cut into desired shapes
Use a brush to coat the surface of the scones with the remaining 20 g of beaten egg
Preheat the oven to 180°C and bake for 27 minutes

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a homemade strawberry ice cream that is easy to make without a blender, featuring a rich fruit aroma and smooth texture. Strawberries are rich in vitamin C, and combined with condensed milk and cream, they provide energy and calcium. The method is simple and doesn't require advanced skills, so beginners can succeed on their first try. The whole process takes about eight hours, but most of that is freezing time; the actual hands-on work is only a few dozen minutes.
cac_buoc: Make the strawberry syrup first. Wash the strawberries and remove the stems. Cut the strawberries into 5 mm pieces. Set aside half of the chopped strawberries to fold into the ice cream later.
Place the other half of the chopped strawberries and the sugar in a saucepan. Stir and cook over medium heat until the strawberries release their juices and form a syrup.
Let the strawberries simmer in the syrup, stirring occasionally, until they break down and the syrup thickens slightly.
When the syrup holds a trail for 3 seconds, it is ready. Remove from heat and stir in the vanilla and salt. Set the strawberry syrup aside to cool.

While the syrup cools, prepare the ice cream base. Combine the condensed milk, heavy cream, vanilla extract, and salt in a bowl. Use a hand mixer to beat the mixture until light, fluffy, and soft peaks form.

Fold the reserved fresh chopped strawberries into the ice cream base. Transfer the whipped base into a freezer-safe container. Drizzle the cooled strawberry syrup over the cream and gently swirl it in.
Cover the ice cream and freeze for eight hours before scooping and serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: An improved version of the classic Italian dessert, adding unsweetened yogurt for a more refreshing and smooth taste that is sweet without being cloying. It is perfect as a light post-meal snack served with fruit or jam. Dairy products provide plenty of calcium and protein for gentle nutrition. The steps are simple, involving only heating, stirring, and chilling; beginners can easily succeed. Takes about 5 hours from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 3-6 people.
cac_buoc: Cut the gelatin leaves into small pieces and soak in cold water
Combine heavy cream and sugar in a pot and heat to 60°C
Turn off the heat, remove the gelatin from the water, squeeze out excess moisture, add to the hot cream, and stir well
When the cream temperature drops to 40°C, add the unsweetened yogurt and stir well
Strain the resulting mixture through a sieve twice
Divide into suitable containers and refrigerate for at least 4 hours

mon_an.mo_ta: Snowflake crisps are a crunchy, chewy, and milky bite-sized dessert. They belong to the category of quick and easy home-baked treats and are perfect for gifting in boxes. Containing butter, milk powder, and mixed nuts, they provide high energy and protein, but are also high in calories, making them a great occasional treat. Moderate difficulty with a slight challenge for beginners, but if you watch the heat and stirring technique, they usually take only 30 minutes.
cac_buoc: Break any biscuits larger than a coin into smaller pieces first
Add unsalted butter to a pot and melt over low heat until completely liquid
Add marshmallows to the pot and stir with a spatula until melted and well combined with the butter
Add 20 g of milk powder to the pot and stir with a spatula; once the milk powder is incorporated into the marshmallow-butter mixture, turn off the heat immediately
Add all the prepared mixed nuts and biscuits to the pot while hot and stir with a spatula

Stir until the temperature is cool enough to touch, then wear disposable plastic gloves and knead in the pot or stretch by hand to evenly distribute the biscuits and nuts throughout the marshmallow mixture.
Press the mixture into a mold, compacting the corners, and flatten with a rolling pin; use your hands to press any empty spots into straight edges
Allow to cool completely at room temperature before unmolding; cut into pieces according to the mold lines or your preferred size, then dust with the remaining milk powder so every side is coated

mon_an.mo_ta: Konjac cake is a low-calorie, gluten-free dessert using erythritol instead of granulated sugar. It has a light, moist texture with a cocoa aroma, making it especially suitable for those on a fat-loss diet. Rich in fiber and protein, it provides a strong sense of fullness. It has some difficulty as it requires whipping egg whites and careful folding techniques, but the total time is only about half an hour, making it a healthy and quick baking option.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Butter knife (for folding and smoothing the batter)
cac_buoc: Before preparing the batter, you can start preheating the oven to 350°F (150°C) to save time
Take fresh eggs out of the refrigerator
Prepare two clean, dry bowls for the whites and yolks
The bowl for the whites can be slightly damp but must be completely free of oil; the bowl for the yolks must be free of water droplets
Crack the eggs and separate the whites and yolks into the two bowls by hand or using a separator
During separation, the yolks must not break, and the whites must not contain any yolk, otherwise it will seriously affect whipping (the chalaza can go into the whites without issue)
(Note: when not using a stand mixer, the bowl for the whites is also the whipping bowl; to avoid overflow, the whites should not exceed 1/8 of the bowl's volume)
Add 1 g cream of tartar to the egg whites
Using the mixer at high speed, beat the whites until *large, coarse bubbles* form, then add 50 g erythritol
Switch to medium-low speed and beat the whites to *stiff peaks* (when the beaters are lifted, a small, short, straight peak forms; when the bowl is inverted, the whites stay attached and do not fall)
At this point, the egg whites have reached the required level of aeration
The mixer should be kept close to the bottom of the bowl to prevent the top from being fluffy while the bottom remains liquid
Add the separated yolks to the whipped whites and mix with the mixer on medium-low speed until combined
Add 10 g cocoa powder and 10 g konjac powder to the mixture; first use a butter knife to fold them in, as using the mixer directly will cause the powder to splatter
The folding technique is as follows:
First, hold the spatula in your right hand and cut through the center of the batter to the bottom of the bowl
Sweep toward the 8 o'clock position until you hit the side of the bowl, then scoop the batter up into the air, move back to the center, and drop it back in
Use your left hand to rotate the bowl from 9 o'clock to 7 o'clock (exactly 60 degrees) to complete one cycle
The speed should be about 2 cycles per second
This method is derived from the book "Master Kojima's Cake Classes." Simply put, fold it like you are stir-frying vegetables.
After folding, use the mixer on low speed to ensure everything is evenly combined
Line the mold with parchment paper, ensuring it fits tightly against the bottom and sides
Pour the batter into the mold, smooth it with a butter knife, and tap it a few times to remove large air bubbles
Bake for 25 minutes
Once baked, remove from the oven using heat-resistant gloves
(Optional) Drop the mold from a height to release the internal hot air
Invert the mold for 10 minutes to let the cake cool
Do not unmold the cake before it has cooled, as this will damage it
This process can be hot; be sure to wear heat-resistant gloves
Unmold and use a butter knife to slice and enjoy

mon_an.mo_ta: Guilinggao is a traditional Cantonese dessert with a smooth, slightly bitter taste and a sweet aftertaste, often served as a cooling summer snack. It has heat-clearing, dampness-removing, and skin-nourishing properties, making it a healthy nutritional treat. The recipe is simple and beginner-friendly; the process involves preparation, stirring, and heating, followed by about two hours of chilling before it's ready to enjoy.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Each batch makes about 3-4 small bowls, suitable for 2-4 people.
cac_buoc: Add 25 g of Guilinggao powder and 120 ml of cold water to a pot, whisking thoroughly until completely smooth with no lumps.
In a separate container, add 100 g of white granulated sugar and pour in 500 ml of boiling water, stirring until the sugar is fully dissolved.
Slowly pour the sugar water into the Guilinggao mixture, stirring immediately to prevent clumping.
Place the mixture on the stove over medium-low heat, stirring constantly to prevent it from sticking to the bottom.
Cook until the liquid thickens and small bubbles begin to appear, then turn off the heat.
Quickly pour the liquid into molds and let it cool naturally to set. It is recommended to refrigerate for 1-2 hours before serving for a better flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: This cocktail features distinct layers of flavor: the initial kick of vodka, followed by the sweet aftertaste of coffee cream. Lighting it on fire before drinking provides a unique "fire and ice" experience, making it a classic creative cocktail. The coffee liqueur and Baileys provide a bit of caffeine and dairy fat, though the overall nutrition is primarily alcohol. It requires practice with layering and lighting techniques, which may be slightly difficult for beginners. The process takes about 5 minutes.
cac_buoc: Pour the Kahlúa coffee liqueur into the bottom of the liqueur glass until it is 1/3 full (10 ml).
Slowly pour the Baileys over the back of a bar spoon to fill the next 1/3 of the glass (10 ml). Pour very slowly to keep the layers distinct (pouring too fast will mix the cream with the coffee).
Finally, pour the Skyy Original Vodka onto the top layer (10 ml).
Use a lighter to warm the rim of the glass.
The final step is to ignite it: can you see the small, pale blue flame?

mon_an.mo_ta: This cocktail is refreshing, sweet, and sour, featuring the coolness of mint and the light buzz of rum, making it a classic summer drink. It has a relatively low alcohol content and contains lime rich in Vitamin C, helping to quench thirst and refresh the mind. It is very simple to make and beginner-friendly, taking only about ten minutes from preparation to completion.
cac_buoc: Cut half of the lime into small wedges, place them in the highball glass, and use a muddler to extract the juice.
Rub 3-4 mint sprigs around the rim of the glass, then drop them into the glass.
Add 20 ml of syrup.
Add 45 ml of gold rum.
Squeeze the juice from the remaining half of the lime into the glass.
Stir gently until the sugar/syrup is partially dissolved.
Fill the glass 3/4 full with crushed ice.
Top with chilled soda water until the ice is just covered.
Stir for half a minute.
Fill the rest of the highball glass with more crushed ice.
Lightly clap the remaining mint sprig to release its aroma and tuck it into the ice for garnish.

mon_an.mo_ta: Winter melon tea is a traditional cooling drink with a mild, gentle sweetness and the characteristic light aroma of winter melon; it tastes even better when chilled. Winter melon itself is low in calories and high in water content, and when cooked with rock sugar, it provides energy and quenches thirst. The process is not complicated but requires patience, taking about 4 to 5 hours in total.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you want to make. One batch is enough for 4-5 people.
cac_buoc: Prepare the winter melon: peel, remove seeds, and cut into small pieces (no larger than 4 cm each).
Add rock sugar: mix the rock sugar with the winter melon, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate for at least 2 hours.

Cook the winter melon: by now, the melon will have released a lot of liquid. Pour everything into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium-low and simmer for 1-2 hours, stirring frequently to prevent burning.
Strain the tea: use a fine-mesh strainer to filter the cooked winter melon tea. Remove the solids and keep only the liquid.
Cooling: let the tea cool, then pour it into a clean container and store it in the refrigerator.
Enjoy: the finished tea is a concentrate. Depending on your preference, dilute it with water or other beverages; it can be enjoyed hot or cold.

mon_an.mo_ta: Bingfen is a traditional snack from Xinyang, Henan, with a smooth, jelly-like texture. It is often paired with mint or hawthorn water for a cooling effect. Made by hand from bingfen seeds, it is completely natural with no additives and is rich in plant pectin. It is very simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 3 hours in total, of which 2.5 hours is passive setting time.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you want to make. One batch is enough for 5 people.
A piece of cheesecloth (soy milk filter cloth)
10 ml mint water / 10 g mint powder
cac_buoc: Pour the cooled boiled water into a basin.
Wrap all the bingfen seeds in the cheesecloth and tie a knot at the top.
Submerge the seed pouch in the water and rub it vigorously for 6 minutes.
Let the liquid sit undisturbed for 2.5 hours until it sets.

Use a spoon to scoop the jelly into the prepared disposable plastic cups. Add 10 ml of mint water or 10 g of mint powder (lime juice, hawthorn juice, or mulberry juice also work), then add the glowing ice cubes and stir gently with a spoon.

mon_an.mo_ta: Masala Chai is a home-style beverage with an exotic flair, brewed fresh from black tea, milk, and various spices. It has a rich, smooth taste with the warm, spicy notes of ginger, cardamom, and cinnamon. Milk provides quality protein and calcium, while the spices help warm the body and aid digestion. The process is simple and straightforward, taking only about 10 minutes from prep to the first sip.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you want to make.
5 g fresh ginger (about a 1 cm piece), bruised
cac_buoc: Bruise the ginger (no need to mince it; just crushing it will release the juice).
Use the flat side of a knife to crush the cardamom pods to expose the seeds inside.
Crush the black peppercorns.
Pour 120 ml of water into the small milk pan.
Add the bruised ginger, cardamom, cinnamon stick, cloves, and black peppercorns.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and simmer for 2 minutes to fully extract the spice flavors.
Add 8 g of black tea and continue to simmer on low for 2 minutes until the *tea becomes dark in color*.
Pour in 120 ml of whole milk.
Increase to medium heat and watch closely. When the milk tea starts to *foam and rise*, immediately turn the heat to low (milk boils over very easily).
Simmer on low for 2-3 minutes. During this time, you can lift the pan and pour the tea back and forth (repeat 3-4 times) to fully blend the tea and milk.
Add sugar and stir until dissolved.
Turn off the heat.
Strain through a fine-mesh sieve into a teacup to remove the tea leaves and spices.
Serve hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: The Cola Bucket is an easy-to-mix party cocktail. It is refreshing and sweet, as the carbonation of the cola and the lime juice balance the strength of the whiskey. It is perfect for gatherings, providing energy while the lime adds Vitamin C. The entire mixing process takes only 5 minutes and is very easy for beginners.
cac_buoc: Prepare the lime.
Cut the lime in half crosswise, and cut one slice from one half to set aside for garnish.
Cut the remaining lime into quarters and use the juicer to extract the juice; set the juice aside in a separate container.
Keep the squeezed lime hulls aside.
Mixing the drink.
Choose a glass; a large glass with a capacity of about 1 liter or a tin ice bucket is recommended.
Place the ice and the squeezed lime hulls into the glass (arrange them according to your preference).
Pour in 15 ml of lime juice (add more or all of it if you prefer it more sour).
Slowly pour the Coca-Cola down the side of the glass until it is 3/4 full (aim for a cola-to-whiskey ratio of about 5:1).
Top off the glass with whiskey.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a unique, healthy, and refreshing fruit and vegetable drink. It has a smooth sweet and sour taste with the natural fruitiness of kiwi and apple, while the spinach flavor remains subtle. Rich in Vitamin C and fiber, it helps promote digestion. It is very simple to make, and beginners will succeed on their first try. The entire process takes about 10 minutes.
cac_buoc: Cut the kiwis in half, then cut each half into four small pieces.
Dice the apple.
Remove the stems from the spinach, keeping only the leaves.
Roughly chop the spinach.
Place all ingredients into the blender jar.
Pour in the water.
Add the white granulated sugar.
Start the blender and blend for about four 15-second intervals (stop every 15 seconds to check the consistency).

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an easy home-style beverage made from black tea and milk powder. The tea and milk flavors blend into a smooth, warm drink. The polyphenols in black tea combined with the protein and calcium in milk provide both a mental boost and daily nutrition. The method is very simple, and beginners will succeed on their first try. You can enjoy homemade milk tea in just half an hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A cup (e.g., a measuring cup, ceramic mug, or thermos)
cac_buoc: Place 2 black tea bags in a cup and add 180-200 ml of boiling water.
Let it steep for 20-30 minutes.
Weigh out 11-12 g of milk powder and 5-7 g of granulated sugar, then add them to the tea.
Stir well and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic Hong Kong-style dessert variation that uses chia seeds instead of sago pearls. It has a smooth texture with a slight chew from the seeds, combining the sweet aroma of mango with the light tartness of pomelo and the richness of coconut milk. It is rich in fiber, Vitamin C, and healthy fats. It is very simple to make and beginner-friendly, taking only about 20 minutes from prep to serving.
cac_buoc: Soak the chia seeds in the milk for 10 minutes.
While the seeds are soaking, peel and dice half of the mango and the pomelo, then place them in a cup.
Cut the remaining half of the mango into small pieces and place in a blender with the ice cubes and coconut milk; blend until smooth.
Pour the mixture into the cup and top with the garnishes (if using).
Enjoy while you write some code!!

mon_an.mo_ta: This drink features fresh lemons as the main star, balanced with fruit syrup for a perfect sweet and sour profile. It is especially refreshing when served chilled. Lemons are rich in vitamin C, and regular consumption helps supplement nutrition, boost alertness, and brighten the skin. The steps are incredibly simple—just muddle, add ingredients, and shake—allowing even beginners to finish it in three to five minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Portion for one glass, approximately 500 ml
cac_buoc: Weigh 40~45 g of lemon and place into the shaker.
Close the shaker lid and muddle/crush about 10 times.
Add 40~45 g of fruit syrup.
Add water.
Shake well.
Finally, add ice according to your preference.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic street-style Thai milk tea with a bold tea flavor and a smooth texture. Condensed milk and fresh milk provide a fragrant, sweet milky taste. The combination of tea and milk provides some protein and calcium, but the sugar content is quite high, making it suitable as a refreshing treat. The steps are simple, but it requires filtering the tea multiple times and a long chilling period. The total time is about 4 hours and 20 minutes; beginners just need a little patience to succeed.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Boil 600 cc of water over high heat.
Put 20 g of tea powder into the filter bag, pour the boiling water through the bag, and filter 20 times.
Use an electronic scale to measure 24 g of condensed milk, 24 g of white sugar, and 18 ml of milk into a pitcher with a capacity of over 1000 ml.
Pour the filtered tea into the pitcher and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Place the pitcher in the refrigerator for over 4 hours.
Before drinking, you can add 6-8 ice cubes.

mon_an.mo_ta: This cocktail features distinct color layers: red grenadine at the bottom like a sunset glow, clear orange juice in the middle, and blue curaçao on top like the ocean. The overall effect creates a seaside sunset scene. It tastes sweet, sour, and refreshing with a hint of rum. The orange and lemon juices provide some vitamin C, while the alcohol helps with relaxation. The preparation is not complex, but pouring the liquids over a bar spoon to create layers requires some patience. Beginners can succeed by following the steps; preparation and mixing take about 15 minutes.
cac_buoc: Prepare the lemon.
Wash the lemon and cut one slice.
Official preparation.
Choose a glass, preferably a clear glass with a capacity of 350~400 ml.
Add large ice cubes and use a bar spoon to stir and chill the glass.
Add the grenadine syrup.
Pour the orange juice over the bar spoon into the glass until it is about half full.
Stir gently for half a turn.
Pour in the soda water.
Take out the mixing glass, add white rum + blue curaçao + lemon juice + ice cubes. Shake well.
Pour gently into the glass.
Garnish with the lemon slice and a straw.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a creative drink combining "lassi," a traditional Indian yogurt drink, with a smooth, lightly sweet, and non-greasy taste. It is particularly suitable as a breakfast or an afternoon pick-me-up. Avocados are rich in monounsaturated fatty acids and fiber, which, combined with the high-quality protein and probiotics in yogurt, provides a long-lasting feeling of fullness. It is extremely simple to make, and beginners will not fail; it takes only about 5 minutes from preparation to enjoyment.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Mint leaves or crushed nuts (optional, for garnish)
cac_buoc: Halve the avocado, remove the pit, peel, and cut the flesh into small pieces; set aside.
Add 120 ml of unsweetened yogurt, the avocado pieces, 1 tbsp of honey, and 60 ml of cold milk into the blender.
(Optional) Add a pinch of cardamom powder to enhance the unique flavor.
Start the blender and blend for about 1 minute until the liquid is completely smooth and thick.
Pour the blended drink into a cup.
(Optional) Place a few mint leaves on the surface or sprinkle 5 g of chopped nuts for garnish.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a refreshing summer drink that combines the tropical aroma of passion fruit with the fresh sweetness of orange. Mixed with jasmine green tea or sparkling soda, it offers distinct layers of flavor that are cool and palate-cleansing. Rich in vitamin C, it helps boost immunity and nourish the skin. The process involves marinating, brewing tea, and juicing; while there are several steps, the difficulty is moderate and beginners can try it. The passion fruit needs to be marinated a day in advance, making the total time about 24 hours, though actual hands-on time is only about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Marinated passion fruit portion (since small amounts are hard to mix, this is for two servings)
Honey 10 g (can be replaced with 5 g of white sugar if unavailable)
Mint leaves or other green leaves (optional, for garnish)
Preparation for the jasmine green tea version, one glass, about 380 ml
cac_buoc: Marinate the passion fruit (this is for two servings).
Scoop out the pulp from three passion fruits (including the juice) and place in a container.
Weigh 30 g of granulated white sugar and add it.
Weigh 10 g of honey and add it (replace with 5 g of sugar if unavailable).
Stir well.
Cover the container with plastic wrap and refrigerate to marinate for 12~24 hours.
Brew the jasmine green tea (suggested ratio => tea: water: ice = 1~2 : 50 : 30).
Weigh 3~6 g of tea leaves into a vessel, add 150 ml of boiling water, and steep for 6 minutes.
Add 90 g of ice cubes to the steeped green tea to cool it down; stir to speed up the process.
Once the ice has melted, filter out the tea leaves to obtain about 240 ml of jasmine green tea.
Prepare the orange (can be done while the tea is steeping).
Cut the orange in half (perpendicular to the axis) and cut one slice from one half; set aside.
Cut the halves again and use a manual juicer to squeeze the juice from the 4 quarters; set aside in a container.
Official preparation.
Choose a glass, preferably a clear glass with a capacity of 350~400 ml.
Place 70 g of ice cubes at the bottom of the glass and pour in all the orange juice.
Place the prepared orange slice against the inner wall of the glass.
Drizzle one portion of the marinated passion fruit over the ice.
Slowly pour the jasmine green tea to fill the glass and create layers.
Place the decorative green leaf on the surface (optional).
Stir well before enjoying.

mon_an.mo_ta: The Coconut Sugar Slushie is a quick-to-make cold drink with a tropical flair. The sweet, light taste of coconut blends with the caramel aroma of coarse brown sugar for a smooth, icy texture. Coconut water is rich in natural electrolytes and minerals for quick hydration, while the coffee sugar adds a touch of energy. The barrier to entry is low—just freeze the coconut water until solid and then crush it into a slush—making it stress-free for beginners. It requires over 10 hours of preparation for freezing, but the actual work takes only a few minutes, making it perfect for a leisurely afternoon treat.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Coffee sugar 10 g (two packets of Taikoo coffee sugar)
The optimal amount of slush is related to the melting speed; 300 g of slush made at -18 degrees typically lasts 30 minutes at room temperature.
cac_buoc: Pour out 200 ml from a 500 ml bottle of coconut water, then immediately tighten the cap.
Place the bottle in the freezer for over 10 hours.

Remove the bottle; once confirmed the coconut water is completely frozen, strike it against hard surfaces like a wall corner, chair back, or table edge. (Ensure the surface will not be damaged by this action).
Once the frozen coconut water has reached a slushie consistency, open the cap and pour the slush into a bowl or glass.
Sprinkle the coffee sugar or chopped nuts evenly over the surface of the slush.
Finished.

mon_an.mo_ta: Baba Citrus Tea is a fruit tea drink that combines the sweet clarity of citrus with the fragrance of jasmine. It has a refreshing taste with a sweet aftertaste and is a creative beverage not limited to any specific cuisine. Baba citrus is rich in vitamin C and fiber, and when paired with green tea, it provides a fresh and awakening experience. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly; the entire process from brewing tea to stirring takes only about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Portion for one glass, approximately 300 ml
cac_buoc: Brew the jasmine green tea (suggested ratio => tea: water: ice = 1~2 : 50 : 30).
Weigh 2~4 g of tea leaves into a vessel, add 100 ml of boiling water, and steep for 6 minutes.
Add 60 g of ice cubes to the steeped green tea to cool it down; stir to speed up the process.
Once the ice has melted, filter out the tea leaves to obtain about 160 ml of jasmine green tea.
Official preparation.
Choose a glass, preferably a clear glass with a capacity of about 300 ml.
Separate the Baba citrus segments and peel off the outer skin to collect the pulp.
Place 130 g of pulp and 130 ml of jasmine green tea into the blender.
Add 10 g of simple syrup (optional, if you prefer it sweeter).
Cover and start the blender, blend for 20 seconds, then pour the mixture into the glass.
Take a small amount of shredded pulp and sprinkle it on top.
Enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: This specialty drink combines bold coffee flavor with the sweet and sour notes of pineapple, refreshing bubbles, and a smooth cream layer for a multi-layered taste. Pineapple is rich in vitamin C and fiber, while coffee helps with alertness. The difficulty is moderate; you only need to whip the cream and mix the liquids. The entire process takes about 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Add ice cubes, coffee, pineapple juice, and soda water into a glass in that order.
Whip the heavy cream with sugar until soft peaks form, then fold in the rum and milk until it reaches a pourable consistency.
Pour the cream over the first mixture.
Sprinkle sea salt over the cream layer.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a traditional Chinese fermented dessert with a light, sweet, and slightly boozy flavor accompanied by a gentle wine aroma. It helps strengthen the spleen, whet the appetite, and promote digestion. The process is simple and fun; although it requires waiting for fermentation, the steps are not complicated, making it a great introductory project for fermentation. The total time is expected to be about 2 days, with actual hands-on time being only about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Glutinous rice 800 g (round glutinous rice recommended)
One packet of Angel sweet rice leaven (8 g) (although the ratio is 3 g leaven per 1000 g of rice, using more leaven increases the success rate)
Clean water 720 g + 600 g (720 g for steaming, 600 g for later fermentation)
Steamer (an electric rice cooker works too)
1 clean, airtight glass or ceramic jar
This recipe makes 1 batch, enough for 6~8 people.
cac_buoc: Wash 800 g of glutinous rice, place it in the rice cooker, add 720 g of clean water, and select the steaming/rice mode.
Once cooked, pour the rice out to cool. Use a clean tool to spread it out until it reaches 30 °C (measure with a thermometer; it should feel warm but not hot to the touch).
Dissolve 8 g of Angel sweet rice leaven in 20 ml of warm water (about 30 °C), sprinkle evenly over the glutinous rice, and mix well.

Add 600 g of clean water to the rice to help the leaven mix evenly. Let it sit for 2-3 minutes until the rice has absorbed the water. This step ensures the fermented rice has plenty of liquid from the start.
Use a rolling pin to make a small hole in the center of the rice (to allow the liquid to pool).
Place the mixed rice into a clean container, press the surface lightly to flatten, and seal with a lid or plastic wrap.
Place in an environment of 28 ～ 32 °C to ferment for 24 ～ 48 hours. Do not shake or move it during fermentation.
Criteria for success: clear liquid has seeped into the center hole, the overall aroma is slightly alcoholic with no off-smells, and it is not sour or spoiled.
Once fermentation is complete, refrigerate immediately (you can add dried osmanthus during the process). Use a clean utensil to scoop it out each time; it keeps in the fridge for 7 ～ 10 days.
You can continue with a second fermentation by adding 500 ml of clean water to increase the amount of liquid (up to 800 g of water is fine).
The rice will continue to ferment. If you want to stop the fermentation, you can steam it for 10 minutes to sterilize it, or keep it in the refrigerator.

mon_an.mo_ta: Smoked Plum Drink is a traditional sweet and sour beverage that is delicious and cooling, especially refreshing when served chilled. The ingredients in this recipe, such as smoked plums, hawthorn, and licorice, help generate fluids, quench thirst, and aid digestion. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, requiring only soaking, boiling, and chilling. The entire process, including soaking, two decoctions, and chilling, takes over 6 hours, so preparation in advance is recommended.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: All quantities can be increased or decreased proportionally.
cac_buoc: Wash the ingredients (except for the dried osmanthus and rock sugar) and soak them in 1.5 liters of room-temperature water for over two hours.
Bring to a boil over medium-high heat, cover, and turn the heat to low to simmer for 40 minutes for the first decoction.
Place the rock sugar in a basin, then pour the first decoction (strained of solids) over it while hot; stir until the sugar dissolves.
Return the solids to the pot with 600 ml of water, bring to a boil over high heat, cover, and turn the heat to medium to simmer for another 20 minutes for the second decoction.

Finally, mix the second decoction with the rock sugar liquid while hot. When the mixture is at 60-70 ℃, add the dried osmanthus (do not exceed 80 ℃), cover, let cool, and then refrigerate for over 3 hours.
When drinking, remember to strain out the dried osmanthus. Sip it like tea; it is ice-cold, refreshingly tart, moderately sweet, with a full and long-lasting flavor profile.

mon_an.mo_ta: Sour plum drink (made from instant mix) is a refreshing sweet and sour summer beverage in the traditional Beijing style. It helps promote fluid production, quench thirst, and aid digestion. The method is extremely simple—just stir in order—making it perfect for beginners. The entire process takes about five minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: All quantities below can be increased or decreased proportionally.
cac_buoc: Measure 1177 g of drinking water.
Add 60 g of instant sour plum crystals and use a spoon to stir clockwise for 50 rotations.
Add the remaining 60 g of instant sour plum crystals and stir clockwise for another 50 rotations.
Add 9 g of rock sugar and stir clockwise for 100 rotations.
Add 48 g of Beijing Erguotou liquor and stir clockwise for 30 rotations.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic gin cocktail with a crisp, slightly bitter taste, featuring the bright acidity of lemon and the fine bubbles of tonic water for a light and refreshing mouthfeel. While it mainly provides hydration and some calories from alcohol, the fresh lemon juice adds vitamin C to help keep you alert. The method is very simple and easy for beginners to master, taking only about 5 minutes.
cac_buoc: Prepare the lemon.
Cut the lemon in half (knife perpendicular to the axis) and cut a slice from one half to set aside for garnish.
Cut the remaining halves again and use the juicer to extract the juice from the 4 wedges; set the juice aside.
Official preparation.
Choose a glass, preferably a clear glass with a capacity of 350~400 ml.
Place 100 g of ice cubes at the bottom of the glass.
Pour in 30~40 ml of gin.
Pour in 15 ml of lemon juice (add more or all of it if you prefer it more sour).
Use a spoon to stir well.
Place the prepared lemon slice into the glass.
Slowly pour the tonic water along the side of the glass until full (do not pour directly onto the ice to avoid excessive foaming and loss of carbonation).
Use a spoon to gently lift up and down to mix the liquid (do not stir in a circular motion to preserve the carbonation).
Place the decorative green leaves on the surface (optional).

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic gin cocktail, perfectly sweet and sour with refreshing bubbles. Lemon provides plenty of vitamin C, combined with simple syrup to balance the acidity. It is very simple to make, taking a beginner only 5 minutes to prepare, making it ideal for enjoying at home. Please note that alcohol consumption is harmful to health; do not drink in excess.
cac_buoc: Prepare the lemon.
Cut the lemon in half (knife perpendicular to the axis) and cut a slice from one half to set aside for garnish.
Cut the remaining halves again and use the juicer to extract the juice from the 4 wedges; set the juice aside.
Official preparation (without a shaker).
Choose a glass, preferably a clear glass with a capacity of 350~400 ml.
Place 100 g of ice cubes at the bottom of the glass.
Pour in 30~40 ml of gin.
Pour in 20 ml of lemon juice (add more or all of it if you prefer it more sour).
Pour in 30~40 g of simple syrup.
Use a spoon to stir well.
Place the prepared lemon slice into the glass.
Slowly pour the carbonated soda water along the side of the glass until full (do not pour directly onto the ice to avoid excessive foaming and loss of carbonation).
Use a spoon to gently lift up and down to mix the liquid (do not stir in a circular motion to preserve the carbonation).
Place the decorative green leaves on the surface (optional).
If using a shaker, replace steps 2~6 above with the following steps:
Add ice cubes, gin, lemon juice, and simple syrup into the shaker and shake well.
Pour the mixture into the glass (if the ice inside is too crushed, you may strain it and add fresh ice cubes to the glass).

mon_an.mo_ta: Long Island Iced Tea is a classic cocktail that tastes very similar to iced tea; it goes down smoothly but has a relatively high alcohol content. Its nutritional value is not high, and while it can help you relax occasionally, you must never drink to excess. The method is very simple, requiring only the mixing of four base spirits, liqueur, and juice in proportion, making it easy for beginners. From preparation to completion takes about 5 minutes.
cac_buoc: Cut the lemon in half and squeeze 30 ml of lemon juice into the glass;
Add the following to the glass in order:
15 ml gin,
15 ml tequila,
15 ml vodka,
15 ml white rum,
15 ml orange liqueur;
Slowly pour 20 ml of maple syrup into the glass, stirring as you pour;
Add 75 ml of cola to the glass;
Fill the glass to the top with ice cubes;
Stir gently for 20 seconds;
Enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Liangpi is a homemade snack originating from Shaanxi, known for its chewy texture and refreshing sour-spicy flavor with a rich sesame aroma. The sesame paste and wheat gluten provide plant-based protein and calcium, combined with crunchy cucumber and mung bean sprouts rich in vitamins and fiber. The difficulty is medium; it only requires blanching, shredding, and mixing the sauce, which a beginner can do at a relaxed pace. From preparation to serving takes about 40 minutes, perfect for a summer meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cucumber 100 g/serving, mung bean sprouts 50 g/serving.
Basin, bowls, plates, mortar and pestle
cac_buoc: Pour 500 ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the mung bean sprouts to the pot and cook over high heat for 60 seconds. Remove the sprouts, rinse in cold water, and set aside on a plate.
Shred the cucumber and set aside on a plate.
Peel 10 g of garlic cloves, place in a mortar with 1 g of salt. Mash into a paste, then add 10 g of water. Set aside.
Note: Liangpi bought from supermarkets often has oil on the surface; you can rinse it with tap water. Do the same for the wheat gluten.
Note: After rinsing the gluten, use your hands to squeeze out the excess water (no need to use too much force).

Prepare a small bowl and add 3 g salt, 2 g chicken bouillon powder, 5 g light soy sauce, 1 g dark soy sauce, 1 g sesame oil, 2 g oyster sauce, and 5 g aromatic vinegar (salt and vinegar can be adjusted to taste; these measurements are for a standard flavor).
Add 25-35 g of warm water to the seasonings (depending on desired saltiness) and stir with chopsticks until dissolved. Set aside to cool.
Note: The following measurements are per person; if serving n people, multiply the quantities by n.
Take a small bowl and add the prepared sesame paste.
Add 4 g salt, 3 g chicken bouillon powder, 5 g light soy sauce, 1 g dark soy sauce, and 3 g oyster sauce.
Use chopsticks to mix the seasonings into the sesame paste.
Add 10 g of filtered water and mix well.
Repeat the previous step 2 or 3 times (depending on your preferred consistency for the sesame paste).
Take the prepared small basin and add the liangpi.
Pour in the salt water mixture and toss well with chopsticks. Then transfer to a small bowl (including the liquid).
Place the bean sprouts on top of the liangpi, followed by the wheat gluten.
Drizzle the prepared sesame paste over the gluten.
Garnish with the shredded cucumber.
Add chili oil if desired.
Your homemade Liangpi, full of color and flavor, is ready!

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a quick Western-style meal using pre-packaged pasta products, featuring chewy noodles and a rich, flavorful pre-made sauce. It primarily provides carbohydrates for quick energy along with some protein. The difficulty is extremely low—impossible for a beginner to mess up—taking only about 2 minutes from turning on the stove to plating.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Using the conditions above, calculate ingredients based on need (including but not limited to daily appetite, mood, and pre-meal activity).
Different types of pasta have different cooking times; this standard is for straight spaghetti.
2 people for 1 meal: 520 g (calculated as ready-to-cook product)
cac_buoc: Heat the pan.
Pour 50 ml of filtered water into the non-stick pan.
Add the pasta and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in the sauce and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Serve on a plate.
Place the pasta on a microwave-safe plate.
Pour the included sauce packet over the pasta.
Add 50 ml of filtered water.
Heat at 700W for 2 minutes.
Remove and mix well to finish.

mon_an.mo_ta: This dessert uses pre-made tart shells and egg custard filling. The shells are crispy and fragrant, while the filling is smooth and soft with caramel spots—the easiest version of this classic Cantonese dim sum. The main ingredients, eggs and milk, provide high-quality protein and calcium, making it a great home snack. The entire process involves only assembly and baking, very friendly for absolute beginners, taking about 40 minutes from preheating to finishing.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Requires 1 oven (preferably with top and bottom heat functions)
Egg tart filling approx. 10 ml, filling to 4/5 of the shell is best
cac_buoc: Preheat the oven to 200 degrees for 10 minutes.
Place the tart shell on a baking tray, pour about 10 ml of egg filling into the shell; the specific amount depends on the shell size, usually 4/5 full is sufficient.

Place the tray in the oven and bake with top and bottom heat at 190 degrees for 10 - 20 minutes. If you want brown caramel spots to form quickly on the filling, the top heat needs to be higher, usually 200 - 210 degrees.
The tarts are done when the filling has brown spots and the shell is fully puffed and slightly oily.

mon_an.mo_ta: French fries are crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, golden brown, salty, and savory—a widely popular quick snack. Potatoes provide starch and fiber, though calories are high when deep-fried or air-fried. Using pre-cut frozen fries and an air fryer makes the process simple and beginner-friendly. From preheating to serving takes about 25 minutes.
