nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Using the conditions above, calculate ingredients based on need (including but not limited to daily appetite, mood, and pre-meal activity).
1 bag frozen pre-cut fries (suggested brand: McCain)
1 air fryer (avoid budget brands if you want them crispy)
Note: different cooking tools may require different methods; this only covers the "air fryer" method.
As a main dish, 1 person for 1 meal: 400 g (frozen weight)
As a snack, 1 person for 1 meal: 1/4 of the main dish weight ± 50 g
cac_buoc: When opening a large bag of frozen fries, make a small opening to reduce frost buildup on the surface during long-term storage.
Plug in and preheat at 200 °C for 5 minutes.
The purpose of preheating is to ensure the air fryer reaches the necessary cooking temperature before adding the ingredients.
Note: take the fries out only after preheating is finished; do not let the fries thaw and soften before frying.
Place the fries in the air fryer and cook at 200 °C for 20 minutes.
When removing the fries, note that pre-packaged fries already contain oil, so use tongs or a tool.
At the 5~10 minute mark, remove the basket and shake it to ensure even cooking and prevent sticking.
At the 10~15 minute mark, remove the basket and spray a layer of oil covering about 2/3 of the surface of the dried fries.

If you like them crispy, remove them and shake the basket to let air circulate over the surface before plating; if you like them soft, plate them immediately. Serve with dipping sauce for better flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: This Chongqing hot pot base uses a heavy beef tallow foundation combined with homemade chili and various spices to create a numbing, spicy, and intensely fragrant base—the soul for dipping beef tripe, duck intestines, and other ingredients. Beef tallow and lard provide high energy, while chili and Sichuan peppercorns help warm the stomach and stimulate the appetite, though the high fat content means it should be eaten in moderation. The process requires precise control of oil temperature and stir-frying heat, which is a bit challenging for beginners. From preparation to completion takes about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Each portion of ingredients makes 7.5 kg of hot pot base/aged hot pot oil
cac_buoc: Place a pot over high heat, add beef tallow and heat until 80% hot (240 ± 10 °C). Add old ginger, shallots, onion, and garlic (100 g each), fry until dry (to remove the gamey smell of the tallow), then remove and discard the aromatics.
Add (salad oil or rapeseed oil) and pure lard. Wait for the oil temperature to drop to 50% hot (150 ± 10 °C), then add the homemade chili and stir-fry continuously for 5-8 minutes.
Add the bean paste and stir-fry until separated. Switch to medium-low heat and stir-fry slowly until the residue turns slightly white and develops a "sandy" texture (making a rustling sound).
When the oil turns a cherry red color, add sliced ginger (150 g) and garlic (100 g) and stir-fry until fragrant, about 15 seconds.
Add fermented black beans and fermented soy beans and stir-fry until fragrant, then add red Sichuan peppercorns and fennel seeds and stir-fry until fragrant.
(For aged oil) add the granular spices at this stage.
Add maltose powder and stir-fry until incorporated, then add white liquor and stir-fry until incorporated.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an extremely "lazy" recipe that uses an air fryer to render out excess fat, resulting in a product that is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside with a strong garlic aroma. The flavor depends primarily on the quality of the lamb chops. Lamb is rich in high-quality protein, iron, zinc, and other micronutrients, helping to nourish the blood and strengthen the body. The difficulty is moderate and easy for beginners; actual hands-on time is only 10 minutes, with a total time of about 40 minutes including marinating.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Butter 1 small tub (10 g) or BBQ seasoning 20 g

Optional: air fryer grill rack (using a rack results in less oil and more even cooking on the bottom, but is harder to clean. Not using one results in more flavor absorption. Choose based on preference.)
cac_buoc: Place the lamb chop in a bowl and rinse off any blood with clean water.
Use kitchen paper towels to pat the lamb chop dry. Rub the black pepper seasoning and garlic paste onto both sides and let marinate for 20 minutes.
Place a foil bowl on the grill rack, place the lamb chop on the rack, sprinkle with chopped basil, and place butter or BBQ seasoning on the lamb. Air fry at 180°C for 10 minutes.

Flip the lamb chop, sprinkle with more chopped basil, add butter (scooped from the foil bowl) or BBQ seasoning on top, and air fry at 180°C for 5 minutes (adjust time slightly based on preference; this timing avoids burning).

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a quick and convenient family dish that saves effort. The chicken wings are crispy on the outside and tender on the inside, with a natural savory aroma that rivals fast-food restaurants. Chicken mid-wings are rich in high-quality protein and healthy fats, providing plenty of energy. Very beginner-friendly, the actual hands-on time is only a few minutes, and the whole process takes about forty minutes before it's ready to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 6 chicken mid-wings (Tyson Orleans mid-wings; other brands like Sheng Nong's Do Do wings may be larger, so please adjust according to your appetite)
Optional: chopped basil (sprinkled purely for garnish)
Optional: Yunnan Danshan dipping spice (as a substitute for grilling seasoning)
cac_buoc: Remove the chicken wings from the refrigerator, place them skin-side down on a foil-lined tray, sprinkle with chopped basil, and cover with plastic wrap to thaw naturally for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with more chopped basil, then air fry at 200 °C for 10 minutes.
Flip the wings over, sprinkle with chopped basil, and air fry at 200 °C for another 7 minutes.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a staple home-cooked dish of Chinese origin. Using ready-made frozen dumplings makes it quick to prepare, resulting in thin skins and generous fillings with a fresh, savory taste. Serving them with vinegar, ginger, and garlic adds layers of flavor. As a complete meal, it provides sufficient protein and starch, making it nutritious and filling. There is no difficulty in making this; even beginners can easily master it in about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Based on the conditions above, calculate the ratio of ingredients to be used.
1 bag of frozen dumplings (within expiration date)
Water volume should be double the volume of the dumplings (when adding dumplings to the pot, the water level should be one to two times the height of the dumplings)
cac_buoc: Set to medium heat, pour water into the pot, and wait for it to boil.
Add the dumplings to the pot.
You may lightly rinse the dumplings with water before adding them to the pot.
After adding the dumplings, use a ladle or spatula to stir the water, but be careful not to hit the dumplings to avoid tearing the skins or causing them to stick to the bottom and remain raw.
Do not stir too frequently; stir for about 3 seconds every 30 seconds. Once the dumplings float, you can stop this step.

After the dumplings float and the water returns to a boil, use a ladle to take one out and check it. If the skin is still doughy, pour in 80 ml of cold water to lower the temperature and continue cooking until it boils again. Repeat the checking and stirring process; adding water a maximum of two times will ensure they are fully cooked.
When all dumplings have floated (about 8 minutes after adding them), use a spatula or slotted spoon to transfer them to a plate or bowl and serve.
After eating, wait for the pot water to cool slightly before discarding it and wash the pot promptly with dish soap; otherwise, the starch will form a sticky residue on the sides of the pot.

mon_an.mo_ta: Frozen Tangyuan (glutinous rice balls) is a quick and convenient microwave dessert with a chewy skin and sweet, fragrant filling, originating from traditional Chinese snacks. It primarily provides carbohydrates for a quick energy boost. The method is extremely easy and beginner-friendly, taking only about 6 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Frozen Tangyuan: 11 pieces. The quantity depends on the size of your bowl. Ensure the stack of balls is at least 5 mm below the rim of the bowl.
cac_buoc: Take the frozen Tangyuan out and place them in a bowl.
Pour in boiling water until the Tangyuan are completely submerged.
Microwave on high power for 4 minutes.
If the Tangyuan have absorbed water and expanded, they are cooked.
If they are not yet cooked, heat for an additional 1 minute.

mon_an.mo_ta: Frozen wontons feature thin skins and tender fillings in a clear, fresh broth, making them a convenient home-cooked meal. They primarily provide starch and protein for a quick energy boost. The method is simple and very beginner-friendly using a rice cooker; it takes about 55 minutes from boiling the water to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 bag of frozen wontons (preferably with a seasoning packet included)
Rice cooker (suggested brand: Xiaomi smart rice cooker)
Salt (if the wontons do not include a seasoning packet)
Chicken powder (if the wontons do not include a seasoning packet)
Pepper powder (if the wontons do not include a seasoning packet)
Sesame oil (if the wontons do not include a seasoning packet)
Note: Different cooking appliances may require different methods; this guide specifically covers the "rice cooker" method.
When all wontons are in the rice cooker, the water volume should be 2–3 times the amount needed to just cover them (about 600 ml of water for one serving)
cac_buoc: Pour water into the rice cooker, select the "Stew" or "Cook" mode and set for 35 minutes; the water should be boiling when you open the lid.
Carefully add the frozen wontons to the water, taking care not to get burned.
You may lightly rinse the wontons with water before adding them to the rice cooker.
If the wontons come with a seasoning packet, add it to the water now.
Close the lid and continue on the "Stew" or "Cook" mode for another 20 minutes.
Ladle all the wontons and enough broth to cover them into a bowl.
If you didn't add a seasoning packet earlier, season with salt, chicken powder, pepper, and sesame oil according to your taste.
You can also garnish with 5–8 cilantro leaves for extra flavor (only for those who enjoy cilantro).

mon_an.mo_ta: This thick shiitake mushroom soup has a rich, fresh flavor and a smooth texture, making it a quick home-cooked soup. Shiitake mushrooms are rich in amino acids and polysaccharides, which help boost immunity. The process requires some basic heat control and thickening techniques but remains beginner-friendly. It takes only about 25 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Slice the shiitake mushrooms (each slice 0.5–1 cm thick; thicker slices are chewier), place in a large bowl, add 2 g of salt, and soak for 15 minutes.
Place the tapioca starch in a small bowl, add 50 ml of water, and stir until smooth with no lumps (this is your starch slurry).
Drain the salt water from the mushroom bowl and squeeze the excess moisture out of the mushrooms (to make frying easier in the next step) [Optional].
Over low heat, pour in the oil and wait for small bubbles to form (about 30 seconds depending on the stove), then add the mushrooms and sear each side for 10 seconds [Optional].
Pour in 300 ml of boiling water, adjust to medium heat, and cook for 3–5 minutes.
Pour in the starch slurry, stir the soup gently, then add 3 g of salt and 3 g of chicken powder. Finally, garnish with green onions and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic French-style thick soup with a silky texture and a blend of mushroom and milky aromas. Mushrooms are rich in fiber and micronutrients, while milk provides high-quality protein and calcium. The method is very simple and easy for beginners to master, taking about 30 minutes from preparation to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 1–2 people.
cac_buoc: Slice the mushrooms and set aside; finely dice the onion and set aside.
Melt the butter in a pan over low heat, then sauté the onion until translucent.
Add the mushrooms and sauté until they release their liquid and soften, then sprinkle in the flour and stir well.
Pour in the milk and water, stir thoroughly, and bring to a boil over low heat, stirring constantly to prevent burning the bottom.
Continue cooking over low heat for about 10 minutes until the soup thickens.
Pour in the heavy cream and cook for another 1 minute, then season with salt and black pepper.
After turning off the heat, you can use a blender to process the soup until smooth (optional).

mon_an.mo_ta: Millet porridge is a popular household staple in Northern China, featuring a smooth texture and rich grain aroma. The "millet oil" (the film on top) is particularly good for stomach health. It is rich in protein, fats, carbohydrates, and carotene, with a vitamin B1 content that ranks among the highest of all grains, making it easy to digest. The method is very simple and easy for beginners, taking about 30–35 minutes from boiling the water to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Based on the conditions above, calculate the ratio of ingredients to be used.
cac_buoc: Place 100 g of millet in a bowl and rinse lightly once with water (stir gently by hand and pour off the water to remove surface dust; do not scrub!!!).
Bring the water to a boil—it must be boiling!!!
When the water is at a rolling boil, add the millet to the pot. (This is a crucial but often overlooked step).
Stir to prevent the millet from sticking to the bottom, continue to cook on high heat for 6–10 minutes, stirring occasionally.
Switch to medium-low heat and cook for 15–20 minutes with the lid slightly ajar. Do not let the "millet oil" boil over! Continue to stir occasionally to prevent burning the bottom.

mon_an.ten: Stewed Chicken with Yam and Pumpkin
mon_an.mo_ta: Stewed Chicken with Yam and Pumpkin is a warming soup for autumn and winter. The yam strengthens the spleen, the pumpkin is sweet and fragrant, and the chestnuts are soft and waxy, creating a naturally sweet broth. It is rich in protein, fiber, and various vitamins for balanced nutrition. The method is simple, taking about 50 minutes from preparation to serving, making it easy for beginners to complete.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 small pumpkin (about 300 g, steamed and mashed into a puree)
cac_buoc: Cut the chicken into pieces. Place in a pot of cold water with ginger and cooking wine to blanch. Once the water boils, cook for 3 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Peel and slice the yam diagonally; peel the chestnuts and set aside.
Wash the small pumpkin, steam until soft, then scoop out the flesh and mash into a puree; set aside.
Place the blanched chicken, yam, chestnuts, and ginger slices into a pot. Cover with water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low heat and simmer for 30 minutes.
Stir in the pumpkin puree until dissolved, add the red dates, and cook for another 10 minutes.
Season with salt and serve.

mon_an.ten: Pork Rib Soup with Yam and Corn
mon_an.mo_ta: This pork rib soup with yam and corn has a clear, sweet, and rich flavor. The yam is soft, the corn provides a sweet aftertaste, and both blend perfectly with the fresh aroma of the ribs. It is a family soup suitable for all ages. Rich in protein, fiber, and vitamins, it helps strengthen the spleen and boost immunity. The method is simple with clear preparation and stewing steps, making it easy for beginners to finish in about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
Fresh ginger (about 20 g, sliced and set aside)
Green onion (about 15 g, tied in a knot or chopped for garnish)
Clay pot or deep soup pot
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients:
Wash the carrot, peel, and cut into 3 cm diagonal slices.
Wash the corn and cut into 4 cm cylindrical sections.
Peel the yam (wearing gloves is recommended to avoid skin irritation from the sap) and cut into 4 cm lengths; set aside.
Blanch the ribs:
Fill a pot with enough cold water and add the washed ribs.
Add about 10 g of ginger slices, the knotted green onion, and 15 ml of cooking wine.
Bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, wait 3 minutes, skimming off the foam from the surface.
Remove the ribs, rinse off impurities with warm water (about 40 °C), and drain; set aside.
Sauté the ribs:
Heat the pan, pour in 10 ml of oil, and wait 10 seconds for it to heat up.
Add the remaining 10 g of ginger slices and sauté until fragrant.
Add all the prepared ribs and sauté over medium heat for about 1 minute until the surface is slightly browned.
Stewing process:
Pour 1500 ml – 2000 ml of drinking water into the pot all at once.
Add all the prepared carrots, corn, and yam.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low heat, cover, and simmer slowly for 40 minutes.
Season and serve:
Add 6 g – 8 g of salt and stir well with a spoon.
Keep on low heat for another 2 minutes to let the salt penetrate the ingredients.
Turn off the heat, garnish with chopped green onions if desired, and serve.

mon_an.ten: Pork Rib and Bitter Melon Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Pork Rib and Bitter Melon Soup is a classic Cantonese-style clear soup that is fresh with a sweet aftertaste. The ribs are tender, and the bitter melon helps clear heat and balance richness. It is rich in protein and vitamins, and the dried shrimp add a boost of calcium. The preparation requires blanching to remove gaminess and careful removal of the bitter melon pith, which can be slightly challenging for beginners. However, using an electric pressure cooker can significantly simplify the process; traditional slow stewing takes 2 to 4 hours (prepare 4 hours in advance), while a pressure cooker takes only about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 4 people.
Electric pressure cooker (greatly simplifies the process and time)
Clay pot (more suitable for stewing soup than a frying pan)
5–10 g fresh ginger (optional, used for blanching)
cac_buoc: Wash the ribs and chop into small pieces about 4 cm ± 2 cm * 3 ± 2 cm (you can ask the butcher to do this).
Pour 700 ml of cold water into a pan with the ribs, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and remove the ribs.
Halve the bitter melon lengthwise, scrape out all the seeds and white pith, then cut into 0.5 ± 0.3 cm slices and wash.
Using a soup pot:
Pour 1100 ml of water and the ribs into the soup pot over high heat.

Wait for the water to boil, then add the bitter melon and dried shrimp. Reduce to low heat and wait 120–240 minutes (after 120 minutes, you can test a piece of meat; if it falls off the bone easily, turn off the heat).
When serving, add salt and white pepper; suggested amounts are 0.3 to 0.6 g of salt and 0.1 to 0.5 g of white pepper per 250 ml of soup.
Using an electric pressure cooker:
Pour 1000 ml of water, the ribs, dried shrimp, and bitter melon into the cooker.
Select the "Soup" function and start the cooking process (usually 45 minutes under pressure).
Serve and season with salt and pepper as you would with the soup pot method.

mon_an.mo_ta: Yellow Catfish and Tofu Soup is a family-style soup with a fresh, tender taste and a milky white, savory broth. The fish is tender with few bones, and the tofu is silky smooth with a hint of warmth from the pepper, making it suitable for all ages. The fish provides high-quality protein, while the tofu adds calcium for a balanced, easily absorbed meal. The process is straightforward—just focus on removing any fishy odors and pan-frying the fish to prevent sticking. Even beginners can master this in about 40 minutes.
cac_buoc: Clean the fish thoroughly (pay close attention to the blood line in the belly to avoid a fishy smell), place in a large bowl, add cooking wine, 10 g sliced ginger, and 5 g salt, then marinate for 15 minutes.
Cut the tofu into pieces, soak in cold water for 5 minutes, then drain and set aside.

Before frying the fish, rub the pot with a slice of ginger to prevent sticking. Pour in the oil (use 15 ml * number of fish), heat it up, then fry the fish for 2-3 minutes. Shake the pan slightly to prevent sticking and flip the fish once.

Once the fish is fried, pour in the boiling water, 5 ml cooking wine, and ginger slices. Switch from low to high heat, cover, and cook on high for 10 minutes (use a bit more water as some will evaporate).

When the broth turns milky white, add the prepared tofu. Adjust to medium heat and cook for another 5 minutes. Season with 10 g salt and 3 g ground pepper. Finally, garnish with green onions and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Vermilion Bird Soup is a quick family-style soup from the Eastern Henan region. It has a smooth, sweet flavor and a rich aroma of sesame oil. Eggs provide high-quality protein, and the method is very simple: just boil water and prepare the eggs. It takes less than ten minutes to get on the table and has a refreshing, heat-clearing effect.
cac_buoc: Beat the egg in a bowl, then pour in the sesame oil.
Once the water reaches a boil, quickly pour the boiling water into the bowl with the egg.
Add the white sugar.

mon_an.mo_ta: Pork Rib and Corn Soup is a fresh, sweet family-style soup where the ribs are fall-off-the-bone tender, and the corn and carrots provide a natural sweetness. It is rich in protein, vitamins, and fiber for a balanced nutritional profile. The method is simple and beginner-friendly: just blanch the ribs, sauté until fragrant, and slow-simmer for about an hour. Total time from prep to serving is about an hour and a half.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 ear of corn (add another if you like corn)
1 carrot (add another if you like carrots)
10-15 g salt (depending on the final amount of broth)
cac_buoc: Cut the shallot into 3-4 cm sections and crush slightly with the flat of a knife.
Cut the corn into small rounds.
Slice the carrot diagonally into chunks.
Peel the fresh ginger and cut into large slices.
Chop the fresh ribs into small pieces.
Place the ribs in a pot of cold water with the shallot, ginger, and cooking wine. Blanch by bringing to a boil over high heat. Skim off the foam, remove the ribs, and drain.

Heat a pan with oil, add the large ginger slices and ribs. Sauté until the surface of the ribs is slightly golden brown, then add the vinegar (helps tenderize the meat quickly) and continue sautéing for one minute.
Pour in the boiling water all at once (do not add more later) and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the corn and pepper first. Cover and simmer on low heat for twenty minutes. Then add the carrots, cover, and continue to simmer on low heat for forty minutes.
Seasoning is simple: three minutes before serving, add the salt (no other seasonings needed). Finally, garnish with a handful of chopped green onions and serve.

mon_an.ten: Fresh Pork Ball Soup (Sheng Tuan Wan Zi)
mon_an.mo_ta: Fresh Pork Ball Soup features tender, bouncy, and smooth meatballs in a pure, natural broth. The pork provides high-quality protein, combined with wood ear mushrooms and dried daylilies for balanced nutrition. This recipe requires hand-mincing the meat and controlling the heat while shaping the balls, making it better suited for home cooks with some experience. Prep to table takes about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Scallion, ginger, and Sichuan pepper water
Potato starch = number of servings * 40 g (this recipe is for one person)
Soaked glass noodles (to place at the bottom of the bowl)
Amount of salt = kg of pork * 6 g
Amount of pepper = kg of pork * 2 g
cac_buoc: Prepare the pork shoulder.
Salt
Ground pepper
Scallion, ginger, and Sichuan pepper water
1 egg white
Potato starch
Cooked soybean oil
Wood ear mushrooms
Dried daylilies
Small green onions
Soaked glass noodles (to place at the bottom of the bowl)
Salt
Chicken powder
Sesame oil
Cilantro
Trim the meat to a 3:7 fat-to-lean ratio.
Mince the meat with a knife, then pound it with the back of the knife to break the tendons and make it fluffy.
Mince and pound until it becomes a fine paste; for the best taste, it must be hand-minced as a food processor makes it too mushy.
For every kg of meat, add 6 g salt and 1 g ground pepper.
Mix well by hand.
Add the scallion-ginger-Sichuan pepper water gradually, stirring as you go. Knead by hand so the meat absorbs the liquid. Use 80 g of water per kg of minced meat.
Add the egg white and continue stirring in one direction.
Add 40 g potato starch and mix well.
Add the cooked soybean oil to keep the texture smooth and bouncy.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer (shimmering but not rolling).
Shape the meat into balls using your hand.
Once all the balls float, cook on low heat for 1 minute.
Place the glass noodles in the bottom of a bowl.
Add wood ear mushrooms, daylilies, and small green onions. Season the bowl with salt, pepper, and chicken powder.
Pour the soup and meatballs into the bowl.
Drizzle with 3-5 drops of sesame oil.
Garnish with a small sprig of cilantro.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tomato, Beef, and Egg Soup is an appetizing, sweet and sour family dish with a smooth and fresh taste. Beef is rich in high-quality protein and iron, tomatoes provide lycopene and vitamin C, and eggs add lecithin. The method is simple and easy for beginners to master, usually taking about half an hour to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Using the conditions above, calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
cac_buoc: Thinly slice the beef.
Cut the tomatoes into small pieces.
Finely chop the green onions.
Slice the ginger.
Mince the garlic.
Place the beef in a bowl.
Add salt and pepper, then marinate for 15-20 minutes.
Bring water to a boil.
Add the ginger slices and beef slices; cook until the beef changes color.
Add the tomato pieces and cook until soft.
Beat the eggs and slowly pour them into the pot, stirring with chopsticks to create egg ribbons.
Season with salt and pepper.
Finally, add the chopped green onions and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Shredded White Radish Soup is a light, refreshing vegetarian family soup that is quick and simple. White radish is high in water and vitamin C, cooking up soft and naturally sweet with very few calories. The difficulty level is extremely low, taking only about 10 minutes to cook.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
3 g lard (or 3 g fragrant sesame oil)
cac_buoc: Peel the white radish and use a grater to shred it into fine strips; set aside.
Pour 800 ml of water into a pot and add the shredded radish.
Add 3 g salt, 2 g white pepper, and 3 g MSG, then stir well with a spoon.
Turn on high heat and bring the water to a boil.
Once boiling, reduce to medium-low heat and continue cooking for 5 minutes until the radish is soft and translucent.
Before turning off the heat, add 3 g lard (or 3 g fragrant sesame oil), stir well, then turn off the heat and serve.

mon_an.ten: Century Egg and Lean Pork Congee
mon_an.mo_ta: Century Egg and Lean Pork Congee is a classic Cantonese family dish. It features a silky smooth rice base, the rich aroma of century eggs, and the tender taste of lean pork for a warm, savory flavor. It is rich in carbohydrates and high-quality protein, and when combined with vegetables, it offers balanced nutrition that is easy to digest. Although it has several steps, the process is straightforward. Beginners following the steps will succeed. Estimated time is about 1.5 hours, but using a rice cooker's timer or keep-warm function makes it an exceptionally convenient breakfast.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: If possible, wear disposable gloves when measuring and handling ingredients; it is recommended to wash the vegetables in advance and set them aside.
cac_buoc: Rice - wash - place in the rice cooker pot - add 1 liter of water.
Lean pork - wash - drain slightly - add 10 ml cooking oil - massage well - add to the rice cooker pot.
Century eggs - peel - wash - cut in half - separate the whites and yolks - dice the whites - mash the yolks - add to the rice cooker pot.
Fresh ginger - wash - peel - remove any withered parts - julienne - add to the rice cooker pot.
Green onion - wash - trim roots - remove any withered parts - finely chop - place in a small bowl and set aside.
Cilantro - wash - trim roots - remove any withered parts - finely chop - place in a small bowl and set aside.
Lettuce - wash - trim base - remove any withered parts - finely chop - place in a small bowl and set aside.
Soy sauce + oyster sauce + salt + ground pepper - stir well - place in a small bowl and set aside.
Main ingredients - use the rice cooker's 'congee' setting to cook until done.
Secondary ingredients - once the main ingredients are cooked, blanch the lettuce separately in hot water, then open the lid and stir it along with the other secondary ingredients into the congee.
Sauce - after the main ingredients are cooked, open the lid and stir the sauce mixture into the congee along with the secondary ingredients.

mon_an.mo_ta: Plain Rice Congee is light, smooth, and a comforting staple for any household. With its pure rice aroma, it is suitable for both the young and the elderly. It is rich in carbohydrates and a small amount of protein, making it easy to digest and beneficial for the spleen, stomach, and lungs. The operation is simple; just master the heat and water ratio. Even beginners can easily complete it in about 25 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Using the conditions above, calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
Usually, one person eats 60 ml - 110 ml of rice.
Water volume is 9-12 times the volume of rice.
Latest time to stop high heat T1: 1.5 min / 500 ml * water volume.
Earliest time congee is ready Tr: 10 min / 500 ml * water volume.
Oil amount Mo: raw rice volume / 10.
Refrigeration time Tc: raw rice volume / 10 ml/min.
cac_buoc: (Optional) Mix Mo ml of oil with the washed rice; *try to ensure complete mixing so every grain is coated with a bit of oil*.
(Optional) Place the rice-oil mixture in the refrigerator for time Tc.
Place the rice and water in the pot.
Turn on high heat and cook until T1.
Before T1, you must turn the heat down to low. If you forget this step, the water may boil over and extinguish the flame. This is very dangerous!
Cook until Tr. At Tr, turn off the heat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Seaweed and Egg Drop Soup is a light and fresh family-style dish, a classic simple Chinese soup. Seaweed is rich in iodine, calcium, and fiber, while eggs provide high-quality protein, making for a nutritionally balanced pair. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 10 g dried seaweed (add more if you like seaweed)
cac_buoc: Soak the dried seaweed in clean water for 15 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Heat the pot, pour in 1.5 liters of clean water, 5 ml oil, and 2 g salt. Once the water boils, add the seaweed.
After the seaweed has boiled for 3 minutes, slowly pour the beaten eggs into the pot; it will be ready in 30 seconds.
Sprinkle with chopped green onions and turn the heat to low for 20 seconds.
Turn off the heat. Before serving, add a few drops of sesame oil; some people also add dried baby shrimp for extra flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: A Shanghai family-style soup adapted from Russian beet soup, using tomatoes and beef as the primary flavors for a rich, sweet, and sour taste. It is smooth and delicious, rich in high-quality protein, lycopene, and various vitamins for balanced nutrition. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, with the whole process taking about 2–3 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 2 cans of tomatoes (can substitute with fresh tomatoes, but flavor will be less intense)
5 g tomato paste (to enhance tomato flavor)
5 ml olive oil (for sautéing vegetables; can substitute with vegetable oil)
5 ml vegetable oil (for searing beef; do not substitute with olive oil)
cac_buoc: Dice the onion, carrot, and parsley/celery into 1 cm cubes.
Cut the red sausage and potatoes into 2 cm pieces.
Remove the cabbage core and tear the leaves by hand into 2 cm pieces.
Sprinkle 3 g salt and 3 g black pepper over the beef and marinate for 5 minutes.
Heat a pan and add the vegetable oil.
Sear the beef until the surface is browned (it can still be raw inside, but do not let it burn); remove and set aside.
Heat a soup pot and add the olive oil, diced onion, diced carrot, and diced parsley/celery.
Sauté until the onions are translucent, then add the tomato paste and canned tomatoes.
Add the beef and diced potatoes, then stir well.
Pour in enough water to cover the ingredients and cook over medium heat for 1 hour.
When the pot is boiling, add the cabbage and diced sausage, then stir well.
Cook over medium heat for another half hour.
Open the lid, add the remaining 15 g of salt, mix well, and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Lamb soup is a warming family dish featuring a milky white broth and tender meat, with the delicate aroma of scallions and white pepper and a hint of spice. Rich in protein, calcium, iron, and other nutrients, it helps warm the stomach and dispel cold. The steps are simple and beginner-friendly, with the entire process taking about 30 minutes.
cac_buoc: Cut the lamb into strips 5 cm long and 0.5 cm wide.
Cut the scallions into small sections.
Place the lamb in a pot, add 1000 ml of water, the cooking wine, and the scallions.
After boiling for 2 minutes, remove the lamb, rinse with fresh water, and drain.
Heat a pan with cooking oil, add the lamb, and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the surface is slightly golden.
Pour in the boiling water and turn the heat to high.
After 5 minutes, add the white pepper powder and salt, and continue to boil for 5 minutes.
Remove from the heat, add the cilantro and cumin powder, and stir well before serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: Laba Congee is a traditional seasonal sweet congee with a thick, silky texture and a complex aroma from various grains, beans, and dried fruits. Rich in carbohydrates, minerals, and vitamins, it also contains lotus seeds which help calm the mind, making it suitable for those under high work pressure. Although it uses many ingredients, the process is simple—just requires patience for slow cooking. Excluding preparation time like soaking, it takes about 3 hours to cook.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: For one person (three small bowls), the amount per serving is:
Congee pot (regular pots burn easily; a pressure cooker is recommended if available)
Medium glass bowl (or other medium stainless steel container)
The above quantities can be adjusted to taste; it is recommended not to exceed 150 g for rice types and 50 g for bean types.
cac_buoc: Wash the mung beans, red beans, peanuts, soybeans, green peas, and red kidney beans; place them in a clean glass bowl, fill 3/4 with water, and soak overnight (or at least 8 hours).
Wash the rice, glutinous rice, Job's tears, black rice, millet, and lotus seeds; place them in a clean glass bowl, fill 3/4 with water, and soak for 3 hours.

Drain the water from the beans and peanuts prepared in step 1, pour the remaining ingredients into the congee pot, add 1 liter of water (or until the water is one thumb-joint above the ingredients), bring to a boil over high heat, then cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Drain the water from the grains and lotus seeds prepared in step 2, add them to the congee pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 60 minutes.
Wash the red dates, longan, chestnuts, walnuts, and raisins (slice the red dates into small pieces); add them along with the rock sugar to the pot, cover, and simmer on low heat for 60 minutes.
Once the congee has reached a thick consistency, turn off the heat, ladle into bowls, and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stewed Squab with Mushrooms features a clear broth and tender meat, with the earthy aroma of mushrooms blending with the freshness of the squab. This is a classic Cantonese-style home-cooked soup. Squab is rich in high-quality protein and amino acids, while mushrooms provide polysaccharides and fiber, making this a gentle and nourishing dish. The squab must be blanched first to remove any gaminess, then stewed with corn and mushrooms. It requires some attention to heat control and timing, but beginners can master it with care. From prep to serving, it takes about 45 minutes in a pressure cooker or over 1 hour in a clay pot.
cac_buoc: Rinse the pre-cleaned squab thoroughly with cold water.
Place the squab in a pot of cold water, add 15 ml of cooking wine and the ginger; remove the squab as soon as the water boils to preserve nutrients.
Place the squab in a pressure cooker or clay pot, cover with water, and add 20 g of fresh ginger, 200 g of corn, and 100 g of mushrooms.
Note: Cook for 30 minutes in a pressure cooker; for a clay pot, bring to a boil then turn to low heat and simmer for 40-60 minutes.
When finished, ladle into bowls, add 3~5 g of salt, and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tomato and Egg Drop Soup is an appetizing, sweet and sour home-style soup with a silky texture. It is extremely easy to make and popular with all ages. Rich in lycopene, vitamin C, and high-quality protein, it offers balanced nutrition that is easily absorbed. Very beginner-friendly and time-saving, it takes about 15 minutes to prepare.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Eggs 1-2 (to taste; use 2 if you prefer more egg, otherwise 1)
cac_buoc: Wash the tomato and cut into wedges.
Mince the scallion, ginger, and garlic.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk well with chopsticks or a whisk.
Heat a pan, add 15 ml of oil; when the oil starts to smoke slightly, add the scallion, ginger, and garlic and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Pour in water until the level is about 1.2 times the height of the ingredients, and add the salt.
Wait for the pot to boil, pour in the beaten eggs, stir with chopsticks to break up the eggs, then add the MSG and sesame oil.
Wait 30 seconds, turn off the heat, and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a light and refreshing home-style soup with a fresh flavor, belonging to the category of quick and simple dishes. Enoki mushrooms are high in amino acids and fiber, and adding eggs provides high-quality protein. With a very low difficulty level, it is easy for beginners to master, taking only about 10 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Enoki mushrooms 400-500 g (one store-bought bag is enough)
cac_buoc: Separate the enoki mushrooms by hand as much as possible to prevent them from getting stuck in teeth; wash and set aside.
Use a kitchen knife or paring knife to cut the enoki mushrooms into sections, preferably no longer than 5 cm.
Place the enoki mushrooms in a pot, add water to about 1.1 times the height of the ingredients, and wait for 3 minutes after it boils.
Add the MSG and salt, then stir.
Continue to cook for about 30 seconds, turn off the heat, and serve.

mon_an.ten: Silver Ear and Lotus Seed Sweet Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Silver Ear and Lotus Seed Sweet Soup has a delicate sweetness and a silky texture, with soft silver ear mushrooms and powdery lotus seeds. It is a common nourishing dessert. Rich in natural collagen, fiber, and trace elements, it helps calm the mind. The process involves soaking and slow cooking, which tests a beginner's patience; the entire process takes about 3.5 hours.
cac_buoc: Soak the silver ear and lotus seeds in fresh water for 2 hours; soak the red dates for 10-20 minutes; rinse the goji berries and set aside.
Pour 600 ml of water into a pot; once boiling, add the silver ear, lotus seeds, and red dates.
Wait for the water to boil again, cover, and switch to medium heat to continue cooking.
After about 1 hour, add 5 g - 10 g of rock sugar and 5 g - 6 g of goji berries, then switch to low heat.
Continue to simmer on low heat for 30 minutes until the silver ear starts to become gelatinous.
Add another 5 g - 10 g of rock sugar and stir with a spoon for 5-10 minutes.
Turn off the heat and ladle into bowls.

mon_an.ten: Pork Rib Soup with Dried Tangerine Peel
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a Cantonese-style slow-cooked soup with a clear broth that is sweet on the palate with a lingering fragrance of aged tangerine peel. The pork ribs provide high-quality protein and calcium, while the combination of tangerine peel, American ginseng, and dendrobium helps regulate energy, strengthen the spleen, and nourish the lungs. It is suitable for those who stay up late or have throat discomfort. The process is not difficult; just prepare the ingredients and manage the stewing time. From prep to serving takes about two hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Dried tangerine peel (preferably aged 8-20 years); usually 1 piece has 3 segments, 1 segment is enough
Ribs (pork bones can be substituted), 4-5 pieces
cac_buoc: Blanch the pork ribs in hot water to remove any blood.
Rinse the tangerine peel, ophiopogon, polygonatum, dendrobium, and American ginseng.
Wash the stewing jar.
Open the stewing jar; first place the ribs at the bottom, then add the tangerine peel, ophiopogon, polygonatum, dendrobium, and American ginseng.
Pour hot water into the stewing jar, ensuring it is not too full.
Place the jar in a steamer or water bath and stew for 1.5 hours.
Add salt and serve while hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cucumber and Century Egg Soup is a quick home-style soup with a light flavor and the savory aroma of sautéed century eggs and garlic. It is warming and comforting without being greasy. The cucumber is cooling and hydrating, while the century egg provides protein with low fat. There is almost no technical barrier, making it easy for beginners to complete in about ten minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Wash the cucumber and cut into thin slices 0.5-1.2 mm thick.
Wash and mince the scallions; crush and peel the garlic, then cut in half.
Peel the century eggs and cut each into 6-8 pieces. Add oil to the pot, then add the cut eggs and garlic.
Stir-fry over low heat until the surface of the eggs and garlic is slightly golden, then add water and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the cucumber slices. As soon as the water boils again, turn off the heat immediately, season with salt and chicken powder, and remove from the heat.
Pour into a bowl and garnish with minced scallions.

mon_an.mo_ta: These pancakes have a slightly crispy exterior and a soft, fluffy interior with a savory meat filling. Rich in carbohydrates and protein, they are made even more nutritious with carrots and eggs. The difficulty is medium as beginners need to manage the heat, but the steps are clear. It takes about 1 hour from prep to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Use the conditions above to calculate the intended ingredient ratios.
Wok (can be replaced by the skillet)
cac_buoc: Take the ground meat (thawed), add 1/2 of all the seasonings listed (oil, salt, sugar, soy sauce, seasoning powder) and all of the starch; mix well and marinate for 30 minutes.
Place the flour in a bowl, add the egg, the remaining 1/2 of the seasonings, and an amount of water equal to 1/2 the volume of the flour (to make a thick but pourable batter); whisk well.
Mince the garlic.
Cut the scallion into sections.
Finely mince the carrot (the smaller the better for the filling).
Heat a wok with oil.
Once the oil is hot, sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the marinated ground meat and stir-fry until just cooked.
Add the minced carrot to the meat and sauté until the oil turns a golden yellow (to extract the carrot flavor).
Turn off the heat and let cool for 2 minutes.
Pour the cooked meat mixture into the raw batter and mix well.
Reheat and grease the flat-bottomed skillet with oil.
Set to low heat, pour the batter into the pan and spread evenly. Ensure it is not too thick. You can tilt the pan to help the batter cover the bottom.
While the surface is still wet, sprinkle the scallion sections on top.
Keep the heat low until the bottom sets.
Flip the pancake and continue to fry on low heat until the other side sets.
Fry each side for an additional 20 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Liangfen is a traditional snack originating from Sichuan, known for its cool, silky texture and appetizing spicy-sour flavor—perfect for summer. The main ingredient is mung bean starch, which is rich in carbohydrates and provides a quick energy boost. The process is not complex but requires patient stirring and a long cooling period to set. It is of medium difficulty for beginners. It takes 3-4 hours from start to finish, though most of that is waiting for it to chill; actual active time is about half an hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The following ingredients are for one person; determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for one person.
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients.
Mix 100 g of mung bean starch with 100 g of water and stir well.
Pour 600 g of water into a pot, bring to a boil over high heat, then turn to low heat.
Pour in the starch mixture while stirring constantly; stir until thick and the color is uniform.
Find a container and brush it with a thin layer of cooking oil.
Pour the cooked starch into the container and refrigerate for 2-4 hours.
Once chilled, remove from the mold and cut into strips.
Mince the garlic and chilies, add 10 g of chili powder and 5 g of crushed peanuts, then drizzle with hot oil and stir.
Add 10 ml of soy sauce, 10 ml of vinegar, 5 g of white sugar, 3 g of chicken powder, and 3 g of salt; stir well.
Drizzle the dressing over the jelly, then garnish with cilantro and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Litti Chokha is a traditional main dish from Bihar, India, consisting of golden-roasted whole wheat balls and smoky mashed vegetables. It features a crispy exterior and a soft interior with a rich, aromatic flavor. The roasted chickpea flour filling is high in plant protein and fiber, combined with eggplant, tomatoes, potatoes, and other vegetables for rich nutrition. The process involves kneading dough, stuffing, roasting, and preparing vegetables; it has several steps and can be a bit challenging for beginners, taking about 60 minutes in total.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: In a mixing bowl, combine 120 g roasted chickpea flour, chopped onion, green chilies, and ginger.
Add 3 g cumin seeds, 5 g sesame seeds, 3 g red chili powder, 3 g Indian black salt, and 3 g salt.
Add 15 ml mustard oil, 10 ml lemon juice, and chopped cilantro.
Mix thoroughly; the filling should be crumbly but hold its shape when pressed. Set aside.
Place 200 g whole wheat flour in a large bowl.
Gradually add warm water while kneading until a *smooth and soft* dough forms.
Let the dough rest for 15 minutes.
Divide the dough into 8 equal portions.
Flatten each portion by hand into a circle about 8 cm in diameter (slightly thicker in the center).
Place about 15 g of filling in the center of the dough.
Gather the edges to enclose the filling, pinch to seal, and roll into a smooth ball.
Preheat the oven to 200°C.
Place the Litti on a baking tray and bake for 25-30 minutes, turning once halfway through, until the *surface is golden brown with cracks*.
If using a direct flame: roast the Litti directly over charcoal or a gas stove on low heat, rotating constantly until *evenly charred*.
Once roasted, brush ghee over the surface of each Litti while still hot to let it *absorb*.
Place the eggplant, tomatoes, and potatoes directly over a flame to roast, or bake in a 200°C oven for 20-25 minutes until the *skin is charred and the inside is completely soft*.
After roasting, peel the skin and mash the eggplant, tomatoes, and potatoes using a fork or by hand.
Mix the mashed vegetables together.
Add minced garlic, green chili, 4 g salt, and 15 ml mustard oil.
Stir and mix thoroughly.
Garnish with cilantro leaves.
Serve the Litti on a plate with the mashed Chokha on the side.
Eat while hot, breaking the Litti by hand and dipping it into the Chokha.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an Indian-style leavened flatbread, slightly charred and crispy on the outside while remaining fluffy and chewy on the inside—a perfect companion for curry. Rich in carbohydrates and protein, the addition of yogurt also makes the bread easier to digest. It requires some skill to manage the dough consistency and heat, but it can be made using just a flat skillet. Allow 1 hour for proofing; total time is about 1.5 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving makes 6 pieces, enough for 2-3 people.
Garlic 3 cloves (about 9 g), minced (for garlic version, optional)
cac_buoc: Dissolve 3 g dry yeast and 10 g sugar in 100 ml warm water (water temperature around 40°C, not too hot).
Let it sit for 5 minutes until *small bubbles appear on the surface* (indicating the yeast is activated).
In a large bowl, combine 300 g all-purpose flour and 5 g salt; mix well.
Pour in the yeast mixture, 60 ml yogurt, and 15 ml cooking oil.
Knead by hand into a *smooth, soft dough* (the dough should be slightly softer than usual and a bit sticky).
Knead the dough for 8-10 minutes.
Brush 3 ml of oil over the surface of the dough to prevent it from drying out.
Cover the bowl with a damp cloth or plastic wrap.
Place in a warm spot to proof for at least 1 hour, until the *dough has doubled in size*.
Take the proofed dough out and knead gently to degas.
Divide into 6 equal portions (about 80 g each).
Take one portion and lightly coat your hands with 3 ml of flour or oil.
Use a rolling pin to roll it into an oval or teardrop shape, about 4-5 mm thick.
If making garlic naan: sprinkle minced garlic and cilantro on the surface and roll gently to press them into the dough.
You can also sprinkle sesame seeds on top.
Method 1: Flat skillet (recommended)
Heat a flat skillet (cast iron is best) over high heat until *very hot* (a drop of water should evaporate instantly).
Brush a thin layer of water on one side of the naan.
Place the water-brushed side face down on the skillet.
Cook for 1-2 minutes until *brown spots appear on the bottom and the bread starts to bubble*.
Flip and continue cooking for 1-2 minutes.
If using a gas stove: after flipping, you can use tongs to lift the naan and char it directly over the flame for a few seconds to make it puff up quickly.
Remove and immediately brush ghee or butter over the surface.
Method 2: Oven
Preheat the oven to its highest setting (usually 250°C).
Place the naan on a baking tray.
Bake for 3-5 minutes until the *surface is golden and puffed*.
Remove and brush with ghee or butter.
Serve while hot.
Pairs perfectly with any Indian curry, such as Butter Chicken or Rajma Masala.

mon_an.mo_ta: Indian Biryani is a royal dish dating back to the Mughal Empire, featuring long-grain rice, bold spices, tender chicken, and fluffy, separate grains with layers of flavor. It is rich in protein and the essence of various spices, which can stimulate the appetite. The steps are quite elaborate and not very beginner-friendly; the entire process takes about 90 minutes (chicken needs to marinate for 1 hour).
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 3-4 people.
Chicken thighs 500 g (boneless, cut into large pieces)
Saffron 0.5 g + warm milk 30 ml (for soaking)
cac_buoc: In a large bowl, mix yogurt, grated ginger and garlic, red chili powder, turmeric, garam masala, salt, and lemon juice.
Add the chicken pieces and coat thoroughly with the marinade.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour (overnight is better).
Soak 0.5 g saffron in 30 ml warm milk for 15 minutes; set aside.
Pour 50 ml cooking oil into a pot and heat over medium heat.
Add the thinly sliced onions and fry until *deep golden brown and crispy* (about 12-15 minutes, requires patience).
Remove the fried onions, drain on paper towels, and set aside.
Drain the soaked Basmati rice.
Bring 2000 ml of water to a boil in a large pot.
Add bay leaves, cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, star anise, and 10 g salt.
Add the rice and cook over high heat for 5-6 minutes until the *grains are about 70% cooked* (soft on the outside but still firm in the core).
Immediately drain the rice, discard the whole spices, and set aside.
Brush 15 g ghee onto the bottom of a heavy-bottomed pot.
Layer 1: Spread the marinated chicken evenly across the bottom of the pot.
Layer 2: Spread half of the parboiled rice over the chicken.
Sprinkle half of the fried onions, mint leaves, cilantro, and green chilies.
Layer 3: Spread the remaining rice.
Sprinkle the remaining fried onions, mint, and cilantro.
Drizzle the saffron milk evenly over the top layer of rice.
Place the remaining 15 g ghee on top (cut into small pieces and scatter).
Seal the lid: use a rope of dough made from flour and water to seal the gap along the rim of the pot (traditional method), or wrap the rim with foil before putting the lid on.
First, cook over high heat for 3 minutes until steam starts to build up inside.
Then switch to the lowest heat and simmer for 25-30 minutes.
After turning off the heat, do not open the lid; let it rest for another 5 minutes.
Open the lid and use a large spatula to gently fold the rice from the bottom up to mix the layers.
Serve on a plate, accompanied by yogurt (Raita).

mon_an.mo_ta: This dish uses Coca-Cola instead of sugar for seasoning, bringing a unique slightly sweet and charred aroma. The rich sauce coats every grain of rice, making it a creative home-style fried rice. Eggs and sausage provide quality protein and energy, combined with rice for a balanced and filling main meal. The steps are straightforward and suitable for beginners; it usually takes about 20 minutes to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Dark soy sauce 7.5 ml (if using sugar-free Coke, add 5 ml; if not using bean paste, add 5 ml)
cac_buoc: Heat the pan, add 25 ml oil, crack two eggs in, and fry until the bottom is fully set.
Flip and fry until both sides are fully set.
Turn off the heat, remove the eggs, cut into 2-5 cm² pieces, then return them to the pan (you can also break them up directly with a spatula).
Turn the heat back on, pour in the Coca-Cola, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, bean paste, and oyster sauce; stir well.
Cook until the liquid in the pan is reduced to 1/3, then add the rice and sausage and stir-fry.
Stir-fry evenly, then turn the heat to low. Create a well in the center of the food, crack the third egg into it, cover the pan, and let it steam for 2 minutes.
Open the lid and stir-fry until the third egg is fully cooked. Sprinkle with chopped green onions and pepper, then serve.

mon_an.ten: Shanghai Salted Pork and Vegetable Rice
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic Shanghai home-style main dish. The savory flavor of salted pork and the sweetness of bok choy are infused into every grain of rice thanks to lard. It features crispy scorched rice at the bottom while maintaining the tender-crisp texture of the vegetable stems, creating distinct layers of flavor. Bok choy is rich in vitamins and fiber, while salted pork provides protein and energy for a balanced meal. The method is not complex, but adding the leaves in stages requires some timing, which can be a bit challenging for beginners. Takes about 1 hour from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 3 people.
Water 310 ml (300 ml for firmer rice, 325 ml for softer rice; add 20 ml if using bamboo shoots)
cac_buoc: If using winter bamboo shoots, slice them thinly and boil in cold water for 10 minutes to remove bitterness.
Dice the salted pork into 1 cm cubes.
Place the salted pork and bamboo shoots in a cold pan with 10 g lard, cooking wine, and white sugar. Stir-fry over medium-low heat until translucent and bubbly.
Chop the bok choy, separating the stems and leaves. Cut the stems into 0.5 cm cubes and the leaves into 2-3 cm long, 1-1.5 cm wide rectangles.
Add the bok choy stems to the pan and stir-fry until they turn a vibrant jade green.
Wash the rice and place it in a rice cooker, then add water.
Spread the stir-fried salted pork and bok choy stems over the rice.
Start the normal rice cooking cycle. During the last 10 minutes, quickly open the lid and spread the bok choy leaves on top.
Once cooked, let it rest for 5 minutes, then drizzle with 5 g lard and white pepper powder. Mix vigorously and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This basic milk bread recipe uses a sponge (pre-ferment) to simplify traditional bread making, resulting in a rich milky aroma and a soft, fluffy texture. Rich in carbohydrates and protein, it provides good energy. The difficulty is moderate, suitable for beginner bakers; the entire process takes about 200 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: Although specific quantities are provided, room temperature, humidity, and even yeast content in the air will affect the process. This recipe will provide adjustment suggestions throughout.
Here, larger quantities use cups, smaller quantities use g.
Butter or corn oil ⅛ cup
Flour 1 cup (scoop and level with a spoon, do not shake)

Milk, heavy cream, condensed milk, or milk powder (milk powder is best for a rich aroma, but do not use formulated powders like adult or baby milk as their chemistry is unstable. You can mix two types of dairy. Avoid ingredients with added sugar as the actual sugar content will exceed the recipe's suggestion)
Butter or corn oil (if the dairy product chosen has a very high fat content, you can omit this. Use unsalted animal butter. Soybean oil may have a beany smell, so try to avoid it)
Vital wheat gluten ¼ ~ ½ cup (optional)
Oven (do not use an oven without temperature control)

Baking tools: measuring cup (using cup units, do not shake when measuring to avoid under-measuring), silicone spatula, towel (to cover the dough and prevent moisture loss; use wet or dry as needed, steamer liners are recommended, or plastic wrap), oven (must be preheated), bench scraper, rolling pin, spray bottle (for water or oil), sieve, silicone mat, pastry brush, silicone baking paper (heat resistant), mold (bread is flexible, but cake molds must be anodized aluminum)
Vital wheat gluten: protein extracted from wheat that creates the structure when hydrated. Vanilla extract: highly refined natural flavoring to add vanilla taste and neutralize egg odors.
Cup is a common baking unit for easy volume-to-mass conversion. 1 cup = 250 ml; typically 1 cup of flour = 120 g. See the supplement for more conversions.
Warm water 30°C (just warm to the touch) 1 cup
Mixed dairy products totaling ¼ cup (mix milk powder with water)
cac_buoc: The sponge is a pre-ferment. Proofing it beforehand not only increases the success rate but also develops a better flavor through a longer fermentation time. If possible, fermenting the sponge for 4 days yields the best flavor. For beginners, a 30-minute sponge already makes a significant difference. Next, make the sponge.
First, mix the yeast and *30°C warm water* with a spatula or kitchen tool; let it sit for 5 minutes. Then mix in the flour and stir well. The sponge should be a very thick paste.
Cover with a towel and place in a warm spot to ferment for 45-60 minutes.
The final mixture should have many bubbles on the surface and a clear increase in volume.

Fermentation failed? Check here: 1. Ensure yeast is not expired; 2. Ensure water temperature is correct; 3. Extend fermentation time, possibly overnight in the fridge; 4. Temperature might be too low—preheat the oven to 60°C, turn it off, then place the sponge inside; 5. Add an equal amount of yeast, stir, and re-ferment; 6. Try adding 3 g of sugar and re-fermenting.

How to have a "permanent" sponge? With a permanent sponge, baking bread anytime is no longer a dream! 1. After making the sponge as above, keep it in a cool place (even the fridge!). Every 1-3 days, sprinkle a thin layer of flour on top (just enough to cover the surface), stir, and cover to continue fermenting. If it grows too fast, discard a portion. 2. When ready to bake, keep a portion equal to the pre-fermented volume to continue the cycle and use the rest for bread. 3. Over time, the sponge develops a unique aroma—the best "ingredient" for bread!
With the sponge ready, you're halfway there!

Step 1: Mix all remaining ingredients with the sponge using a spatula. Scrape the sides of the bowl to ensure everything is fully incorporated. Once it forms a dough with no dry flour, use one clean hand to press the dough while the other holds the bowl. Transfer to a silicone mat or cutting board. The dough should be formed and quite soft. If it's too sticky to hold shape, add ¼ cup of flour and mix until it holds. If it's too dry, increase kneading time. Use your fist to push the dough out, fold it, and repeat, incorporating all flour from the bowl.

Step 2: Use the heel of your hand to push the dough out, fold, and repeat until the surface is free of dry lumps. It won't be perfectly smooth yet. If using a board, it might stick; use a bench scraper to lift it. If the dough is formed but very stiff, it lacks water. Use wet hands or a spray bottle to dampen the surface, cover with a wet towel, and let it rest for 20 minutes; repeat if necessary.

Step 3: Spray a container (at least three times the volume of the dough) with vegetable oil, place the dough inside, cover with a towel, and proof for 1 hour. If there are issues, refer to the sponge troubleshooting. The surface should be slightly tacky. If not, spray with water and proof for another 20 minutes.
Step 4: The dough should now be double its original size. Sprinkle a thin layer of flour on the mat or board, take the dough out, and press it down with your hands to degas.
Step 5: Use a rolling pin to roll it into a sheet 1 cm thick. Roll it up tightly from one edge, leaving no gaps.
Step 6: Rotate 90° and repeat steps 4 and 5.

Step 7: Shape the bread and place it on a baking tray lined with silicone paper or in a greased mold. Ensure the seam is facing down. You can spray the tray with oil or brush with butter before laying the paper so it doesn't slide.
Step 8: Proof for another 30-45 minutes in the tray or mold. Refer to troubleshooting if needed.
Step 9: Meanwhile, preheat the oven. Preheat by running the oven at its highest temperature for at least 20 minutes.
Step 10: Use scissors or a knife to score the top of the bread with patterns.
Step 11: Brush with beaten egg. (optional)

Step 12: Place in the oven. Bake at 180°C (top and bottom heat) for 30 minutes, then reduce to 165°C for another 10 minutes. Every oven is different. If it hasn't browned after 30 minutes, the temperature is too low; increase by 5-10°C or bake longer. If the surface is bitter, the temperature was too high; reduce by 5-10°C or shorten the time. If the outside is caramelized but the inside is raw, reduce the heat by 5-15°C and extend the time by 10-20 minutes. If the surface is very hard or cracks severely, cover with foil and remove it for the last 10 minutes.

Step 13: Let it cool, then place in a food bag; it keeps for a week. It can be frozen for a month. Storing it in a sealed bag overnight will soften the crust and interior further. The best time to enjoy it is the next morning.

mon_an.mo_ta: Purple sweet potato mooncake is a variation of the traditional mooncake, featuring a crumbly and soft purple sweet potato crust on the outside and a nutty, fragrant lotus seed filling inside. One bite offers a gentle sweetness that still captures the essence of the traditional Mid-Autumn Festival!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Condensed milk or honey - to taste
Blender, steamer, stainless steel sieve, mooncake mold - tools
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for the purple sweet potato mooncakes.
Wash the purple sweet potatoes and peel them completely.
Slice the potatoes into small pieces.
Peel the lotus seeds, remove the bitter germ from the center, and rinse with water to ensure they aren't bitter.
Step 2: Steps to make the purple sweet potato mooncakes.
First, place the potatoes in a steamer or a sticky rice steamer and steam until cooked through.
Next, place the lotus seeds in a pot and add just enough water to cover them. Place on the stove over medium heat and boil until the seeds are soft.
Once the potatoes and lotus seeds are cooked, remove them and let them cool slightly.
Mash the purple potatoes until smooth using a mortar and pestle, a rolling pin, or a fork.
Pass the mashed potato through a stainless steel sieve in small batches to remove any fibers.
After sieving, mix the potato with a little condensed milk or honey according to your preference. Taste as you mix to adjust the sweetness to your liking.
Roll the potato mixture into round balls that fit your mooncake mold.
Place the cooked lotus seeds into a blender along with the white sugar. Blend until completely smooth.
Once the lotus seeds are pureed, pour the mixture into a non-stick pan or pot and place on the stove to cook the paste.
As the lotus seed mixture heats up, turn the heat to very low and stir constantly to prevent burning and to ensure a smooth texture.

When the mixture thickens and dries out slightly, gradually add the cooking oil while stirring so it absorbs into the paste. Continue cooking until the paste is slightly glossy and no longer sticks to your hands.
Once the lotus seed paste is done, transfer to a bowl to cool. Shape the paste into round balls corresponding to the number of potato balls, but make them smaller in size.

Take a potato ball, flatten it in your palm, place a lotus seed ball in the center, and wrap the potato around it. Roll it back into a ball, ensuring the filling is completely enclosed so it won't leak when molded.
Repeat the process until all potato and lotus seed portions are used.
Lightly coat the inside of the mooncake mold with a little oil for easy release.
Place each ball into the mold, press firmly to shape, and release.
Arrange the cakes on a plate and enjoy.
Notes for delicious purple sweet potato mooncakes:
Since the potatoes are naturally sweet and the filling contains sugar, adjust the amount of condensed milk or honey carefully.
For the best results, choose starchy potatoes. They should be fresh with firm, smooth skin and no rot.
You can also use yellow sweet potatoes to add more color to your plate.
For the filling, you can use dried lotus seeds, though they may not be as sweet or creamy as fresh ones. Alternatively, mung bean paste also makes for a delicious filling.

mon_an.mo_ta: Instead of the usual mixed nut filling, enjoy a new and unique flavor with these matcha mooncakes. Let's get baking!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: For the sugar syrup - 1 kg sugar, 600 ml boiling water, 2 lemon slices, 200 g sugar, 50 ml water
For the crust - 200 g mooncake sugar syrup, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 50 g cooking oil, 320 g flour
For the filling - 200 g peeled mung beans, 150 g sugar, 2 tbsp glutinous rice flour, 50 ml cooking oil, 2 tsp matcha powder
Egg wash mixture - 1 egg yolk, 1 tsp water, a few drops of caramel sauce (for color), 1 tsp sesame oil, mixed in a small bowl
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cook the sugar syrup

Place 200 g sugar and 50 ml water in a pot. Heat over medium heat until it turns a caramel color, then pour in 600 ml boiling water. Add 1 kg sugar and lemon slices, bring to a boil, then reduce heat to low and simmer for 30 minutes until slightly thickened. Let it cool, then pour into a clean glass jar. The longer the syrup sits, the better the cakes will be.
Step 2: Make the filling

Wash the mung beans and soak in water for 2 hours to soften. Cook them in a pot like rice, then mash them thoroughly in a mortar or use a blender for speed. Place the beans in a pan with sugar and oil, mix well, and turn on low heat to cook the filling. Stir constantly with a spoon, then add the glutinous rice flour and continue to mix and cook.

Dissolve the matcha powder in 2 tbsp boiling water. When the filling is smooth and no longer sticks to the pan, add the matcha mixture and stir well for another 10 minutes. Let the filling cool slightly, then roll into balls.
Step 3: Make the crust
Mix the sugar syrup and oil in a bowl. Combine the flour and baking soda, then add to the syrup mixture. Mix until smooth and a dough forms. Wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Step 4: Mold the cakes

Divide the crust and filling at a 1:2 ratio (or 2:2 if you prefer a thicker crust). Flatten the crust, place the filling in the center, and wrap it tightly. Lightly brush the mold with oil to prevent sticking.
Place the dough into the mold, press firmly, and release onto a tray.

Bake at 180°C for 7-10 minutes. Remove, spray lightly with water to cool, and brush a thin layer of egg wash on top. Return to the oven for another 7-10 minutes. Repeat this process 3 times in total until the cakes are golden brown.
Remove and let cool. The color will deepen and the flavor will improve after 1-2 days.
Good luck and enjoy your Matcha Mooncakes!

mon_an.mo_ta: Originating from Hong Kong and Singapore, this version of the snowskin mooncake features a delicious three-layer filling. It's not as sweet as traditional snowskin cakes, making it hard to stop at just one! Learn how to make these three-layer mooncakes with this guide.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: For the crust: - Cooked glutinous rice flour (Kao Fen) - 130 g
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pandan water
Wash 8 pandan leaves, cut them into segments, and boil in 1 liter of water for 15-20 minutes.
Turn off the heat and strain the water through a sieve into a bottle or jar. Let it cool.
This pandan water can be stored in the refrigerator for future use.
Step 2: Make the crust
Sift the cooked glutinous rice flour and powdered sugar into a bowl, then add the shortening and mix well.
Gradually add the prepared pandan water (follow the ratio in the ingredients list) and knead until the dough is smooth, elastic, and soft.
Once the dough reaches the desired consistency, divide it into equal portions of about 60 g each and roll them into balls.
Step 3: Make the custard filling
In a large bowl, combine all custard ingredients: egg yolk, sugar, sifted flour, cornstarch, tapioca starch, coconut milk, milk, butter, and yellow food coloring. Whisk until well combined.
Prepare a steamer and steam the mixture for 30 minutes over medium heat.
After 30 minutes, remove the mixture and use a fork to mix and knead until very smooth. Roll into a long log and divide into 35 g portions, then roll into balls like the crust.
Step 4:
Separate the salted egg yolks and steam them for 10 minutes over medium heat, then let them cool.
Step 5:
Divide the pandan lotus seed paste into 50 g portions, roll into balls, and flatten. Do the same with the custard portions.
Place a salted egg yolk in the center of the pandan lotus seed paste and wrap it up. Then place this ball onto the flattened custard filling and wrap it again.
Repeat until all salted egg yolks are used. Refer to the images for clarity.
Step 6:
Roll out the crust dough, place the filling inside, and seal it tightly, ensuring no air is trapped. Coat the outside with a little extra glutinous rice flour to prevent sticking.
Place the balls into the mooncake mold and press down firmly.
Since the dough, lotus seed paste, custard, and salted egg yolks are all pre-cooked, the cakes can be eaten immediately after molding.
Note: For better flavor, refrigerate the cakes overnight. This helps the texture become firmer and more elastic. They can be stored for a week but are best within the first 3 days!

With three layers consisting of a savory salted egg yolk in the center, pandan lotus seed paste in the middle, and rich custard on the outside, this perfect combination is irresistible from the very first bite!

mon_an.mo_ta: You can hand-make these special mooncakes for your loved ones, showing your care and skill through every detail. A cute rabbit-shaped bun is also a wonderful gift idea for children during the Mid-Autumn Festival. This article shares how to make and shape these adorable rabbit buns. Hand-make these cute rabbit buns for your family. Detailed instructions for skillful shaping. A lovely gift for kids during the holiday.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Red beans - as needed (or black beans for the rabbit's eyes)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Knead the dough

Microwave the milk for 2-3 minutes until warm, then dissolve the sugar in it. Let the milk cool completely. Mix the flour and baking powder together, then gradually pour in the milk while kneading until a smooth, non-sticky dough forms. Add the milk slowly to avoid making the dough too wet. Place in a bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and proof for 2-3 hours until doubled in size. Divide the dough into equal small pieces.
Step 2: Shaping

There are two ways to shape the rabbits. Method 1: Roll the dough into a long strip, fold it in half, and coil it. Use scissors to snip the dough to create the feet and mouth, and use the side of the scissors to press and shape the ears. Use red or black beans for the eyes.
Method 2: Take a small amount of dough and form 3 small strips for the ears and tail. Shape the remaining dough into the body, then attach the ears and tail. Press red or black beans in for the eyes.
Step 3: Steam the buns
Place the buns in a steamer and steam for 15-20 minutes until cooked through.
Notes for making rabbit-shaped steamed buns:
Rabbit-shaped buns are a fun and adorable gift for the Mid-Autumn Festival. Here are some tips to ensure success:
Ingredients: Choose high-quality ingredients. Use specialized flour for the crust and soak the red beans long enough so they are soft and easy to work with.

Shaping: When shaping, follow each step carefully. Roll the dough into even balls and ensure the crust is neither too thick nor too thin. Place the filling inside and wrap the dough around it to form the rabbit.

Rabbit details: Create the ears by shaping small, elongated pieces of dough. Use a toothpick to create a line down the center of the ears. Use black beans for the eyes and you can add a small bow for decoration.

Baking/Steaming: If baking, preheat the oven to 180°C. Place the rabbits on a tray lined with parchment paper. Bake for the specified time and check periodically to ensure they are evenly cooked and not burnt. (Note: This recipe primarily uses steaming).
Enjoy: Once the buns are cooked and cooled, enjoy these adorable and delicious rabbit treats with family and friends during the festival.

mon_an.ten: How to make Bánh Dẻo for Mid-Autumn Festival
mon_an.mo_ta: I love eating mooncakes, both the baked and the sticky varieties. However, due to concerns about food safety and hygiene of commercial cakes and a dislike for their overly cloying sweetness, I often prefer to get into the kitchen and make Bánh Dẻo for my family. Here is how to make soft, sweet, and delicious Bánh Dẻo (a type of mooncake) to prepare for the Mid-Autumn Festival.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the mooncake filling

Use mung beans, red beans, lotus seeds, or taro for the filling according to your preference. Steam the filling ingredients until tender, mash them finely, and then stir-fry with sugar to your desired sweetness. Roll the filling into medium-sized balls. If you like salted egg yolks, place one in the center before rolling the filling into a ball.
Step 2: Prepare the crust
Place the crust ingredients in a large tray, mix well, then slowly add water while kneading until the dough forms a cohesive mass.
Divide the dough into small portions and roll them out thinly. Place the prepared filling in the center and wrap the dough around it, rolling it into a ball.
Place the cake into a mold, press firmly to emboss the pattern, then gently tap the mold to remove the cake.

mon_an.ten: Mung bean Bánh Dẻo with fragrant pomelo blossom water
mon_an.mo_ta: This Mid-Autumn Festival, add this easy-to-make mung bean Bánh Dẻo to your recipe collection. It features the wonderful aroma of pomelo blossom water—let's learn how to make it!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Bánh Dẻo flour (cooked glutinous rice flour) - 100g
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, pour the sugar syrup into a bowl, then add 5g of cooking oil and the pomelo blossom water. Mix well.
Step 2:

Gradually add the flour one tablespoon at a time, mixing well until dissolved. Remember to add it spoon by spoon, ensuring each is well incorporated before adding the next to avoid lumps, which would ruin the texture of the crust!
Set aside 2 tablespoons of flour to use for dusting; do not mix it all into the syrup!
Step 3:

When the dough becomes heavy and difficult to stir, move it onto a tray dusted with flour. Spread the dough evenly so it is well-coated. Cover tightly with plastic wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes!
Step 4:
Roll the mung bean filling into balls using a ratio of 2 parts crust to 1 part filling.
Step 5:
Take the rested dough and roll it out thinly. Place the filling inside, roll it into a ball, and coat the outside with a layer of dusting flour.
Dust the mold with flour, place the dough inside, and press to shape. You have almost finished the cake!
Step 6:
Place the cakes in a container and seal tightly. Let them sit until the next day; the cakes will look better and become chewier.
Bánh Dẻo can be kept for 3 to 5 days at moderate temperatures. When eaten, the cake is soft, chewy, and has the characteristic aroma of pomelo blossoms and glutinous rice.

mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to make a unique Mid-Autumn treat with this delicious custard-filled Bánh Dẻo recipe.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the custard filling
Mix all filling ingredients together until very smooth.
Steam the mixture for about 15 minutes until the custard is cooked. Divide into equal portions and roll into balls to use as filling.
Step 2: Prepare the crust

In a bowl, mix the fresh milk, condensed milk, and oil. You can microwave it for 1-2 minutes to fully dissolve the condensed milk. Mix the flours and sugar together first, then slowly add them to the milk mixture, stirring well until the flour is dissolved and no lumps remain.
Place the dough in a steamer and steam for about 15 minutes.
Remove the dough and knead until chewy and smooth. Divide into equal portions and roll out thinly to make the crusts.
Step 3: Assemble and shape the cakes
Place the filling in the center of the crust, wrap it up, and put it into a mold to shape. Remove the cake, and your attractive custard Bánh Dẻo is ready.

mon_an.ten: Green tea Bánh Dẻo with mung bean and lotus seed filling
mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to make green tea Bánh Dẻo with mung bean and lotus seed filling for Mid-Autumn Festival following this recipe.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the filling

Soak the mung beans until soft, steam until tender, and mash finely. Mix the sugar, matcha powder, oil, and Bánh Dẻo flour with the mashed beans. Cook the mixture over low heat, stirring constantly, until the paste doesn't stick to your finger when touched lightly. Turn off the heat and let it cool completely. Once the mung bean paste has turned a dark green, mix in the candied lotus seeds. Divide into 4 equal balls for the filling.
Step 2: Prepare the crust

Boil the sugar and water, stirring until the sugar dissolves, then add 1/2 tsp of lemon juice. Add the matcha powder and pomelo blossom water, stirring well. Gradually add the flour and knead into a uniform, lump-free dough. Let the dough rest for 20 minutes, then knead until smooth. Divide the dough into 4 portions for the crust. Roll into balls and flatten.
Step 3: Assemble the cakes
