Place the filling in the center of the dough, wrap it, and roll into a ball. Dust the mold with a little flour, insert the cake, and press to shape. Gently tap the mold to release the cake. You now have beautiful green tea Bánh Dẻo.
Here is the final product. It looks delicious, doesn't it? ^^

mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to make Mid-Autumn mooncakes with Món Ngon Dễ Làm. Today's dish is a fragrant and eye-catching steamed Bánh Dẻo. Let's get started to prepare for the Mid-Autumn Festival.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Sugar - To taste for desired sweetness
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the mooncake filling

Sort and rinse the mung beans or lotus seeds. Steam until tender, then mash finely. Mix in sugar to your desired sweetness and roll into small balls. You can adjust the size of the balls depending on how big you want your cakes to be.
Step 2: Make the mooncakes

Mix all the crust ingredients together, then slowly add water and mix until the dough no longer sticks to your hands. You can color the cakes naturally using pandan juice, matcha powder, wine, or other natural coloring agents instead of harmful food dyes.
Roll the dough into balls and flatten them. Place the filling in the center, wrap it up, and roll back into a ball.
Place the cake into a mold and press to shape.
Steam the cakes until cooked. You now have a unique and delicious steamed Bánh Dẻo.
Once steamed, place the finished cakes on a tray for a beautiful and elegant presentation. They look just like cakes bought from famous bakeries or large hotels, and the flavor is just as wonderful.

mon_an.ten: How to make cute pig-shaped mooncakes
mon_an.mo_ta: Mid-Autumn is a time for family gatherings around a table filled with fragrant fruits and indispensable mooncakes. For a simple, time-saving version that kids will love, try making these adorable pig-shaped mooncakes! The steps are easy and won't take much of your time!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 50g Bánh Dẻo flour + 70ml oil - mixed together in a bowl
cac_buoc: How to make the filling:

Step 1: Soak the mung beans in water for at least 3 hours (the longer you soak, the softer they become when cooked). Rinse the beans thoroughly. Place the beans in a steamer with 700ml of cold water and salt, and cook over medium heat. When the water has mostly evaporated, cover and cook until the beans are tender. Once the water is gone and the beans are thick and pasty, turn off the heat.
Step 2: While the beans are still hot, blend them with sugar until smooth.

Step 3: Transfer the pureed beans to a non-stick pan with 80ml of oil. Cook and stir for 15 minutes. Add the bowl of flour and oil mixture and continue stirring until the paste forms a cohesive mass that doesn't stick to the pan. Let the filling cool completely, then roll into small balls.
Mung bean filling is typically cooked for about 40 minutes.
How to make cute pig-shaped mooncake crusts:
Step 1: In a large bowl, mix the sugar syrup, oil, maltose, and eggs until dissolved.

Step 2: Place the flour in a large bowl, make a well in the center, and pour in the syrup mixture. Knead until the dough is smooth and pliable. To check if it's ready, pull the dough; it should stretch without breaking immediately. Cover with plastic wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Dividing the filling and dough:
Divide the filling and dough into equal portions: 50g of dough and 50g of filling per cake.
Step 1: Wrap the dough around the filling and roll into a ball.
Step 2: Attach two red beans to make the eyes. Roll a small piece of dough, flatten it, and attach it below the eyes for the snout.
Step 3: Take another small piece of dough, roll it into a ball, then pinch one end to make a pointed ear. Attach the ears above the eyes.
Step 4: Use the tip of a chopstick to poke two holes in the snout.
Step 5: Preheat the oven to 210°C with top and bottom heat for 10 minutes. Place the tray on the middle rack and bake for 5 minutes. Remove the tray and brush the egg wash over the cakes.

Step 6: Return the tray to the oven and bake for another 6 minutes at 200°C. Remove, apply another layer of egg wash for a better color, and bake for a final 6 minutes. After that, turn on the top heat only for 1-2 minutes to finish.
Notes:
Watch carefully when using the top heat to prevent burning.
When cooking the mung bean paste, ensure it doesn't burn or become too dry, which could ruin the cake.
Baking and brushing times may vary by 1-2 minutes depending on the size of your cakes.
Egg wash mixture:
Lightly beat one egg yolk with 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp water, 1/2 tsp caramel sauce, and 1 drop of yellow food coloring.

mon_an.mo_ta: Mooncakes are a favorite for almost everyone, especially children. This year, mothers can hand-make baked mooncakes for their kids using this fun-shaped recipe. Moving away from traditional designs, mooncakes shaped like rabbits, cars, or fish will delight anyone who sees them. These are baked cakes with a mild mung bean filling, so you can enjoy many without getting tired of them. The process is very easy, so give it a try.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Bánh Dẻo flour or tapioca starch - 10g
Blender, mini rice molds (rabbit, car, fish, etc.), pastry brush - tools
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Crack the egg and separate the yolk. Mix the yolk with the caramel sauce and water, then beat well.
Soak the mung beans in water until they expand, then rinse thoroughly.
Step 2: Cooking process
The Filling
First, place the mung beans in a pot and add enough water to double the volume of the beans. Bring to a boil over high heat.

Once boiling, reduce the heat to low to prevent overflowing and skim off any foam. Check if the beans are soft by pressing one against the side of the pot; if it mashes easily, turn off the heat. Keep the lid on for a while longer.
Transfer the beans to a bowl to cool.
Once cooled, blend the beans in a blender until smooth. Pour the puree into a pot and place it on the stove to cook the paste.
During this process, keep the heat low and stir constantly to prevent the beans from burning.
Add the white sugar to the pot and stir well.
When the moisture has reduced, transfer the paste to a non-stick pan. Place over low heat and continue stirring.
Slowly add the cooking oil and stir until it is fully absorbed into the beans.
Continue stirring until the paste thickens, then add the Bánh Dẻo flour or tapioca starch.
Stir for a few more minutes until the starch is cooked, then turn off the heat. Continue stirring for a bit longer to make the paste very smooth and let it cool slightly.
Once the filling has cooled, roll it into several small balls.
The Crust
First, place the flour in a bowl and create a well in the center.
Pour the sugar syrup, lye water, and oil into the well.
Knead the dough thoroughly until it is uniform, smooth, and pliable.
Divide the dough into small portions that correspond to the number of filling balls, making the dough portions slightly larger. Roll them into balls.

Take a piece of dough, roll it out or flatten it in your hand, place a filling ball in the center, and roll it back into a ball. Ensure the dough tightly encloses the filling so it doesn't break during molding.
Repeat until all dough and filling are used.
Divide the cakes and place them into various molds to create fun shapes.
Place the cakes on parchment paper (do not crowd them) and put them into an oven preheated to 230°C.
Bake for 10 minutes or until the crust turns opaque. Remove from the oven and let cool, then use a brush to apply a thin layer of egg wash.
Once the egg wash has set, bake for another 10 minutes, then turn off the oven and remove the cakes.
The longer you leave the cakes, the softer they become and the better the color develops.
Notes
Filling: Cooking the paste takes a long time and requires patience as the stirring can be tiring.
The mung bean paste should be shiny, pliable, and thick—not dry, but slightly moist.
If you are not using the filling immediately, cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap to prevent it from drying out. This method can also be used for red beans or lotus seeds.
Adjust the temperature and time according to your specific oven. Remember to preheat the oven before you start so you don't have to wait.

mon_an.mo_ta: Many people think mooncakes must be baked or sticky and that an oven is essential for that golden, crispy finish. Try something new with these purple sweet potato mooncakes—delicious, sweet, beautiful, and no oven required.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Honey or condensed milk - To taste
cac_buoc: Step 1: Boil or steam the sweet potatoes until tender (you can also microwave them for speed). Peel and cut into small pieces.

Step 2: Gradually pass the sweet potato through a fine-mesh sieve, using a spoon to mash it until smooth. Scrape the mash from the bottom of the sieve to get a fine, uniform purple sweet potato flour. Add condensed milk or honey to the mash and mix well to create a soft, sticky mixture with the right amount of sweetness.
Step 3: Finally, press the mixture into a mooncake mold to shape it, then gently remove. You now have stunning purple sweet potato mooncakes.
When serving, sprinkle some crushed roasted peanuts or cashews over the cakes.
Tips for delicious purple sweet potato mooncakes:

Besides boiling or steaming, you can cook the potatoes in the microwave. I usually microwave them at the highest power for about 5 minutes, flip them, and cook for another 4-5 minutes. Test with a chopstick; if it slides through easily, they are done. This method is very tasty and saves the effort of boiling/steaming. ^^
The version I made is without filling. If you like, you can add mung bean or lotus seed filling to make them more like traditional mooncakes.

mon_an.ten: Purple sweet potato mooncakes with lotus seed filling
mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to make purple sweet potato mooncakes with lotus seed filling with Món Ngon Dễ Làm.
cac_buoc: Wash the lotus seeds, remove the skin and embryos, then stew until tender. Blend them with sugar until smooth, then transfer to a large pan. Cook over low heat until the paste thickens, then add the oil, stir well, and turn off the heat.
Steam the purple sweet potatoes, peel, and cut into small pieces. Pass them through a sieve to mash finely. You can mix in a little condensed milk to make the crust smooth and pliable.

Divide the sweet potato crust and the lotus seed filling into equal portions (ensure you have the same number of each :P). Flatten the crust, place the filling in the center, wrap it up, and press into a mold to shape. Your purple sweet potato mooncakes with lotus seed filling are done.
Here is the final product.

mon_an.mo_ta: Instead of buying from a store, you can hand-make mooncakes at home to treat your kids and family, or to give as gifts to relatives and friends. Learn how to make custard mooncakes following the instructions below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: For the custard filling - 18g all-purpose flour + 32g cornstarch + 2 medium eggs + 18ml condensed milk + 135ml fresh milk + 30g sugar + 30g melted butter + ½ tsp vanilla extract
For the egg wash - 1 egg yolk beaten with ½ egg white
cac_buoc: Step 1: First, let's start with the mooncake filling!
Sift the cornstarch into a clean bowl.
In a medium bowl, combine the sugar, condensed milk, and fresh milk. Stir well until the sugar and condensed milk are fully dissolved into a thin liquid.
Next, add the eggs to the bowl and beat well. You can use an electric mixer or a hand whisk. Add the sifted cornstarch and beat, then add the milk mixture and beat everything together.

Strain the mixture through a sieve into a pot. Place on the stove and stir constantly over low heat until the mixture thickens into an egg custard. Turn off the heat, remove from the stove, and let it cool.
Once the custard has cooled, roll into small balls of about 35g each. Continue until all the custard is used.
Step 2: After finishing the delicious filling, we move on to the crust.
Sift the all-purpose flour into a clean bowl.
Add all remaining crust ingredients: sugar syrup, oil, egg yolk, and peanut butter according to the ratios listed. Mix until the dough is smooth and pliable, then cover with plastic wrap.
Wrapping is essential to keep the dough from drying out. Let it rest for 30-45 minutes.
Step 3: We have completed the filling and the crust, the two most important parts. Now for the final step: shaping and baking. Let's begin!
Prepare your mooncake molds. Use a small brush to apply a very thin layer of oil (very thin!) inside the mold.

Proceed to assemble the cakes. Typically, the filling should be twice the weight of the crust. For a 75g mold, use 50g of filling and 25g of crust. If your child prefers more crust, you can use 40g of filling and 35g of crust.

Roll the crust dough out very thinly and evenly. Place a custard ball from Step 1 in the center. Wrap the dough around the filling, smoothing it as you go to ensure no air is trapped between the filling and the crust!
Place the assembled cake into the mold. Press firmly and evenly so the cake takes the shape of the mold, then release it onto a tray lined with parchment paper.
Preheat the oven to 180°C for 20 minutes. Place the tray on the middle rack and bake with top and bottom heat for 10 minutes.
After 10 minutes, remove the cakes and brush the egg wash over the top and sides. Use a small brush to apply it evenly; be careful not to leave bubbles, as they will burn. Bake for another 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, apply a second layer of egg wash and bake for a final 5 minutes. This step gives the cakes a beautiful golden color.

Finally, remove the cakes and place them on a plate. When first removed, the crust will feel very hard—don't worry. Just let them cool for a few hours and they will soften. You can then enjoy them or package them as gifts.
It's not too difficult to make mooncakes for your kids, family, and friends this Mid-Autumn Festival!

mon_an.mo_ta: Mid-Autumn Festival is just around the corner. Quickly buy your ingredients to make mooncakes; check out this recipe for delicious baked taro mooncakes!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Syrup - 1kg sugar, 600ml boiling water, 2 lemon slices and 200g sugar, 50ml water
Dough - 200g syrup, 1/4 tsp baking soda, 50g cooking oil, 320g all-purpose flour
Filling - 1 taro root (peeled, washed, and cut into chunks), 1 tbsp glutinous rice flour, 150g sugar, 50ml cooking oil
Egg wash - 1 egg yolk, 1 tsp sesame oil, 1 tsp water, a few drops of caramel coloring mixed in a small bowl
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cook the syrup

Add 200g sugar and 50ml water to a pot. Cook over medium heat until the syrup turns a caramel color, then pour in 600ml boiling water. Add the remaining sugar and lemon slices, bring to a boil, then reduce to low heat. Simmer for 30 minutes until the syrup is slightly thickened, then turn off the heat and let cool.
Step 2: Make the filling
Place the taro and water in a pot and cook until the taro is soft.
Blend the taro, sugar, and cooking oil until smooth and fine.

Transfer the taro to a pan and stir-fry over low heat. Stir constantly, then add the glutinous rice flour and mix well. Stir-fry until the filling is smooth, pliable, and non-stick, then turn off the heat. Let it cool slightly, divide into equal portions, and roll into balls.
Step 3: Make the dough

Mix the syrup and cooking oil in a bowl. Combine the flour and baking soda, then add the flour to the syrup mixture. Mix well until the dough is smooth and forms a single mass. Wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes.
Step 4: Shape and bake

Divide the dough and filling at a 1:2 ratio. Roll out a piece of dough, place the filling in the center, and wrap it tightly so the dough covers the filling completely. Brush a thin layer of oil on the mold to prevent sticking. Press the dough into the mold firmly, rotating to ensure even patterns, then gently remove the cake.

Place the cakes on a baking tray at 180°C. Bake for 7-10 minutes, then remove and spray a little water on the cakes to cool them down. Brush a thin layer of egg wash on the surface and bake for another 7-10 minutes. Repeat this process 3 times until the cakes are golden brown.
Remove the baked taro mooncakes and let them cool. Store in an airtight container or bag. After 1-2 days, the cakes will develop a deeper color and taste better than when freshly baked!
Good luck and enjoy your homemade taro mooncakes!

mon_an.ten: Jelly Mooncakes with Salted Egg Yolk
mon_an.mo_ta: The Mid-Autumn Festival, a time for reunion and family, is approaching. On this occasion, show off your skills by making jelly mooncakes with salted egg yolk for the whole family to enjoy and strengthen family bonds. Homemade mooncakes are delicious, safe, and healthy. Let's learn how to make them! Ingredients for jelly mooncakes with salted egg yolk:
cac_buoc: 1. Mooncake filling:
Peeled mung beans
Red beans
Matcha powder (about 1 tsp)
Sugar, cooking oil
Salted egg yolks
2. Mooncake shell:
Agar-agar powder (2 packs of 25g)
Condensed milk
A bowl of thick coconut milk
Syrup of your choice (strawberry, orange, mint...)
Coffee or cocoa powder
Plastic mooncake molds
Steps to make jelly mooncakes with salted egg yolk:
1. How to make the filling:
Soak the mung beans for about 4 hours until they expand.
Soak the red beans overnight, or for 5 hours in hot water if you are in a hurry.
Steam the mung beans until soft, or cook them in a rice cooker with slightly less water than usual.
Once the mung beans are soft, mash them until smooth.

Place half of the mashed mung beans, cooking oil, and sugar in a pan over low heat. Stir the mixture constantly. If the beans seem dry, add a little more oil. Stir until the beans look glossy and do not stick to your hands. Remove to a plate and let cool.
Prepare the remaining mung beans in the same way but add matcha powder.
Simmer the red beans until soft, drain well, and blend until smooth. Stir-fry with sugar just like the mung beans. Remove the red bean paste to a plate.
Steam the salted egg yolks until cooked.
Wrap the mung bean paste around the salted egg yolks. Shape into balls or squares depending on your mold.
Do not add salted egg yolks to the matcha and red bean fillings.
2. How to make the jelly shell:

Use about 2 liters of water for 25g of agar-agar powder. Place the pot on the stove and stir constantly until it has boiled for 10 minutes, then turn off the heat. You must work quickly before the jelly sets. Keep the stove on very low heat if needed.
3. How to assemble the mooncakes:
Mix a little jelly with the syrup, sweeten to taste, and pour a thin layer into the mold. Place in front of a fan.
Wait for the surface of the jelly in the mold to set slightly, then place the filling inside.
Mix more jelly with some milk and coconut milk, then pour into the mold.
While waiting for that layer to set, mix coffee or cocoa and condensed milk with more jelly and continue pouring into the mold.
Repeat the layering process until the mold is full.
Let the jelly cool completely before removing from the mold.
Store the jelly mooncakes in the refrigerator.
Serve chilled.
And that's it, we have finished the jelly mooncakes with salted egg yolk!

mon_an.mo_ta: If you are tired of traditional mooncake fillings, head to the kitchen and try making these delicious jelly mooncakes. With attractive colors and great flavor inside and out, the process is simple and definitely won't disappoint you.
cac_buoc: Step 1:

First, prepare a mooncake mold. Then, select round-bottomed plastic cups that are slightly smaller than the interior of the mold. These cups should be somewhat thick, as thin ones may break during the process.
Step 2:

Cut the fresh grass jelly into small strips about 4 cm long and knot the pandan leaves. Add the pandan leaves to a pot of water where the sugar and agar-agar have been dissolved, and cook over medium heat.
While cooking the pandan leaves, remember to stir constantly. Once the mixture boils, turn off the heat and remove the pandan leaves.
Step 3:

In this step, add the cut grass jelly to the pot and stir with a spoon for a few minutes so the jelly absorbs the liquid and flavor. Once the mixture is fully combined, pour it into the small cups to form the filling.
Step 4:

Let the grass jelly cups cool for a while, then place them in the refrigerator until completely firm. This grass jelly part must be very firm because it is the filling. If it is too soft, the filling will leak and the cake won't be good.
Once the grass jelly is firm, remove it from the cups onto a plate. Use a knife to lightly score the surface so the filling and shell will stick together better later.
Step 5:

Mix all the shell ingredients: 500 ml soy milk, 125 ml fresh milk, 45g sugar, and 10g agar-agar powder in a pot and bring to a boil over medium heat. Remember to stir constantly so the sugar dissolves and the mixture blends without burning or clumping!
Step 6:
After finishing the soy milk jelly mixture, let it cool slightly and then pour it into half of the prepared mooncake molds.
Step 7:
Wait for this shell layer to set slightly and become firm (no longer liquid), then gently place the grass jelly filling in the center.
Step 8:
Finally, pour the remaining soy milk mixture to fill the mold and place it in the refrigerator until set.
Notes:
When cutting the grass jelly, you should cut small, medium-length pieces. If the pieces are too large, the mixture will be difficult to set and won't be even.
Pay attention to the time the grass jelly spends in the fridge. If the time is too short, it won't be firm enough; if it's too long, the jelly will become too hard and won't taste good.
When boiling the milk mixture with sugar and agar-agar, remember to stir constantly and continuously so the mixture blends well, doesn't clump, and doesn't burn at the bottom of the pot.
Remember to wait for the soy milk to set a bit before adding the grass jelly filling; if you add it too early, the filling will sink and ruin the cake's appearance.

mon_an.mo_ta: These rainbow mooncakes are unique, beautiful, and delicious. They are very easy to make—get your ingredients ready!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Water dough (makes 6 cakes): 20g softened butter; 120g all-purpose flour; 40ml water; 40ml oil
Oil dough: 80g all-purpose flour; 50ml cooking oil. Add food coloring to this portion.
Taro filling (or any filling you prefer): 300g taro; 60g sugar; 60g mooncake syrup; 30g glutinous rice flour + 40ml oil mixed in a bowl.
cac_buoc: Step 1: MAKE THE FILLING

Peel, wash, and slice the taro, then steam or boil until cooked. Blend the hot cooked taro with sugar until smooth. Pour the taro into a non-stick pan along with the oil-flour mixture and mooncake syrup. Stir-fry over medium heat for about 15 minutes.
Reduce the heat and continue stir-frying until the filling forms a mass that doesn't stick to the pan, then turn off the heat. Once the filling has cooled, roll into 80g balls.
Step 2: MAKE THE WATER DOUGH
Place all ingredients in a bowl and knead until the dough is smooth and pliable.
After kneading, let the dough rest for 30 minutes. Then divide into 2 portions.
Step 3: MAKE THE OIL DOUGH

Mix the flour and oil in a bowl and knead into a mass. Divide the dough into 4 portions and add food coloring, then let rest for 30 minutes. Cut each colored portion in half and roll into balls (8 balls total).
Step 4: LAMINATE AND SHAPE
Flatten a portion of the water dough slightly. Place 4 small colored oil dough balls inside. Seal the edges and roll into a ball.
Roll the dough out into a long strip, then roll it up from the edge. Roll it out lengthwise once more, roll it up again, and cut in half.
Place the cut side down on the table, roll the dough into a circle, and place the filling in the center. Place the dough in your palm and gently seal the edges.
Arrange the cakes on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Preheat the oven to 150-160°C for 15 minutes. Place the tray one level below the middle rack and bake for 30-35 minutes.
To check if the cakes are done, look at the bottom. If it is dry and golden, they are ready.

mon_an.mo_ta: Matcha snowskin mooncakes are a delicious highlight of this Mid-Autumn season, featuring soft, crumbly mung bean filling and a fragrant crust that is perfectly sweet while retaining the true taste of matcha. With attractive colors and easy-to-find ingredients, it won't be hard for you to make and enjoy them to the last bite!
cac_buoc: How to make matcha snowskin mooncakes for the Mid-Autumn Festival

Step 1: First, soak the mung beans in water for 3-4 hours until they expand (the longer you soak, the softer they become). Drain the beans and steam them for 5-10 minutes or until they are cooked, soft, and fragrant.

Step 2: Next, place the cooked mung beans in a bowl and blend until smooth. Add 100g sugar and 2 tbsp matcha powder. Mix the mixture well so the ingredients are evenly flavored and have a beautiful green color. Place a pan on the stove and stir-fry the matcha mung bean mixture, pressing down until it thickens, then remove and let cool.
Step 3: Once the mixture has cooled, take a small amount and shape into balls weighing about 75g each.
Step 4: Next, bring a pot of water to a boil with the remaining sugar. Once boiling, add the matcha powder and stir constantly until the mixture is smooth, thick, and soft, then turn off the heat.
Step 5: Continue kneading the mixture until very smooth, then gradually add the syrup. Keep kneading until the dough no longer sticks to your hands.
Step 6: Divide the dough into small portions, flatten them into circles, and wrap them around the prepared matcha mung bean filling. Roll into balls and place them into the mooncake molds.
Step 7: Finally, after shaping the cakes, remove them from the molds and enjoy.
Tips for delicious and attractive matcha snowskin mooncakes

When stir-frying the mung bean filling, remember to use a non-stick pan and stir constantly so the mixture doesn't burn and remains smooth. Besides mung beans, you can do the same with red beans for a delicious and unique cake.
You can leave the mung bean filling plain without matcha to create two beautiful colors for the cake.
When making the dough, use a moderate amount of matcha; too much will make the cake too dark and bitter.
When shaping the cakes, ensure the dough completely covers the filling so the mung beans don't fall out. Press firmly into the mold so the cake keeps its shape and attractive appearance.

Matcha snowskin mooncakes are a delicious highlight of this Mid-Autumn season, featuring soft, crumbly mung bean filling and a fragrant crust that is perfectly sweet while retaining the true taste of matcha. With attractive colors and easy-to-find ingredients, it won't be hard for you to make and enjoy them to the last bite!

mon_an.mo_ta: Do you want to make meaningful homemade mooncakes for your loved ones and friends? It's not difficult if you take the time to learn. Pandan mung bean snowskin mooncakes, with their soothing green color and easy process, are a great choice for home baking. Let's learn how to make them.
cac_buoc: Prepare ingredients
Finely chop the candied winter melon.
Soak the mung beans for 3 hours to absorb water and expand, then wash thoroughly.
Prepare the mooncake molds and dust them with dry glutinous rice flour to prevent sticking.
Steps
Filling:
Step 1: Place the soaked and washed mung beans in a pot with 600ml water. Cook over medium heat, skimming off any foam so the beans are clean and flavorful.
Cook until the water has mostly evaporated, then cover and simmer until the beans are soft.
Step 2: Once the beans are cooked, blend them with sugar in a blender until smooth.

Mix the mung beans with the flour and oil. Transfer to a non-stick pan and stir-fry over medium heat until the filling forms a mass that doesn't stick to the pan. Add the candied winter melon, stir-fry for a bit longer, then turn off the heat.
Step 3: Let the filling cool slightly, then roll into equal-sized balls. (Do not make the filling balls too large, or the cake will lose its balance between filling and dough).
Dough:
Step 4: Combine the syrup, oil, pandan essence, and grapefruit flower water. Gradually whisk in the flour. Add the flour in small amounts to avoid clumping.
Knead the dough thoroughly until it is smooth, well-combined, and doesn't stick to the bowl. Once mixed, wrap the dough tightly and let it rest overnight or for 6 hours to expand.

Step 5: Take the rested dough and divide it into portions so that the dough is twice the weight of the filling. Place the filling in the center of the dough and roll into a ball, ensuring there is no excess air.
Step 6: Molding:
Place the ball into the mold, press firmly at all corners, then tap gently to remove the cake. The finished cake will have a beautiful shape, attractive color, and a soft texture.
Notes:
When stir-frying the mung beans, remember to stir constantly so the filling is well-combined and doesn't burn.
Resting the dough is essential as it helps the dough expand and prevents it from losing its shape or detail after molding. Rest it as long as possible, at least 6 hours.
After finishing, you can wrap the pandan snowskin mooncakes in plastic wrap or place them in beautiful bags or boxes as gifts.
The finished cakes have an attractive light green pandan color, a soft crust, and an inviting aroma.

mon_an.mo_ta: Mid-Autumn is coming! Learn how to make traditional mung bean baked mooncakes with this extremely easy recipe!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 2 tbsp Mai Que Lo rice wine
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the dough. Mix 200g baked mooncake syrup, 50ml vegetable oil, 1 tsp peanut butter, 1 egg yolk, and 2 tbsp Mai Que Lo wine together and let rest for 15 minutes. Sift the flour and mix with the liquid ingredients. Knead until smooth; do not over-knead. Let the dough rest for another 30 minutes before molding.
Step 2: Roll the pre-made mung bean filling into equal balls using a ratio of 2 parts filling to 1 part dough.
Step 3: Flatten the dough, place the filling in the center, roll into a ball, and press into the mold to create the pattern.
Step 4: Preheat the oven for 15 minutes at 180°C with both top and bottom heat. Arrange the cakes on a tray lined with parchment paper and bake in two stages.

For the first stage, bake for 20 minutes. Remove and let cool, then brush the surface with a mixture of egg yolk, fresh milk, a bit of sesame oil, and a bit of water. For the second stage, bake for another 10 minutes, then remove and let cool completely before boxing. After 1 to 2 days, the cakes will develop a beautiful color, soften, and taste delicious.
Good luck with these attractive mung bean baked mooncakes for a meaningful festival!

mon_an.mo_ta: Mid-Autumn Festival reminds us of delicious baked mooncakes, an essential treat for the occasion. Instead of buying them, you can make them at home for your family to enjoy!
cac_buoc: Step 1: First, we will make the custard filling.
Sift the all-purpose flour, cornstarch, and custard powder into a large bowl.
In another bowl, cream the butter and sugar until light in color. While beating, gradually add the prepared egg yolks and mix until completely incorporated.
Step 2:
Next, add the heavy cream, coconut milk, and condensed milk to the bowl and mix well.
Sift the flour mixture into the wet ingredients and mix until it looks like the mixture in the photo.
Step 3:
Prepare a steamer and steam the mixture for 25 minutes over medium heat. Note: every 5 minutes, use a spoon to stir the mixture.
Once finished, turn off the heat and let the filling cool slightly.
Step 4:
Using clean gloves, knead the filling while it is still warm until very soft. Wrap the custard filling and refrigerate for 1 hour.
You can keep the filling in the refrigerator for up to a week if you are busy or want to make multiple batches.
Step 5:
In another bowl, whisk 1 egg yolk with 15ml milk and strain the mixture to remove any lumps.
Use a brush to apply this egg wash to the cakes.
Step 6: Now we move on to the dough.
Cream the butter and sugar in a bowl until light, then add the egg yolk and continue beating until fully combined.
Step 7:
Sift in the flour, custard powder, and baking powder. Mix well and knead by hand to form a dough. Wrap and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Step 8:
After 1 hour, take out the filling and the dough. Roll the filling into 20g balls and the dough into 35g balls. Keep them separate so they don't get mixed up!
Step 9:
Now we shape the cakes. Place a piece of dough in your hand and flatten it. Place a custard filling ball in the center and wrap it tightly so no air is trapped between the filling and the dough.
Step 10:
Dust the mold with flour, insert the cake ball, and press down to shape.
Step 11:

Preheat the oven to 175°C. Brush a layer of egg wash on the cakes and bake for 25 minutes. Do not remove the cakes immediately after 25 minutes or they may be hard; leave them in the oven for 10 minutes before taking them out.
And that's it—we've finished these wonderful mooncakes. It's so easy to have a perfect treat.
The golden crust wraps around a smooth, delicious custard filling, creating a wonderful flavor!

mon_an.mo_ta: Have you ever tried baked mooncakes with purple sweet potato filling? They are beautiful and incredibly delicious. Let's start making these special mooncakes right away!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Make the dough

Mix 200g baked mooncake syrup, 0.3g baking soda, 1 egg yolk, 1 tbsp peanut butter, 2 tbsp Mai Que Lo wine, and 40ml oil. Let the mixture rest for 30 minutes, then sift in 320g flour and knead until smooth. Let the dough rest for another 30 minutes before wrapping the filling and molding.
Step 2: Make the filling
Peel and wash the purple sweet potato, drain, cut into chunks, and steam until cooked.
Place the potato in a blender with sugar and unsweetened milk and blend until smooth.
Strain the blended potato through a sieve for a fine texture, then place it in a pan on the stove with a little oil. Stir constantly.
When the potato starts to feel heavy, continue stirring until it no longer sticks to your hands.
Let the filling cool, then roll into balls using a ratio of 2 parts filling to 1 part dough. In this recipe, the filling balls are 100g.
Step 3: Molding
Using a 150g mold, take 50g of dough and 100g of filling. Flatten the dough, place the filling in the center, roll into a ball, and place into the mold.
Press firmly and evenly, then place on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Step 4: Baking
Preheat the oven for 15 minutes at 180°C. Bake the cakes with both top and bottom heat for 20 minutes.
When the timer goes off, remove the cakes, spray with water, and let cool before brushing with the egg wash (a mixture of egg yolk, oil, and water). Bake a second time for 10 to 15 minutes at 170°C.
Step 5: Let the cakes cool completely before boxing. After 1 to 2 days, the color will deepen and the cakes will become soft.
Good luck and enjoy your purple sweet potato baked mooncakes!

mon_an.ten: Matcha Mooncakes with Salted Egg Yolk
mon_an.mo_ta: Matcha mooncakes with salted egg yolk appeal to everyone with their striking golden appearance and fragrant aroma. The salted egg yolk provides a savory touch that turns sweet on the palate, perfectly balanced by the fragrant matcha and rich mung bean paste.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Make the matcha filling
First, mix the matcha powder with the syrup and 200ml boiling water. Stir well to avoid lumps and ensure everything is combined. Cook the mixture until it softens.
Soak the peeled mung beans for 3-4 hours and drain. Steam the beans until soft. Once cooked, remove and let cool slightly.
Use a blender to blend the cooked beans until smooth.

Place a pan on the stove and strain the beans into the pan through a sieve. Add the oil and mix well. Add the matcha mixture and stir. After 45 minutes, add the cornstarch mixed with water and stir-fry for another 20 minutes, then turn off the heat. Use low or medium heat to prevent burning.
Once the mixture is finished, divide into filling portions of about 75g each and roll into balls.
Flatten a matcha filling ball, place a salted egg yolk in the center, and roll it back into a ball. Be careful not to let the egg yolk show, or the cake will be too salty.
Step 2: Make the dough
Sift the flour until fine, then mix with the syrup and add one egg yolk. Mix well until the ingredients are combined and the dough is soft and pliable.
Divide the dough into nine 50g portions and refrigerate for 1-2 hours to firm up.
Step 3: Shape the cakes
Flatten a piece of dough into a circle, place the filling inside, and roll into a ball.
Ensure the ball is perfectly round and place it into the mold.
Place the cake in the mold so the bottom is level and press down firmly on the surface.
Step 4: Baking
Preheat the oven for 15 minutes at 185°C.

Once hot, place the tray on the middle rack and bake for 5 minutes. Remove and spray with a fine mist of water. Let rest for 2-3 minutes, then brush with a thin layer of egg wash (use a fine brush and apply thinly).
Return the tray to the oven for 6 minutes. Remove, repeat the water misting and egg wash. Finally, bake for another 6 minutes until done.
Once cooked, remove the cakes, arrange on a plate, slice into bite-sized pieces, and enjoy.

Matcha mooncakes with salted egg yolk appeal to everyone with their striking golden appearance and fragrant aroma. The salted egg yolk provides a savory touch that turns sweet on the palate, perfectly balanced by the fragrant matcha and rich mung bean paste. All blend together to create a wonderful cake.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Shaping Mooncake Fillings Correctly
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for shaping mooncake fillings correctly so they do not leak or deform after baking, helping you fully enjoy the form and flavor of the mooncakes.
cac_buoc: How to divide the filling and dough proportionally:
For a standard baked mooncake, the crust accounts for 1/4 of the total weight. For example, if the cake weighs 50g, the crust will weigh about 12g and the filling will weigh 38g.
If you use salted egg yolks in the filling, you must include the weight of the salted egg yolk in the total filling weight.
If the filling leaks or deforms after baking, it is because air was trapped inside during the shaping process.
Therefore, here is the method to prevent air from getting trapped, ensuring the filling doesn't leak or deform so you can enjoy both the appearance and taste. Let's get started!
Step 1:
Roll the filling into a ball, then use your thumb to press a small indentation in the center.
Step 2:
Next, place the salted egg yolk in the center. If you are using only half a salted egg yolk, place the cut side facing up; if placed face down, more air will be trapped inside the filling.
Step 3:
Then, use your thumb to gently press the salted egg yolk into the filling, then smooth the filling from the bottom up to fully enclose the yolk.
Roll the filling into a smooth ball as in step 1.
Step 4:
Roll the dough into a ball similar to the filling, then use your palm to flatten it.
Step 5:
Sprinkle a little tapioca starch on both sides of the dough and use a rolling pin to roll it out thinly.
Note: Roll the dough in a cross pattern to keep it circular, and stop when the dough is large enough to cover 2/3 of the filling ball.
Step 6:
Place the filling ball in the center of the rolled-out dough.
Step 7:
Unlike the salted egg yolk step, do the opposite for the crust. Turn the dough over and smooth it from top to bottom so the crust tightly hugs the filling, leaving no room for air.
Step 8:
Continue smoothing the crust until it completely covers the entire filling.
Step 9:
Use a brush to apply a thin layer of cooking oil to the mold so the cake doesn't stick and the crust comes out smooth and beautiful.
Step 10:
Rub a little tapioca starch evenly over the shaped cake.
Step 11:
Place the cake neatly into the mold, with the smoothest side facing down.
Step 12:
Quickly press the mold firmly to release the cake.
Then bake the cake at 200°C for 7 minutes.
Remove the cake and spray with water, let it dry for 10 minutes, then bake for another 7 minutes. Spraying water prevents the crust from drying out and cracking during baking.
At this point, the surface will be slightly golden; spray with water again and let dry. Then, brush with egg wash and bake for another 5 minutes.
After baking, let the cakes rest for 1-3 days before enjoying!
With this shaping secret, you won't have to worry about the filling leaking or deforming, and you'll have perfectly delicious baked mooncakes.

mon_an.ten: Sweet and Fragrant Carrot Steamed Buns
mon_an.mo_ta: Sweet and fragrant carrot steamed buns with a unique crust mixed with nutritious carrot juice. Learn to cook delicious Sweet and Fragrant Carrot Steamed Buns.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Sesame oil, salt, sugar, seasoning powder
cac_buoc: Sweet and Fragrant Carrot Steamed Buns
Step 1: Warm the carrot juice and dissolve 8g of yeast into the juice.
Step 2: Mix the carrot juice with the flour, kneading thoroughly until the dough no longer sticks to your hands. If you prefer a sweeter crust, add a little sugar.
Step 3: Wrap the dough tightly with plastic wrap and let it rest for 1-2 hours until it doubles in size.
Step 4: Finely mince the pork and mushrooms, then mix with a bit of salt, seasoning powder, and sesame oil.
Step 5: Divide the dough into 15 equal portions, roll them out thinly, and place a little filling in the center. Seal the buns tightly.
Step 6: Arrange the buns in a steamer and steam for about 20 minutes until cooked. You have now finished cooking Sweet and Fragrant Carrot Steamed Buns.

mon_an.mo_ta: Let's get in the kitchen to make soft, fragrant, and nutritious red bean steamed buns to treat your whole family!
cac_buoc: Ingredients you need to prepare for red bean steamed buns
Step 1:
First, add sugar and yeast to the warm water and let it rest for a while.
Step 2:
Combine the flour, butter, and baking powder, then pour the yeast mixture into the bowl.
Step 3:
Knead the dough until it becomes smooth, soft, and elastic.
Step 4:
Proof the dough until it triples in size.
Step 5:
Next, divide the dough into 12 equal portions.
Step 6:
Roll the dough flat and press a depression in the center.
Step 7:
Add the red bean filling and shape into rounds or any shape you like.
Step 8:
Cut small squares of parchment paper to line the buns and place each bun on a piece of paper. Prepare a steamer, arrange the buns inside, and steam for about 10 minutes.
The red bean steamed buns are ready to enjoy!
A batch of red bean buns is a wish for luck and happiness for the whole family during the New Year!
Steamed buns are best eaten while hot!

mon_an.mo_ta: These cold winter days will become truly warm when enjoying soft, sweet, and refreshing lemon sponge cake. So don't hesitate, let's get in the kitchen and make this delicious dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Yellow lemons - 2 fruits (squeeze for 25ml juice; use 10ml for the cake batter and 15ml for the honey-lemon glaze)
cac_buoc: You should preheat the oven to 165°C for about 10-15 minutes before putting the cake in.
Step 1: Zest 2 yellow lemons, then squeeze them to get 25ml of juice.
(Since the recipe uses lemon juice for both the cake and the glaze, you must zest them first because it is very difficult to zest a squeezed lemon).
Add 10ml (out of the 25ml) of lemon juice to 150ml of fresh milk and let it sit for 10-15 minutes to curdle.
Step 2: Sift the flour and baking powder into a bowl and mix until smooth.
Step 3: Set the mixer to medium speed and beat the butter and salt until the butter is soft (about 30 seconds).
Gradually add the sugar. Once all the sugar is in, beat the butter and sugar until fluffy and pale ivory.
Step 4: Put the eggs in a small bowl with the lemon zest and vanilla. Whisk them together.
Divide the egg mixture into 3 parts. Add each part to the butter mixture one by one, beating at the lowest speed until well combined before adding the next part.

Step 5: Divide the sifted flour (from step 2) into 4 parts and the curdled milk (from step 1) into 3 parts. Sift 1/4 of the flour into the butter-egg mixture and beat at the lowest speed until combined.
Next, add 1/4 of the milk and mix well. Continue alternating the flour and milk until finished, ending with the final 1/4 of the flour.
The purpose of alternating the flour and eggs is to help the ingredients combine better, making the batter smoother and the cake fluffier.
Occasionally, remember to scrape down the sides of the bowl so the ingredients are evenly mixed!
Step 6: Before pouring the batter into the mold, remember to brush a thin layer of butter inside the mold for easy removal.
After pouring the batter, use a spatula to level the surface and bake for about 45 minutes.
Step 7: While the cake is baking, mix the remaining lemon juice with 45g of powdered sugar and 10g of honey.
When the cake is done, remove it from the oven and wait about 10 minutes before taking it out of the mold. A characteristic of this cake is a crack running down the center.
Brush the honey-lemon mixture onto the sides and top of the cake while it is still warm.
Finished product requirements:

When the cake is done, the surface will be slightly crispy and the inside will be dry and fluffy. Eaten while warm, the cake is airy, moist, and fragrant with lemon. It's delicious with milk or hot tea!

mon_an.ten: Taiwanese Matcha Swiss Roll with Fresh Cream
mon_an.mo_ta: The gentle taste of matcha blends with cool fresh cream, melting in your mouth from the very first bite of this soft, sweet sponge cake! Let's make it! Refer to the recipe for Taiwanese Matcha Swiss Roll with Fresh Cream below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fresh cream filling: 250ml whipping cream, 60gr sugar.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Preheat the oven to 170°C, grease the mold, then line it with parchment paper, pressing the four corners firmly.
Step 2: In a bowl, mix the egg yolks with 10g of sugar until dissolved, then stir in the cooking oil. Next, stir in the milk, then add the sifted matcha powder and mix well; set aside.
Step 3: In the egg white bowl, add a pinch of salt and use a mixer to beat until foamy. Add the lemon juice and continue beating, gradually adding sugar until the whites reach stiff peaks.

Step 4: Add 1/3 of the egg whites to the yolk bowl and mix well with a whisk. Then, pour the entire mixture back into the egg white bowl and fold gently with a spatula from the bottom up until the mixture is uniform.
Step 5: Pour the batter into the prepared tray and place it in the oven. After 25 minutes, the cake is done; remove it and place it on a rack to cool.

Step 6: Take the fresh cream, add sugar, and whip until stiff, then spread the cream over the cooled sponge cake. Gently roll the cake, pulling away the parchment paper as you go, being careful not to crack the cake.
Place the matcha cream roll in the refrigerator for 30 minutes to 1 hour to set, then take it out, slice into rounds, and enjoy.
Good luck to you and your family with this soft and delicious matcha cream roll!

mon_an.ten: How Many Calories in Salted Egg Sponge Cake? Does It Cause Weight Gain?
mon_an.mo_ta: Salted egg sponge cake is becoming a more popular choice than traditional cream cakes, thanks to its combination of salty, sweet, and rich flavors. Many people are concerned about the calorie count in salted egg sponge cake and whether eating it leads to weight gain. The following article will help answer those questions and provide detailed information on the nutritional components of a salted egg sponge cake. How many calories are in a salted egg sponge cake?
thoi_gian: The best time to enjoy salted egg sponge cake is in the morning, at lunch, or before you exercise. At these times, the body will use the calories from the cake to provide energy for activities throughout the day.
cac_buoc: According to food experts, each salted egg weighing 100g contains about 130 calories. A standard 50g sponge cake contains about 148.5 calories.
When combining these two components, an average cake will have the following calorie counts:
If following the standard weight of 50g, the cake contains about 215 calories.
With a weight of 250g, the cake contains about 850 calories.
If the cake is fully decorated with toppings like cheese, beef jerky, salted egg, etc., it can contain up to 1000 calories.
In short, the calorie count in salted egg sponge cake varies depending on individual consumption. However, the larger the cake size, the higher the calories.
Does eating a lot of salted egg sponge cake cause weight gain?
Salted egg sponge cake is an interesting and attractive dish; however, eating too much or too often can lead to uncontrolled weight gain.

The reason is that salted egg sponge cake is high in calories, coming from ingredients rich in fat and protein such as salted eggs, beef jerky, cheese, and egg oil sauce. Additionally, sponge cakes contain a lot of starch and little fiber, which easily causes fat accumulation and is difficult to digest.

According to the World Health Organization (WHO), women need about 2000 calories and men need about 2500 calories per day. Meanwhile, 250g of salted egg sponge cake provides nearly 1000 calories. Therefore, to maintain weight and good health, you should eat salted egg sponge cake in moderation, no more than 50g.
Some benefits of eating salted egg sponge cake
1. Nutritional supplement

Each salted egg sponge cake contains many nutritional components. In particular, the egg yolk provides lecithin and the yellow pigment vitello lutein, supporting brain development and improving memory. Despite the nutritional benefits, consuming too much cake can lead to weight gain and affect health.
2. Stress reduction

With a life full of stress and pressure, many people seek relief by enjoying their favorite foods. A salted egg sponge cake is one of them, offering a rich and sweet flavor combined with a hint of saltiness, which can help soothe negative moods and make you feel more upbeat and optimistic.
3. Cancer prevention

A lesser-known benefit of this cake is its ability to prevent cancer, thanks to the vitamin B2 (riboflavin) found in salted eggs. This vitamin is water-soluble and participates in many basic body activities. Riboflavin deficiency can lead to issues like iron-deficiency anemia, inflammation, and an increased risk of various cancers. Therefore, eating salted egg sponge cake can help strengthen the immune system and reduce the risk of cancer symptoms.
Ways to eat salted egg sponge cake without gaining weight
1. Limit consumption
Salted egg sponge cake is a high-calorie food. Therefore, to reduce calorie and fat intake and avoid negative effects on health and weight, you should limit consumption to about 50g per week.
2. Do not eat the cake in the evening

Do not use the cake as a replacement for a main meal because it does not provide enough essential nutrients. Also, avoid eating the cake in the evening because the body does not have enough time to burn off the calories consumed, leading to a risk of weight gain.
3. Homemade preparation
If you make the cake at home, you can control the calories and make it healthier. Here are some tips to make a lower-calorie cake:
Replace sugar with diet sugar: Diet sugar has fewer calories than regular sugar but still maintains the sweetness of the cake. You can use diet sugars like stevia, erythritol, xylitol, or monk fruit.

Limit the use of too much beef jerky, cheese, egg oil sauce, sausages, etc., in the cake. These toppings are very high in calories. Instead, you can use other toppings like strawberries, dark chocolate, or low-fat fresh cream.
4. Supplement with adequate nutrients
Salted egg sponge cake only provides high starch and fat but does not meet other nutritional needs like protein, vitamins, minerals, and fiber necessary for body development and function.
Therefore, combine eating the cake with other healthy foods like vegetables, tubers, fruits, meat, fish, milk, and dairy products to balance your diet and actively support the weight loss process.
5. Drink enough water
Water plays an important role in maintaining stable weight and health. It helps reduce hunger, enhances metabolism, and purifies the body.

Try to drink at least 2 liters of water a day and drink a glass of water before eating the cake to reduce the amount you consume. However, limit drinking sodas, juices, or carbonated drinks, as they contain a lot of unnecessary sugar and calories.
6. Calculate calorie intake
Each person has different calorie needs to maintain activity and overall health. You can calculate the necessary calories based on height, weight, age, gender, and activity level.

Ensure that the calories you consume in a day do not exceed the calories burned to avoid weight gain. Monitor calories from salted egg sponge cake as well as from other foods to adjust your diet to suit your needs.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Delicious Vung Tau Salted Egg Sponge Cake
mon_an.mo_ta: Vung Tau salted egg sponge cake is a soft, airy cake with a characteristic milky aroma that attracts everyone to enjoy and buy as gifts whenever they visit Vung Tau. The delicious and fragrant flavor of the cake never loses its appeal; on the contrary, it makes people more and more infatuated with this unique taste. Let's learn how to make Vung Tau salted egg sponge cake through the article below! Discover the recipe for wonderful Vung Tau salted egg sponge cake! Immerse yourself in the sweet flavor of soft sponge cake, perfectly combined with the signature taste of Vung Tau salted eggs.
cac_buoc: 1. Making the cake

First, crack the prepared eggs into the bowl of a stand mixer and beat until the foam is soft and fluffy. If desired, you can add a pinch of salt to help the eggs beat more evenly. During the beating process, gradually add the prepared sugar to create a sweet flavor for the cake. Next, add a few drops of vanilla to the mixture for extra aroma.

Then, mix the flour and yeast together and sift through a flour sifter to make the flour finer. Slowly pour the flour into the bowl containing the beaten eggs and continue to stir well. However, note that you should stir gently to keep the batter airy and smooth, ensuring the lightness and softness of the previously prepared egg cream.

Once the batter is ready, place a layer of parchment paper at the bottom and around the sides of the baking pan or the inner pot of a rice cooker to prevent the cake from sticking. Next, slowly pour the batter into the pan and tap it a few times by hand to distribute the batter evenly. If using an oven, bake the cake at 170°C for 15 to 25 minutes until cooked. If using a rice cooker, turn on the "Cook" mode and cook as usual until the cake is soft and done.
2. Making the salted egg filling

Once the cake is finished, proceed to make the rich salted egg filling. Crack all the prepared salted eggs, discard the shells, and collect the yolks. Rinse the yolks clean and place them in the oven to bake for about 2-3 minutes. Then, you can cut the salted egg yolks into small pieces according to your preference.

To make the sauce, whisk an egg yolk with sugar and a little cornstarch. Heat a pan and cook the mixture until thickened. Then, pour the sauce over the cake and sprinkle with salted eggs and pork floss butter. With these steps, you have completed the rich salted egg cake.
Notes when making Vung Tau salted egg sponge cake
Choose quality ingredients: Ensure you use fresh salted eggs, quality flour, good margarine, and other high-quality ingredients to achieve the best results.
Beat eggs evenly: When beating eggs, ensure they are beaten evenly and long enough to create soft, fluffy foam. Use a mixer or a whisk for the best results.
Smooth the flour: Before using the flour, sift it to remove lumps and make it finer. This helps the cake have a smooth structure without flour pockets.
Parchment paper in the pan: To prevent the cake from sticking, place a layer of parchment paper at the bottom or use heat-resistant foil to create a non-stick layer.
Bake at the correct temperature and time: Follow the recipe instructions or experience to bake at the correct temperature and time to ensure the cake is evenly cooked and not dry.

Check the cake before turning off the oven: Before turning off the oven, check the cake by inserting a bamboo skewer or a sharp knife into the center. If it comes out clean without wet batter, the cake is done.

Make sauce and decorate: Create the sauce from egg yolks, sugar, and cornstarch, ensuring it is fully cooked. Then, decorate the cake with the sauce, salted eggs, and pork floss butter for a signature look and flavor.
Storage and preservation: Once finished, Vung Tau salted egg sponge cake can be stored in an airtight container at room temperature or in the refrigerator to maintain its freshness and texture.
How to make safe and hygienic salted eggs at home
1. Ingredients for salted eggs
When making salted eggs at home, you need to prepare: duck eggs or clean chicken eggs, pure sea salt, filtered water, and a cleaned, dry glass jar.
For the sea salt, choose to buy from reliable locations, stores, or supermarkets to ensure the salt contains no preservatives and is completely safe for health.
Additionally, you can add a bit of white wine and a few star anise pods during the process. These two ingredients will enhance the delicious aroma of your salted eggs.
2. How to make salted eggs

The first step is to wash the duck and chicken eggs with clean water, then use a dry towel to wipe them dry to ensure no moisture remains. Place the eggs gently into the glass jar to avoid breaking or cracking.

The brine mixture consists of filtered water, sea salt, white wine, and star anise. Boil this mixture until the salt is completely dissolved. Then, wait for the mixture to cool before pouring it into the glass jar, ensuring the eggs are fully submerged.

For the salted eggs to have a good flavor, you need to seal the jar tightly and leave it for about 3 to 4 weeks before use. Depending on your family's needs, you can adjust the number of eggs to avoid keeping them too long and ensure the best flavor.

mon_an.ten: Instructions for Making Delicious Strawberry Mayonnaise Sponge Cake
mon_an.mo_ta: Sponge cake is a familiar treat, but now it's prepared in a new style; the filling with a slightly rich, sweet, and sour taste makes the dish even more attractive. Let's make this delicious strawberry sponge cake!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Sift the flour. Melt the butter over low heat. Put the eggs and sugar into a mixer and beat until fluffy, add the flour, mix evenly and gently, finally add the orange juice, fresh milk, butter, and 1 tbsp of grated orange zest and mix well.
Step 2: Grease the bottom of a rice cooker with a little butter, pour the batter in, and bake for about 20 minutes until the cake is done.
Step 3: Make the sauce: mix 2 tbsp of mayonnaise, 2 tbsp of sweetened condensed milk, 1/2 tbsp of lemon juice, and 1 tbsp of grated orange zest.
Step 4: Cut the cake horizontally into 3 thin layers, spread the prepared sauce on the first layer, place the second layer on top and spread sauce on it, finally place the third layer on top.
Step 5: Decorate the cake and serve with strawberry jam and hot tea.
Refer to the strawberry jam recipe at: How to make strawberry jam

mon_an.ten: Lemon Bars – A Delicious Treat You Can't Miss
mon_an.mo_ta: Lemon bars with a rich buttery crust and a chewy, tangy, sweet custard layer—a wonderful combination you shouldn't miss!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, we will make the crust. Preheat the oven to 170°C. Line a 20x20x5cm rectangular mold with parchment paper.
Step 2:
Mix all the crust ingredients including flour, sugar, salt, lemon zest, and butter in a food processor.
Note that the butter should be chilled and cut into small cubes before adding to the processor; do not let it melt into liquid!
Step 3:
Spread the mixture evenly into the prepared mold and bake for 30 minutes. Remember to press it down firmly to create an even, beautiful golden layer when cooked!
Step 4:
For the lemon custard: Mix the eggs, egg yolks, sugar, and lemon zest in a small saucepan.
Step 5:
Add the lemon juice and cook over low heat, stirring constantly for 3 minutes. Then, gradually increase the heat and continue stirring.
Step 6:
When the mixture thickens (about 8 minutes), immediately remove from the heat, strain the mixture through a sieve, and pour it over the pre-baked crust. Cover with foil and bake for 10 minutes.
Once baked, remove the foil and let it cool at room temperature, then cover with foil again and refrigerate for 1 hour before eating!
That's it! You can decorate the lemon bars with powdered sugar like this...
... then add a bit of whipped cream and pistachios!

mon_an.ten: Lemon Cake – A Unique and Delicious Treat
mon_an.mo_ta: For those who want to lose weight but love sweets, lemon cake is the perfect choice. The cake has a moderate sweetness, a soft interior, and a thin lemon filling on top that is slightly sweet and sour, especially when eaten cold, providing a very interesting sensation. What are you waiting for? Get in the kitchen and learn how to make this delicious lemon cake!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for the lemon cake:
Wash the lemons, cut them in half, squeeze for juice, discard the seeds and pulp, and keep the zest.
Crack the eggs into a large bowl.
Soften the butter at room temperature or heat it briefly to melt, which makes processing quicker and easier.
For the lemon zest, grate it finely or use a knife to mince it as small as possible. The finer the zest, the better.
To speed up the process, preheat the oven to 175°C.
Step 2: Cooking stages for the lemon cake:

First, mix the sugar and ½ tsp of salt into the butter, then heat over a water bath until the butter is completely melted. If you already melted the butter in the prep stage, just add the sugar and salt and stir until dissolved. To save time and effort, you can heat the mixture.

Next, sift 4/5 of the flour through a fine-mesh sieve, shaking your hand so the flour falls evenly and doesn't clump. After sifting, mix the flour with the butter. You should add it bit by bit while mixing so the mixture blends better, stays smooth, and becomes uniform.

Then, grease the inside of the cake mold with a thin layer of oil so the cake doesn't stick when baking and is easier to remove. After greasing, press the batter firmly into the bottom of the mold and bake for about 20 minutes.
Next, mix the remaining flour into the bowl of eggs, add 2 tbsp of sugar, and stir well.
Then add the lemon juice and lemon zest, and stir well. Remember to stir thoroughly so the sugar dissolves and the zest is evenly distributed in the mixture.

Next, pour this filling over the previously baked crust, place in the oven, and bake for about 30 minutes or until the surface is a beautiful golden brown at 150°C so the cake continues to cook and the top filling is set.
Finally, when the cake is done, remove it from the mold, cut into bite-sized pieces, and enjoy.
Some notes for a delicious lemon cake:

Be careful not to bake the cake at too high a temperature as it will make the cake dry, the ingredients will lose their softness and aroma, the crust will burn easily, and the filling may not cook through.
Use an appropriate amount of lemon zest. Adding too much can make the cake bitter and ruin the flavor.

If you don't like eating it hot, you can keep the lemon cake in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours before enjoying. At that time, the top filling will give you a light, cool, refreshing, and moderately sweet sensation.
This lemon cake is very suitable for home parties or picnics with friends and relatives.

mon_an.ten: Sweet Almond Chocolate Cake for Winter
mon_an.mo_ta: If you are a chocolate lover, this is a chocolate cake recipe that is hard to resist. There is nothing better than sipping tea and enjoying a sweet, warm almond chocolate cake when winter arrives!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Line a bowl (used as a cake mold) with plastic wrap, then tightly arrange thin slices of sponge cake inside the bowl. Set aside about 9-10 slices for the base.
Pro tip: To enhance the flavor and softness of the cake, mix a little liqueur (of your choice) with a bit of water and brush it evenly over the cake surface!
Step 2:
Melt the chocolate using a double boiler until completely smooth.
Step 3:
Whip the cream with powdered sugar until stiff peaks form.
Fold half of the whipped cream into the melted chocolate and mix well.
Step 4:
Spread the chocolate cream layer over the sponge cake.
Step 5:
Mix the remaining half of the whipped cream with sliced almonds. Note: Toast the almonds until fragrant before mixing.
Step 6:
Spread the almond cream over the chocolate cream layer, then cover the top with the remaining sponge cake slices.
Refrigerate for 3 hours to overnight before serving.
When serving, sprinkle cocoa powder on top to make the cake more attractive!

mon_an.mo_ta: Cold winter days will feel warmer when you enjoy fried ginger banana cakes with the sweet, nutty taste of bananas and the warm, spicy kick of ginger. It all creates a simple yet incredibly nutritious dish.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the ripe bananas and mash them thoroughly (the finer the mash, the softer the cake).
Step 2: Finely mince the ginger.
Step 3: Finely chop the rock sugar.
Step 4: Place all ingredients in a large bowl and mix thoroughly until the mixture is smooth and soft.
Step 5: Use a spoon to scoop bite-sized portions and drop them into hot oil; fry until golden brown.
Step 6: Remove and place on paper towels to absorb excess oil, so they won't feel greasy when eaten.

mon_an.mo_ta: Picnics will become more exciting with the food you bring along. Why not try making these S'mores cupcakes to accompany you on your trip?
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 100g marshmallows (about 12 large pieces or 120 mini pieces)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Preheat the oven to 170°C. Crush the crackers (using a knife or food processor) and mix with sugar and melted butter, then press the mixture into the bottom and sides of cupcake molds.
Step 2:
Bake the crust for 5 minutes. Break the chocolate into pieces that fit the molds and place one on each crust. Cut the marshmallows in half and place them on top of the chocolate layer.
Step 3:
Bake for another 2-4 minutes until the marshmallows soften, then remove from the oven.
Once removed, let them cool for 15 minutes before eating!
They look so attractive!
Absolutely delicious, everyone!

mon_an.mo_ta: These fruit-shaped mung bean cakes are crafted to look exactly like real fruit, with a beautiful glossy finish that makes everyone admire them at first sight!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Peeled mung beans - 150g (washed, soaked for 2-4 hours, steamed for 30 minutes, then pureed)
Food coloring: red, orange, lemon yellow, green, purple
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Place the soaked and steamed mung beans into a blender along with coconut milk and 115g of sugar; blend until smooth.
Step 2:
Transfer the mung bean mixture to a pot and cook over low heat, stirring constantly until the mixture thickens.
Step 3:
Now for the most exciting part: shape the mung bean paste into any fruit shapes you like and pierce the center with a toothpick.
Step 4:
Dilute food coloring with a little water, then use a small, clean brush to paint the fruit shapes you have created.
Step 5:

In a small pot, combine agar-agar powder, sugar, and water. Cook over medium heat until the agar-agar dissolves, then turn the heat to low. Dip the shaped beans into the agar-agar layer; let them dry briefly. If the coating is too thin, you can dip them a second time. Finally, refrigerate for a while before serving.
Hand-making these mung bean fruit cakes is not only delicious but also very fun; it's also a great opportunity to invite your kids to help shape the fruit and learn about different varieties.
Fruit-shaped mung bean cake is a famous snack in Thailand called Lookchoop. The method is not too complicated but requires a bit of skill to shape and color them beautifully.

mon_an.mo_ta: You love sweets but fear the sugar might make you gain weight? Don't worry, this donut recipe will satisfy your cravings without the weight gain concerns!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, place all the ingredients into a bowl.
Step 2:
Mix well for 1-2 minutes until the mixture is smooth and free of lumps.
Step 3:
Preheat a donut maker (you can also use a non-stick pan), brush with a thin layer of oil to prevent sticking, then pour the batter in.
Step 4:
Fry for about 3 minutes per side until both sides are golden brown. That's it! Remove and serve on a plate.
If you prefer it a bit sweeter, you can sprinkle a little diet sugar on top for a more eye-catching decoration!
These golden donuts look just like they were made in an oven!
This is a lifesaver for those on a diet who suddenly crave sweets!

mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to make these wonderful Baked Coconut Bird's Nest cookies! Guaranteed the kids will love them because they are beautiful, fragrant, delicious, and crunchy!
cac_buoc: Step 1: For this easy-to-make treat, mix the shredded coconut, condensed milk, and vanilla thoroughly.
Step 2: Scoop spoonfuls of the coconut mixture onto a baking sheet.
Step 3: Use your thumb to press gently in the center to create a bird's nest shape!
Step 4: Place the tray in the oven and bake at 300°F for 20-30 minutes. Remove, let cool, and decorate with candies to complete the bird's nests!
Source: ST

mon_an.mo_ta: Homemade Tteokbokki – An easy-to-make dish for girls who love Korean culture and spicy food to show off their skills. Cooking tutorial for homemade Tteokbokki.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Mix the flour and salt with 360ml of water, then knead thoroughly.

Step 2: Knead the dough for another 15 minutes until very smooth. Prepare a steamer; wrap the lid with a thick cotton cloth to prevent condensation from dripping and making the Tteokbokki dough soggy.
Step 3: Place the kneaded dough in the steamer for about 20 minutes. While steaming, open the lid every 5 minutes to check for water buildup on the lid and ensure it isn't dripping through the cloth.

Step 4: Remove the dough from the steamer, let it cool slightly, then knead thoroughly for another 15-20 minutes. During the kneading process, dip your hands into a bowl containing 360ml of water mixed with 5ml of oil to prevent the dough from sticking. Roll the dough into long strips; you can cut them into long cylinders or small rounds as desired.
Source: Kenh14

mon_an.mo_ta: Christmas is just around the corner, a time for fun and gathering with friends. Let's make a Yule Log cake for these days! The Yule Log is an indispensable part of a family Christmas party. Let's start making a Yule Log to welcome Christmas!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cocoa powder - 50g (if you prefer a cocoa-flavored cake)
cac_buoc: Mixture A:
Sift the powdered sugar.
Separate the eggs; use the yolks for Mixture A and the whites for Mixture B.
Sift and mix the flour, cornstarch, and baking powder.
In a separate bowl, mix the milk, oil, and vanilla.
Add the sifted flour mixture and mix well.
Then add the powdered sugar and mix well.
Finally, add the egg yolks and mix until smooth.
Continue until you have a golden, smooth, and thick batter as shown.
Mixture B:
Place egg whites in a bowl, add cream of tartar (if unavailable, substitute with a pinch of salt and 5ml lemon juice) and mix.
Use a hand mixer to beat the whites; when they start to foam, add the powdered sugar.
Continue beating until stiff peaks form.
Mixing the batter:
Fold 1/2 of Mixture B into Mixture A and mix gently.
Then pour this mixture into the remaining 1/2 of Mixture B and fold gently to get the final cake batter.
Baking:
Line a baking sheet with parchment paper or brush with melted butter, then pour the batter in and spread evenly.
Bake in the oven for 7-10 minutes at 190°C. Check with a toothpick; if it comes out clean, the cake is done.
When done, remove the cake, place a piece of paper on top, flip the tray to release the cake, and let it cool.
Making the frosting:
Pour heavy cream into a bowl.
Mix the cream with cocoa powder, salt, and sugar.
Place the bowl in the refrigerator for about 5 minutes.
After 5 minutes, remove and whip until stiff peaks form, then transfer to a piping bag (you can use a clean plastic bag with one corner cut off).
Rolling and decorating:
Spread any filling you like onto the cooled cake. You can use fruit jam or whipped cream. Here, I use strawberry jam because I plan to decorate with strawberry Santas.
Slowly roll the cake, peeling off the parchment paper as you go.
Be careful to roll gently so the cake surface doesn't crack.
Use a knife to cut a section of the cake at an angle.
Attach the cut section to the side of the main log.
Pipe the cream in parallel lines along the body of the cake.
Use a knife to smooth the cream evenly.
Use a toothpick to draw parallel lines to mimic the rough texture of tree bark.
Then decorate as desired, and you have a delicious and attractive Yule Log for Christmas.
You can also refer to how to make strawberry Santas and three-color jelly to decorate your Yule Log beautifully.

mon_an.mo_ta: Hawaiian Manapua is quite a unique dish for many, but it will make you fall in love from the first bite. The crust is soft, fluffy, and moist, while the filling is colorful, fragrant, and features tender char siu that blends perfectly with the bun. One bite offers a full range of flavors that will keep you coming back for more.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Red food coloring - a few drops
Whisk, steamer, parchment paper, plastic wrap - tools
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for Hawaiian Manapua
Sift the flour until smooth.
Next, place the dry yeast in a bowl and mix with 3 tbsp of warm water until it blooms.
Finely dice the char siu.
Cut the parchment paper into 12 equal squares.
Step 2: Steps to make Hawaiian Manapua.
The Dough
First, prepare a bowl and add: 2 cups of warm water, salt, sugar, and oil. Use a spoon to stir well until the sugar and salt dissolve and everything is combined.
Then, pour this sugar-water mixture into the yeast mixture prepared earlier.
Next, gradually add the flour to the yeast mixture. You should add the flour in several batches to make kneading easier.

Use a whisk to mix the flour thoroughly, then use your hands to knead. Knead well, as the longer you knead, the better the dough will be. Knead until the dough is soft, smooth, non-lumpy, and no longer sticks to your hands.
Shape the dough into a ball and coat it with a layer of sesame oil.
Cover the bowl tightly with plastic wrap and let the dough proof for about 1 hour or until it has doubled in size. Place the dough in a warm spot for better rising.
The Filling
Prepare a medium pot and add: water, sugar, cornstarch, and salt.
Use a whisk to mix the ingredients until well combined.
Once mixed, place the pot on the stove over medium heat.
When the mixture boils, add the diced char siu and a few drops of red food coloring. Continue to stir well.
Once the filling boils again, turn off the heat.
Assembling the Buns
Take the proofed dough out and press down firmly with your hands to deflate it.
Divide the dough into 12 equal portions and roll them into balls.
Take one portion of dough in your palm and flatten it, making sure the center is thicker than the edges.
Cup your hand slightly and scoop an appropriate amount of filling into the center.
Start shaping the bun. Twist the edges of the dough together first, then roll it into a smooth ball so the filling is fully enclosed and doesn't leak out.
Place the bun onto a square of parchment paper.
Repeat with the remaining dough and filling.
Let the buns rest for about 10 minutes.
Finally, arrange the buns in a steamer, keeping them on the parchment paper. Space them about 5cm apart so they don't stick together when they expand.
Steam for about 15 minutes over high heat or until cooked through.
When the time is up, turn off the heat but leave the Manapua in the steamer for a few more minutes.
Once done, arrange on a plate and enjoy.
Notes for perfect Hawaiian Manapua
As mentioned above, you can bake these buns instead of steaming them.

To make the dough better, you can let it rise multiple times. After the first rise, deflate it and let it rise a second or third time. Alternatively, you can proof the dough in the refrigerator for 3-4 hours. Although it takes more time, the buns will be much tastier.

mon_an.mo_ta: Bánh ít trần is a simple and delicious snack from Central Vietnam. It is somewhat similar to Northern Vietnamese sticky rice cakes, featuring a mung bean filling combined with pork, wood ear mushrooms, and black pepper, all wrapped in a chewy glutinous rice crust. When eating Bánh ít trần, remember to serve it with a bowl of very spicy chili fish sauce to fully experience the unique flavor of this Central region specialty! Let's learn how to make Bánh ít trần – a dish rich with the flavors of the beloved Central homeland!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, sugar, pepper, oil - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: For this easy-to-make dish, put the flour and salt in a large bowl, create a well in the center, pour in the oil and half of the water, and knead thoroughly. Initially, the dough will be wet, but keep kneading steadily and it will become a cohesive, flexible mass. At this point, cover with plastic wrap and let the dough rest for about 10 minutes.

Step 2: After 10 minutes, continue kneading. If the dough feels dry, add a little more water. Be careful to adjust the water so the dough is flexible enough; too much water will make it too soft to shape. Check the dough by taking a small piece and rolling it; if it is smooth and doesn't crack, it is ready.
Step 3: Steam the mung beans until cooked, then mash them finely.
Step 4: Place a pan on the stove, add oil, and sauté the pork. When the pork turns white, add the shrimp and stir well. Add pepper and salt, mix thoroughly, then turn off the heat and let it cool.

Step 5: Wash and finely mince the wood ear mushrooms. In a bowl, mix the mushrooms, mashed mung beans, and meat; add a little water if the mixture is too dry. Shape the filling into 18-24 small round balls.
Step 6: Divide the dough into portions corresponding to the number of filling balls. Knead each piece, flatten into a thin circle, place the filling in the center, and roll into a ball.
Step 7: Cut banana leaves into small rectangles, brush with a little oil, and place a finished cake on each piece.

Step 8: Steam the cakes for 12-15 minutes; do not steam too long or they will become mushy. Remove the Bánh ít trần and sprinkle with shrimp floss if desired. Serve with fish sauce mixed in a ratio of 1 fish sauce - 1 sugar - 1 water, adding garlic and chili as preferred.
Source: ST

mon_an.mo_ta: These pancakes are delicious, rich, and infused with a fragrant coffee aroma! If you are looking for a new flavor for your family, try making these pancakes.
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Preheat the oven to 150 degrees F.
Step 2:
In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and sugar until well combined. In a small bowl, lightly beat the egg.
Step 3:
Whisk the instant coffee into the egg until they are completely blended. Mix the wet egg mixture and the dry flour mixture together until just combined and smooth.
Step 4:

Spread about 1 tbsp of butter evenly on a baking tray. Scoop ¼ tbsp of batter, flatten it into a pancake shape, and arrange them evenly on the tray to bake. Bake until slightly golden, then flip and continue baking until fully cooked. - Now you have delicious pancakes. Simply serve on a plate and enjoy with syrup.
