Step 2: Add the wood ear mushrooms, onion, and seasonings. Stir-fry for about 15 minutes over medium heat or until the ingredients are cooked through, then turn off the heat. Add quail eggs and toss together (optional).

Step 3: Mix the rice flour and cornstarch in a bowl, add water and dissolve. Let it sit for 3 hours for the starch to settle, then pour off the clear water on top. Replace the discarded water with fresh cold water and the seasonings listed above up to the original water level (this removes the raw flour smell and makes the cake clearer).
Step 4: Pour the mixture into a pot and stir over low heat. Stir continuously until the batter thickens slightly, then turn off the heat.
Step 5: Pour the batter into a bowl and place in a steamer for 15-20 minutes until the cake is fully cooked.
Step 6: Scoop the steamed cake into a serving bowl, add the pork topping, sprinkle with fried shallots, pour over the sweet and sour fish sauce, and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Freshwater mussel congee with its delicious flavor and appealing color is served hot with pepper, chili powder, and crispy breadsticks to warm you up during the cold winter days!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Garnish - Shallots, ginger, green onions, Vietnamese coriander
Seasonings - Pepper, seasoning powder, salt, fish sauce
cac_buoc: How to cook delicious freshwater mussel congee
Step 1: Soak the mussels in water with a few slices of chili so they release all the mud. Then, scrub the shells clean. Alternatively, you can soak them in rice water for a clean result.
Step 2: Soak the glutinous rice, jasmine rice, and mung beans together in water for 5-6 hours until softened.
Step 3: Place the mussels in a pot with a large bowl of water and boil until they open their shells, then turn off the heat. Strain the mussel broth and let it settle to remove any sediment.

Step 4: Rinse the soaked rice and mung beans, then pulse in a blender until coarsely cracked. Place the mixture into a rice cooker, pour in the mussel broth (leaving out the sediment), and add enough water so the total liquid is 3 times the amount of rice.

Step 5: Close the lid, press the "Cook" button. Once it boils, switch to the "Warm" setting. After 10-15 minutes, press "Cook" again. Repeat this process several times until the rice and beans are soft and the congee has thickened. Season with seasoning powder and salt to taste.
Step 6: While the congee is cooking, remove the mussels from their shells. Remove the dark digestive tract and wash the mussel meat thoroughly.
Step 7: Slice the mussel meat into 2, 3, or 4 pieces depending on their size.

Step 8: Sauté the minced shallots and ginger until fragrant, then add the mussel meat. Season with a bit of fish sauce and seasoning powder. Stir-fry quickly so the meat absorbs the flavor, then turn off the heat (do not overcook or the meat will become tough and shriveled).
Step 9: Ladle the congee into a bowl, top with chopped green onions, Vietnamese coriander, and the sautéed mussels. Mix well and sprinkle with pepper or chili powder as desired.
How to choose fresh mussels

To prevent poisoning, do not buy or eat dead mussels. The best way to check is to touch the shell; if it is alive, it will slowly close. Also, pay attention to the smell. Fresh mussels should not have an overpowering or overly fishy odor.
Avoid mussels with chipped, broken, or crushed shells, as they are prone to harmful bacteria.
Do not buy frozen mussels or those in plastic bags, as they may not be fresh or might have been treated with chemicals.
Freshwater mussel congee with its delicious flavor and appealing color is served hot with pepper, chili powder, and crispy breadsticks to warm you up during the cold winter days!

mon_an.ten: Warm and Delicious Cassava Sweet Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: This cassava sweet soup features an eye-catching color and a delightful aroma. The cassava is tender and well-infused with a gentle sweetness, offering a satisfying treat. Follow our recipe below to make this delicious dessert.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the cassava, cut into sections, and soak in a bowl of diluted salt water for about 6 to 7 hours before cooking. Soaking helps prevent the cassava from browning and removes the sap.
Step 2: Next, place the cassava in a pot, cover with water, and boil until fully cooked.

Step 3: Once cooked, remove the cassava and let it cool slightly. Dice it into small bite-sized pieces. (You should boil the cassava whole before dicing to better preserve its sweetness compared to dicing before boiling).
Step 4: Place a pot of water on the stove and bring to a boil. Add sugar and some julienned ginger, stirring well until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Step 5: Once the water boils, add the cassava. Lower the heat to a simmer so the sweetness can penetrate deep into the cassava. Adjust the seasoning to your taste.

Step 6: Mix the kudzu powder with a little filtered water until dissolved. Slowly pour the mixture into the pot while stirring gently. Continue stirring until the soup thickens and reaches a light simmer, then turn off the heat.
Step 7: Finally, ladle the cassava soup into bowls, top with shredded coconut, and serve warm. For a richer flavor, you can add a splash of coconut milk.
Notes for a delicious warm cassava sweet soup:
How to choose good cassava:

When choosing cassava, look for hill-grown varieties as they are starchier and more fragrant. Select fresh, plump, straight roots with smooth skin for fewer fibers and a sweeter, softer texture. You can use your fingernail to scrape the outer skin; if the inner layer is light pink, it is a good choice. Avoid those with a white inner layer as the pink-skinned variety contains fewer toxins.

Do not leave fresh cassava for too long after purchase, as it will lose its flavor. Proper preparation is crucial because, like bamboo shoots, cassava is healthy but can cause poisoning if not handled correctly.

Before cooking, peel both layers of the skin and cut off the ends, as these parts contain the most toxins. Soak the cassava in water for 30 minutes to 1 hour, then rinse several times with cold water. If boiling, use plenty of water and keep the lid open so toxins can evaporate. Discard the boiling water afterward for a safe and tasty snack.
You can use brown sugar to enhance the color of the dish.
Alternative method for making cassava sweet soup:

Prepare a bowl of clean water. Use a grater to shred the fresh cassava directly into the water. Drain the shredded cassava, squeeze dry, and set aside. Let the water in the bowl sit until the starch settles at the bottom, then discard the clear water to keep the thick starch. Boil about 1 liter of water, turn the heat to very low, and add both the starch and shredded cassava, stirring gently until cooked. Once cooked, add sugar and a slurry of tapioca starch, stirring constantly. When the soup boils again and becomes translucent, add vanilla, pomelo flower extract, shredded coconut, or coconut milk as desired, then turn off the heat.

mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little time in the kitchen and familiar ingredients, you can make fresh, fragrant, and warm shrimp and pork dumplings. The sweet shrimp filling, chewy wrapper, and crunchy carrots provide a truly enjoyable culinary experience.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Ginger, pepper, green onions, salt - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, put 180g of flour into a large bowl, add salt, and mix well. Gradually pour in water while stirring with chopsticks until the mixture begins to thicken.
Step 2:
Once the dough forms a sticky mass, cover the bowl with a damp towel and let it rest for about 5 minutes.
Step 3:

The dough will become firmer after resting. Sprinkle in the remaining 20g of flour and knead until the dough is smooth, dry to the touch, soft, and has the right moisture—neither too mushy nor too hard.
Step 4: Making the filling
To prepare the filling, peel the shrimp and finely mince them.
Peel the carrots, wash them, and finely dice into small cubes.
Peel and wash the ginger, then mince it finely.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the green onions, wash, drain, and chop finely.
Step 5:
Next, combine the shrimp, pork, ginger, and green onions in a bowl and mix well.
Step 6:
Add the diced carrots, more green onions, and a bit of seasoning powder or MSG. Mix thoroughly so the ingredients are well-seasoned and fully combined.
Step 7:
Once the filling is ready, roll the dough into a long log and cut it into small pieces about the size of 4 knuckles.
Step 8:
Use a rolling pin to flatten each piece of dough into a very thin, round circle.
Step 9:
Place 1 tablespoon of filling in the center of the dough circle, fold it in half, and press the edges firmly to seal.
Step 10:
Slice the remaining carrot into thin rounds and arrange them in a steamer basket. Place the dumplings on top of the carrot slices. Steam for about 6 minutes, or until the wrappers become translucent.
Once the dumplings are cooked, arrange them on a plate and serve with soy sauce or sweet and sour fish sauce.
To ensure delicious dumplings, choosing fresh shrimp is very important.
You can select shrimp using the following tips:
Good shrimp should have firm bodies, hard shells, and a translucent white color rather than being opaque, red, or yellow.
The head should be firmly attached to the body, legs should be intact, and there should be no fishy or spoiled odor.
Secrets to identifying freshness by shrimp type:
1. Lobster: Look for those with translucent blue claws and shiny shells.
2. He shrimp (Penaeus): Choose those that are still jumping, with a pinkish-white color and green eyes.
3. Tiger shrimp: Should have a smooth, shiny shell with a clear, translucent line along the back.
Absolutely do not buy shrimp that have turned deep pink, have heads or legs detached from the body, or smell spoiled; these are old and can be dangerous to eat.

With just a little effort, you have a fresh, fragrant, and hot batch of dumplings to treat your family and loved ones. The sweet shrimp filling, chewy skin, and crunchy carrots will surely delight everyone.

mon_an.mo_ta: Regularly drinking these fruit smoothies will help you maintain good health, youthful skin, and a fit body!
cac_buoc: Banana, Avocado, and Kiwi Smoothie:

As you may know, bananas help reduce stomach acidity. Kiwi is rich in calcium, minerals, and vitamins while promoting digestion. Avocado is high in folate, helps lower cholesterol, protects the heart, boosts the immune system, strengthens bones, and helps prevent or treat the flu. Therefore, this blend is nutrient-dense, aids digestion, and helps prevent constipation.
To make this delicious smoothie:
Peel the banana, avocado, and kiwi, then cut them into small pieces. Place them in a blender with sugar and ice cubes. Blend for about 30 seconds until smooth. Pour into a glass, garnish, and enjoy.
Apple Lemon Smoothie:

Lemon is both refreshing and aids digestion while supporting weight loss. Apples are sweet, help stimulate the appetite, promote digestion, and provide potassium and vitamins. This smoothie is an essential choice for summer.
To make this delicious smoothie:
Peel and dice the apple. Place it in a blender with fresh milk, lemon juice, honey, and ice. Blend until smooth. Pour into a glass and enjoy.
Avocado and Durian Smoothie:
This is an extremely nutritious smoothie, perfect for a summer energy boost, especially for those who love avocado and durian.
To make this delicious smoothie:

Remove the pit from the durian. Peel and dice the avocado. Place both in a blender with fresh milk and condensed milk, then blend until smooth. Pour into a glass, add crushed ice, and enjoy. Alternatively, you can blend the ice with the ingredients. However, adding ice afterward keeps the smoothie fresh and allows you to adjust the sweetness to your preference.
Orange and Grapefruit Smoothie:

Oranges and grapefruits are rich in vitamin C, pectin, protein, calcium, and phosphorus, and they provide iron and vitamin B1 to boost the immune system. This smoothie is a great choice for health and resistance, and it is also excellent for those looking to maintain a slim figure and a toned waist!
To make this delicious smoothie:
Peel and chop the oranges and grapefruit.
Place the fruit and honey into a juicer.
Finally, pour the mixture into a glass, add ice, and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Learn the secret to making easy, crispy golden French fries. With this method, you will have golden, delicious fries that stay crispy for a long time without getting soggy.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the potatoes
Peel the potatoes, cut them into batons, and soak them in a bowl of cold water mixed with a little salt for about 2-3 hours.

Drain the potatoes and place them in a colander to dry. To speed this up, you can spread them on a wide tray lined with paper towels and use a dry cloth or paper towels to pat the tops dry. This step is crucial to prevent oil from splattering during frying.
Step 2: First fry
Heat cooking oil in a pan or a deep pot until hot, then slowly add the potatoes in batches and fry for about 4-5 minutes.
When the potatoes start to become soft and cooked through, remove them from the oil.
Place them on a tray to drain, then spread them on a tray lined with paper towels to absorb any remaining oil. Repeat until all the prepared potatoes are fried.
Step 3: Second fry
After the first fry, increase the heat to high and add the potatoes for a second fry.
Fry until the potatoes turn a vibrant golden brown, then remove them.
Place the fries on a plate lined with paper towels, then sprinkle with a little salt and pepper or fine salt to finish the dish.
Note the following points to ensure your French fries are both delicious and healthy.

Choose fresh, round potatoes that feel heavy for their size, with smooth skin and no scratches or soft spots. Use yellow-fleshed potatoes (experience shows they are sweeter and more fragrant than white ones); avoid green-tinted or sprouted potatoes as they contain harmful substances.
Avoid over-frying, reusing the oil multiple times, or frying over excessive heat, as the potatoes may burn and become unhealthy to consume.
The preparation step is important to minimize toxins that can form during frying. Therefore, remember to peel them thoroughly and soak them in diluted salt water before frying.

Before frying, make sure the potatoes are completely dry; you can use a towel or paper towels to blot out all the moisture. If water remains on the potatoes, it will cause the hot oil to splatter when frying. Splattering oil can cause burns and mess up the kitchen, making cleaning a real chore.
Once the fries are done, serving them with chili sauce or soy sauce is the perfect combination.

mon_an.mo_ta: Here are some tips for making hot, crispy, and delicious Quẩy using a recipe perfect for cold days. Hot Quẩy can be served with clam porridge, pork rib porridge, Phở gà, Bún măng gà, or even cut into short pieces and dipped in chili sauce or lime salt. (I used to be addicted to this; hot Quẩy dipped in chili sauce with a bit of seasoning salt and kumquat is absolutely delicious).
cac_buoc: Sift the flour into a large bowl, add the baking powder and salt, and mix well.
Add the peanut oil and then slowly pour in the water, mixing as you go.
Knead the dough by hand until it becomes a smooth, soft, and homogenous ball. Then, wrap it tightly in plastic wrap and leave it at room temperature for about 1 hour to let it rise.
Take the dough out, flatten it, fold it in half, and continue kneading for about 5 minutes.
Place the dough in a plastic bag, squeeze out all the air, tie it tightly, and store it in the freezer overnight.

After one night, remove the dough and let it soften, then roll it into a thin sheet and cut it into small pieces about 1-1.5cm thick. Stack two cut pieces on top of each other and use a long skewer to press down lengthwise on the top piece so they stick together. Continue until all the dough is used.

Use a small, deep pan to fry the Quẩy. Pour in enough oil to reach a depth of about 4-5cm and heat until hot. Using both hands, hold the ends of the dough, stretch it to nearly the width of the pan, give it a slight twist, and drop it into the hot oil.
Use chopsticks to flip the Quẩy until they puff up and turn golden brown on all sides, then remove and place on a rack to drain.
Here is the final result. Served with a bowl of clam porridge ^^

mon_an.mo_ta: Cherries are delicious and visually stunning with their bright red color, often used for decoration and as a key ingredient in various pastries. Beyond their beauty, cherries are rich in potassium, which helps lower blood pressure, supports cardiovascular health, and provides anti-inflammatory benefits for joint pain. Cherry pie is a popular dessert in the West with a simple recipe that only requires a bit of basic skill to create an excellent treat for your family. Let's get into the kitchen and make this delicious dish!
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients
First, prepare all the necessary tools: mixing bowl, stand mixer, toothpick, knife, wooden cutting board, oven, and pot.
Wash the cherries thoroughly, cut them into halves or thirds, remove the pits, and place them in a bowl.
Instructions:
Step 1: Add the flour, butter, salt, sugar, and water into a bowl and use a stand mixer to mix thoroughly. Mix until the dough is uniform, smooth, and free of lumps.
Step 2: Remove the dough from the bowl and knead it thoroughly. Form it into a ball, wrap tightly in plastic wrap, and place it in the refrigerator for 1 hour to let the dough rest.

Step 3: While the dough is chilling, place the cherries in a pot on the stove. Add powdered sugar, cornstarch, and water. Sauté the cherries over low heat until they soften and slightly break down, and the filling mixture thickens. Stir constantly to ensure the ingredients are well combined and the cherries do not burn or scorch.

Step 4: Once the dough has rested, take it out and divide it into 2 equal parts. Roll out each part until it is about 5mm thick and slightly larger than your pie mold. Be careful not to make the crust too thin, as it may burn during baking and lose its fragrant, crispy texture.

After rolling the dough, place it into the mold. Use a toothpick to prick small holes across the surface of the dough (without piercing all the way through) to allow heat to circulate and help the pie cook evenly.
Step 5: Pour the cherry filling over the dough in the mold.
Step 6: Take the remaining portion of dough and cut it into long strips about 2cm wide.
Step 7: Use the strips to weave a lattice pattern over the top like a lid.
Step 8: Once the lattice is finished, place the pie in the oven at 175°C for 40-45 minutes.
Step 9: When the pie is done, remove it from the oven, let it cool, and slice it to serve.
Notes for making cherry pie:
The finished dough must be smooth and pliable, neither dry nor crumbly.
The amount of sugar can be adjusted to your preference. If the cherries are too tart when sautéing, add more sugar; if they are too sweet, add a little water.
If weaving a lattice pattern is too difficult, you can skip that step; the pie will still be delicious.
Fresh cherries provide plenty of Vitamin C, along with other vitamins and minerals that support weight loss.
Good cherries are bright or dark red with green stems. Avoid soft, bruised, or mushy fruit. Hard and small cherries are often less juicy and less fragrant.

mon_an.ten: Crispy Fried Rice Cake with Egg (Bột Chiên)
mon_an.mo_ta: Bột chiên is a rich and appealing traditional dish in Vietnamese cuisine. With a crispy outer crust and a soft interior, it has become a favorite not only at street food stalls but also at family gatherings. Let's explore how to make this mesmerizingly delicious bột chiên and bring the signature flavors of Vietnamese cuisine right to your meal! Discover the detailed instructions and secrets to success for a perfect batch. Enjoy the crispy texture and savory flavor of this traditional Vietnamese dish at home.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, soy sauce, green onions, seasonings - as needed
Shredded papaya and carrots - 1 bowl each
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Trim the roots of the green onions, wash them, and finely chop.
Green papaya: Shred the green papaya into thin strips. Soak in salt water for about 15 minutes. Drain well, then add sugar, salt, and vinegar, mixing thoroughly. Let it marinate for about 30 minutes.
Rice flour: In a large bowl, combine 200g rice flour, 20g tapioca starch, 1 tsp cooking oil, and 1 tsp salt. Gradually add 60ml cold water and stir well by hand.
Batter mixture: Add 120ml boiling water to the flour mixture and continue stirring by hand until it becomes a smooth, thick batter.
Step 2: Cooking the fried rice cake
2.1. Steaming the dough
Place a non-stick pan on the stove and add 1 tbsp of cooking oil. Pour the thick batter into the pan and cook until it thickens further.
Prepare a steaming tray by brushing the sides with 1 tbsp of oil to prevent sticking. Transfer the cooked dough from the pan into the tray.

Steam the dough over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until cooked. Test by poking a chopstick into the dough; if it comes out clean, it is done. Remove and let it cool completely. To make the dough firm and easier to fry, you can refrigerate it for 30 minutes to 1 hour.
2.2. Frying the cake
Once the dough has hardened, cut it into bite-sized pieces about 3cm long and 2cm thick. Avoid cutting them too large, as they can become greasy and lose their crispy appeal.
Place a pan on the stove and add about 2 tbsp of cooking oil. Once the oil is hot, add the dough pieces and fry until they are golden brown and crispy on all sides.
2.3. Adding eggs and green onions
When the cakes are golden and crispy, crack the eggs and spread them evenly over the surface, then sprinkle the chopped green onions on top.
Flip the cakes to ensure the eggs and dough are fully cooked and golden. Transfer the fried egg rice cakes to a plate.
2.4. Making the dipping sauce
In a bowl, combine 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp vinegar, a little sugar, and chili. Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Adjust the seasoning to your family's taste and pour into a serving bowl.
2.5. Finished product
Serve the fragrant, golden-brown fried cakes on a plate. Top with a bit of the pickled papaya salad and serve with the chili soy sauce.
Enjoy the dish with its crispy yet chewy crust and soft, slightly sweet interior. Dipping it in soy sauce with the crunchy papaya makes it even more delicious.
Tips for making delicious bột chiên
During the process, keep these points in mind to achieve a crispier and tastier result.

When mixing the batter, follow the ratios strictly to get a smooth, thick consistency. Avoid making it too thick or too thin. If the batter is too thin, the cake will not bind well and won't get crispy.
When frying, use medium heat and gradually reduce it. Ensure the oil is hot before adding the cakes to achieve maximum crispiness with minimum oil absorption.

Another way to fry quickly and save oil is to use an oil-water separation fryer. This allows you to fry various foods efficiently. Since food crumbs are separated during the process, the oil stays golden and maintains its quality.

mon_an.mo_ta: Lemon cookies might not be familiar to everyone, but once you try them, you won't be able to resist. They feature a soft, smooth, and fluffy interior fragrant with fresh lemon, topped with a white chocolate and lemon zest glaze that is sweet, cool, and slightly tart, melting in your mouth. Enjoy these wonderful cookies with a cup of tea on a relaxing afternoon while reading on the porch. Savoring the cookies and tea helps you feel the rhythm of a beautiful life, making it feel more meaningful, colorful, and interesting!
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients for lemon cookies:
Wash the lemons thoroughly and let them dry completely.
Use a fine grater to zest the lemons to obtain fine lemon zest.
Instructions:
First, mix the lemon zest with the granulated sugar.
Preheat the oven to 165°C.
Mix the all-purpose flour with the cornstarch. Use a hand mixer to cream the butter, powdered sugar, lemon zest, and salt until the mixture is smooth, uniform, and well combined.
Gradually add the flour mixture into the lemon zest mixture and mix until the dough is smooth.
Use a small spoon to divide the dough into equal portions and place them on a baking tray lined with parchment paper.
Use a spoon to flatten each cookie. Bake for 12-14 minutes until the cookies turn golden brown.
Melt the white chocolate with half of the remaining lemon zest in the microwave.
Mix the other half of the lemon zest with some fine sugar.

When the cookies have cooled slightly, drizzle the white chocolate sauce over them. Sprinkle the lemon zest and sugar mixture on top. Place in the refrigerator for 2-3 hours for the chocolate to set before serving.
Notes for perfect lemon cookies:
With this method, you can use the lemon zest from lemons you have already used for juice.
To ensure the zest isn't bitter, you can soak it in limewater for 30 minutes to 1 hour, then rinse thoroughly until the lime smell is gone.
Note that once the cookies turn golden, they are done. Do not bake them for too long or they will become dry and burnt.
You can also use Meyer lemon zest or orange zest to make these cookies; each type of citrus will provide a unique and distinct flavor.
If you want to shape the cookies, use small molds to create cute shapes that appeal to everyone.

Lemon cookies might not be familiar to everyone, but once you try them, you won't be able to resist. They feature a soft, smooth, and fluffy interior fragrant with fresh lemon, topped with a white chocolate and lemon zest glaze that is sweet, cool, and slightly tart, melting in your mouth. Enjoy these wonderful cookies with a cup of tea on a relaxing afternoon while reading on the porch. Savoring the cookies and tea helps you feel the rhythm of a beautiful life, making it feel more meaningful, colorful, and interesting!

mon_an.mo_ta: These crispy, golden-brown fried dumplings are a classic Northern Vietnamese treat, typically served with a sweet and sour dipping sauce and fresh herbs—perfect for a chilly afternoon. Bánh gối is simple to make; you can even repurpose spring roll filling for the center. Wrappers are easily found at supermarkets or specialty bakeries. Follow this detailed guide to master traditional Northern-style Bánh gối at home, from preparing the savory filling to achieving that perfect golden crunch.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the pork shoulder and mince it. Peel the jicama, wash, and finely dice. Blanch the glass noodles in boiling water, then chop into short strands. Peel the kohlrabi; finely dice 1/2 of it for the filling, and thinly slice the remaining 1/2 into small squares for the pickles.

Step 2: Prepare the carrots in the same way as the kohlrabi (half diced, half sliced for pickles). Soak the shiitake and wood ear mushrooms until soft, remove the stems, and mince. Mix all filling ingredients together with pepper, fish sauce, and MSG to taste. Stir-fry the mixture in a pan until just cooked through. Transfer to a large bowl and let cool.

Step 3: Place a wrapper on a shallow plate. Lightly moisten the edges with a bit of water. Press the center of the wrapper down slightly, add the filling, and fold in half. Press the edges firmly to seal. Heat oil in a pan until hot, then fry the dumplings over medium heat until golden brown. Once cooked, remove and drain on paper towels.

Step 4: For the pickles, take the sliced kohlrabi and carrots, toss with salt, rinse, then mix with a little sugar and vinegar. For the dipping sauce, combine a small bowl of filtered water with sugar, MSG, fish sauce, and vinegar. Stir well until you achieve a balanced sweet, sour, salty, and spicy flavor.
Ladle the dipping sauce into bowls, add the pickled vegetables, sprinkle with black pepper, and serve alongside the hot Bánh gối.
Final Requirements:
The dumplings should be golden brown, intact, and crispy. The filling should be fragrant, and the dipping sauce well-balanced.
Notes for making Bánh gối:
Choose quality ingredients: Use standard flour and ensure meat, vegetables, and mushrooms are fresh.
Prepare the wrappers: Handle the wrappers gently and ensure they are of even, moderate thickness—neither too thick nor too thin.
Shape and size: Traditionally shaped into a half-moon (pillow shape). Adjust the size to suit your preference.
Peanuts and seasoning: Roasted peanuts or extra pepper can be added to the filling for enhanced flavor.
Cooking: Ensure the oil is hot enough so the dumplings cook evenly and turn golden. If boiling (for other variations), cook in boiling water for 5-7 minutes.
Enjoy hot: Bánh gối is best enjoyed immediately after frying. Serve with sweet and sour fish sauce or your favorite dipping sauce.

mon_an.ten: Fried Sweet Potato Balls with Sugar
mon_an.mo_ta: Sweet potatoes are excellent for your health, but simply boiling or steaming them can get boring. Try these sugar-coated fried sweet potato balls! They are incredibly fragrant, delicious, easy to make, and not at all heavy. Give it a try!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A pinch of cinnamon powder (for coating)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the sweet potatoes thoroughly. You can either boil or steam them until tender.
Step 2:
Once cooked, peel the potatoes and mash them until smooth.
Step 3:
In a large bowl, combine the rice flour, all-purpose flour, sugar, salt, and baking powder.
Step 4:
Add the mashed sweet potatoes to the bowl and mix well.
Step 5:
Slowly pour in the hot fresh milk.
Step 6:
Use a spoon to incorporate the milk into the potato and flour mixture.
Step 7:
Wear plastic gloves and knead the dough until smooth and all ingredients are fully combined. Using gloves ensures hygiene.
Step 8:
Once the mixture is smooth, divide the dough into equal portions and roll them into small balls. Repeat until all the dough is used.
Step 9:
Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, drop the potato balls in to fry. Occasionally turn them with chopsticks to prevent burning and ensure even cooking.
Step 10:
Fry until the balls are golden brown, then remove and drain on paper towels.
Step 11:
While the balls are still hot, roll them in sugar and sprinkle with a bit of cinnamon powder for aroma (optional).
And there you have it—delicious sugar-coated fried sweet potato balls! So easy, right?

mon_an.mo_ta: Cat's tongue cookies (Langues de Chat) are a beloved classic known for their simple shape, easy preparation, and sweet, crispy, buttery flavor. These cookies are addictive and perfect for snacking on all day! Making them at home allows you to adjust the ingredients to suit your family's taste. Let's start baking a batch for your family to enjoy.
cac_buoc: Preparation
Prepare the necessary tools: oven, baking tray, hand mixer, parchment paper, and a piping bag with a plain tip (1cm diameter).
Sift the flour until fine and set aside in a bowl.
Cooking Steps
Step 1: Preheat your oven to 180°C before starting the other steps so it reaches the correct temperature.
Step 2: Place the butter and salt in a bowl. Use a hand mixer to cream the butter until smooth.
Step 3: Add the sugar and continue beating until the mixture is well-combined and smooth.
Step 4: Take the egg whites and pour them slowly into the mixture, whisking constantly. Continue mixing until the batter is uniform in color, soft, and smooth.
Step 5: Gradually add the sifted flour, folding it in gently by hand. Mix until the batter is well-incorporated.
Step 6: Add the vanilla to the mixture and stir for a moment longer.
Step 7: Transfer the batter into the piping bag. Line the baking tray with parchment paper. Pipe the batter into strips about 5cm long, leaving about 3cm of space between each cookie.

Step 8: Place the tray in the oven. Bake each batch for about 10-12 minutes until the cookies are cooked through, golden, and slightly browned around the edges. Remove and repeat with the remaining batter.
Notes
Wait for the cookies to cool completely before storing them in an airtight container.
If the cookies lose their crunch, bake them in the oven at 110°C for about 5 minutes to crisp them up again.

mon_an.mo_ta: This Kimchi Pizza is visually stunning with its golden-brown, slightly charred crust, rich and creamy cheese, and the aromatic, tangy-spicy kick of kimchi. Combined with savory bacon and crunchy mushrooms on a crispy base, every bite is a delight. Served with chili sauce or ketchup, it offers a fantastic flavor experience.
cac_buoc: How to make delicious Kimchi Pizza
Soak the shiitake mushrooms in water until soft, wash thoroughly, drain, and slice into bite-sized pieces.
Grate the mozzarella or cut it into small strips.
Squeeze the excess liquid from the kimchi (reserve the juice) and chop into bite-sized pieces.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the green onions, wash, and finely chop.
Slice the bacon into small pieces. Pan-sear the bacon until cooked and the fat has rendered, making it slightly crispy. Remove the bacon and set aside.

In the same pan with the rendered bacon fat, sauté the kimchi. Add the bacon back in, season with a little sugar, and toss briefly. Keep the reserved kimchi juice to use as a sauce for the pizza topping.

Place the pizza crust down, then spread the sautéed kimchi and bacon over it. Sprinkle a layer of mozzarella on top and drizzle with the kimchi sauce. Bake in the oven at 260°C for 5-10 minutes. Once cooked, turn off the oven, remove the pizza, sprinkle with sesame seeds and green onions, and serve hot.
Tips for a perfect Kimchi Pizza
You can use mushrooms specifically recommended for pizza toppings.
Add various bell peppers to increase the color and flavor profile of the pizza.
Feel free to use any type of cheese you prefer.
Black olives or sweet corn can be added to make the pizza more attractive and flavorful.
Besides bacon, you can add sausages or similar meats. You can also experiment with seafood, BBQ pork, chicken, or salmon.
If you don't want to use a store-bought base, you can make your own pizza dough from scratch.
Adjust the amount of green onions and toasted sesame seeds according to your preference.

The finished Kimchi Pizza features a beautiful golden-brown crust, rich melted cheese, and the unique tangy-spicy flavor of kimchi and bacon. It's a wonderful fusion dish that you can easily make at home with familiar ingredients. It's a great way to show off your culinary skills to friends and family—you're sure to receive plenty of compliments. Don't hesitate, get in the kitchen and try it now!

mon_an.mo_ta: With a very simple method and easy-to-find ingredients, making butter milk cookies is easier than ever. Get into the kitchen and whip up these delicious treats for the whole family!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cream the butter and sugar together until the mixture is smooth and well-combined.
Step 2: Add the eggs, fresh milk, and vanilla extract. Whisk until you have a smooth butter-milk mixture.
Step 3: Gradually sift the flour into the mixture. Do not dump all the flour in at once to avoid clumping. Knead until the dough is smooth, elastic, and no longer sticks to your hands.

Step 4: Place the dough on a clean flat surface and roll it out to a thickness of about 3-5mm. Use cookie cutters to create beautiful shapes. You can find various shapes at baking supply stores or supermarkets.
Step 5: Bake the shaped cookies at 180°C for 15-20 minutes until golden.
Once the cookies are done, remove them from the oven and let them cool before enjoying.

Children will love these cute cookies; they are crispy, rich, and buttery—truly addictive. There's no need to buy store-bought cookies anymore; with this simple recipe, you can have fragrant, crispy homemade butter milk cookies in no time.
Pairing these cookies with a glass of fresh milk makes them even more delicious. Give it a try today!

mon_an.ten: Crispy Sweet Potato and Shrimp Fritters
mon_an.mo_ta: Sweet potato and shrimp fritters attract diners with their vibrant golden color and delicious aroma. When enjoyed, you will experience the crunchiness of the crust and the fresh, flavorful taste of the shrimp. Serving these fritters with a sweet and sour dipping sauce and fresh herbs makes for a wonderful snack! Let's explore how to make these incredibly delicious and crispy sweet potato and shrimp fritters!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - Salt, turmeric powder, fresh herbs, sweet and sour dipping sauce
cac_buoc: How to make sweet potato and shrimp fritters:
Peel the sweet potatoes and cut them into strips about 5 cm long.

Remove the heads, tails, and legs of the shrimp, devein them, then rub with salt and rinse thoroughly. Let them drain completely. If you don't use salt, you can rinse the shrimp with a little wine to remove the fishy smell before rinsing with water.

Place the crispy frying flour in a large bowl with 1/4 tsp salt and 3/4 tsp turmeric powder, then mix with 425 ml of water until the batter is smooth. Adding turmeric powder enhances the flavor and gives the dish an eye-catching color.
Next, add the julienned sweet potatoes and shrimp into the batter bowl and mix well.

Once the ingredients are prepared, place a pan over medium heat and add enough oil to submerge 3/4 of the fritters. When the oil is hot, use a large flat spoon to scoop up some sweet potato strips, place a shrimp on top, and gently slide it into the hot oil. Next, scoop a little extra batter over the shrimp to bind it to the potato base. Fry for about 4–5 minutes until the bottom is golden and crispy, then flip and fry for about 1 more minute. Note that this side fries quickly because shrimp cooks very fast; do not overcook or the shrimp will become tough.

Once cooked, remove the fritters and place them in a colander to drain, then move them to a tray lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil. Finally, serve the fritters with various fresh herbs and sweet and sour dipping sauce. You can also serve them with fresh rice vermicelli if desired.
Notes for perfect sweet potato and shrimp fritters:
1. When mixing the batter, do not make it too thin or too thick, as it will affect the taste and cooking time.
2. If you do not like turmeric powder, you can omit it.
3. Besides sweet and sour dipping sauce, you can serve these with chili sauce or any sauce of your choice.
4. Depending on the saltiness of the fish sauce used, adjust the amount of sugar and water to suit your family's taste.

5. How to make sweet and sour dipping sauce: Mix 1/4 cup fish sauce + 1/4 cup sugar + 1 cup filtered water until dissolved, then slowly add lime juice for a light sourness. Finally, stir in minced garlic and chili.
How to choose fresh shrimp:
Good shrimp should have firm bodies and hard shells. They should be translucent white, not cloudy or turning red or yellow.
The head should be firmly attached to the body, legs should be intact, and there should be no fishy or spoiled odor.
Secrets to distinguish freshness by shrimp type:
Lobster: Those with translucent blue legs and shiny shells are fresh.
He shrimp: Should still be jumping, with a pinkish-white color and green eyes.
Tiger shrimp: Should have a smooth, shiny shell with a clear and translucent line along the back.

Absolutely do not buy shrimp that have turned deep pink, where the head and legs are detached from the body, or that have a spoiled smell, as they are old, won't taste good, and can be dangerous to eat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Bánh Tôm Hồ Tây is not only a popular dish loved by both adults and children but also stands out with its rustic yet rich flavor that leaves a lasting impression on anyone who tries it. This dish has even conquered international diners, leaving a deep mark in their hearts. If you want to learn how to make delicious West Lake shrimp fritters, follow this article! Enjoy crispy Bánh Tôm Hồ Tây - one of the best dishes in Vietnam. Simple instructions for making shrimp fritters at home. Awaken your taste buds and discover the signature flavor of this Hanoi specialty.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Dipping sauce - As needed (includes fish sauce, sugar, vinegar, garlic, chili, filtered water, lime)
cac_buoc: 1. Ingredient preparation
1.1. Prepare the shrimp

To reduce the fishy smell, soak the shrimp in diluted salt water for about 10 minutes. Then, cut off the heads and peel the shells, keeping only the tail shells. Next, devein the shrimp and rinse with water several times until clean and drained.

To devein the shrimp quickly, count back from the tail and find the second joint between the shell segments. Pierce a toothpick through this spot and gently pull the black vein out. You can also use a toothpick to lift the vein from the head area and pull it out by hand.
1.2. Prepare other ingredients
Peel the sweet potatoes, slice them, and cut them into small strips, then soak them in a bowl of diluted salt water for about 10 minutes. Rinse with water and drain in a basket.
Peel the carrot, carve it into flower shapes, and slice thinly. Peel the kohlrabi, slice it, and cut into bite-sized squares or rectangles.
To pickle the carrot and kohlrabi, place them in a bowl and soak with about 2 tbsp of vinegar for 15 minutes, then remove and drain. Peel and mince the garlic. Rinse and finely chop the chili.
Remove the roots and damaged leaves from the lettuce, wash thoroughly, and soak in diluted salt water for 15 minutes. Rinse again with clean water and drain.
2. Mix the batter and marinate the shrimp
In a bowl, combine 200 g of all-purpose flour and 100 g of tapioca starch. Gradually add 150 ml of water and mix until the batter is smooth.
Next, crack 2 eggs into the batter bowl and mix well. Let the batter rest for 30 minutes.
To marinate the shrimp, use 1 tbsp seasoning powder, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Mix these ingredients and marinate the shrimp for about 15 minutes.
3. Fry the fritters
After cutting the sweet potatoes into strips, add them and the shrimp into the batter mixture and mix well.
Place a pan on the stove over high heat. Add 4 tbsp of oil and wait until hot. Then, scoop a portion of the batter, sweet potato, and shrimp mixture into the pan.
Ensure the shrimp is in the center and fry for about 4 - 5 minutes until both sides are golden and crispy. Remove the fritters and place them on paper towels to drain the oil.
4. Prepare the dipping sauce

In a bowl, pour 50 ml of filtered water. Add 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tsp MSG, and 1/2 tsp pepper. Stir until the seasonings dissolve. Next, add 2 tbsp vinegar, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp minced garlic, and 1/2 tsp minced chili. Stir well to combine all ingredients.
Adjust the seasoning to your taste and pour the sauce into small bowls. You can add the pickled carrots and kohlrabi to the dipping sauce for a sweet and sour mix.
Arrange the shrimp fritters and lettuce on a plate and enjoy with the sweet and sour dipping sauce.

The fritters have a beautiful golden color and a fragrant aroma. With the crispy sweet potato crust combined with the sweet shrimp meat, you will feel the harmony of these two ingredients. When eaten with fresh lettuce and dipped in the flavorful sweet and sour sauce, you will experience an irresistible taste.
Notes for making crispy shrimp fritters
Do not add too much sweet potato or make the fritters too large, as smaller fritters will be crispier from the inside out. The ideal temperature for frying is between 170 and 180 °C.
If you don't eat all the fritters at once, fry them until just cooked and remove. When ready to eat, fry them a second time to make them extra crispy.
For a crispy exterior and soft interior, fry the fritters at a high temperature of 190 to 200 °C so the crust crisps up quickly.
How to buy fresh ingredients
1. How to choose fresh shrimp
Choose shrimp with transparent shells that are active and jumping.
Shrimp should be intact, with the head and body firmly attached, legs not detached, and the tail folded neatly.
Avoid buying shrimp that are mushy or have a strange odor.
2. How to choose good sweet potatoes
Choose sweet potatoes with smooth surfaces and no cracks.
When picked up, they should feel heavy, firm, and not bruised.
Avoid buying very large potatoes as they may be fibrous; choose medium-sized ones.
Pay attention if the sweet potatoes have black spots or pits, as these are signs of spoilage.
3. How to choose good carrots
Choose carrots with a straight shape, shiny skin, and bright color.
When held, they should feel firm, hard, and heavy, which are signs of fresh carrots rich in vitamins.
Prioritize carrots with a small core as they are usually sweeter.
Avoid buying carrots with leaves/stems still at the base if the shoulder is very large and thick, as these are often less sweet and nutritious.
Do not choose misshapen, dark-colored, bruised, or wilted carrots.
4. How to choose good kohlrabi
Choose kohlrabi bulbs with a diameter of 7 to 9 cm, as these are usually the best.
When held, they should feel heavy and firm, not soft.
Prioritize bulbs with a fresh light green color, no insect damage or bruises, and no rotten or chemical smell.
Avoid buying pre-peeled kohlrabi, as they are often soaked in chemicals to maintain freshness.
Do not choose bulbs that are too large, bruised, or crushed.
Avoid bulbs without stems and leaves, as this may be a sign they are not fresh.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Delicious Homemade Bánh Tráng Trộn Recipe
cac_buoc: Bánh tráng trộn is a popular Vietnamese street snack, especially loved by young people. With its versatile variations, each version brings unique flavors and colors, making it unforgettable after every taste. In the article below, we will share a simple and delicious way to make bánh tráng trộn.
I. Simple and Delicious Bánh Tráng Trộn Recipe
1. Ingredients
1 pack rice paper
5 quail eggs
2 kumquats
1/2 green mango
20g liver jerky (black beef jerky)
20g beef jerky or shredded dried squid
25g green onions and shallots
25g Vietnamese coriander
25g roasted peanuts
1/4 cup cooking oil
1/2 tbsp chili oil (sa tế)
1/2 tbsp dried tiny shrimp
1/2 tsp shrimp salt
1 tbsp liver jerky sauce
Soy sauce and some fried shallots
Prepare knives, scissors, bowls, plates, a peeler, and disposable gloves
2. Cooking Steps
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Cut the rice paper into bite-sized strips.
Wash the mango, peel it, and shred it into thin strips.
Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, sauté the chopped green onions for a few seconds, then turn off the heat and pour into a bowl.
Boil the quail eggs and peel them.
Step 2: Mix the rice paper
Combine the cut rice paper and Vietnamese coriander.

Next, add the shredded mango, dried tiny shrimp, chili oil, beef jerky, liver jerky... and other prepared ingredients, then squeeze the kumquat juice into the bowl. Add the liver jerky sauce, scallion oil, a little soy sauce, and fried shallots. Mix everything thoroughly.
Place the mixed rice paper on a plate, then add the boiled quail eggs and roasted peanuts.
Step 3: Finish

Once the mixing process is complete, the bánh tráng trộn can be enjoyed immediately, with a flavor that rivals any snack shop. The combination of Vietnamese coriander, beef jerky, peanuts, dried shrimp, quail eggs, and sauce creates an attractive and unique taste.
II. Bánh Tráng Trộn with Scallion Oil Recipe
1. Ingredients
Rice paper: 100g
Cooking oil: 200ml
Green onions: 5 stalks
Shallots: 10 bulbs
Shrimp salt: 2 tsp
2. Preparation Steps

Use scissors to cut the rice paper into bite-sized strips according to your preference. Clean the green onions by removing the roots, washing thoroughly, and finely chopping. Peel the shallots, wash, drain, and slice thinly.
Note: For this dish, choosing thin rice paper will result in a better flavor.
Step 2: Fry the shallots and make scallion oil

Place a pan on the stove. When hot, add 100ml of cooking oil and heat over low heat until simmering, then add the sliced shallots. When the shallots are dry and golden, turn off the heat and use a slotted spoon to remove them into a bowl.

To make scallion oil, place the finely chopped green onions in a large bowl. Boil 100ml of cooking oil, then pour the hot oil over the green onions and stir well with a spoon until the onions are cooked.
Step 3: Mix the rice paper and enjoy
Place the shredded rice paper in a large bowl, then add 2 tsp of shrimp salt, fried shallots, and scallion oil. Stir well so the ingredients coat the rice paper evenly to complete the dish.

Bánh tráng trộn with scallion oil is best enjoyed right after mixing. The rice paper has just the right chewiness from being evenly coated in oil without being too soggy; the shrimp salt provides a salty and spicy kick, while the crispy fried shallots combined with the richness of the scallion oil create an irresistible flavor.
III. Tây Ninh Style Bánh Tráng Trộn Recipe
20g beef jerky
20g dried squid
20g liver jerky
100g rice paper
10 quail eggs
20g peanuts
10g Tây Ninh shrimp salt
10g dried tiny shrimp
Shallots, garlic
Cooking oil
3 kumquats
1 mango
Vietnamese coriander
2. Preparation Steps
Use scissors to cut the rice paper into bite-sized pieces.
Peel the mango, wash, and shred into strips.
Trim the Vietnamese coriander, wash, and chop finely.
Boil the quail eggs, then peel them.
Roast the peanuts until fragrant, then remove the skins.
Peel and thinly slice the shallots.
Halve the kumquats and squeeze for juice.
Step 2: Prepare fried shallots, fried garlic, and chili oil
Pour 3 tbsp of oil into a pan and heat. Add the shallots and fry over high heat, stirring constantly until fragrant and golden, then remove and drain through a sieve.
Add 2 tbsp of oil to the same pan, heat, then add the garlic and stir constantly. When the garlic turns slightly golden, remove and drain.
Heat the remaining oil in the pan and turn off the heat. Add the dried chili flakes and stir well to complete the chili oil.

Place the rice paper in a large bowl, add 1 tbsp of Tây Ninh shrimp salt and 1-2 tbsp of kumquat juice to taste. Mix well. Next, add 1 tbsp of fried garlic, 3 tbsp of peanuts, 2 tbsp of fried shallots, 2 tbsp of dried shrimp, 2 tbsp of chili oil, Vietnamese coriander, shredded mango, a bit of beef jerky, and dried squid. Mix until the rice paper is evenly seasoned. Finally, add the quail eggs and mix gently.

Serve the bánh tráng trộn on a plate, sprinkle with more peanuts, beef jerky, dried squid, liver jerky, mango, and Vietnamese coriander. You can now enjoy your delicious homemade Tây Ninh style bánh tráng trộn!
IV. Tips for Making Bánh Tráng Trộn at Home
You can adjust the amount of chili oil and kumquat juice to suit your personal taste.
Do not add the quail eggs too early to avoid crushing them.
Making your own fried shallots, fried garlic, and chili oil will provide the best flavor, but if you are short on time, you can use pre-made products.
Bánh tráng trộn is most delicious when eaten immediately after mixing to prevent the rice paper from losing its texture if left for too long.

mon_an.ten: Irresistible Pandan Bánh Trôi Nước Recipe
mon_an.mo_ta: This chilly weather is perfect for enjoying a warm sweet soup. Learn how to make Pandan Bánh Trôi Nước to treat your family—it's absolutely delicious! Check out our recipe below.
cac_buoc: Wash the pandan leaves and cut into sections. Blend them in a blender until smooth. Filter to get the pandan juice, pour into a clean bowl, and set aside.
Put the glutinous rice flour in a bowl. Boil the pandan juice and slowly pour the hot liquid into the flour. Knead until the dough is smooth and has a beautiful green color.
You can buy prepared mung beans at the market or make the filling yourself using the method below:

Soak the mung beans for 4-5 hours, then rinse and steam until tender. Blend the sugar and mung beans until smooth. Use a non-stick pan to sauté the blended mung beans over low heat until thickened, then pour in the coconut milk and continue cooking over low heat. Stir constantly with a spatula until the mung beans form a non-stick mass, then turn off the heat. Add the shredded young coconut, mix well, and roll into small balls. Adjust the size of the balls as desired.

Once the filling is ready, divide the dough into equal small pieces and roll them into balls. Flatten each piece of dough, place a mung bean ball in the center, and wrap the dough around it, rolling it back into a ball. Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook the rice balls until they float.

Once the balls float, boil for a few more minutes, then remove and place them in a bowl of cold water. Then, take the balls out and add them to a pot of ginger-sugar syrup. Bring the syrup to a boil once more to finish.
Ladle the bánh trôi nước into small bowls. Drizzle with coconut milk and sprinkle with some toasted sesame seeds and shredded young coconut. Serve this warm sweet soup to everyone.
It's so simple to make this delicious Pandan Bánh Trôi Nước!

mon_an.ten: Simple and Delicious Homemade Potato Chips Recipe
mon_an.mo_ta: Potato chips are a favorite snack for many young people, but not everyone knows how to make them well at home. Today, we will share a recipe for crispy and delicious potato chips!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash and peel the potatoes. Use a peeler or a paring knife to slice them as thinly as possible. Next, soak the potato slices in diluted salt water for about 30 minutes to prevent browning and make them crispier.

Step 2: Drain the potatoes and place them in a large bowl. Marinate with 1.5 – 2 packs of Hảo Hảo noodle seasoning powder. Mix well so the potatoes are evenly coated and let them marinate for about 30 minutes.

Step 3: Place a pan on the stove, add oil, and heat it up. Fry the potatoes in enough oil to keep them fully submerged so they don't burn. When the chips are golden brown and float to the surface, remove them and drain the oil before enjoying.

mon_an.mo_ta: Fried fish balls are a popular dish in Vietnamese family meals and a favorite snack among young people during gatherings. With this recipe, you can treat your whole family to these delicious fish balls right at home.
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Cut the fish into small pieces and grind into a fine paste.
In a large bowl, combine the fish, garlic, green onions, onion, flour, eggs, salt, sugar, seasoning powder, and pepper.
Mix everything thoroughly and shape the mixture into small balls.
Place a pan over heat, heat the oil, then add the fish balls and fry until golden brown.
Step 2:
Make the sweet and sour sauce:
Add vinegar, sugar, ketchup, and salt to a pot and heat, stirring well; reduce to low heat until the sugar dissolves.
Dissolve cornstarch in water, then pour the mixture into the sauce, stirring constantly, and cook until the sauce is clear and thickened.
Serve the fried fish balls with the sweet and sour sauce for an irresistible treat.

mon_an.mo_ta: These fragrant fried corn patties will surely delight your family members. They are simple to make with easy-to-find ingredients, so why wait? Let's get cooking!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 2 slices of sandwich bread or 1 bread roll, shredded
2 tbsp finely chopped scallions and cilantro
Seasoning: 1 tsp seasoning powder; 1/3 tsp sugar; 1/4 tsp pepper.
cac_buoc: Ingredients you need to prepare for the fried corn patties:
Step 1: Pulse the corn in a blender until slightly broken down.
Step 2: Pour the corn into a bowl and mix with cornstarch, seasoning, scallions, and cilantro.
Step 3: Boil the potato until tender, mash it finely, then mix it into the corn bowl along with the shredded bread. Mix until well combined.
Step 4: Mold small portions of the corn mixture around skewers (you can also shape them into small rounds or logs as desired).
Step 5: Heat oil in a pan; once hot, add the corn skewers and fry over medium heat. When golden brown and even, remove and place on a plate lined with paper towels.
Arrange the fried corn patties on a plate. This dish is best served hot with ketchup, and kids will love it.

mon_an.ten: Grilled Chicken Feet with Sate Sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: Grilled chicken feet are a favorite snack for many. Recently, concerns about food safety at street stalls have made people hesitant to eat them out. Refer to this recipe to make safe and delicious grilled chicken feet at home! Discover this amazing sate-flavored dish with simple, rustic instructions. Perfect for snacking or as a side dish for gatherings.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Preparation
After purchasing the chicken feet, peel off the yellow outer skin, clip the claws, and split the feet in half. For convenience, you can ask the seller to process them beforehand.
Next, use a mixture of vinegar and salt to scrub the chicken feet clean and remove any odors. Rinse several times with clean water and drain.
There are several ways to deodorize chicken feet:
Method 1: Soak the chicken feet in diluted lemon water to remove odors. After soaking, rinse with water and split them.
Method 2: Soak the chicken feet in diluted salt water with ginger for about 15-20 minutes. Then, rinse with clean water and they are ready to use.
Method 3: If using frozen chicken feet, thaw them first, then rinse multiple times with water and use the deodorizing methods mentioned above.
Peel the shallots and garlic, remove the chili stems and lemongrass ends, then wash everything. Finely chop the shallots, garlic, and lemongrass for later use.
Step 2: Marinating the chicken feet

Once prepared, place the chicken feet in a large bowl, then add 4 tbsp sate sauce, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1 tbsp minced shallots, 1/2 tbsp sea salt, 1 tbsp crushed lemongrass, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp honey, and 1 tbsp chili powder.
Mix thoroughly so the chicken feet are evenly coated. Let them marinate in the refrigerator for about 1-2 hours to allow the flavors to penetrate the meat.
Step 3: Grilling the chicken feet

Place the marinated chicken feet in an oven or air fryer and grill at 200°C for about 20 minutes until cooked through. During the process, you can set it for the first 10 minutes, then open the oven or air fryer to flip the feet and grill for another 10 minutes.

Once the chicken feet are cooked, you can garnish with some lettuce for an attractive presentation. Arrange the feet on a plate and serve with a bowl of dipping sauce. This completes the grilled chicken feet with sate sauce.
Step 4: Finished product

Chicken feet grilled in an air fryer have an attractive amber-brown color. They are evenly cooked with crispy skin and well-absorbed spices, creating a savory flavor. When enjoying, you can dip them in a sour, spicy, salty, and sweet chili sauce for a full range of flavors. This is a must-try dish for gatherings with friends!
Tips for delicious grilled chicken feet:
Remember to clean the chicken feet thoroughly and peel the skin to remove any odors.
Marinate the feet for at least 20-30 minutes so they absorb the ingredients and release a wonderful aroma when grilled.

When grilling, remember to occasionally open the oven and flip the feet so they cook evenly on both sides. If you prefer not to boil them first, you can grill them raw, but be sure to grill thoroughly so the inside is fully cooked.
Besides chicken feet, you can use the same method for chicken wings, which are also very tasty.
How to choose good chicken feet:
You can buy chicken feet from reputable sources with clear origins, such as supermarkets or clean food stores. Additionally, you can identify unsafe chicken feet by observing the following:

Water-injected feet look plump and uniform without skin wrinkles. If squeezed lightly, they feel soft, and the toe tips become bloated. Upon further pressing, they are not firm but feel spongy, like a bag of liquid.
If you stroke from the sole down, there may be signs of water dripping or the skin feeling damp as if soaked in liquid.

Besides touching, you can distinguish water-injected feet by the toes. Natural chicken feet usually have 4 curved toes that tend to fold inward; they only bulge when squeezed hard. In contrast, water-injected feet have bloated claws and clearly separated toes.

To identify safe, high-quality feet, look for any abnormalities. Generally, chicken feet are in constant contact with impurities. If not raised in clean conditions, the feet often have calluses or defects and may have an unpleasant smell.
Color: Choose feet with a natural pale pink color; avoid those with strange spots (red, blue, yellow) or a slimy texture.

Nutritional comparison: Experts note that broiler chicken feet have more fat and protein, while free-range chicken feet are much richer in calcium. Consider your needs to choose the most suitable type.

mon_an.mo_ta: This frog porridge features eye-catching colors and a savory aroma. The frog meat is tender and deeply infused with spices. Enjoying it with plain white porridge swirled in the flavorful frog sauce will give you a truly delicious experience!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - ½ tsp salt, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tsp tapioca starch, a pinch of dried chili
cac_buoc: How to make Singaporean frog porridge as good as at a restaurant
Part 1: Preparing the frogs
Wash the frog meat, rub it with a bit of rice wine to remove the fishy smell, then rinse thoroughly with water. Cut the frogs into bite-sized pieces.
Peel and chop the onion.
Clean the green onions, removing the roots and wilted leaves, then rinse and cut into 3cm lengths.
Next, marinate the frog meat with salt, soy sauce, tapioca starch, and dried chili for 20 minutes. Stir occasionally so the spices penetrate evenly.
Once marinated, place a pan on the stove and add oil.
When the oil is hot, fry the frogs until the meat is firm, then remove and drain.

Using the same pan, pour out the excess oil, leaving about 2 tbsp. Heat it up and sauté the onion, ginger, and dried chili. Add the frogs and the pre-mixed sauce, cooking for 2-3 minutes until thickened. Dissolve tapioca starch in water, pour it into the frog mixture, stir well, and cook until the sauce reaches a thick consistency.
Add the green onions and annatto oil, stir to combine, and turn off the heat.
Part 2: Making the white porridge

After washing the rice, add it to 2 liters of chicken stock and cook until the rice is soft. Stir occasionally to prevent the bottom of the pot from burning. You can add more boiling water if the porridge is too thick. Simmer over medium heat until it reaches the desired consistency. When the porridge boils, add the tied pandan leaves and cook until done, then remove and discard the leaves.
Ladle the porridge into a clay pot, then add green onions and sesame oil.
Finally, enjoy the white porridge with the prepared frog meat.
Tips for delicious frog porridge
Soak the rice for 2-3 hours beforehand so it cooks faster and tastes better.
How to choose good frogs
You should buy wild-caught frogs (field frogs) as they are very fragrant, with firm, meaty, and flavorful flesh.
Note the seasonality: Field frog meat is best from September and October onwards. At this time, the frogs are very fat as they store fat for a long winter hibernation.
Key identification: Field frogs usually have slender heads, bright eyes, large muscular thighs, yellowish or white bellies, and black or bright yellow mottled skin on their backs.

When buying, choose large frogs with yellow skin, as these are fat. It is best to buy live frogs and have the seller clean them for you; avoid frozen frogs. Frog meat should be cooked immediately after preparation; if left too long, it loses its aroma and the meat becomes bland.

This frog porridge features eye-catching colors and a savory aroma. The frog meat is tender and deeply infused with spices. Enjoying it with plain white porridge swirled in the flavorful frog sauce will give you a truly delicious experience!

mon_an.ten: Mung Bean Sweet Soup with Tapioca Pearls
mon_an.mo_ta: Mung bean sweet soup with tapioca pearls is incredibly easy to make and tastes wonderful. it is a great way to cool down your whole family during this hot season. To beat the summer heat, today's article will guide you through making this delicious dessert. Hopefully, this will help you have a great treat for your family!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
To make the mung bean sweet soup, first, rinse the beans thoroughly to remove any grit. Soak the beans for about 1 to 2 hours.
Step 2:
Boil the beans for 15-20 minutes until they are fully expanded and soft. During the process, remember to skim the foam and leave the lid slightly ajar to prevent boiling over.
Step 3:

Next, add sugar to the pot of mung beans. Dissolve 1 tbsp of tapioca starch in a little water, then pour it slowly into the pot while stirring constantly. Stop when the soup reaches your desired thickness. Turn off the heat and add 1 tsp of banana essence.
Step 4:
Finally, boil the tapioca pearls until cooked, then remove them and place them in a bowl of cold water.
Step 5:

When serving, layer shaved ice, the sweet soup, grass jelly, tapioca pearls, and coconut milk, then sprinkle shredded coconut on top. With just a few simple steps, you have finished making mung bean sweet soup with pearls and jelly.

mon_an.mo_ta: Those in the South may be very familiar with Chè Khúc Bạch, an attractive snack featuring rich, creamy jelly cubes, the fragrant scent of almonds, and sweet, crunchy longans served chilled for summer. Chè Khúc Bạch has recently moved North and is currently a trending dessert in Hanoi this summer. Today, let's learn how to make delicious Chè Khúc Bạch using this recipe.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Making the Khúc Bạch jelly
Soak the gelatin in a bowl of cold water until soft, then remove and squeeze out excess water.

Combine heavy cream, milk, and sugar in a pot, stirring to dissolve the sugar. Turn on the heat and warm the mixture, then add the softened gelatin and stir until completely dissolved. Add a few drops of almond extract and turn off the heat.
Pour the mixture into a mold; you can use plastic wrap to prevent sticking. Let the mixture cool naturally, then refrigerate until the jelly is firm.
Once the jelly has set, remove it from the mold and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Step 2: Cooking the syrup and other ingredients

Peel the longans and use a sharp knife to carefully cut around the pit, separating the flesh without tearing it. You can refer to the longan and lotus seed sweet soup recipe for the pitting technique.
Toast the almonds until golden or buy pre-toasted ones from supermarkets or bakery shops.
Place a pot on the stove, add water and sugar to reach a moderate sweetness, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat. You can add a few jasmine flowers for fragrance and let it cool.
When serving, place the jelly cubes and longan flesh in a bowl, pour in the syrup, and sprinkle toasted almonds on top to enjoy your delicious Chè Khúc Bạch.
Here is my finished product:
A few notes for cooking Chè Khúc Bạch:

I notice some people boil the longans in the syrup, but in my experience, this makes the longan flesh soft and less crunchy. Therefore, I usually keep the longans fresh (similar to the longan and lotus seed sweet soup method). You can try both ways to see which you prefer.
Chè Khúc Bạch should have a moderate, refreshing sweetness. Depending on your taste, you can adjust the amount of sugar.

When pouring the jelly into the mold, you can line it with parchment paper or plastic wrap for easy removal. The jelly is typically cut into bite-sized cubes. You can use a wavy cutter for a more attractive look.
Adding a few jasmine flowers to the syrup makes the dish even more fragrant (this is optional ^^).

mon_an.ten: Sweet Corn and Tapioca Pearl Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: With chewy tapioca pearls and the sweet fragrance of corn, this sweet soup will definitely keep you coming back for more!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Coconut milk sauce - 200ml coconut milk; 15g sugar; 1 tsp cornstarch + 30ml water mixed in a bowl; a pinch of salt.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the corn, remove the silk, and thinly shave the kernels.
Step 2: Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the tapioca pearls and parboil for 5 minutes. Remove from heat, let sit for a few minutes for the pearls to settle, then drain the water.

Step 3: Now add 800ml of water and the pandan leaf to the pot with the tapioca pearls. Return to medium heat and cook until the pearls are translucent, then add the corn and stir well, cooking for 5 minutes. Finally, add the sugar and a pinch of salt, stirring for another 5-7 minutes.
Stir while cooking to prevent the soup from burning. Adjust the sweetness to your taste before turning off the heat.
Remember that the soup is slightly thin when hot but will thicken as it cools. Therefore, the amount of water may vary.

Step 4: Combine coconut milk, sugar, and salt in a pot. Place over low heat; when it starts to simmer, slowly add the cornstarch mixture, stirring to create a slight thickness before turning off the heat.
Ladle the soup into a glass, pour the coconut milk sauce on top, and enjoy. You can also put the soup in small plastic bags for a fun way to eat it.

mon_an.ten: Spicy and Sour Pickled Baby Ambarella
mon_an.mo_ta: Pickled baby ambarella with chili salt has a sour and spicy taste, perfect as a snack or served with grilled dishes.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the ambarella, peel them, and drop them into a bowl of water mixed with a little salt.
Step 2: Soak for about 15 minutes, then remove and drain well.
Step 3: Add sugar to the bowl of ambarella and let it sit for about 20 minutes until the sugar dissolves and absorbs.
Step 4: Once the sugar has absorbed, add 3 tbsp of salt and 2 or 3 tbsp of chili powder, then toss well.
Step 5: Leave the bowl in a cool place for another 30 minutes, and it's ready to enjoy.
Sweet and sour pickled baby ambarella is very popular among the ladies.
Good luck with this recipe for crispy and delicious spicy pickled baby ambarella!

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy rice is a favorite dish for many, featuring the crunch of rice combined with the savory, chewy texture of pork floss and an attractive color. To ensure health, we should make this delicious, nutritious, and affordable crispy rice at home. Let's learn how to make simple and tasty Cơm Cháy Chà Bông!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cooked rice - neither too dry nor too wet
Seasoning - Fish sauce, sugar, seasoning powder...
cac_buoc: Step 1: Place the cooled rice into a non-stick pan, press it thin, and cook over low, even heat until the rice forms a crust and smells fragrant.
Step 2: When a golden crust forms on the bottom, turn off the heat and carefully remove the rice from the pan. Place it on a cutting board and cut into bite-sized squares.
Step 3: Sun-dry the rice pieces until they are completely dry and the edges start to curl up.
Step 4: Heat a pan with plenty of oil. When the oil is very hot, add the dried rice pieces and deep-fry until golden brown. Once even, remove and place on paper towels.
Step 5: Boil 1 tbsp of water, then add 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp fish sauce, minced chili, and scallion oil. Simmer until it boils, then pour into a bowl.
Step 6: Arrange the crispy rice on a plate, drizzle with the sauce, and sprinkle with fried shallots, fresh scallions, and pork floss.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cơm Cháy Kho Quẹt delights diners with crispy rice served alongside a savory, flavorful caramelized fish sauce dip, featuring tender meat and well-seasoned shrimp. With just a little time in the kitchen, you will have a wonderful dish to treat your family and friends!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Aromatics - Scallions, garlic, shallots, fresh chili
cac_buoc: How to make delicious Cơm Cháy Kho Quẹt
Rinse the dried shrimp to remove dust, soak until soft, then drain.
Peel the shallots and garlic, rinse, and roughly mince.
Clean the scallions and chilies, removing roots and wilted leaves, then rinse and chop finely.
In a small bowl, combine fish sauce, sugar, and 100ml of water, stirring until dissolved.

Use a fragrant, sticky rice variety to cook the rice, then let it cool. Place a heavy stone pan or cast-iron skillet over medium heat until very hot. Lower the heat, add the cold rice, and use a spoon to spread it into a thin, even layer, pressing firmly so the rice sticks together. Cook over very low heat for about 10 minutes until golden and crispy. While still hot, gently fold the rice in half and remove to a plate. If you prefer it crispier, flip it and cook the other side for a few minutes.
Wash the pork belly, drain, and cut into small 1.5x2cm pieces. Place the pork in a pan and stir-fry until golden brown and the fat is rendered, then remove the meat to a separate bowl.

Next, add the minced shallots and garlic to the rendered fat and sauté until fragrant and golden. Add the soaked dried shrimp and stir-fry. Pour the entire fish sauce and sugar mixture into the pan and simmer the shrimp over low heat until they become slightly firm.

Continue adding the golden pork belly to braise with the shrimp until both are firm and the sauce has thickened. Adjust the seasoning to your family's taste. Once the Kho Quet is thick and glossy, add the scallions and minced chili to your preferred spice level, then turn off the heat.
Finally, serve the crispy rice on a plate alongside the bowl of Kho Quet. You can leave the rice in large pieces for diners to break off and dip, or cut it into bite-sized pieces.
Tips for delicious Cơm Cháy Kho Quẹt
If you are short on time, you can pan-fry the rice with a little oil to make it crispy faster.
You should use dried shrimp to maintain the authentic flavor of the dish.
Adjust the seasoning and spice level to suit your family's preferences.
For the best Kho Quet, use pork belly so the dish has both lean meat and fat, making it more flavorful and easier to eat with the crispy rice.

Cơm Cháy Kho Quẹt delights diners with crispy rice served alongside a savory, flavorful caramelized fish sauce dip, featuring tender meat and well-seasoned shrimp. With just a little time in the kitchen, you will have a wonderful dish to treat your family and friends!

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy rice with scallion oil is an irresistible and attractive snack. The crunchy rice pieces, evenly drizzled with rich scallion oil, offer a delightful experience for the taste buds. Making this dish is very simple and can be done by anyone. Use your leftover rice and follow the instructions below! I. Instructions for making crispy rice with scallion oil
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare ingredients
To make crispy rice with scallion oil, prepare the following ingredients:
2 bowls of leftover rice.
4 scallions.

To make this snack, you can use leftover rice from the night before. However, if you don't have leftover rice, you can use hot rice and let it cool naturally to the appropriate temperature before starting. An important note is to let the rice cool completely before processing.
2. Steps to make crispy rice with scallion oil
Step 1: Make scallion oil
Trim the roots and wash the scallions, then finely chop them and place them in a bowl.
Add 1 tbsp of fish sauce and 1/2 tsp of seasoning powder to the scallion bowl, then mix well.
Heat a pan, then add 3 tbsp of cooking oil and bring to a boil.
Pour the boiling oil directly into the scallion bowl and mix well.
Step 2: Make the crispy rice
Place the leftover rice in a pan and use a spoon to spread the rice evenly across the surface. The thinner the rice layer, the crispier it will be.
Turn on low heat and rotate the pan by hand in various directions so the rice browns evenly on the bottom.
When the rice starts to crisp and turn golden, use a spoon to scrape off the top layer of rice to make the crispy base even crunchier and more delicious.
The scraped-off rice can be used to make a second batch of crispy rice following the same steps.
Step 3: Assemble the dish
Scoop the scallions onto the crispy rice in the pan.
Use a spoon to spread the scallion oil evenly over the rice while rotating the pan to prevent burning.
Finally, use a spoon to pry the crispy rice out of the pan, place it on a plate, and prepare to enjoy.
Step 4: Finished product

Crispy rice with scallion oil is a wonderful dish with its crunchiness and vibrant golden color. Topped with fragrant, rich scallion oil and paired with spicy chili sauce, it brings a fantastic flavor.
Crispy rice with scallion oil should be eaten while hot to fully enjoy its flavor. On chilly days, enjoying crispy rice dipped in chili sauce will surely captivate anyone.
II. How to make crispy rice with scallion oil using an air fryer
Glutinous rice: 350g
Sugar: 3 tbsp
Fish sauce: 3 tbsp
Scallions
Horn chili
Shallots
Chili powder
Pork floss
Cooking oil
2. Steps to make crispy rice using an air fryer
Step 1: Prepare the glutinous rice
Soak the glutinous rice in water before use to achieve the best expansion. Soaking overnight gives the best results. If you are short on time, you can soak the rice in hot water for 1-2 hours.
Rinse the rice in water, then pour it into a basket to drain. Add 1 tsp of salt to the rice and stir well so the salt absorbs into the grains.
Wash the scallions and cut into short segments. Finely mince the shallots and horn chili.
Step 2: Steam the glutinous rice
Pour all the prepared glutinous rice into a mesh tray and place a muslin cloth underneath for steaming.
Select the "Steam" mode at 100°C for 30 minutes to cook the rice. Once cooked, pour it into a bowl to cool slightly.
Step 3: Dry the rice

Divide the cooked glutinous rice into bite-sized round pieces, using the rim of a bowl as a mold to flatten the rice onto a drying tray. Place parchment paper under the rice so the pieces don't fall apart. Dry the rice twice to ensure it is as dry as possible.
Drying 1: Place the steamed rice in the dehydrator at 70°C for 60 minutes.
Drying 2: Continue drying the rice at the same 70°C for 90 minutes. This time, parchment paper is not needed.
Step 4: Fry the rice in oil
Use a deep fryer or pot to fry the rice.
Heat the oil and check the temperature by dipping the tip of a chopstick into the oil. If bubbles sizzle up, the oil has reached the right temperature.
Add each piece of dried rice into the hot oil. Fry until the rice is golden brown on both sides and very crispy.
Step 5: Make the scallion oil sauce
Pour the hot oil used for frying the rice into the mixture of chopped scallions and chili to lightly cook them.
Sauté the shallots and horn chili until fragrant.
Add all the fish sauce and sugar, stir well, and cook together. Stir until the fish sauce and sugar thicken into a syrupy glaze.
Step 6: Complete the dish
Brush the fish sauce and sugar mixture onto the crispy rice pieces to create a sweet and salty flavor. The amount of sauce can be adjusted to personal taste.
Add the scallion oil and pork floss on top of the crispy rice according to your preference.
The crunchy rice pieces will blend with the rich flavor of the sauce and pork floss. The richness and aroma of the scallion oil in the sauce will be the highlight of the dish.
Finally, brush on the sauce, add scallion oil and pork floss as desired to create a crispy, delicious dish that harmonizes sweet, salty, and the characteristic aroma of scallion oil.
III. Notes for making crispy rice with scallion oil at home
Apply these tips to achieve even better crispy rice:
To keep the scallion oil a beautiful green color, add a little sugar to the scallions before pouring in the hot oil. This helps the scallions stay bright green and prevents them from turning dark.
Using aromatic jasmine rice or sticky rice to cook the base will make the dish more delicious.
When spreading the rice thinly in the pan, dip the spoon in cold water to prevent the rice from sticking to it.
When making the crispy rice, use low heat and patiently tilt the pan so the rice browns evenly without burning on the bottom.

mon_an.mo_ta: Every day you rack your brain thinking of which side dishes to serve with attractive fish or meat dishes. This pickled cucumber dish is an interesting choice.
