Soak the pith in cold water for about 15 minutes, then drain.
Next, boil another pot of water and dissolve the sugar (amount to taste). Add the mung beans and cook for about 10 minutes or until tender.

Dissolve the tapioca starch in water and slowly pour it into the pot while stirring constantly until the soup begins to thicken (do not make it too thick). Add the pomelo pith and stir over low heat. Add pomelo flowers for fragrance (or substitute with vanilla extract). Turn off the heat once the soup starts to boil.
Finally, ladle the soup into bowls, top with a little coconut milk, and enjoy. Serve hot or with ice.
Tips for making delicious Chè Bưởi:

When removing the bitterness, remember to massage the pith gently but thoroughly with salt to make it crunchy and less bitter. You should also blanch the pith and then soak it in sugar to make it more fragrant and sweet.
When adding the tapioca starch, do not let the soup become too thick, as it will affect the taste.
The sweetness is up to your preference; add more sugar if you like it sweeter, or adjust for a moderate sweetness.
Simmer the mung beans for a bit longer to ensure they are fully cooked and soft, which makes the soup more fragrant and prevents a raw texture.
You can substitute vanilla for pomelo flowers if they are unavailable.

mon_an.ten: Thai-style Chè Củ Năng with Coconut Milk
mon_an.mo_ta: Water chestnuts (also known as mã thầy) are a cooling ingredient perfect for hot summer days. They are often used in sweet soups, pickles, or stews. Chè Củ Năng, coated in tapioca starch and cooked with coconut milk or lotus seeds, is refreshing, fragrant, and has a delightful crunch. Let's learn how to make this delicious Thai-style Chè Củ Năng with Coconut Milk!
cac_buoc: Peel, wash, and dice the water chestnuts.
Wash, blend, and strain the beetroot to get the juice.
Place the water chestnuts in a pot, add the beetroot juice, and add enough water to cover.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce the heat to low.
Once the water chestnuts have absorbed the color, remove them to a bowl. Sift the tapioca starch over them and shake gently to coat all the pieces evenly.
Boil the sugar with water, adjusting the water to your preferred sweetness.
Once the syrup boils, add the water chestnut pearls and cook until the starch coating is translucent and they float.
Serve this Thai-style Chè Củ Năng cold with coconut milk and shaved ice.

mon_an.ten: Red Bean Sweet Soup with Coconut Milk
mon_an.mo_ta: Red bean sweet soup with coconut milk is a very popular dessert. The soft, floury beans combined with the rich, fragrant coconut milk will make anyone who tries it offer nothing but praise. This is an essential dish at any dessert stall, but with this simple recipe, you can enjoy this delicious treat made right in your own kitchen. Please refer to our recipe below.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Tapioca starch or arrowroot powder - 10 gr
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Soak the red beans in water for about 6-8 hours.
Step 2: Cooking steps
After soaking, you will see the beans have expanded and softened enough to be broken in half. Drain the beans and let them dry.
Place the beans in a pressure cooker and add enough water to cover them, about 1 liter. Add a tiny pinch of salt, then cook the beans for about 30-40 minutes.
To check if the beans are tender, use a spoon to take out a bean and try mashing it; if it mashes easily into a paste, the beans are ready.
Next, add the sugar and stir well until completely dissolved, keeping the pot on cooking mode.

Dissolve the tapioca starch or arrowroot powder in a little water, then slowly pour it into the pot. Stir continuously so the starch dissolves completely. Once the pot comes back to a boil and the liquid is clear without lumps, you can turn off the heat.
Ladle the sweet soup into small bowls, top with coconut milk, and enjoy.
Note:
If you find the soup too thin and prefer it thicker, add more starch. However, remember to dissolve it in water first.
If you do not have a pressure cooker, you can use a rice cooker to cook the beans; though it takes a bit longer, the beans will still be soft and delicious.
You can also mix the sweet soup with yogurt; it is guaranteed to be many times more delicious.
Red beans: Choose medium-sized beans rather than very large ones for better flavor. Select fresh beans, avoiding old ones; they should be bright red, free of insects, and have no unpleasant odor.

mon_an.ten: Red Bean Sweet Soup with Jelly
mon_an.mo_ta: Let's upgrade the red bean sweet soup recipe by adding red bean jelly and coconut jelly to make it even more refreshing. This chilled dessert is perfect for students during exam season. Back when I was taking my university entrance exams, my mother used to cook this for me to ensure I stayed cool, refreshed, and alert!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Sort the beans to remove any hollow or spoiled ones. Soak the red beans in cold water for about 4-5 hours until softened.
Step 2: Cook the red bean soup:

Place the beans in a pot of cold water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the beans are soft (use a pressure cooker for speed; it only needs about 10 minutes from the point of boiling). Add sugar to taste and simmer for another 10 minutes for the beans to absorb the sweetness.
Step 3: Make coconut jelly and red bean jelly
Soak the gelatin in cold water until softened, then remove and squeeze out excess water.
Drop 1 sheet of gelatin into the pot of bean liquid and stir until completely dissolved. Let it cool, then place in the refrigerator to set quickly to finish the red bean jelly.
For the coconut jelly, add gelatin to the coconut water and double-boil until the gelatin is completely dissolved, then turn off the heat. Let it cool and refrigerate until set.
Once the jellies have set, cut them into bite-sized pieces. Place them in a bowl, add the red beans, fresh milk, and coconut milk to complete this sweet, refreshing dish.
The finished sweet soup is not only visually appealing but also incredibly refreshing and thirst-quenching.
Secrets to a delicious sweet soup:

With this method, you can use either red beans or black beans. Regardless of the type, selection is very important. Choose plump, even beans that are not spoiled, moldy, or hollow. Always soak the beans until they expand and soften before cooking to speed up the process.

You must simmer the beans until soft before adding sugar. If you add sugar while the beans are still raw, they will become hard and tough and will never soften. I made this mistake the first time I cooked it, so I am sharing this to help you succeed.

Since sugar was added during simmering, the beans and jellies (made from bean liquid and coconut water) are already sweet. I personally do not have a sweet tooth, so I usually use unsweetened milk. If you prefer it sweeter, you can use sweetened fresh milk or add more sugar.

mon_an.ten: Mung Bean and Pumpkin Sweet Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Pumpkin and mung beans are two nutrient-rich foods that have cooling and detoxifying effects, making them excellent for health, especially for the elderly and children. From these ingredients, you can prepare many delicious and attractive dishes for the whole family, particularly sweet soups with their characteristic flavors. In the heat of summer, nothing is better than enjoying a bowl of mung bean and pumpkin sweet soup to cool down. Try this recipe to treat your family to a delicious and enticing dish. Enjoying this fragrant soup is a great way to reap the health benefits of these two nutrient-dense ingredients. Discover how to cook this soup to serve your family a meal that is healthy, refreshing, and full of flavor.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Pumpkin balls - 50g steamed and mashed pumpkin, chilled; 80g glutinous rice flour; 10g sugar; 25g hot water
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the pumpkin and mung beans
Soak the mung beans in water for 1 hour and wash thoroughly. Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds, wash, and cut into small chunks.
2. Make the pumpkin balls

Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the pumpkin and 600ml of water, plus 1g of salt. Cook until the pumpkin is soft. Remove 100g of pumpkin and mash it with a spoon. Add 15g of sugar and 80g of tapioca starch, then mix well. Knead the dough and roll into small balls, then boil until cooked.

Continue to simmer the remaining pumpkin in the pot. If the dough mixture is too runny, you can put it in a non-stick pan and cook over low heat for 30 seconds to 1 minute until the dough becomes pliable. Ensure the outside of the pumpkin balls is dry before boiling. When the color of the pumpkin balls turns translucent, they are cooked.
3. Cook the pumpkin sweet soup
Coconut milk part:
Over low heat, heat 100ml of coconut milk until it begins to simmer.
Add 20g of sugar to the coconut milk and stir until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Dilute 2g of tapioca starch with 1 teaspoon of water, then add it to the coconut milk and stir well. Turn off the heat.
Pumpkin soup part:
In a pot, add the 100g of soaked mung beans to the pumpkin and cook over medium heat for about 10 minutes until the mung beans are soft.
Then, add 800ml of boiling water and 100g of sugar to the pot, continuing to cook until the mixture thickens slightly.
Mix 10g of tapioca starch with a little water and stir well.
Finally, add the boiled pumpkin balls, the starch mixture, and 1 teaspoon of vanilla to the pot, stir well, and turn off the heat.
4. Finished product
After cooking, pour the soup into bowls and drizzle the coconut milk on top. To add more flavor, you can also add a bit of dried coconut. This completes the dish.

This mung bean and pumpkin sweet soup has an eye-catching yellow color and offers a nutty taste from the mung beans and pumpkin, along with the richness of the coconut milk. When eating, you will experience the soft and chewy pumpkin balls which are extremely delicious. You can enjoy this soup hot or cold, depending on your preference.
Secrets to choosing ingredients for a delicious soup
1. How to buy fresh pumpkin

The pumpkin should typically be orange-yellow, combined with a bit of dark green. Its flesh is yellow and offers a sweet fragrance and a relatively chewy texture. When choosing a pumpkin, select those that are heavy, firm to the touch, and have smooth skin.

You should choose pumpkins with stems 2-5cm long and a round shape. These pumpkins are usually naturally segmented into relatively even parts, giving them a better sweet taste and texture. Avoid buying pumpkins with short stems, as these are often prone to rot and spoil quickly.
2. How to buy mung beans
To buy delicious and high-quality peeled mung beans, prioritize purchasing from reputable stores or supermarkets to ensure product quality.
Quality peeled mung beans are usually light yellow, bright in color, large, and plump. The beans should be whole and uniform.

Avoid buying peeled mung beans that are broken, crumbled, or have a musty smell. Such mung beans have usually been stored for a long time and will have a mealy texture, lack fragrance, and won't be nutty when eaten.
Remember to choose carefully and check the product before buying to ensure quality and enjoy the delicious flavor of peeled mung beans.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chè Đậu Xanh Hạt Sen is a refreshing dessert, perfect for hot summer days. Featuring soft mung beans that are good for digestion and nutty, delicious lotus seeds, all combined with a hint of banana essence, coconut milk, and fresh shredded coconut, this dish provides a cooling sensation. Take a little time to make this fragrant dessert! Refer to the recipe for Chè Đậu Xanh Hạt Sen below.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the lotus seeds

You can buy pre-peeled fresh lotus seeds, or buy lotus pods and shell them yourself. To choose delicious fresh lotus seeds, select pods or seeds with dark green skins, which indicates they are mature enough to be nutty and sweet when cooked.

When buying fresh lotus seeds, remove all the lotus germs (the green core), as they have a bitter taste that can ruin the flavor of the dessert, even though they are effective for sedation and treating insomnia. You can use a small pointed toothpick to push through the round hole at one end of the seed until the green germ emerges from the other side.

After removing the germs, briefly blanch the seeds in water with a pinch of salt to remove sap and enhance the nuttiness. Next, change the water and simmer the lotus seeds in a pot until they reach your desired tenderness. You should simmer them for 3-4 hours to ensure they are soft and delicious.
Once the lotus seeds are stewed, remove them and drain in a colander, then rinse with cold water so that the dessert broth remains clear and appetizing.
Step 2: Prepare the mung beans
Wash the mung beans thoroughly before soaking them in cold water to soften. Soak for about 3 hours, then drain, rinse with cold water, and simmer in a pot until they reach your desired softness.
Step 3: Cook the Chè Đậu Xanh Hạt Sen

When the mung beans are soft enough, add the stewed lotus seeds and some sugar. Keep on low heat for another 5 minutes, then turn off the heat. Before serving, taste and adjust the sweetness to your preference.
Finally, ladle the dessert into bowls and enjoy.
Notes for a delicious Chè Đậu Xanh Hạt Sen
The lotus seeds and mung beans should be simmered just right so they are not overcooked while still retaining their delicious flavor.
To enhance the flavor, you can add banana essence, a bit of coconut milk, and fresh shredded coconut when eating for an extra delicious treat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Aloe vera is known as a plant that is very beneficial for beauty and health care. According to scientific research, aloe vera contains many vitamins A, C, E, B1, and minerals good for the human body. Therefore, aloe vera is used as an ingredient in many dishes, especially in summer when Chè Nha Đam becomes a favorite for many. To cook these refreshing bowls of aloe vera dessert yourself, don't miss the instructions below.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Thick, fresh aloe vera leaf - 1 leaf
cac_buoc: Prepare ingredients for Chè Nha Đam:
First, wash the peeled mung beans and soak them in warm water for 30 minutes.
Next, cut the aloe vera leaf into small sections, peel off the green skin, dice into cubes, and soak in water mixed with a few drops of lemon juice and 2 tsp of salt.
Gently rub the aloe vera pieces with your hands to remove all the slime.
Next, drain the aloe vera in a colander and rinse under running water while tossing them. Remember to rinse until the aloe vera pieces become translucent.
How to cook Chè Nha Đam:
Drain the mung beans and put them in a pot with 600 ml of water, then bring to a boil. While boiling, remember to keep the lid open and skim off any foam that rises to the surface.
Once the mung beans have bloomed evenly, add sugar to suit your taste.
Drain the aloe vera, add it to the pot, stir gently, and pour in the vanilla.
Wait for the dessert to boil for about 1 minute, then turn off the heat. Wait for it to cool, then ladle into bowls and enjoy with 2-3 tablespoons of coconut milk.
Tips for cooking Chè Nha Đam:
You should buy fresh aloe vera leaves that are not crushed or scarred, and wash them before preparation.
Aloe vera is naturally slimy and has a pungent smell, so you should soak it in lemon-salt water or limewater to make it crunchier. Then rinse thoroughly with water.
Using rock sugar to marinate the aloe vera after preparation will give the dish a refreshing sweetness and better cooling properties.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chè Nha Đam is a dish perfectly suited for dry, hot days like these. With easy-to-find mung beans and healthy aloe vera blended in a light, moderately sweet broth with a bit of cold ice, it brings a wonderful feeling to the diner. Spend some time in the kitchen to make this wonderful dessert for your family. Everyone will love it, and you'll have a chance to show off your great cooking skills. Let's learn how to cook this delicious dish and get into the kitchen!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Thick, fresh aloe vera leaf - 1 leaf
cac_buoc: Preparation steps:
Wash the peeled mung beans and soak them in warm water for 30 minutes so they bloom and soften.

Next, cut the aloe vera leaf into small sections, peel off the green skin, dice into cubes, and soak in water mixed with a few drops of lemon juice and 2 tsp of salt. This step helps the aloe vera lose its sap and become clearer and tastier.
Then, gently rub each piece of aloe vera with your hands to remove all the slime.
Next, drain the aloe vera in a colander and rinse under running water while tossing them. Rinse until the aloe vera pieces become translucent.
How to cook Chè Nha Đam:
First, drain the mung beans and put them in a pot with 600 ml of water, then bring to a boil. While boiling, keep the lid open and skim off any foam that rises.
Once the mung beans have bloomed, add sugar to suit your taste.
Next, drain the aloe vera, add it to the pot, stir gently, and pour in the vanilla.
Wait for the dessert to boil for about 1 minute, then turn off the heat. Wait for it to cool, then ladle into bowls and enjoy with 2-3 tablespoons of coconut milk.
Notes for a delicious Chè Nha Đam

How to choose good aloe vera: Buy fresh leaves that are not crushed or scarred, and wash them before preparation. Aloe vera is naturally slimy and has a pungent smell, so you must soak it in lemon-salt water. To make it crunchier, you should use limewater for soaking, then rinse thoroughly with water.
Using rock sugar to marinate the aloe vera after preparation will give the dish a refreshing sweetness and better cooling properties.
Mung beans: Choose round, plump, evenly yellow beans so that when eaten, they are soft, smooth, and creamy.
When cooking mung beans, remember to stir occasionally so they don't stick to the bottom and burn.
The sweetness of the dish depends on individual preference. If you like it sweet, add more sugar; if not, add a moderate amount and serve with ice to increase the cooling effect.
When enjoying the dessert, add a little coconut milk to enhance the flavor.

Chè Nha Đam is a dish perfectly suited for dry, hot days like these. With easy-to-find mung beans and healthy aloe vera blended in a light, moderately sweet broth with a bit of cold ice, it brings a wonderful feeling to the diner. Spend some time in the kitchen to make this wonderful dessert for your family. Everyone will love it, and you'll have a chance to show off your great cooking skills. Let's learn how to cook this delicious dish and get into the kitchen!

mon_an.mo_ta: Hot summer days will be more pleasant when this Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu appears. Quickly learn how to cook this delicious, beautiful, and easy dessert for the whole family! You can refer to the method below. ## What is Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu? Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu is a traditional dessert in Vietnamese cuisine. This dish is made from sương sa, a type of transparent and chewy gelatin, combined with fresh "pomegranate seeds." Sương sa is usually made from agar-agar or seaweed powder, then cut into small shapes like pomegranate seeds.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fruits/Vegetables for coloring - purple (magenta plant), green (pandan essence), pink (strawberry essence), yellow (gardenia seeds).
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the jicama, peel, and dice into small cubes (pomegranate seed size).

Step 2: Soak mung beans in warm water for about 1 hour to bloom, then put in a rice cooker, add water just covering the surface, and simmer until tender. Add a little sugar to the beans and blend until smooth.
Step 3: Divide the diced jicama into equal parts and soak them in the prepared colors for about 30 minutes to absorb the pigment.
Step 4: Use 100g of tapioca starch kneaded with hot water until flexible and non-sticky, then shape into small tapioca pearls with coconut meat filling.

Step 5: After the diced jicama has absorbed the color, drain it in a colander. Place each color in a separate bowl to avoid mixing. Pour dry tapioca starch over them and toss well so the starch coats each piece of jicama. Keep each portion separate on a tray.

Step 6: Bring a pot of water to a boil and drop each portion in to cook. Prepare a large bowl of cold water nearby so that when the starch is cooked, you can use a slotted spoon to remove them and immediately place them in the cold water to prevent sticking.
Step 7: Boil 300ml of water, add the coconut milk powder, stir until dissolved, and let cool.

Step 8: Place the colored "pomegranate seeds" into a glass, add tapioca pearls, mung beans, then sprinkle shredded coconut on top. Pour the coconut milk over everything. You can add shaved ice if it's hot and serve.
Wishing you and your family a delicious meal with this fragrant Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu for summer!
How to enjoy Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu
Prepare the dessert: First, ensure the Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu is made and cooled.
Presentation: Place a portion of Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu into a decorative bowl or cup. Try to create a transparent and even layer of gelatin.
Add pomegranate seeds: Spread the fresh "pomegranate seeds" evenly over the gelatin layer. They provide crunch and sweetness.
Add sugar and fruit juice: If desired, you can add a little sugar and fruit juice like orange, pineapple, or mango to increase flavor and freshness.
Scoop and enjoy: Use a spoon to scoop up pieces of gelatin and seeds. Sip the cold dessert, feeling the combination of crunchy seeds, chewy gelatin, and sweet flavor.
Enjoy cold: Chè Sương Sa Hạt Lựu is best enjoyed cold. You can keep it in the refrigerator before serving for a more refreshing experience.

mon_an.ten: Fruit Carving: Animal Shapes for Mid-Autumn Festival
mon_an.mo_ta: In recent years, decorating Mid-Autumn festival trays has become more diverse and creative than ever. One of the prominent trends is carving fruit into animal shapes, creating beautiful and interesting works of art. Let's explore how to carve fruit into animals to create a special highlight for the Mid-Autumn tray! Learn how to carve fruit into animals to decorate the Mid-Autumn tray. Turn fruits into unique and creative artworks, creating a joyful and interesting atmosphere for this traditional festival.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Red cardboard or rose petals - as needed
cac_buoc: 1. How to make a pomelo dog
Peel the pomelo and remove all the pith surrounding the flesh, then separate the pomelo into segments, being careful not to tear the membrane of the segments.
Next, cut off the inner edge of each segment and peel back the membranes on both sides to expose the pulp. You can use a toothpick to gently fluff the pulp and remove the seeds.

Then, use toothpicks to join the large orange and the tangerine together to form the body and head of the "pomelo dog." Pin each fluffed pomelo segment onto this core. Pin horizontally for the body and vertically for the head. Cover the entire frame until no gaps remain.
Next, pin two long pomelo segments on either side of the head for ears. Arrange four segments as legs to make it look more like a dog.

To make it more realistic, use longan seeds, round buttons, or craft eyes for the eyes. Add a round nose and a red tongue made from red paper or rose petals. Add a cute bow, and the pomelo dog is complete.
2. How to make a hedgehog from pear and green grapes
Divide the pear into two parts (the round bottom and the pointed top) and peel the skin off the pointed top part.
Then, use toothpicks to skewer green grapes through the middle and stick them evenly around the round part of the pear.
Next, cut the tip of a black grape and hollow out the core so the circumference fits the pointed tip of the pear; attach it as the hedgehog's nose.
Finally, use black beans for the hedgehog's eyes. The hedgehog is now complete.
The finished hedgehog will be very cute and lovely!
3. How to make a crab from guava and apple
Cut the apple vertically into 3 parts. Use the widest middle part to cut the crab's claws.
Use 1/3 for the shell and the remaining 1/3 to carve the legs.
Take the thick middle part, remove the core, and take the two semi-circle pieces. Use a sharp knife to trace two connected arcs like half of a figure 8.
Next, taper one end to make the claw smaller. Carve a V-shape at the other end.
Carve the legs from the 1/3 portion: cut 8 thin vertical slices.
Arrange 4 slices on each side, larger slices at the bottom and smaller ones on top in a fan shape.
Next, place the 1/3 apple piece on top as the shell. Arrange the claws and press two black beans in for eyes.
Do the same with a guava to get a green crab.
Note: After cutting apples, soak them in light saltwater or water with a few drops of lemon to prevent browning and keep the color beautiful.
4. Carving a crab from an orange
Wash the orange skin and use a sharp knife to peel off a large piece of orange zest.
Next, place the zest on a flat surface. Use the tip of a sharp knife to cut a zigzag pattern, creating two claws at once. If you're not used to it, you can use scissors to cut each part one by one.
Then take another orange and cut it vertically into several wedges. You can cut it into 6 or 8 pieces, then use a knife to slightly separate the flesh at both ends of the wedge.
Once done, tuck the two carved zest claws into the two ends of the orange wedge, turn the skin side up, and use toothpicks to pin two cherries in the middle of the wedge for eyes.
This funny crab is very adorable and not difficult to make!
5. Shaping an owl with an apple
To shape an owl from an apple, you will need 2 green apples, 2 raisins or black beans for eyes, 1 small slice of carrot for the beak, and toothpicks for fixing.
Start by taking one apple for the head and the other for the body. For the head apple, cut two small slices so the white flesh is exposed in a heart shape, intersecting to create a ridge.

Next, hollow out two small holes in the middle of the cut surface of the head apple, then attach raisins or black beans for eyes. Cut a small triangle of carrot and attach it about 1 cm below the eyes for the beak. You can also cut a small apple slice into a triangle and attach it to the top of the head for ears.

With the remaining apple, cut two opposite slices and use toothpicks to fix these two slices to the sides as wings. Use a toothpick to pin the middle and then fix the head on top. When finished, you will have an apple owl ready to decorate your Mid-Autumn tray.
6. Shaping a turtle with an apple
To shape a turtle from an apple, you need 1 slightly long red apple and a small fruit carving knife.

Start by halving the apple. One half will be used as the shell; carve hexagonal patterns onto the surface of this half. The other half will be used for the body. Carve the head, 4 legs, and a tail. Then, use toothpicks to fix the two parts together, and you have completed the red apple turtle.
When choosing apples, select ones with beautiful shiny skin, no scratches or black spots. You should also check the firmness by gently squeezing to avoid old, mealy apples.

Each apple variety has its own size; if using green apples, avoid overly large ones. Instead, choose ones that fit your hand and feel heavy. For red apples, color is key. Choose dark-colored ones as they are usually sweeter and crunchier.
7. Carving a serving bowl and decorative bird from a pineapple

To create a bird from a pineapple, you need a large pineapple with a fresh green crown. Cut off one-quarter of the fruit, including the crown, and trim away half of the leaves, leaving only the top half. The pineapple flesh attached to the crown will be carved into the bird's head.
For the body, scoop out the flesh, leaving the hollow shell intact. The removed flesh is cut into bite-sized pieces and placed back into the hollow shell.
Finally, use toothpicks to fix the bird's head (made from the crown) onto the body. Once these steps are done, you have a pineapple artwork in the shape of a bird.
To choose a fresh, ripe pineapple, look for ones that are evenly yellow across the surface. The fresher the crown leaves, the better and juicier the pineapple.

Additionally, choose pineapples that feel heavy and firm with a faint sweet aroma. When pressed lightly, if it smells sweet and feels slightly soft and elastic, it is ripe. Avoid hard pineapples as they will be sour.

mon_an.mo_ta: This honey glazed chicken wing recipe is a fantastic alternative for those who love this dish but don't have an oven. The wings are crispy and fragrant from being pre-fried, and with every bite, you'll experience a perfect balance of sweet and savory flavors. A special tip in this method is using ketchup, which helps balance the sweetness and saltiness if you happen to over-season. In just about 30 minutes, you can complete this wonderful dish. These honey glazed chicken wings will surely make your family meal much more cozy and enjoyable.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for the honey glazed chicken wings.
Wash the chicken wings thoroughly and cut them into bite-sized pieces.
Drain the chicken wings well and use paper towels to pat them dry.
Next, marinate the chicken wings with 1 tsp salt and 1.5 tsp pepper. Mix well so the chicken absorbs the seasoning and let it marinate for about 10 minutes.
In a small bowl, combine the honey, ketchup, and soy sauce. Stir the sauce mixture well until the ingredients are fully incorporated.
Step 2: Cooking steps for the honey glazed chicken wings.
First, place a pan on the stove and add plenty of cooking oil to heat up.
Once the oil is hot, add the chicken wings and fry until golden brown on both sides. During frying, be sure to flip the wings frequently so they don't over-brown and become dry.
Once the chicken wings are cooked and have a beautiful golden color, remove them and drain the excess oil.
Next, place another pan on the stove and heat 2 tbsp of vegetable oil. Keep the heat at a low or medium level.
Add the fried chicken wings and toss them briefly.
Quickly pour the sauce mixture over the chicken wings.
Simmer the chicken wings in the sauce for a few minutes so the meat absorbs the rich glaze, then turn off the heat.
Finally, serve the chicken wings on a plate, garnish with some greens for extra appeal, and enjoy while hot.
Tips for delicious honey glazed chicken wings:
When simmering the wings, keep the heat at the lowest setting; this allows the wings to absorb the most sauce without burning.
To make the dish tastier and less heavy, serve it with some vegetables.
Besides chicken wings, you can use other parts like chicken thighs or breasts.
For those on a diet, use chicken breast and follow this recipe but use an oven at 180°C.

This honey glazed chicken wing recipe is a fantastic alternative for those who love this dish but don't have an oven. The wings are crispy and fragrant from being pre-fried, and with every bite, you'll experience a perfect balance of sweet and savory flavors. A special tip in this method is using ketchup, which helps balance the sweetness and saltiness if you happen to over-season. In just about 30 minutes, you can complete this wonderful dish. These honey glazed chicken wings will surely make your family meal much more cozy and enjoyable.

mon_an.ten: Pumpkin Sweet Soup with Coconut Milk
mon_an.mo_ta: Pumpkin is a highly nutritious food rich in beta-carotene (a form of provitamin A) which is very beneficial for the body. From pumpkin, you can cook many delicious and attractive dishes such as stir-fries, soups, stews, or pumpkin puree. Additionally, you can use pumpkin to cook various types of pumpkin sweet soup (suitable for both summer and winter) to refresh and detoxify the body. Let's cook this cool and sweet pumpkin sweet soup with coconut milk that is both easy and delicious.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds, and scrape away the inner pulp. Wash and cut into small pieces (to help it cook until tender faster).
Step 2: Boil water, add the pumpkin to the pot and cook until soft, then turn off the heat. Let the mixture cool slightly, then pour into a blender and blend until smooth.
Step 3: After blending, strain the mixture through a sieve to remove any lumps, then pour it back into the pot. Add sugar to taste and bring back to a boil.

Step 4: Dissolve the kudzu powder in water, then slowly pour it into the boiling soup while stirring constantly until the soup reaches your desired thickness. Add the coconut milk, stir well, bring back to a boil, and turn off the heat. Ladle into bowls or cups for a sweet, cool, and delicious pumpkin dessert.
A few tips for a delicious pumpkin sweet soup with coconut milk:

A good pumpkin should feel heavy and firm, with smooth skin, no spots or blemishes, and must be fresh without being soft or rotten. The inner pulp should be completely scraped away for a smooth soup. Although pumpkin cooks quickly, cutting it into thin slices will reduce cooking time and save electricity or gas.

If you don't have a blender, you can remove the boiled pumpkin to a bowl and mash it with a spoon. Boiled pumpkin is very soft, so it is easy to mash smoothly. Remember to strain it through a sieve when putting it back into the pot to remove any large lumps for a smooth consistency.

Using rock sugar is best for pumpkin sweet soup as it provides a very refreshing sweetness. However, if rock sugar is unavailable, you can use regular white sugar, or even brown sugar or palm sugar. I have tried cooking it with brown sugar and palm sugar, and it tastes very good too.
The amount of sugar for pumpkin sweet soup will be less than other types of sweet soup because pumpkin is naturally sweet. It is best to add sugar gradually and taste to suit your preference.
Cooking pumpkin sweet soup with kudzu powder helps with cooling and detoxification. However, if you don't have kudzu powder, you can substitute it with tapioca starch.
You can also add a bit of mung beans or peanuts for extra flavor.

The bowl of pumpkin sweet soup will have a beautiful orange-yellow color with a smooth, velvety consistency. You can drizzle coconut milk on top or decorate with patterns as desired, then garnish with a mint leaf for a professional look.
Using a similar method, you can also try the recipe for purple sweet potato soup with coconut milk, which is also very delicious!

mon_an.mo_ta: Make refreshing and delicious Chè Bưởi with crunchy pomelo pith, soft aromatic mung beans, and rich, creamy coconut milk for the whole family on a hot day.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pomelo pith for Chè Bưởi
1. Prepare the pith:
Peel the green skin off the pomelo, keeping only the white pith. Score the pith vertically and gently remove it from the fruit.
Remove any remaining fibers from the inner side of the pith and cut into bite-sized pieces.
2. Mix the pith with about 6 tbsp of salt, then add warm water to soak. Place a heavy object on top to keep the pith submerged. Soak for about 5-6 hours.
3. Squeeze the pith and rinse thoroughly with clean water to remove the bitterness, pungency, and saltiness.
Tip: If you're short on time, massage the pith with salt and a bit of warm water, then squeeze and rinse with cold water. Repeat this process 2-3 times to remove the bitterness.
4. Blanch the pith: Bring water to a boil, add the pith, and bring back to a boil. Quickly remove the pith and submerge it in a bowl of ice water to keep it crunchy.
5. Remove and squeeze dry.
6. Marinate the pith with sugar: Place the pith in a pot or deep pan, add sugar, and toss well until evenly coated.

7. Let sit for 10-15 minutes until the sugar dissolves and absorbs. Turn on low heat to simmer the pith, gradually adding water so the pith absorbs it and expands. Once the pith is plump and hydrated, quickly add tapioca starch and toss until it's absorbed and forms an even coating outside.
8. Prepare a separate bowl of ice water.

9. Bring a pot of water to a boil, then gradually drop in the starch-coated pith. Cook until the pith becomes translucent like pearls and floats to the surface. Quickly remove and transfer to the ice water to keep them crunchy and prevent sticking.
Step 2: Steam the mung beans
1. While waiting for the water to boil in Step 1.4, rinse the peeled mung beans and soak in warm water until softened.
2. While boiling the pith in Step 1.9, steam the mung beans until tender.
Step 3: Make the coconut milk

Add a little warm water to the grated coconut and squeeze to extract the milk. Bring to a boil on the stove, then add cornstarch slurry (cornstarch dissolved in a little water) and stir until thickened. If you prefer, you can use canned coconut milk from the supermarket, which costs about 20-25k per can.
Step 4: Cook the Chè Bưởi

Use the water from Step 1.9, add pandan leaves, and bring to a boil for aroma. Remove the leaves, add sugar to taste, then add the pomelo pith. Mix tapioca starch with water and slowly pour into the pot, stirring constantly until it reaches your desired thickness. Add the steamed mung beans and stir well.
Adjust the sweetness to taste and turn off the heat. You can add a drop of pomelo flower essential oil for extra fragrance.
Once cooled, serve in a bowl with crushed ice, ladle the sweet soup over it, and drizzle with coconut milk.
My tips for delicious Chè Bưởi:

In the process of making Chè Bưởi, preparing the pith is the most complex and decisive factor. The pith must be free of bitterness while remaining crunchy and chewy. Some suggest using lime water or alum, but you can try my method: just soak and massage with salt 2-3 times, then shock in ice water after blanching. It will be crunchy without any chemicals.
Be sure to toss the pith with tapioca starch while it's still hot so the starch absorbs deeply. This is the secret to a crunchy and chewy texture.
Mung beans should remain whole and not mushy, so only steam them until just tender.
Homemade coconut milk is best, but canned is a convenient alternative (about 20-25k). You can also use coconut milk with other desserts like purple sweet potato or pumpkin sweet soup.

mon_an.ten: Refreshing Chè Đậu Xanh for Summer
mon_an.mo_ta: This mung bean ball sweet soup is not only delicious and refreshing but also great for cooling down. Give it a try!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Rinse the mung beans and soak for 4-5 hours. Rinse again with cold water, then steam or cook until tender.

Step 2: Blend the hot mung beans with coconut milk until smooth. Pour into a bowl, gradually add glutinous rice flour, and knead (wear gloves). The dough should be smooth, pliable, and non-sticky. Note: Adjust with more flour or liquid if needed.
Step 3: Roll the dough into small marble-sized balls.
Step 4: Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the mung bean balls and cook until they float, then remove to a bowl.

Step 5: Combine sugar, water, and pandan leaves in a pot over medium heat. Once the sugar dissolves, add the cooked balls. Lower the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes until the balls absorb the sugar and develop a beautiful color, then turn off the heat.
Ladle the soup into a bowl, drizzle with coconut milk, add ice, and serve.
This mung bean ball sweet soup is delicious served either hot or cold.

mon_an.ten: Chè Khoai Lang Tím with Coconut Milk
mon_an.mo_ta: A delicious purple sweet potato sweet soup with coconut milk to refresh yourself and share with friends and family. Check out the recipe below!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the potatoes
Wash the purple sweet potatoes and steam or boil until tender. Peel and mash or puree them. If you don't have a masher, use a spoon to mash them through a sieve for a fine, even texture.
Step 2: Cook the sweet soup

Add 1-2 bowls of water to a pot, stir in sugar until dissolved, then add the mashed potatoes and stir until boiling. Mix tapioca starch with a little water and slowly pour it in, stirring until thickened and boiling again. Add 100ml of coconut milk, stir well, and turn off the heat.
Step 3: Presentation
Ladle the soup into bowls. Use the remaining coconut milk to decorate with flowers or patterns as desired.
Tips for delicious Chè Khoai Lang Tím:
Choose medium-sized, starchy potatoes with deep purple color and minimal fibers.
You can boil or steam the potatoes, but steaming preserves more sweetness. They are done when they start to crack open.
To save time, you can microwave them at 850-1000W for about 8 minutes (flip halfway).
Try using palm sugar for a better, more refreshing flavor.
Use coconut milk for decoration. Put it in a container or a small plastic bag with a tiny hole to draw patterns.
You can also try the Chè Bưởi recipe using this method.

mon_an.ten: Western Vietnamese Chè Thưng (Chè Bà Ba) with Mung Beans
mon_an.mo_ta: Chè Thưng may sound like a unique name, but it is made with familiar ingredients that you will love. The nutty, tender lotus seeds and rich peanuts pair perfectly with soft mung beans, crunchy wood ear mushrooms, and chewy tapioca pearls and strips. Combined with fragrant coconut milk and eye-catching colors, this dish is truly irresistible. Enjoying a bowl of Chè Thưng on an autumn day will let you savor the delicious flavors and the poetic atmosphere of the season. Discover this simple yet attractive recipe for authentic Western Vietnamese Chè Thưng (Chè Bà Ba) with mung beans below.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
First, soak the peanuts, mung beans, and tapioca strips in water overnight so they expand evenly and cook better.
Soak the tapioca pearls in water until softened.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms in hot water until expanded, then rinse thoroughly and thinly shred.
Grate the fresh coconut into a bowl, add a little warm water, and squeeze to extract the coconut milk.
Soak the lotus seeds for 3–4 hours until they expand.
Dissolve the tapioca starch in a little water until smooth.
Step 2: Cooking process
First, simmer the mung beans until tender or steam them. Once cooked, remove to a bowl and mix with 2 tablespoons of sugar so the sugar dissolves and absorbs into the beans.

Simmer the lotus seeds until tender, then remove and mix with 2 tablespoons of sugar. If you prefer it sweeter, you can add sugar while simmering, but since lotus seeds have a natural sweetness, mixing sugar after cooking works well too.
Boil the peanuts until soft.

Next, use a large pot to bring about 1 liter of water to a boil. Add the tapioca pearls and tapioca strips, stirring well. Stir until the pearls float and the liquid thickens, then add the lotus seeds, peanuts, mung beans, and wood ear mushrooms.
Add the dissolved tapioca starch, turn the heat down to low, and stir until the soup thickens.
Finally, add the coconut milk, stir well, adjust the sweetness to taste, and turn off the heat. Ladle into bowls and serve.
Tips for a delicious Chè Thưng
You can reduce the peanuts or add sweet potatoes or cassava for extra flavor.
While cooking, stir constantly to ensure the soup is smooth and does not burn at the bottom.
Taste the soup and add more sugar if it is not sweet enough for your preference.
Add a little vanilla for a more enticing aroma.
To add more texture, you can include fresh seaweed to make the dish more diverse and interesting.

mon_an.ten: Simple Fruit Dessert Soup – Love at First Bite
mon_an.mo_ta: Fruit dessert soup is a perfect summer snack, offering a balance of sweet, sour, and nutty flavors from watermelon, ripe bananas, green grapes, mango, and dragon fruit, all presented in vibrant colors. Check out our simple recipe for this fruit dessert soup in the article below!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Soak the snow fungus until expanded, then chop into small pieces. Prepare a pot of cold water, add rock sugar, and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the snow fungus and simmer over low heat for 12-15 minutes.
Step 2: Peel the peach, banana, dragon fruit, and mango, then cut them into small pieces. Halve the grapes.
Step 3: Peel the watermelon and dice it into small cubes.
Step 4: Gradually add the grapes, banana, watermelon, mango, peach, and dragon fruit into the cooled sugar water. Stir well, ladle into bowls, and enjoy.
You can keep the fruit soup in the refrigerator for 1-2 hours to make it even more refreshing!

mon_an.ten: Warm Pandan Chè Trôi Nước with Mung Bean Filling
mon_an.mo_ta: Enjoy this warm and attractive Pandan Chè Trôi Nước (sticky rice balls), featuring a fragrant, chewy crust and a rich, nutty mung bean filling.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: For the filling: - Peeled mung beans - 150g
cac_buoc: Ingredients needed:
Preparation:
Step 1:
Cook the coconut sauce: Add 200 ml of coconut milk to a pot with 100 ml of cold water + 1/5 tsp salt + 30 g sugar + 2 tied pandan leaves. Bring to a boil over low heat.
Step 2:
Mix 1 tsp tapioca starch with 2 tsp cold water until dissolved. Pour into the boiling coconut sauce, stirring constantly to prevent lumps. Turn off the heat.
Cook the ginger syrup:
Place 1 liter of cold water in a pot with 150 g white sugar + 100 g brown sugar + some thinly sliced ginger. Cook over medium heat until the sugar dissolves. Turn off the heat after about 20 minutes.
Kneading the dough:

Step 1: Put the glutinous rice flour in a large bowl, then gradually add hot water while kneading thoroughly. Add the pandan juice and continue kneading until the dough is smooth and no longer sticks to your hands. Wrap with plastic wrap and let the dough rest for 30 minutes. While waiting, prepare the filling.
Step 2: Soak mung beans for 4-5 hours, rinse well, and steam until cooked.

Step 3: Blend the cooked mung beans with sugar until smooth. Place the pureed mung beans in a non-stick pan over low heat. When the beans start to thicken, add coconut milk and continue stirring over low heat.

Step 4: Use a spatula to stir until the mung beans form a unified mass that doesn't stick to the pan, then turn off the heat. Mix in the shredded young coconut and roll into small balls. Size is up to your preference.
Step 5: Knead the dough for another 5 minutes, then divide into small portions slightly larger than the filling balls.
Step 6: Flatten a piece of dough, place the filling in the center, and roll it into a smooth ball.
Step 7: Bring a pot of water to a boil with a pinch of salt. Drop the balls in to boil.
When the balls float to the surface, boil for a few more minutes, then remove and immediately place them in a bowl of cold water.
Transfer the balls from the cold water into the pot of ginger syrup. Bring the syrup back to a boil, and it's done.
Presentation: Serve the balls in small bowls, drizzle with coconut sauce, and sprinkle with toasted sesame seeds and shredded young coconut before serving to family and friends.

mon_an.ten: Ambarella with Beef Jerky - A Snack You Can't Resist
mon_an.mo_ta: Ambarella with beef jerky is a favorite snack among teenagers, featuring the sour and crunchy taste of ambarella, the spicy and tender texture of beef jerky, and an irresistible sweet and sour dressing. This dish is delicious from the first bite to the last. Let's learn how to make this tasty treat with staynauan.com.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Boil sugar and fish sauce in a 1:1 ratio to make the dressing, then let it cool completely.
Step 2: Peel the ambarella and slice into pieces or wedges as desired.

Step 3: Soak the ambarella in ice water for about 30 minutes to reduce the acidity and increase crunchiness. Since baby ambarella is not very sour, you don't need to add salt or sugar to the soaking water.
Step 4: Drain the ambarella and toss with the fish sauce-sugar mixture. Let it sit for about 10 minutes to absorb the flavors (it's best to keep it in the refrigerator during this time).
Step 5: Finally, mix in the beef jerky and roasted peanuts, and it's ready to serve!

mon_an.ten: Fruit Cocktail to Brighten Your Weekend
mon_an.mo_ta: Fruit cocktail is a nutritious and healthy beverage. Its intense aroma and eye-catching colors make it an irresistible treat for anyone. Fruit cocktail is a nutritious and healthy beverage. Its intense aroma and eye-catching colors make it an irresistible treat for anyone.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Mix the salt and sugar together. Then, add 1-2 drops of food coloring.
Step 2: Mix well. If the color is too light, add another 1-2 drops and mix again.
Step 3: Cut a lemon slice and rub it around the rim of the glass.
Step 4: Dip the rim of the glass into the salt-sugar mixture.
Step 5: Squeeze the oranges and lemons for juice.
Step 6: Finely chop the orange and lemon peels, add them to the juice, and muddle with a spoon for a while.
Step 7: Add syrup and crushed ice, then stir well.
Step 8: Pour a little tequila into the glass first. Next, strain the citrus juice into the glass. Finally, top with a bit of crushed ice, and your fruit cocktail is ready to enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: Avocado is an incredibly healthy fruit. The following benefits will help you make better use of this nutritious fruit!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Regulates blood pressure:
High levels of folic acid and potassium in avocados help regulate blood pressure, prevent strokes, and protect against heart and circulatory system issues.
Step 2: Reduces harmful cholesterol:
Oleic and linoleic acids in avocados help lower bad cholesterol (LDL) and increase good cholesterol (HDL). They also contain beta-sitosterol, a compound that lowers cholesterol and protects health.
Step 3: Treats stomach ulcers:
Avocados soothe the sensitive lining of the stomach and duodenum, making them effective in treating ulcers.
Step 4: Boosts the immune system:
Regular consumption of avocado helps maintain overall health and strengthens the immune system.
Step 5: Improves vision:

Antioxidants in avocados neutralize free radicals, improving vision and preventing eye diseases like astigmatism, glaucoma, and cataracts. They contain more lutein carotene than any other fruit, which protects against macular degeneration and cataracts.
Step 6: Freshens breath:
Components in avocados help eliminate decomposed waste products in the intestines, which is a common cause of bad breath.
Step 7: Prevents kidney stones:
The high potassium content in avocados reduces the amount of calcium excreted through urine, thereby lowering the risk of kidney stones.
Step 8: Benefits for pregnant women:
Supports fetal development: Folic acid is crucial for the healthy development of fetal tissues.
Prevents morning sickness: Vitamin B6 helps soothe nausea and stomach discomfort during pregnancy.
Prevents birth defects: Pregnant women should eat avocados for their high folate content, which helps prevent birth defects.

Avocados are also safe and nutritious for breastfeeding mothers. Eating avocado helps the body absorb other nutrients like alpha-carotene, beta-carotene, lutein, and lycopene, as these require healthy fats for absorption.
Reduces morning sickness: Additionally, the rich source of Vitamin B6 boosts the immune system, promotes metabolism, and supports red blood cell production.
Step 9: Prevents dangerous diseases:
Cancer prevention:

Chemical compounds in avocados inhibit the growth of pre-cancerous and malignant cells in the throat and prostate. High beta-carotene levels also support cancer treatment. Avocados can help prevent kidney, breast, oral, and prostate cancers.
Diabetes prevention: Oleic acid can reduce blood lipid disorders, a risk factor for type 2 diabetes. It also reduces atherosclerosis, minimizing microvascular damage from diabetes complications.
Step 10: Strengthens the nervous system and muscles:
Potassium helps balance electrolytes, allowing muscles to function effectively while boosting energy for the nervous system and metabolism.
Step 11: Prevents psoriasis:
Experts suggest that avocado oil is very useful in treating skin conditions like psoriasis and dry skin.
Step 12: Heart health:
One cup of avocado provides 23% of the daily folate requirement, which is proven to reduce heart disease risk. Vitamin E and glutathione are also excellent for the heart.
Step 13: Better nutrient absorption:

Studies show that eating salad with avocado increases carotenoid absorption (including lycopene and carotene) fivefold compared to eating salad without it. Thus, avocado is a great nutritional food for children.
Notes when using avocado:
Overuse can be counterproductive:
Impact on the liver: Avocados are rich in collagen, which is good for skin regeneration. However, if eaten in excess, undigested collagen can accumulate and damage the liver. Eat in moderation.
Weight gain: Avocados are high in calories. If you add them to your diet, be sure to reduce calories from other foods to avoid weight gain.
Interactions with medication:
Avocados have anti-inflammatory properties but can interfere with certain medications. If you are taking blood thinners, consult a doctor, as avocado may reduce the drug's effectiveness.
To maximize benefits, experts recommend consuming about 2 teaspoons of avocado (roughly 1/6 of a fruit) per day.

mon_an.ten: What is Waxberry? Benefits and Recipes
mon_an.mo_ta: Waxberry is not only a rich source of vitamins and minerals but also offers amazing health benefits that not everyone knows about. Notably, this fruit can be prepared in various ways to create delicious dishes. Explore more in the article below to understand the wonders of waxberry! I. What is Waxberry?
cac_buoc: Waxberry, also known as yumberry or mountain berry, belongs to the Myricaceae family and the Fagales order. The tree grows naturally in India, Nepal, Southern China, Laos, and Japan. In Vietnam, it is common in the North, Central, and Central Highlands provinces. The fruit is small, grows in clusters, is bright red, has many small segments, is juicy, and has a characteristic sweet and sour taste.

Waxberry contains many nutrients such as sugar, organic acids, vitamin C, and anthocyanin pigments. Additionally, the leaves contain tannins, taraxerol, and essential oils, all of which provide valuable health benefits.
II. Benefits of Waxberry

According to traditional medicine, waxberry is a useful remedy for digestive conditions like constipation or colonic hemorrhage. Especially for middle-aged people, it is known for cooling the body, enhancing respiratory health, supporting skin, strengthening the immune system, and preventing several dangerous diseases.

Furthermore, waxberry supports skin care, maintains healthy skin, and prevents aging. For those with blood pressure issues, using waxberry is considered an effective method to stabilize blood pressure and reduce the risk of obesity.
III. Delicious Recipes from Waxberry
1. How to make Waxberry Syrup
Soak 500g of waxberries in diluted salt water for 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Place the berries in a glass jar, add 300g of sugar and ½ tsp salt, then close the lid.
Macerate for 1-2 months to get delicious syrup. To serve, add crushed ice to a glass, pour in the syrup, stir well, and enjoy.
How to make Dried Waxberry (Ô Mai):
Soak 1kg of waxberries in diluted salt water for 30 minutes, then soak in lime water (about 2 liters) for 30 minutes.
Simmer the berries with 150g of minced ginger and 900g of sugar until the sugar melts.
Cook over low heat until the syrup thickens and coats the berries, then dry them to get delicious, firm dried fruit.
2. How to make Waxberry Wine
Soak 1kg of waxberries in diluted salt water for 30 minutes, then rinse and drain.
Place the berries in a glass jar, add 200g of sugar and 2 liters of white liquor, then seal the lid tightly.
Infuse the berries in the liquor for about 4-6 months before use. Store the jar at 25°C.
Drink waxberry wine twice a day, only 1 small glass each time, to enjoy its unique flavor.
3. Instructions for making Dried Waxberry (Ô Mai)
Step 1: Soak the berries
Soak 1kg of waxberries in diluted salt water for 30 minutes.
Then, remove and soak in lime water (about 2 liters) for 30 minutes.
Rinse thoroughly and drain.
Step 2: Cooking the Ô Mai
Place the waxberries in a pot with 150g of minced ginger and 900g of sugar.
Marinate until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Simmer over low heat until the sugar syrup thickens.
Dry the fruit to create a delicious and attractive snack.
By following these steps, you will have a batch of tasty dried waxberries to enjoy with family and friends.
IV. How to choose good Waxberries
To buy quality waxberries, follow these principles:
Choose fruits that are not too soft, not bruised, and have a fresh outer color.
Avoid fruits that are too hard, as they may be dry or spoiled.
After buying, before consuming, perform these steps:
Soak the berries in diluted salt water to remove any insects that might be hiding in the segments.
Check the origin and source when buying, especially with large quantities imported from China.
To avoid poisoning:
Do not eat waxberries with seafood, cucumbers, or milk.
People with symptoms or diseases related to the gallbladder, gallstones, or pleural heat shock should also avoid waxberries.
V. Essential notes when eating Waxberry
Choose fruits that are not too soft or bruised and still look fresh. Avoid very hard fruits to prevent dryness and spoilage.
After purchasing, follow these steps:
Soak the berries in diluted salt water to remove insects between the segments.
Note that besides Vietnamese berries, many are imported from China, so choose products with clear origins.
To avoid poisoning:
Do not combine waxberries with seafood, cucumbers, or milk to prevent poisoning.
People with gallbladder issues, gallstones, or pleural heat shock should avoid using waxberry.

mon_an.mo_ta: Combining yogurt with pure aloe vera doubles the benefits for health and beauty. Aloe vera essence, with over 19 vitamins (A, B1, B2, B6, B12, C, E), folic acid, niacin, and various minerals, penetrates the skin to nourish it, making it healthy and smooth. Meanwhile, selenium prevents skin aging, providing a fresh and youthful look from within. By removing the green skin and keeping the transparent core of the aloe vera to mix with yogurt, you create a nutritious food – aloe vera yogurt.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Yogurt containers and other tools - tools
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the aloe vera, peel off the outer skin to get the transparent flesh inside. Soak the aloe vera in diluted salt water to remove the slime, then dice into small cubes.

Step 2: Mix the sweetened condensed milk with fresh milk and heat until warm. Add the sugar and aloe vera, stirring well. Turn off the heat. When the mixture is around 40-45°C, stir in the starter yogurt.
Step 3: Wait for the yogurt mixture to cool, then pour it into yogurt containers. Incubate for 6-8 hours to allow the yogurt to ferment. Afterward, place in the refrigerator to chill and enjoy.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Delicious Fresh Mango Strawberry Smoothie
mon_an.mo_ta: The harmonious combination of strawberries and mango creates a characteristic delicious flavor, helping you reduce stress and fatigue after long days of studying and working. Check out the recipe for this mango strawberry smoothie in the article below!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the strawberries and remove the stems.
Cut the strawberries in half.
Step 2:
Peel the mango, remove the pit, and cut the flesh into small pieces.
Step 3:
Place all ingredients into a blender and blend until smooth.
Pour the strawberry mango smoothie into a large glass, add a few ice cubes, and enjoy!

mon_an.ten: Refreshing Sticky Rice Ball Soup for Hot Days
mon_an.mo_ta: Cool down on sunny days with this refreshing sticky rice ball soup. The ingredients and method are extremely simple.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Tapioca starch or corn starch - 20g mixed with 30ml cold water in a separate bowl.
Coconut milk - 100ml coconut milk boiled with 20g sugar and a little corn starch slurry to thicken.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Put the glutinous rice flour in a bowl, then gradually pour in the hot water. Knead for 5-7 minutes until the dough reaches the necessary smooth and elastic consistency.
Roll the dough into small balls, about the size of marbles.

Step 2: Place cold water, sugar, and pandan leaves in a pot and cook until the sugar dissolves. Add the dough balls and cook in the syrup for 15 minutes. Finally, pour in the starch mixture and stir well until the syrup thickens slightly.
Presentation: Ladle the soup into glasses or bowls, drizzle with coconut milk, and garnish with pandan leaves. This dessert can be enjoyed hot or cold.

mon_an.ten: Delicious Peanut Butter Sauce for Ice Cream
mon_an.mo_ta: With this peanut butter sauce recipe, anyone who tastes your creation will surely shower you with compliments.
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, place the sugar and heavy cream into two separate saucepans.
Step 2:
Heat the sugar over low heat, watching carefully as it melts.
Step 3:
Cook until the sugar is completely melted and turns a light amber color. Heat the heavy cream over medium heat; once it just begins to boil, turn the heat down to low.
Step 4:
Pour the heavy cream into the caramel; the mixture will bubble up, but keep stirring steadily.
Step 5:
Place the pan back on the heat and cook for about 12-15 minutes until the caramel is fully dissolved and no lumps remain. Add the salt and stir well.
Step 6:
Add the peanut butter and stir until the mixture is perfectly smooth, then turn off the heat. Store the peanut butter sauce in a sealed jar in the refrigerator.
Since the flavor of this peanut caramel sauce is quite bold, it is best served with basic ice cream flavors like vanilla or chocolate.
Sprinkle a little cinnamon on top to make the ice cream look even more appealing!
The peanut butter sauce can be kept for at least 1 week if stored in the refrigerator.

mon_an.mo_ta: With very easy-to-find ingredients, you can make yourself a cool corn and coconut jelly for this hot weather!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, remove the corn kernels from the cob, place them in a bowl, and steam until cooked.
Step 2:
Mix the agar-agar powder with the sugar. Boil about 1L of water; once boiling, add the agar-agar and sugar mixture, stirring until the powder is completely dissolved.
Step 3:
Add the steamed corn to the agar mixture.
Step 4:
Cut the coconut meat into small squares and add them to the corn mixture.
Step 5:
Pour the mixture into a tray and refrigerate until the jelly is set.
Step 6:
Cut into bite-sized pieces and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Durian cupcakes are quite attractive due to their beautiful appearance and the intoxicating aroma of durian. When eaten, the cake is soft, smooth, fluffy, not dry, and has just the right amount of sweetness. This dish is perfect for home parties or family picnics. Let's get into the kitchen and learn how to make this delicious treat!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Mashed durian flesh, at room temperature - 150 g
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, place the cream cheese in a large bowl and beat at low speed for 1 minute until you get a soft, smooth mixture without lumps.
Step 2:
Next, add the sugar to the bowl and beat for 4 minutes at low speed until the sugar is completely dissolved and the mixture is smooth.
Step 3:
Then, add the eggs one by one and continue beating until smooth and the mixture has a nice color.
Step 4:
Next, add the remaining sugar to the egg mixture and beat for 4 minutes at low speed to continue dissolving the sugar into the mixture.
Step 5:
Next, add the cornstarch to the mixture.
Step 6:
Then, fold the mashed durian into the mixture.
Since the durian flavor is the main highlight, choose ripe durian with sweet, soft flesh and no hard spots for a better quality cake!
Step 7:
After adding everything, use a mixer to beat until the mixture is well combined, soft, smooth, and lump-free with an appealing color.
Step 8:
If you prefer a slightly more fragrant aroma or want to tone down the durian scent (for those who aren't big durian fans), you can add a small tube of vanilla to the mixture and mix well.
Step 9:
Once the mixture is smooth and soft, place paper liners into the muffin tin and put one Oreo cookie at the bottom of each liner.
If you don't like Oreos, you can use regular biscuits instead! (If using regular biscuits, Cosy brand is recommended to enhance the flavor).
Step 10:
Pour the durian cream cheese mixture into each mold and bake for 20 - 25 minutes at 160°C or until the cakes have a beautiful golden exterior.
Notes for perfect durian cupcakes:
When mixing the batter, remember to beat steadily so the mixture is soft, smooth, and lump-free. If you don't have a mixer, you can beat by hand until you achieve a similar consistency.
If you don't want the durian smell to be too overwhelming, choose a moderately ripe durian.
How to choose delicious durian:

Choose fruits with even segments (the grooves are long and almost equal in size). Don't pick misshapen ones; look for those with a "bread waist" shape that is plump all over. Buy fruits that have slightly cracked open and have a strong aroma.
Check if the stem is fresh or withered. Choose fruits with a firm green stem and a long-lasting, sweet, rich fragrance.
Durian thorns: Should be large, even, less pointed, and firm. Squeeze two adjacent thorns together; if the fruit is mature, the thorns will be hard. If young, the thorns will be soft.
Observe how the seller opens it: Mature and ripe durian will have 5 natural seams that open easily. If the seller has to struggle to pry it open, the fruit is still young.

mon_an.ten: Stir-Fried Balut Quail Eggs with Tamarind Sauce
cac_buoc: Stir-fried balut quail eggs with tamarind is one of the most popular snacks. The unique flavor of the quail eggs combined with the sweet and sour taste of tamarind attracts every diner. Let's make this sweet and sour dish using the recipe below!
I. Traditional Sweet and Sour Tamarind Quail Eggs
1. Ingredients
30 balut quail eggs
30 g ripe tamarind
3 cloves garlic
A handful of Vietnamese coriander (rau răm)
1 tbsp tapioca starch
2 tbsp fish sauce
4 tbsp sugar
1 tsp salt
1 tbsp cooking oil
2. Preparation Steps
2.1. Prepare the ingredients
Place 30g of ripe tamarind in a bowl and add about 100ml of hot water.
Use a spoon to mash the tamarind until it dissolves into the water, then extract the juice.
Prepare the garlic and coriander:
Peel and mince the garlic.
Pick the young coriander leaves, wash them, and let them drain.
Prepare the starch:
Put 1 tbsp of tapioca starch in a small bowl.
Add 2 tbsp of warm water and stir until the starch is completely dissolved.
Tips:
Using tapioca starch mixed with water helps the tamarind sauce thicken and coat the quail eggs better.
If you prefer, you can skip this step.
Depending on your preference, you can strain out the tamarind seeds or leave them in.
Now the ingredients are ready for cooking.
2.2. Boil the quail eggs
Place 30 quail eggs in a pot and add enough water to cover them.
Turn the heat to high and add 1 tsp of salt to the water.
Boil the eggs for about 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and remove the eggs to cool.
Carefully peel the shells to avoid breaking the eggs.
Cook the tamarind sauce
Heat a pan, add 1 tbsp of oil, and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the tamarind juice, 1/2 cup of water, 2 tbsp of fish sauce, and 4 tbsp of sugar, then bring to a boil.
Stir the starch mixture into the pan to thicken the sauce.
Add all the peeled quail eggs to the pan, continue to cook and stir gently until the sauce thickens and coats the eggs.
Adjust the seasoning to taste.
2.3. Tips for delicious tamarind quail eggs
You can add chili powder or fresh minced chili if you like it spicy.
Remember to stir the sauce constantly to prevent it from sticking to the pan.
Seasoning the sauce before adding the eggs makes it easier to adjust the flavor.

This is a dish full of flavor and attractive colors. The quail eggs stir-fried with tamarind sauce offer a wonderful combination of sweet and sour from the tamarind and sugar, along with the richness of the fish sauce. The aroma and eye-catching colors are irresistible. This dish is enjoyed with a bit of Vietnamese coriander, creating a perfect taste experience. If you haven't tried it yet, get in the kitchen and try it now!
II. Restaurant-Style Tamarind Quail Eggs Recipe
1. Ingredients
Quail eggs: 30 eggs
Sour tamarind: 100g
Butter: 100g
Minced shallots: 1 tbsp
Minced garlic: 1 tbsp
Sugar: 2 tbsp
Fish sauce: 2 tbsp
Tapioca starch: 1 tbsp
Vietnamese coriander: 1 bunch
2. Preparation Steps
Quail eggs:
After buying, place the eggs in a pot and cover with water.
Turn the heat to high and add 1 tsp of salt.
Boil for about 15 minutes, then turn off the heat and let them cool slightly.
Peel the shells.
Make the sauce:
Place the tamarind in a bowl, add a little warm water, and mash to extract the juice.
Strain the tamarind through a sieve to get the smooth juice.
Finish the sauce:
Heat a pan and add the butter. Once melted, add 1 tbsp of minced shallots and minced garlic.
When fragrant, add the tamarind juice.
Add 2 tbsp of sugar, 2 tbsp of fish sauce, and 1 tbsp of the starch mixture.
Finally, add the quail eggs and toss until the sauce thickens, then turn off the heat.
Now the ingredients are prepared and the sauce is done, ready to serve.
2.2. Finished Dish
To make the dish more attractive, add some Vietnamese coriander and crushed peanuts. The tamarind quail eggs will have a perfectly balanced sweet and sour taste.
This dish is very suitable as a snack or a side dish for drinks. Good luck!

By adding coriander and peanuts, the dish becomes more diverse in texture and flavor. The coriander brings a natural aroma, while the peanuts add a nice crunch. Combined with the sweet and sour sauce, it creates a very appealing balance.
You can enjoy this as a snack or pair it with drinks like beer or wine. The rich and easy-to-eat flavor will surely satisfy you and your guests.
III. Notes on Choosing Ingredients

Quail eggs are very nutritious, but you should not eat too many, as excessive nutrients can lead to digestive, cardiovascular, or diabetic issues. Note the following consumption guidelines based on age:
Infants under 5 months: Should not eat balut quail eggs.
Children 5 – 12 months: 1 – 2 quail eggs (balut or regular) per day.
Children 1 – 3 years: 3 – 4 quail eggs per day.
Adults: 5 – 10 eggs per day.
Pregnant women: Should only eat about 4 balut quail eggs per week.
Quail egg consumption should be adjusted according to age to ensure balanced nutrition without causing health problems. Pregnant women should specifically follow a doctor's advice for the best diet.
IV. Conclusion

Sweet and sour tamarind quail eggs are a unique dish that carries both traditional flavors and modern appeal. The gentle sweet and sour taste combined with the rich flavor of the quail eggs creates a compelling harmony. This dish is not only highly nutritious but also brings great satisfaction.

With simple steps, anyone can make this dish at home. Choosing fresh ingredients and using proper preparation techniques will make the dish more attractive and authentic. This is an excellent choice for family meals or special parties.

mon_an.ten: Coffee Granita – A Refreshing Summer Treat
mon_an.mo_ta: Shaved ice is a very useful refreshment in the summer heat, and coffee granita is a particularly interesting version to enjoy. The aroma of Espresso is very seductive; the slightly bitter coffee is frozen into cool ice crystals that help dispel the sweltering summer heat. Additionally, the rich whipped cream and a bit of chocolate make this dish more diverse and special. Check out how to make coffee granita below!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for Italian-style coffee granita
Whip the cream until stiff peaks form and set aside.
Use a grater to shave some of the chocolate. Cut the remaining chocolate into small squares.
Step 2: Steps to make Italian-style coffee granita.
First, place a pot on the stove and bring 250 ml of water to a boil.
Then, add the granulated sugar and the vanilla bean. Remember to stir so the sugar dissolves completely.
When the water boils, pour in the Espresso, stir a few times, and turn off the heat.
Next, pour the coffee mixture into a metal bowl through a fine-mesh sieve to remove the vanilla bean bits.
Place the bowl in the freezer for about 1 hour.
After 1 hour, take the bowl out and use a whisk to break up the frozen coffee.

Return the bowl to the freezer. About 30 minutes later, take it out and whisk again. Repeat this process until the coffee ice is fluffy and no longer freezes into a solid block; this is your coffee granita.
Once finished, spoon the coffee granita into glass cups. Sprinkle with a little powdered sugar if you like it sweeter, then pipe the whipped cream on top.
Decorate each cup with chocolate chunks or shavings and enjoy.
Notes for delicious Italian-style coffee granita
Espresso is an Italian coffee; however, if you cannot find it, you can use regular black coffee or any coffee you prefer.
Similarly, if you cannot find a vanilla bean, you can substitute it with a few drops of vanilla extract.
When pouring the coffee into a bowl, use a metal bowl as it freezes much faster than plastic or ceramic.

Shaved ice is a great summer refreshment, and coffee granita is a fun way to enjoy it. The Espresso aroma is very inviting, and the icy texture helps beat the heat. The rich cream and chocolate add a special touch. With simple ingredients and a little effort, you'll have a refreshing treat to keep you cool during hot summer days.

mon_an.ten: Almond-Crusted Baked Chicken – Unique and Delicious
mon_an.mo_ta: Almond-crusted baked chicken is a unique dish for many, but it brings immediate delight with its soft, fresh chicken infused with flavors and wrapped in a crunchy, rich almond coating. The combination of meat and almonds creates a wonderful sensation. Let's learn how to make this delicious dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Table salt or Kosher salt - 1 tsp
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for almond-crusted baked chicken.
Wash the chicken, pat dry with paper towels, and cut into bite-sized squares.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well.
Preheat your oven to 400°F. Line a large baking sheet with parchment paper or aluminum foil.
Step 2: Steps to make almond-crusted baked chicken
Add the almonds to a blender or food processor and pulse until finely ground without large chunks.
Place the ground almonds in a small bowl along with the salt, chili powder, black pepper, and garlic powder. Mix well until combined.
Beat the eggs to combine with other ingredients. You can add extra salt and pepper if desired to enhance the flavor.
In a second bowl, whisk the eggs and water (or milk) until well blended.
Use a third bowl for the flour. Now set up a breading station: (1) chicken, (2) flour, (3) egg mixture, (4) almond mixture, (5) baking tray.

First, dip a piece of chicken into the flour until fully coated, then shake off the excess. Next, dip it into the egg wash, then roll it in the almond mixture, and finally place it on the baking tray. Repeat with the remaining chicken pieces.

Bake for 8-10 minutes, or until the chicken is golden brown and no longer pink inside. Flip the pieces halfway through for even cooking. (For a crunchier coating, bake for 6-8 minutes, then broil for another 1-2 minutes. Watch carefully so the almonds don't burn).
Finally, remove the chicken from the oven and serve immediately with your favorite sauce such as chili sauce, mayonnaise, or dipping sauce.
Notes for perfect almond-crusted baked chicken

If you don't have an oven, you can follow the same steps and deep-fry the chicken instead. Use plenty of oil so the chicken cooks evenly and quickly without becoming greasy, resulting in a beautiful golden crust.
Adjust the seasonings to suit your preference for spicy, sour, salty, or sweet flavors!
For the best results, you can use chicken thighs or breasts to enhance the flavor of the dish.

mon_an.mo_ta: Yakitori in Japanese means grilled skewered chicken and is also used to refer to skewered dishes in general. Yakitori is made by skewering pieces of chicken or other meats onto bamboo sticks and grilling them over charcoal. Yakitori is commonly found in restaurants or as street food in Japan. In most Japanese restaurants, yakitori is seasoned with either salt (shio) or yakitori sauce (tare). With these two seasonings, every part of the chicken is transformed into an attractive dish. Tare is made from soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar, creating a balance between salty and sweet. You can add ginger or other ingredients to suit your taste. If you prefer salt over tare, simply sprinkle with salt before grilling. For yakitori, bamboo skewers are typically used. One common type is "teppogushi" (gun-shaped skewers). The flat shape makes them easier to hold and prevents the meat from rolling on the grill, allowing the chef to grill one side at a time. As you can see, Yakitori is similar to Vietnamese grilled skewers, but the sauce has its own unique character. Let's explore the difference with this Japanese Yakitori recipe!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Soak the bamboo skewers in water for about 30 minutes, wash them, and let them drain.

Step 2: In a small saucepan, combine mirin, soy sauce, sake, water, sugar, the green parts of the onions, and minced garlic and ginger. Bring to a boil over high heat. Once boiling, reduce heat to a simmer and cook uncovered until reduced by half. This takes about 30 minutes; the sauce will become thicker and glossy. Set aside 1/3 of the sauce in a small bowl for the final glaze.

Step 3: Wash and cut the white parts of the green onions into 3-4 cm lengths. Slice the chicken into 0.5 cm thick pieces, then fold the meat and thread onto the skewers. Alternate between chicken and onion, with about 3-4 pieces of meat per skewer.

Step 4: Brush a layer of oil onto each skewer and grill over glowing charcoal, placing the skewers about 5 cm above the coals. Grill each side for 6-7 minutes, brushing with Yakitori sauce each time you flip. Grill until the meat is cooked through and the outside is golden brown.
Step 5: Remove the Japanese Yakitori skewers, drizzle with the reserved sauce immediately, and serve hot!

mon_an.ten: Refreshing Orange and Tofu Pudding Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Orange and tofu pudding soup is not only a delicious dessert to beat the summer heat but also an effective folk remedy for common summer ailments like fever, flu, and heatstroke. Eating a bowl of this soup makes you feel healthier and improves your mood. Just smelling the bowl brings a cool orange scent, and each sweet and sour orange segment blends with the silky tofu pudding that gently melts in your mouth.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Tofu pudding (tào phớ) - 1 small bowl or to taste
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for orange and tofu pudding soup.

Divide the oranges into two parts: Grate a little zest from one orange, then peel and separate it into segments, setting them aside on a plate. Squeeze the juice from the remaining two oranges and strain out the seeds.
Peel or scrape the ginger, wash it, and slice it thinly.
Dissolve the tapioca starch in a bowl of filtered water.
Step 2: Steps to make orange and tofu pudding soup.
First, put the orange juice, filtered water, ginger slices, and sugar into a pot and bring to a boil.
Once the orange mixture boils, pour in the starch mixture and stir until combined.
When the pot comes back to a boil, add the orange segments. Stir gently to avoid breaking the segments.
Finally, add the tofu pudding to the pot and turn off the heat. Be careful not to stir too much to prevent the tofu pudding from breaking apart.
Once the soup is ready, ladle it into bowls, ensuring each bowl has enough tofu pudding and orange segments. Sprinkle a little orange zest on top and enjoy.
If you prefer it cold, you can refrigerate the bowls or mix with shaved ice.
Notes for delicious orange and tofu pudding soup

How to choose good oranges: To pick sweet, juicy oranges, look for round fruits that aren't misshapen and have fresh stems.
