Mix all the above ingredients in a bowl with the sauce components and stir well until the flavors are fully combined.
Step 2: Cut the rice noodle sheets into bite-sized pieces and arrange them neatly on a plate.
Cut the century egg into small bite-sized wedges.
Step 3: Boil the chicken.

Place a pot of water on the stove, add ginger and garlic, then add the chicken to boil (ginger and garlic make the chicken more fragrant and flavorful). You should add a little seasoning salt and MSG to enhance the sweetness of the meat.

Step 4: Once the chicken is cooked, remove it and drain well; let it cool. You can place the chicken in the refrigerator for 15 minutes to firm up the meat. Afterward, chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces and place them on top of the rice noodles. Add the prepared century egg and drizzle the sauce over everything.
Step 5: For the final step, simply sprinkle some sesame seeds and crushed peanuts around the dish and garnish with a few sprigs of cilantro on top.

mon_an.mo_ta: If you are tired of rice and want to change up your family meals, seafood stir-fried glass noodles is an exciting suggestion. This dish is easy to prepare with a harmonious combination of ingredients and spices. With a little culinary skill, you can create a flavorful and unforgettable meal. Let's learn how to make this dish in the article below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms - 5 gr
Seasoning powder, dried shallots, garlic, pepper, cilantro, celery, leeks - Spices
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cut scallions and chives into 3 cm lengths. Soak wood ear and shiitake mushrooms until expanded, wash, remove stems, and julienne. Thinly slice the dried shallots and onion. Wash the bean sprouts and chop the Vietnamese coriander into 1 cm pieces.
Step 2: Clean the squid, score a flower pattern, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Step 3: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails intact, and devein. Boil the squid and shrimp until cooked, then sauté until firm. Sauté the crab meat with fragrant shallots until firm.

Step 4: Soak the glass noodles until soft, cut into short lengths, crack an egg in and mix well, then season to taste. Place a pan on the stove, stir-fry the noodles until firm, and remove to a plate.
Step 5: Sauté the shallots until fragrant, then add the prepared ingredients one by one and stir-fry until soft. Finally, add the glass noodles, toss well, and adjust the seasoning to taste.
Enjoy your delicious meal!
Tips to make seafood stir-fried glass noodles more flavorful
To make this dish even more delicious and sweet, you can apply the following tips:
Use fresh seafood: Choose fresh seafood like shrimp, squid, and fish to ensure the best flavor and freshness. Avoid using expired or low-quality seafood.

Cook properly: When cooking glass noodles with seafood, be careful not to overcook them to prevent the seafood from becoming tough. Stir-fry quickly over high heat so the seafood cooks fast while remaining tender.
Choose appropriate seasonings: Use spices like shallots, garlic, pepper, salt, and sugar to enhance the flavor. Adjust the amount of seasoning to suit your taste.
Add natural sweetness: To add natural sweetness, you can use ingredients like fish sauce, soy sauce, honey, or sugar. Add them gradually and taste until you reach the desired flavor.
Combine with fresh herbs: To make the dish more vibrant, add fresh herbs like lettuce, fish mint, or aromatic herbs when serving. Fresh herbs increase freshness and flavor diversity.
Add final seasonings: Before turning off the heat, you can add a little toasted sesame oil or oyster sauce to increase the aroma and flavor of the dish.
Beautiful presentation: When serving, pay attention to the decoration to make the dish more appealing. You can use fresh herbs, fried shallots, or tomatoes to create highlights.
Remember to balance the scents and flavors when adding ingredients. Customize according to your taste to create a delicious and attractive dish.

mon_an.ten: Two Ways to Make Delicious Stir-Fried Intestines with Pickled Greens
cac_buoc: Stir-fried intestines with pickled greens is a dish particularly suitable for rainy or cold days. Known for its attractive flavor, this dish will surely bring you interesting and memorable experiences. Today, we will guide you through 2 ways to make this dish that everyone will love!
Preparation: 20 mins
Processing: 30 mins
I. How to make stir-fried pork intestines with pickled mustard greens
1. Ingredients
Pork small intestines: 300 grams
Pickled mustard greens: 200 grams
Tomato: 1 fruit
Scallions: 10 grams
Small ginger: 1 bulb
White wine: 1 tbsp
Fish sauce: 1 tbsp
Cooking oil: 3 tbsp
Common spices: a little (salt, sugar, MSG).
2. Processing
2.1. Ingredient preparation
Preparing the pork intestines
First, soak the intestines in a mixture of salt water mixed with vinegar or wine.
Next, squeeze the intestines firmly in this mixture. You can also sprinkle salt directly on the intestines and rub vigorously to completely remove impurities.
Then, rinse the intestines with clean water and squeeze to drain all the water.
Preparing other ingredients
You can buy pickled mustard greens at the market, supermarket, or make them at home.
To prepare the pickled greens, soak them in diluted salt water to reduce saltiness. Then, rinse with clean water and squeeze dry.
Wash the tomatoes and cut them into wedges.
Wash the scallions and cut them into 3-4 cm lengths.
No need to peel the ginger, just slice and crush them.
2.2. Blanching the intestines
Place a pot on the stove, add about 200ml of filtered water. You can add the scallion segments and crushed ginger and bring to a boil.
Once the water is boiling, put the cleaned intestines into the pot and blanch. If desired, add 1 tbsp of white wine or a little lemon juice to effectively remove the odor.
Blanch for about 5-7 minutes, then turn off the heat, remove the intestines, and place them in a bowl of cold water to keep them crunchy.
Rinse the intestines again with clean water, then cut into small bite-sized pieces.
2.3. Stir-frying the intestines with pickled greens
Place a pan on the stove, add about 1 tbsp of cooking oil and some minced garlic to sauté until fragrant.
When the garlic is fragrant, add the blanched intestines to the pan and stir-fry for about 5-7 minutes, then remove to a clean plate.
Continue heating the pan with 2 tbsp of cooking oil, then add the tomatoes and sauté for 2-3 minutes.
Add the pickled mustard greens to the pan and stir-fry well. Season with 1 tbsp of fish sauce, 1/2 tsp of MSG, and 1 tsp of sugar.

Finally, add the intestines back into the pan and stir-fry for another 2-3 minutes. The dish is finished with attractive colors and a seductive aroma. The pork intestines will be crunchy without any odor, combined with the tasty pickled greens. It is wonderful when enjoyed with hot rice and a bowl of spicy chili fish sauce.
II. How to make stir-fried large intestines with pickled greens
1. Prepared ingredients
1kg pork large intestines
500g pickled mustard greens
100g celery
200g pineapple
Minced shallots, chili, garlic
Cooking oil
Spices: salt, seasoning powder, fish sauce, MSG, sate sauce, sugar.
Cut the pineapple into bite-sized pieces; finely chop the celery, scallions, and chili.
Clean the intestines and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Then, marinate the intestines with 1 tbsp of fish sauce, 1 tbsp of sate sauce, 1 tsp of MSG, and 1 tsp of seasoning powder. Mix well and let the intestines absorb the spices for 10-15 minutes.
2.2. Stir-frying large intestines with pickled greens
First, place a pan on the stove and add 5 tbsp of cooking oil. Wait for the oil to get hot, then add the minced garlic and sauté until fragrant.
When the garlic is fragrant, add the pineapple and continue to sauté. Season with 1 tbsp of sugar and sauté for about 2 minutes before adding the marinated intestines to the pan.
Note: When putting the intestines in the pan, ensure high heat so they don't release water and become tough.

When the intestines have firmed up, add the pickled mustard greens and stir-fry together. Cover the lid and continue cooking until the intestines are evenly cooked. Occasionally open the lid and stir, cooking for about 15 minutes until just done.
Then, adjust the seasoning to suit your taste.
2.3. Finished product

When the intestines are cooked, add the chopped celery and chili to the pan, then turn off the heat. The stir-fried large intestines with pickled greens is now complete. When you try a piece, you will feel the rich flavor from the marinated intestines, the crunchy texture without being tough, along with the appealing sourness from the greens and pineapple. It is delicious when served with hot rice. This is a tasty and easy-to-make dish that will surely satisfy you and your family.
III. Notes when making stir-fried intestines with pickled greens

Preparation: Ensure the intestines are cleaned and cut into bite-sized pieces. Pickled greens should be ready, chopped as desired. Celery and chili should also be prepared and chopped for easy addition during stir-frying.
Heat the pan and oil: Ensure the pan and oil are hot before starting to stir-fry. This helps prevent the food from sticking and ensures the intestines are cooked quickly and evenly.

Stir-fry intestines before adding pickled greens: During the process, stir-fry the intestines first. This gives them time to firm up and stay crunchy, while the pickled greens only need a short stir-fry to maintain their slight sourness.

Ensure high heat when stir-frying: When adding the intestines to the pan, use high heat to quickly cook them without releasing water or making them tough. Intestines need to be stir-fried quickly and steadily to maintain tenderness and crunchiness.

Seasoning and tasting: After the intestines and greens are cooked, taste and check the flavor. Depending on your palate, adjust the seasoning with salt, sugar, fish sauce, MSG, or other spices to reach your personal preference.
IV. How to choose fresh intestines
Choose intestines with small tubes, plump and round shapes, and a fresh pinkish-white color. This indicates the intestines are fresh.
Fresh intestines usually have a milky white fluid inside and no foul odor. This is a sign of good quality.
Avoid buying intestines that have turned greenish-white, have large tubes, or have yellow fluid inside. These are signs of old intestines, which will not be tasty when cooked.
VI. Conclusion

Stir-fried intestines with pickled greens is a delicious and easy-to-make dish. Choosing and preparing fresh intestines is the key factor. After preparing the ingredients, simply stir-fry the intestines before adding the pickled greens. High heat and short cooking time keep the intestines crunchy and not tough. The important part is seasoning and adjusting the taste. This dish should be enjoyed hot with steamed rice to fully appreciate its wonderful flavor. Surely, this dish will make you and your family fall in love with it.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Meat-Stuffed Tofu for Hot Summer Days
mon_an.mo_ta: The hot summer has arrived, and to avoid boredom in the family menu, why not explore a unique and interesting dish? Today, we will discover the simple steps to make meat-stuffed tofu, an excellent choice for hot days. With this recipe, you can enjoy the wonderful flavor of tofu and meat, combined with essential nutrients for the whole family. Enjoy the sweltering summer with this simple and attractive meat-stuffed tofu dish. Discover the easy recipe to make a delicious meal that provides nutrients for your family.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Spices - seasoning powder, MSG, and cooking oil
cac_buoc: 1. Ingredient preparation
After a light rinse, place the tofu on a plate.
After washing the meat, it can be finely minced or ground using a meat grinder if available.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms in water until they expand. Once expanded, wash and remove the stems, then mince finely.
Combine the minced meat and finely chopped wood ear mushrooms and mix well. Add seasonings like seasoning powder and MSG to create a suitable flavor.
2. Frying the tofu

To prevent the tofu from breaking when stuffing the meat, you can pre-fry the tofu. First, place a pan on the stove and heat it up. Then, pour cooking oil into the pan and heat until the oil boils. Next, cut the tofu into pieces and place them in the pan to fry until golden on both sides.

Note that you only need to lightly fry the tofu without cooking it for too long, as you will continue to fry it again after stuffing the meat inside. If the tofu is over-fried, it may burn and not taste good.
3. Stuffing the meat
To begin, use scissors or a knife to slit the tofu piece lengthwise. Then, use a small spoon to scoop out the tofu inside.
Next, take the previously mixed meat filling and stuff it inside the tofu piece.
4. Frying the stuffed tofu

Using the same pan used for frying the tofu earlier, place it on the stove and add cooking oil. Place the meat-stuffed tofu into the pan to fry. To ensure the meat inside is evenly cooked and the tofu doesn't burn, adjust to low heat.
Fry the tofu until one side is golden brown, then flip the tofu piece to fry the other side until it is evenly golden on both sides.
5. Finished product

Once finished, remove the meat-stuffed tofu to a plate; it can be served with rice or used as an attractive snack for your husband. In particular, you can also enjoy meat-stuffed tofu with chili sauce or tomato sauce to enhance the special flavor. When eating, you will feel the softness of the tofu combined with the rich meat and mushroom filling. When served with rice and some vegetables, the dish becomes even more wonderful and attractive.
Notes when making meat-stuffed tofu
Choose the right type of tofu: Choose tofu with a soft texture that doesn't crack easily for convenient stuffing. The tofu needs to be soft enough to cut and stuff without breaking the piece.
Fry the tofu before stuffing: To ensure the tofu doesn't fall apart when stuffing, you can pre-fry it to create durability and hold the shape. Frying until light golden is enough.

Stuffing technique: Use a knife or small spoon to scoop out the inner tofu, creating space for the meat. Ensure not to scoop too deep to avoid tearing the tofu. Stuff the meat into the tofu carefully and firmly, ensuring no empty space or over-stuffing, so the stuffed tofu has a beautiful and uniform shape.

Frying the stuffed tofu: When frying the stuffed tofu, adjust to low heat to ensure the meat is cooked through and the tofu doesn't burn. Fry slowly and flip the pieces once one side is golden. The stuffed tofu is done when it is evenly golden on both sides.
How to buy good ingredients for meat-stuffed tofu
1. How to buy good tofu
Good tofu will have an ivory white color, feel light in the hand, have a smooth surface, and carry a subtle soybean aroma.
To avoid buying the wrong kind, be careful with tofu pieces that are yellow, feel heavy, and have a faint smell of lime, as they may contain additives like gypsum.
To ensure safety and quality, buy tofu from reputable tofu production shops.
2. How to choose good meat
To ensure quality, buy fresh whole pieces of meat and then ask the seller to grind it for you or grind it yourself at home with a meat grinder.
Choose a piece of meat with a balance of lean and fat so that when ground or minced, the meat will be soft and fatty, avoiding cases where the meat is dry or too greasy due to too much fat.

Fresh pork will have a dry outer membrane, light red or bright pink color. When cut, the meat is bright pink, the skin is pinkish-white and soft. The fat layer between the lean meat is bright and firm.
Avoid buying meat with an unusual smell or meat fibers showing small white spots, as those may be signs of infection with parasites and larvae.

If you buy pre-packaged ground pork, check the packaging carefully to see if it is still intact. An expiration date within the day is best, and ensure it is stored in the refrigerator's cool compartment to maintain quality.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Delicious Caramel-Glazed Baked Banana Cake
mon_an.mo_ta: Each soft, smooth slice of cake, rich with banana flavor and covered in sweet, fragrant caramel sauce, is mouth-watering just to look at! Let's learn how to make caramel-glazed baked banana cake.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Ripe bananas - 225g (about 2-3 fruits, sliced about 0.5 cm thick)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, put the bananas in a large bowl and mash them thoroughly.
Step 2:
Put the brown sugar into a 23x13 cm rectangular cake mold.
Step 3:
Scatter the butter pieces over the brown sugar layer.
Preheat the oven to 160 degrees C, then place the mold in the oven and bake for 8 minutes.
Step 4:
While waiting, mix all the dry ingredients in another bowl.
Step 5:
Remember to add the cinnamon powder to the dry mixture above.
Step 6:
When finished baking the base, take the mold out of the oven and stir well so the sugar and butter melt completely. Use a spoon to spread the butter-sugar mixture evenly.
Step 7:
Arrange the sliced banana pieces one by one over the butter-sugar layer.
Step 8:
Next, pour the mashed bananas, the dry flour mixture along with the eggs and all other ingredients into a mixer.
Step 9:
Turn the machine to medium speed and mix until everything is well combined.
Step 10:

Pour the mixture into the mold. Bake the cake at 160 degrees C for 1 hour. You can test for doneness by inserting a bamboo skewer into the center of the cake; if it comes out clean without sticking batter, it is done.
When finished baking, let the cake cool for about 20 minutes in the mold before removing it to a wire rack.
Step 11:

To prepare the caramel sauce, put the heavy cream, brown sugar, and butter into a small pot and bring to a boil. Continue to simmer the sauce over low heat for another 2 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Let the sauce rest for 1 minute and pour it evenly over the top of the inverted cake.
Invert the cake onto a wide plate and pour the caramel sauce over it, and you have finished this cake!
Enjoy!

mon_an.ten: How to Cook Unique and Delicious Field Crab Rice Porridge
mon_an.mo_ta: Field crab rice porridge is a dish that is both familiar and unique, with a familiar bowl of porridge but a novel field crab meat topping. The field crab meat is fragrant, flavorful, rich, and greasy, carrying a deep flavor along with smooth, shiny golden crab roe. This field crab porridge is both easy to cook and rich in nutrients, making it an excellent choice for children. Let's get into the kitchen to learn how to make this delicious dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Spices, fish sauce, chili, pepper - seasonings
cac_buoc: First, wash the rice thoroughly and soak it in water for about 45-60 minutes for the rice to expand. After soaking, drain the rice and crush the grains. If you are hesitant to crush the rice, you can soak it for 3-4 hours; the grains will become soft, expand evenly, and dissolve easily when cooked.
Next, after buying the field crabs, wash them clean, separate the shells, and remove the aprons. Scoop out the crab roe and set it aside in a small bowl.

Then, put the crabs in a mortar and pound them finely; remember to add a little salt while pounding, filter to get the liquid, and discard the residue. If you are hesitant to pound them, you can put the field crabs in a blender and blend; remember to add a little salt and water to extract the essence.

Next, place the pot of filtered crab water on the stove, stir constantly until you see the crab meat starting to flocculate, then stop and wait for the pot to boil. When the crab meat forms a raft, lower the heat.
After the crab meat has formed into 'roe' clouds, scoop the crab meat out into a bowl.

Next, keep the crab water pot on the stove, turn the heat to medium-high, and add each handful of crushed rice. Pay attention to stirring constantly while adding the rice to prevent it from clumping and sticking to the bottom of the pot.

After adding all the rice, you must continue stirring constantly until you see the rice starting to expand evenly, then you can stop. Partially cover the pot lid, turn the heat to low, adjust the seasonings, and check if the amount of water for the porridge is appropriate. Simmer like that for another 20-30 minutes.

Next, you will sauté the crab roe to prepare for the porridge: Peel and wash the dried shallots, then slice them thinly and fry with cooking oil until they turn golden and fragrant, then pour the crab roe in and stir well with chopsticks.
Sauté until the roe is fragrant and golden, then you can add the crab meat and turn the heat to low.
Season with spices and fish sauce, and leave on the stove for about 10-15 minutes so the crab meat, sautéed roe, and spices are evenly absorbed and cooked through.
Finally, pour the prepared crab meat into a separate bowl.
Finely chop the scallions and dill, and arrange them on a separate plate.
Decoration: Scoop the porridge into a bowl, spoon the crab roe on top, and sprinkle with chopped scallions and dill. Sprinkle with pepper and chili for aroma. Eat hot with fried dough sticks.
Notes for a great field crab porridge
When adding the rice, remember to stir constantly so the rice doesn't stick to the pot and easily dissolves into porridge.
How to choose delicious field crabs:
Crab color: Field crabs usually have a dull gray color, and the shell part is brighter.

Strong, fresh crabs: You should choose crabs that move quickly, have strong claws that always point upwards, are plump, and have all their legs. Press your finger into the crab's apron; if you see air bubbles, the crab is still fresh.

Identifying male and female crabs: The simplest way to distinguish them is to observe the crab's apron. If the apron is small, it's a male crab; if the apron is larger, it's a female crab. If you want to cook with a lot of roe, choose female crabs; if you want more meat, choose male crabs.

Checking for firm meat: Flip the crab over and press on the apron; if it doesn't sink, the crab has firm meat. If it sinks, it's a hollow crab with little meat; these crabs are often pungent and not tasty.
Best time for crabs: Crabs are fattest, firmest, and sweetest at the beginning and end of the lunar month. The middle of the month is usually when crabs molt, so they are thin and have little meat.

mon_an.ten: Shrimp and Pumpkin Porridge for Babies
mon_an.mo_ta: Shrimp and pumpkin porridge is not only visually appealing for babies and families but also provides many healthy nutrients. Simmering glutinous rice with pumpkin gives the porridge a natural sweetness, combined with nutritious shrimp to create a dish that children will surely love. Let's learn how to cook this delicious dish to add variety and interest to your family menu!
cac_buoc: 1. How to cook shrimp and pumpkin porridge
1. Wash the glutinous rice thoroughly and soak it in water for about 2 hours to let it expand, which helps it cook faster and become smoother.
2. Peel the pumpkin, wash it, and cut it into small chunks. Clean the scallions and cilantro, then mince them.
3. Trim the heads and tails of the fresh shrimp, peel them, remove the black veins on the back, wash them, and drain.
4. Let the shrimp drain for about 10 minutes, then grind or pound them finely. Marinate the minced shrimp with seasoning powder and minced scallions.

5. Next, bring water to a boil in a pot, add the glutinous rice and pumpkin at the same time, and cook. Stir frequently to make the porridge smoother and prevent it from sticking to the bottom of the pot. If the pumpkin is still lumpy, use a spoon to mash it finely.
6. Once the porridge is cooked, add the shrimp and continue to cook. When the shrimp is done, season with salt, seasoning powder, and minced scallions. Stir well, then remove from the heat and serve.
2. Shrimp and pumpkin porridge with cheese
2.1 Ingredients
3 - 4 fresh tiger prawns.
100g pumpkin.
1 bowl of pre-cooked plain white porridge.
1 slice of cheese.
Cooking oil for babies.
Minced shallots.
2.2 Instructions
Peel the shrimp, remove the heads, legs, and the vein on the back. Wash the shrimp and mince or chop them finely.
Peel the pumpkin, wash it, and slice it into small pieces.

Place a pan on the stove, add a little cooking oil, and wait for it to heat up. Add the shrimp to the pan and stir-fry until cooked. Once cooked, turn off the heat and let it cool. Then, put the shrimp in a blender and blend until smooth.

Place a pot on the stove and add about 500ml of water along with 1 bowl of pre-cooked porridge and the pumpkin. Cook until soft. Once the porridge and pumpkin are tender, use a ladle to mash the pumpkin into the pot, then add 1 slice of cheese and stir well.
Turn off the heat and ladle the porridge into a bowl. Top with the blended shrimp and a little cooking oil. Serve to the baby while still warm.
3. Shrimp and pumpkin porridge with carrots
3.1 Ingredients
1 bowl of plain white porridge.
2 fresh shrimp.
50g pumpkin.
50g carrots.
A little cooking oil for babies.
3.2 Instructions
Peel the shrimp, remove the legs, head, and the vein on the back. Wash the shrimp and steam until cooked. Then, blend or mince the shrimp finely.
Peel the pumpkin and carrots, wash them, and slice into small pieces. Steam the carrots and pumpkin until soft. Then, mash or blend the carrots and pumpkin.

Place a pot on the stove, add the white porridge and 200ml of water, and bring to a boil. Add the pumpkin, shrimp, and carrots to the pot. Stir well and bring the porridge back to a boil. Turn off the heat and add a little cooking oil. For older children, you can season according to their taste.
Ladle the porridge into a bowl and serve to the baby.
4. Shrimp and pumpkin porridge with lotus seeds
4.1 Ingredients
100g lotus seeds.
100g fresh tiger prawns.
50g glutinous rice.
50g plain rice.
Minced shallots.
Cooking oil and seasoning for babies.
4.2 Instructions
Wash the glutinous rice and plain rice, then soak in water for about 2 hours to let them expand.
Wash the lotus seeds, remove the bitter core (germ), and soak in water for about 1 hour.
Peel the pumpkin and dice it.
Peel the shrimp, remove the heads and legs, pull out the black vein on the back, and wash. Marinate the shrimp with a little seasoning powder for babies, then blend or mince finely.
Put the rice, pumpkin, lotus seeds, and 1 liter of water into a pot and simmer until it becomes a soft porridge.
Sauté the minced shallots with a little cooking oil, then add the shrimp and stir-fry until cooked.

Wait for the porridge to soften, then add the sautéed shrimp and stir well. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then cook for another 3 minutes. Finally, turn off the heat and ladle the porridge into a bowl for the baby to enjoy.
5. Shrimp, pumpkin, carrot, and apple porridge
5.1 Ingredients
1 bowl of pre-cooked porridge.
20g shrimp.
5g pumpkin.
5g carrots.
10g apple.
Cooking oil for babies.
5.2 Instructions
Peel and wash the pumpkin and carrots, then cut into small pieces. Boil the pumpkin and carrots until soft, then mash them.
Peel the shrimp, remove the vein, head, and legs, then mince finely. Mix the shrimp with 1/3 bowl of filtered water, use chopsticks to stir well, then cook until done and blend until smooth.
Wash the apple, peel it, and remove the seeds. Blanch it in boiling water and mash it finely.
Put the porridge, shrimp mixture, carrots, and pumpkin into a pot and simmer over low heat. When the porridge boils, stir well and add the apple. Add a little cooking oil and turn off the heat.
Ladle the porridge into a bowl and let it cool slightly before serving while still warm.
How to choose shrimp and pumpkin
1. Tips for buying fresh shrimp
Choose shrimp with firm shells that are uniform in color and transparent. This is a sign of fresh shrimp.

Observe the tail of the shrimp. If the tail is folded tightly together, it is naturally fresh shrimp. Conversely, if the tail is flared out, the shrimp may have been injected with water to increase weight.

Avoid buying shrimp with backs curved into a circle and those that leak slimy fluid. These are signs that the shrimp have been kept for a long time and will not retain their characteristic sweetness when cooked.
2. How to choose delicious pumpkin
A good pumpkin should feel heavy and have a certain degree of firmness when picked up. Soft pumpkins are usually old, starting to wither, and no longer fresh.
Observe the stem of the pumpkin. If the stem is still soft, it is a sign of a newly harvested pumpkin. Conversely, if the stem is dry and withered, the pumpkin was harvested a long time ago.
Choose pumpkins with stems longer than 2 pinky finger joints. This helps the pumpkin stay preserved longer after purchase.
Avoid buying pumpkins with cracks, bruises, or unusual slimy discharge. These are signs of poor-quality pumpkins.

mon_an.ten: Delicious Braised Potatoes You Might Not Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Braised potatoes feature small potatoes that are soft and smooth on the inside, crispy on the outside, and soaked in a savory, delicious sauce. This is a unique and tasty dish that many people have never tried. Today, let's get into the kitchen to make braised potatoes for the whole family to enjoy.
cac_buoc: Prepare bite-sized bags of small, pretty potatoes like these.
Steps to make braised potatoes:
Select potatoes that are not rotten and wash them thoroughly with cold water. Let the potatoes drain.
Add cooking oil to a pan and set the stove to medium heat. Once the oil is hot, start adding the potatoes to the pan.
Cover the pan and cook the potatoes until fully softened, about 20 minutes.
Open the lid and toss the potatoes occasionally so they cook evenly; do not use heat that is too high to avoid burning the potatoes.
After 20 minutes, reduce the heat and add the soy sauce, sugar syrup, and garlic to the potatoes. Stir everything well.
Increase the heat, stir the potatoes constantly, and continue cooking for another 5 minutes until the sauce thickens into a glaze, and the potato skins look shiny and slightly wrinkled.
Turn off the heat and mix the potatoes with sesame oil. Sprinkle some toasted sesame seeds on top.
Transfer the potatoes to a plate and enjoy with hot rice.
You can store these braised potatoes in the refrigerator and continue to use them for 2-3 days; they will still be delicious.
These braised potatoes are excellent with this method; try making them for your family.
Enjoy your meal and success with this Korean-style braised potato dish!

mon_an.ten: Tips for Making Excellent Shrimp Salad
mon_an.mo_ta: Shrimp salad is low in fat and very good for those who want to lose weight or stay in shape. Additionally, you can make this dish for family parties; it is quite delicious and elegant!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Lettuce, purple cabbage, a few stalks of Malabar spinach
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the shrimp, peel them, and remove the back veins.
Place the shrimp in a bowl and toss well with cornstarch.
Wash the vegetables, shake dry, and tear into small pieces.
Step 2:
Heat a pan with just enough olive oil to coat the surface.
Add crushed garlic and sauté until fragrant, then add the shrimp, using chopsticks to spread them evenly across the pan.
Watch for the shrimp meat to turn pinkish-red, then lower the heat and add half of the salt, pepper, and chili powder, stirring well.
Step 3:
Quickly squeeze the juice of half a lemon directly into the pan with the shrimp and continue to stir quickly.
This process only takes about 2–3 minutes until the shrimp turn a golden color, then turn off the heat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tamarind beef is a favorite dish for many families, featuring fresh, tender beef soaked in a sweet and sour tamarind sauce that provides a delicious sensation for the diner.
cac_buoc: Prepare ingredients for tamarind beef:
Wash the beef with water. Next, slice the beef into bite-sized pieces and marinate with oyster sauce and soy sauce; let it sit for 20 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Peel the onion, remove the root, wash, and cut into wedges.
Clean the scallions, removing the roots and wilted leaves, then wash. Wash the chilies and mince them.
Peel the garlic, wash, and mince.
Steps to make sweet and sour tamarind beef.
Step 1: First, heat cooking oil in a pan and sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Then, add the beef and stir-fry quickly for about 2 minutes or until the beef is just cooked through. Remove and set aside.

Step 2: Next, in another pan, sauté more garlic, then pour in the tamarind juice and bring to a boil. Keep over medium heat for a few minutes, then add the cornstarch (mixed with a little water), stir well, and cook until the sauce thickens.
Step 3: Then, add the cooked beef back in, stir for 1-2 minutes, then add the onion, scallions, and minced chili. Stir until just cooked, then turn off the heat.
Finally, present the beef on a plate and enjoy.
Notes for delicious tamarind beef
Do not stir-fry the beef over the fire for too long as it will lose its flavor and become tough; remove from heat as soon as the beef and onions are just cooked.
If tamarind juice is not available, buy ripe tamarind pods, soak them in boiling water, mash them, and strain to get the clear liquid.
*How to choose good beef:*

When buying, choose meat that is bright red (not too dark), with small fibers, dry, smooth, firm, and not sticking to your hands. If the fat is yellow, the meat will be soft and fatty. Young beef has white fat, soft meat, and very fine fibers. Old beef has large fibers, a purplish-red color, and grayish fat; it is tough and takes a long time to soften. Female beef is usually tastier than male beef. If you can choose heifer beef, it is even better as the meat is soft with white fat and fine fibers.
Beef that is pale green with white spots between the fibers may be infected with parasites. Do not buy meat that has a foul odor.
Distinguishing between buffalo and beef
You can immediately identify buffalo meat: it is pale pink, has large fibers, and a deep red color, but the fat is whiter than beef fat.
Some ways to process and tenderize beef

Slicing meat: To slice beef thinly without it crumbling, wrap the meat tightly and place it in the freezer until it is slightly firm. When cooking, take it out and slice; it will be easier and look better.
Removing beef odor: Take a piece of ginger, grill it until cooked, scrape off the burnt skin, crush it, and rub it on the meat. Rinse the meat thoroughly with cold water.

Tenderizing beef: The simplest way is to add a little salt to the pot when cooking. For tough beef, you can tenderize it by boiling. When the water boils, skim off the foam and add about one teaspoon of white wine for every 1 kg of meat. Continue to simmer for 10–15 minutes, and the meat will soften immediately. Additionally, before stir-frying, you can wash raw papaya leaves, crush them, wrap the meat, and leave it near the stove to warm up; when stir-frying, take it out and slice thinly. For beef tendons, shanks, or ribs that you want to eat quickly without long stewing times, add a piece of pineapple, an ice cube, or an aluminum spoon to the cooking pot.

mon_an.ten: Effective Ways to Remove Burnt Food Odors from Your Home
cac_buoc: How to remove burnt food odors from the house – After a busy day, sometimes you might lose focus while cooking, causing food to burn and the smell to linger throughout the house.
How to remove the smell of burnt food lingering in the house

The first thing you should do is quickly open all windows and doors to let the smoke escape. Turn on fans, ventilation fans, or the kitchen hood; at this time, better air circulation will reduce the amount of burnt smoke.
Methods for deodorizing the house:
Step 1: Prepare a natural deodorizing mixture: Mix water and lemon juice in a 1:1 ratio, put it in a spray bottle, and spray throughout the kitchen.
Step 2: Place bowls of baking soda around the house; this powder absorbs odors quite well.
Step 3: Burn lemon, kumquat, or grapefruit peels, or dry out used tea leaves; the burnt smell will quickly disappear.
Step 4: Use onions to deodorize: Cut an onion and place it in a bowl of water. Place a bowl of this onion water wherever the burnt smell is strongest; the effect will be immediate.
Handling burnt food

When food is burning on the stove, quickly turn off the heat, move the cookware to a cool place, and then remove the food. If it is completely burnt, you should discard it as burnt food is not good for your health. If the food is not entirely burnt, take the unburnt part and put it on a plate, then quickly put the burnt part into a trash bag, tie it tightly, and put it in the trash can.

With the remaining food, you can continue cooking by first rinsing it with clean water, then placing it back on the stove. At this point, you don't need to add too much seasoning as it has already been seasoned once.

To mask the burnt smell during cooking, you can add sauces such as tomato sauce or garlic butter sauce to overpower the odor, or add scallions and cilantro after cooking; the burnt smell will be significantly reduced.

mon_an.mo_ta: Eggs are exceptionally nutritious and an essential food for every family. However, not every home cook knows the best ways to use and store them. Today, we will guide you through some handy tips for using eggs.
cac_buoc: To prevent boiled eggs from cracking: When boiling eggs at high temperatures, shells often crack, and the whites may even leak out. To avoid this, add a pinch of salt to the water before boiling to help keep the shells intact.

Good eggs vs. bad eggs: You can use a pot or pan, fill it with water, and add a little salt. Place the eggs in the water. If they sink to the bottom, they are good. If they float to the surface, the eggs are spoiled.

Storing eggs: You should put the entire bag of eggs bought from the market directly into the refrigerator (it is even better if they are packed in a cardboard carton). Placing eggs right in the refrigerator door is not ideal for storage for the following reasons: + Eggs are subject to frequent temperature changes every time you open the door. + You can easily break the eggs accidentally if they are placed there.
We hope this article provides you with more useful experience in using eggs and managing your kitchen!

mon_an.ten: Cooking Tips to Improve Your Culinary Skills
mon_an.mo_ta: During the food preparation process, just a few small tips can make your dishes much more attractive. Let's refer to the cooking tips below to enhance your culinary talents!
cac_buoc: Tips to know when grilling meat

You should not grill directly over coal with high flames; instead, grill over low heat, as this temperature is enough to cook the meat while ensuring nutrients are preserved. When grilling on a gas stove, wrap the meat in foil to prevent it from charring. Avoid burning the edges of the meat; after each use, you must scrub the grill grate clean, as charred spots on the meat and the grate contain acrolein, which can be carcinogenic.
When grilling meat, pay attention to the following issues.
Before putting the meat on the grill, dip it in boiling water or hot broth to help soften the meat; once grilled, it will be crispier and more succulent.
When grilling, cook one side thoroughly before flipping to the other; do not flip back and forth constantly as it wastes time and takes longer to cook.
In the oven, place a bowl (or basin, depending on the oven size) of water; the water will heat up and evaporate, preventing the meat from burning or becoming tough.

You should marinate meat with shallots, as shallots and garlic contain substances that inhibit the growth of microorganisms. Therefore, using crushed shallots and garlic to marinate meat will keep it fresh longer and make it more delicious.
Tips for steaming and double-boiling
When steaming fish or meat, use boiling water in the steamer pot to ensure continuous heat application.
Steaming eggs: Use low heat so the heat acts gently and gradually.
Steaming cakes: Use high heat to make the cakes rise and become fluffy.

When steaming multiple dishes at once, do not open the lid frequently. Drop a clean piece of pottery into the boiling water; it will be pushed to the bottom and make a sound. If you no longer hear the sound, the water in the pot has run dry.
Tips for stir-frying dishes

First, place the pan on the stove and use high heat to get it hot. Prepare a sufficient amount of oil for the dishes you want to stir-fry in a large, dry, and clean bowl. Once the pan is hot, ladle a spoonful of oil from the bowl into the pan, swirl it to coat the sides, and then start stir-frying the first dish. When cooked, drizzle in another spoonful of oil, toss quickly, and remove from the pan to a plate. After the first dish, continue with the second, third, and so on. Note: Adjust the heat according to each dish, and always heat the pan first before adding room-temperature oil.

You should also plan the order of the dishes. Even within the same dish, consider the order of ingredients. For example, for a dish with both meat and green vegetables, stir-fry the meat first, remove it to a bowl, then stir-fry the vegetables, and finally mix the meat back in and add seasonings.
Tips for frying
When the center of the oil surface bubbles vigorously, the temperature is about 100°C; at this point, you can fry peanuts or eggs.
When smoke begins to rise, the oil temperature is about 170°C; you can fry poultry.

When the oil is smoking heavily and the surface appears calm again, the temperature is about 200°C; at this point, you can stir-fry ribs or cartilage with sugar and vinegar for the second time (the first time the oil should not be too hot).
To make a dish crispy on the outside but tender on the inside, you can process the food twice at two different temperatures.
Tips for braising and stewing
When braising, use only low heat; you can add a little fat or vegetable oil and do not flip the ingredients.
When frying, the most important issue is mastering the oil temperature; different ingredients require different levels of heat.

mon_an.ten: Ways to Decorate the Lunar New Year Feast
mon_an.mo_ta: As Tet approaches, decorating the feast becomes an important part of creating a solemn and festive atmosphere. Whether you prefer traditional or modern styles, they all create a cozy and meaningful space for family and loved ones to gather. Today, we will share some ways to decorate the Tet feast in the article below! Explore decoration ideas that create a warm and meaningful space for your family during the New Year.
cac_buoc: 1. How to decorate pickled onions
"Fatty meat, pickled onions, red couplets. Ritual poles, firecrackers, green Bánh Chưng." This traditional saying highlights the importance of pickled onions in the Tet feast.
To decorate a beautiful plate of pickled onions, arrange the onions in circles with overlapping layers to create a stunning white chrysanthemum shape.

Then, use a green chili, slice it lengthwise, and use one half as the flower stem and the other half carved into two leaves. Finally, add a drop of chili sauce to make the flower stamen, enhancing its beauty.
2. How to decorate a beautiful plate of Vietnamese ham (Giò)
To decorate a plate of Giò, cut the four edges of a round slice so the middle part is square. Then, cut each edge piece in half and piece them back together for a very eye-catching display.
You can also cut the round slice in half, then slice it thinly and arrange it in a fan shape. You can add cucumber flowers and various herbs to make the plate more beautiful.
If you have cinnamon ham (chả quế), you can cut the Giò into 6 or 8 equal pieces. Arrange the Giò on the bottom and place diamond-shaped pieces of cinnamon ham on top.
If you don't want a complicated decoration, you can use a wavy knife to cut the ham slices for a very nice look.
3. How to carve various types of flowers

With one carrot, you can carve a very beautiful rose. Use a medium carrot, shave it into thin horizontal slices, and soak them in sugar-vinegar for 30 minutes to soften. Then, layer them to form a flower.

To carve a rice stalk shape, use a cucumber, cut it at a 45-degree angle, then use a knife to cut an odd number of thin slices (5 or 7). Next, use your hand to roll one slice straight and one slice curled, then soak in water for 5-7 minutes to get a beautiful flower.
If you love lotuses, carve a tomato by dividing it into 6 parts and using a knife to lightly cut the outer skin. Then, simply separate them into petals.
4. How to decorate boiled chicken for Tet

Lemon leaves and banana leaves can be used to decorate boiled chicken. Slice lemon leaves thinly and sprinkle them evenly over the chicken to enhance flavor and color. Banana leaves can be used to line the plate or decorate around it, bringing a natural and fresh beauty.
You can also carve flowers from vegetables like carrots, celery, or onions and place them around the chicken plate. This creates color highlights and makes the feast more attractive.
To create a traditional and unique atmosphere, place the boiled chicken on bamboo trays lined with banana leaves. This not only looks beautiful but also creates a traditional space.
To make the chicken plate more eye-catching, cut cucumbers and tomatoes into beautiful shapes like flowers or stars and arrange them around the chicken.
Finally, place a bowl of dipping sauce in the center of the plate and decorate around it with chopped red chilies. This creates a focal point and makes the dish more appealing.
5. How to decorate Bánh Chưng and Bánh Tét for Tet

Decorate Bánh Chưng and Bánh Tét by lining the plate or wooden tray with banana leaves before placing the cakes. Banana leaves not only create a highlight but also bring a characteristic aroma to the cakes.

Using a wooden tray to present Bánh Chưng and Bánh Tét is a way to create a focal point and bring a traditional feel to the meal. You can decorate the tray with banana leaves, fresh flowers, or candles to make the feast more special.

To create a fresh and stylish feast, choose Bánh Chưng and Bánh Tét with diverse colors. You can choose magenta plant Bánh Chưng (lá cẩm), banana leaf Bánh Tét, or even white Bánh Tét to create color variety on the table.
Finally, place a sprig of fresh flowers between the Bánh Chưng and Bánh Tét to add freshness and vibrancy to the dining space. This will make the feast more attractive and radiant.
6. How to decorate fried spring rolls (Nem rán) for Tet

Using a bamboo tray to decorate the plate of fried spring rolls is a popular way to create a special highlight. Placing spring rolls on a bamboo tray brings a natural look and highlights their shape and color.

Additionally, you can carve flowers from vegetables like carrots, onions, or cucumbers to decorate around the spring roll plate. This not only creates a beautiful feast but also adds flavor and nutritional value to the dish.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried squid tentacles with vegetables not only offer great flavor but also provide many health benefits. Squid tentacles are a source of protein and omega-3 fatty acids beneficial for heart health. Vegetables are also rich in vitamins and fiber, helping to improve digestion and support weight loss. Let's explore the recipe for stir-fried squid tentacles with vegetables! Enjoy this delicious and nutritious dish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, salt, pepper, garlic, chili - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients
Crush and mince the garlic. Peel and julienne the ginger.

First, separate the squid head from the body, then clean the inside of the mantle, removing the eyes and the internal bone (pen). The squid can be cut into rings or cross-hatched into a dragon scale pattern depending on preference.
Next, to reduce the fishy smell, boil 2 bowls of water in a pan, then add the julienned ginger and blanch the squid quickly. Remove and drain.
Then, marinate the squid with 1 tsp of seasoning powder and let it sit for about 15 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Slice the cucumber lengthwise. Cut the tomatoes into wedges. Trim the celery, removing old stalks, and cut into sections. Cut the onion into wedges and soak in salt water to reduce the pungency.
Step 2: Cooking

Place a pan on the stove and add cooking oil. Once the oil is hot, add the minced garlic and sauté until fragrant. When the garlic is light golden and aromatic, quickly add the squid to the pan to sear it.

Next, add the onion, celery, and cucumber to the pan and stir-fry for about 2 minutes. Then, turn off the heat and sprinkle with a bit of ground pepper to enhance the aroma. The squid will be perfectly cooked, with a beautiful white color, sweet meat, and a crunchy texture without being fishy. The beautifully carved squid combined with the colorful variety of vegetables creates an attractive and delicious meal for your family.
How to choose fresh squid
Select squid with a shiny color, a milky white body, and firm, highly elastic meat.
Fresh squid will have clear eyes that are not bulging. The tentacles should be firmly attached to each other.
Avoid choosing squid with cloudy eyes, fluid leakage, or an unpleasant odor, as these are signs of spoiled or poor-quality squid.
Notes for stir-fried squid with vegetables
Choose fresh squid: Select squid with bright colors, milky white bodies, and firm meat. Avoid those with cloudy eyes, leakage, or bad smells.
Prepare vegetables: Choose fresh and clean vegetables. Wash and prepare them according to instructions for the right size and shape for stir-frying.
Cut squid evenly: When cutting the squid, make uniform pieces to ensure they cook evenly and quickly.
Stir-fry quickly: When stir-frying squid, use high heat and work quickly so the squid doesn't lose its elasticity and become tough.
Boil water to reduce fishy smell: Before stir-frying, you can boil water and dip the squid in quickly to reduce the fishy odor. Then, remove and drain.
Season to taste: Marinate the squid with seasonings like salt, pepper, seasoning powder, or your favorite spices to enhance the flavor.
Stir-fry vegetables briefly: When stir-frying vegetables, do it for a short time to maintain their crunch. Ensure the vegetables are not overcooked and still retain their bright colors.

mon_an.ten: Lucky Foods to Eat for the New Year
mon_an.mo_ta: Grapes, pork, green vegetables, pomegranates... are foods that signify luck for several countries around the world during the New Year.
cac_buoc: For many people, January 1st is an opportunity to forget the past and make a fresh start. Instead of leaving it to fate, why not enjoy a wonderful meal that also brings luck for the new year? There are many types of food believed to bring luck and great things if enjoyed on New Year's Day.

New Year traditions vary by country, but they all share common cultural and culinary characteristics. Popular foods used to welcome the new year and bring luck often include: grapes, green vegetables, fish, pork, beans, and cakes.
Grapes

In Spain, grapes are an indispensable food for the New Year. On New Year's Eve, family members usually eat one grape at a time until the clock strikes midnight. If someone finishes all 12 grapes before the new year begins, it means they will have a prosperous year. Each grape symbolizes a month of the year; therefore, Spaniards often choose plump, sweet grapes for a sweet and lucky new year.
Green vegetables

On New Year's Day, people from the South American coast to Europe often eat leafy green vegetables, including kale and cabbage, because their color and shape resemble paper money. People in these countries also believe that the more leafy greens you eat, the wealthier and healthier you will be throughout the new year.
Beans

Beans include peas, lentils, etc. On New Year's Day, Italians often prepare Cotechino con Lenticchie (green lentils with sausage) because they believe lentils are green and shaped like coins. Notably, when cooked, lentils swell up in the water, symbolizing prosperity and wealth.

Lentils are also considered a lucky food in Hungary, where they enjoy lentil soup on New Year's Day. Additionally, Germans use beans and pork served with soup to welcome the new year. In Japan, osechi-ryori—the traditional symbolic food served during the first three days of the year—also includes a type of sweet black bean called kuro-mame.
Pork

In countries like Cuba, Spain, Portugal, Hungary, and Austria, pigs symbolize growth and prosperity. They believe this animal always moves forward, typically pushing its snout forward to eat all the food in the trough. Because of this characteristic, these countries never forget to serve pork dishes with the hope of a successful and prosperous new year.
Not limited to pork meat, foods shaped like pigs (such as cookies, cakes...) are also lucky foods on New Year's Day in these countries.
Herring

In Germany, Poland, and Scandinavia, it is believed that eating herring at midnight on New Year's will ensure a year of wealth and abundance. Furthermore, their silver color is similar to that of coins, a good omen for future fortune. Germans even put a few herring scales in their wallets at the beginning of the year for good luck.
Cakes

Baked goods or pastries used to welcome the new year are often round—symbolizing coins and a prosperous year. In many countries, people even hide a coin inside the cakes when baking to bring unexpected luck to the person who finds it.

For example, in the Southern United States, cornbread is a very popular dish. This dish is indispensable on New Year's Day because its color resembles the color of gold. For extra luck, many people add corn kernels because they look like natural gold nuggets.
Pomegranate

For Turkish people, the pomegranate represents luck. They believe the red color of the pomegranate symbolizes the human heart, signifying life and fertility; the medicinal components of the pomegranate represent health, and the round seeds symbolize prosperity and progress. For these reasons, this fruit is always considered a lucky fruit for Turkish people every New Year.

Additionally, some foods are considered unsuitable for the New Year and are avoided in many places, such as shrimp because they move backward and may represent failure; poultry is also "tabooed" because they have wings and might carry luck away.

mon_an.ten: Important Notes on Eating Jackfruit in Hot Weather
mon_an.mo_ta: Many women choose jackfruit as a fruit to enjoy this summer; therefore, knowing some important notes when eating this delicious fruit will help prevent illness!
cac_buoc: Eating jackfruit is not as "hot" as you think

Addressing the concern of most women that eating jackfruit causes internal heat and acne: nutritionists say this concept is incorrect. No ripe fruit is inherently "hot"; there are only fruits with high sugar content. If eaten in excess, it is not good for health.

People prone to acne, heat rash, or styes should not eat too much, especially on hot days, because the high sugar content in ripe fruit increases blood sugar, creating a favorable environment for bacteria to grow, especially staphylococcus, the cause of acne and impetigo.

Besides, many people fear eating jackfruit will make you gain weight? Not really. Jackfruit only causes weight gain if you eat too much. If eaten in reasonable amounts, jackfruit can actually help with weight loss and is good for health.

Additionally, jackfruit is an excellent source of vitamin C and vitamin A, which increase the body's resistance. With high vitamin A and strong antioxidant properties from vitamin C, and because it is eaten raw, the fruit retains its full vitamin and mineral content, helping to maintain moisture for glowing skin and reducing wrinkles.
Although it is a fruit with many health benefits, the following 4 groups of people should be cautious as eating jackfruit may worsen their condition:
Fatty liver

According to research, jackfruit is rich in nutrients and vitamins, but it contains a lot of sugar and is not good for the liver. Therefore, advice for people with fatty liver is not to eat jackfruit frequently, or even avoid it entirely.
Chronic kidney failure

Patients with chronic kidney failure should avoid potassium-rich foods like jackfruit. When the kidneys fail, potassium accumulates, leading to hyperkalemia, which can cause sudden cardiac arrest and death without warning if levels are too high.
Diabetes

Diabetic patients need to follow a "sugar-restricted" diet. Meanwhile, jackfruit contains a lot of fructose and glucose, which are absorbed immediately by the body, leading to a rapid increase in blood sugar levels.
Chronic illnesses
Advice for people with chronic illnesses: it is best to only view jackfruit as a treat for enjoyment and avoid eating it regularly.
How to eat jackfruit healthily
Only eat jackfruit 1-2 hours after a meal; avoid eating on an empty stomach as it can cause bloating and indigestion.
Eat in moderate amounts; for those with chronic illnesses, eat a maximum of 80g (about 3-4 segments per day).
Eat jackfruit along with other ripe fruits to provide sufficient vitamins and minerals for the body.
Chew thoroughly and avoid eating in the evening.
If you have internal heat or are prone to acne, supplement with enough water (2 - 2.5l/day) and green vegetables when eating jackfruit.
Tips for cutting jackfruit without the sap sticking

When cutting jackfruit, to prevent sap from sticking to your hands, you should wear gloves, or you can rub a layer of cooking oil on your palms, or rub your hands in a rice bin. Afterward, wash your hands with warm salt water, and the sap will not stick.
To clean jackfruit sap off a knife, put the knife in the freezer to let the sap harden, then it can be easily peeled off. You can also use a plastic bag to dab and pull the sap off the knife.

mon_an.ten: Useful Kitchen Hacks for Home Cooks
mon_an.mo_ta: For home cooks who are frequently in the kitchen, many may feel puzzled while cooking, such as not knowing how to fry fish without it sticking, the most effective way to remove garlic and onion smells from hands, or how to boil eggs without cracking... With a few kitchen hacks we share below, you will gain knowledge to apply effectively. Please refer to this article!
cac_buoc: Useful kitchen tips for home cooks 1
Tip for frying fish without sticking

For a regular pan, how do you prevent fish from sticking? You can do the following: Put 2 tablespoons of fine salt in the pan and roast it evenly. When the salt turns light yellow, pour it all out and start adding oil to fry the fish. This tip ensures your fried fish won't stick and will be very crispy, delicious, and attractive.
Tip for removing onion and garlic smells from hands

While preparing food, you cannot avoid direct contact with onions and garlic, and this scent can be unpleasant and linger on hands for a long time, even after using hand wash or soap. To solve this, use a stainless steel spoon to rub firmly over your hands under cold running water for about 5 minutes. You will see the onion and garlic smell completely vanish. You can also use fresh lemon to clean and leave a pleasant scent on your hands.
Tip for boiling eggs without cracking

Many women wonder and want to find a way to boil eggs so they stay intact without cracking. You should put the eggs in cold water and add a little salt. Remember not to put the eggs in while the water is already boiling!
Tip for simmering bones to soften quickly

If you don't have a pressure cooker but want to simmer bones quickly until tender to save time and effort, try this: Add a teaspoon of MSG to the pot of simmering bones. When the pot boils, drop in 3-4 ice cubes, cover tightly, and continue to simmer. This ensures your bone broth will become tender very quickly!
Tip for marinating food to absorb flavor quickly

In the process of making a delicious dish, the marinating step is very important. Add 1 tablespoon of cooking oil to your marinade and mix well. The oil helps the seasonings dissolve quickly and allows the food to absorb the flavors much faster, so you don't have to wait long.
Tip for handling over-salted dishes
If you accidentally find a dish too salty, don't worry; try the following:
Add water: For soups or broths, simply add a little more water. It will neutralize the dish, which is very effective for salty food.
Add a few potato slices: For soups or stir-fries, just drop in a slice of potato. The potato will help absorb the saltiness quickly and effectively.
Add a little lemon juice: Lemon juice helps eliminate the salty taste and also enhances the flavor of the dish.

mon_an.ten: Tips to Prevent Vitamin Loss When Cooking Vegetables
mon_an.mo_ta: These tips to limit vitamin loss when processing vegetables will help you preserve the nutrients in your greens while preparing and cooking.
cac_buoc: Tips to limit vitamin loss when processing vegetables
Vegetable dishes easily lose vitamins during processing such as cooking, stir-frying, or boiling. To limit this, here are a few great tips:
1. Before boiling or stir-frying, note that finely chopped or shredded vegetables lose vitamins faster than those cut into larger pieces.

2. To boil vegetables quickly while minimizing nutrient loss, use a large pot and enough water to ensure the vegetables are fully submerged. This way, the vegetables cook faster than in a small pot. When removing the vegetables, the water also cools down faster, preventing it from turning dark.
3. When boiling vegetables, add a little salt to the water to limit vitamin loss during processing. This is the simplest way in cooking, but not everyone remembers to apply it.

4. You should add vegetables to water that is about to boil (many bubbles rising) rather than when it is already boiling, and absolutely never add vegetables to cold water, as vitamins will be completely destroyed during the heating process.
5. This tip reminds you to use just enough water to cover the surface of the vegetables. Exposing vegetables to air during the boiling process is one of the reasons vitamins decompose.

6. For dishes like steaming, always keep the lid tightly closed. For stir-fried or fried dishes, ensure there is a thin layer of cooking oil covering the vegetables. As mentioned in tip 5, when vegetables are processed in contact with air, vitamins decompose very quickly.

mon_an.ten: Simple Ways to Thaw Meat Quickly
mon_an.mo_ta: Thawing meat is an important step for home cooks preparing food from the freezer. However, not everyone knows how to thaw quickly while maintaining food quality. Let's explore quick meat thawing methods in the article below! I. Quick meat thawing methods
cac_buoc: Step 1: Thawing meat using kitchen seasonings
1.2. Using salt
Thawing quickly with salt not only speeds up the process but also helps prevent bacterial growth in the meat.

To thaw meat this way, place the frozen meat in warm water at about 40°C diluted with 2 tablespoons of salt, then let it sit to thaw gradually. To prevent the meat from partially cooking and to stop bacteria from entering, avoid using water below 30°C or above 50°C.
1.3. Using sugar
When thawing meat with sugar, you should only use it for meat and avoid seafood, as sugar can change the characteristic flavor of seafood.

To perform this method, mix cold water and warm water at 40°C in a ratio of 5 parts cold to 1 part warm, then add 2 tablespoons of sugar and stir well. Place the frozen meat in the water for about 7–10 minutes to thaw, then remove and drain.
1.4. Using vinegar

The acetic acid in vinegar helps melt ice in water, thereby speeding up the meat thawing process. To do this, dilute and stir warm water at about 40°C with 2–3 drops of vinegar and 1 teaspoon of salt.
Next, place the frozen meat in the vinegar water and soak for about 3–5 minutes. After this time, the meat will be thawed quickly, and it also helps reduce the natural fishy smell of the meat.
Step 2: Thawing with cold water

Thawing meat quickly with hot water is not recommended because it can lose protein and flavor while creating conditions for bacteria to enter. Conversely, the cold water thawing method is a suitable choice, helping to preserve vitamins and minerals in the meat.

The process is quite simple: wrap the meat tightly and place it in cold water, soaking for 30 minutes and changing the water once. A small but effective tip is to use an aluminum or stainless steel pot with cold water; the metal's thermal conductivity helps thaw faster. You can do it as follows: turn one pot upside down and place the tightly wrapped meat on the bottom. Next, pour cold water into another pot and place it on top of the meat for 3–7 minutes to thaw completely.
Step 3: Thawing meat quickly in the refrigerator

Thawing with hot water is not recommended because it can lose protein and flavor while creating conditions for bacteria to enter. Conversely, the cold water thawing method is a suitable choice, helping to preserve vitamins and minerals in the meat.
Step 4: Thawing with a microwave
Microwave thawing is a popular method used by many because it saves time. Simply wrap the meat carefully with plastic wrap, then place it in the microwave to thaw for 5 minutes at a low temperature.
However, after microwave thawing, it is important to cook the meat immediately to prevent bacterial entry, which leads to spoilage.
Also, pay attention to the thawing time to avoid overcooking the meat, which makes it bland and loses nutrients.
Step 5: Thawing meat with an oven
Take the meat from the freezer and place it in the refrigerator for 10–20 minutes to easily remove the plastic wrap.
Next, place the meat in a heat-resistant container like glass, cover it, and place it in the oven. Thawing meat in the oven for 10 minutes at 70°C will make the meat soft.
When thawing with an oven, be careful not to set the temperature too high to avoid the meat being frozen inside while the outside is partially cooked.
Step 6: Thawing with an air fryer
Take the meat from the freezer and remove the plastic wrap or container, then place the meat in a heat-resistant tray.
Next, place the meat in the air fryer and thaw for 5–7 minutes at 80°C. If the meat is not completely thawed after that time, flip it and continue thawing for another 3–5 minutes.
Once the meat is completely thawed, cook it immediately to avoid quality loss and prevent bacteria from entering the meat.
II. Notes when thawing meat

In modern life, we often store meat in the freezer to prevent spoilage and extend shelf life. This method helps reduce microbial and enzymatic activity and limits the oxidation rate of fats and proteins. However, improper freezing and thawing can increase the risk of harmful bacterial growth. Here are some things to avoid:
Thawing with hot oil: Although many think hot oil will help thaw meat faster, in reality, combining water and boiling oil can cause splattering, posing a danger.
Thawing with an oven: Meat after being thawed in an oven becomes "sensitive" to bacteria, so this method should be limited.
Thawing by heating: Placing meat in a pot and cooking it immediately without thawing not only extends cooking time but also reduces nutrients.
Thawing at room temperature: Letting meat thaw naturally at room temperature can create conditions for bacteria to enter and harm the meat.
Refreezing thawed meat: Thawed meat is easily contaminated with bacteria; refreezing can affect quality and cause poisoning.
Thawing but not using immediately: If meat is thawed but not processed immediately, bacteria can grow, spoiling the meat.
Soaking frozen meat in hot water: Using hot water to thaw can warm the surface of the food while the inside remains frozen, creating conditions for bacteria to grow.

mon_an.ten: Japanese Beef Curry with Potatoes and Carrots
mon_an.mo_ta: This delicious, warm, and spicy Japanese beef curry with potatoes and carrots is perfect for a meal on a cold day! Quickly head to the market for the necessary ingredients and make this delicious dish together! Here is the guide to cooking Japanese beef curry. Simple steps to create a tasty and rich meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Carrot - 1 unit, cut into bite-sized pieces
Potato - 1 unit, cut into bite-sized pieces
Onion - 1 unit, cut into large pieces
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the beef and slice it into pieces that are not too thick. Place the beef in a pot of boiling water and boil for 5-7 minutes to remove impurities and parcook it, then drain the beef in a colander and rinse with cold water until clean.
Step 2: Place the beef in a pot with 2 liters of water, ginger, and 3 scallion stalks. Place the pot on the stove and cook over medium heat until the meat is tender.

Step 3: Place a pan on the stove, add 2 tablespoons of oil, and once the oil is hot, sauté the onions for 2 minutes. Then add the garlic along with the carrots and potatoes and sauté until fragrant; season with a little salt for flavor.

Step 4: When the beef is slightly tender, add the potatoes, carrots, bay leaves, and curry powder to the pot. Season to taste and continue to simmer until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened slightly, then turn off the heat.
Enjoy your Japanese beef curry!
Notes when cooking Japanese beef curry with potatoes and carrots
Choose fresh ingredients: Select fresh beef without any odor, and choose potatoes and carrots that look fresh, without signs of wilting, discoloration, or damage.

Prepare seasonings to taste: Japanese curry usually has a mild and delicate flavor. Use main seasonings including curry powder, curry roux, sugar, soy sauce, and salt. Adjust the amount of seasoning to suit your personal taste.
Cut ingredients uniformly: Slice the beef, potatoes, and carrots into bite-sized pieces, ensuring they cook through at the same time.

Cook for the right amount of time: Cook the beef before adding the potatoes and carrots to ensure the meat is tender and absorbs the flavors. When adding potatoes and carrots, cook until they are soft but still retain some texture.
Add coconut milk for extra richness and smoothness: Adding a little coconut milk to the curry will create a smooth and rich creamy layer.
Enjoy the curry hot: Japanese beef curry with potatoes and carrots is best enjoyed while still hot to experience the best flavor.
How to choose fresh ingredients
How to choose beef

When buying beef, note the following: Choose pieces with a bright red color, white tendons, and bright yellow fat. Check elasticity by pressing the meat; it should bounce back, not be sticky, and have no unusual odor.
Limit buying pieces that are pale green or dark red, have dark yellow fat, or feel mushy and slimy to the touch, as the quality may not be guaranteed and could be hazardous to health.
How to choose good potatoes

When choosing potatoes, pay attention to the following: Choose yellow-fleshed potatoes to ensure sweetness, aroma, and high nutrient content. Avoid buying those that have sprouted or have green skin, as these can be toxic and dangerous, even fatal. Buy potatoes that feel heavy, have smooth skin, and show no unusual signs like black spots, insect damage, or rot.
How to choose good carrots

Choose medium-sized carrots that are straight and have smooth outer skin. Good carrots usually have a bright color; when held, they feel firm and have a small core. This type of carrot is the best for crunchiness and sweetness. Avoid choosing oversized ones, those with very large cores, or those that are misshapen, cracked, or bruised.
