mon_an.ten: Foods for people with high blood fat
mon_an.mo_ta: With foods beneficial for people with high blood fat—such as onions containing prostaglandin A, apples to help reduce blood fat, bean sprouts to lower bad cholesterol, salmon rich in omega-3, carp, and skinless chicken high in unsaturated fatty acids—you just need to pay a little attention. Increasing these foods in your daily diet contributes to reducing blood fat. These foods are not only good for those with high blood fat but for everyone. Just a small change in your meals can help the body absorb good nutrients, avoid toxins, and maintain a resilient, strong health.
cac_buoc: Onions – Help increase good cholesterol in the body

Onions are one of the very few foods containing prostaglandin A—a substance that helps dilate and soften blood vessels, reduce blood viscosity, increase coronary blood flow, and promote the excretion of blood lipids.
Additionally, regularly eating onions can reduce bad cholesterol, improve atherosclerosis, and increase beneficial cholesterol for the body.
Bean sprouts – Eliminate bad cholesterol

Bean sprouts are a type of food that functions to reduce bad cholesterol in the body. Notably, during the sprouting process, the vitamin content in bean sprouts increases about 67 times compared to the original beans. Vitamin C can promote cholesterol excretion and prevent accumulation in arterial walls. Bean sprouts contain a lot of fiber to help the body eliminate harmful cholesterol.
Apples – Absorb excess cholesterol
Apples are effective in reducing blood fat. They contain a lot of fiber soluble with acid. Imagine this compound like a sponge that absorbs excess cholesterol and triglycerides.
Furthermore, apples contain Pectin which can lower cholesterol and thus enhance the effectiveness of lowering blood fat levels.
Not only that, apples can break down acetic acid, an activity beneficial for preventing the catabolism of cholesterol and triglycerides.
However, to achieve maximum effectiveness in lowering blood fat, it is best to eat plenty of meat alongside vegetables and fruits for the best health protection.
Salmon – An "assistant" for lowering triglycerides
Salmon is rich in Omega-3 unsaturated fatty acids, which can reduce triglycerides, increase high-density lipoprotein cholesterol, and improve blood vessel elasticity.
Carp
Besides salmon, carp is also an excellent food for people with high blood fat.
Skinless chicken

Compared to pork, beef, lamb, and many other red meats, chicken contains more unsaturated fatty acids, making it very suitable for treating high blood fat. However, when eating chicken, you should remove the skin because it contains many impurities that are not good for health.

With a variety of foods like onions containing prostaglandin A, apples to reduce blood fat, bean sprouts to lower bad cholesterol, omega-3 rich salmon, carp, and skinless chicken high in unsaturated fatty acids, just a little mindfulness in your daily diet will help reduce blood fat. These foods are good for everyone. A small change in your meals helps the body absorb healthy nutrients and maintain a strong, durable health.

mon_an.mo_ta: Eggs are a familiar and easy-to-eat dish for Vietnamese people, but how many ways do you know to turn them into attractive meals? Today, I will guide you on how to make a Spanish-style egg dish! This Spanish Omelet is perfect for cold, damp days and offers a unique taste.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel and dice the onion. Peel, wash, and cube the potatoes. Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well.
Step 2: Add oil to a pan. When the oil is hot, add the onion and 1 tsp of salt. Fry over low heat for about 1-2 minutes.
Step 3: Add the potatoes. Cook over medium heat for 1-2 minutes, then turn the heat to low and simmer for 15 minutes. Afterward, remove everything and drain the oil.
Step 4: Mix the potatoes and onions thoroughly with the eggs, then pour the mixture back into the pan to fry until golden brown on both sides.
The omelet is soft and delicious, with the unique addition of potatoes and onions—it will be very tasty.

mon_an.mo_ta: Beef dishes are very diverse and abundant. However, not everyone has the secret to cooking these dishes successfully. Let's refer to a few small tips for preparing delicious beef.
cac_buoc: How to choose fresh meat: You should choose fresh meat so that when cooked, it is soft, sweet, and odorless. Fresh meat will have a layer of dry, bright yellow fat on the surface. The surface of the meat should be moist but not sticky. The meat should have good elasticity, a firm surface, and clearly visible muscle fibers.
Choosing meat based on cooking method: For stir-fry dishes, you should use fillet or tenderloin; these cuts will be tender after stir-frying.
For hotpot dipping, salads, or mixed salads, use beef shank because the tendons here are very crunchy, tender, and easy to eat.
For grilling or frying, you should choose a cut with a bit of fat so the meat doesn't dry out after cooking.

How to marinate meat: Do not marinate beef with salt before cooking because salt causes the meat to release its juices, reducing sweetness and making it tough. To make beef tender, mix the meat with 2 tsp of cooking oil before cooking to create a glossy, smooth texture. Do not marinate beef with too many spices; remember that the simpler the marinade, the more delicious the beef.
How to cook:

For stir-fry dishes: Stir-fry over high heat, tossing quickly and evenly so the spices penetrate and the pieces cook uniformly. As soon as the beef is just cooked, turn off the heat and remove it to serve immediately to maintain heat and sweetness.

For stewed dishes: Wait until the water is boiling vigorously before adding the meat to preserve nutrients and flavor. During the simmering process, add a little white wine or vinegar to help the meat become tender and soften quickly. Use beer for stewing to make the beef softer and more flavorful.

mon_an.ten: 10 secrets to becoming a great cook
mon_an.mo_ta: When entering the kitchen to prepare a family meal, we all hope to cook the most delicious, beautiful, and nutritious dishes. Today, I will share 10 small secrets that will help you cook much better! Refer to these and share them so everyone can become a professional home cook!
cac_buoc: 1. Tips for cooking porridge

When cooking porridge, you should soak the rice for 1 hour, then rinse it clean and add a small handful of glutinous rice to cook together. When the pot starts to boil, add a tablespoon of cooking oil to prevent it from overflowing and to enhance the flavor. If you have time, soak the rice for 2-3 hours so the grains expand evenly. If you don't want to use oil, place a wooden spoon across the top of the pot to prevent overflowing.
2. Tips for boiling noodles

Noodles, especially pasta, are a favorite for many. To boil pasta perfectly, wait until the water starts to bubble slightly, then add the noodles and stir so they are fully submerged. Add 1 tbsp of olive oil (or regular oil if olive oil is unavailable) and stir. Cover the pot until the water boils, then add a little cold water. Bring it back to a boil, then remove from heat, drain, and rinse with cold water. The noodles will be cooked through without being tough or sticking together.
3. Tips for seasoning with salt correctly

Not all dishes should have salt added directly at the start. For root vegetables, add salt earlier so it penetrates evenly. For boiled greens, only season with salt just before removing from the heat to prevent nutrient loss and to keep the vegetables from turning red or yellow, preserving their beautiful green color!
4. Tips for using soy sauce
Soy sauce contains sugar, so if added too early, the sugar will break down and create a sour or bitter taste. Therefore, you should only add soy sauce to the dish just before serving.
5. Seasoning with MSG

You should only use a small amount to enhance the flavor, as MSG is not great for health. Additionally, do not add MSG directly to the dish; dissolve it in a little stir-fry liquid or broth first before mixing it in.
6. Use extra water for stir-frying

When stir-frying vegetables, the dish often becomes dry and the nutrients in the vegetables evaporate. To retain nutrition, when the pan is hot, add 2-3 tbsp of water so the steam can cook the vegetables through without losing too much of their natural sweetness.
7. Tips for steaming fish

When steaming fish, if you rub a little beaten egg over the fish, it will absorb the nutrients from the egg, making the fish meat softer, more fragrant, and more nutritious. The dish will also have more depth of flavor.
8. How to remove fishy odors
After buying fish, to completely remove the fishy smell, you can soak it in a solution of 1 liter of water mixed with 3 tbsp of white wine and crushed ginger.
9. How to fry without oil splattering

To prevent oil from splattering when frying meat or fish, lightly dust the pan with a bit of flour first. If you want fried dishes to have a beautiful golden color—especially spring rolls—squeeze a few drops of lemon juice into the hot oil; your dish will have an extremely eye-catching color!
10. Using cooking oil vs. animal fat

You should use cooking oil for frying or cooking seafood because oil deodorizes fishy smells well. When stir-frying vegetables, use animal fat (lard) to give the greens a glossy finish and a better aroma.

mon_an.mo_ta: Gout is an increasingly common disease, but not everyone knows how to treat it effectively. Diet significantly affects those with gout. Note these 10 beneficial foods to build a suitable diet for yourself.
cac_buoc: The main cause of gout is consuming too much protein and alcohol while lacking physical activity. Therefore, gout patients must avoid purine-rich foods like seafood and organ meats.
Step 1: 1. Mustard greens

Mustard greens are excellent for gout patients as they help excrete uric acid. Boil mustard greens and drink the water daily instead of plain water. Regular consumption helps flush out uric acid and effectively prevents gout.
Step 2: Strawberries

Strawberries are low in calories but rich in nutrients, Vitamin C, and flavonoids. Not only do they beautify the skin and fight aging, but the Vitamin C in strawberries also helps treat the disease effectively.
Step 3: Pineapple

Pineapple is rich in organic acids like citric and malic acid, Vitamins A and B, and especially high in Vitamin C (60%), along with trace minerals and the digestive enzyme bromelain. Pineapple juice is nutritious, benefits digestion, and reduces atherosclerosis, kidney stones, arthritis, and gout.
Step 4: Adzuki beans

Also known as red beans, they are neutral in nature with a sweet and sour taste, helping to strengthen the spleen. Adzuki beans contain almost no purines, making them a very good food for gout patients.
Step 5: Cauliflower

Cauliflower is a vegetable low in purines (less than 75mg per 100g). According to traditional nutrition, cauliflower is cooling and sweet, helping to clear heat and act as a diuretic, making it suitable for those with high blood uric acid.
Step 6: Cherries

Cherries are very rich in Vitamin C, which can reduce uric acid levels in the blood. Gout patients who eat at least half a kilogram of cherries daily will feel more comfortable and experience less pain. In Vietnam, acerola cherries can be used as a substitute.
Step 7: Radish
Radishes are cooling and sweet, helping to benefit joints and eliminate heat and dampness. They are an alkaline vegetable, rich in vitamins and water, and contain almost no purines.
Step 8: Cabbage
Cabbage contains almost no purines. It benefits the joints and meridians, making it an excellent food for those with high blood uric acid.
Step 9: Winter melon

Winter melon clears heat, eliminates phlegm, acts as a diuretic, detoxifies, and aids weight loss. As an alkaline, water-rich food with very few purines, it effectively clears uric acid through the urinary tract.
Step 10: Watermelon

Watermelon is cold and sweet, clearing heat and acting as a diuretic. It contains many potassium salts and water, with almost no purines. This fruit is particularly good for those in the acute stage of gout.

mon_an.mo_ta: Hemorrhoids are a common condition. One of the causes is an improper diet, eating too many spicy foods, and drinking too little water. So, what is a proper diet? Which foods are best for people with hemorrhoids? This article answers those questions, hoping to help those concerned about this condition.
cac_buoc: The first rule for hemorrhoid patients regarding diet is to avoid spicy and hot foods (limit chili, ginger, pepper, alcohol, beer...). To reduce constipation (a cause of hemorrhoids), increase fiber by eating more vegetables and fruits. Drinking plenty of water also makes bowel movements easier.
Some foods are very good for hemorrhoid patients:
1. Blueberries: These are rich in iron, helping to restore damage to blood vessel walls and strengthen the overall vascular system.
2. Spinach: Helps bowel activity by cleaning and restoring the intestines thanks to its magnesium content. This nutrient-rich vegetable is very suitable for hemorrhoid sufferers.
3. Tonkin jasmine: Often used in soups or stir-fries. A folk remedy for hemorrhoids: 150g Tonkin jasmine flowers, 50g peeled tiger prawns, 50g tofu, and scallions/seasoning to make a soup.

4. Rice paddy herb: Those with hemorrhoids often suffer from constipation and internal heat, so they should eat cooling, laxative, and anti-inflammatory foods. One such dish is eel porridge with rice paddy herb. Method: 1-2 eels (100g) cleaned, 100g rice, 100g mung beans, 30g rice paddy herb, 50g culantro, and seasonings to cook the porridge.

5. Red radish: The Betacyanin in red radishes (which gives them their purple-red color) has anti-cancer effects. The high fiber content helps waste move through the intestines easily, preventing constipation and hemorrhoids.

6. Papaya: Green, fresh papaya with lots of sap can be used by cutting it in half and tying each half to the shins overnight (stem facing up) to help swollen hemorrhoids shrink. Use until they disappear.
Additionally, ripe papaya smoothies are great: 50g ripe papaya, 50g ripe sapodilla, and 50g strawberries blended together, drink 1-2 times a day.
7. Luffa: Use in soup: 100g luffa, 100g jute leaves, 50g ivy gourd leaves, 50g field crab meat, and seasonings. Eat a few times a week.

8. Fish mint: Use for steaming, washing, or as a poultice for prolapsed or painful hemorrhoids. Boil with water, steam the area while very hot, then wash when warm. Crush fresh fish mint to apply to the painful area.
9. Raisins: Internal hemorrhoids can cause significant blood loss leading to anemia, so supplement with iron-rich foods like raisins.
10. Figs: Figs treat many conditions like ulcers and gallstones, and are very effective for hemorrhoids.

Use figs for steaming and washing: Use 10 figs (or a piece of fig tree bark or a large handful of fig leaves) boiled with 1.5 - 2 liters of water. Steam the area for 30 minutes before bed, then wash with the water once it cools to 37°C - 38°C. Do this once daily for 8-10 days.

A proper diet is vital for prevention, treatment, and preventing recurrence. Don't forget that traditional herbal remedies are also very effective in quickly relieving the discomfort of this condition.

mon_an.mo_ta: Your bones need specific nutrients to grow healthy. Calcium and Vitamin D are well-known, but others like protein, omega-3 fatty acids, and Vitamins A, C, and K are also essential. Below are 18 foods that provide the necessary nutrients for bone development within a balanced diet. Let's explore these 18 foods!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Oranges and orange juice:

Oranges are rich in Vitamin C, which helps form collagen and contributes to bone health. One orange is also an effective source of Vitamin A for normal bone growth. Besides whole oranges, orange juice provides vitamins and helps beautify the skin.
Step 2: Milk:
Milk is an excellent source of calcium to keep bones strong. One cup of milk provides nearly 1/3 of your daily calcium needs. Milk is also fortified with Vitamin D to enhance calcium absorption.
Step 3: Parmesan cheese:

Parmesan contains 63mg of calcium in just one tablespoon of grated cheese—a large amount for such a small portion. It is also a source of protein and Vitamin A. Furthermore, it is very low in calories, making it great for weight loss. Other cheeses are also beneficial.
Step 4: Rhubarb leaves:

Rhubarb is rich in calcium—250ml of cooked rhubarb can provide 350mg of calcium. It also provides Vitamins C and A. If you aren't used to the taste, cook it with a little sugar and gradually reduce the amount. Research this plant before use to avoid side effects.
Step 5: Figs:
Figs contain essential minerals and vitamins for bones. One fresh fig provides about 20mg of calcium along with Vitamins C and K. Fresh figs are also high in fiber for digestion.
Step 6: Spinach:
Spinach is rich in Vitamins A, C, and K. It is delicious, versatile, and low in calories, making it a great staple for family meals.
You can cook spinach or eat it raw in salads or as a replacement for lettuce in sandwiches.
Step 7: Cashews:
Cashews contain small amounts of calcium and Vitamin K, but what makes them great for bones is the magnesium, other minerals, and protein they provide.
Step 8: Kiwi:
Kiwis are good for bones because they are rich in Vitamin C and magnesium. They also add calcium and Vitamins A and K to your daily intake. They are delicious and not fattening.
Step 9: Salmon:
Salmon is rich in Vitamin D and omega-3. It is also an excellent source of protein. Although salmon contains fat, it is not high in calories.
Canned salmon is a very convenient daily option.
Step 10: Soy milk:
Soy milk is a source of protein and omega-3 fatty acids. It is also fortified with calcium and Vitamin D for bones.
Step 11: Pumpkin seeds:
Pumpkin seeds contain calcium and protein, and are an excellent source of magnesium and omega-3. They are high in fiber and can be eaten as a snack or added to salads.
Step 12: Tomato juice:

Tomato juice contains many vitamins and minerals including magnesium, and Vitamins A and C. It also contains small amounts of calcium and Vitamin K. Drink juice to get the most concentrated nutrients.
Step 13: Bell peppers:
Bell peppers are good for bones because they are rich in Vitamins C and A, plus some Vitamin K. They are great for diets as they are low in calories and provide Vitamin B and fiber.
Step 14: Brussels sprouts:
Brussels sprouts contain calcium, magnesium, and Vitamins A, C, and K. You can use them instead of cabbage in salads.
Step 15: Walnuts:
Walnuts contain calcium, magnesium, and protein. Use them as a daily snack. Store them in the refrigerator or freezer to preserve the healthy fats in the nuts.
Step 16: Yogurt:
Yogurt is high in calcium and protein. One cup of yogurt has about 450mg of calcium and over 12g of protein.
Step 17: Asparagus:
Asparagus contains most of the nutrients good for bones while being low in calories; 1 cup of cooked asparagus contains only about 40 calories.
Step 18: Artichokes:
Artichokes contain a large amount of magnesium and are rich in Vitamin C. They are high in fiber and low in calories, perfect for dieting.

mon_an.ten: 3 simple and effective ways to clean a microwave
mon_an.mo_ta: Without needing too much water or soap, just a lemon, a bit of vinegar, or a little dish soap will make your microwave sparkle in 5 minutes and leave your kitchen smelling fresh. An old, smelly microwave will become shiny and fragrant, helping your food taste better without unpleasant odors. Try these 3 methods immediately to save time and effort. Good luck with your clean, fresh microwave!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Method 3 - Using dish soap and baking soda
cac_buoc: Method 1: Using lemon
Steps to clean the microwave with lemon:
Step 1: Wipe away any food crumbs or debris inside the microwave.
Step 2: Slice the lemon thinly. Fill a bowl about 3/4 full with water, add the lemon slices, and squeeze in a bit of lemon juice.
Step 3: Place the bowl in the microwave. Set the power to High and the time for 3-5 minutes, checking frequently until the water boils.
Step 4: Once the water boils, turn off the microwave and let the steam fill the interior for 1-2 minutes. Open the door, remove the bowl, and wipe the microwave clean with a towel.

Step 5: Remove the glass turntable to wash it, and wipe the inside of the microwave with a cloth. Even the most stubborn stains will come off easily. Your microwave will be as clean as new in just 5 minutes.
Method 2: Using vinegar
Steps to clean the microwave with vinegar:
Step 1: Take half a bowl of warm water, add 1-2 tbsp of vinegar and 1-2 drops of lemon essential oil. The oil is optional but helps neutralize the vinegar smell.

Step 2: Place the vinegar bowl in the microwave and run it for about 5 minutes. If the microwave is very dirty, let it sit for 2-3 minutes after it stops so the steam can spread and soften the grime; the vinegar will deodorize the food smells.
Step 3: After a few minutes, use an oven mitt to remove the bowl and wipe the interior gently with a sponge. Stains will be easily "defeated," and food odors will be gone.
Method 3: Using dish soap and baking soda
Steps to clean the microwave with dish soap and baking soda:
Step 1: Add a little dish soap and baking soda to a bowl of warm water. Like lemon oil, baking soda is very effective at deodorizing the microwave.
Step 2: Place the soapy water bowl inside and run for 2-3 minutes or until the water starts to steam.
Step 3: Remove the bowl and wipe the interior with a sponge. The steam makes the stains very easy to wipe away. Your microwave will quickly be clean and fresh.

Without needing too much water or soap, just a lemon, a bit of vinegar, or a little dish soap will make your microwave sparkle in 5 minutes and leave your kitchen smelling fresh. An old, smelly microwave will become shiny and fragrant, helping your food taste better without unpleasant odors. Try these 3 methods immediately to save time and effort. Good luck with your clean, fresh microwave!

mon_an.ten: 4 ways to cook delicious golden chicken without water
mon_an.mo_ta: Usually, chicken is boiled in water and then soaked in cold water to prevent the skin from cracking. However, today I will introduce 4 ways to cook delicious chicken without any water at all. This will surely result in a more flavorful and savory chicken dish. Let's take a look!
cac_buoc: Method 1:
Ingredients:
1 chicken
Rock salt
Thick-bottomed pot
Execution:
The chicken can be left whole, halved, or chopped into pieces as desired.
Wash the chicken and pat dry; you don't necessarily need to season it.
Before placing the chicken in the pot, spread a thick layer of rock salt on the bottom to prevent the skin from sticking and to allow the heat from the salt to make the chicken fragrant.

Stuff some salt into the chicken cavity. Place the chicken in the pot, cover tightly, and cook over low heat for 40-50 minutes or until cooked through. (You can use a regular pot on the stove or a rice cooker, but the lid must be airtight to retain heat and steam.)
Do not open the lid frequently during the process. Only check when you start to smell a strong aroma. Chopping the chicken into smaller pieces is recommended for faster cooking.
Method 2:
Preparation:
Garlic
Peel the garlic and scatter it evenly across the bottom of the pot so the chicken does not touch the pot surface.

Stuff the remaining garlic into the chicken cavity, cover, and cook over medium heat for 20 minutes. Do not open the lid while cooking. Once cooked, the chicken will not smell like garlic and will be very sweet.
Method 3:
Lime leaves
Lemongrass stalks
Green bird's eye chilies
Rock salt + fine salt
How to make:
This method is similar to salt-steaming, but the lime leaves, lemongrass, and chilies provide an incredible aroma and tender, sweet meat.
Wash the chicken and leave it whole. Grind the fine salt with a little MSG and the green chilies (green chilies are mandatory for the best aroma). Rub this chili salt all over the chicken.

Using a thick-bottomed pot, layer rock salt on the bottom, followed by crushed and sectioned lemongrass, then lime leaves. Place the chicken on top and cover with another layer of lime leaves. Steam for about 60 minutes. Use a glass lid to monitor easily. Do not open the lid for at least the first 30 minutes to avoid losing heat.
Method 4:
1 large ginger root
1 cup of white wine
Spatchcock the chicken and place it skin-side up (or down) in the pot.
Crush some ginger and pour 1 cup of white wine over the chicken.
Cook over low heat for about 25 minutes.
The chicken will be tender, very fragrant, and sweet.

mon_an.mo_ta: 5 Secrets to Delicious Grilled Meat – Everyone likely knows at least one recipe for marinating grilled meat to make it flavorful. We will introduce you to 5 secrets to make your grilled dishes even better. These tips will suggest 5 secrets for delicious grilled meat.
cac_buoc: Every family has its own secret for marinating meat to be fragrant and tender. However, there are small tips that many people overlook or don't know, which can result in grilled meat skewers that aren't quite perfect. Here are the secrets we recommend:

1. If you want the meat to be fragrant and tender and you are not in a hurry, marinate the meat overnight. Whether grilled or pan-fried the next day, it will be incredibly tender and aromatic. If you have plenty of time, keep it in the refrigerator until the next day. Marinating for this long allows the flavors to fully develop.
2. Sometimes, instead of using fruit juice, I crack an egg into the meat mixture. This method also makes the meat significantly more fragrant and tender when eaten.

3. You can marinate the meat with fruit juices, such as pear, apple, or orange... the sweetness of the meat will become natural and fragrant. In addition to other necessary spices, you should squeeze the juice of one king orange and gently massage it into the meat. The grilled meat will not be dry or tough; adding orange juice ensures it stays very soft.

4. If you don't like grilling pork belly, you can choose pork shoulder for a bit of fat marbling. This cut is better for grilling because it is tender without being too fatty or too lean, which is one of the 5 secrets to delicious grilled meat.
5. Additionally, when marinating, add a little condensed milk. This makes the meat tender and fragrant without burning easily. Not to mention, the meat will be sweeter and have a richer flavor.

mon_an.ten: 6 Taboos When Eating Tomatoes You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Tomatoes are known as a fruit with many benefits and effects that are extremely good for health and women's beauty. Tomatoes contain many vitamins, minerals, antioxidants, and are especially rich in lycopene – the substance that gives this fruit its deep red color and is a beneficial nutrient that helps your skin stay healthy and slows down the aging process. However, using tomatoes incorrectly can be harmful to your health or even life-threatening. This guide will provide you with things you need to know about tomatoes to prevent unfortunate consequences.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Do not eat green tomatoes

Green tomatoes contain solanine, a substance that scientists have found to be very toxic. Eating green tomatoes can cause poisoning symptoms such as dizziness, nausea, fatigue, and many other dangerous symptoms. Without timely treatment, it can be life-threatening. In ripe tomatoes, the amount of solanine disappears, so you should absolutely never eat tomatoes while they are still green.
Step 2: Do not eat tomatoes on an empty stomach

Tomatoes contain a lot of pectin and phenolic resin. When eaten on an empty stomach, these substances easily react with acid and harm the stomach. This causes symptoms such as abdominal pain, vomiting, and can even be life-threatening. Therefore, absolutely do not eat tomatoes when you are hungry.
Step 3: Do not overcook tomatoes
If you cook tomatoes at high temperatures for too long or reheat them many times, it will destroy the vitamins and reduce the nutritional value found in the tomatoes.
Step 4: Do not eat raw tomatoes with cucumbers

Tomatoes are a fruit and plant food rich in vitamins; every 100g of tomatoes contains 550mg of carotene, thiamin, 0.03mg of riboflavin, 10.6mg of niacin, 19mg of vitamin C, 0.57mg of vitamin E, and 92mg of vitamin A. Cucumbers contain vitamin C-decomposing enzymes, which can damage the tomatoes and reduce other nutrients. Therefore, you should not eat cucumbers and raw tomatoes at the same time.
Step 5: Do not eat tomatoes while taking anticoagulants

Tomatoes contain a lot of vitamin K. The main function of vitamin K is to catalyze the synthesis of prothrombin and coagulin in the liver. Therefore, if you eat tomatoes while taking anticoagulant medication, it will affect the effectiveness of these drugs.
Step 6: Do not eat tomatoes before a meal

Eating tomatoes before a meal can increase stomach acid, causing heartburn, abdominal pain, and other discomforts. Therefore, you should eat tomatoes after a meal because the stomach acid has already mixed with food, reducing the acid concentration and helping you avoid these symptoms.
Wishing you the best in using tomatoes correctly.

mon_an.ten: 6 Dishes to Effectively Prevent High Blood Pressure
mon_an.mo_ta: High blood pressure or hypertension is a condition that can lead to many severe neurological complications such as vegetative coma, hemiplegia, heart failure, and myocardial ischemia, affecting quality of life and, most severely, causing death. Below are 9 dishes that can help you prevent this dangerous high blood pressure. 6 Dishes to effectively prevent high blood pressure.
cac_buoc: High blood pressure can be prevented and well-controlled if you have a healthy lifestyle and a proper, balanced nutritional diet. This is true even for cases with a genetic risk. Here are 9 delicious dish suggestions to help you effectively prevent high blood pressure.
Step 1: Mixed Mushrooms
Ingredients:
30g straw mushrooms, 20g shiitake mushrooms, 50g wood ear mushrooms
50g water chestnuts, 100g carrots, 30g cucumber, 50g tofu skin, 500ml chicken stock
Method:

Wash the straw mushrooms and shiitake mushrooms. Slice the water chestnuts, bamboo shoots, carrots, and cucumber into bite-sized pieces. Soak the tofu skin and cut into segments. Soak the wood ear mushrooms in water until they expand, then wash and shred into thick strips.

Pour the chicken stock into a pot, add all ingredients, and bring to a boil. Lower the heat to a simmer. Once the mushrooms have absorbed the flavors, season to taste, add green onions and a little sesame oil, and serve immediately.
Step 2: Garlic Soaked in Vinegar
500g fresh garlic
500g brown sugar, 500ml rice vinegar

Peel the outer layers of the garlic and place them in a glass jar. Spread a layer of brown sugar over each layer of garlic, then pour in the rice vinegar. Close the lid and shake the jar; shake it 1-2 times every day. After soaking for 10 days, you can take out 6-7 cloves daily to chew.
Step 3: Winter Melon Stew with Straw Mushrooms
500g winter melon, 100g straw mushrooms
Herbs, broth

Wash the winter melon and slice into bite-sized pieces. Add a little cooking oil to a hot pan and lightly sauté the melon. Next, add the straw mushrooms and broth, and cook until the winter melon is soft. Season to taste, transfer to a bowl, and garnish with herbs.
Step 4: Bitter Melon Salad
250g bitter melon, seeds removed
Green onions, ginger, sugar

Boil the bitter melon for 3 minutes, then shred it into small strips. Mix with minced ginger, minced green onions, salt, sugar, sesame oil, soy sauce, and seasoning powder. Wait for the flavors to absorb and serve immediately.
Step 5: He Shou Wu Porridge
30g roasted He Shou Wu powder
100g rice, 5 jujubes

Cook the rice until it is almost porridge, then add the He Shou Wu powder and jujubes. Continue to simmer over low heat for about 40 minutes before turning off the heat. You should eat He Shou Wu porridge once a day.
Step 6: Brown Rice and Hawthorn Porridge
100g brown rice
10g hawthorn, 15g codonopsis
Cook the brown rice into porridge, add the hawthorn and codonopsis, then simmer for 5 minutes before scooping into a bowl to eat. Brown rice and hawthorn porridge should be eaten in the morning.

In addition to the 6 suggestions above, you can also cook simple dishes that families often eat, such as beef stir-fried with onions, sautéed onions, boiled tomato juice, or boiled celery and apple juice.
Some ways to help you effectively prevent high blood pressure:
Eat healthily: This helps stabilize blood pressure and supports effective treatment. Limit salt intake, increase foods high in potassium, and eat heart-healthy foods.
Exercise daily: Spend 30–45 minutes every day on gentle exercises such as walking, swimming, cycling, yoga, etc.
Maintain and control a healthy body weight.
Give up the habit of drinking alcohol.
Use OB Fresh Lotus Leaf Extract, made 100% from selected lotus leaves, to help stabilize blood pressure and effectively prevent hypertension. Or you can view the benefits of lotus leaves here.

mon_an.ten: How to Choose and Prepare Beef Correctly
mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know how to choose and prepare beef correctly? Let us reveal the secrets to you. Do you know how to choose and prepare beef correctly? Refer to the following tips to always have the perfect beef dish.
cac_buoc: How to choose and prepare beef correctly to remove the gamey odor

For many people, beef has a gamey smell that is hard to eat. To completely remove this odor, place the beef in a pot of cold water and heat it up (note: do not let it boil). At this point, the surface of the beef will heat up and coagulate, removing much of the gamey smell. However, this method should not be applied to stir-fry or grilled dishes; it is only for boiled or stewed dishes where the meat is cut into large pieces.
Tips for tender, non-chewy beef

For stir-fry dishes, after marinating with spices, add 2-3 tsp of cooking oil and marinate for about 20-30 minutes. The effect of the oil is to make the beef tender, fragrant, and shiny. When stir-frying, use very high heat and stir-fry very quickly; remove from the heat as soon as it is just cooked.

For grilled or stewed beef dishes, when marinating, add a little pineapple juice and leave for 5-10 minutes; the beef will be tender and delicious. Additionally, during the cooking process, you can add a little beer; the beef will be more fragrant, tender, and flavorful than usual.
*How to choose and prepare beef correctly* How to choose delicious beef

Beef and buffalo meat are sometimes sold mixed together. The tip for choosing beef is to observe the color; buffalo meat is usually darker than beef, and buffalo fat is white while beef fat is yellow. Buffalo meat fibers are larger and coarser than beef fibers.

Furthermore, there is currently a situation where pork and beef are mixed, usually old pork (because old meat is redder than young pork). Therefore, at a glance, many people are easily fooled. But usually, no matter how red pork is, it cannot compare to beef. Beef has a strong scent; just touch it and smell it to feel the gamey aroma. If you suspect pork is mixed in, press your finger into the meat, flip it over to examine closely, and then try to smell it. The best way is still not to choose meat that is not fresh in color, slightly pale, or dull.

mon_an.ten: How to Store Spices Properly: A Handy Guide
cac_buoc: If not stored correctly, spices can quickly lose their flavor or become damp. These handy tips will help you store your spices the right way. Let's take a look!
1. Salt
Hot weather can easily cause salt to become damp or clumpy. To fix this, simply place a piece of absorbent paper at the bottom of the salt jar. This absorbs moisture and keeps the salt dry.
2. Peppercorns

For dried peppercorns and white peppercorns: To maintain their original aroma and spiciness, store them in a cool, dry place in a sealed glass jar. They can last for 2-3 years. Ground pepper should also be kept in an airtight glass jar. Once ground, pepper only retains its best flavor for a few months and loses its aroma over time, so it's best to grind only a small amount as needed.

For fresh peppercorns: Since green peppercorns are not fully mature, they should be used immediately after harvesting or kept refrigerated for a short time to prevent dehydration and loss of nutrients.
3. Shallots and Garlic

For dried shallots and garlic: Store them in mesh bags, paper bags, or baskets to allow for ventilation. If kept in sealed bags or plastic containers, they are prone to rotting and mold. The storage area must be dry and cool. Avoid damp places as they can cause sprouting. Regularly check the bags or baskets to remove any bulbs that show signs of rot, softness, or discoloration to prevent mold from spreading.

For fresh shallots and garlic: You can wrap them in fresh vegetable leaves like cabbage or banana leaves and keep them in a cool, shaded spot. This keeps them fresh for several days, or longer in cold weather.
4. Chili Peppers

For dried chilies and chili powder: Store them in airtight glass jars in a cool, well-ventilated place away from direct sunlight. Humidity, temperature, and light can cause chili to quickly lose its characteristic flavor.

For fresh chilies: To prevent them from spoiling or drying out in the fridge, wash them after harvesting or buying, drain well, and place them in a zip-lock bag in the refrigerator crisper. They will stay fresh for a long time. Alternatively, after washing and drying thoroughly, remove the stems and pickle them in a mixture of vinegar, garlic, and a little sugar. Ensure the chilies are completely dry before pickling to prevent film from forming on the vinegar mixture.
5. Vinegar

Besides glass, certain types of plastic can be used to store vinegar, such as polyethylene (preferably white) and PET plastic. PVC plastic should only be used for neutral and dry foods like water pipes, tobacco, coffee, or tea containers. Therefore, choosing the right container material is crucial for storing vinegar properly.
We hope these 5 tips prove useful in helping you store your spices effectively.

mon_an.ten: How to Properly Maintain Your Cutting Boards
mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know how to properly maintain your cutting boards? Let us share some useful tips! Cutting boards are essential for prepping ingredients. A clean, high-quality board makes preparation easier and more efficient.
cac_buoc: Proper Maintenance: Wooden Cutting Boards
Wooden boards have the ideal weight for chopping and hacking. However, they are prone to mold, odors, cracking, and rotting. Keep these points in mind when using wooden boards:
When first purchased, soak the board in a brine solution (200g salt per 1 liter of water) for 24 hours, then let it dry. This prevents the board from cracking during use.

To prevent the board from shedding fibers or developing unpleasant odors, avoid chemical cleaners. Instead, use natural cleaners like lemon, salt, white vinegar, or boiling water to scrub the surface, then dry in a well-ventilated area. This prevents mold, odors, and deterioration.
Clean wooden boards regularly, as they can harbor thousands of bacteria that are harmful to health.
Proper Maintenance: Plastic Cutting Boards
Plastic boards are lightweight and don't have the same drawbacks as wood, making them ideal for slicing cooked foods or vegetables. Note the following when using plastic boards:
Avoid pressing the knife too hard, which creates deep grooves where bacteria can live and makes the board look old quickly.

If the board becomes stained or discolored, soak it in vinegar or lemon juice for two hours. Then, wash with dish soap and rinse with boiling water to clean and refresh the board, extending its lifespan.
Regularly clean the board with natural agents like lemon, white vinegar, or salt to keep the surface clean.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Preserving Fresh Fish, Shrimp, and Crab
mon_an.mo_ta: Here are some very useful tips and secrets for preserving fresh fish, live crabs, and fresh shrimp: 1. Tips for keeping fish fresh without a refrigerator
cac_buoc: For freshly bought fish, you can pour a few drops of white wine into its mouth, place it in a cool, dark spot, and cover it with a fine-mesh basket. Even in summer, the freshness of the fish will be maintained.
Place a small amount of mustard powder on a small plate and put it in a sealed container with the fresh fish. Keep it in a room with a moderate temperature; it can last for 4-5 days without spoiling.

If you have fresh fish but aren't cooking it immediately, gut it completely but do not scale it or wash it with water. Submerge the fish in a bowl of salt water (made with boiled and cooled water) for one day, then remove and drain. Next, rub a little rapeseed oil on the body of the fish and hang it to air dry until needed.
2. Preserving fresh fish in the refrigerator

Spoilage in fish always starts from the guts and the gills. Therefore, immediately after buying fish, scale it, remove the gills and guts, wash it thoroughly, and wrap it in a plastic or cloth bag. If you won't use it for a while, store it in the freezer; if you plan to use it soon, keep it in the chiller. A plastic bag is best as it prevents moisture loss, keeps the fish fresh, and prevents the fishy smell from contaminating other foods.
3. How to prevent fish from drying out when chilled
When stored in the refrigerator, fish often becomes too dry. To prevent this, chill the fish in a light brine solution.
4. How to preserve live crabs in the refrigerator

What should you do if you buy live crabs and can't eat them all at once? You can use the refrigerator. First, pull out the bottom drawer of the fridge and place the live crabs inside freely. Then, sprinkle a little food that crabs like (such as black sesame seeds). With this method, you can keep crabs alive for 3-5 days.
5. How to preserve shrimp

Wash the shrimp in water, drain, and place them in a pot. Add an adequate amount of salt and stir-fry until cooked. Then, spread them out in a basket, rinse off the surface salt with water, and sun-dry them. With this method, shrimp can be preserved for a long time without spoiling.

mon_an.mo_ta: Improve your cooking with these 12 useful food preparation tips: 1. Peeling lemons
cac_buoc: Place the lemon between your palms and roll it firmly for a few minutes; this softens the peel, making it much easier to remove.
2. Peeling oranges

The most delicious and hygienic way to eat an orange is to slice it vertically into long wedges and peel as you eat. If you soak the orange in boiling water for a few minutes (not too long) before removing it, the peel will come off much more easily.
3. Peeling garlic
Separate the garlic cloves and soak them in boiling water for a few minutes; they will be much easier to peel.
4. Removing slime from fish
To clean the slime off fresh fish, add a few drops of vegetable oil to the basin of water while cleaning the fish.
5. How to scale fish
To scale fish easily, use a soft brush dipped in vinegar or rub vinegar by hand onto the body of the fish before scaling.
6. How to soak mud out of snails, clams, and mussels
Soak them in water for at least 2 hours, and remember to drop a vegetable cleaver into the water while soaking.
7. How to remove impurities from meat
Use warm rice water to wash the meat; the impurities will come off easily.
8. How to clean pork stomach

Wash it twice with cold water, then place it in a pot of boiling water briefly. Turn it over and back; as soon as the water is about to boil again, remove it and scrape off all the impurities from both sides of the stomach.
9. How to wash off chemical residues from fresh vegetables

After cleaning the vegetables, place them in a basin of clean water and add an appropriate amount of sodium carbonate based on the quantity of vegetables. After soaking for 5 minutes, remove the vegetables and rinse them several times with clean water. This will remove chemical residues.
10. How to remove insects from vegetables

Dissolve a little salt in the washing water. Soaking for a while will irritate the insects, causing them to release their grip and float to the surface, where you can scoop them out. After soaking for a few minutes, remove the vegetables and rinse them several times with clean water.
11. How to remove the stale smell from pork

Pork left for too long will develop an unpleasant stale smell; if left too long, it will spoil. When cooking this type of meat, add a few strands of straw while the meat is still raw. Once finished cooking, add a few drops of white wine. This will eliminate the stale odor, and your meat will be fragrant and delicious again.
12. How to remove the gamey smell from duck and goose
To remove the gamey smell from duck or goose, remove the oil gland (tail) during preparation. For the best flavor, do not just stew or braise; boil the meat with salt or stir-fry it.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cucumbers can be prepared into many delicious dishes such as salads, Vietnamese slaws, kimchi, pickles, or quick-pickled slices... even just eating them raw with chili salt is wonderful. By spending just a little time to learn these tips, you can select the freshest cucumbers to ensure delicious meals for your family.
cac_buoc: Causes of bitter cucumbers
Over-fertilizing with nitrogen causes the plant to grow too long, making the fruit on the branches or weak stems prone to bitterness.
Lack of sunlight and low temperatures during growth cause the plant to absorb water and nutrients poorly, leading to the accumulation of bitter substances.
The plant suffers from water deficiency or prolonged drought.
Storage temperatures are too high or there is a lack of humidity.
How to choose fresh cucumbers
Regarding color, you should choose fruits with a bright green color. Good cucumbers are usually quite even in color, without bruises or yellow spots.
Regarding shape, you should choose straight fruits with little to no curvature.
Long, slender cucumbers of uniform size are usually dense; they will be crunchier and tastier than short, round ones.
Note that you should choose fruits that feel heavy in the hand, are firm but slightly yielding, and have a smooth skin without bumps.
Furthermore, small cucumbers tend to be sweeter than large ones.
Avoid buying cucumbers that bulge in the middle or have a large head and small tail (and vice versa), as these are old cucumbers with many seeds and high water content, which are not tasty.
Cucumbers with yellow spots on the body indicate they have been sitting for a long time and are starting to spoil. These will not taste good and may be bitter.

Sometimes when buying, you may see a thin layer of white powder on the cucumber; this powder helps retain water and keeps them fresh and crisp. If you choose these, wash them thoroughly with water mixed with lemon, vinegar, or hot water.

If the skin is thin and has no powder, you can slice and use them immediately after washing. However, before slicing or processing, you should taste a bit; if it is bitter, you need to peel the skin to remove the bitterness. Small cucumbers are generally less bitter than large ones.

Cucumbers are processed into many delicious dishes like salads, slaws, kimchi, pickles, or quick-pickled slices... even just dipped in chili salt raw is very good. Moreover, cucumbers are very healthy. Eating them not only keeps you hydrated but is also great for weight loss as they are low in calories and help you feel full. Additionally, cucumbers help women achieve beautiful skin and are a top choice for face masks to help the skin stay firm, clean, and rosy!
Whole cucumbers can be stored in a plastic bag in the refrigerator crisper drawer for about 10 days without affecting the quality.
Spending just a little time to learn these tips will help you choose fresh cucumbers for delicious family meals.

mon_an.ten: Fruit Selection Secrets for Home Cooks
mon_an.mo_ta: It has become a habit after every meal for Vietnamese families to choose delicious fruits for dessert or to treat guests. Below are a few small suggestions and secrets for choosing delicious fruit.
cac_buoc: Tips for choosing watermelon

Choose watermelons with a veiny, hard rind that feels heavy for its size. When tapped, it should produce a dull thud; this indicates a good melon. If the watermelon is large but light, it is likely hollow inside because it is overripe.

Additionally, pay attention to the stem. For red-fleshed watermelons, the stem will be curled; if the stem is straight, the flesh is likely not as red. However, the white rind of the watermelon has higher nutritional value than the flesh. You can use this white part for many recipes.
Tips for choosing mangosteen

Mangosteen is grown mostly in the South, so many people in the North or Central regions may not know how to pick the best ones. Choose medium-sized fruits with a dark brown color, no yellow sap spots on the outside, and a shell that is not too thick or hard. Buy them at the beginning of the season; end-of-season mangosteens are often not as good.

You should also notice the stem; if the stem is fresh and has a bit of powder around it, it is a tree-ripened fruit and will be delicious. If there are many sap marks and the shell is hard, it usually won't taste good.
Tips for choosing mangoes

For mangoes, look for those with firm, plump skin and a sweet aroma. Do not choose mangoes with black bruises or wrinkled skin, as these are overripe or have been kept too long, leading to mushiness or spoilage.
Mangoes with a yellow, firm top and a single "eye" at the bottom usually have small seeds. This is a great secret for choosing delicious fruit.
Tips for choosing grapes

Grapes are berries with high nutritional value and great anti-aging properties, so choosing a good, sweet cluster brings many benefits. Choose large clusters with plump, juicy grapes. A cluster with a thin layer of white powder on the skin is a sign of good grapes.
Avoid grapes with dry stems and wrinkled skin, as they have been stored for a long time and have lost their nutritional value.

mon_an.mo_ta: Jackfruit is a delicious fruit loved by many. There are many different types, each with its own unique flavor and texture, from crunchy jackfruit with thick flesh to honey jackfruit with a deep yellow color and cool sweetness. Besides eating it fresh, jackfruit is used in many popular dishes like jackfruit sweet soup, jackfruit yogurt, jackfruit sticky rice, and salads. Not everyone knows how to choose a ripe, delicious jackfruit. Today, we share the secrets to choosing delicious jackfruit, hoping to help you!
cac_buoc: Types of jackfruit: There are many types, but the most common are crunchy jackfruit (mít dai), honey jackfruit (mít mật), mushy jackfruit (mít nhão), and Tố Nữ jackfruit. Characteristics:
Crunchy jackfruit (mít dai): Thick, crunchy flesh, pale yellow, and usually very sweet.
Honey jackfruit (mít mật - also called "wet jackfruit"): Bright yellow, soft segments, slightly mushy, with a cool sweet taste.

Mushy jackfruit and Tố Nữ jackfruit: Usually smaller than honey or crunchy types, with a paler yellow color. When Tố Nữ jackfruit is ripe, the segments cling to the central core like a cluster of grapes, which looks very beautiful.
Tips for choosing jackfruit:
Based on shape: This is an easy step to observe. You should choose fruits that are even and have no indentations or hollow spots. Dented areas are prone to pests, hard flesh, or excessive fiber.

Check the spines: Good jackfruits have large, even spines. The spines should not be long or sharp, and the distance between them should be wide. These characteristics indicate a fruit with many segments and sweetness.

Based on the stem: Like many other fruits, you can tell by the stem. Specifically: Tố Nữ jackfruit should have a stem about 0.5 cm long, while Western jackfruit (mít tây) stems should be 1-1.5 cm long.
Check quality by sound: When you lift the jackfruit and it feels heavy, tap it lightly or flick the rind. If it makes a dull "thud" sound, it is a good jackfruit.

Check the firmness of the rind and the aroma: If the rind feels soft when pressed, it is ripe; a hard rind with stiff spines indicates a green fruit. Additionally, naturally ripened jackfruit always has a very attractive aroma, unlike those ripened with chemicals, which may have a yellow rind but remain very hard and have a strange or faint smell, or even a starchy taste.
A small note: if you are buying pre-peeled segments, choose bags with a deep golden yellow color.
Delicious dishes from jackfruit:
You can use the segments to make delicious, refreshing jackfruit yogurt, jackfruit smoothies, jackfruit sticky rice, or jackfruit sweet soup.
The jackfruit rags (xơ mít) can be pickled, while the seeds can be boiled, roasted, or stewed for a nutty, delicious treat.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Irresistible Thịt Kho Tàu
mon_an.mo_ta: This incredibly familiar dish seems easy to cook, but to get a truly authentic and delicious Thịt Kho Tàu, you need these secrets!
cac_buoc: A delicious Thịt Kho Tàu first has a glossy, beautiful reddish-brown color. The meat is fragrant and tender with a natural sweetness, and the sauce is thickened and rich—just looking at it is enough to make you crave it. However, during cooking, some may forget certain details, resulting in meat that isn't tender enough, a pale color, or a lack of natural sweetness.
Therefore, to have a perfect Thịt Kho Tàu, refer to these 5 secrets:
Making the caramel sauce (nước màu)

To create color for the meat, you can buy pre-made caramel sauce (nước hàng). Some people even use bitter candy. This is convenient, but the aroma often doesn't reach the perfection of homemade sauce.

Making your own caramel sauce is very simple. Just put sugar in a pan and heat until it bubbles and turns an amber color. Then add a moderate amount of water. Don't add too much water or the color will be too light. Also, be careful not to let the sugar burn black, or the sauce will be bitter and the meat won't have that beautiful reddish-brown hue.
Fresh coconut water

Many people have the habit of not using coconut water. The dish is still attractive, but the meat won't have the natural, special sweetness that coconut water provides as it seeps into every piece. Furthermore, coconut water creates a richness in the meat. Once you try it, you'll definitely use it every time.
Note: Choose a coconut that is neither too young nor too old.
Choosing the meat
For Thịt Kho Tàu, you need to select high-quality pork belly that is fresh and odorless. Do not choose purely lean cuts, as the meat will become dry and lack the necessary richness for this dish.
Marinating

Some marinate very elaborately with cinnamon, basil powder, five-spice, garlic, or lemongrass... but it depends on personal taste. The simplest seasonings for Thịt Kho Tàu are just a bit of salt, fish sauce, bouillon powder, black pepper, minced shallots, and chili (if you like heat). Sometimes too many spices can mask the original flavor of the meat.

After washing, cut the meat into uniform cubes. This ensures the meat stays tender and doesn't shrink too much. Marinate with the prepared seasonings for 15-20 minutes if you are short on time. If you have more time, marinate longer or wrap it and leave it in the fridge overnight for even better flavor.
Braising the meat

Place the marinated meat in a pot and stir-fry until the meat firms up, then add the caramel sauce. Add the coconut water and cover with a lid. Bring to a boil, then lower the heat (skim off any foam), and simmer gently until the meat is tender and the sauce has reduced and thickened. Do not use high heat throughout the process or the meat will burn.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Keeping Fish Fresh and Odor-Free
mon_an.mo_ta: This guide will show you simple yet extremely useful ways to preserve fish so it stays fresh longer without a fishy smell. With these simple secrets, you can have plenty of fish dishes without worrying about the odor!
cac_buoc: Preserving fish without a refrigerator

It can be difficult to keep fish fresh and odorless without a fridge, but you can use diluted vinegar poured over the body of the fish and keep it in a dry, airy place. This way, the fish can last until the next day without becoming fishy or smelly (provided it was fresh to begin with).
Keeping fish fresh longer

Use a piece of wet paper to cover the fish's eyes; this can keep the fish fresh for 3-5 hours. In the fish's optic nerve, there is a tissue system that breaks when the fish leaves the water, causing it to die quickly. Covering the eyes with wet paper delays this process, keeping the fish fresh longer.
Handling a broken gall bladder

When a gall bladder breaks, it makes the fish meat bitter and unpleasant. To fix this, apply some baking soda to the area affected by the bile, then rinse with clean water; the bitterness will disappear.
Preventing flies
Fresh or cooked fish always attracts flies. To prevent this, place a few slices of onion or raw onion stalks in the fish's mouth, and flies will stay away.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Keeping Grapes Fresh Longer
mon_an.mo_ta: Secrets for selecting and preserving fresh grapes – Grapes are delicious and healthy, but if you don't know how to store them, they won't last long or may spoil. Today, let's explore tips for choosing and preserving fresh grapes for a long time while maintaining their quality.
cac_buoc: Grapes are very good for health. To keep them for a long time, you first need to choose fresh ones. The way to choose fresh grapes is simple: pay attention to their color. Specifically, for green grapes, the skin should be a cool green with a layer of white powder on the outside; they should not be crushed, should be firmly attached to the stem, and should not smell sour.
Similarly, red grapes should maintain a dusty brown color, not be mushy, and feel firm to the touch.
Next, check the entire cluster for any mold or strange signs; if found, remove them immediately to avoid affecting the other clusters.
Another important note is that you should not wash grapes if you do not intend to eat them immediately. Washing removes the protective powder layer, causing the ripening process to happen faster.

To store grapes in the refrigerator, put them in a sealed plastic bag and keep them at a temperature of 30-32°F (equivalent to -1 to 0°C). Place the grapes toward the back of the fridge where the temperature is lower and air circulation is high. You can also use vacuum bags or containers to increase preservation efficiency.
Additionally, keep these small points in mind:
Do not stack grapes on top of each other as this causes them to spoil faster.
Avoid storing grapes near strong-smelling foods like onions or garlic. Grapes absorb odors easily, which can ruin their flavor.
When eating, wash the grapes thoroughly to remove bacteria and dirt.
Once taken out of the fridge, eat them as soon as possible. Ideally, consume them within 72 hours of removal. If left too long, they will wrinkle and shrink.
Above are some great tips for you. We hope this helps you preserve grapes and other foods better for your health. Good luck!

mon_an.mo_ta: Kimchi is a favorite dish for many families due to its sour, slightly spicy, and crunchy taste. Serving kimchi with boiled pork or using it in kimchi soup or hotpot provides a delicious experience.
cac_buoc: To make delicious napa cabbage kimchi, you need a few secrets and tips. Below are some techniques gathered to help you achieve authentic kimchi with a beautiful color.
How to choose napa cabbage

When buying, look for fresh, evenly sized cabbages weighing about 1.5 - 2kg each. The leaves should be thin and green. Thick leaves take longer to absorb the sauce and require more time for the salting and pressing process. If the leaves are too thick, the spices won't penetrate properly, making it less tasty.
Ingredients and seasonings
Common ingredients for the stuffing include carrots, radish, scallions, chives, ginger, garlic, 1 pear, glutinous rice flour, water, and sesame seeds.
Seasonings include Korean chili flakes (gochugaru), coarse sea salt, fine salt, sugar, high-quality fish sauce, and salted shrimp (saeu-jeot, available at Korean grocery stores).
Additionally, authentic Korean kimchi is quite spicy, so if following a Korean recipe, adjust the heat to suit your family's taste.
Salting
Rubbing salt into the cabbage is very important, as this step largely determines the crunchiness. When salting, rub more on the white stems and only a little on the thin green leaves.

Then place the cabbage in a clean basin, pour in a bucket of water so the cabbage is submerged in brine, and place a heavy wooden cutting board on top for about 5 hours until the cabbage is soft and pliable. Remove the cabbage and rinse with clean water 3 to 4 times to remove the saltiness. Drain in a colander before applying the seasoning paste. Note: if making a small amount, you only need to soak for about 2 hours.
Storage

Once finished, place the kimchi in airtight containers, glass jars, or tightly sealed bags. To speed up fermentation, leave it at room temperature for 1-2 days depending on the weather before moving it to the fridge, where it can be kept for a week.
After a week, the kimchi will start to sour and ferment; you can eat it fresh or use it for kimchi soup, kimchi hotpot, grilled meats, fried rice, or other dishes you enjoy.

mon_an.ten: Super Fast Fruit Peeling Hacks Everyone Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Most people love eating fruit not only for the vitamins and natural nutrients but also for its refreshing taste. However, some fruits are avoided because peeling them takes too much time. To help you comfortably choose any favorite fruit for your family, today we share super fast, time-saving fruit peeling secrets!
cac_buoc: 1. How to peel a pomelo
Pomelo is very healthy as it contains a lot of vitamin C and has a refreshing sweetness; it is also helpful for weight loss. Here is how to peel it in a flash.

Place the pomelo horizontally on a table. Use the tip of a knife to score a circle about 2 cm deep around the middle for thick-skinned varieties; for thinner-skinned ones like Diễn or Đoan Hùng pomelos, score a bit shallower. Use both hands to twist the two halves of the rind in opposite directions to separate them.
By peeling this way, you can place the segments back inside and close the two halves if you don't eat it all, keeping the fruit from drying out.
2. How to peel a pomegranate

To peel a pomegranate, do not cut it directly in half. Instead, cut off a bit of the skin at both ends, score thin lines around the fruit, and gently pull it apart along those lines. This way, the pomegranate won't lose its juice, and you won't have to struggle with the thin inner membranes.
3. Super fast orange peeling

There is a small tip to peel an orange quickly without cutting into the flesh. Cut off both ends of the orange, then use a knife to score a vertical line through the peel. Place your fingers into the scored area and gently pull the peel away. Then just separate the segments to enjoy.
4. How to peel a mango quickly without mashing it

You can peel ripe mango slices very quickly without mashing them or losing juice. Use a glass rim; take a slice of mango that has been cut away from the pit, press the bottom edge of the mango slice against the rim of the glass, and slide it down. The flesh will separate from the skin easily and instantly.
5. Fast and beautiful apple peeling

For apples, here is a suggestion to make peeling simple and visually appealing. Wash the apple, use a knife to score a diagonal line on the skin a few mm deep, remove the core, and slice the apple horizontally into even rounds. Peel off part of the skin divided by the diagonal line. Use the knife to score the remaining skin but leave 1cm attached to the flesh. The apple slices will have white flesh with beautiful pink skin accents.
6. Super fast pineapple peeling
Pineapple is loved by many but peeling it is difficult. Try this method:
Cut off the base of the pineapple, slice off the outer skin, quarter the pineapple vertically, use a knife to cut away the core, and then slice into bite-sized pieces.
We hope these small tips will be useful to you!

mon_an.mo_ta: A few meat-cooking secrets that will greatly help your kitchen work: When cooking beef or buffalo, you can add dry tea leaves to help the meat soften faster. When cooking goat, add some radish to remove the gamey smell. For pork, use low heat and add hawthorn to help it cook quickly and stay fresh and tender.
cac_buoc: When cooking meat, bring the water to a boil before adding the meat; this keeps the meat tender and retains more nutrients.
When starting to cook meat, use low heat and simmer slowly, adding more water after a while.

You can also put the meat and water in the pot at the same time, cook for a bit, then remove the meat and soak it in cold water until cooled before continuing to cook. This helps the meat soften faster.
When you start cooking meat, never add too much salt or soy sauce. This causes the meat fibers to tighten, making it tough and coarse when eaten.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Boiling White, Crispy Pork Intestines and Stomach
mon_an.mo_ta: To get white, fresh, and crunchy pieces of pork intestines and stomach, refer to the secrets shared below!
cac_buoc: Step 1: How to boil pork intestines to be delicious and crunchy
How to choose good intestines
Small intestines (lòng non) can often be bitter, so when buying, choose the front section with small vessels, a plump and round tube, pinkish-white color, and a milky white internal fluid.
Segments that are thin and flat with yellow fluid, or those with visible blood vessels, will be tough and bitter.
Cleaning the intestines
For small intestines, just rinse the inside briefly under a tap to remove the fluid, or pull through once. This keeps them plump after boiling.
Alternatively, use flour to clean them:

Turn the intestines inside out and remove the fatty membrane. Mix flour with a little salt and rub thoroughly, then rinse under clean water. Finally, rub with lemon to remove any remaining impurities.
Using this method, the intestines will be fragrant and have an appetizing white color after boiling.
Boiling the intestines
Prepare a bowl of cold water with a few drops of lemon juice.

Bring water to a vigorous boil before dropping the intestines in. This step is crucial. Many people put them in cold water and then boil, which makes them tough. Dropping them into boiling water ensures they are just cooked and crunchy.

Add a bit of ginger for fragrance. When the water returns to a boil and the intestines turn pink, leave for another 2-3 minutes then remove. Remember, the longer they boil, the tougher they get. Total time is usually 7-10 minutes.

Once cooked, immediately drop them into the bowl of ice water with lemon (some use alum or rice vinegar). Ensure they are fully submerged. The sudden cold and acidity make them white and crunchy. Once cooled, slice and serve. For extra safety, you can dip them back into boiled cooled water after the ice bath. Serve with Thai basil and ginger-chili-lemon fish sauce.
Step 2: How to boil pork stomach correctly
Choosing a good stomach
A stomach usually weighs 600-800 grams. Choose one that looks medium-sized but feels heavy and firm; it will be thicker than a large, light one.
Choose a stomach with an even white color, no bruises, no ulcers, and no bloating or gas.
How to clean the stomach

Method 1: Most common—use vinegar, lemon, or especially fermented rice (mẻ) to rub the stomach; it cleans well and removes odors. Turn inside out, rub the folds thoroughly, and use a knife to scrape off any residue. Rinse several times.
Method 2: Boil a pot of water with ginger and lemongrass, then blanch the stomach for a few seconds. Rinse immediately under cold water.

Method 3: Place the inverted stomach on a hot pan for a few seconds, then flip. You can drizzle a tablespoon of fish sauce over it. Immediately remove and rinse under cold water. This removes all slime and the fish sauce neutralizes the odor. Then rub with lemon.
How to boil the stomach
Method 1:
Place the cleaned stomach in a pot and cover with water. To make it more fragrant, add a tablespoon of salt, a crushed ginger root, a tablespoon of vinegar, and a little wine.
Cover and boil for about 20 minutes. Test with a chopstick; if it pierces through easily, it is tender. Immediately soak in cold water to keep it crunchy.
Method 2:
Bring water to a boil first, then drop the stomach in. Boil until the water just starts to bubble again, then remove and soak in cold water.
While soaking, keep the pot boiling. Put the stomach back in until it bubbles again, then remove and soak in cold water.
Repeat a third time, but use a fresh bowl of water with ice and a few drops of lemon. This ensures the stomach is very white and crunchy.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Cooking and Braising Fish
mon_an.mo_ta: Choosing the right time to cook fresh fish: When a fish has just been gutted and sliced, the protein has not yet had time to decompose into amino acids. Exposing it to heat immediately not only affects the freshness and flavor but also hinders the body's ability to absorb nutrients from the fish. Therefore, it is best to let the fish sit for 2-2.5 hours after gutting and slicing; this time can be shortened in hot weather and extended slightly in cold weather. This ensures the fish remains delicious, nutritious, and fresh when cooked.
cac_buoc: Secrets to cooking and braising fish
Sear the fish briefly before cooking. The oil should be at a normal temperature when searing.
Apply moderate heat when cooking; the water only needs to just cover the fish. After the water boils, reduce to low heat and simmer until it releases a rich, fragrant aroma.
While simmering over low heat, flip the fish gently to prevent it from sticking to the pot, or occasionally shake the pot lightly.
To remove the fishy odor, besides adding a bit of cooking wine, you can add an appropriate amount of vinegar to the pot.
If the fish is not very fresh, rub it with a little salt once, two hours before putting it in the pot. When cooking, you may not need to add more salt, just other seasonings.
Add 1 tbsp of milk to the pot when braising; this will both eliminate the fishy smell and make the fish whiter, softer, more delicious, and more nutritious.
You can fry fresh fish until cooked, simmer in water for 10 minutes, then add salt and cook for another 5-10 minutes before adding other seasonings; this keeps the fish very fresh and tasty.
Soak the fish in a mixture of water and vinegar before braising to make the cooked fish soft and sweet.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Frying Chicken Without Greasiness
mon_an.mo_ta: With these chicken frying secrets, you won't have to worry about the chicken absorbing too much oil, so it won't be greasy anymore!
cac_buoc: Ingredients to prepare:
Step 1:
Mince the garlic and cut the green onions into sections.
Step 2:
Cut the chicken thighs into bite-sized pieces.
Step 3:
Make the marinade by mixing the chili paste, rice vinegar, honey, minced garlic, salt, and pepper in a large bowl.
Step 4:
Add the chicken to the bowl and toss well to coat the meat with the seasonings. Marinate the chicken for 20 minutes.
Step 5:
Use parchment paper (the type used for lining cake molds) to wrap each piece of chicken with a few green onion sections into rolls. In this step, we wrap them just like spring rolls!
Step 6:
Deep-fry the chicken rolls over medium heat until the chicken is cooked through. Because they are wrapped in parchment paper, you can easily check the color of the chicken as it cooks.
It's just as good as oven-roasted honey chicken!
This method helps the chicken absorb the seasonings and prevents the meat from drying out, giving you chicken with crispy skin that is still juicy inside without being soaked in grease.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Cleaning and Preparing Meat
mon_an.mo_ta: A few secrets for cleaning, washing, and preparing meat 1. Removing slime from fish
cac_buoc: When preparing fish, add a few drops of vegetable oil to the basin of water.
2. Scaling fish
Use a soft brush dipped in vinegar or apply vinegar by hand to the fish's body; the scales will come off very easily.
3. Removing mud from snails, mussels, clams, and cockles
Place a kitchen knife in the soaking water with them for two hours or more.
4. Preparing eel

Rinse the eels with water, put them in a basin, and pour over a cup of medium-strength liquor; the eels will make a chirping sound. Once they are "drunk" and stop making noise, preparing them becomes a simple task.
5. Removing impurities from meat
If meat has impurities stuck to it, it is difficult to clean with plain water. It is best to use warm rice water for washing.
6. Cleaning pig stomach and intestines
Wash the stomach twice with cold water, then put it in a pot of boiling water briefly, flipping it over. Just before the water boils again, remove it and scrape off all impurities from both sides.

Wash the pig intestines repeatedly with cold water, then place in warm water, wait a few minutes and remove. Rinse once more with cold water, then place back into hot water. Repeat this two or three times until all impurities and odors are gone. Rinse with clean water, then rub with a mixture of vinegar, wine, ginger, and onion. Finally, put them in a pot to boil; once it reaches a boil, remove and rinse with clean water one last time.
You can drizzle a little peanut oil evenly over the pig intestines, then massage by hand and rinse clean with water.
You can also add 1-2 tbsp of salt, then rub and rinse clean. Salt can be combined with vinegar or alum.
7. Slaughtering a chicken

Usually, the neck is cut to let the blood drain, but blood often remains in the vessels and mucus from the esophagus can leak out, which is unhygienic. You should use sharp scissors to pierce inside the chicken's mouth to cut the blood vessel so the blood drains from the mouth. This way, the chicken dies quickly and the blood is drained cleanly.

The chicken meat is only delicious if it dies quickly and stops moving after the blood is drained. If the chicken continues to run after its throat is cut, the meat will not be tasty and will be tough.
8. Plucking chicken feathers
About 15-20 minutes before slaughtering, give the chicken a tablespoon of white wine or vinegar. After blanching in hot water, pluck the feathers against the grain; it will be both fast and clean.

Pour a little vinegar into the pot of hot water used for plucking. After draining the blood, submerge the chicken and flip it over to soak. Wait a few minutes before removing; the feathers will come off very easily.

Dissolve a little salt in the boiling water for plucking (25g salt / 1000g water), then put the slaughtered chicken in and soak for about 5-6 seconds before removing. Plucking against the grain will be fast and very clean.
*Note:* Prepare hot water at no more than 70-80°C to soak the chicken after the blood is drained. When plucking, do it slowly and steadily to avoid tearing the skin.
9. Plucking duck feathers
The chicken feather plucking method can be applied to ducks.

However, there is a difference: after the duck's blood is drained, soak it in cold water first, then put it in hot water at about 40°C. Continue heating to increase the temperature while flipping the duck evenly. When you feel the feathers can be pulled out easily, remove the duck and pluck against the grain from the feet up.
10. Cleaning chemical residues from fresh vegetables

After cleaning the vegetables, put them in a basin of clean water and add an amount of sodium carbonate corresponding to the amount of vegetables. Soak for 5 minutes, remove the vegetables, and rinse multiple times with clean water. This will clean the chemical residues from the vegetables.
11. Removing insects from vegetables

Dissolve a little salt in the vegetable washing water and soak for a while; the insects will feel the sting, release their grip, and float to the surface. After soaking for a few minutes, remove the vegetables and rinse multiple times with clean water.
12. Cleaning dirt and sand from mushrooms
For button mushrooms, dissolve a little salt in the washing water, stir well, and soak for a while. Then remove and rinse multiple times with cold water.
For shiitake mushrooms, the dirt sticks more firmly and is harder to clean. You need to soak these mushrooms in warm water for about an hour, then stir for about 10 minutes.

mon_an.mo_ta: High blood fat is a condition that causes atherosclerosis, leading to hypertension, stroke, cardiovascular diseases, gallstones, or diabetes. Lipids (fat) themselves are not a toxic substance, and high concentrations in the blood do not directly poison the human body. Cholesterol is not a harmful substance; it plays a role in producing new cells and hormones in the body; additionally, it acts as a protective layer for nerve cells. Cholesterol is a very necessary and indispensable substance for the human body; it only has a very negative impact when excess concentrations are too high and the composition is disordered: an increase in very low-density lipoprotein (LDL-c) and a decrease in high-density lipoprotein (HDL-c).
cac_buoc: Complications of high blood fat include causing atherosclerosis which increases the patient's blood pressure, stroke, cardiovascular diseases, gallstones, and diabetes. The process of atherosclerosis occurs gradually over many years, and the arteries usually affected are: the thoracic aorta, abdominal aorta, and coronary arteries...
The factors causing complications of blood fat disease are: an increase in low-density lipoprotein (LDL-c).

The low-density LDL group mainly carries apoprotein B; this is the form in which cholesterol is carried to all cells. When there is too much LDL, more cholesterol is deposited into the arterial membranes, gradually narrowing the diameter of the vessels. Later, it combines with other substances in the arterial wall membrane to form plaques (atherosclerosis). These plaques can crack and make the arterial wall no longer smooth, making it easy for blood clots to form. Atherosclerotic plaques develop in many layers and overlap, which can block the arteries. If this occurs in the coronary arteries, the result will be a blockage of the heart vessels, causing a myocardial infarction (heart attack).

In cases where a blood clot breaks off from the arterial wall and flows with the bloodstream until it gets stuck in a vessel with a smaller diameter, it blocks that vessel. If it is a vessel supplying blood to the brain, the result is a stroke. Additionally, if the triglyceride index is high and the HDL-c index (high-density type) is low, it will significantly increase the dangerous harmfulness of LDL-c.
Thus:
Increased LDL-cholesterol (LDL-c) is one of the main causes of atherosclerosis leading to vessel blockage and is one of the essential factors causing complications of blood fat disease.

Additionally, there is another factor: Lipoprotein (a) is a substance similar to LDL-c but has a special apoprotein attached. This is a hereditary condition passed from generation to generation, cannot be treated by changing diet or exercising, and there is no effective medication for treatment yet.

mon_an.ten: Essential Tips for Fixing Common Mistakes When Making Mứt Dừa
