mon_an.mo_ta: Mứt dừa is a familiar Tet treat for every Vietnamese family, but some people still encounter mistakes when cooking the jam. Check out these timely rescue methods to make your mứt dừa turn out perfectly!
cac_buoc: Many people still believe that mứt dừa is one of the simplest and easiest jams to make because it only requires washing, soaking in sugar, and cooking. However, many still end up frustrated because no matter how they cook it, the sugar won't crystallize, and the mứt dừa stays sticky and gooey without them knowing why... This often results in having to discard an entire batch after the hard work of hand-shredding the coconut.
Therefore, you can refer to the information below to know how to fix errors when cooking mứt dừa:
Step 1: The sugar fails to crystallize
According to experienced home cooks, the reason mứt dừa fails to crystallize is a lack of sugar.

Normally, when making mứt dừa, the ratio is 500-600g of sugar to 1kg of coconut flesh. If the sugar is less than this ratio, the mứt dừa is very difficult to crystallize. If the jam doesn't crystallize due to a lack of sugar, pour in more sugar and continue cooking.
Step 2: The sugar burns and turns into caramel

This happens because during the cooking process, many people use heat that is too high, causing the sugar to burn and turn into a syrup that cannot crystallize. Therefore, when cooking, use very low heat; you must be patient and not rush.
If the sugar keeps turning into syrup and won't crystallize after long cooking, wash off all the old sugar, add the correct ratio as mentioned above, and cook over very low heat.
Step 3: The jam is dry and hard

If the sugar has already crystallized during cooking but you continue to toss and heat it, the mứt dừa will become dry, hard, and unpleasant to eat. The best way is to cook until it feels heavy in the hand and the sugar begins to crystallize, then remove the pan from the stove and toss continuously off the heat until it fully crystallizes, rather than tossing it over the flame.
Step 4: The jam becomes watery

To avoid the situation where young mứt dừa becomes wet the next day, you should air-dry the jam in front of a fan after removing it from the pan. You can also sun-dry it or put it in an oven at 100°C for 15 minutes to dry it completely, then repeat the step of wearing gloves and tossing the jam in front of a fan until fully dry, and continue fanning for about 2-3 hours.
Another way is to put the wet coconut back into the pan and cook it again; the mứt dừa will become drier. Then put it in a bag and tie it tightly.
Since young coconut has a higher water content than mature coconut, you should soak it in sugar a bit longer so the young coconut releases more water, making it drier when cooked.

If you follow the above steps and it is still watery, put the coconut back on the stove at the lowest temperature and cook for a while longer, then toss and air-dry in front of a fan for several more hours before packaging.

mon_an.ten: Essential Foods for Winter Skin Hydration
mon_an.mo_ta: Hydrating foods such as fish, oranges, oats, eggs, and carrots help keep the skin smooth, prevent dryness, and ensure a glowing, radiant complexion throughout the winter. Simply incorporating these into your daily diet will help you achieve the skin you desire.
cac_buoc: Filtered water

In the cold, dry winter weather, many people tend to drink less water. However, your skin actually needs more hydration during these dry days. Increase your water intake to help the skin maintain essential moisture and avoid roughness or cracking. Furthermore, water helps the body flush out toxins, which are a primary cause of skin dullness. Drinking 2 liters of water daily will maintain necessary skin moisture, promote a beautiful complexion, and support a fit physique.
Carrots

Did you know that the carotene and lycopene in carrots act as antioxidants, protecting the skin from sunlight and environmental damage? The Vitamin A and Vitamin C in carrots are excellent for healing damaged epidermal tissue and boosting collagen production to rejuvenate your skin. Additionally, eating carrots provides essential fiber and promotes soft, healthy skin.
Eggs

Applying an egg mask this winter can also provide better protection for your skin. Eggs are rich in protein, particularly those that help regenerate skin, along with lutein which hydrates and improves elasticity. However, many people are hesitant to use this mask due to the fishy smell. To eliminate the odor, wash your face with warm water to remove impurities and reduce the scent. After washing, immediately apply toner or moisturizer to help the skin absorb nutrients more effectively.
Oats

The abundant nutrients in oats help protect the skin from environmental impacts. Adding oats to your diet is an effective way to hydrate the skin and keep it moist during winter. You can prepare oats in various ways, such as making porridge, eating them for breakfast, or baking oat cakes.
Fish

Omega-3 fatty acids found in fish help maintain the water content of cell membranes, keeping the skin hydrated. Tuna and salmon contain high levels of Vitamin B, which prevents skin peeling. You can also eat oily fish such as mackerel, carp, or eel. To absorb the nutrients most effectively, you should steam the fish to preserve its nutritional value.
Oranges

A very popular food known among women for its beauty benefits, oranges contain high amounts of Vitamin C, which balances skin moisture and strengthens collagen in the tissue structure. Furthermore, eating oranges or other citrus fruits can help reduce cravings and make weight loss easier.

By paying a little attention to your daily diet and adding beneficial foods like water, fish, oranges, oats, eggs, and carrots, you can keep your skin smooth, hydrated, and glowing throughout the season.

mon_an.ten: How to Peel and Prep Various Foods
mon_an.mo_ta: Instructions for removing the outer skin or shells of various foods. 1. Removing peach fuzz and skin.
cac_buoc: Dissolve a pinch of salt in cold water and soak the peaches for a few minutes; the fuzz will come off with a gentle rub.
Blanch the peaches in boiling water for about one minute, then remove and plunge them into cold water; the skin will peel off very easily.
2. Peeling lemons
Roll the lemon between your palms for a few minutes to soften the peel, making it easier to remove. Roll gently and evenly to avoid bruising the fruit.
3. Peeling oranges

Use a knife to slice the orange vertically into long wedges, then peel as you eat. Alternatively, soak the orange in boiling water for a few minutes (not too long) before removing; it will be much easier to peel.
4. Peeling jujubes (red dates)

Most of the nutrients in jujubes are located just under the skin, so peeling them can be wasteful. However, if needed, soak them in boiling water for 2-3 minutes; once removed, the skin will strip off easily.
5. Peeling lotus seeds

Add a little salt to a pot with enough water and add the lotus seeds. Bring to a boil while stirring constantly with a ladle. After about 10 minutes, the skins will shrink; remove them and drop them into cold water to peel easily.
6. Peeling garlic
Separate the garlic cloves and soak them in boiling water for a few minutes.

mon_an.ten: Beauty Benefits of Lemon Peel You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: With its amazing properties, lemon peel is an incredibly effective ingredient for beauty care. With just a little attention, you can create highly effective beauty recipes at a low cost.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Weight Loss:

Lemon peel contains a lot of soluble fiber, which provides a feeling of fullness and helps control fat and cholesterol levels. Therefore, you can drink lemon peel water to curb cravings and manage weight gain.

To do this: Slice fresh lemon peel into thin strips and boil them in water with a few dried apples. Keep the pot covered, as opening the lid will allow beneficial substances to evaporate. Boil for about 10 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Step 2: Brightening Age Spots:
Using lemon peel to brighten age spots is quite effective, but it requires long-term patience for the spots to gradually fade.
To do this: Rub a piece of lemon peel onto the area with age spots, leave it for one hour, then rinse clean. Do not rub too hard, as it may damage the skin.
Step 3: Softening Dry Elbows:
The skin on the elbows often lacks moisture and becomes dry, especially in winter. You can use lemon peel to quickly restore the skin's original softness.
To do this: Place your elbow into the hollow of a lemon peel and rotate gently, pressing slightly so the juice soaks into the skin. Do this for 10 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Step 4: Moisturizing and Beautifying Skin:

Lemon peel is a source of vitamin C and citric acid, which help cleanse blood vessels and remove impurities from skin cells. Lemon peel combined with olive oil and sugar not only promotes healthy skin but also makes it visibly softer.
To do this: Mix half a cup of sugar with finely chopped lemon peel and olive oil. Wet your body, then rub the mixture onto your skin while massaging for 10-15 minutes before rinsing with plain water.
Step 5: Protecting Teeth:

Lemon peel is rich in citric acid, which has antioxidant effects and fights gum problems caused by vitamin C deficiency. Additionally, the vitamin C in lemon peel cleans teeth, reducing bleeding gums and gingivitis. It is also an effective ingredient for removing tartar due to its cleansing and hygienic properties.
To do this: Finely chop lemon peel and mix it with 1 tsp baking powder, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp water to create a thick paste.
To clean your teeth and remove tartar, rinse your mouth with water mixed with this paste or use it as a substitute for toothpaste.
Step 6: Treating Dandruff and Enhancing Hair:
Lemon peel helps your hair become healthier and smoother while removing dandruff. The scent of lemon peel on your hair is also wonderful, isn't it?
To do this: Finely chop or crush the lemon peel, boil it with a little water, then apply this mixture to your hair and let it sit for about 15 minutes before shampooing.
With the amazing benefits mentioned above, lemon peel is truly an effective beauty ingredient. With just a little care, you can have highly effective beauty formulas at a very low cost.

mon_an.ten: Useful egg tips and egg-based recipes
mon_an.mo_ta: Today, we would like to introduce useful tips and cooking secrets for egg dishes.
cac_buoc: How to boil eggs without cracking or bursting
Place the eggs in a pot of cold water and gradually bring to a boil.
Use a needle to prick a small hole in the larger end of the egg before placing it in the boiling water.
If the eggshell is cracked, add a little salt to the water to prevent the egg white from leaking out.
A new method for stir-frying eggs

When stir-frying eggs, add a little cooled boiled water to prevent them from overcooking. Crack the eggs into a bowl (avoid using aluminum bowls), add lard, salt, and cooled boiled water (water should be about 1/10 of the total volume), then whisk well with bamboo chopsticks. Stir-fry as usual.
Adding a few drops of wine to the eggs while stir-frying will make them more fragrant.
Using goat fat to stir-fry eggs will make them more delicious.
A new method for making omelets
When the omelet is almost cooked and the yolk is starting to set, drizzle a tablespoon of cooled boiled water over the surface; the finished egg will be golden, soft, and delicious.

When making an omelet, after pouring the eggs into the pan with lard, drizzle a little hot water over and around the egg; this prevents the edges from curling or tearing, making it softer and smoother to eat.
Use low heat when making an omelet to ensure it is tender and thin.
Before making the omelet, you can sprinkle a little flour into the hot lard; the cooked egg will look more attractive, taste better, and use less lard.
You can use butter for the omelet if you prefer the flavor.
A new method for making egg soup

When making egg soup, pour an appropriate amount of boiling water into the beaten eggs, add a few drops of wine, and then add shiitake mushrooms or seasoned minced meat according to your taste; the soup will be fragrant, delicious, and nutritious.
Separating egg whites and yolks
Usually, a spoon is used to scoop the yolk from the white. However, it is better to do the following:
Crack the egg into a funnel; the egg white will flow through the hole while the yolk remains inside.
Prick a hole at both ends of the egg, making the hole at the larger end slightly bigger; tilt that end down to let the white flow out, leaving the yolk inside the shell.
Using salted duck eggs

Poke a hole in either end of a raw salted duck egg, use a small bamboo chopstick to mix the yolk and white together, then add vinegar, seasonings, and MSG and mix again. When cooked, this egg will be as delicious as a fresh one and taste like shrimp.
Cut the cooked salted duck egg white into small pieces, season with a little white sugar, sesame oil, MSG, and vinegar. You can also add some sliced tofu. This dish is very savory.
Mash the cooked salted duck egg yolk and braise it with tofu, then season with soy sauce, sesame oil, MSG,
scallions, and chives... it will be very fragrant and delicious.

mon_an.mo_ta: Spices are essential in any kitchen. However, not everyone knows how to store them to preserve their full flavor. With these simple storage tips, you will always have fresh spices ready in your kitchen!
cac_buoc: 1. Storing Peppercorns

Peppercorns contain a small amount of essential oil. If ground, they won't last long as the aroma will evaporate. The best way to store peppercorns is to keep them whole in a glass jar, covered with plastic wrap before sealing the lid. Only grind small amounts for use over a short period.
Before putting peppercorns in the jar, you should also place them in the refrigerator for 2-3 days to dry them out further; this allows you to store them for 2-3 years.
2. Storing Ginger
The simplest way to store ginger is to fill a wide container with damp sand and bury the ginger inside. This way, you will have fresh ginger ready to use at any time.

If you prefer not to use sand, you can crush the ginger with a little salt, lemon juice, and a pinch of sugar. Transfer the mixture to a clean glass jar, cover with plastic wrap, and store in the refrigerator. Use a separate clean stainless steel spoon to scoop out the mixture when needed.

The key to preserving ginger is preventing air exposure. You can wrap the ginger in aluminum foil, which blocks air and maintains a stable temperature to keep the ginger from spoiling for a long time.
3. Storing Salt

Salt is an essential seasoning for cooking and cleaning food, but it easily becomes damp and clumpy. A small tip to fix this is to place a piece of absorbent paper at the bottom of the salt jar; the paper will absorb all the moisture in the jar, keeping the salt dry.
4. Storing Chilies

Over time, chilies can become dry and brittle, losing the qualities of fresh chilies. To store them, slit the chilies to remove the seeds, place them in a sealed plastic bag, and keep them in the refrigerator. You can also trim the stems and soak the chilies in a mixture of vinegar and a little sugar; this way, the chilies will stay fresh and spicy as if they were just picked, even after a long time.
5. Storing Shallots and Dried Garlic

To store shallots and dried garlic, people in rural areas of Vietnam often hang bunches of shallots and garlic or place them above the kitchen stove, where the clinging soot prevents bacteria from spoiling them. If you don't have a wood stove, store them in bamboo baskets or mesh bags in a cool, airy place. Never store them in damp areas, as this will cause the shallots and garlic to sprout.
6. Storing Lemons

Lemons are an essential seasoning in Vietnamese meals, but they do not last long and quickly turn yellow and bitter. To keep lemons fresh for a whole week, wash the skin thoroughly and drain well before storing. Place them in a plastic bag, tie it tightly, then put it in another plastic bag and store in the refrigerator; this prevents the skin from drying out, allowing you to preserve the lemons for a full week.
With these spice storage tips, we hope you always have fresh and high-quality spices in your kitchen.

mon_an.ten: How to Cut and Slice Meat
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for preparing and slicing meat. Beef should always be sliced against the grain.
cac_buoc: For goat meat, you must remove all membranes. Otherwise, when stir-fried, those membranes become hard and chewy, making it difficult to swallow.
For pork, slice diagonally to prevent the meat from crumbling or becoming too mushy when cooked, and to ensure it doesn't get stuck in your teeth.

For chicken, cut or chop along the grain to keep the meat intact and more appetizing. Note that for old hens, you should adjust the technique to slice against or diagonally across the grain depending on the part.
For fish, cut quickly with clean strokes. It is best to cut along the fish bones.
For pork liver, slice it immediately before putting it into the pot. After slicing fresh liver, quickly season it, toss with starch, and cook right away.

mon_an.mo_ta: Learning how to choose fresh seafood will help you impress your family!
thoi_gian: The beach season is approaching; refer to these tips on how to choose fresh seafood to help you buy the best ingredients for your dishes.
cac_buoc: 1. How to choose fresh seafood: Choosing shrimp
For fresh shrimp, choose those with intact legs and antennae, the head firmly attached to the body, and no fishy or spoiled smell. Different types of shrimp have different selection tips:
For sea shrimp (banana prawns), choose those that are still jumping and have a pinkish-white color; these are fresh and healthy.
For tiger prawns, the shell should be shiny and smooth, and the spine should be transparent; these will have firm meat.
For lobsters, choose those with clear blue legs and a bright, healthy, shiny shell.
2. Choosing fish

Freshly caught fish will have elastic flesh; if you press down and the meat springs back, it is fresh. The gills should be bright red, not dark or bruised. If eating immediately, choose these; if you need to transport them, you can ask the shop to sun-dry or lightly grill them to preserve the sweetness and flavor.
3. Choosing snails and shellfish
For snails, choose those with the operculum (trapdoor) near the outside; it should close tightly when touched, and there should be no foul smell.

For shellfish, choose those with open shells that close immediately when touched. For some species, simply smell them; they are good if there is no spoiled odor. For blood cockles, choose slightly larger ones so they don't shrink too much during cooking. For ark clams, choose medium-sized ones; very large ones can be chewy.
A tip for choosing hard clams: choose those with closed mouths; those with open mouths are already dead.
4. How to choose fresh seafood: Choosing squid
For squid, choose those with thick bodies and the characteristic brown membrane still intact on the outside. The head should be firmly attached to the body, and the ink sac should not be broken.
For calamari (squid tubes), choose those with a pinkish-white color and no fishy smell.
For cuttlefish, choose those with a milky white color.
5. Choosing crabs and blue crabs

Choose blue crabs with a red apron and curled legs; these are fresh. Medium-sized blue crabs are often more flavorful than very large ones. To check for meatiness, press near the apron; if it doesn't feel hollow, the crab is firm. If you want roe, choose females, which have a yellowish tint and very firm legs when squeezed.

For mud crabs, choose those with a grayish-brown shell. Press the apron; if it feels firm and the apron is large, the crab has plenty of meat. The spines on the claws should be sharp, and the legs and claws should move actively.

Another tip for choosing crabs and blue crabs is to avoid buying them during the full moon (the 15th of the lunar month), as they are often less flavorful and the meat is watery and soft during this time.

mon_an.ten: How to Choose Quality Honey and Ginseng
mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know how to buy honey? Or how to buy ginseng? What makes them high quality? Here are some ways to help you select the best honey and the finest ginseng: 1. Choosing honey
cac_buoc: It should be thick with high viscosity, fragrant, and come in colors like white, pale yellow, or light pink, appearing very clear. How to identify authentic honey:
When stirred, it feels very smooth and soft with no gritty sensation. When tasted, it melts very quickly in the mouth with a deep sweetness and strong aroma; it is sweet but not cloying.
No cloudiness should appear when it is stirred thoroughly.
Pull the honey into a thread; when it breaks, it should coil back into a round shape, and the flowing thread should fold into a pyramid shape.
Insert a red-hot steel wire into the honey; it should not bubble or release steam.
It should absorb very slowly into white paper.
Mix 1 part honey with 5 parts water, stir well, and cover; after one day, there should still be no sediment at the bottom.
Mix 1 part honey, 2 parts rice water, and 4 parts 95% alcohol, stir well, and cover; after 24 hours, there should be no impurities settling at the bottom.
Boil 1 part honey with 10 parts water, let it cool, and add 2 drops of iodine. If it turns purple, it is fake honey (containing starch).
2. Distinguishing ginseng

Ginseng has a very characteristic taste: bitter with a slight sweetness. Ginseng is usually divided into 4 grades: Heaven, Earth, Good, and Cut. You should choose the largest ginseng possible, as the concentration of nutrients and medicinal benefits is higher. If they are the same size, choose the heavier one.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for buying delicious poultry: Choosing chicken: Choose healthy birds with bright red combs, straight smooth legs without scales, thick breasts, dry vents, and dry mouths. Avoid chickens that are too old or too young. The best tasting is a young hen about to lay (pullet). Free-range chicken has yellow meat and is more fragrant and flavorful than industrial chicken.
cac_buoc: How to distinguish between young hens, old hens, and sick chickens:
Young hen: Yellow skin, soft feathers, small pores, thick neck and thighs, slender shanks, bright red comb, and a small vent.
Old hen: Hard legs with scales, messy and dull feathers, large pores, thin neck, grayish-white skin with many bumps, and a large vent; old roosters will have long spurs.
Sick chicken symptoms: Pale comb, cold feet, lethargic appearance, shaking the beak, or drooling. The crop feels tight like a balloon when touched.
Choosing duck: Choose ducks that are mature and fat, with round breasts, full skin on the neck and belly, and full plumage (the tips of the two wings should just cross each other).

Avoid young ducks as they are not as tasty and take a lot of effort to pluck pinfeathers. Young ducks have large, soft beaks, while old ducks have small, hard beaks. A duck that has laid many eggs will have a sagging lower belly. Unlike chickens, drakes (male ducks) are tastier than female ducks.
What are your shopping tips? Please share them with everyone!

mon_an.mo_ta: Here are some tips for choosing delicious meat: 1. Fresh pork:
cac_buoc: The exterior should have a dry membrane, the surface should be slightly firm, and the cut surface should be bright pink. The skin should be soft, the grain firm, and the elasticity good (meaning when you press your finger into the meat and release, it leaves no indentation). The fat should be bright in color with a firm consistency and a normal smell. Joint surfaces should be smooth and clear, and the marrow should adhere tightly to the bone.
If the pork is dark red, the grain is loose, and the belly skin is thick, it is from an old pig or a sow; it will be tough and not tasty when cooked.
Sick pork will have loose meat, yellow fat, and you may see opaque white spots in the grain, or small spots on the liver or kidneys.
*2. Fresh beef:* Fine, dry grain, bright red color, white tendons, and yellow fat.
*3. Veal:* Fine grain and white fat.
*4. Buffalo meat:* Coarse grain, deep reddish-purple color, and whiter fat than beef.

mon_an.mo_ta: Are you feeling confused when shopping for groceries? Here are some tips on how to choose the best seafood. 1. Choosing soft-shell turtles
cac_buoc: Soft-shell turtles with a sea-blue shell are better than those with a sandy yellow shell. Males are tastier than females, so look for males (the tail of a male turtle extends past the shell, while the female's does not). The best type is a male with a sea-blue shell weighing about 750gr. Avoid turtles with insect or mosquito bites. For example, in the image below, you should choose the one in the top left corner.
2. Choosing sea cucumbers
The best sea cucumbers are the prickly variety (Stichopus japonicus); they should be large, fleshy, free of sand, and have fleshy spines protruding from their backs.
3. Choosing shellfish
The most delicious and nutritious are fresh shellfish that are light yellow and about the size of a child's fist. Avoid small, black ones.
4. Choosing freshwater shrimp

Choose shrimp with hard shells and whiskers, a green tint, bulging eyes, and meat that is tightly attached to the shell with a fresh fishy scent. If they are molting, the shell will be soft, but the meat and shell should still be firm and free of any foul or rotten odors. Avoid shrimp with sunken eyes, a dark yellow tint, hollow meat, broken heads, or missing legs.
5. Choosing dried shrimp

Pick up a handful of dried shrimp, squeeze firmly, and then release; if the shrimp straighten out immediately, they are high quality. Choose bright-colored, intact shrimp with the head and body firmly attached and eyes still present. Opt for shrimp with a natural red color (shrimp-brick red) as this indicates they were sun-dried while fresh. Avoid dried shrimp that are too pale or too dark, as they may be old, boiled before drying, or treated with food coloring.

mon_an.mo_ta: Are you feeling confused when shopping for groceries? Here are some tips on how to choose the best seafood. 1. Choosing fresh fish
cac_buoc: Fresh fish have a white anus and clean edges; the gills are pink and the gill covers are tightly closed; both eyes are bulging and clear with transparent corneas; scales are firm and not loose or falling off; the body is firm and wiggling; the belly is firm and not bloated with gas.
It is best to choose fish that are still swimming actively in the water.
How to choose fresh fish
2. Identifying contaminated fish

Contaminated fish have cloudy eyes that do not reflect light, and sometimes the eyes protrude significantly. The gills turn dark red and the folds are messy; the body is limp and distorted, with a curved or deformed spine. Sometimes the skin turns yellow, the tail turns blue, and the fishy smell is mixed with other odors like petroleum, coal oil, ammonia, or even a faint perfume scent.
3. Choosing fresh sea fish
The fish should have firm scales that are not loose or falling off, with no exposed bones. The meat should be firm without spots, not turning pink, and free of strange odors.
Fresh sea fish
4. Choosing sea crabs

The best time to buy sea crabs is around April or May when they are at their fattest. Choose crabs with intact claws and legs, a grayish shell, and unbroken spines at the ends of the shell. Place the crab in your palm; the joints of the claws should be responsive and move quickly.
Avoid crabs that look slightly green on the claws and shell; if the apron feels soft when pressed, the crab is watery, hollow, has little meat, and is not tasty.

A pointed apron indicates a male crab, while a round apron indicates a female. Female crabs have more roe, while male crabs have less roe but the meat is fattier and tastier. This also applies to field crabs.
5. Choosing field crabs

The period around the beginning of autumn is when field crabs are at their fattest. Choose crabs with strong claws that are always pointing up ready to pinch; they should have all their legs, move quickly, be large and plump with a dark green shell, and constantly blow bubbles.
In today's article, we will guide you on how to choose fresh seafood. We hope this helps you easily select the best fresh seafood for your family!
Guide to choosing fresh seafood:

Choosing fish: You must choose fresh, high-quality fish. Stale fish tastes fishy, makes the broth cloudy, and can cause allergies in sensitive people. Distinguish between fresh and stale fish as follows:

Fresh fish: The body is firm (specifically for goby fish, a firm but cloudy body means the fish is dead), the flesh is elastic when pressed, and the scales are shiny and not easily detached. The eyes are bright, clear, full, and clean. Gills are bright red and free of slime.

Stale fish: Has a characteristic foul fishy smell, eyes are cloudy and sunken. The body is soft and looks pale. Gills are gray and slimy. For large fish sold in steaks, the cut surface is pale with no blood or dark red clotted blood.

*Choosing shrimp:* Fresh shrimp are shiny, translucent gray, smooth, firm, and long. Note that stale shrimp have dull shells that turn reddish, a foul smell, and the heads, claws, and legs fall off easily.

*Choosing crabs:* Use your finger to press firmly on the crab's apron; if the crab is meaty, the apron will be hard and won't sink—this is when it's most delicious. Crabs with legs and claws that look watery are not good. To buy crabs with roe, choose females (large apron); for meat, choose males (small apron).

*Choosing snails:* Lightly touch the snail's trapdoor; if it's alive, it will automatically close. For fat snails, the trapdoor is near the shell opening. For thin snails, the trapdoor is recessed further inside. Dead snails have a trapdoor that is deep inside the shell and they emit a foul odor.

mon_an.mo_ta: Here are some collected tips for choosing eggs: – *Fresh poultry eggs:* The shell is bright with a thin, powdery film on the surface; the shell should not look shiny. When held against a light or sunlight, the white and yolk are clearly distinguishable, with the yolk appearing as a faint shadow centered in the middle.
cac_buoc: Old eggs: The shell is rough but the surface is slightly shiny; when candled, the yolk appears dark and is off-center near the shell, or dark spots are visible.
If placed in water: Fresh eggs will sink and lie horizontally at the bottom. Spoiled eggs will stand upright. Eggs that have started to develop an embryo will float to the surface.
Do you have any other tips for choosing and identifying eggs? Share them with everyone!

mon_an.ten: How to Choose Vegetables | Buying Fresh Produce
mon_an.mo_ta: The secret to choosing vegetables is to look for produce that is fresh, not bruised, not waterlogged, free of strange odors, and has leaves that are not wilted or insect-eaten. Here are specific tips for each type. 1. Choosing good celery
cac_buoc: Celery should have a bright green color, be clean, with thick stalks and round stems.
2. Choosing cucumbers

Choose cucumbers that are fresh, straight, and uniform; small bumps on the outside indicate they are dense. Green or white skin indicates young cucumbers, while yellow indicates they are old or wilted. Cucumbers with a layer of white powder on the outside are freshly picked and will taste sweeter than those kept for a long time.
3. Choosing eggplants
Choose eggplants that are deep purple with shiny, tight skin.
4. Choosing good bean sprouts
Bean sprouts should be white, with short stalks about 6cm long, not too thick or coarse, and have no strange odor other than the characteristic scent of bean sprouts.
5. Choosing spinach
Choose spinach with thick leaves, a wide leaf surface, and short stems.
6. Choosing green onions
Choose plump bulbs that are not bruised, with green leaves that are fresh all the way to the tips.
7. Choosing onions
Choose onions with skin as dry as possible and a tightly closed neck; you should be able to see green veins running through the outer skin.
8. Choosing potatoes
Choose potatoes with thin skin, no spots, no bruises, and no wrinkles. Potatoes must not be sprouting or have green skin.

mon_an.ten: How to Choose the Best Pork Ribs for Your Dishes
mon_an.mo_ta: Discover the secrets to choosing the right pork ribs for every dish. With these selection tips, you can pick the best ingredients to cook for your whole family.
cac_buoc: How to choose fresh pork ribs:
The most important factor when choosing food is freshness. When picking ribs, look for a light pink color, no unpleasant odors, and meat that is elastic to the touch with a dry surface.

Choose ribs with small, flat bones. These typically have more meat and less bone than those with large, round bones. Also, ensure the ribs are not too small. Very small rib sets are often from piglets, which may lack flavor or come from unhealthy livestock.
Choosing the right ribs for specific dishes:

For sweet and sour stir-fried ribs, braised ribs, or fried ribs: Choose lean ribs with little to no fat. Rib tips with cartilage (sườn non) are excellent for these. Loin ribs (sườn thăn) are generally the best choice for these preparations.
For soups, congee, and noodle soups: Choose ribs that have a mix of lean meat and fat so the meat remains tender, fragrant, and rich when eaten.
For pork chops (sườn cốt lết): Look for thick loins with minimal fat for the most tender and delicious results. Pork chops are best suited for grilling, frying, roasting, braising, or smoking.

Go to the market early to get the freshest selection. If you go late, the best cuts are often sold out, or the meat may have lost its freshness due to being displayed at room temperature without specialized refrigeration.

Buy your ribs (and other fresh proteins) last after you have finished buying vegetables and fruits. This minimizes the time the meat spends in plastic bags, which can cause spoilage or allow chemicals from the bag to leach into the meat.
Once home, remove the ribs from the bag and cook them immediately. If not cooking right away, wash them thoroughly and store them in an airtight container or zipper bag in the refrigerator.

mon_an.ten: Unique Fish Steaming Tips – How to Refresh Salt-Cured Fish
mon_an.mo_ta: A unique steaming method: When steaming fish, you can crack an egg over it. The fish will absorb the nutrients from the egg, making it much more delicious and fresh.
cac_buoc: If you have leftover steamed fish, crack an egg over it when reheating; the fish will taste better and the egg will be delicious.
How to refresh salt-cured fish:

Pour 100-150g of vinegar into a bowl of warm water and soak the salted fish for 4-6 hours. Alternatively, use rice water mixed with 50g of salt, stir well, and soak the salted fish for 4-5 hours before cooking. This makes the fish as tender and tasty as fresh fish.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Perfect Caramel Sauce (Nước Hàng)
mon_an.mo_ta: Caramel sauce (nước hàng) has many culinary uses, from making flan (creme caramel) to adding a beautiful color to braised dishes. While pre-made coconut caramel sauce is available at markets, making it at home ensures hygiene and quality. Here is a simple guide to making your own caramel sauce.
cac_buoc: Add the sugar to a pot.
Add the lemon juice (optional).
Add the water and stir well.
Turn on the heat. Stir while heating until the sugar dissolves completely into a clear, slightly thickened syrup.
Continue heating until the syrup turns a deep amber (caramel) color, then turn off the heat. Your caramel sauce is ready.

Note: During the process, when the sugar syrup is thickened but still clear, it is perfect for serving with pancakes or crepes. This clear syrup can also be used to sweeten fruit juices or other beverages.

mon_an.ten: How to Use Spices Safely and Healthily
mon_an.mo_ta: Using or combining spices incorrectly can create substances that ruin the flavor of food and harm your health. Refer to this guide to use them correctly!
cac_buoc: Vinegar: This spice helps deodorize and enhance flavors. It is commonly used in dipping sauces. While fresh lemon can be used, vinegar provides a milder acidity. Usually, vinegar is added during the marination stage.

Cinnamon and Star Anise: When using whole pieces, add them during marination and cooking to extract the full aroma. If using powder, mix it with a little water first. Do not add cinnamon or star anise directly to hot oil as they burn easily, making the dish pungent and bitter.

Sugar and MSG: When frying or grilling, use only a small amount of sugar for marination. Too much sugar causes food to burn easily and turn dark and bitter. Nutritionists recommend not adding MSG while food is boiling at high temperatures; add it only when the food has cooled to about 70-80°C. Use MSG sparingly to stimulate the taste buds, as excessive amounts can cause headaches or dizziness in sensitive individuals.

Garlic and Shallots: These have strong aromas, so use them carefully. Over-marinating can mask the natural flavor of the main ingredients. When making fried eggs with shallots, do not mix them together before hitting the pan. Instead, sauté the shallots in oil first until fragrant, then add the eggs. Do not use onions or leeks solely for garnish; cook them with other ingredients to fully release their flavor.

Honey: Honey contains many beneficial nutrients like antioxidants and amino acids, which can break down at high temperatures. Only mix honey into warm water, tea, or milk at 40°C or below. Store honey in glass jars away from sunlight. Avoid metal containers as they can cause chemical changes. If the honey has many air bubbles, it has likely spoiled and should be discarded.

Ginger: Ginger is used to marinate meat and fish to remove fishy odors. It contains the enzyme Zingibain, which helps tenderize meat. Wash it well and keep the skin on for medicinal benefits and extra flavor. Avoid using old, shriveled ginger as it may contain sulfur toxins harmful to the liver.

Black Pepper: Many people marinate food with pepper before cooking, but high heat can destroy its characteristic aroma. It is best to sprinkle pepper only after the food is cooked. Additionally, pepper contains a small amount of essential oil to hold its scent. Pre-ground pepper loses its aroma quickly, so it is better to store whole peppercorns and grind them only when needed.

Sour agents for soups: For sour soups (canh chua), choose the souring agent based on the ingredients. Tamarind (me) pairs well with fish, dracontomelon (sấu) works best with meat, and dried sour fruit (tai chua) is great for vegetable broths. Dried Hibiscus calyces are also excellent for sour sauces or fish/meat soups. These natural agents are safe to use; simply add them near the end of cooking, then remove the solids or strain the broth.

mon_an.ten: How to Tenderize and Stew Beef Quickly
mon_an.mo_ta: Beef or buffalo meat, especially from older animals, can be very tough to stew. Here are a few ways to speed up the process: Rub the meat with dry mustard powder the night before. The next morning, wash the meat thoroughly before cooking.
cac_buoc: When cooking beef, you can add a bit of wine or vinegar. Generally, for every 1000g of beef, add 2-3 tbsp of cooking wine or 1-2 tbsp of vinegar.
When stewing beef, place some dry tea leaves in a small cheesecloth bag, tie it tightly, and place it in the pot with the meat.
Add a bit of young papaya peel or a few hawthorn berries (potatoes also work) to the pot when cooking beef. This method also works well for goat meat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fry dishes play an important role in the delicate culinary tradition of Vietnam. This guide introduces several effective ways to make your stir-fries more appetizing. These tips will provide you with secrets to ensure your stir-fried dishes are always delicious.
cac_buoc: Tips for Delicious Stir-fries

Step 1: In stir-fried dishes, garlic, shallots, ginger, or lemongrass are vital aromatics that create the dish's fragrance. Depending on the specific recipe, choose the appropriate aromatics to sauté in hot oil first; this will make your dish much more flavorful.

Step 2: For recipes with specific instructions, follow them closely to know the exact cooking time and the order in which to add ingredients. If you are creating your own dish, cut the ingredients into bite-sized pieces—not too large or too small—to ensure they cook evenly and maintain the best quality.

Step 3: Stir-fries are a combination of many ingredients, but they often have different cooking times. You should prepare all ingredients before you start stir-frying. Avoid a situation where one ingredient is overcooked while others are not yet ready to be added.

Step 4: Some vegetables tend to lose their vibrant color during stir-frying. To keep them looking beautiful, you can blanch them in boiling water and then immediately plunge them into a bowl of cold water. This helps the vegetables retain their bright color.

Step 5: If the stir-fry includes meat or seafood, marinate them with salt, seasoning powder, etc., depending on the dish, so the ingredients are well-seasoned. For fish stir-fries, use a bit of wine to remove any fishy odor and enhance the taste. This is a very useful tip.
Step 6: Stir-fried dishes with a sauce look more appetizing and taste richer. Mix in a little cornstarch or tapioca starch to make the sauce glossy and thick.
Above are some great tips for delicious stir-fries.

mon_an.ten: How to Remove Odors from Different Types of Meat
mon_an.mo_ta: Some types of meat, if not pre-processed properly, can leave an unpleasant smell that ruins the dish. Below are several methods to remove odors from various meats that every cook should know.
cac_buoc: Duck

Duck meat often has a distinct odor; therefore, if you don't know how to deodorize it, the dish will lose its appeal. To prevent this, before boiling, rub the duck with a bit of salt, pepper, crushed ginger, and optionally some white wine. Let it sit for 30 minutes, then rinse thoroughly and drain before cooking.
Add a piece of crushed ginger to the pot when boiling. This will eliminate any remaining odor, ensuring your duck is fragrant and delicious.
Pork
Pork is a staple food used in daily family meals. Generally, healthy pork is very fragrant. However, if you happen to buy a piece with an unpleasant smell, do not worry.
In this case, add 3-5 pieces of clean straw to the pot while boiling. Once cooked, add a few drops of white wine, remove the meat, and drain. Proceed with your recipe, and the odor will be gone.
Pork Kidneys

Good pork kidneys should be uniform and dark in color, without yellow or red spots. After washing, slice the kidneys and soak them in a bit of vinegar and water for about 10 minutes. The kidneys will expand, the blood will be removed, and the fishy odor will vanish, leaving them white and crunchy.
Goat Meat

Goat meat is used in many delicious dishes, but it can have a strong gamey smell. To deodorize it, you can mix the meat with a little vinegar or the juice of two lemons and a bit of cooking oil. Store it in the refrigerator for a few hours to reduce the odor.

Another way is to use cinnamon to deodorize the meat, or skim off the fat while the meat is boiling. In some places, people rub the meat with white wine mixed with minced ginger and then rinse with cold water. Others use beer or briefly blanch the meat in boiling water with lemongrass or segments of sugar cane. Choose the method that best suits your needs.
Rabbit Meat

Rabbit meat is delicious, but if not prepared correctly, it can have an unpleasant smell. When preparing rabbit, clean it thoroughly, cut into pieces, and rub with wine and crushed ginger. This will effectively remove any odor.
Fish

After cleaning the fish (removing gills, scales, fins, and innards), rub it thoroughly with regular salt or rock salt. To remove stronger odors in certain types of fish, make sure to strip away the black membrane and bloodlines inside the belly, then rinse well. For better results, soak the fish in rice water or salt water for 15 minutes before rinsing again to remove slime and fishy smells.
Beef
For many, beef has a stronger, more distinct odor than pork. If this smell isn't removed, it can be off-putting.

To handle this, place the beef in a pot of cold water (submerged) and heat it up on the stove (do not let it reach a full boil). The surface of the meat will heat up and coagulate, reducing the strong odor. This method is best for dishes where the beef is stewed or cut into large chunks.
Alternatively, rinse the beef with water and then wash it again with wine, or soak it in wine for 15 minutes before rinsing with clean water. This makes the beef more fragrant when cooked.
To make beef even more appetizing, besides marinating with garlic, you can roast some dried shallots, peel off the charred skin, crush them, and marinate them along with the beef and garlic.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Effective Ways to Deodorize Cutting Boards
mon_an.mo_ta: A cutting board is an indispensable kitchen tool. Almost all types of food require a board for portioning and cutting. Therefore, having a clean cutting board is essential for delicious and hygienic meals. However, boards can often absorb food odors. Learn these simple tips to deodorize your cutting board. Method 1: Utilize rice water mixed with a bit of salt. Soak the board for 3-5 minutes, wipe it thoroughly with a cloth, and then rinse with hot water. This is guaranteed to remove odors immediately.
cac_buoc: Method 2: Use sliced onions to rub over the surface of the board, then rinse with hot water to eliminate the smell instantly.
Method 3: You can use vinegar or lemon juice, let the board air dry, and then wash it clean to remove any lingering odors.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Pork Stomach, Salted Meat, and Pork Trotters
mon_an.mo_ta: Hello everyone! Today I would like to share some tips for preparing pork stomach, refreshing salted meat, and cooking delicious pork trotters. Cleaning pork stomach:
cac_buoc: After the pork stomach is boiled and sliced, place it in a bowl and add a little broth. Place the bowl in a pot and steam/cook it further; the stomach will double in size and become both delicious and crunchy. Note: do not add salt beforehand, or it will become as tough as beef tendon.
How to refresh salted meat

When meat has been heavily salted, soak it in rice water to make it taste as good as fresh meat. You can also rinse it several times in a very light salt solution (lower concentration than the meat itself). Repeat this a few times with even lighter salt water before processing.
How to cook pork trotters
Before adding pork trotters to the pot, rub a little white sugar onto the outer skin. This helps the skin cook faster and makes it more fragrant and delicious.

mon_an.ten: How to Grow Clean and Delicious Bean Sprouts at Home
mon_an.mo_ta: Bean sprouts are a familiar ingredient for many families. They are not only highly nutritious but also very easy to prepare. When enjoyed, bean sprouts have a beautiful color, a crunchy texture, and a naturally mild sweet taste. With fresh mung beans and a little effort, you can have delicious bean sprouts for various dishes. Making bean sprouts is not difficult, so don't hesitate to spend some time in the kitchen to ensure you have clean ingredients for your family and friends.
cac_buoc: How to make bean sprouts at home
Step 1:
Soak the mung beans in 1 liter of 40°C warm water overnight (11-12 hours), changing the water every 6 hours.
Step 2:
Next, wash the milk cartons thoroughly and carefully open the top along the sealed seam so the mouth is fully open.
Step 3:
Use a knife or sharp scissors to poke many small holes in the bottom of the carton (creating a surface like a strainer for drainage).
Step 4:
Once the mung beans are fully soaked and the shells have started to crack, pour all the beans into the prepared milk cartons.
Step 5:
Rinse the milk carton under the tap.
Step 6:
Store at room temperature (25 – 35°C) for 4-5 days, watering them twice a day, morning and evening. After each watering, rinse them and use clips to seal the mouth of the carton.
If followed correctly, by the 2nd day, the sprouts will have grown about 1 cm.
By the 3rd day, the sprouts will be longer and plumper, about 2-3 cm each.
By the 4th day, the sprouts will be 3 – 4 cm long, pushing up toward the mouth of the carton.
By the 5th day, the sprouts will have emerged from the mouth of the carton.
Step 7:
Once the sprouts have reached full length, use scissors to cut along the length of the carton and remove the sprouts. Rinse them thoroughly with water, drain, and they are ready for cooking.
Notes for delicious homemade bean sprouts
If you want to grow a larger quantity, you can use a small ceramic jar and follow the same process.
Additionally, you can cover the top of the jar with a damp cloth to help the sprouts grow faster while providing enough moisture.
You can use bean sprouts for various dishes such as stir-fries, salads, kimchi bean sprout soup, etc.
Besides the towel-covering method, you can make sprouts grow plumper using bamboo leaves or wood ash.
How to choose good mung beans: Choose beans that are free from pests, weevils, or grit. Plump, round, and glossy beans are mature. The beans should feel heavy and have smooth skin.

Bean sprouts are a familiar ingredient for many families. They are not only highly nutritious but also very easy to prepare. When enjoyed, bean sprouts have a beautiful color, a crunchy texture, and a naturally mild sweet taste. With fresh mung beans and a little effort, you can have delicious bean sprouts for various dishes. Making bean sprouts is not difficult, so don't hesitate to spend some time in the kitchen to ensure you have clean ingredients for your family and friends. You can also share this homemade method with those around you to enjoy clean food at home!

mon_an.ten: How to make lotus flowers and pineapples with Oishi candy
mon_an.mo_ta: Lotus flowers and pineapples made from Oishi candy will make your altar look more beautiful and appealing. With just a little time and skillful hands, you can create a lovely lotus flower or pineapple display. Let's explore how to make these using Oishi candy. With creativity and dexterity, you can transform sweet candies into art. Each Oishi candy becomes a lotus petal, and soft candy slices turn into juicy pineapple pieces. With patience and a meticulous style, you will create impressive and lifelike works of art. Try it now and discover the joy of creating with Oishi candy! Explore how to use Oishi candy to create eye-catching lotus petals and pineapples, bringing freshness and sophistication to your dessert display. Creativity and skill are key—try it now and experience the fun of making lotus flowers and pineapples from Oishi candy.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Other ingredients - same as for the pineapple
cac_buoc: 1. How to make a lotus flower with Oishi candy
Step 1: Create lotus petals with Oishi candy
First, fold the top of the Oishi candy into a triangle.
Then, use a small staple to secure the top of the candy.
Step 2: Create the lotus frame from a plastic bowl and plate
Use single-sided tape to fix the plastic bowl and plate together.
Next, wrap double-sided tape from the bottom of the bowl outwards.
Step 3: Assemble the lotus flower with Oishi candy
Remove the double-sided tape layer at the bottom of the bowl and attach 4 yellow Oishi candies to serve as the flower core.
Next, use single-sided tape to secure the base and tops of these 4 candies so they cluster together.
Then, attach the next layer of yellow Oishi candies for the second row.
Repeat the process with the remaining red and green candies until finished.
Once completed, you will have a beautiful lotus flower display.
2. How to make a pineapple with Oishi candy:
Step 1: Preparation:
First, fold the end of the candy with text into a triangle. Note: fold on the inside of the candy!
Then, use a stapler to secure these ends.
Next, roll the cardboard into a cone shape with a base matching the indentation of the plastic bottle and a length equal to the bottle's height.
Use clear tape to secure the cardboard into a cone, then fix the cardboard to the plastic bottle.
Step 2: Make the pineapple leaves
First, use scissors to cut the green ribbon into flag shapes of various lengths.
Then, use clear tape to attach these ribbons to the cardboard core from top to bottom.
Step 3: Assemble the pineapple with Oishi candy
Wrap double-sided tape completely around the plastic bottle. Note: do not peel off the second side of the tape yet!
Next, attach the candies to the bottle body. Peel the double-sided tape as you go to ensure it remains sticky.
After each layer of candy, use clear tape to secure their bases.
Finally, use tinsel to cover the bottle cap.
You have now finished making a beautiful pineapple from Oishi candy!

Try this method to create unique decorations for your ancestral altar or Tet space. Surely, Oishi candy lotus flowers and pineapples will transform your family's space. Let's get creative and experience the beauty of these candy crafts this Tet!

mon_an.ten: How to make irresistible tomato sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: Making your own tomato sauce for yourself and your family is wonderful—it's delicious, healthy, and hygienic.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 4 - 8 tbsp lemon juice or red wine vinegar
cac_buoc: Tomato sauce is an indispensable ingredient in many dishes, such as spaghetti, stuffed tofu in tomato sauce, fish in tomato sauce... It is considered the soul of the dish, greatly enhancing the flavor.

However, few people know how to make a delicious, rich, and standard bowl of tomato sauce; most buy pre-made canned sauce from food stores. Therefore, if you are still struggling to find a way to make delicious tomato sauce, check out this method. Success and "explosive" flavor are guaranteed.
Instructions:
First, boil water and drop a few tomatoes in. When the skin wrinkles (about 45 seconds to 1 minute), remove the tomatoes and place them in an ice bath. Repeat with the remaining tomatoes.
Peel the tomatoes and discard the boiling water.
Finely mince the tomatoes or pulse them in a blender until slightly pureed.
Place the tomatoes in a pot and simmer over medium heat for 30 to 90 minutes. Stir occasionally so the sauce thickens beautifully.
Once the sauce reaches your desired consistency, turn off the heat and add the lemon juice, vinegar, and salt. Taste and stir well.
Storage:
You can freeze the tomato sauce using ice cube trays or small containers in portions suitable for one-time use. Frozen tomato sauce can be stored for at least 3 months.
If not freezing, pour the sauce into clean glass jars, seal tightly, and store in the refrigerator for up to 1 week.

mon_an.ten: How to make crunchy pickled cà pháo without browning
mon_an.mo_ta: Pickled eggplant is a popular rustic dish. Especially on summer days, eating white rice with a bowl of water spinach soup and crunchy pickled cà pháo is incredibly delicious and appetizing. Today, we will guide you through the traditional way to pickle eggplants so they are crunchy and do not turn brown.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Choose cà pháo (Thai eggplants). You should pick freshly harvested ones. Cut one open to check that the seeds are moderate in size and white, not yellow.

Step 2: Sun-dry the eggplants for 3 to 4 hours, then trim the stems and wash them. Halve the eggplants and soak them in diluted salt water for about 15 minutes to help remove toxins. Rinse with cold water and drain.

Step 3: Mix lukewarm water (40°C) with salt and 1 small tsp of sugar. Taste the brine; it should be salty like the seasoning for braised meat—not harshly salty, but not bland either, or the eggplants will spoil. Peel and lightly crush the garlic. To keep the eggplants crunchy and long-lasting, prepare a small bowl or a plastic bag filled with water to weigh them down once they are in the jar. This prevents them from floating, browning, and ensures they taste better.

Step 4: Sprinkle a little salt at the bottom of the pickling jar, then add a layer of eggplants. Repeat until finished, then pour in the prepared brine. Ensure the brine covers the eggplants by about 1.5 finger joints (add more brine if needed). Close the lid and use the weight to keep the eggplants submerged.
Wait for 1-2 days to see the results of your handiwork! Good luck with this kitchen tip!

mon_an.ten: Discover how to cook soft, delicious, and nutritious cháo quickly
mon_an.mo_ta: Cháo (porridge), a familiar and popular dish in Vietnam, is not only convenient but also attractive with its characteristic flavor. Discover simple ways to cook cháo in the article below to enjoy a delicious bowl at home! I. Guide to cooking cháo in a rice cooker
thoi_gian: Cooking cháo on a gas stove:
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare ingredients
Non-glutinous rice: 100g (about 1 cup)
Glutinous rice: 20g (1/4 cup)
Salt: a pinch
2. Processing steps
To cook cháo in a rice cooker, start by putting the soaked rice into the cooker, then add 1.5 liters of water and 1/4 tsp salt. Close the lid and turn on "Cook" mode.
After about 10 minutes, when the cháo is boiling, unplug the cooker and let it sit for 10 minutes to allow the rice to bloom.

A small tip: For a smoother texture, after unplugging, let the cháo stay hot for another 10 minutes. The result will be a fragrant, easy-to-make, and delicious bowl of white cháo. This is a great choice for taking care of sick people or for the whole family to enjoy on weekends. With smooth, soft, and delicious grains, you can confidently show off your skills in the kitchen!
II. Guide to cooking white cháo on a gas stove
1. Prepare ingredients
Non-glutinous rice: 100g (equivalent to 1 cup)
Glutinous rice: 20g (equivalent to 1/4 cup)
Soak the rice before cooking:
Place 100g non-glutinous rice and 20g glutinous rice in a bowl, rinse 2-3 times, then soak for 6-8 hours or overnight.
After soaking, gently rinse the rice once more and drain.
Cooking cháo on a gas stove:
Pour the rice into a pot, add 1.5 liters of water and 1/4 tsp salt. Place the pot on the stove and bring to a boil over medium heat.
When the cháo boils for about 2-3 minutes, reduce to low heat, stir gently, and cook for another 5-7 minutes until the grains are smooth. Finally, turn off the heat and enjoy.
III. Tips for cooking soft and delicious cháo successfully
If you have time, soak the rice for 5-6 hours or overnight before cooking to help the cháo soften faster and taste better. Before soaking, wash the rice to remove grit and dirt.

Alternatively, you can wash the rice, drain it, and then toast it in a pan over medium-low heat. When the grains turn light yellow, you can proceed to cook. This method helps the grains bloom evenly and become more fragrant.
The water ratio is also very important. You can try a 1:5 ratio of rice to water, or adjust according to your preference for thicker or thinner cháo.
When cooking, you can use both glutinous and non-glutinous rice to make the cháo softer and more fragrant. Add a little cooking oil to the rice while cooking to prevent it from boiling over.

White cháo can be combined with many different foods such as sugar, salt, kho quẹt (caramelized fish sauce), duck embryos, century eggs, pickles, braised anchovies, pepper braised pork, braised shrimp, and many other dishes.

To store white cháo, after cooking and if not used up, you should put it in a non-metal container such as ceramic or plastic, then store it in the refrigerator for 1-2 days to ensure the flavor and nutrients are preserved.
IV. Secrets to cooking cháo soft and fast
Method 1:
Bring water to a boil, then add the rice to the pot, cover, and turn off the heat for about 15 minutes. Next, turn on low heat to bring it back to a boil.
Method 2:

Alternatively, you can add rice to a pot of boiling water, cover tightly, and turn off the heat. After a while, turn on the heat to boil again and repeat this process a few times to ensure the cháo cooks quickly and tastes good.
Method 3:

Finally, the fastest way to cook cháo is to prepare it the night before. Put the rice into boiling water in a thermos flask and close the lid. In the morning, when the cháo is soft, pour it into a pot, prepare the side ingredients, and stir for about 5 minutes until hot and thick. Season to taste, then turn off the heat.
Method 4:
During the cooking process, adding a little cooking oil to the pot helps the cháo look glossy and more attractive. It will be easier to eat and more visually appealing.
Method 5:

To ensure the best quality and flavor, cook the cháo and other ingredients separately. Do not cook cháo together with seafood, meat, or vegetables. Instead, cook the cháo, meat, seafood, and vegetables each independently.

After all components are cooked, combine them in the pot only for the final 10 minutes before turning off the heat. This technique keeps the cháo clear and delicious, with distinct flavors that are not muddled.
Method 6:

During the cooking process, do not stir too much. Although you might think stirring helps it cook evenly and faster, it's actually a mistake! Over-stirring causes the rice grains to break and mush, and if cooked with other ingredients, the cháo can become fishy.
For the best quality, you should only stir the cháo twice:
The first time is when adding rice to boiling water; remember to stir in only one direction.
The second time is after cooking for about 20–25 minutes; stir gently for about 5 minutes in one direction, then cover and simmer for another 3–5 minutes to finish.

mon_an.ten: How to distinguish between different types of sponge cakes
mon_an.mo_ta: Here are some ways to distinguish between different types of sponge cakes and how to combine them—very useful! Please take a look!
cac_buoc: For Vietnamese people, sweet cakes in general are often referred to as "bánh bông lan" (sponge cake)—a fluffy dessert eaten plain or covered in cream to make a cream cake. However, cake bases actually come in many types with different flavors, textures, and methods, rather than just being a generic "sponge cake"!
High-fat cake – Rich and buttery

It's no coincidence that baking is defined by flour, butter, sugar, eggs, and milk. In the most basic and oldest European cake recipes, fat from animal butter plays a crucial role. High-fat cakes are classic cakes built on a foundation of fat and leavening agents: fats like butter or oil make the cake moist and soft, while leavening agents like baking powder or baking soda create volume and a crumbly texture. High-fat cakes are basic and familiar, featuring a relatively dense, moist texture with a moderate rise and an unmistakable rich buttery aroma.

The two most common types of high-fat cakes are pound cake and butter cake. The biggest difference is that while pound cake uses almost no liquid like milk or juice, butter cake contains a significant amount of milk. Pound cake sticks to a balanced ratio of 1 flour: 1 butter: 1 sugar: 1 egg, making it simple and foundational for beginners. However, the downside is that it can feel heavy and dry, so it is often served with syrup, jam, or fresh fruit to reduce the dense sensation.

Butter cake includes milk, which makes the texture silkier and moister. Modern cakes, from tiny cupcakes to elaborately decorated cream cakes, favor this recipe. The sensation of butter cake is described as a "gentle melt" of butter on the tongue because it is high in both moisture and fat. While popular in the West, the high flour and butter content can feel a bit heavy or greasy for Asian palates if eaten in large quantities.

Despite some drawbacks, high-fat cakes remain popular because of their delicious flavor (if not overeaten), relatively simple recipes, and a dense structure that supports elaborate cream decorations without collapsing.

The most common mixing method for high-fat cakes is the creaming method: Butter is beaten until fluffy and pale, then liquid ingredients (eggs, milk, or juice) are added gradually, and finally, sifted dry ingredients (flour, leavening agents, additives like cocoa or matcha) are folded in quickly and gently before baking.
Foam cake – Light as a cloud

In contrast to traditional high-fat cakes, modern baking has trended toward foam cakes that are soft as cotton and light as a cloud. Inspired by fragile soap bubbles, foam cakes use recipes with little to no fat, creating a weightless texture. Foam cakes rely on whipped eggs for leavening instead of baking powder or soda and contain very little flour to avoid the heavy feeling of classic cakes.

A typical foam cake is the chiffon cake—one of the most challenging bases for bakers. With very little flour and relying entirely on whipped egg whites to rise, chiffon is difficult because it requires precise temperature and timing to rise tall but remain structurally sound without collapsing after leaving the oven. Chiffon is famous for its specialized tube pan, which helps heat distribute evenly from the inside out, preventing the cake from collapsing or hollowing.

The strength of chiffon is its airy, melt-in-your-mouth feel without any greasiness, making it easy to eat an entire cake. However, due to its delicate structure, it is less suitable for heavy decorations. Thus, sponge cake was developed to bridge the gap, maintaining the cloud-like lightness while being sturdier. Sponge cakes whip whole eggs—rather than just whites—for a slightly denser texture. Americans created their own version called Genoise, characterized by whipping eggs over a double boiler and adding butter for moisture without making the crumb heavy.

Most foam cakes require much gentler and more delicate handling than high-fat cakes. Since the rise depends on air bubbles in the whipped eggs, the baker must minimize bubble breakage when mixing. The most important technique is "folding"—incorporating ingredients by turning them over from the bottom rather than stirring. Correct folding, precise timing and temperature, and balancing moisture are just a few requirements for a perfect foam cake.

In general, gateau cakes with vibrant cream and fluffy bases are common today. But the story of complex classifications, diverse recipes, and techniques behind different cake bases always surprises enthusiasts. It turns out the concept of "bánh bông lan" is both familiar and full of new things to discover!

mon_an.ten: How to marinate food for great flavor
mon_an.mo_ta: Whether grilling, stir-frying, or roasting, food needs to be marinated before cooking. This step helps the food absorb flavors and develop an appealing aroma. But marinating effectively is an art. Let's learn some secrets to marinating food perfectly!
cac_buoc: Olive oil

Marinades often use olive oil for its fragrance. You can also use other oils (like sesame oil) or alternative liquids like soy sauce, red wine, white wine, vinegar, yogurt, honey, lemon juice, orange juice, or a mixture. You need enough liquid to submerge the meat. Use at least 250ml (1 cup) of marinade for 1 kg of meat. Using oil or liquid helps the meat stay moist, tender, and delicious.
What should you add to a marinade?

For a simple marinade, mix aromatic herbs with olive oil, and perhaps add some mustard, shallots, garlic, or pepper. For vegetables, you can use finely chopped or sliced carrots, tomatoes, and celery to add depth; bay leaves are also a good choice. Lemon juice is a constant companion for fish dishes, helping to reduce fishiness and provide a pleasant aroma.
How long should you marinate meat?

The longer you marinate, the more the flavors penetrate. You can marinate for several days, overnight, or just a few hours, depending on the dish. Always marinate for at least 1 hour to allow the flavors to soak in. If the marinade contains lemon juice, do not leave it too long, as the acid will "cook" the fish to some extent and ruin the texture.
Marinades aren't just for meat

Besides meat, you can marinate fruits and vegetables for skewers and grilling. Cut them into small pieces and soak them. For vegetables, use olive oil and spices. For fruit, use liquid sugars (honey, maple syrup, or cane sugar) mixed with spices (cinnamon, vanilla, etc.). You can also add a splash of rum or other liqueurs like Grand Marnier for a pleasant fragrance.
Tips
Use glass, stainless steel, or ceramic dishes; avoid using aluminum for marinating. Aluminum can react with the marinade and leach harmful substances into the food.
You can also place meat in freezer bags, add the marinade, squeeze out all the air, and seal. This saves time and helps the spices penetrate deeper into the food.
When marinating, use fresh spices; they provide a better aroma than old ones.
Additionally, you can use the marinade liquid while cooking the meat or fish. However, watch the flame carefully if your marinade contains alcohol to avoid fires or accidents.
Hopefully, these tips will help you in your cooking and lead to many delicious meals.

mon_an.ten: How to decorate a beautiful Mid-Autumn Festival fruit tray
mon_an.mo_ta: The following fruit tray decoration guide will make your Mid-Autumn Festival warmer and more communal! On Mid-Autumn Festival, the fruit tray (mâm ngũ quả) is an indispensable part of the party. This is a cherished tradition, as it shows respect and carries meanings of goodness and luck. To create a beautiful and impressive fruit tray, there are simple yet sophisticated decoration methods you can apply. From choosing fresh fruits and arranging them harmoniously to adding decorative details like flowers and leaves, the fruit tray will become a charming highlight on the table, bringing a joyful atmosphere to this special day. ## Which fruits are included in the fruit tray?
cac_buoc: According to Vietnamese customs, Mid-Autumn Festival is an occasion for the whole family to gather and share affection. Children especially look forward to it, hoping for lanterns, toys, and the "breaking of the feast" (phá cỗ).
Guide to arranging the Mid-Autumn fruit tray:

A full and meaningful Mid-Autumn tray varies by region but typically includes: mooncakes, green pomelo, custard apples, shiny red persimmons, crunchy persimmons, pomegranates, guavas, oranges, purple sugarcane, bananas, watermelon, fragrant yellow thị fruit... Among these, pomelo is essential everywhere.

The meanings of the fruits are very interesting. Red persimmons represent hope. Custard apples represent the wish for prosperity and growth. Pomelo symbolizes goodness. Pomegranates bring sweetness and luck. Watermelons and cantaloupes represent peace...

To make the tray most visually appealing, pay attention to the colors. Regardless of the fruit types, there should be both green and ripe fruits. Green represents Yin, while ripe represents Yang, symbolizing the balance of the universe.
Besides traditional arrangements, you can add animals made from fruits and vegetables to make the tray more lively.
Making a pomelo dog:
Making a beautiful peacock:
Ingredients to prepare:
1 ripe pineapple, unpeeled
1 long, slender zucchini
8 long bell peppers
10 small ripe chilies
Floral foam
Two longan seeds
1 slice of carrot
Instructions:
1. Cut the zucchini to take the top, slender part, and attach it firmly to the bottom of the ripe pineapple. You can use double-pointed toothpicks for a secure fit.
2. Use toothpicks to attach the large red peppers to both sides of the peacock's body, and the small chilies at the base of the neck to create a full, vibrant look.
3. Carve the carrot slice into a point for the beak and use the two longan seeds for eyes.
4. Finally, bend the floral foam into small branches to serve as the peacock's crest.
With a little meticulousness, you will have a very pretty peacock.

The elegant peacock with its long slender neck and vibrant red tail made of peppers and green pineapple leaves will add color to your tray. However, this peacock is for display only and is not edible.
Making a funny round-eyed frog family:

At first glance, it's hard to imagine this playful green frog family is made from chayote, with round black eyes made from longan seeds. You'll be surprised how a little creativity can completely transform a chayote.
Preparation:
1 wicker basket lined with foil
4 equal-sized chayotes
1 carrot
8 longan seeds
1. Wash the chayotes, then cut a slit at the head to make the frog's mouth.
2. Place a thin slice of carrot into the slit to serve as the tongue. Attach 2 longan seeds for eyes.
Red fish to brighten the Mid-Autumn tray:

You've seen goldfish, but a pinkish-red fish with a wide, adorable smile made from dragon fruit will surely surprise and delight many. These fish "swimming" in the fruit tray will excite the children.
To make a dragon fruit fish, prepare:
1 red dragon fruit with white flesh
Pomelo peel
1. First, cut the pomelo peel into a dorsal fin and two side fins. Leave a bit of peel to tuck into the dragon fruit and trim the edges into serrated shapes.
2. Slit the dragon fruit along the top and on both sides of the body.
3. Tuck the pomelo peel fins into the slits, then attach eyes using longan seeds or black grapes.
This pinkish-red fish with its wide smile is very cute. Children will love seeing these fish in the tray.
Funny fat pig:
Using the same dragon fruit but changing the shape slightly, you can create a very cute pink pig.
Making a hedgehog from pear and grapes:

A beautiful Mid-Autumn tray must balance warm and cool colors. The cool green of a hedgehog made from pear and grapes helps achieve this. To make this adorable hedgehog, you just need green grapes, a pear, a black grape, and some skill.
Preparation:
1 green pear
1 bunch of green grapes
1 black grape
Toothpicks
Knife
Instructions:
1. Divide the pear into two parts (the round base and the pointed top). Peel the skin off the pointed top to make the hedgehog's face.
2. Pierce the green grapes with toothpicks.
3. Stick the grape-laden toothpicks into the round part of the pear to form the quills. Finally, attach the black grape for the nose and add eyes (you can use black beans for eyes).
With these simple steps, you can decorate a beautiful fruit tray for Mid-Autumn.
Beyond these animals, you can skillfully carve many other shapes. The more whimsical creatures you have, the more lively the tray becomes.
A flower pot made from pineapple is very appetizing.
A watermelon fish filled with fruit.
Watermelon carved into a cute rabbit!
Under your skillful hands, watermelon can be carved into many beautiful patterns.
Completing the Mid-Autumn tray:

To arrange the most beautiful tray, choose a sturdy square table and cover it with your best tablecloth. Carefully place your carved fruit plates and cute animals on it. Remember to add a vase of fresh flowers, a plate of sliced mooncakes in various flavors, and a pot of fragrant lotus tea.

Nowadays, no matter how busy they are, families bustle to learn how to arrange the best Mid-Autumn tray as the holiday approaches. The Mid-Autumn fruit tray is a symphony of flavors and colors, a message from parents to children that life is full of color.
Regional notes for Mid-Autumn fruit trays

In the North, you can place a bunch of bananas at the bottom, symbolizing the protection of heaven and earth. Place a pomelo in the center of the bananas and surround it with ripe red fruits like persimmons, peaches, and tangerines. You can also add pears, apples, oranges, dragon fruit, mangosteen, etc., according to preference.
In the Central region, the specific five fruits are less important. It mainly features homegrown products like custard apple, banana, mango, papaya, coconut, fig, etc.
In the South, bananas are not used as the main fruit. Instead, they often use watermelon or green-skinned pomelo in the center, surrounded by custard apple, mango, and papaya.

mon_an.ten: How to treat mouth ulcers with natural foods
mon_an.mo_ta: Mouth ulcers are a common ailment in summer. They cause pain, discomfort, and hinder daily communication, making you look for the fastest way to treat them. The following methods are simple and will help you quickly eliminate the pain within 2-3 days.
cac_buoc: Use radish juice:
Chop the radish, blend it with a little water, and strain for the juice. Mix with cooled boiled water and rinse your mouth 3 times a day.
Use katuk (rau ngót) juice:

Wash the katuk leaves, then crush or blend them. Extract the juice and mix with a little honey. Use a cotton swab to dab the juice onto the ulcer. Repeat 2-3 times a day for immediate effect. The sores will soothe, and the pain will subside. Remember to use only the leaves and do not dilute with water; use pure juice for maximum effectiveness.
However, nowadays, katuk is often sprayed with chemicals or growth stimulants, so you should use katuk from a safe source to avoid unwanted side effects.
Use starfruit water:

Take 2-3 starfruits, cover with water, and bring to a boil. Let the water cool, then gargle and swallow slowly. Do this several times a day for effectiveness. Sour starfruit is better as it stimulates more saliva and clears heat better.
Use tomatoes:
Peel the tomatoes and juice them to drink daily. Hold the juice in your mouth for a while to let it penetrate deeply.
Use watermelon rind:
Char the watermelon rind until golden brown, then grind it into a powder. Mix the powder with honey and apply it to the ulcer 1-2 times a day.
Use Thai basil leaves:
Simply chew 3-5 Thai basil leaves several times a day to treat mouth ulcers.
Notes on treating mouth ulcers:
Besides the above methods, you should follow these rules to treat mouth ulcers at the root:
Avoid foods that irritate the mouth, such as salty foods, oily foods, and highly acidic fruits.
Regularly eat green vegetables and fruits to treat internal heat.
Practice proper oral hygiene.
Drink plenty of water.
Rinse your mouth with salt water 3 times a day.

mon_an.ten: How to stir-fry, fry, braise, double-boil, and steam
mon_an.mo_ta: Are you confident in your food preparation methods? How do you stir-fry, fry, braise, double-boil, and steam correctly? Read this article to check your knowledge!
cac_buoc: First, use high heat to heat the pot. Prepare enough fat (oil/lard) for the dishes you want to stir-fry. Once the pot is hot, add a spoonful of fat, swirl to coat the sides, then start stir-frying the first dish. When cooked, drizzle in another spoonful of fat, toss quickly, and remove from the heat to serve. After the first dish, continue with the second, third... When stir-frying, note:
Adjust the heat according to the dish. Always heat the pot first before adding cold fat.

Plan the order of the dishes. Even within one dish, consider the order of ingredients. For example, if a dish has both minced meat and green vegetables, stir-fry the meat first, remove it to a bowl, stir-fry the vegetables, then mix them back together and add seasonings.
The order of ingredients is discussed in many books; you can refer to them.
Before stir-frying, prepare and mix the seasonings so they are ready to be added when the dish is done.
Frying

Mastering the oil temperature is most important. Different ingredients require different heat levels. When the oil is at level 3-4 (about 100°C), you can fry peanuts or eggs. At level 5-6 (about 170°C), you can fry poultry. At level 7-8 (about 200°C), you can stir-fry ribs or cartilage with sugar and vinegar for the second time (the first time the oil should not be too hot). To make food crispy on the outside but tender inside, process it twice at two different heat levels.
Braising (Om)
