Use only low heat for braising. You can add a little fat or vegetable oil. Do not flip the food while braising.
Steaming and Double-boiling
When steaming or double-boiling meat or fish, use boiling water for an immediate heat effect. For eggs, use low heat for a gentle and gradual effect. For cakes, use high heat.
How to prevent burning when steaming

The simplest way is to open the lid to check. However, many dishes require the lid to stay closed; in that case, place a clean ceramic shard in the pot. When the water boils, the shard will continuously hit the bottom and sides, making a sound. If the sound stops, it means the water has run dry.

mon_an.ten: How to stir-fry tender beef and buffalo
mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried beef and buffalo is a rich and attractive dish, combining the flavor of fresh meat with a variety of spices. This will be a wonderful dish for family meals. Follow the article below to master the way to stir-fry tender beef and buffalo! Stir-frying meat is not just a cooking skill but a way to explore and convey culinary culture.
cac_buoc: 1. How to stir-fry tender beef
1.1. Prepare ingredients
Beef tenderloin: 250g
Sugar: 1 tsp
Minced ginger
Soy sauce
Potato starch
1 tbsp vegetable oil
1.2. Stir-fry the beef

After buying the beef, wash and pat it dry. Next, slice the meat into bite-sized pieces, making sure to cut against the grain and slice thinly so the meat isn't tough. Place the sliced beef in a bowl, then add 1 small tsp sugar, 1 small tsp minced ginger, and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Mix by hand and marinate for 20 minutes. Once the meat has absorbed the flavors, add potato starch and vegetable oil, and stir well.

Sugar helps the beef become more tender when stir-fried, while oil creates a protective layer to prevent the meat from losing moisture. Note: do not marinate beef with salt as it will make the meat dry and tough.

Heat the pan with oil, then sauté ginger and garlic until fragrant. Next, add the beef to the pan and stir-fry over low heat for about 30 seconds to 1 minute. Then, increase the heat to stir-fry. This prevents the meat from sticking to the pan and releasing too much water, keeping it tender.

Stir-fry until the meat changes color (medium-rare). If you want a better color, add a small tsp of dark soy sauce. Then, add your favorite vegetables and stir-fry as desired. When adding vegetables, push the meat to one side, stir-fry the vegetables for a moment, then toss the meat and vegetables together. Add salt or other seasonings to taste.

Turn off the heat and serve the stir-fried beef on a plate to eat while hot. Note: if the vegetables take a long time to cook, stir-fry them first until nearly done, remove to a plate, and then stir-fry the beef. Since the beef was marinated, it won't be dry. Adding sugar to the marinade makes the beef much more tender and delicious.
2. How to stir-fry tender buffalo
2.1. Prepare ingredients
Buffalo meat: 300g
Water spinach: 2 bunches
Garlic: 2 bulbs
Chilies: 2 pieces
Seasoning: Cooking oil, oyster sauce, soy sauce.
2.2. Stir-fry the buffalo

Step 1: Prepare the ingredients for buffalo stir-fried with water spinach. Wash the buffalo meat and slice into bite-sized pieces. Wash the water spinach, pick the young stems, then place in a basket to drain. Wash the chilies, slice lengthwise, and remove seeds. Peel, crush, and mince the garlic.
Step 2: Place the sliced buffalo in a bowl, add 1/2 of the minced garlic, 1 tsp seasoning powder, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, and some pepper. Use chopsticks to mix well and marinate for 15-20 minutes.

Step 3: Heat the pan, add oil, and wait until hot. Add the remaining 1/2 of the minced garlic and sauté until fragrant. Then, add the buffalo meat and stir-fry over medium heat until cooked. Turn off the heat and remove the meat to a plate.

Step 4: Use the same pan to stir-fry the water spinach. Add oil and heat, then add the water spinach, 2 tsp MSG, 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 2 tsp seasoning powder, and 2 tbsp soy sauce. Stir-fry the water spinach for about 5 minutes.

Step 5: When the water spinach is cooked, add the sliced chilies and the cooked buffalo meat back into the pan. Re-season to taste and toss well. Turn off the heat and serve on a plate. Sprinkle pepper on top to enhance the aroma. Invite your family to enjoy this delicious dish immediately.

mon_an.ten: How to stir-fry sliced meat to keep it tender and juicy
mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know how to stir-fry meat so it stays tender and juicy? Don't miss these useful cooking tips! Adding a bit of cooking wine, starch, and soy sauce after slicing the meat thinly and mixing well will remove any gamey odors and keep the meat fresh. Note that you should not add salt at this stage, otherwise the meat will toughen. Wait until the oil is hot before adding the meat, then use chopsticks to spread it evenly. When the meat expands and changes color, add other seasonings and stir-fry for a few more minutes. The cooked meat will be tender and juicy.
cac_buoc: Place the sliced meat in a slotted spoon or spider strainer and blanch it in boiling water. As soon as the meat changes color, lift it out and drain well before stir-frying. After just 3-4 minutes of stir-frying, the meat will be cooked, tender, and juicy.
Heat the oil to heat level 8, then add the sliced meat to stir-fry. When the meat changes color, splash in a little cold water, then season and stir-fry for a few more minutes until done.

mon_an.ten: Tips for cutting cake without sticking to the knife
mon_an.mo_ta: Have you ever had to cut a cream cake? Do you know how to cut it so the knife doesn't stick? If it sticks, the cake slices won't look beautiful and will be difficult to plate. So how do you cut it so the slices maintain a beautiful shape and you don't "lose points" in front of your guests? Refer to these small cake tips below! – To cut a sponge cake without sticking, dip the knife in boiling water for a moment before cutting, then use the hot knife to slice.
cac_buoc: If you want to cut sliced bread perfectly, heat the knife before cutting. The bread will not stick together or crumble.
To preserve bread, put any leftovers in a plastic bag. Adding a sprig of cleaned celery to the bag can help maintain the bread's flavor and prevent it from hardening.

If cookies become soft, use a hairdryer to blow on them for a few minutes; once they cool down, they will be crispy again. Alternatively, place the cookies in the refrigerator for 1 hour to restore their crunch.

Leftover cake can be kept in an airtight container with a slice of fresh bread. When the bread slice becomes hard, replace it immediately with a new one. The cake will keep for a long time without spoiling.

mon_an.ten: Effective herbal remedies for high blood lipids
mon_an.mo_ta: Herbal medicine has been used by Vietnamese traditional medicine since ancient times for prevention and treatment. These are familiar plants in our daily lives that have been studied for their specific medicinal properties. Thanks to scientific progress, many herbs have been proven to be very valuable in effectively supporting the treatment of high blood lipids. Methods for using herbs to treat blood lipids:
cac_buoc: Non-drug method: A very important cause of high blood cholesterol is daily diet and lifestyle. Therefore, for those showing early signs of high cholesterol, this method should be applied immediately. The main focus is changing diet and lifestyle habits to adjust blood cholesterol levels.

Drug method: When medication is necessary, doctors often choose statins, which are effective at lowering LDL-cholesterol. However, modern drugs in general, and statins in particular, can have unwanted side effects. Consequently, many people are now choosing herbal treatments for high blood lipids.
Using herbs to treat high blood lipids:

Treating high blood lipids with herbs is considered safe by many because these are natural remedies with few side effects, and the cost is relatively reasonable. Notably, while the effects of herbal medicine are slow, the success rate in improving the condition is very high, as proven by generations of traditional use.
5 ways to use herbs in treating high blood lipids today:

Method 1: This herbal method supports fat loss and reduces obesity. Mix 3g of dried tea with 15g of Alisma (trạch tả), then pour in boiling water and wait 20 minutes before drinking. Use this method daily.

Method 2: Use 30g of tea root, 60g of Alisma, and 10g of Cassia seeds (thảo quyết minh). Chop them finely and steep in boiling water to use daily. This formula uses herbs that reduce blood lipids, making it suitable for those with chronic high cholesterol.

Method 3: Finely chop all the herbal ingredients: 3g dried tea, 10g kudzu (sắn dây), and 20g lotus leaf. Place everything in a pot with boiling water and drink daily to help eliminate toxins and balance blood lipid levels. This method is also suitable for overweight and obese individuals. You can also use lotus leaves alone to brew tea for daily use with relatively good results.

Method 4: Eating fish mint (rau dấp) regularly helps reduce excess fat in the body, contributing to the treatment of high blood lipids. Fish mint is an herb high in cellulose, which creates a feeling of fullness and reduces food absorption, thereby supporting the elimination of fat and waste from the intestines.

Method 5: Include winter melon in your daily meals. Winter melon has long been known as a very healthy food, containing no lipids, a very high water content, and many beneficial nutrients. Winter melon contains malonic acid, an active ingredient that helps reduce blood lipids and eliminate harmful excess fat inside the body.

The above are just 5 herbal remedies for treating high blood lipids among many methods currently in use. The effectiveness of these methods depends on individual constitution and how they are applied. Furthermore, your daily habits will also affect the treatment results. When using herbs, it takes a considerable amount of time to see the real benefits. Be patient and follow the advice above to successfully manage high blood lipids.

mon_an.mo_ta: Lemon kitchen hacks will surprise you with the wonderful uses of lemons. These tips include cleaning greasy dishes for the family or polishing furniture at a very low cost.
cac_buoc: Removing grease from dishes

If dishes are too greasy and still feel oily after washing, mix a few drops of lemon juice with dish soap, or spray it directly onto the grease. Rinse with water, and the dishes will be squeaky clean. This is the first tip in our Lemon Kitchen Hacks.
Deodorizing the home

You can place lemon slices in the refrigerator to remove odors, or add a few drops of lemon juice to floor cleaning water for a fresh, pleasant scent. Simply placing a few lemon slices on a small plate near the cat litter box or in the kitchen will significantly reduce unpleasant smells.
Brightening furniture
Use fresh lemon juice and a soft cloth to clean glass surfaces or polished wood. However, be careful as the acid in lemons can discolor marble. This is another useful tip from Lemon Kitchen Hacks.
Disinfecting cutting boards

Cutting boards used for raw food are ideal places for bacteria to grow, making them unhygienic. Lemons contain high levels of acid, making them a safe disinfectant for cleaning boards. Simply cut a lemon in half and rub it over the surface, squeezing to release the juice. Rinse with warm water, and you have a perfectly clean board ready for your next meal.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tomato season is short, and buying out-of-season greenhouse tomatoes is very expensive. Here are some home processing methods to prepare tomatoes and extend their shelf life:
cac_buoc: Making tomato paste: Three methods

Method 1: Select about 5kg of good tomatoes, wash them, steam until cooked, then peel. Filter through cheesecloth to remove seeds, keeping only the flesh. Mix 1kg of vinegar with 50g of five-spice powder and soak for two hours. Add 600-800g granulated sugar and 100-150g salt. Once dissolved, add a little peeled and crushed onion and garlic along with a moderate amount of pepper. Pour into a pot and cook over medium heat, stirring constantly. When thickened, taste to adjust seasoning. Pour into clean, dry ceramic jars, seal tightly, and store in a cool, dry place. It can be kept for a long time.

Method 2: Select about 5kg of fresh, good tomatoes. Wash, cut, and place in a pot over low heat without stirring for about 1 hour. Use a flour sieve or cheesecloth to filter out residue, seeds, and skins. Pour the tomato liquid back into the pot to reduce. Skim off any foam that rises to the surface. After about two hours, when the liquid is thick, continue cooking over low heat for another 30 minutes. Add 75g salt, 500g granulated sugar, 6g white pepper, 7g cloves, and 100g mustard powder. Mix well and cook over low heat for another 30 minutes. Add 3g MSG, cook briefly, and it's done.

Method 3: Select fresh tomatoes, wash, and drain. Blanch in boiling water for 2-3 minutes, peel, and cut into even slices. Place in a pot and cook at heat level 6-7 until done. Transfer to clean glass bottles with stoppers, being careful not to overfill. Seal tightly with a rubber stopper, insert a needle through the stopper, then place the bottles in a pot of boiling water to steam for 15 minutes (a pressure cooker is even better). When removing, pull the needle out and seal the hole with beeswax. Store in a cool place. Tomato paste made this way can be preserved for at least six months.
Tomato juice:

Select fresh, ripe tomatoes, wash, and blanch briefly to peel. Use clean cheesecloth to squeeze out the juice. Add a moderate amount of white sugar. For long-term storage, pour the sweetened juice into clean, dry glass bottles, adding salt and pepper to taste. Seal the bottles and submerge them in 80-90°C water for 30 minutes. Remove, seal tightly, and store in a cool, dry place. For even longer storage, refer to Method 3 above.
Tomato powder:

Select fresh tomatoes, wash, and drain. Slice them, removing stems and seeds. Place in an enamel tray and dry in an oven. Once dry, grind into powder. Store directly and use for cooking soups or stir-fries. Keep away from moisture to preserve the powder well.

mon_an.mo_ta: How do you properly prepare frozen meat without losing flavor while ensuring food safety? Please read our following notes!
cac_buoc: Frozen meat must be processed immediately after thawing and should not be refrozen.
When processing and cooking, adjust the heat appropriately for each type. Generally, start with high heat, then reduce to a simmer once it boils.
Use as little water as possible when cooking to prevent water-soluble vitamins and most nutrients from dissolving away.
To reduce nutrient loss, you can add a little thickening starch (a type of seasoning available at the market).

mon_an.ten: Proper ways to prepare green vegetables
mon_an.mo_ta: Green vegetables and root vegetables provide many essential vitamins for body growth. However, fear of chemicals and certain cooking habits often cause home cooks to lose the vital vitamin content in greens. If these bad habits persist, they will affect the body's nutrient absorption, which over time can harm human health. Refer to these tips for proper vegetable preparation to limit bad cooking habits!
cac_buoc: Do not peel all root vegetables: Many people think the skin is dirty or contaminated with chemicals and peel it all off. However, according to nutritionists, the skins of vegetables like pumpkin, radish, carrots, and eggplant contain more vitamin C than the flesh or leaves. Therefore, unless the skin is too tough to soften during cooking, you should not peel it all; just wash thoroughly before processing.

Do not overstock green vegetables: Many women, especially office workers, buy a week's worth of vegetables at once to save time. While convenient, storing greens for too long causes nutrients to be lost. Most vitamins, especially vitamin C, oxidize and disappear when exposed to air or light.

Wash before cutting: Nutritionists recommend washing vegetables before cutting them to ensure vitamins remain intact. Since many vitamins are water-soluble, cutting them before washing accidentally removes a large amount of nutrients.
Do not reheat green vegetables multiple times: Reheating vegetables repeatedly destroys a large amount of vitamins. Eating them this way provides no benefit and can even be harmful.

Stir-fry on high heat: If you stir-fry on low heat, the vegetables cook slowly, leading to the loss of vitamins, especially C and B1. It is recommended to use high heat. Some vegetables should only be eaten raw, such as cucumbers, tomatoes, and lettuce.
Do not boil for too long: If green vegetables are cooked for too long at high temperatures, the vitamins are destroyed, resulting in a significant loss of nutrients.

Eat immediately after cooking: Leaving vegetables to soak in the pot after turning off the heat destroys nutrients. Therefore, only cook the vegetables when you are ready to eat to preserve the vitamins.

mon_an.mo_ta: Using fruit in savory dishes is a compilation of kitchen tips for using fruit as cooking ingredients. Fruits carry many vitamins and are great for health, plus they make dishes more fragrant and delicious. However, because fruits are high in vitamins, special care is needed during preparation to cook the best meals for your family.
cac_buoc: Fruit is not just for dessert; it can be used to create many delicious meals for the whole family.

Before peeling fruit, wash it thoroughly with water or soak it in diluted salt water. Do not assume that cooking the fruit makes washing unnecessary. If the skin is dirty, parasites can transfer from your hands and the knife to the flesh, causing contamination.
If the fruit is acidic, add it last to the dish so it doesn't break down the nutrients in the other ingredients.
Do not cook pineapple with shrimp or crab. The acid in pineapple will make the meat mushy and lose its firm, delicious texture.
Do not use knives or cutting boards that have touched raw meat or organs to cut fruit. Keeping fruit away from fishy odors is a great tip for home cooks.

Some fruits like jackfruit or mangosteen have sap that sticks easily and is hard to remove. You can apply cooking oil to your hands or the knife; the sap will gradually dissolve as you rub, then wash with soap to clean.
Some fruits like apples and pears brown quickly. If you aren't processing them immediately after peeling, soak them in diluted salt water.
Depending on the firmness of the fruit, time the addition to the dish appropriately so the fruit stays soft or crunchy without losing its nutrients.

Fruits for salads should be firm-fleshed, like pears, apples, or golden melon. You can add berries like strawberries or raspberries, but depending on the type, either mix them in or just scatter them on top for the diner to mix themselves.

mon_an.mo_ta: Choosing good tomatoes is not difficult with these useful tips for those going to the market for the first time. Learn to cook well with these tips to help you select ripe, mealy tomatoes.
cac_buoc: Tomatoes are a favorite for both women and men. They are packed with nutrients, especially vitamin A, which is good for children's eyes. Tomatoes also help reduce blood lipids, aid weight loss, and improve beauty. Because of these benefits, they are widely sold.

Naturally ripened tomatoes are usually red with beautiful yellow seeds, not green ones. The inside should be juicy and red. Choose tomatoes with taut skin that are reddish-pink and feel heavy in the hand. If you find ones with slight ridges, those are usually mealy and taste the best.

Additionally, observe the stem. Vine-ripened and freshly picked tomatoes will have fresh green stems, not wilted or yellowed ones. Tomatoes picked green and chemically ripened often have an unattractive, wilted color that is easy to spot.
Unlike other fruits, tomatoes are best stored in a cool, airy place, avoiding plastic bags or the refrigerator.
Tomatoes ripened with chemicals are usually hard, lack aroma, and aren't juicy. When cooked, they take a long time to soften, or when they do, they have very little pulp and a pale red color.

Since chemically ripened tomatoes are common in markets, home cooks should be careful. It is best to buy from familiar vendors or those who grow their own; it's cheaper and better for your health. We also suggest trying to make tomato sauce for longer preservation.

mon_an.mo_ta: In cooking, seasonings enhance the appeal and flavor of a dish, providing a sense of enjoyment. Understanding and knowing how to use seasonings is the key to success for every chef. Today, we will learn how to distinguish between different seasonings. In this article, we will focus on *cooking oil, sesame oil, soy sauce, and MSG*.
cac_buoc: If cooking oil is adulterated with starches (rice, arrowroot, sweet potato), it will turn blue when a drop of iodine solution is added.

Heat half a tsp of cooking oil in a cast-iron ladle to 150°C, then let it cool. Standard oil will have no sediment; the more sediment there is, the higher the impurity level and the lower the quality.
Cooking oil mixed with tung oil will be cloudy or lumpy when a few drops of concentrated sulfuric acid are added or when soaked in 60°C water for 15 minutes.
2. Identifying sesame oil
Fresh sesame oil has a reddish-yellow color, a strong aroma, no sediment, and a viscous consistency.
3. Identifying soy sauce
Good soy sauce has a dark reddish color, smells of fermented soy and rich fat, and tastes savory—only slightly sweet, not sour, bitter, or acrid.
4. Identifying MSG

Pure crystalline MSG is bright, with even, snow-white transparent grains. If mixed with gypsum, it will look dull gray with small, square grains. Pure powdered MSG is bright and fine, feeling slightly gritty to the touch. When tasted, it feels cool on the tip of the tongue and has a slight fishy scent.

mon_an.ten: How to Select and Prepare Live Field Eels Quickly
mon_an.mo_ta: Eel is a high-value food, and its meat is used in many different dishes. In our country, eel is commonly used as an ingredient for eel porridge, eel hotpot, eel glass noodles, eel braised with bananas, and more. Eel meat also contains many vitamins and minerals such as vitamins A, B1, B6, iron, sodium, potassium, and calcium, which are very good for our health; however, pregnant women should avoid eating eel as it is considered too "cool." Selecting and preparing the best, most hygienic eel while ensuring no loss of nutritional components is quite simple—let's find out!
cac_buoc: Tips for choosing eel: Good eels are large, of moderate length, with a black back and a bright yellow belly. This type is field eel, which has fragrant and delicious meat, unlike farmed eel, which has crumbly and fishy meat.

Preparing eel: If you have time, after buying the eels, place them in a bucket of rice water for about half a day to clean their intestines. If you don't have time, you can process the eels immediately.

Step 1: Cleaning: Select and prepare the eel correctly. Hold the eel's head with your left hand, grip the body tightly with your right hand, and rub it with a mixture of lemon juice and salt. Rub repeatedly until the eel is no longer slimy, then rinse with clean water. Wait a moment for the eel's blood to clot before gutting.
Step 2: Gutting: Use a sharp knife or a piece of mature bamboo to make a straight cut from the head down and remove the internal organs.
Step 3: Filleting:
Cooked meat: Steam or boil the eel until just cooked, remove it, use chopsticks to grip the eel from the neck, and pull firmly downward; the meat will separate quickly.
Raw meat: Use a sharp knife to cut each side just below the head, then slice along the spine to separate each side.
Note: Once the eel is cooked, avoid letting plain water touch it, as this will make the eel smell fishy.

mon_an.ten: Choosing Durable and Beautiful Ceramic Tableware
mon_an.mo_ta: Choosing durable and beautiful ceramic tableware involves simple tips that not every housewife knows. Selecting the right ceramic dishes helps make meals more eye-catching and full of flavor.
cac_buoc: Here are some tips to help you choose durable and beautiful ceramic tableware:

Use a chopstick to tap lightly on the rim of the bowl or the edge of the plate. If the sound is crisp and clear, it is good; if the sound is dull, it indicates cracks or ripples that you may not have seen.
A good bowl has a shiny glaze that is not dull or cracked. You should choose bowls with a high base, as they will be less hot to hold and safer to use.
You can check for warping by placing the dishes upside down on a flat surface; this makes it easy to check for unevenness when choosing durable and beautiful ceramic tableware.

Check if the ceramic has been fired at a sufficient temperature. If the bowl is under-fired, the lead in the glaze can leach into food and enter the body, causing harm. To check, simply pour water into the ceramic bowl or plate. If the bowl does not absorb water, it is good. Alternatively, soak the bowl in a vinegar solution; if the bowl shows signs of whitening or the vinegar changes color, do not use it.

mon_an.ten: Choosing Wood Ear Mushrooms, Shiitake, and Bird's Nest
mon_an.mo_ta: How to choose various types of wood ear mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms, and bird's nest: 1. White wood ear mushrooms
cac_buoc: The best type is yellowish-white, dry, with large lobes, thick flesh, and a rich aroma.
2. Distinguishing black wood ear mushrooms
Good wood ear mushrooms are shiny black, thin-winged, light, and look bright and clean. One side is grayish; they feel dry to the touch without a gritty sensation and have no strange odor.
3. Distinguishing bird's nest

Real bird's nest (yến sào) has silk strands arranged in an orderly fashion. After soaking, it becomes silvery-white, transparent, soft, highly elastic, and stretches like rubber when pulled gently. Blood bird's nest with a slightly blackish-pink color is the best, followed by White bird's nest which is grayish-white, and then Mao bird's nest which is grayish-black.
4. Types of shiitake mushrooms
Three commonly used types of shiitake are flower mushrooms, winter mushrooms, and fragrant mushrooms.

Flower mushrooms: Light black cap with patterns; these patterns become prominent and white when dry. The underside of the gills will be light yellow after being roasted over red charcoal. The colder the weather, the wider the flower mushrooms bloom, and the better the quality, with thick, tender, and crispy flesh.
Winter mushrooms: Black cap, light yellow gills, relatively thick flesh, crispy when eaten, with a fresh sweet aftertaste.
Fragrant mushrooms: Umbrella-shaped, fatty, thin flesh, not very fine-grained, and not crispy.

When choosing shiitake, you need to distinguish the aroma. Press your finger on the "umbrella" of the mushroom, then release and sniff; if the scent is pure, it is a good mushroom. A yellow or white top surface is a sign of quality.
5. Non-toxic wild mushrooms

These are edible, mainly harvested in summer and autumn, growing in open, high grasslands and the soil of pine forests. The color is not very bright, the cap is quite flat, the top surface is smooth, and the base is dry. After cutting, a white liquid is secreted with a characteristic aroma. The upper part of the stem has no rings, and the base of the stem has no sheath.
6. Toxic wild mushrooms

These often live on manure or decaying matter in fields, mounds, old graves, or fertile, shaded, low-lying areas. The top of the mushroom cap is brightly colored, often in green, pink, yellow, black, or purplish-green; the purplish-black type is particularly toxic. The middle part is swollen and strangely shaped, with rings on the stem and a sheath at the base, and it breaks easily. This type of mushroom often has threads, scales, or reddish-gray warts on the cap. After being cut and exposed to air, it changes color easily and has a pungent or foul, fishy smell.
Signs of toxic mushrooms:
Turn grayish-blue when an onion stalk is rubbed on the cap.
A rush wick turns blue or purplish-blue when cooked with the mushrooms.
Silver cooking utensils turn black.

Boil the mushroom juice, apply it to old newspaper, dry it, then sprinkle a little concentrated hydrochloric acid on it; a blue color will appear, or it may turn pink first and then blue after half an hour.

mon_an.ten: Choosing Vegetables, Tubers, Fruits, and Beans
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for choosing vegetables, tubers, fruits, and beans 1. Choosing celery
thoi_gian: General characteristics of good vegetables and beans to buy: fresh appearance, not crushed, not waterlogged, no strange odors, leaves not wilted or insect-eaten, and always cool to the touch.
cac_buoc: Good celery must be fresh, bright green and clean, with thick leaf stalks and round stems.
2. Choosing cucumbers

When buying cucumbers, choose those with a beautiful color and smooth skin; the best ones have small bumps on the surface. If they feel soft to the touch and the stem is turning yellow, the cucumber is definitely withered and has many seeds.
3. Choosing eggplants
When buying eggplants, choose those with a deep purple color and shiny, taut skin; these are the freshest and most delicious.
4. Choosing bean sprouts
When buying, remember these checks:
Color: Normal bean sprouts are yellow; problematic ones are pale white, and the beans are green.
Texture: Normal bean sprouts have stems that are not too large or coarse, while problematic ones have stems that are unnaturally thick and look greasy.
Smell: Normal bean sprouts have no strange odor, only the characteristic scent of sprouts; problematic ones will smell of chemical nitrogen.
Good and safe bean sprouts are those with short stems.
5. Choosing scallions

To get good scallions, choose those with plump bulbs that are not crushed, fresh green leaves all the way to the tips, and roots that clearly distinguish the green and white parts. These are the best scallions.
6. Choosing onions
Choose onions with skin as dry as possible, tightly wrapped, where you can see green veins running inside through the outer skin.
7. Choosing potatoes
Choose potatoes with beautiful skin, no spots, no scars, and no wrinkles. Especially remember: when potatoes have sprouted, they should not be eaten, as consumption can lead to complications.
8. Choosing tofu

Good tofu is milk-white, highly elastic, with a soft, smooth texture, not too mushy and not too hard. When stacking two blocks, they should not stick, break, or crumble. When cut with a knife, the cross-section should be bright, free of impurities, not coarse, and have the characteristic aroma of tofu without any sour, acrid, or bitter smell.

mon_an.mo_ta: Choosing dried squid correctly – A new travel season has begun, and many families choose to buy dried squid as gifts. The following tips will help you buy delicious dried squid. Currently, the situation of fake dried squid is increasing, so it is necessary to pay attention to choosing dried squid correctly to buy high-quality squid with Learn to Cook Deliciously.
cac_buoc: Choosing dried squid correctly
Choose dried squid where the head is firmly attached to the body, with many tentacles that are pinkish-white and straight.

Dried squid with straight, thick bodies will be sweeter when grilled than thin ones. When buying, you should purchase dried squid that has been hung to dry, as these are high-quality line-caught squid, thick and firm.

Semi-dried squid (mực một nắng) is very delicious, sweet, and thick with a layer of fine powder and a fresh pink color. Poor quality squid often has dark red spots on the body and back, with light red spots on both sides. It should not smell fishy and should not feel wet to the touch. The body must be dry and not leave a fishy smell on your hands. This is a very important and easily recognizable characteristic.
Distinguishing real vs. fake squid
Currently, some restaurants mix fake squid to sell at real squid prices to tourists. Therefore, you need to pay attention to a few characteristics to avoid buying poor quality squid.
Do not buy dried squid that is too cheap, as it is likely fake or low-quality, old squid. Learn to Cook Deliciously advises against buying these types.
Fake dried squid has tentacles that do not curl naturally and lacks natural eyes and ink glands; when shredded, it appears fluffier than real squid.

Fake squid is made to look exactly like the real thing, so when buying in large quantities, to avoid being cheated, you should try grilling a piece first. When burned, whole real dried squid usually curls up and scorches from the outside in, while poor quality or smuggled dried squid burns almost to ash, has a burnt smell, and lacks the fishy and sweet taste of natural squid.
Storing dried squid
Wrap the squid tightly in newspaper or white paper, then place it in a plastic bag, tie it shut, and put it in the freezer.
Dried squid should be used within 4 months of purchase. To keep it delicious, you should sun-dry the squid once every 3-4 weeks.
Do not store dried squid near fresh raw foods.

mon_an.ten: Choosing Delicious Mushrooms Is Not Difficult
mon_an.mo_ta: Mushrooms are delicious and nutritious foods; however, if we do not know how to choose them, we not only fail to get the nutrition but also risk poisoning because spoiled mushrooms can produce toxins. To help you select the best mushrooms, we would like to share some secrets with you!
cac_buoc: Straw mushrooms: These are white or grayish-black; a tip is that grayish-black ones taste sweeter. Good mushrooms are those that haven't bloomed, have a light pleasant earthy scent, no unpleasant odor, no mushy spots, are firm and plump, and look clean and attractive. Be observant so you don't buy white mushrooms treated to look grayish-black!

Oyster mushrooms (abalone mushrooms): Fresh mushrooms have a pleasant aroma and come in white or purple varieties. Choosing oyster mushrooms correctly means they have a beautiful color and feel slightly spongy; preserved mushrooms feel soft and wet. The caps should not be torn, the whole cluster should grow evenly, and choosing medium-sized ones—not too big or too small—will taste better. The stems should be thick and the caps not yet fully expanded.

Dried shiitake mushrooms: The mushrooms should be uniform in size, with stems intact and not broken or crumbled. Choose those with a good color, no mold spots, and small stems. When soaked, they should have a fragrant aroma and firm flesh that is not soft or crumbly.

Button mushrooms: These have a "plump" shape compared to straw mushrooms. Choosing good ones is not hard; buy those with round caps, white color, short stems, and no sour or foul odor. Lightly press the cap; it should be firm yet spongy.

Enoki mushrooms: Choose medium-sized ones, not too long; about 10 to 12cm is best. Do not choose mushrooms with yellow or mushy bases, foul odors, or stems that feel too hollow when squeezed. The caps should be small and not fully bloomed.
For fresh mushrooms, you should buy just enough for one meal, as leftovers will not be as delicious when saved.

mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know how to choose delicious grapes or watermelon yet? If not, read the selection methods below! 1. Choosing grapes
cac_buoc: Choose large clusters with big, juicy berries; tasting one berry will tell you the flavor of the whole cluster. Alternatively, clusters with fewer, sparser berries are often sweeter. Grapes at peak ripeness have shiny black skins; the "Rose Honey" variety is purplish-black, the "Longan" variety is purplish-pink, the "Queen Bee" variety is purplish-black, and the "Cow Milk" variety is pale yellow.
2. Choosing watermelon

Choose fruits with a balanced shape, hard and smooth skin, and clear, bright patterns. The bottom should be yellowish, the top and bottom should be proportional, the navel should be deeply recessed, and the stem in the center of the navel should be gray. Lift the watermelon and tap it lightly; if it sounds dull and heavy and you feel a slight vibration inside, the melon is ripe. Lift the melon close to your ear and press the ends with your thumbs; if you hear a slight cracking sound, it is a good melon.

mon_an.mo_ta: How to choose and distinguish some types of food 1. Choosing rice
cac_buoc: Good rice has beautiful grains—round and slender, not necessarily very translucent. New-crop rice may not be translucent but is bright and white. Do not choose rice with many white chalky spots, as it will become very mushy when cooked and won't taste good.
Try chewing a few grains slowly; if you feel a sweet and fragrant taste, it is good rice.
2. Choosing sunflower seeds
The best type has large, firm, plump, uniform, and clean seeds.

Pick up a few seeds and drop them slowly; if they fall individually, they are dry. Peel one; if the kernel is white, the seeds are fresh and dry. Squeeze a handful and release; if more than 10% of the seeds are crushed, the quality is poor.
3. Choosing good milk powder

Good milk powder is pale yellow with a fresh milky scent and feels soft and smooth. There should be no residue when dissolved in boiling water and left to settle for 5 minutes. If dropped into room-temperature water, it must be stirred to dissolve; it will float and form clumps in hot water. When placed in the mouth, it feels smooth and sticky on the tongue and palate, dissolving very slowly.
4. Choosing tofu

Good tofu is milk-white, highly elastic, with a soft and smooth texture, not too mushy or too hard. Stacking two blocks should not cause them to stick, break, or crumble. When cut, the surface should be bright, free of impurities, and not coarse. It should have the characteristic aroma of tofu without any sour, acrid, or bitter smell.
5. Choosing and distinguishing canned food

Choose cans with lids and bases that are slightly concave rather than flat; they should make a clear, crisp sound when tapped. Discard cans that are crushed, deformed, or showing signs of rust. Check the embossed lettering on the lid, usually in three rows; the middle row indicates the production date. The shelf life is usually within two years.
Test for leaks by placing the can in water and pressing firmly to see if air bubbles rise. Alternatively, heat it to the boiling point; if the can is good, both ends will bulge out.

mon_an.mo_ta: Some ways to distinguish and choose delicious ingredients and beverages 1. Choosing good dried tea
cac_buoc: Heat the tea over an alcohol lamp; it should emit a rich, fragrant aroma.
Brew a little tea with boiling water, wait for it to steep thoroughly, then pour the liquid into two clean cups and observe closely:

Tea leaf veins: Clearly visible in a mesh pattern; the veins have small segments connecting them. They do not run straight to the edge but curve upward about 2/3 of the way, forming a wave shape. The tea leaves are thick with a straight main vein.
Serrated edges: Sparse at the edges, with no serrations near the stem.
Aroma: Characteristic, bold flavor, without any foul or oily smells.
Color: Fresh color, either bright green or dark green.
2. How to distinguish types of beer

Color and clarity: Beer with a bright, clear, pale yellow color is good. For bottled beers on the market, the shelf life is 40-60 days; "fresh" (draught) beer lasts only 7 days, and opened draught beer lasts only 3 days.

Beer foam: High-quality beer will immediately produce tiny bubbles that rise when poured, dissolving very slowly and staying on the surface for 4-5 minutes. Even after finishing the beer, foam should still cling to the glass.
Flavor: Different beers have different flavors. However, you must be able to perceive the rich, pure scent of hops, malt, and esters for it to be considered good beer.
3. Choosing white liquor

Drop a bit of liquor into your palm, press your hands together and rub; if it smells fresh and fragrant, it is the best quality. Next is the type with a slightly sweet smell. The poorest quality has a pungent, foul, and bitter smell.
Drop a bit of cooking oil into the liquor; if the oil spreads and sinks at a uniform rate, it is good liquor.

Check if white liquor has been mixed with industrial alcohol by mixing 1 part liquor with 2 parts water; if it does not turn cloudy, it is mixed with alcohol. If it turns cloudy, it is pure rice wine.

mon_an.mo_ta: Besides being a seasoning, vinegar has many other uses. Refer to this article on the Uses of Vinegar to learn many helpful kitchen hacks!
cac_buoc: Tips for the Uses of Vinegar:
Cleaning stains on ceramic cups and mugs: Swirl two tsp of vinegar around the inside of a dirty cup, then rinse with clean water; you will be pleased to have a cup that looks like new.

Removing coffee stains: This is another interesting use for vinegar. Simply fill the water reservoir of your coffee maker with a vinegar-water solution and run the machine as if brewing a batch of coffee. Doing this a few times will make your coffee maker shine and remove long-standing coffee stains.
Cleaning the dishwasher: Once a month, pour a cup of vinegar into an empty dishwasher and run a full cycle. The vinegar will help remove soap scum buildup inside the machine and on glass components.

Easily remove stubborn stickers or labels from any product. Brush a little vinegar onto the surface of the price tag or label, wait 5 minutes for it to soak in, then gently wipe away the loosened paper.
Vinegar can be used as a descaler for items that hold hard water, such as thermoses and kettles.
Deodorizing kitchen drains: Once a week, pour a cup of vinegar down the drain, let it sit for 30 minutes, then rinse with water.
Removing onion smell: Rub vinegar on your fingers before and after cutting onions.
Cleaning and disinfecting wooden cutting boards: Use undiluted vinegar to wash the board.
Removing fruit sap from hands: Rub vinegar on hands stained with sap.
Degreasing and deodorizing dishes: Mix 1 tbsp of vinegar with warm soapy water to wash dishes.
Cleaning teapots: Boil a mixture of vinegar and water, pour it into the teapot, and stubborn yellow stains will be removed.
Washing and deodorizing bottles: Use vinegar to wash bottles to remove lingering odors.
Cleaning food containers: Soak a piece of bread in vinegar, place it in the container, and leave it overnight.
Vinegar can replace lemon in recipes for certain vegetable salads. Use 1/2 tsp of vinegar to replace 1/2 tsp of lemon juice in many family recipes.
Cleaning the refrigerator: Wipe down the refrigerator with a mixture of 1/2 warm water and 1/2 vinegar.

mon_an.mo_ta: We have long used chili peppers as a common spice, but few know of their other wonderful benefits. Refer to this article on the Benefits of Chili Peppers to discover the amazing value they bring!
cac_buoc: Benefits of chili peppers:
Stimulates appetite and digestion: Chili can promote the secretion of digestive juices and increase appetite.
Fights the cold: Chili can warm the stomach. If you are suffering from vomiting, diarrhea, stomach pain, or other digestive symptoms, a little chili can be very effective.

Promotes blood circulation: Chili has certain medicinal properties that can help with "external sweating, clearing phlegm, and removing dampness." According to modern medicine, chili can promote blood circulation and improve frostbite, coldness, and headaches.

Beautifies the skin: Women might be surprised to learn that chili can beautify the skin. Chili can promote hormone secretion and improve skin conditions. Many people think spicy food causes breakouts and worsens skin, but in reality, the problem does not stem from the chili itself.
Lowers dietary lipids: Capsaicin in chili can speed up the breakdown of fat and is rich in fiber.
Strong anti-inflammatory: Chili has powerful anti-inflammatory effects. American research shows that capsaicin can reduce neurotransmitter pain signals, helping people feel less pain.
Cancer-fighting potential: A miraculous use of chili peppers. Capsaicin can accelerate the death of cancer cells without damaging healthy cells.
Protects the heart: Regularly eating chili effectively can delay the development of atherosclerosis.
Lowers blood pressure: Recent British experiments found that capsaicin may play a role in reducing blood pressure, though the exact mechanism remains unclear.
Beneficial for diabetes: Capsaicin may play a role in alleviating some symptoms of type 1 diabetes.

Although chili is very good, due to its strong spiciness, you should not consume too much just for the benefits. You can refer to the article "Using Chili Correctly" to learn how to store and use it, and who should limit their chili intake!

mon_an.mo_ta: Benefits of Fresh Milk – Besides common uses like drinking or mixing with coffee and tea for delicious milk tea, fresh milk has many other wonderful uses. These tips will bring you 8 benefits of fresh milk for homemakers.
cac_buoc: Fresh milk has long been an indispensable drink for the elderly and children because it contains a lot of calcium, which is good for health and increases the body's resistance. Not only that, fresh milk also has many other uses that we may not know about. This article will introduce you to 8 very useful benefits of fresh milk:
Makeup removal

For girls with sensitive skin, fresh milk is very effective for removing makeup. However, milk can only remove regular makeup; it is not very effective against waterproof types. Apply a little warm milk to the face to remove makeup, then wash with a facial cleanser; your skin will be moisturized and smooth.
Soothes sunburned skin

Mix milk powder with just enough water to create a thick paste, then gently apply it to the sunburned skin. The sunburn will soothe significantly. Anyone who has just returned from the beach should try this method to restore their skin. Milk has cooling properties, so it is effective at cooling and smoothing the skin after a sunburn while also nourishing it.
Hand skin care

For those with rough hands who want them to become smooth and white, you can mix fresh milk with oatmeal into a paste. Apply it to your hands, massage for 15 minutes, then rinse clean; your skin will improve greatly. This method can be used for the whole body, but it is quite expensive, so consider it before use.
Defrosting fish

Frozen fish is not always fresh and delicious, especially those kept in the family freezer for a long time, which often pick up other food odors. To fix this, you can defrost fish in fresh milk. The milk will help defrost the fish and also enhance its flavor.
For the tips below, you can use leftover milk or milk that has just expired. Since fresh milk is expensive, using leftover or recently expired milk saves money and avoids food waste.
Removing stains from clothes

Ballpoint pen ink stains on shirts can be very annoying, especially for students. To completely remove the ink, apply a little milk to the stain and leave it overnight. Wash it normally the next morning, and the ink stain will be gone.
Cleaning leather goods

If your leather items have become worn or dirty, use a soft cotton cloth dipped in milk to gently rub the surface to refresh them. For items like leather wallets or leather clothing, you should wipe them once more with clean water to avoid attracting ants or insects.
Polishing silver

Add 2 tsp of vinegar to a small glass of fresh milk to create a solution for cleaning silver items. Soak the silver in this mixture for 15 to 20 minutes, then rinse with water and wipe clean; the silver will shine like new. This method is quite fast, convenient, and saves a trip to the shop.
Repairing cracks in porcelain

When your ceramics have many cracks, pour milk into the ceramic item and place it in a heat-resistant pot on the stove. Heat until the milk boils, then turn the heat to low. The entire heating process takes about 45 minutes. The protein in the milk can bond with the clay in the ceramic to fill the cracks. Your ceramics will become beautiful and durable as new.

mon_an.ten: Special Benefits of Pumpkin You Might Not Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Among all fruits, pumpkin is the champion in iron content and is rich in vitamins, mineral salts, and organic acids. The ascorbic acid in pumpkin helps prevent colds, while B vitamins help fight fatigue, irritability, and insomnia, and strengthen hair and nails. Vitamin A in pumpkin helps improve vision. The flesh and seeds contain plenty of vitamin E – a natural antioxidant that strengthens the immune system, prevents early wrinkles, protects skin from aging, and improves cardiovascular function. Pumpkin is truly a useful food for homemakers; let's explore its health benefits!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Good for bones and eyes

Pumpkin is rich in carotene (which the body converts into Vitamin A), helping to maintain physical strength and eye development. Furthermore, pumpkin contains a large amount of minerals like calcium, sodium, and potassium. Especially for the elderly and those with blood pressure issues, these substances help prevent osteoporosis and hypertension. It also contains magnesium, phosphorus, iron, copper, manganese, chromium, and many other elements that help bone development.
Step 2: Aids in weight loss
Pumpkin is a high-fiber food with low calorie and fat content. It is an ideal food for those who want to lose weight or for those who are overweight or obese.
Step 3: Beneficial for cardiovascular health
Physterols and omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids are substances that reduce bad cholesterol and prevent cardiovascular disease and hypertension. Pumpkin seeds are particularly rich in these substances.
Step 4: Good for brain development

Pumpkin contains a lot of glutamic acid, which is essential for brain activity. This substance plays an important role in assisting metabolic reactions in nerve cells and the brain. Especially for pregnant women, the substances in pumpkin seeds and flowers not only help the fetus develop brain cells and increase vitality but also help prevent edema, hypertension, and other pregnancy complications, as well as preventing postpartum hemorrhagic fever.
Step 5: Strengthens the immune system
Pumpkin is very rich in vitamin C, which enhances the body's resistance and helps the immune system become healthy. With a strong immune system, our bodies can fight off harmful bacteria and viruses.
Step 6: Prevents diabetes

For diabetic patients, pumpkin is truly a good food. Pumpkin helps lower blood sugar levels, thus preventing diabetes. Furthermore, it helps inhibit the progression of the disease into a chronic state for those who already have diabetes.
Step 7: Deworming

Eating raw pumpkin or roasted pumpkin seeds in combination with deworming medication will yield high deworming efficiency. Especially for young children, eating pumpkin regularly also helps prevent intestinal parasites.
Enhances skin beauty
The carotenoids in pumpkin slow down the skin aging process, helping the skin stay bright, acne-free, and with fewer wrinkles.
Step 8: Prevents cancer
Yellow foods like pumpkin, carrots, and sweet potatoes contain many antioxidants and beta-carotene, which help prevent various types of cancer.
Wishing you many useful insights.

mon_an.ten: Beauty Benefits of Lemon Peel You Didn't Know!
mon_an.mo_ta: The beauty benefits of lemon peel are something not everyone knows or pays attention to. Therefore, just save your lemon peels and try these simple beauty methods; you will see the surprising results they bring!
cac_buoc: Weight loss

Lemon peel contains a lot of soluble fiber, which provides a feeling of fullness, controls fat, and cholesterol levels. Therefore, you can drink lemon peel water to limit cravings and control weight gain.

How to do it: Shred fresh lemon peels and boil them in water with a few dried jujubes. Keep the lid tightly closed; opening it will let the beneficial substances evaporate. Boil for about 10 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Lightens age spots
Using lemon peel to lighten age spots is quite effective but requires patience over a long period for the spots to fade.
How to do it: Use a piece of lemon peel to rub on the area with age spots, leave it for an hour, then rinse clean. Do not rub too hard as it may damage the skin.
Softens dry elbows
The skin on the elbows often lacks moisture and becomes dry, especially in winter. If you use lemon peel, you will soon regain the original softness of the skin.
How to do it: Place your elbow into the hollow of a lemon peel and rotate gently, pressing slightly so the juice soaks into the skin. Do this for 10 minutes, then wash and dry your hands.
Moisturizes and beautifies skin

Lemon peel is a source of vitamin C and citric acid that helps clean blood vessels and remove impurities from skin cells. Lemon peel combined with olive oil and sugar not only promotes healthy skin but also makes it visibly softer.
How to do it: Mix half a cup of sugar with finely chopped lemon peel and olive oil. Wet your body, then rub the mixture onto the skin while massaging for 10-15 minutes, then rinse with plain water.
Protects teeth

Lemon peel is rich in citric acid, which has antioxidant effects and fights gum problems if vitamin C is deficient. Additionally, the vitamin C in lemon peel cleans teeth, reducing bleeding gums and gingivitis. Lemon peel is also an ingredient to effectively remove tartar due to its cleaning and oral hygiene capabilities.
How to do it: Finely chop lemon peel and mix with 1 tsp baking soda, 1 tsp salt, and 1 tsp water to create a thick paste.
To clean your mouth and remove tartar, rinse your mouth with water mixed with this paste or use it in place of toothpaste.
Treats dandruff and beautifies hair
Lemon peel will help your hair stay healthy, smooth, and dandruff-free. The scent of lemon peel on the hair is also wonderful, isn't it?
How to do it: Simply chop or crush lemon peel, boil it with a little water, then apply this mixture to your hair and let it sit for about 15 minutes before shampooing.

The beauty benefits of lemon peel are something not everyone knows or pays attention to. Therefore, just save your lemon peels and try these simple beauty methods; you will see the surprising results they bring!

mon_an.ten: Amazing Benefits of Cabbage You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Cabbage is a familiar vegetable to many Vietnamese families. Cabbage has many benefits that you may not know about. Today, we will help you better understand the effects of this food!
cac_buoc: Aids in red blood cell formation

Iron is a component that promotes the formation of red blood cells, thereby avoiding symptoms of anemia. Consuming cabbage combined with orange or grapefruit juice can optimize the absorption of iron from the cabbage.
Prevents cancer

Cabbage and related vegetables contain a substance that can fight cancer cells in the body. They stimulate enzymes to inhibit tumor growth rates. Research in China also indicates that women who consume a certain amount of vegetables like cabbage and broccoli reduce their risk of breast cancer symptoms.
Good for cardiovascular health

What else is cabbage good for? The potassium content in cabbage is very high, which is good for heart health and maintains healthy blood circulation while avoiding blockages in the blood vessels to the heart.
Potassium is also a good compound for reducing symptoms of hypertension. The high potassium content in cabbage makes it one of the recommended foods for hypertension.
Boosts immunity

Not only fruits like oranges, grapes, or apples are high in vitamin C; cabbage also contains a lot of this vitamin, so a benefit of cabbage is making the immune system grow stronger. Vitamin C is also very good for skin care.
Reduces body weight

Cabbage is one of the top recommended vegetables for those who want to lose weight naturally and healthily. Cabbage contains many useful components of vitamins, minerals, and other nutrients. You can eat cabbage in large quantities because it is high in fiber and low in calories; it will not increase your weight.
Detoxifies the body
Due to its high vitamin C and sulfur content, cabbage can help remove toxins (free radicals). Free radicals are one of the main causes of arthritis, skin diseases, rheumatism, and gout.
Good for the brain

Cabbage or cruciferous vegetables are a source of vitamin K and anthocyanins that can help with mental health and brain concentration. These nutrients can also prevent nerve damage, helping to prevent Alzheimer's disease and dementia. Therefore, cabbage is very beneficial for your brain health.
Good for the eyes

Cabbage is a rich source of vegetables containing beta-carotene. Most people, especially the elderly, who regularly eat cabbage have the ability to prevent macular degeneration and can improve eye health as well as prevent cataracts. According to some studies, beta-carotene can also reduce prostate cancer.
Anti-inflammatory

Cabbage has anti-inflammatory properties and is a major source of glutamine. Glutamine is a powerful anti-inflammatory agent, so eating cabbage can reduce the effects of conditions such as inflammation, irritation, allergies, joint pain, fever, and skin disorders.
Bone health
Cabbage contains minerals like calcium, magnesium, and potassium. These minerals are known for their ability to maintain bone health.
Managing headaches

Using cabbage leaves as a warm compress can help relieve headaches. Furthermore, crushing cabbage leaves and placing them on the forehead can also reduce headache pain. For chronic headaches, drinking cabbage juice (25-50ml) can help eliminate the pain.
Laxative effect
The benefits of cabbage are similar to eating other vegetables; cabbage is a vegetable that aids in easy bowel movements due to its high fiber content.
Good for fetal development
Folic acid is very important for the development of the fetus; therefore, giving pregnant women cabbage helps support their nutritional need for folic acid.

mon_an.ten: Amazing Benefits of Lemons You Might Not Know
mon_an.mo_ta: In daily life, lemons are a widely used citrus fruit, especially during hot summer days. Beyond being a refreshing drink, a food additive, or a medicinal ingredient, lemons offer many surprising benefits in daily life that you may not be aware of. Below are some useful lemon tips for everyday life that everyone, especially homemakers, should know.
cac_buoc: Squeeze a few drops of lemon into milk to aid digestion, which is particularly helpful for children with weak digestive systems.
People suffering from constipation should drink lemon water daily to promote bowel movements and strengthen the body's immune system.
2. Feverish conditions: Drink plenty of lemon water

Most feverish conditions cause a loss of appetite, leading to weakness and fatigue. Drink 2-3 glasses of lemon water with sugar daily to provide Vitamin C and glucose, which helps cool the body and speed up recovery.
3. Salted lemon water
This drink helps quench thirst, eliminate phlegm, and soothe the throat. It is especially suitable for heavy laborers who lose many vitamins and minerals through sweat.
4. Use as an antiseptic
Lemon acts as an antiseptic for wounds caused by insects or reptile bites. For red eyes, applying one drop of thoroughly filtered lemon juice can also be very effective.
5. Fresh lemon peel
Cooking lemon peel with duck meat helps counteract the "cold" nature of the meat.
6. Cleaning a baby's tongue
Mix a little salt with lemon juice and use a clean cotton cloth dipped in this solution to clean a baby's tongue effectively.
7. Beauty benefits
Mix lemon juice into your shampoo for shiny, soft hair and to remove dandruff;
For oily skin: Mix a few drops of lemon juice with 2 tablespoons of orange juice, apply to the face for 10 minutes, and rinse off; the oiliness will gradually decrease;
For wrinkled skin: Mix honey with a few drops of lemon juice, apply to the face for 15 minutes, then rinse with cold water.
Exfoliation: A mixture of lemon juice and sugar or honey is a very effective and convenient exfoliant for the face and body;
Treating underarm odor: Apply lemon juice to the underarms after bathing, leave for 15 minutes, then rinse with warm water; the odor will disappear after a short period of use.
8. Removing fishy smells
Use lemon juice to wash fish to make it cleaner, keep it fresh longer, and eliminate fishy odors.
9. Cleaning vegetable sap from hands
When preparing water spinach, sweet potato greens, or slicing banana blossoms, use lemon juice to quickly wash away any sticky sap from your hands.
10. Removing soap residue
If your hands feel slippery due to excess alkali from soap, wash them with lemon juice to neutralize the alkali and remove the residue instantly.
11. Cleaning moldy nylon items
If nylon items become moldy, cut a lemon in half and rub it over the moldy spots until clean, then wipe with a dry cloth.
12. Renewing old leather shoes
When leather shoes become old and stiff, apply lemon juice to the leather, wipe dry, and then apply shoe polish.
13. Cleaning scorched irons
If an iron becomes yellowed from being too hot, turn it on until warm, unplug it, rub half a lemon over the yellowed area, and wipe clean with a dry cloth to restore its brightness.
14. Deodorizing the fridge and pantry
Place half a lemon in a corner of the refrigerator or pantry to effectively eliminate odors.
These are the many useful benefits of lemons. Try them out to see the results for yourself. They are very effective. Wishing you many more useful insights!

mon_an.ten: Amazing Benefits of Garlic Salt You Might Not Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Garlic salt contains most of the culinary properties and medicinal benefits of its constituent ingredients. Below are some health benefits of garlic salt that you should know.
cac_buoc: Garlic salt is a seasoned salt made by mixing dried garlic (preferably in powder form) and table salt. It is typically made with a ratio of 3 parts salt to 1 part garlic powder.
Lowering cholesterol

Garlic powder has many health benefits. It is particularly effective in helping to lower LDL (bad cholesterol) and increase HDL (good cholesterol) in the body. High amounts of trans fats and other saturated fats in the diet can increase your cholesterol levels.
This can lead to diseases such as atherosclerosis. The properties of garlic powder in garlic salt can help reduce cholesterol.
Lowering blood sugar

Garlic powder helps naturally increase insulin levels in the blood. This makes it an ideal remedy for people with high blood sugar and can help manage diabetes, making garlic salt beneficial for diabetic patients.
Lowering blood pressure
Garlic salt, like other forms of garlic, can help lower blood pressure. Garlic contains compounds that dilate blood vessels, which helps ease blood flow and subsequently reduces blood pressure.
Consuming garlic salt helps control blood pressure and prevent disease. A recent study showed that using garlic capsules helps reduce blood pressure in hypertensive patients.
Anti-inflammatory

Garlic salt is an effective anti-inflammatory agent. Therefore, it is widely used to treat inflammatory disorders such as bronchitis and rhinitis. The sulfur-containing compounds in garlic provide these anti-inflammatory properties.
Rich in minerals and vitamins

Garlic powder (used to make garlic salt) is quite nutritious, rich in essential vitamins and minerals. Garlic is one of the healthiest foods containing most nutrients. Despite the processing, garlic powder retains most of the nutrients found in fresh garlic.
Anti-cancer

Garlic is full of antioxidants that help remove free radicals from the body. Cancer cells often rely on free radicals to grow tumors. Using garlic salt can help increase the amount of antioxidants in the body, thereby helping to prevent cancer and inhibit cancer cells.
If you or your family have a history of cancer, consider using garlic salt along with other garlic products. This will help your body fight against cancer growth.
Improving bone health
Garlic powder or garlic salt helps overcome estrogen deficiency. Estrogen deficiency is a factor that contributes directly to bone loss; therefore, garlic powder helps strengthen bone health.
Dried garlic extract (powder or minced garlic) reduces estrogen deficiency. Foods like garlic and onions have also been proven beneficial for osteoarthritis.
Stimulant
Garlic powder, like garlic, has stimulant properties that help promote and stimulate various processes. It contains allium, which is a well-known stimulant.
Treating Scurvy
Garlic salt contains a significant amount of Vitamin C, which can help treat vitamin deficiencies like Scurvy and protect you from many other diseases.
Improving digestion

Garlic salt, specifically the garlic powder component, is quite rich in fiber. This fiber is an important agent that helps waste move easily along the digestive tract. Fiber helps reduce certain conditions, such as constipation.

mon_an.ten: Eliminating Unpleasant Odors in Your Refrigerator
mon_an.mo_ta: Eliminate unpleasant odors in your refrigerator to keep it fresh and prevent food from absorbing unwanted smells. This article introduces several very useful tips. Kitchen appliances always need deodorizing as they are often permeated by various food smells, especially the refrigerator. This can affect your cooking process when food flavors become mixed.
cac_buoc: As the saying goes, "Prevention is better than a cure." These tips will show you how to prevent and eliminate unpleasant odors in your refrigerator:
Preventing unpleasant odors in the refrigerator
Drain vegetables thoroughly before putting them in the fridge; otherwise, they will easily rot and cause unpleasant smells.

Regularly check the food stored in the refrigerator. Any food that has been kept for too long or shows signs of spoiling should be removed immediately to avoid affecting other foods and causing odors.
Both cooked and raw food must be kept in airtight containers or tied in plastic bags. If possible, use vacuum-sealed bags.
Eliminating existing odors in the refrigerator
If your refrigerator already has an odor, do not hesitate to eliminate it using these 5 tips:
Use a small amount of crushed charcoal, place it in a clean cloth bag, and put it in the refrigerator. Note that the charcoal bag should be placed away from food.
Use fresh orange or tangerine peels to effectively remove fishy smells. Replace with new peels once they dry out for the best results.
Use breadcrumbs, coffee grounds, or a slice of pineapple to absorb odors in the refrigerator.
Place lotus tea dregs in a dry cloth bag; this will not only remove odors but also leave a fresh scent in the fridge.

Fold a clean cotton towel neatly and place it on the top shelf of the refrigerator. The small pores in the fabric can absorb odors. After some time, remove the towel, wash it with warm water, dry it, and it can be reused.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Fatty Meat Less Greasy
mon_an.mo_ta: Fatty meat, with its rich and tender layers of fat, always brings a special flavor and delight to food lovers. However, the cloying sensation from excessive fat can make many people hesitate to enjoy it. Save these instructions on how to make fatty meat less greasy! Combine fatty meat with raw greens and refreshing acidic seasonings to create balance and harmony for the dish. These simple changes help you enjoy fatty meat without the heavy, greasy feeling.
cac_buoc: There are many ways to make fatty meat less greasy; here are a few simple but easy-to-implement tips.

Soak fatty meat in salt water: Before processing, soak the fatty meat in salt water for about 30 minutes. Salt helps absorb some of the excess fat in the meat, reducing the greasy feeling when eating.

Use low heat: When cooking fatty meat, use low heat. This helps the fat melt gradually and render out, preventing a heavy, greasy sensation. Wait until the meat is cooked through without overcooking to prevent the fat from becoming too oily.

Apply the pan-searing method: Searing fatty meat in a pan is a great way to remove excess fat. Before searing, place the pan over low heat for a short time to melt any fat in the pan. Then, place the fatty meat in the pan and sear until the fat renders out and the meat is evenly cooked.

Combine with raw greens and acidic seasonings: To reduce the greasy feeling, pair fatty meat with raw greens such as lettuce, watercress, or other herbs. Raw vegetables create balance and cut through the fat. You can also add acidic seasonings like fish sauce, lemon, or vinegar to enhance the flavor and balance the richness.
Notes when preparing fatty meat to be less greasy
Choose fresh fatty meat: Select fresh meat that has no foul odor or signs of spoilage. Choose meat from reliable sources to ensure quality.
Hygiene and preparation: Before processing, wash the fatty meat under cold water to remove dirt or impurities. Also, clean the workspace, knives, and tools used to avoid bacterial contamination.

Control the temperature: When processing fatty meat, ensure you control the cooking or grilling temperature so the meat cooks evenly without melting the fat too quickly. This helps maintain the deliciousness and tenderness of the meat.

Processing techniques: Apply techniques such as grilling, steaming, stir-frying, or stewing. To save on fat, you can remove excess fat before cooking by trimming it off or heating it over low heat to render it.

Use seasonings and side dishes: Fatty meat is often combined with seasonings like pepper, onions, garlic, BBQ spices, or regional spices to enhance the flavor. You can also pair it with raw greens, chutney, or a refreshing sour sauce to reduce the greasy feeling.

Proper storage: If there is leftover fatty meat, store it in the refrigerator in an airtight container to avoid contamination and air exposure. Use it quickly to ensure the quality and freshness of the meat.

mon_an.ten: How to Prepare a Complete Offering for the Kitchen Gods
mon_an.mo_ta: Every year on the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, families busily prepare offerings for the Kitchen Gods (Ông Táo), but not everyone knows how to arrange a truly complete ceremony. Let's see what the experts have to say!
cac_buoc: According to Vietnamese tradition, the Kitchen Gods are the deities who stay throughout the year to oversee all affairs in the household. The set of deities consists of three members: two male gods and one female goddess. Every year on the 23rd of the 12th lunar month, they ride carps to heaven to report the family's good and bad deeds to the Jade Emperor for fair rewards or punishments. Therefore, this day is also known as the Kitchen Gods' Festival.

To "please" these important deities, people usually prepare a farewell offering tray to send them to heaven, featuring sweets or traditional dishes along with votive paper money, boots, hats, and paper carps.
According to feng shui expert Pham Cuong, a complete offering ceremony for the Kitchen Gods includes the ceremonial hats, a savory food tray, and live carps (for ceremonial release).
The offerings usually consist of the Kitchen God hats, a savory feast, and carps to be released into the wild.
According to expert Pham Cuong, the first essential items are the three hats. Two of these are for the male gods (with "dragonfly wings" ornaments) and one is for the goddess (without wings).
To simplify, some people only offer a symbolic set of one hat (with wings) accompanied by a paper robe and a pair of boots.
The colors of the hats, robes, and boots change annually according to the Five Elements. These items (hats, robes, boots, and paper gold bars) are burned after the ceremony on the 23rd day.

In addition to the hats, each family typically prepares a savory tray, sweets, betel leaves and areca nuts, wine, incense, candles, fresh flowers, a plate of five fruits, votive money, and 3 live carps. Specific details are provided below.

A traditional Vietnamese offering tray for the Kitchen Gods includes many items. Expert Pham Cuong states: "A complete tray usually features: 1 plate of rice, 1 plate of salt, 500g boiled pork shoulder, 1 bowl of meatball soup (canh mọc), 1 plate of stir-fried mixed vegetables, 1 plate of giò (Vietnamese ham), 1 fried carp (or live carp), 1 plate of xôi gấc (red sticky rice), 1 plate of chè kho (mung bean pudding), 1 fruit platter, 1 pot of lotus tea, 3 cups of wine, 1 pomelo, 1 areca nut, betel leaves, 1 small vase of peach blossoms, 1 vase of chrysanthemums, and a set of votive paper money and gold."

However, nowadays, the offering tray has been simplified and does not strictly require every single traditional dish. The tray depends on the family's circumstances and tastes; the most important thing is the sincerity of the heart.

Besides the votive paper, depending on the household, people may prepare a savory tray (with chicken sticky rice, boiled pork hock, mushroom or bamboo shoot dishes...) or a vegetarian offering (with betel, flowers, fruit, and votive paper) to see off the Kitchen Gods.

mon_an.ten: Don't Throw Away Eggshells: Their Miraculous Uses
mon_an.mo_ta: Eggshells might seem useless, but they are incredibly beneficial. Read this article to discover their miraculous effects!
cac_buoc: The calcium source in eggshells is among the best, equivalent to refined calcium carbonate, and can be used for health treatments. An Argentine study published in the International Journal of Food Sciences and Nutrition found that one chicken eggshell contains about two grams of calcium, nearly double the average daily requirement for an adult. Researchers also found that homemade eggshell powder can be added to dishes like bread, pizza, or spaghetti to supplement calcium without changing the flavor.
Additionally, eggshells contain many essential minerals such as iron, manganese, phosphorus, and zinc... so we should not waste them after cooking.
How to make eggshell powder
Preparation:
Eggshells (can be from boiled or raw eggs)
Pot
Blender or coffee grinder
Sterilized glass jar (boiled in water and dried)
Instructions:
Boil or eat eggs (fried, poached, etc.) as usual and collect the shells. Once you have 10-15 shells, wash the outside thoroughly but do not remove the inner membrane, as it also contains nutrients.
Place the shells in a pot of water and boil for 10 minutes to clean them and eliminate any potential pathogens. Drain well.

Place the shells on a glass sheet or a stainless steel baking tray and let them air dry overnight. The next day, bake the tray of shells at 200°F (about 93°C) for about 10 minutes until completely dry.
Remove from the oven. Place a few shells at a time into a blender and pulse into small bits. Then, grind until they turn into a fine powder.
Store the eggshell powder in the sterilized glass jar in a cool, dry place, away from high heat and humidity.
How to use

One teaspoon of eggshell powder contains about 800-1000mg of calcium. Use this calcium powder by mixing it with a small amount of water and adding it to daily meals. You can consume 3/4 to 1 teaspoon per day, divided into 3 portions with meals. Do not exceed 1 teaspoon per day as it may affect digestion.

Besides using it as a supplement, this powder is also used in remedies for stomach ulcers, mouth sores, boosting the immune system, blood purification, bad breath, thyroid issues, and some gynecological conditions.

mon_an.ten: Benefits and Proper Use of Roselle Flowers
mon_an.mo_ta: Roselle, scientifically known as Hibiscus sabdariffa L., belongs to the Malvaceae family. Originating from West Africa, it is grown for its shoots and calyces to be used as a sour vegetable or medicine, and was introduced to our country in the 1970s. It is a small shrub, 1 – 1.5m tall, with a stiff stem and many branches. Flowers grow solitary in leaf axils with short stalks. The corolla is yellow-pink, purple, or sometimes white. The fruit is an ovoid capsule with coarse hairs, surrounded by a bright red persistent calyx. The calyx is succulent, deep red, and very sour (like vinegar). Roselle can be processed into syrup, jam, or used as a flavoring for ice cream and pastries. This flower has effects such as cooling the liver, acting as a diuretic, boosting resistance, and treating coughs and sore throats. However, it does have limitations. Refer to this article to use Roselle correctly without affecting your family's health!
cac_buoc: Benefits of Roselle:

Rich in vitamins and minerals: The leaves and red calyces are rich in acids and proteins. The dried fruit contains calcium oxalate, gossypetin, anthocyanin (which has antibiotic effects), and Vitamin C. The seeds contain 7.6% water, 22.3% oil, 24% protein, 13.5% fiber, and 7% minerals. Roselle seed oil is similar to cottonseed oil, having antifungal properties and treating skin diseases. The oil contains vitamins and unsaturated fats, which are good for the elderly and those on a diet.
Good for people with high blood pressure: Scientists have proven that consuming Roselle at a rate of 100 - 200mg/kg/day regularly can reduce blood glucose levels by 60 – 65%.

Helps reduce liver enzymes: Drinking Roselle tea or syrup daily helps overcome metabolic disorders and other liver-related diseases. Even if you don't have liver disease, Roselle can help protect your liver.

Boosts the immune system: Thanks to its very high Vitamin C content and the synergy of organic acids, Roselle has antibacterial effects and helps the body increase resistance and immune system activity. Regular daily consumption can reduce the risk of flu and other common viral or bacterial infections.

Anti-obesity: Drinking a cup of Roselle tea after a meal reduces the absorption of sugar and starch, thereby contributing to weight loss and fighting dangerous obesity. Additionally, Roselle contains high fiber content, which is useful for treating constipation and helping the body eliminate toxins through the digestive system easily. This also aids in weight loss.
Notes when using Roselle:
The maximum dosage should not exceed 2g of dried calyces per 60kg of body weight, as excessive use can be toxic.
Do not process at very high temperatures for a long time because the main active ingredient, anthocyanin, is easily decomposed by high heat.
You should divide the tea into several small portions throughout the day rather than consuming a large amount at once.

Pregnant and breastfeeding women should not use it: While there is no definitive evidence of adverse effects on human pregnancy, experiments on pregnant rats and for 21 days postpartum showed that Roselle caused pregnancy malnutrition, leading to increased body weight and delayed puberty in the offspring (according to a 2008 study by Lyare et al.).

Be cautious when using with other medications: Roselle tea can reduce serum diclofenac levels by 62% and decrease the urinary excretion rate of diclofenac. Similar results were found with acetaminophen (paracetamol).
Although Roselle has many benefits, its effectiveness depends on age, health status, and chronic conditions of the user.
Choose products with clear origins, read labels carefully, and consult a doctor, especially if you are taking medication for acute or chronic illnesses.

mon_an.mo_ta: If you need to defrost frozen meat, pay attention to these collected tips
cac_buoc: Frozen meat (all types) should not be thawed by pouring hot water over it, as this causes the meat to lose its juices, promotes bacterial growth, and depletes nutrients.

The correct way to thaw is to let the meat defrost naturally in the air at around 15°C or use tap water at that temperature to spray evenly over the meat. This is the standard method.
