To speed up the process, you can place frozen pork, chicken, or fish in lightly salted water; it will thaw faster and the meat will stay fresher without losing nutrients.
If available, using the defrost function of a microwave is also very convenient, fast, and safe.

mon_an.ten: Essential Foods and Drinks for Christmas
mon_an.mo_ta: With Christmas approaching, you've likely heard of these familiar foods and drinks. Let's find out what they are!
cac_buoc: Turkey
Roast turkey has long been an indispensable dish for Thanksgiving and Christmas. The flavor of roast turkey is both unique and nutritious.

The use of turkey for Christmas began with the British. Later, in 1863, when US President Lincoln declared Thanksgiving a national holiday, turkey began to be used as the main dish for Thanksgiving. When Thanksgiving ends and the winter holidays begin, turkey remains the staple dish throughout winter, and naturally, it became an essential Christmas Eve dish since then.
Turkey is usually stuffed with various spices and served with sauces, pudding, and other dishes on Christmas Eve.
Drinks
Apple Cider

Apple cider is a beverage made from fermented apples, with alcohol content ranging from very low to none. Therefore, it is very popular at family parties with both adults and children, such as Christmas.
Eggnog

Eggnog is a cocktail made with cream, milk, sugar, and egg yolks, often combined with cinnamon or nutmeg, and spiked with brandy, rum, or whiskey. If the alcohol is removed, eggnog becomes a rich, nutritious egg cream suitable for both children and adults. This is why it is a very popular drink in Western Christmas celebrations.
Sweets and Candies

During Christmas, one can get lost in a maze of sweets with diverse colors, shapes, and historical stories. These include Yule logs, gingerbread, pumpkin pie, candy canes, marshmallows, fruitcake, pastries... but all share a cozy Christmas vibe and represent dreams of a prosperous, happy life. Some types are rarely missing on this day.
Yule Log (Bánh khúc cây)
Many believe this cake was born around 1875 when a French baker had the idea of making a log-shaped cake for Christmas Eve.
The Yule log is a traditional French-style cake used during the Christmas season. Modern Yule logs are decorated with powdered sugar like snow, fresh fruit, and mushrooms made of buttercream.

The Yule log originates from the custom where, on Christmas Eve, people would cut a large log and bring it into the house for a ceremony. The log was placed in the hearth, and the head of the household performed a wine offering by sprinkling oil, salt, and warm wine on the log while reciting prayers.

Legend has it that the charcoal from this burnt log would protect the house from natural disasters and evil spirits. The choice of wood, the way the log was burned, and the duration of the ritual varied by region.
Gingerbread (Bánh quy gừng)

Like the Yule log, gingerbread is a treat that is rarely absent from Christmas. These delicious, crunchy cookies in various shapes and colors are made to be enjoyed and served to guests. The warm flavor of the ginger seems to chase away the Christmas cold.
With unique creativity, gingerbread is made into many beautiful shapes like people, snowmen, reindeer, snowflakes, or gingerbread houses... Each has a unique look and is loved by many.
Candy Canes (Kẹo gậy)

It is said that the candy cane carries a very special meaning. When turned upside down, the candy forms the letter J, the first letter of the name Jesus. The colors also have their own meaning. The pure white represents the Virgin Mary and the sinless purity of Christ.
Thus, the Christmas candy cane appears as a sacred symbol, helping people aim for a holier and better life.

mon_an.ten: Simple Tips to Keep Your Home Clean
mon_an.mo_ta: Keeping your home clean with simple tips using available kitchen items will help you have a sparkling, fragrant house. During cooking, stains and dirt on long-used items are unavoidable, so these simple tips will help you keep everything clean.
cac_buoc: Simple tips to keep your home clean
An orange peel rubbed with salt has high cleaning properties and can remove coffee and tea stains.
Aluminum foil is the fastest way to scrub stains off glass trays.
Irons used for a long time will have dirt on the soleplate; to remove this, use the tip of ironing over a little clean salt.
Baking soda has many uses in keeping the house clean with simple tips.
Another wonderful use for baking soda.
Computer keyboards are places where a lot of hard-to-clean dust accumulates; using adhesive tape will save you a lot of time.

mon_an.ten: Simple Sweet and Sour Pork Ear Salad
mon_an.mo_ta: Summer has just begun, making heavy foods lose their appeal at the dinner table. The heat can dampen the family's appetite. Don't worry, this recipe will solve that. Today we bring you a simple sweet and sour pork ear salad that everyone will love. The crunchiness of the pork ear, the sourness of the mango, and the coolness of the cucumber make for a perfect combination.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, garlic, chili, vinegar, lime, sugar, dried shallots - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Peel the green mango and carrot, then shred them into small strips.
Step 2:
Wash the pork ear thoroughly with salt water, especially the crevices where a lot of dirt can hide.

Place the pork ear in a pot, cover with water, add a pinch of salt, and boil until cooked. After about 20-30 minutes, pierce it with a chopstick; if it goes through easily, it's done. Remove and rinse with cold water. Once cooled, slice into bite-sized strips.
Step 3:
Pick and wash various herbs, then chop them finely.
Step 4:
Peel the garlic and remove seeds from the chili, then mince them finely.

Prepare the dressing: Dissolve 2 tbsp of premium fish sauce and 2 tbsp of sugar, then add the minced garlic and chili. Squeeze in some lime juice and adjust the seasoning to achieve a balanced sweet and sour taste.
Step 5:
Place the prepared ingredients: cucumber, mango, carrot, and pork ear into a bowl. Slowly pour the dressing over them and toss well.
Just before serving, add the herbs and roasted peanuts, then mix again.
Step 6:
Serve the pork ear salad on a plate and enjoy.
Enjoy your meal with this delicious sweet and sour pork ear salad!

mon_an.mo_ta: Onions and these useful tips will help you handle many kitchen tasks such as preventing mold, repelling flies and mosquitoes, and enhancing the flavor of steamed fish... These tips help homemakers prepare meals more simply and economically.
cac_buoc: This article on onions and useful tips will provide you with some helpful hacks for your family kitchen.
Preventing mold
Adding 2 - 3 slices of onion to a bottle of soy sauce or vinegar with pickled garlic and chili will effectively prevent mold.
Removing burnt smell

If you accidentally burn the rice, while it is still hot, quickly cut onion slices and place them inside the pot, then close the lid tightly. This way, the top layer of rice will not smell burnt. You can then scoop out the good rice and discard the burnt part to continue your meal.
Delicious steamed fish

If your steamed fish often breaks apart, place a few slices of onion under the fish on the steaming plate. The fish will be tasty, sweet, and won't break during steaming. This is one of the very useful onion tips.
Preventing flies from landing on food
Wash raw food, drain well, and place a few clean onion slices on top; this is guaranteed to keep flies away.
Handling rusty knives and cleaning kitchen tools

Cut an onion in half and rub the cut surface on the rusty part of the knife; the rust will disappear. Clean kitchen utensils by using onion roots to rub surfaces with grease buildup; this works especially well for copper and tin items, making them bright and beautiful. Additionally, if you cut an onion in half and rub the cut surface on glass windows, then quickly wipe with a dry cloth before the juice dries, the glass will be as shiny as new.

mon_an.ten: How to Reheat Leftover Rice to Taste Fresh
mon_an.mo_ta: Reheating leftover rice to taste as good as fresh rice with 4 simple tips will help you have better breakfasts with leftovers. These tips also help you save time on cooking.
cac_buoc: Tip 1:

You can reheat leftover rice in a rice cooker by adding a little water to the pot, placing the leftover rice in a bowl, and putting the bowl inside the pot. Then, press the cook button; in just a few minutes, the rice will be hot. It will taste as good as fresh rice because the steam softens and fluffs it.
Tip 2:

If not using a rice cooker, you can reheat leftover rice in the microwave for a delicious, non-dry result that tastes just like freshly cooked rice. Simply place the rice in a glass bowl or a microwave-safe dish. Cover tightly with plastic wrap. Then microwave it; the rice will be very tasty and not dry.
Tip 3:

To make reheated rice taste fresh, once a new pot of rice has absorbed all the water, dig a small hole in the new rice just big enough for the leftovers. Pour a little hot water into the hole, add the leftover rice, and cover it with the new rice. Press the "cook" button again. When steam rises, you will have hot, delicious rice.
Tip 4:

If you have leftover rice, remember to store it in the refrigerator. When reheating, just put the rice in a colander, rinse lightly, then put it in the rice cooker and press the button. When you eat it, it will still be like fresh rice (no need to add extra water).

mon_an.ten: Diet Guide to Prevent and Treat Hair Loss
mon_an.mo_ta: Below are food groups that are excellent for preventing and treating hair loss. Just pay a little attention and include these foods in your daily diet to provide energy for your body while supplying nutrients to nourish strong hair, preventing split ends, hair loss, or premature graying.
cac_buoc: Zinc
Zinc functions to create cells that balance hormones and develop hair follicles. Without zinc, your hair will always be prone to breakage and split ends because it becomes very brittle.
Foods containing zinc:
Seafood, especially clams and shrimp: These are excellent because they contain not only zinc but also Vitamin B12, which helps prevent and treat hair loss and breakage.
Red meats: Red meats are rich in zinc and Vitamin A, helping to prevent dandruff and hair loss.
Silica
Silica acts like a tonic, helping the body absorb vitamins and minerals better, thereby preventing weak hair and hair loss.
Foods containing silica:

Potatoes: Potatoes contain many substances good for health and hair loss prevention, such as potassium, iron, zinc, phosphorus, and Vitamin C. Not only do they prevent and treat hair loss, but potatoes also help eliminate gray hair.
Bean sprouts: Mung bean sprouts contain plenty of Vitamin B and Vitamin C, which boost energy and help produce blood cells, keeping the body healthy and nourishing strong hair.
Iron

Iron is a primary nutrient that nourishes strong hair, playing an important role in the production of hemoglobin, a component of blood that transports oxygen to the skin surface and organs. The more oxygen transported in the blood, the stronger the hair.
Foods containing iron:
Nuts and grains: Both nuts and grains contain a lot of iron, which is not only good for treating hair loss but also provides iron for pregnant women.
Raisins: Raisins contain iron, B-complex vitamins, and essential minerals that help your body increase red blood cell production, promote blood clotting, and prevent the aging of hair roots.
Dates: Dates are arguably the fruit highest in iron and will quickly help treat hair loss.
Dairy products:

Dairy products are a rich source of calcium, zinc, Vitamin D, magnesium, and protein, reducing the risk of obesity and tooth decay, and especially preventing hair loss and stimulating hair follicle growth. Even yogurt contains nutrients necessary for hair growth.
A cup of warm fresh milk before bed every day will give you both a good night's sleep and strong hair.

Above are the food groups that are excellent for preventing and treating hair loss. Just pay a little attention and include these foods in your daily diet to provide energy for your body and nutrients to nourish strong, healthy hair. Wishing you good health and shiny, strong hair!

mon_an.ten: How to Make Docynia Apple Vinegar for Weight Loss and Beauty at Home
cac_buoc: Apple cider vinegar is a common staple in many family kitchens. However, not everyone knows how to make delicious Docynia apple vinegar. Let's explore apple vinegar and learn how to make your own fragrant Docynia apple vinegar at home through the article below.
I. What is apple cider vinegar?

Vinegar, a sour liquid produced through the fermentation of alcohol, is an indispensable ingredient in many home cooks' kitchens. The main component of vinegar is acetic acid (CH₃COOH) with a pH level of about 2.4.
The acid in vinegar is stronger than the acid in coffee and orange juice; however, this concentration is still lower than the acid concentration in the stomach.
II. Instructions for making clear Docynia apple vinegar
1. Prepare ingredients
Docynia apples (Sơn tra) – 200g
Warm water – 1 liter (temperature 40 – 50°C)
Ripe banana – 1 (Sứ or Già variety)
2. Preparation steps
To begin the process of making apple vinegar, you need to perform the following steps:

Wash the Docynia apples: Start by cutting off the stems and ends of the apples to remove dirt and insects. Then, cut the apples in half and soak them in diluted salt water for about 10 – 15 minutes to remove any damaged parts.

Prepare the vinegar jar: Place the washed apples into a jar, add 1 ripe banana to maintain moisture and facilitate the fermentation process. Pour warm water into the jar so that the apples are completely submerged.
Sealing the jar: Use a towel, cheesecloth, or oil-absorbing paper to tightly cover the mouth of the jar. This helps the vinegar ferment more effectively and prevents spoilage.
Fermentation process: Place the jar in a cool, dry place, away from direct sunlight, and let it soak for about 30 – 35 days. After this time, the apple vinegar will be ready for use.
Remember to follow the steps carefully to get the most fragrant and high-quality apple vinegar!
Once finished, the vinegar will have a cloudy yellow color and be covered by a thin white film on top. Quality vinegar will have a pleasant aroma and no insects lingering around the lid.
III. Secrets for successful apple vinegar
1. Selecting ingredients
To make delicious vinegar, you should choose Sứ bananas that are just ripe, avoiding those that are still hard.
Prioritize choosing small or medium-sized Docynia apples that are flat with rough, coarse skin.
Choose Docynia apples with pinkish-white or yellow skin and a natural color, as these are usually signs of good apples.
Good Docynia apples typically have a mildly sour, slightly tart flavor and are not too sweet, reflecting the characteristics of the Northwest region.
If you cannot find Docynia apples, you can use other types of apples, but Docynia apples are still preferred for their health benefits.
Docynia apples usually only appear from July to October each year, so if you want to make vinegar, you need to seize the opportunity to buy them during this time.
2. During the vinegar-making process
To make the vinegar ferment faster, cover the jar with a piece of cloth or oil-absorbing paper to allow for gas exchange.
If possible, ask for a bit of "vinegar mother" from someone who has made vinegar before. This not only helps the vinegar ferment faster but also helps create a better batch.
Add pineapple to the vinegar mixture along with the banana to create a beautiful yellow color and a natural fragrance.
To preserve the vinegar jar, place it in a cool place away from direct sunlight, whether it is the mother vinegar or the extracted vinegar.
IV. Storage and notes when using vinegar
To avoid reactions between the acid in the vinegar and substances in plastic bottles/jars, transfer the vinegar to bottles/jars made of glass, polyethylene, or PET for long-term storage.

Avoid storing vinegar in containers made of ceramic or porcelain. These items mainly contain clay and may contain heavy metals. This can create a high risk of toxic exposure due to the reaction of the acid in the vinegar with those metals.
V. Health benefits of apple cider vinegar

Support diabetes treatment: Apple cider vinegar helps reduce blood glucose levels and improves insulin sensitivity by about 19 – 34%. At the same time, it also increases good HDL cholesterol, reducing the risk of cardiovascular diseases.

Weight loss: Using about 30ml of apple cider vinegar daily can help reduce 1 – 2 pounds of body weight. The acetic acid in vinegar prevents fat accumulation, suppresses hunger, promotes metabolism, and reduces water retention.

Beauty: In addition to health benefits, apple cider vinegar is also beneficial for the skin. Its mild acidity, antibacterial, and anti-inflammatory properties help balance the skin's natural pH, improve dermatitis, reduce excess oil, treat acne, heal sunburned skin, and protect the skin effectively.
VI. Effective weight loss with Docynia apple vinegar

After 1-3 months of soaking, the Docynia apple vinegar is ready for use. During the fermentation process, a thin layer of film may appear on the surface, which does not affect the quality. Skim off this layer before use. If you detect mold inside, the batch may be faulty and should be discarded.
Docynia apple vinegar has a naturally light sour taste and a faint aroma of rice wine.
How to use Docynia apple vinegar for weight loss:
Mix apple vinegar with warm water and honey to drink before and after meals or before going to bed.
Use apple vinegar in salads to enhance flavor and support weight loss.
Mix apple vinegar with water to drink before meals to support weight loss or treat fatty liver.

Soak black beans in apple vinegar for weight loss. Roast the black beans until cooked, then soak them with apple vinegar in a glass jar for 4-5 days. Take 3 tablespoons before each meal for effective weight loss.

mon_an.mo_ta: Some tips for removing fishy odors from fish: Heat the fish up, wait until the protein in the fish firms up before adding ginger to thoroughly eliminate the fishy smell. You can also add a little vinegar when stewing fish to remove the odor.
cac_buoc: *– Removing fishy odors from hands:* After cleaning fish, your hands will have a fishy smell. Wash thoroughly once with soap, then squeeze a little toothpaste onto your hands and rub for a while, then rinse with cold water. Alternatively, rub your hands with a little white wine or fresh ginger before washing again with soap.

Removing fishy odors from cookware: Soak the items in tea water then rinse with cold water. You can also put a pinch of dry tea or a few slices of radish into the pot or pan with a little water and boil for a while. After cooking, pour in a tablespoon of vinegar while the cookware is still hot; the fishy smell will also disappear.
*– Removing fishy odors from knives:* Rub the knife thoroughly with fresh ginger after preparing fish, then rinse with cold water.

*Removing fishy odors from cutting boards:* Drip a little vinegar on the board before washing, dry it under sunlight, then use a brush to scrub with plain water. You can also soak the cutting board in rice water mixed with a little salt, use a brush to scrub it clean, then rinse with hot water.
*Removing fishy odors from the kitchen:* Put a little vinegar into the pan before frying to prevent the kitchen from being permeated with a fishy smell.

mon_an.ten: Making Delicious Kimchi is Not Difficult
mon_an.mo_ta: Making delicious kimchi is not difficult – This article introduces home cooks to tips for making delicious, simple kimchi that is as good as Korean restaurants. Making delicious kimchi is easy with simple tips for beef kimchi soup, side-dish kimchi, or tasty kimchi kimbap.
cac_buoc: To keep kimchi crunchy

Keep the napa cabbage leaves whole, wash away dirt, and soak in salt water to clean. Then drain and air-dry until wilted. For accompanying ingredients like carrots and radishes, you must also wash, grate, or slice them into bite-sized pieces and air-dry until wilted. This will make the kimchi crunchy.
Choosing good napa cabbage
Making delicious kimchi is not difficult, but for the best results, the most important step is choosing good napa cabbage. Choose young plants with fresh hearts.
How to make kimchi
There are 2 basic ways to make kimchi: for instant consumption or for long-term storage.
Step 1: Long-term kimchi

Ingredients: 2kg napa cabbage, 1 large carrot (shredded), 200g ginger (peeled and shredded), 20 garlic cloves (sliced), 100g Korean chili powder, 15 horn chilies, 2 tsp roasted salt, 4 tbsp fish sauce.

Method: Wash the cabbage and carrots and air-dry until wilted (note: do not cut the cabbage, keep the leaves whole). Mix the seasoning ingredients together. Layer the cabbage in a jar and rub the seasoning onto each layer of cabbage, leaf by leaf. Cover tightly and ferment for 5 days. After 5 days, it will be very delicious and crunchy. You see, making delicious kimchi is not difficult.
Step 2: Instant kimchi
Ingredients: 1kg napa cabbage, 3 tbsp Korean chili powder, 50g chives, 1 apple, 1 pear, 5 red chilies, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 20g salt, 50g sugar, 1 tbsp MSG.

Method: Wash the cabbage and keep the leaves whole to air-dry until wilted. Puree the apple, pear, and red chilies with the chili powder. Mix the seasonings in a large bowl. Layer the cabbage and add the seasoning, rubbing it onto each leaf. Let it sit for 10 hours and it is ready to eat.

mon_an.ten: How to Make Proper Soy Milk
mon_an.mo_ta: Hot soy milk without preservatives is very good for health. To make delicious milk that lasts long, it is important to soak and boil it correctly. Soy milk is a nutrient-rich drink suitable for both winter and summer, but it does not keep for long. Street vendors often store soy milk in plastic containers and keep it hot until serving. However, due to unhygienic production, soy milk is often contaminated with bacteria. Boxed soy milk is flavored with soy aroma, contains preservatives (E451, 407, 460, 466, 500ii, 471, etc.), and is sterilized. Refer to the following tips on how to make proper soy milk to have healthy cups of milk for your family!
cac_buoc: Tips for buying and storing soybeans:

Soybeans are nutrient-rich and need proper storage. However, shops in markets and supermarkets often just keep them in plastic basins or plastic bags. Consumers often store them poorly at home; soybeans exposed to air for a while will be invaded by moisture and deteriorate, becoming harder as they absorb more moisture. Therefore, when buying soybeans, consumers need to check the packaging date. Do not buy those kept in basins; even if the skin looks good, they have deteriorated. Buy from trusted sources or look for vacuum-packed soybeans with Food Safety certification, printed expiration dates, and clear origins. After buying, put them in a glass jar or a sealed plastic bag.
Soaking and handling foam from soybeans:

Soybean skins contain oil and impurities that create foam, making the milk less tasty and prone to spoiling quickly. Experience shows that soybean foam should be handled carefully during processing. Specifically, use a pump to bubble water from the bottom of the tank throughout the soaking time so that foam and sour water overflow without soaking into the beans. This technique keeps the soybeans in a low-acidity environment. To apply this, do the following:
Step 1: Measure the soybeans into a large pot. Use a strong water jet to flush out foam and any flat or moldy beans. Handling the foam thoroughly will make the soy milk tastier and last longer.

Step 2: Wait until the foam is all gone before starting to soak. Use a large pot and soak in as much water as possible. This helps dilute the soaking water and reduces acidity. For example: soak 200g of soybeans in 5-10 liters of water. Do not soak with hot water. Do not cover with a lid. Place in a cool, dry place. Soaking time in summer is 6-8 hours, in winter 8-10 hours. It is best to change the soaking water every 2-3 hours.
Step 3: After soaking, drain the water and continue to flush with a strong jet to remove all foam before rubbing off the skins. This technique prevents sour water from soaking into the bean flesh.

Step 4: If making it daily, you should soak enough soybeans for 3-4 batches. The soaked and peeled beans not yet used should be covered with a little water and placed in the refrigerator, to be used within 2 days. Each time you take them out, change the water and flush the foam thoroughly before grinding. This method saves you time.
Grinding and boiling:

Put the soaked and peeled soybeans into a blender, slowly add 200ml of water, grinding and stopping intermittently to saturate the bean water. Adding water slowly helps the beans grind finely without foam. Next, pour the finely ground soybeans into a large pot and mix with the remaining 1100ml of water. Use a cloth to filter the bean water and discard the pulp. Put the bean water in a pot and simmer over low heat; after 20-25 minutes, the milk is cooked and can be drunk hot. Many families choose to buy Korean-made soy milk machines that can grind finely enough to drink without filtering; these machines can also make very delicious tofu and tofu pudding.

Note: When boiling the milk, turn the heat very low. Occasionally stir the bottom of the pot gently. This helps the milk cook without burning. When the milk boils up, remove it from the heat, skim off the foam, then put it back on to boil 2-3 more times.

Supplementary ingredients should be added while boiling the milk. You can use 5-10 peeled peanuts with 3-5 tablespoons of black sesame; the resulting soy milk will be creamy and more nutritious. Or add a few stalks of pandan leaves for a special fragrant flavor.
Reference recipe for delicious soy milk: 120-130g soybeans, 1300ml water, 5-10 peanuts, 20-30g black sesame or 2-3 pandan leaves.

mon_an.mo_ta: Not only an important seasoning in the kitchen, vinegar also has many health benefits. Refer to this article on the Benefits of Vinegar to learn more about the advantages of vinegar that we might not know!
cac_buoc: Tips on the benefits of vinegar:
Refreshing the spirit: Add 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar to a glass of water, add a little sugar. You now have a refreshing drink beneficial for the body.

Helping with weight loss: Weight loss is an eternal topic for women. Vinegar contains 20 types of amino acids and 16 types of organic acids, which can promote sugar excretion and lower cholesterol. The amino acids in our daily vinegar can not only consume body fat but also promote smooth sugar and protein metabolism, achieving weight loss effects.

Anti-aging: Traditional Chinese Medicine believes that vinegar has the effect of removing accumulation and producing the new, supporting the improvement of blood circulation for the skin and promoting skin metabolism. Modern medical research proves that vinegar has antioxidant, anti-aging, and wrinkle-reducing effects.

Improving sleep: Traditional Chinese Medicine believes vinegar can activate blood and disperse stagnation. Soaking feet in vinegar can promote blood circulation, relieve fatigue, and help us sleep well. Therefore, those who often suffer from insomnia should try mixing 2,500ml of hot water at about 40°C with 150ml of rice vinegar for a foot soak. When bathing, adding an appropriate amount of vinegar to the bathtub will help eliminate fatigue and improve sleep.

Preventing gynecological diseases: White vinegar has a bactericidal effect and is very effective in treating vaginal inflammation and external itching. Each time, use about 1L of warm water with 10-15ml of white vinegar added, then use this water to clean the external area and wash the bathtub. Compared to other daily hygiene products, after washing with white vinegar, the area becomes smooth, comfortable, and does not feel dry.

Treating acne, melasma, or freckles: These are often associated with varying degrees of constipation. Modern medical research proves that aged vinegar contains rich amino acids, various catalysts, and many types of unsaturated fatty acids, which can promote intestinal peristalsis, maintain the ecological balance of intestinal bacteria, and keep bowel movements smooth.

Treating constipation: If constipation is severe, we can drink a tablespoon of vinegar on an empty stomach every morning upon waking up, then drink a glass of cooled boiled water. Doing this continuously for 1 week will have a very good laxative effect.
Soothing a sore throat: Mix 1 tablespoon of apple cider vinegar into a glass of water. Use this water to gargle and drink.
Treating tinea versicolor: Use edible vinegar (4%) to apply to the fungal skin area 2-3 times/day.
Treating athlete's foot: Soak feet in salt water mixed with vinegar, or apply vinegar to the spaces between the toes.

mon_an.mo_ta: Toothpaste is not just for brushing teeth; it has countless "side effects." Today, these tips will introduce a few benefits of toothpaste in the kitchen that you might not know. I believe it will help homemakers a lot!
cac_buoc: Toothpaste helps remove unpleasant odors from hands when cooking, such as the smell of fish, garlic, onions...

Cleaning glass gas stoves: Rub a small amount of toothpaste on the glass surface, then wipe thoroughly with a damp cloth; you will see the glass surface much brighter and clearer. Avoid rubbing too vigorously, as the abrasive components in toothpaste can scratch the glass.
Similarly for glass bottles, cups, porcelain mugs, or plastic boxes, the benefits of toothpaste work the same way as cleaning the gas stove surface. Remember to rub glassware gently.

Cleaning water stains on tables: Your table often has round stains in the shape of cup bottoms. If you often drink tea and coffee and like using wooden tables, it is even easier to leave stains. To remove these stains, just put a little toothpaste on a soft cloth, rub it on the stain, and then wipe clean with a damp cloth.

mon_an.mo_ta: Benefits of pineapple – delicious pineapple (thơm) pieces are especially tasty, and there are many other benefits. Here are some tips on the benefits of pineapple.
cac_buoc: Pineapple (thơm) is not just a delicious dessert fruit; it also provides many vitamins and prevents many different types of diseases.
Step 1: Weight loss

Pineapple is a fruit rich in vitamins and minerals, including vitamin C, vitamin B1, manganese, and enzymatic proteins. Bromelain is a protein-digesting enzyme found in the stem and core of the pineapple, which has medicinal effects. On average, a slice of pineapple contains only 40 calories, while the rest is mainly water and fiber. Both of these substances help hinder the weight gain process.
Step 2: Anti-cancer

Latest studies show that pineapple fights carcinogens and plays a role in protecting healthy cells. A cup of fresh pineapple contains about 70mg of Vitamin C, enough for the body's daily requirement, and 95mg of vitamin A, equivalent to about 1/5 of the daily recommended amount.
These compounds protect healthy cells from damage by free radicals and heal damaged cells, reducing aging and the development of other diseases.
Step 3: Improving the digestive system

Bromelain is an extract found in the pineapple stem that neutralizes body fluids so they don't become too acidic. Bromelain also regulates pancreatic activity, supporting digestion. You can maintain a healthy digestive tract because pineapple helps digest protein faster. Especially for those who often experience uncomfortable symptoms of constipation, try eating a few slices of fresh pineapple with breakfast.
Step 4: Increasing resistance

Vitamin C in pineapple is always considered a natural medicine that provides you with good resistance for health. Eating pineapple daily also helps the body increase the absorption of iron from vegetables and speeds up the healing of scars.
Step 5: Helping bones stay strong

Pineapple contains manganese, a mineral essential for the body to build bones and connective tissue. You don't even need to eat a lot of fruit; just one bowl of pineapple provides your body with 73% of the required manganese.
Issues to note when eating pineapple
Choose to buy fresh and intact pineapples.
Do not eat bruised or crushed pineapples; soak and wash pineapple with salt water before eating.
When peeling pineapple, remove all the skin and cut deep to remove all the eyes.
People with bleeding disorders or at risk of bleeding (nosebleeds, dengue fever, large wounds, women with uterine bleeding...) should not eat pineapple.
Do not eat fresh pineapple when hungry because the organic acids and bromelain in pineapple act strongly on the stomach and intestinal mucosa, causing nausea and discomfort...
Source: Ngôi sao (The Star)

mon_an.mo_ta: Diet is extremely important in the process of nourishing a baby for pregnant women. Below are some very useful dietary tips for pregnant women that we want to share with you!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Fruits and vegetables:

Pregnant women should eat plenty of fruits and vegetables: because these are sources of vitamins and minerals, as well as fiber, which helps with digestion and prevents constipation. Eat at least 5 portions of fruits and vegetables daily – they can be fresh, frozen, canned, dried, or juiced.

Remember to always wash them carefully. You can cook vegetables in a little water, or eat them raw, but they need to be soaked and washed thoroughly to avoid parasites found in raw vegetables, while still retaining the vitamins and minerals.
Step 2: Starchy foods (carbohydrates):

Starchy food is an important source of vitamins and fiber without containing too many calories. Starchy foods include: bread, potatoes, breakfast cereals, rice, pasta, noodles, corn, millet, oats, sweet potatoes, yams, and cornmeal.
For rice or flour, you should not eat types that are bleached too white, as they lose vitamins.
Step 3: Protein:

Protein sources include meat (but avoid liver), fish, poultry, eggs, beans, and nuts. You should eat lean meats and remove the skin from poultry. Cook meats thoroughly before eating; it is best to boil or steam them. Avoid rare meats and limit grilled food.

Poultry eggs also need to be cooked thoroughly; do not eat soft-boiled eggs. In particular, you should eat fish 2-3 times a week to increase the necessary omega-3 for the body and the fetus. Oily fish like salmon, sardines, or mackerel are very good for pregnant mothers.
Meat, fish, eggs, and whole grains are protein-rich foods that help strengthen the health of the mother and the fetus.
Step 4: Milk and dairy products
Dairy foods like cheese, milk, Fromage Frais, and yogurt are very important because they contain calcium and other nutrients that the baby needs.
Pregnant women should choose low-fat or skimmed milk options. Pregnant women often feel hungry and have cravings more quickly, so choosing to drink milk for snacks is best.
Depending on the body's needs, pregnant women can eat 2-3 extra snacks per day. Besides milk, fresh fruit, dried fruit, some types of biscuits, etc., are also good choices for snacks.
Step 5: Foods to limit
Pregnant women should not eat many foods high in sugar and fat: including all spreads (like butter), oils, salad dressings, cream, chocolate, crisps, biscuits, cakes, puddings, and carbonated drinks.

Pregnant women should only eat small amounts of these foods. Sugar contains calories without providing any other nutrients and can contribute to weight gain, obesity, and tooth decay. Too much saturated fat can increase blood cholesterol, increasing the risk of developing heart disease. Try to cut down on saturated fats and foods rich in unsaturated fats.
Step 6: Healthy snacks
If you feel hungry between meals, try not to eat snacks high in fat and sugar like candy, biscuits, crisps, or chocolate. You should choose healthier foods like bread, milk, or fresh fruit.
Step 7: Eat every 4 hours

Even if you are not hungry, you should eat something every 4 hours. If you feel nauseous, have food aversions, heartburn, or indigestion, you should snack even more. You can eat 5-6 meals, each only 1/3 of a portion, as long as you feel you can eat.
Pregnant women must absolutely not skip meals. Even when you do not feel hungry, the fetus needs a continuous supply of nutrients.

mon_an.ten: How to Boil Fluffy Potatoes Simply
mon_an.mo_ta: Potatoes are a tuber that can be used to prepare many delicious and nutritious dishes. When preparing dishes from cooked potatoes, we usually boil them first, but not everyone knows how to boil potatoes correctly. If boiled incorrectly, the potatoes can become waxy or discolored. Refer to "How to Boil Potatoes Correctly" for the best technique!
cac_buoc: With potatoes, you can boil them whole or cut them into small pieces; both ways work and the potatoes will cook, but the boiling time for each method will differ.

To ensure the boiled potatoes are evenly cooked, for both methods above, you must ensure all potatoes are of similar size. For example, if boiling whole, select tubers that are equally round with similar weight and shape; if cutting small, you must also cut them into equal-sized pieces. This way, you won't have to worry about which potato cooks first or last, and you can remove all pieces at once without some being overcooked and others undercooked.
You can boil potatoes with the skin on or peel them first. If not peeling, ensure you wash the potatoes thoroughly; once boiled, the skin will still be easy to peel.
Below are instructions on How to Boil Potatoes Correctly:
Step 1: Cut the potatoes
Use a peeler to remove the skin, then depending on preference, you can cut the potatoes into thin slices or bite-sized chunks.
Step 2: Soak the potatoes
Next, soak the potatoes in a bowl of diluted salt water for about 10 - 15 minutes. Then, remove the potatoes, rinse with clean water, and dry the surface with a clean towel.
Soaking potatoes in diluted salt water not only prevents them from browning but also helps them cook faster when boiled.
Step 3: Boil the potatoes
Once soaked, slowly put the potatoes into a pot. To ensure even cooking, place the larger potatoes at the bottom to contact the heat faster.

Add a little water (just enough to cover the potatoes) and a teaspoon of salt to the pot, place the pot on the stove, and boil over medium heat for about 10 - 20 minutes. When the water boils and you can easily pierce the potato with a chopstick or toothpick and see starch sticking to it, the potato is soft and cooked; you can turn off the stove. Quickly remove the potatoes from the pot, drain them, and then they can be prepared into many delicious dishes!
Notes when boiling potatoes
1. Need to choose delicious potatoes

Choosing good potatoes is an important first step in the cooking process. To choose good potatoes, look for tubers with firm, heavy skin that is smooth and healthy-looking. Light yellow potatoes usually have a more fragrant flavor and higher sweetness than white potatoes.

Avoid choosing potatoes with wrinkled, wilted, or soft skin, as they will not have a sweet flavor or provide much nutrition when cooked. Especially avoid buying potatoes with nodules, spots, many indentations, black marks, or those that are leaking fluid.
Additionally, do not choose fresh potatoes with scratched skin, because if not used immediately, they will quickly rot and may infect other potatoes.
Limit choosing potatoes with sprouts, because when sprouts have developed, potatoes contain solanine, a type of glycoalkaloid that causes a bitter taste and can be harmful to health.
2. How long to boil potatoes? How many minutes?

For potatoes harvested a long time ago, the ideal cooking time for them to be soft and delicious is about 20-25 minutes. For freshly picked potatoes, only 15-20 minutes are needed. After cooking, to ensure even ripeness, note the following:

After the pot of potatoes boils, turn down the heat to avoid the outside being mushy while the inside is still raw. This helps the potatoes cook evenly from the inside out and prevents the skin from cracking.
If you only cook a portion of the potato instead of the whole tuber, the cooking time will be significantly shortened. Potatoes cut into small pieces only need 5-10 minutes to cook.

There is no need to use too much water when cooking. The right amount of water will help the potatoes cook just as the water evaporates. Arrange the potatoes reasonably, placing them close together and ensuring the water covers them.
Adjust the boiling time just enough so the potatoes do not fall apart.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Complete Kitchen God Offering for Busy Cooks
mon_an.mo_ta: The day the Kitchen God returns to heaven is approaching. If you are busy with work but still want a complete offering tray, check out these suggestions!
cac_buoc: According to Vietnamese traditional customs, the Kitchen God (Táo Quân) is the deity who stays year-round to oversee all affairs in the earthly realm. On the 23rd day of the 12th lunar month, the Kitchen Gods ride carp to heaven to report the year's events to the Jade Emperor for fair reward and punishment.
To "please" these important deities, people often prepare an offering tray to see off the Kitchen God with sweets or traditional dishes along with joss paper, boots, hats, and paper carp.

However, nowadays, the Kitchen God offering tray has been simplified and it is not strictly mandatory to have all traditional dishes. The offering tray also depends on the circumstances and taste of the homeowner.
Below is a suggestion for a simple tray that busy women can prepare:
Boiled chicken
Xôi gấc (Red sticky rice)
Pickled onions
Pig ear and green mango salad
Giò lụa (Vietnamese pork roll)
Broccoli and carrot soup
Stir-fried chayote with pork heart
Beer/soft drinks
Fruit
BOILED CHICKEN

Wash a dressed rooster (1 - 1.5kg) and place it in a pot of cold water with a few slices of ginger. After the water boils, lower the heat, simmer for about 10 minutes, then turn off the stove and cover to soak for a while. You can use a chopstick to pierce the thigh meat; if the juice is not pink, it is cooked. Generally, depending on the size of the chicken, choose a reasonable boiling time.
When the chicken is cooked, remove it, rinse with cool water, then chop into pieces and arrange on a plate. You can also offer it whole if you prefer.
GIÒ LỤA
I buy giò lụa ready-made from a reputable shop. Cut the giò lụa into bite-sized pieces and arrange them on a plate.
PICKLED ONIONS

Ingredients for pickled onions include 300g white onions (choose slightly young ones to be ready faster); 200ml vinegar; 100ml filtered water; 50g sugar, 40g salt, and rice water. Soak the onions in rice water overnight. Dissolve 20g of salt in 1.5 liters of water. Cut the onion roots, peel, rinse in salt water, then drain. Note: do not cut too deep into the onion flesh to prevent spoilage. Cook the vinegar water: put 200ml vinegar, 100ml water, 50g sugar, and 20g salt in a pot and boil; when the sugar is dissolved, turn off the heat and let cool. Arrange onions in a jar, add chilies if desired. Keep the onions in a cool, dry place. With this young type of onion, it is ready in 4-5 days. For older onions in warm weather, they take 1 week to 10 days. If it's cold, it may take longer.
XÔI GẤC
Ingredients for xôi gấc include 1 gấc fruit; 1kg good glutinous rice; 1 tsp salt; 3 tbsp sugar; 2 tbsp white wine.

Wash the glutinous rice and soak it in water for about 6 – 7 hours. Then rinse and drain. Cut the ripe gấc in half, scoop out the flesh into a bowl, and marinate with 2 tbsp of white wine to make the color redder. Mix the gấc flesh, glutinous rice, and salt thoroughly, then put the rice into a steamer for about 25 to 30 minutes.

When the rice is soft, use chopsticks to fluff it up. Add a little cooking oil and steam for another 10 minutes. When the xôi gấc is soft and sticky, remove the steamer from the stove, wait for the steam to dissipate slightly, then sprinkle with sugar and mix well. Then serve the rice on a plate or press it into a mold for a nice appearance.
PIG EAR AND GREEN MANGO SALAD

Ingredients for the pig ear and green mango salad include 250g thinly sliced pig ears; 250g shredded green mango; 2/3 medium onion, thinly sliced; 1.5 tsp seasoning salt; 4 tsp sugar; 1 small lime; 2-3 red chilies, chopped; 6-7 garlic cloves, minced; crushed roasted peanuts (optional); Thai basil and culantro. Accompanying ingredients include raw vegetables and rice paper.

Mix the pig ears, mango, and onion in a bowl. Add seasoning salt and sugar and mix well. Add lime juice and mix again. Then add garlic, chili, and crushed roasted peanuts, and mix well. Finally, add chopped herbs and mix one last time. Serve the salad on a plate and roll it with raw vegetables and rice paper, dipping in sweet and sour fish sauce.
STIR-FRIED CHAYOTE WITH PORK HEART

Ingredients for this dish include 2 chayotes, 1/2 pork heart, and seasonings. Wash the pork heart and slice thinly. Peel the chayote, wash, and slice thinly. Crush and sauté dried shallots until fragrant, add the pork heart and stir-fry until almost cooked, season slightly, then remove to a plate. In the same pan, add a little oil and sauté more shallots. Add the chayote, stir-fry until almost cooked, then add the pork heart back in. Season to taste and toss for a moment until completely cooked. Sprinkle with a little black pepper and chopped green onions. Serve on a plate.
BROCCOLI AND CARROT SOUP

Prepare 1/2 head of broccoli, 1 small carrot, 10 shiitake mushrooms, and seasonings. Break the broccoli into small florets and wash. Peel the carrot, wash, and slice into thin rounds. Soak the shiitake mushrooms until soft. Use the chicken boiling water to cook the soup. Bring the chicken broth to a boil, season, then add the carrots to cook for about 2 minutes before adding the broccoli and mushrooms to cook until done. Ladle the soup into a bowl and place it on the offering tray.
Additionally, the tray includes beer/soft drinks and fruit as desired.

Besides the above dishes, you can add dishes like dried bamboo shoot and pork trotter soup, meatball soup, beef roll, cinnamon pork pâté, fried spring rolls... or any dishes that suit your taste for the offering; the most important thing is the family's sincerity.

mon_an.ten: Full Moon Feast for the First Lunar Month for Busy Moms
mon_an.mo_ta: As the first full moon of the lunar year approaches, grandmothers, sisters, and mothers prepare a complete feast to worship their ancestors. Below is a suggestion for a simple yet comprehensive feast for the first full moon; please feel free to refer to it.
cac_buoc: "The first full moon is the most important of the year," so home cooks should take the time to prepare a simple meal for worship, expressing respect and gratitude to ancestors while praying for peace and luck for everyone.
Below is a suggested feast for home cooks, including:

Vietnamese pork roll (giò lụa), pandan sticky rice with pork floss, crispy roasted pork belly, sweet corn shrimp patties, coconut heart salad with shrimp and pork, boiled broccoli with caramelized fish sauce, and vegetable pork rib soup.
Pandan Sticky Rice with Pork Floss
Ingredients: 300g glutinous rice, 50g pork floss, 1 bunch pandan leaves, salt, cooking oil.

Method: Wash the pandan leaves; set aside about 2 leaves to cook with the rice later. Cut the remaining leaves into segments and blend with a little water. Strain to get the extract to soak the rice for color. Pour the pandan water over the glutinous rice until just covered and soak for 6-7h. Then wash thoroughly, drain, and toss with a little salt for flavor. Note to use a moderate amount of salt so the rice is slightly lighter than usual, as it will be eaten with pork floss.

Boil water in a steamer, add the rice along with the 2 reserved pandan leaves and steam until cooked. While steaming, occasionally stir with chopsticks so the rice cooks evenly and the bottom doesn't get mushy. When the rice is just cooked, remove the pandan leaves, then add 1 tbsp of cooking oil, stir well, and it's done.
Vietnamese Pork Roll (Giò Lụa)
Take about 300g of giò lụa, peel and cut into 2 thick rounds, then cut each round into 6 wedges. Arrange on a plate and garnish with cucumber.
Crispy Roasted Pork Belly
Ingredients: 500g pork belly, 100g pickled leek bulbs, salt, sugar, pepper, shallots, garlic, cooking oil, 1 packet five-spice powder.

Method: Cut the pork belly into 2-3 smaller pieces depending on the size, wash thoroughly, then place in a pot of salted water to blanch briefly, then wash again. Next, boil the pork with seasonings (salt and a little minced shallot and garlic). Boil for about 10-15 minutes depending on the thickness until 60-70% cooked. Remove and use a sharp toothpick to prick the skin evenly, then rub a little salt into the skin so it becomes crispy when fried. Marinate the meat with a little seasoning, pepper, five-spice powder, and minced shallot/garlic for at least 2-3 hours in the refrigerator to infuse.

For the marinated meat, scrape off all the minced shallot/garlic so it doesn't burn when frying. Use paper towels to pat the meat completely dry. Place a pan on the stove, add oil, then add the meat to fry over medium heat (fry the skin side first until golden, puffed, and crispy) then flip to fry the meat side. Once the meat is evenly golden, remove to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess fat, then slice into small pieces and arrange on a plate. This is very delicious when eaten with pickled leek bulbs.
Sweet Corn Shrimp Patties
Ingredients: 250g shrimp, 100g minced pork, 1/2 sweet corn, 1 stalk green onion, 1 tbsp frying flour, pepper, seasoning powder, salt, cooking oil.

Method: Peel and devein the shrimp, remove heads, wash with salt water, then drain and mince or blend finely. Wash the sweet corn and shave it thin with a knife. Trim the green onion, wash, and chop finely.

Place the shrimp, minced pork, and corn into a bowl. Add the chopped green onion along with a little pepper and seasoning powder, then mix thoroughly. Next, add 1 tbsp of frying flour and mix to create binding for the patties. Place a pan on the stove; once dry, add cooking oil. When the oil is very hot, use a spoon to scoop the mixture into the pan and fry until golden on both sides. Remove to a plate lined with paper towels to drain excess oil.
Coconut Heart Salad with Shrimp and Pork

Ingredients: 200g coconut heart, 100g pork belly, 150g shrimp, 1 cucumber, 1 small carrot, Vietnamese coriander, cilantro, 50g peanuts, 2-3 small garlic cloves, 3-4 shallots, 1 lime, 1-2 chilies, and seasonings like fish sauce, salt, sugar, cooking oil.

Method: Choose the tender part of the coconut heart, discard the tough parts, and slice thinly into cold water. Then wash again and drain. Wash the pork, boil with a little salt until cooked, then slice thinly. Wash the shrimp, trim the whiskers, boil until cooked, and peel, leaving the tails for presentation.

Wash the cucumber, halve it, and slice diagonally. Peel the carrot, wash, and julienne. Trim the Vietnamese coriander and cilantro, keeping the tender parts and washing them. Roast the peanuts, peel, and crush slightly. Peel and mince the garlic. Wash and slice the chilies. Cut the lime and squeeze for juice. Peel and slice the shallots, then fry until crispy.
Prepare the dressing by mixing 1.5 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp lime juice, minced garlic, and chili. Adjust the ratio according to the type of fish sauce and your taste.

Place the coconut heart, carrot, and cucumber into a large bowl. Slowly pour 2/3 of the dressing over and toss well; let sit for 5' to absorb. Then add the shrimp, pork, and the remaining dressing and toss together, seasoning to taste. Transfer the salad to a plate, sprinkle with chopped herbs, roasted peanuts, and fried shallots.
Boiled Broccoli with Caramelized Fish Sauce (Kho Quẹt)
Ingredients: 500g broccoli, 100g pork belly, 30g dried shrimp, 2 chilies, 1 shallot, peppercorns, sugar, salt, cooking oil, fish sauce.

Method: Trim the broccoli by removing tough stems and wilted leaves, soak in diluted salt water for 30 minutes, then wash and drain. Place a pot of water on the stove; when boiling, add a pinch of salt and 1 tbsp of oil, then add the broccoli to boil. Once cooked, remove to a plate.

How to make the caramelized fish sauce (kho quẹt) for dipping: Dice the pork belly into 1cm cubes. Crush the peppercorns, slice the chilies, peel and mince the shallot. Wash the dried shrimp and soak in water until soft.

Place a pan on the stove, add the pork fat and stir until rendered and crispy. Then, pour off some fat, add the shallot to sauté until fragrant, then add the shrimp and stir-fry until firm. Add fish sauce, sugar, and chili to the pan and simmer until thickened, seasoning to taste. Turn off the heat, then add the chili and pepper.
Vegetable Pork Rib Soup
Ingredients: 300g pork ribs (about 2 ribs), 1 daikon, 1 carrot, 1 chayote, 3-4 small potatoes, 1 stalk green onion, salt, seasoning powder.

Method: Cut the ribs into small pieces, wash, then place in a pot of boiling water with a little salt to blanch. Discard this water, wash the ribs thoroughly, then simmer with a little salt until tender.

Peel and wash the vegetables, then cut into bite-sized pieces. Trim and chop the green onion. When the ribs are tender, add the vegetables and simmer until cooked. Season to taste, turn off the heat, ladle into a bowl, and sprinkle with green onions.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Preserving Rice Paper Wrappers
mon_an.mo_ta: Rice paper wrappers used for wrapping or making spring rolls are even better than regular rice paper because they are paper-thin, making the wrapper almost unnoticeable when eating. Usually, these wrappers are only at their best for a short time; if you buy a lot and don't use them all (requiring long-term storage), you must preserve them correctly to avoid them becoming dry, brittle, or spoiled. Today we share some simple tips to keep your rice paper soft, delicious, and free from oxidation. – Wrap the rice paper with banana leaves before use to make them softer; you can even leave them out for a few days, and as the leaves dry, the rice paper stays soft.
cac_buoc: If banana leaves are unavailable, you can use other leaves like cabbage or lettuce; wipe them dry and wrap the rice paper for a few hours before use; the wrappers can soften again even if they have become hard.

Additionally, you can wrap the rice paper in paper and then place them in a sealed plastic bag (ziplock) to keep them for a long time. You should divide them into small portions enough for each use to avoid opening and closing the bag many times, which can spoil the wrappers.
For rice paper that has already become dry and brittle, layer them with cabbage leaves before preparation; after a while, they will become soft again.
(Collected)

mon_an.ten: Tips for Preserving Pork, Potatoes, and Tomatoes
mon_an.mo_ta: 1. Methods for preserving pork: In summer when temperatures rise, meat can easily develop an odor. You can wrap the meat in a piece of cheesecloth or a clean napkin dampened with vinegar and place it in a cool, ventilated spot; it will stay fresh and odorless for 1-2 days because vinegar inhibits bacterial growth.
cac_buoc: You can also place a little mustard powder in a small tray, then put the pork in the same container and seal it tightly; at normal room temperature, it can be kept for 4-5 days.
2. Methods for preserving potatoes

Choose large, beautiful potatoes and discard any that are diseased, bruised, or withered. Then place the selected potatoes in a place with a temperature of 12-16°C. Over the next 40 days, gradually reduce the temperature to 3-5°C, keeping the relative humidity between 85-95%. Meeting these standards will keep potatoes for a long time.
You can dig a small pit in the ground to maintain a moderate temperature, and every few days poke a hole for ventilation; this can keep potatoes for several months without spoiling.
3. How to keep tomatoes fresh

First is the selection process. Choose beautiful, newly ripened tomatoes that are free from disease and bruising; you should choose late-ripening varieties rather than early ones. Then prepare a storage pit or container and disinfect the ripe tomatoes; you can use a 1% bleach solution for soaking or smoke them. Next, arrange the tomatoes into baskets, wooden crates, bags, or jars and place them in the pit for preservation. The temperature needs to be maintained at around 11-12°C, and air humidity must always be kept at 85-95%. If the storage pit is 2m deep underground, it is even better. With this preservation method, after 45 days, 80-90% of the fruit will remain in good condition, appearing no different from fresh tomatoes. If using plastic wrap for the exterior, you can place a little lime inside; the effect is even better, with the success rate reaching 92-95%.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Choosing Fresh, Chemical-Free Avocados
mon_an.mo_ta: With these useful tips, we hope you will be able to choose fresh, delicious avocados to prepare nutritious and healthy dishes.
cac_buoc: How to choose delicious, chemical-free avocados

Forced-ripened avocados will be bitter. Many people think bitterness comes from scraping the green part near the skin, but with naturally ripe avocados, you can scrape all the way to the skin without bitterness; in fact, the outer flesh is very rich and creamy.
To tell if an avocado is young or mature, look at the stem; if the stem scar is large, it means the avocado is young. Therefore, it is important to choose a ripe and fresh avocado.

Don't take those that feel mushy to the touch, as they are spoiled and have lost their flavor. Squeeze gently; if it feels slightly soft but still firm and not hollow, it's good. Or press the stem; if it feels slightly soft, choose it even if the rest isn't soft yet, as it will ripen toward the base (however, only eat it when the whole fruit is ripe).
A delicious ripe avocado has a taut, glossy but slightly bumpy skin and feels heavy in the hand.
Who should avoid avocados

Avocados are highly nutritious and very good for health. They contain vitamins A, B1, E, C, D along with minerals like calcium, protein, and iron. These nutrients give avocados many benefits such as treating stomach ulcers, eliminating bad breath, and maintaining heart health.
However, according to nutritionists, people with the following conditions should ideally avoid avocados:
People with liver disease or a weak liver

Some studies suggest that certain oils in avocados are harmful to the liver, causing deeper damage when existing liver problems are present. Therefore, those with liver disease or a weak liver should not eat avocados.
People on a diet

The calorie content in avocados is quite high, so eating a lot can lead to high calorie intake and weight gain. If you decide to add avocado to your diet, be sure to cut calories from other dishes so your weight loss plan doesn't fail.
Avocado is a high-calorie food and will make you gain weight. Therefore, avoid eating avocados daily if you are dieting.
Breastfeeding women

Many studies indicate that avocados are great for pregnant women but harmful for breastfeeding women, as substances in avocados can reduce milk production. Additionally, if breastfeeding women eat too many avocados, it can cause stomach aches, potentially affecting the baby's health.
Sensitive individuals

Sensitive people should avoid eating many avocados as they can cause skin reactions or vomiting. Side effects on the skin include allergic issues. Symptoms of an allergy when eating too many avocados are usually rashes, itching, redness, or eczema. Overconsumption can also cause an itchy mouth and a swollen tongue.
People with digestive issues
Although avocados are good, eating too many can cause stomach discomfort. "Overdosing" can also irritate the gastrointestinal tract, especially for those with existing digestive diseases.
With these small tips, we hope you will choose fresh avocados to prepare nutritious meals.

mon_an.mo_ta: Just spend a little time learning about rambutans and you can buy fresh, juicy, sweet, and refreshing fruit for your family's dessert after intimate meals.
cac_buoc: How to distinguish Vietnamese rambutans from Chinese rambutans
Identification is not difficult; you just need to look at the external appearance to know which are forced-ripened and which are Chinese rambutans.

Look at the leaves and spines: Chinese rambutans may have fresh leaves and branches, but the spines are withered and blackened, and the skin is no longer a natural bright red. Many fruits may even be blackened, rotten, or leaking fluid.
Natural rambutans can be preserved for quite a long time without turning black. Conversely, forced-ripened rambutans will have blackened skin and spines from the start.

Look at the flesh: When forced-ripened rambutans are split open, a lot of water leaks out, and the flesh is mushy and quite soft. Additionally, you should avoid fruits with yellow stains as they are spoiled.
Standard Vietnamese rambutans have thick, milky white flesh with no unusual colors.
Flavor: Forced-ripened rambutans are often sour and quite bland. Naturally ripened rambutans have a cool, sweet, and delicious flavor.

Furthermore, to buy fresh rambutans, you can press firmly on the fruit. If the skin is still firm and doesn't feel hollow or waterlogged, it is a good fruit. If the skin feels soft, leaks water, or cracks easily, you should not buy it.
Additionally, you should buy fruits with green or bright red spines; those are fresh. Fruits with black or bruised spines are withered.

Note that rambutan season usually only lasts from April to June. By the 7th lunar month, it is off-season, and the fruit is prone to worms at the stem. Therefore, you should limit buying rambutans at this time.
Also, if you prefer something sweeter and tastier, you can choose "chôm chôm nhãn" (longan-rambutan).
How to identify chôm chôm nhãn vs. regular rambutans:

Ripening characteristics: Chôm chôm nhãn is normally green; when ripening, it turns from green to yellow, then pink, and finally red. 1-2 days after picking, the entire fruit will turn red; any that are not red are of poor quality.

External characteristics: Chôm chôm nhãn is spherical and small, weighing only 20-30g per fruit; 1kg of quality fruit contains about 40-50 pieces. Notably, it has "rough" patches on the skin, with sparse and short spines (compared to other varieties). Appearance-wise, it is not very pretty, which is a key identifying feature.
Flesh characteristics: Chôm chôm nhãn has thick, crunchy flesh that peels easily from the seed, a sweet taste, a very delicious and characteristic aroma, and a longer shelf life than other types.
Just spend a little time learning about rambutans and you can buy fresh, juicy, sweet, and refreshing fruit for your family's dessert after intimate meals.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Choosing Delicious, Clean, Chemical-Free Longans
mon_an.mo_ta: To help you avoid buying poor quality longans or fake "Hưng Yên" longans, and to ensure they haven't been soaked or preserved with chemicals, here are tips for choosing delicious longans, distinguishing varieties, and picking preservative-free fruit.
thoi_gian: It is currently longan season in the Southern regions, Hưng Yên, Hòa Bình, etc. With many different varieties, sellers may label them all as Hưng Yên longans to reassure customers. And of course, food preservatives to keep them fresh longer are unavoidable.
cac_buoc: Types of longans:
Chinese Longans:
Large fruit, thinner skin, and larger, thicker leaves than Hưng Yên longans.
The flesh appears thick but has a bland sweetness and no aroma.
Chinese longans often use preservatives, so they look very clean and pale, with thinner skin that quickly bruises or rots and carries a chemical smell.
Thai Longans:
Thai longans take 1-2 days to reach wholesale markets, so they are often treated with preservatives or become mushy due to being packed in sealed crates.
The skin is thin and easily splits or spoils if soaked in water.
Distinguishing Thai longans is quite easy due to their bright skin and strange, pungent smell without aroma. Especially when first opening a crate, the smell will rise along with white dust.
Hưng Yên Longans:
Large fruit with a bumpy, thick-looking skin. The color is a deeper yellow and stays fresh longer because they are harvested, transported, and consumed immediately.
The flesh is thick and dry, with a small seed. The taste is as sweet as rock sugar. The base of the fruit has two overlapping layers of flesh that fit very tightly (unlike other longans).
Tips for choosing delicious, clean, fresh, preservative-free longans:

The safest way is to buy longans still attached to the branch with fresh leaves and green, sturdy stems that emit a pleasant fragrance. Avoid buying longans with overly bright, clean skin or those that have fallen off the branch.
Longans using preservatives have a pungent smell and brighter skin than natural ones. Sulfur makes the skin brighter; if used in high concentrations, it will have an unpleasant pungent odor.
It is best to taste them to avoid being misled.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Choosing Kumquat and Peach Blossom Trees for Tet
mon_an.mo_ta: With these simple tips for choosing kumquats and peach blossoms, you can easily select a beautiful tree as desired to welcome a New Year with peace and happiness.
cac_buoc: Step 1: How to choose kumquats for Tet

When choosing a kumquat tree, a beautiful shape is the top factor to notice. You should choose trees with a natural shape, sturdy base, and straight trunk, featuring a full range of green fruit, ripe fruit, buds, and flowers.

A beautiful kumquat tree must have the "four excellences," meaning a beautiful shape, beautiful fruit, and a mix of green, ripe, and large fruit. Conversely, a tree with small, yellow leaves and tiny fruit is a poor choice and may not last long. Choosing is hard, but transporting and planting is even more important to keep the pot beautiful and long-lasting. Move it gently, don't break the root ball, snap roots, or drop leaves and fruit.
When planting the kumquat in a pot, you should line the bottom with straw or cinders for easy drainage and airflow. Then, place the tree in the pot and pack fine soil around it.

To make the tree more beautiful for Tet, you can decorate it with ribbons, tinsel, and hanging ornaments to make it sparkle. You should also hang twinkling lights so the tree looks beautiful at night.
Step 2: How to choose peach blossoms for Tet

Along with kumquats, Northern Tet cannot lack peach blossoms, the flower symbolizing a New Year with luck and prosperity. If buying a branch, choose one with a circular canopy and even twigs. Avoid branches with lopsided canopies or twigs that don't start from the same point on the stem. When buying, choose branches with many buds and sear the base before placing in a vase.

If choosing a potted tree, you should buy those with small, short twigs (dăm), and main branches that all originate from one point on the trunk for balance. However, note that potted trees bloom slower than branches, so you must choose a tree with many flowers near Tet. Do not overwater, as it can kill the tree. When planting in a pot, you can spread a little sand on top to help the tree live longer and stay fresh. Like kumquats, decorate with tinsel, hanging ornaments, and lights for a sparkling look. If possible, buy some white pebbles to spread at the base for beauty.
With these simple tips, you can easily choose a kumquat or peach blossom tree as desired for a peaceful and happy New Year. Wishing your family a perfect tree.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Choosing Quality Meat, Eggs, and Poultry
mon_an.mo_ta: 1. Tips for choosing good meat: Quality meat has a bright pink color (buffalo and beef are darker), does not feel sticky when pressed with a fingertip, has no odor, and has high elasticity.
cac_buoc: 2. Distinguishing old sow pork

Old sow pork has a lot of lean muscle and little fat but is not tasty. You can distinguish it by: the fat is yellowish, the muscle is dark red or blackish with large, coarse fibers, the udder area has many black spots, and the connection between muscle and fat is weak, appearing as if there is an extra layer of skin between them. The skin is notably thick and coarse.
3. Good Chinese sausage (Lạp xưởng)
The outer casing is clean and firm, the fat is white, the meat is bright pink, and there is no strange odor.
4. Choosing poultry (duck, chicken, goose)
Quality poultry has bright, clear eyes, and the vent is not darkened or foul-smelling.
5. Diseased livestock and poultry

With pre-processed livestock or poultry, you will see many blood clots in the vessels, possibly with air bubbles, and the blood vessels will be prominent and purple-red; the muscles are very limp and dark purple; the fat is deep red, pale red, yellow, or green; the skin often shows signs of bleeding, with spotted blood clots or a bright yellow color.
6. Choosing fresh eggs

When shining a light through the egg, the white should be transparent, the two parts clearly defined, with no black spots and a very small air cell. When dropped into a basin of plain water, the egg sinks and lies horizontally at the bottom. Place the egg on a smooth flat surface and spin it gently; it should only spin 2 or 3 times before stopping, and as it spins, it feels as if there is resistance inside. Shaking the egg should produce no sound. You can also lift the egg to check its weight; if it feels heavy, it is still good.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Preventing Food from Sticking to the Pan
mon_an.mo_ta: These tips will reveal a few tricks to help prevent food from sticking to your pots and pans, making dishes tastier and more attractive. These tips will help you cook with less effort.
cac_buoc: Tips for preventing food from sticking to the pan
Heat the pan then add oil; only add food to fry when the oil is hot to limit sticking to the bottom.
Adding a little butter to the pan or pot will also prevent food from sticking.
Wash pots and pans thoroughly so there is no food residue, as residue burns quickly during cooking.
Follow the recipe steps correctly and have ingredients ready before frying or stir-frying with a non-stick pan.
Overcooked food also has a higher risk of sticking.
When using a non-stick pan
Metal utensils should not be used with non-stick pots and pans as they can cause scratches on the surface of the non-stick coating.

Do not use metal scouring pads to clean pots and pans as they can create small scratches on the surface. Consequently, food will stick firmly to the bottom during cooking, and the non-stick layer will be lost.

mon_an.mo_ta: Canker sores are a common ailment. They cause discomfort and, if severe, can cause pain or swelling. With these provided tips, we hope you can overcome canker sores quickly and no longer feel pain or discomfort. Don't forget to share these effective treatments with your friends, family, and loved ones!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Treat canker sores with radish juice:

First, chop the radish, place it in a blender with a little water, then strain for the juice. Mix with cooled boiled water and rinse your mouth 3 times a day. Usually, rinsing with radish juice only takes 2 days to heal canker sores.
Step 2: Treat canker sores with katuk (rau ngót) juice:

Simply wash katuk leaves, crush or blend them. Then extract the juice and mix with a little honey. Use a cotton swab to dab the katuk juice onto the sore. Repeat this 2-3 times a day for immediate results. The ulcer will soothe, and the pain and discomfort will vanish. Remember to use only the leaves and do not add extra water; use pure extract for full effect.
Since katuk is currently prone to chemical sprays and toxic growth stimulants, you should use katuk from a safe source to avoid unwanted side effects.
Step 3: Treat canker sores with starfruit water:

This method is quite simple. Take 2-3 starfruits, cover with boiling water, and bring to a boil. Then, remove from heat and let it cool; gargle and swallow slowly. Do this many times a day for effectiveness. You should choose sour starfruit to produce more saliva and clear heat better.
Step 4: Treat canker sores with tomatoes:
Peel the tomatoes and extract the juice to drink daily. You should also hold the juice in your mouth for a while to let it soak in.
Step 5: Treat canker sores with watermelon rind:
Toast the watermelon rind until golden, then grind into a powder. Mix the powder with honey and apply to the sore 1-2 times a day. After 2-3 days, the sore should be healed.
Step 6: Treat canker sores with Thai basil:
This method is extremely simple. Just chew Thai basil leaves 3-5 times a day to treat canker sores.
Notes on treating canker sores:
Besides using the above methods, you must also follow these rules to treat canker sores at the root:
Avoid foods that irritate the mouth such as: salty foods, oily foods, and highly acidic fruits.
Regularly eat green vegetables and fruits to clear internal heat.
Furthermore, maintain proper oral hygiene.
Drink plenty of water.
Rinse your mouth with salt water 3 times a day.

Canker sores are a common ailment. They cause discomfort and, if severe, can cause pain or swelling. With these provided tips, we hope you can overcome canker sores quickly and no longer feel pain or discomfort. Don't forget to share these effective treatments with your friends, family, and loved ones!

mon_an.mo_ta: Here are several ways to select fresh, high-quality meat to ensure your dishes are flavorful and safe for your family's health. Let's look at these tips for choosing fresh meat!
cac_buoc: Pork
To buy fresh pork, you need to observe and choose carefully:
Healthy pork usually has a light pink to deep red color.

The meat should be firm, not mushy, with good elasticity, no fluid leakage, and no sliminess. Press your finger into the meat; it should form a depression but leave no trace when you lift your finger. The meat fibers should be even.
The cut surface should be dry, slightly tacky, and the muscle slightly constricted; the skin should be soft, and the fat should be white to slightly ivory with no rancid smell.
Organs from healthy, fresh pigs have a natural color and a shiny, glossy surface.
Beef
Good beef is bright red (note: dark red beef is not high quality).
Beef fat must be bright yellow, with white tendons that feel hard when pressed. If the fat feels soft when pressed, do not buy it.
Choose beef with small, soft fibers that are not too smooth. Avoid large, tough fibers.
Finally, press the meat with your finger. Fresh beef will have good elasticity, won't be sticky, and won't have a foul odor.
Meat from female cows is often tastier than from bulls. If you can find young beef (veal), it is even better, as it has white fat and fine fibers.
Distinguishing Beef from Pork
Currently, some sellers use pork disguised as beef to sell at a higher price. Therefore, you need to know how to tell them apart.
Beef that is pale blue or has round white spots between the fibers indicates infection with flukes or parasites. Do not buy any meat with a foul odor, as it can be dangerous to your family's health.
Other signs of stale beef include: dark red color, deep yellow fat, and yellow bones. The meat will have poor elasticity, be mushy, feel slimy on the surface, and stick to your hand when pressed.
Beef fibers are long but small, while pork fibers are larger and shorter.

Regarding color, real beef is deep red, while pork is a lighter pink. Beef fat is pale yellow, while pork fat is white. If you press the meat, pork feels slightly soft, while beef feels very soft and tends to stick to your finger.

Beef also has a stronger scent than pork; if you touch it and smell it, you will notice a gamey aroma. If you suspect pork is mixed in, press the meat, flip it over to examine it closely, and smell it. The best way is to avoid meat that is discolored, pale, or dull.
Duck
Live Duck

When buying, choose mature, plump ducks with round breasts, thick neck and belly skin, and full feathers (the tips of the wings should just cross over each other). These ducks are faster to pluck and save time.
Avoid young ducks as the meat will be mushy and not firm, and it takes a lot of time to pluck the downy feathers. Young ducks have large, soft beaks. Older ducks have small, hard beaks.

Ducks that have laid many eggs also have very fragrant meat. These ducks have a sagging lower belly. Unlike chicken, when eating duck, it is better to choose a male duck as they are tastier than females.
To check if a duck is healthy, part the feathers near the tail; if the vent is clean and free of runny droppings, the duck is healthy.
Pre-processed Duck
Observe the thighs and breast; if they look overly plump and tight, do not buy. If you hold the duck upside down and it deforms, it has likely been injected with water.
Press your hand into the thighs and breast; water-injected meat feels bouncy and mushy.

If the duck is split open, check the inside; if there is a lot of water trapped inside the membranes, it is due to water injection. If you buy this duck, a lot of water will leak out when you chop it, and the meat will taste bland and lack freshness.
Chicken
Pre-processed Chicken
Free-range chicken (gà ta) is usually compact and firm with a narrow breast.

Industrial egg-laying chickens look similar to free-range chickens, so distinguish them carefully. Free-range chicken skin is naturally pale yellow and only darker in areas like the breast, wings, and back, while industrial chickens are white or yellow all over (possibly due to toxic dyes).
To tell if a chicken has been dyed, observe if the skin is yellow but the fat underneath is white; if so, it has been chemically dyed.
Free-range chicken skin is thin, smooth, and highly elastic. Choose meat that looks fresh, has no foul or antibiotic smell, and no bruises or blood clots on the skin.
To buy good chicken, avoid those with dark, dull skin, as they likely died before being processed.
To avoid water-injected chicken, press on suspected areas (mainly thighs and breast); if it feels mushy, slippery, or deforms, do not buy it. Water injected into chickens is often mixed with borax.
Live Chicken

Avoid chickens with pale or purple combs, those that look lethargic, have runny beaks, hard crops, dull eyes, drooping wings, or a tired appearance with their heads hanging down. These chickens often have wrinkled skin, thin bodies, bony breasts, and ruffled feathers; their feet are cold and dry, and the vent is pale or red with droppings stuck around it. These are signs of a sick chicken.

If you want good free-range chicken without slaughtering it yourself, choose a healthy live one and ask the seller to process it on the spot. This ensures the meat is fresh and fragrant without the risk of buying sick or dyed chicken.
Goat

Goat meat is a popular choice for many during holidays. It can be used for stir-fries, rare lime-marinated goat, hotpot, salads, etc. However, you must choose carefully to ensure freshness and safety.
Fresh goat meat is bright red and glossy, with even, firm fibers. It should feel soft, smooth, elastic, not sticky, and have no strange odor.
Goat meat that is pale, lacks firmness and elasticity, has an overly dry or slimy surface, or a foul smell is spoiled meat.

mon_an.ten: Tips to Reduce Fat While Cooking
