mon_an.mo_ta: Reducing the amount of fat during cooking helps you consume fewer calories. However, making dishes low-fat while maintaining fresh flavor is a challenge for home cooks. These tips for limiting fat while cooking will help you achieve this without compromising the quality of your meals.
cac_buoc: In modern life, almost every type of food contains some amount of fat. We all know fat isn't entirely bad, but if not consumed in the right amounts, it can lead to health issues like fatty liver or high cholesterol. Let's remember some ways to reduce fat in our cooking and limit its absorption into the body.

1. Substitute Milk: In recipes that call for milk, use fat-free or low-fat varieties. Replacing 1 cup of whole milk with 1 cup of skim milk reduces about 70 calories, 8g of fat, and 28 mg of cholesterol. Using fat-free evaporated milk instead of regular evaporated milk has a similar effect. 2. Fat and Flour Ratio: When preparing flour-based dishes, reduce the fat content to a 1/3 ratio (1 part fat to 3 parts flour). To reduce oil in baked goods and bread, stick to a ratio of at least 2 tbsp of oil for every 1 cup of flour. You will still get delicious results.

3. Pay Attention to Yogurt: Use yogurt to replace part or all of the fat content. For brownies, you can replace ½ the fat with fat-free, unsweetened yogurt. For mixed baked goods, add more yogurt to ensure the cake stays moist. 4. Separate Egg Whites and Yolks: Use 2 egg whites to replace one whole egg. This substitution reduces calories from 80 (one whole egg) to 32 (two egg whites). Cholesterol also drops from 215mg to just 1mg. 5. Understand Your Dish: Stews and soups are the easiest dishes to modify by substituting ingredients. Most baked goods are also easy to change, with cookies being more flexible than other cakes. However, for pickles, preserves, jams, jellies, or candies, do not change the traditional recipe. To ensure the best quality, do not try to substitute everything in the original recipe. Sometimes, replacing fat doesn't yield the desired result. While reducing fat is good for health, you must also consider the flavor, as taste is very important.
With these simple cooking tips, we can significantly reduce fat intake, leading to better health and a stronger body.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Boiling Chicken with a Beautiful Golden Skin
mon_an.mo_ta: Introducing a great tip for boiling chicken so it has an attractive, golden-yellow color, perfect for holiday offerings or family anniversaries. This method is not difficult at all; give it a try.
cac_buoc: To have a delicious chicken, you should choose a free-range chicken (gà ta). If buying live, look for a healthy bird with shiny feathers that lay flat against the body and a bright color. For pre-processed chicken, choose one with naturally pale yellow, thin skin all over, firm meat, a small oil gland, and not too much yellow fat at the neck and thighs. Industrial chickens will be soft and mushy when boiled, so free-range or garden-raised chickens are best.
Step 1:

After the chicken is slaughtered and plucked, rub it with salt and wash thoroughly both inside and out, then let it dry. Prepare the boiling aromatics: wash 3 scallions (you can keep the roots) and tie them in a bundle. Crush 1 piece of ginger (keep the skin on and wash clean).
Break off half a star anise and 15 Sichuan peppercorns. If you don't have Sichuan peppercorns, substitute with: 10 black peppercorns, 1/2 tsp chili powder, and 1/3 tsp mustard.
Step 2:
Prepare 3 scallions for the sauce: wash and finely chop the green tops; for the larger stems and white parts, cut into 4cm lengths and shred (optional).
Place the chicken in a pot, pour in cold water until the chicken is just submerged, and add all the aromatics (prepared in Step 1) along with a pinch of salt.
Step 3:

Start the chicken in cold water so it cooks evenly from the outside in. If you add it to boiling water, the chicken won't cook evenly and the skin may crack. If using frozen chicken, it must be completely thawed before boiling; otherwise, it will take a long time and the center may remain raw.
Place the chicken breast-side down and fill with enough water to submerge the whole bird. The pot shouldn't be too large (which takes too long) or too small (making it hard to turn the chicken).

Once the water boils, turn the heat down. If left at a rolling boil, the meat on the thighs will shrink upwards, which looks unappealing. After boiling for 5 minutes, turn the gas to the lowest setting for another 5 minutes, then turn off the heat and cover tightly for about 20 minutes. You can test by piercing with a chopstick; if it goes through easily and the juices run clear (not red), it is cooked.
The fastest a chicken can boil is about 20 minutes (average 30 minutes), but for even cooking and golden skin, it takes about 45-60 minutes (on low heat).
Step 4:

When the water has cooled significantly or is only slightly warm, skewer the chicken with a long chopstick and rest it over the pot to drain. Only carve the chicken once it has cooled completely, using a sharp, heavy knife for clean, decisive cuts. Sauté the scallions with 30ml of oil (or rendered chicken fat), then add 50ml of soy sauce and bring to a boil to make a soy dipping sauce. If desired, simmer until the sauce reduces and thickens slightly.
Note:

To keep the boiled chicken plump and the skin color fresh, immediately submerge it in a pot of room-temperature boiled water (cold water is even better) after removing it from the heat. Only move it to a plate once it is completely cold; otherwise, the skin will dry out and darken. Afterward, let it drain slightly, then crush some turmeric, squeeze the juice, and mix it with rendered chicken fat. Brush a layer over the skin for a glossy, tight, and attractive golden finish.

Boiling a chicken is simple, but missing a few steps can ruin the result. Most importantly, stay focused—don't leave the pot to boil unattended while doing other chores, or the meat may overcook and fall apart!

mon_an.ten: Essential Kitchen Hacks You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Every chef has their own secrets for making delicious food. We will share with you some very useful kitchen tips you should know to always have wonderful meals!
cac_buoc: Tip for Frying Fish Without Sticking

When frying fish, if you aren't using a non-stick pan, the fish may stick and break apart, which looks unappealing, especially when serving guests. To prevent this in a regular pan: Add 2 tbsp of fine salt to the pan and toast it until it turns slightly yellow. Discard the salt, then add oil and start frying the fish. This hack ensures your fried fish won't stick and will be crispy and delicious.
Tip for Removing Onion and Garlic Smells from Hands

When cooking, it's hard to avoid direct contact with onions and garlic, and the scent can linger on your hands for a long time even after using soap. To solve this: Rub a stainless steel spoon vigorously over your hands under cold running water for about 5 minutes. You will find the smell completely gone. You can also use fresh lemon to clean and leave a pleasant scent.
Tip for Boiling Eggs Without Cracking
This is a great tip that many people find effective. To keep eggs intact while boiling: Place the eggs in cold water and add a little salt. Remember not to drop eggs into already boiling water!
Tip for Stewing Bones Quickly

If you don't have a pressure cooker but want to stew bones quickly until tender: Add one tsp of MSG to the pot. Once the water boils, drop in 3-4 ice cubes, cover tightly, and continue stewing. Your bones will become tender much faster!
Tip for Marinating Food Faster

Marinating is crucial for flavor, but if you're short on time, try this: Mix your spices with 1 tbsp of cooking oil before rubbing them on the food. The oil helps the spices dissolve and penetrate the food much faster, reducing the waiting time.
Tip for Fixing Salty Dishes
If you accidentally over-salt a dish, don't worry; try these methods:
Add more water: For soups or broths, simply add a little more water to neutralize the saltiness.
Add potato slices: For soups or stir-fries, drop in a few slices of raw potato. The potato will quickly and effectively absorb the excess salt.
Add lemon juice: Lemon juice helps counteract saltiness while also enhancing the overall flavor of the dish.

mon_an.mo_ta: Useful tips for maintaining kitchen tools and food containers for the home cook.
cac_buoc: Porcelain should be washed immediately after use. To keep it shiny and durable, wash with a specialized tea set cleaner or a solution of lemon juice/vinegar mixed with salt. Avoid washing with very hot water, as it can cause yellow staining.

Aluminum should be washed with hot soapy water or a bit of vinegar. First wash with hot water, then rinse with cold water and air dry. Do not use water mixed with lye, ash, or other alkaline substances, as they quickly damage aluminum. The black film on frequently used frying pans does not affect food safety. Do not leave salty food in aluminum containers for long, as salt corrodes them. For the same reason, do not cook acidic or salty liquids (soups, porridges) in aluminum pots.

Enamelware is suitable for acidic liquids, but avoid using high heat. After buying new enamelware, fill it to the brim with water and boil it, then let it cool completely before the first use. Wash with hot water and a little dish soap. For tools used for dough, eggs, milk, or rice, soak them in cold water for a while before washing. If the bottom is burnt, do not scrape it; soak it in soapy water until the burnt food loosens.
Grease is easily cleaned with a vinegar solution (2 tbsp vinegar per 1 liter of water).

Scale buildup in enamel pots or kettles can be removed with a vinegar solution (1 part vinegar to 5 parts water). Boil the solution until the scale softens, then discard, wash with a baking soda solution, and finally rinse with cold water.
To remove odors from cookware or containers, use crushed charcoal soaked in water to scrub them.

Glassware should be washed with hot water, then rinsed with a salt and vinegar solution (1 tbsp salt and 2 tbsp vinegar per 1 liter of water). Rinse again with cold water to make the glass shine. New glassware should be "tempered" by placing it in cold water and heating it on low until it boils for about 1 hour, then turning off the heat and letting it cool in the water.

Stainless steel should be washed with hot water, rinsed with cold water, and wiped dry. Silver should be cleaned with a mixture of chalk powder and ammonia (1 tbsp chalk to 1 tbsp ammonia), then washed with soapy water, rinsed, and dried thoroughly.
To remove garlic or onion smells, use soapy water followed by a cold water rinse.

Wooden tools should be washed with a baking soda solution, then rinsed with hot water. Once a week, boil wooden items in a baking soda solution (1 tbsp baking soda per 1 liter of water), then rinse with cold water.
These are just a few essential kitchen experiences. We hope readers will share more. Good luck experimenting with these skills that are often hidden within yourself.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Delicious and Flavorful Braised Fish
mon_an.mo_ta: Braised fish is a family favorite due to its nutrition and flavor. However, making it perfectly seasoned and fragrant isn't always easy. Here are some tips to help you achieve a perfect pot of braised fish.
cac_buoc: Braised fish is a family favorite due to its nutrition and flavor. However, making it perfectly seasoned and fragrant isn't always easy. Here are some tips to help you achieve a perfect pot of braised fish.
Choosing Fish
First, observe the eyes, gills, body, and skin to identify fresh fish.
When choosing, look for fish with clear, bright eyes; avoid those with cloudy or dull eyes.
Check the gills; if they are still bloody, the fish is fresh. Fresh gills are usually red or pink. Do not buy fish with dark or blackened gills.

Some fish look fresh but feel soft and slimy when pressed; if the indentation remains or the fish has a strange smell, avoid it. If scales fall off easily or the meat is mushy, it may have been treated with preservatives. Only buy fish that is glossy, firm, and elastic.
Removing the Fishy Smell
During prep, you can rub the fish with a little salt and soak for a few minutes before cleaning to remove slime and odor.
When gutting the fish, remove the gills and the black membrane inside the belly to reduce the fishy smell.
For scaleless fish like basa, catfish, or eel, pour a little hot water over them and scrape off the slime. This ensures they are clean and odorless.
You can also soak fish steaks in rice water or salt water for 15 minutes, then rinse and drain before cooking.
Marinating

The marinade for braised fish is simple: use good fish sauce, soy sauce, pepper, salt, and minced shallots (optional). Marinate for about 2 hours to let the flavors penetrate. This also makes the fish firmer and more fragrant.
Alternatively, you can lightly pan-fry the fish before braising to keep it firm and prevent it from breaking apart.
Braising

Typically, fish is braised with galangal, homemade caramel sauce, coconut water (optional), chili, and oil. To make it richer, you can add pork belly, radish, or pickled greens. This makes the flavor much more appealing.

When braising, layer the fish with the other ingredients in the pot. Galangal or pork should be layered between the fish. Bring to a boil first, then lower the heat to a gentle simmer until the fish is tender. If you need to add liquid, only use hot water; cold water will make the fish smell fishy. Add chili or pepper near the end of cooking.
With these small tips, we hope you will have a delicious, perfectly seasoned pot of braised fish with a beautiful color that suits your family's taste!

mon_an.mo_ta: Today, we will guide you on how to make Grilled Pork Belly with Kimchi. With this method, you and your family will have an attractive dish to enjoy with rice or vermicelli. Please take a look!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the pork belly and slice thinly. Marinate the meat with all the seasonings listed above. Leave for at least 3-4 hours in the refrigerator.
Step 2: Thread the meat and kimchi alternately onto bamboo skewers and place them on a tray lined with aluminum foil.

Step 3: Preheat the oven to 200°C for 10 minutes. Place the tray on the middle rack and grill for 15-20 minutes per side. When the skewers are golden, fragrant, and the fat has rendered, they are done. Turn off the oven and remove the tray.
Arrange the grilled pork belly and kimchi on a plate. This dish is delicious with either rice vermicelli or steamed rice.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Making Professional-Style Nem Chua
mon_an.mo_ta: Nem chua is a favorite snack for many, but not everyone knows how to make it well. We will share tips to help you make fresh, sweet, and delicious fermented pork rolls!
cac_buoc: How to Choose Good Pork
Since nem chua is made from raw pork, you must know the source of your meat. Buy from trusted suppliers or directly from a fresh slaughter if possible.

Fresh meat: The outside has a dry film and the surface is slightly tacky. The cut surface is bright pink, the skin is soft, the fibers are firm, and it has good elasticity (pressing it leaves no mark). The fat is bright, firm, and has a characteristic aroma. Joint surfaces are smooth and clear.
Stale meat: The surface starts to feel slimy, the cut is wet, and elasticity is poor (pressing leaves a depression). The fat is dark, less firm, and smells off. Joints are slimy and cloudy.

Avoid meat that is too old or too young. Choose medium-aged pork with pink meat and thin skin. There are two types of lean meat: tenderloin and ham (rump). Tenderloin is tastier but can become dry if overcooked. Ham meat is softer.
Besides choosing fresh meat, the best part for nem chua is the lean ham (rump) without fat. This part is firm but not too dry, with a slight chewiness perfect for fermentation.
Spices for Nem Chua
Because nem chua needs to ferment to "cook," essential spices include fresh chili, black pepper, and garlic. Their heat helps process the meat.
Furthermore, these spices enhance the flavor significantly. Other ingredients include fish sauce, seasoning powder, and especially the Thai nem chua seasoning mix...
Principles of Grinding and Chilling
Making nem chua isn't just about chopping meat and mixing. The meat must be chilled in the freezer before grinding.

After washing, pat the meat very dry. It must then be placed in the freezer for about 45 minutes. This keeps the meat cold during grinding so it stays bouncy and doesn't get "cooked" by the heat of the grinder motor.
After 45 minutes, slice the meat and put it in the grinder. Note: only grind for 1-2 minutes; do not grind too long or it will turn into a smooth paste (giò sống).
Then, mix the meat with the prepared spices. Note: the small packet of curing salt inside the Thai seasoning mix should be added last after everything else is well mixed.
This is a crucial step for successful nem chua.
Wrapping and Fermenting

Place the mixture into a container lined with plastic wrap for easy removal. Press the meat down very firmly to ensure good cohesion. Finally, wrap it up and keep it in the refrigerator for 24 hours; the nem chua will turn a beautiful red color and taste delicious.
You can also ferment it at room temperature, but the refrigerator is safer and still yields great results.

mon_an.ten: Clean Your Microwave in a Flash
mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little lemon juice, your microwave will look like new without the need for heavy scrubbing. Let's see how to clean your microwave!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cleaning cloth, sponge, etc. - as needed
cac_buoc: Fill a cup with about half a cup of water.
Cut the lemon in half, squeeze the juice into the cup, and drop the rinds in as well.
Place the cup in the microwave. Set it to the highest power for 3 minutes, enough to boil the water.
When the timer goes off, leave it inside (do not open the door) for another 5 minutes. The steam will soften the grime inside.
Open the door and remove the cup; be careful not to get burned. Remove the glass turntable to clean it separately.
Use a cloth to wipe the inside of the microwave, starting with the door and the ceiling.
Next, wipe the sides and finally the floor of the microwave.
For stubborn stains, dip a corner of the cloth into the lemon solution and scrub them away.

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Boiling Vibrant Green Vegetables
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for boiling vegetables will help them stay colorful and retain essential vitamins. Boiling is a simple and healthy cooking method. These tips will help you understand how to boil vegetables perfectly.
cac_buoc: Tip for Boiling with Cooking Oil:

For some vegetables, adding a little oil to the boiling water makes them look glossy and vibrantly green, such as various types of bok choy or mustard greens. However, this will leave a thin layer of oil in the broth; consider this based on whether you plan to use the broth.
Tip for Boiling with Lemon or Vinegar:
Not all vegetables pair well with lemon or vinegar, but for cauliflower and carrots, they are very useful for maintaining color.
Tip for Boiling with Salt and Ice Water:

Boiling with salt is the most effective and common method. Wait until the water is at a rolling boil, add a little fine salt, then quickly drop in the vegetables. If the water isn't hot enough, vitamins will be lost and dissolve immediately.
Once the vegetables are cooked, plunge them into a bowl of ice water. Once cooled, transfer to a colander to drain; this keeps them crisp and bright.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for boiling meat perfectly; if not cooked correctly, meat can easily turn dark, develop an unpleasant odor, and lose its nutritional value. This article introduces handy tips to help you boil meat better while preserving its full nutrients.
cac_buoc: Duck

Duck meat will have an unpleasant odor if not cleaned thoroughly. Remember to remove the scent gland at the tail. You can then marinate it with crushed ginger, salt, and white wine for 30 minutes. When boiling, add shiitake mushrooms, crushed ginger, or crushed lemongrass to eliminate any remaining odor. Don't forget to skim the foam, and remove the duck as soon as it is cooked; overcooking will make the meat tough.
Pork

Pork should be boiled starting from cold water; if you drop the meat into boiling water, the nutrients will be locked inside and lost. When cooking, pour enough cold water to just cover the meat, add a little salt for flavor, and continuously skim the foam once it reaches a boil. When you can pierce the meat with a chopstick and no red juice runs out, it is cooked. Remove it and soak in a bowl of cooled boiled water so the meat looks appetizing and doesn't fall apart.
Beef Shank

Marinate the beef shank with a little salt, then use kitchen twine to tie it tightly into a round shape. When cooking, add some crushed lemongrass, crushed ginger, salt, sugar, honey, and a few fresh chilies. Use a pressure cooker for boiling. Once it reaches pressure, turn the heat to low and simmer for a while before turning off the stove. Remove, let it cool, and slice to serve immediately, or store in the refrigerator for later use.
Chicken

For a whole chicken, wash it thoroughly and rub salt both inside and out to remove odors. When boiling, pour in enough water to just cover the bird and place it on the stove. Once the water boils, turn the heat to low and flip the chicken over. Simmer for about 15 - 20 minutes, then remove the chicken. Rinse with cold water, let it drain, and then brush chicken fat or cooking oil over the skin to make it glossy, plump, and fragrant.
Chitterlings and Pig Ears

Chitterlings and pig ears must be boiled until just cooked; overcooking will make them tough immediately. You also need to ensure they maintain a beautiful white color. To achieve this, do not start boiling from cold water; wait until the water is boiling before adding them. After boiling for about 10 minutes, turn off the stove, remove them, and soak in a bowl of cooled boiled water to keep them crunchy and white.

mon_an.ten: Healthy Cooking Tips to Prevent Weight Gain
mon_an.mo_ta: Below are cooking tips to help you prepare delicious meals without worrying about weight gain. With just a little attention to preparation, changing cooking methods, adding more green vegetables and fruits, and increasing protein and fat-burning substances in your daily menu, you can effectively speed up weight loss, stay in shape, and limit health risks!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Use plenty of lemon juice to cook delicious, low-fat meals:

When cooking vegetable dishes and salads, you should use more lemon juice. This not only enhances the flavor but also adds zero calories to the portion. You should also replace salad dressings with lemon juice, as most dressings contain a lot of fat and chemicals that can sabotage your weight loss efforts.
Step 2: Bake instead of grilling for better flavor without oil:

Grilling food quickly at high temperatures has been shown to denature proteins and fats into harmful substances. Conversely, the baking process preserves the nutrients of the dish, even if it takes a bit more time.
Step 3: Use coconut oil in your healthy cooking menu:

Coconut oil is a familiar ingredient in diet and weight loss menus. By using coconut oil instead of regular cooking oil, you can still have delicious stir-fried and fried dishes without using animal fats. Although coconut oil is primarily fat, it consists of unsaturated fats that do not cause obesity and actually help the body burn excess energy.
Step 4: Limit deep-fried dishes in your healthy menu:

This is essential when you want to avoid weight gain. There are many attractive steamed, boiled, pan-seared, baked, and soup dishes that do not require frying or adding oil and fat. By constantly rotating these dishes, your healthy menu will feel incredibly diverse, and you will no longer crave fried foods.
Step 5: Add plenty of fresh vegetables to your weight loss menu:

When cooking, you should balance your meals so that at least 75% of the food is plant-based. Eat plenty of vegetables, substitute them for starchy grains, and add more fruit to your portions. This method reduces calories, aids digestion, and helps you lose weight quickly.
Step 6: Limit salt for better flavor and effective weight loss:
To lose weight, the best way is to stop adding salt to your dishes and use herbal seasonings instead. This not only helps reduce your waistline but is also extremely good for cardiovascular health.

The above are small tips so you can cook better without fear of getting fat. Just a little note in processing, changing different processing methods, adding many green vegetables, fruits, increasing protein and substances that help burn excess fat in the daily menu, you have helped speed up, more effectively the process of losing weight, keeping shape and limiting bad effects on health!

mon_an.ten: Tips to Identify Poor Quality Food
mon_an.mo_ta: The following tips will help you identify high-quality food to ensure delicious and nutritious meals for your whole family.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Chicken

When choosing chicken, pay attention to white stripes and the fat layer on the breast. If these are present, it means the poultry has been injected with growth hormones. Families should definitely stay away from this type of unhealthy chicken.
The color of the chicken is also very important: if it is yellow, it means the meat is no longer fresh. A good chicken breast will be pale pink and not too soft.
Step 2: Fresh Cheese (Cottage Cheese)

Dropping a bit of iodine solution onto fresh cheese will help you check its quality. If the stain on the cheese turns dark blue, it has been mixed with starch or impurities; otherwise, the iodine drop will remain yellow or brown.

Another way is to leave the cheese out at room temperature; if it contains vegetable fats, it will turn a deep yellow. After this experiment, the cheese might turn sour, but the color should not change.
Step 3: Honey
Pour a little honey onto a flat surface; fake or poor-quality honey will drip very quickly and spread immediately, while real honey is thick and flows very slowly.
When tasting, if the honey has a caramel-like flavor, it means it has been mixed with caramelized sugar. If it tastes excessively sweet, it has likely been diluted with sugar.
Step 4: Sour Cream

To check if sour cream contains vegetable fats, stir a spoonful into a cup of hot water. Poor quality cream will form clumps and white flakes on the surface. Pure sour cream will dissolve evenly into the hot water.
Step 5: Frozen Fruits and Vegetables
Check if the package of frozen fruits or vegetables is covered in frost or contains ice chunks. If so, it means it has been stored incorrectly.
Step 6: Fish
A fresh fish will have clear eyes and bright red gills. Additionally, the scales should be slightly iridescent, firmly attached, and evenly distributed across the body.
Step 7: Meat

When choosing meat, press your finger into it. Fresh meat will have enough elasticity to bounce back after leaving a slight fingerprint. Another way to tell is to cut a large piece; if the meat is dark inside but has a pink or white outer edge, it means the meat is old but has been treated to look fresh.
Additionally, you can blot the meat with a paper towel; if it is fresh, the towel will not be overly damp or soaked with blood.
Step 8: Green Vegetables

To know if a bunch of dill is fresh, hold the stalk vertically. If the stem and leaves droop to the sides, it is wilted. Furthermore, if the dill is too dark green and the stems are too long, it may contain nitrates. Fresh vegetables always have a natural green color.
Step 9: Ice Cream

Leave the ice cream at room temperature; if it contains vegetable fats, it will take longer to melt and turn into a thin liquid. High-quality ice cream will melt faster and turn into a thick, heavy cream.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Crispy Golden Fried Fish
mon_an.mo_ta: If you are wondering what to do with the fish you just bought at the market, this recipe will reveal how to make crispy golden fried fish very quickly. It doesn't take much time but is incredibly fragrant and attractive. If you don't have much time for elaborate dishes, you should memorize this recipe.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Red tilapia, carp, or tilapia - 1 fish (1kg)
All-purpose flour or frying flour - 30 g
cac_buoc: Clean the fish scales, remove the gills, and wash thoroughly. Use paper towels to pat the fish completely dry; this helps the meat stay firm and prevents oil from splattering during frying.
Next, evenly coat both sides of the fish with flour or frying flour.
Place a pan on the stove, add oil, and wait until it is very hot. Place the fish in and fry until golden brown on both sides, then place it on paper towels to drain any excess oil.
Wash, peel, and mince the chili, scallions, and garlic. Add this mixture to the soy sauce, then add sugar, sesame oil, and toasted sesame seeds. Stir well to create a sauce.
Finally, drizzle the sauce evenly over the fish. You can present it by placing the fish on a bed of raw vegetables or garnish with chili and tomato flowers for an eye-catching look.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cold weather is the season for grilled food; what could be better than family and friends gathering to cook and chat! However, not everyone knows that grilled food, especially grilled meats, is currently not encouraged by nutritionists. It is classified as a food to be cautious of in cancer prevention because during high-heat grilling, fat from the food and oil used for brushing drips onto the flames below (hot coals or heating elements in an electric oven) and burns, creating toxic PHA (polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon) gases. PHA attaches to the food through smoke. Furthermore, excessive heat causes a reaction between creatine and amino acids in meat protein, producing other toxins, typically HCA (heterocyclic amine). Fatty meats like pork and goat carry the highest risk. HCA is usually created when cooking high-protein meats at high temperatures, such as grilling or frying. To minimize harmful components during grilling, remember a few small rules. We will guide you through these golden rules!
cac_buoc: Tips for healthy grilling:

Always marinate the food with a sauce before grilling. Besides enhancing flavor, the sauce increases food safety. The coating of sauce reduces the amount of fat dripping down, thereby limiting the formation of toxins. The thicker the sauce, the more effective it is.

The quality of the grill grate is also important. Choose grates made of high-heat resistant ceramic or stainless steel. Absolutely do not use aluminum grates, as the reaction between acid and aluminum during grilling can create harmful substances.
Grill at low or medium heat to limit smoke.
Flip the food frequently to ensure it cooks evenly and avoid charring on one side.
Reduce grilling time by cutting the food into small, thin pieces.
Limit fat dripping onto the heat source by trimming excess fat from the food before grilling. The safest option is to choose lean foods that do not contain much fat.
When eating grilled food, remove all charred parts, as these contain the most toxins.
You should only eat grilled food no more than 2 times per week.
Source: Food Safety Department (Ministry of Health)
Wishing you a warm winter with family and friends! Please support us so the page can continue to improve!

mon_an.ten: Tips for Making Perfectly Flavored Dipping Sauces
mon_an.mo_ta: Dipping sauce is essential for every meal and every dish. For a dish to express its full, exquisite flavor, the accompanying sauce must also be superb. Therefore, we would like to introduce tips for making various delicious dipping sauces to help your dishes become even more flavorful and attractive.
cac_buoc: Remember to mix the dipping sauce according to the ratio: 1:1:1:5. This means 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar, and 5 tbsp filtered water. However, this ratio can be adjusted to suit your taste and the specific type of fish sauce or vinegar you are using.

Pour the fish sauce into a bowl. Add the sugar and vinegar, stir well, then add the water. Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved. Mince the garlic and chili. You can slightly crush the garlic before mincing so that the garlic and chili can float on the surface of the sauce.
Snail Dipping Sauce
Ingredients: High-quality fish sauce: 2 tbsp; Boiled water (cooled): 1 tbsp; Lime juice: 1 tbsp; Sugar: 3 tbsp; Minced ginger, chili, and garlic; Finely chopped cilantro; Finely sliced lemongrass.
Preparation:

Combine the fish sauce, cooled boiled water, and sugar in a pot. Bring to a boil to dissolve the sugar, then let it cool. Afterward, add the finely minced ginger, garlic, chili, and lime juice, and mix well.
Sprinkle the chopped cilantro and sliced lemongrass on top and stir. If you like it spicy, adding hot chili or crushed chili flakes will make it much more delicious.
Bánh Gối Dipping Sauce

The dipping sauce for Bánh Gối is usually a traditional blend of sour, spicy, salty, and sweet, similar to spring roll sauce, made with fish sauce, sugar, vinegar, garlic, and chili. Add a bit of chili sauce to the bowl for a bright red color. You can replace vinegar with lime or calamansi juice for extra aroma if desired.
You can also add thinly sliced papaya, carrots, and cucumbers to soak in the dipping sauce. These additional ingredients make the Bánh Gối much more appealing.
Bánh Cuốn

Unlike Bánh Gối, the dipping sauce for Bánh Cuốn follows this ratio: 1 sugar + 1/2 vinegar + 1.5 fish sauce + 3-4 warm water (you can also use chicken broth or fresh coconut water if preferred). Use sliced or minced chili and lime or calamansi. Calamansi, however, provides a unique fragrance and appeal.

To make Bánh Cuốn dipping sauce, first caramelize the sugar. When the sugar melts and turns light yellow, add the vinegar, then the fish sauce, and stir in the water (chicken broth is best). When ready to eat, squeeze in the calamansi and add the chili. This method is delicious but can be tricky as the sugar might burn if overcooked, or you might be unsure when to add the vinegar, sauce, and water. To avoid "risks," you should mix it normally using the formula above.
Bánh Bột Lọc

For people from Hue, most simply eat it with pure fish sauce and finely sliced bird's eye chili. However, many people prefer a mixed dipping sauce. Especially as Bánh Bột Lọc becomes more popular across different regions, the sauce is often prepared to suit local tastes.
Therefore, you can prepare a sweet and sour fish sauce that is slightly bolder than the sauce used for spring rolls, Bánh Bèo, or Bánh Xèo. Specifically:
Pound the garlic and bird's eye chili into a smooth, slightly thick paste.

Add the fish sauce. Add a little filtered water. Mix in sugar and lime juice to taste. The fish sauce for Bánh Bột Lọc should not be too sour and should be slightly bold, spicy, and fragrant with garlic.
Bánh Bèo Dipping Sauce
Ingredients: 1 cup high-quality fish sauce; 2 cups white granulated sugar (ratio 1:2).
Mix the fish sauce with honey (or the sugar mixture). Gently simmer the fish sauce and sugar mixture until it becomes thick and syrupy like honey. Then store it in a jar.
When ready to eat, take out about 2-3 tbsp, mix with 2-3 tbsp of filtered water, stir until well dissolved, and add lime and chili (Bánh Bèo sauce does not use garlic).
However, you should try it first and adjust to your preference, then choose the best ratio and continue using it for future batches.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Identifying Bleached Chicken Eggs
mon_an.mo_ta: Chicken eggs are a familiar food in every family because they are convenient and nutritious. However, it is necessary to know how to choose good eggs and store them properly to prevent the risk of food poisoning.
cac_buoc: When buying eggs, choose fresh ones so they can be stored longer. Do not wash eggs with water when you bring them home; instead, use a soft, damp cloth to wipe them clean before storing. If eggs are not cleaned before storage, chicken or duck droppings remaining on the shell are very unhygienic and can even cause illness.

Many people have the habit of placing the large end of the egg downwards and the small end upwards, but this is incorrect. According to experience, to keep eggs fresh longer and prevent the yolk from sticking to the shell, always keep the large end of the egg facing up, standing vertically; do not lay them flat or turn them upside down.

Do not store eggs in the refrigerator door because the door is opened frequently, causing the temperature there to be uneven and constantly changing, which makes the eggs spoil very quickly. Therefore, the best way is to wipe the eggs clean, wrap them in newspaper or put them in a cardboard box, and then store them inside the main refrigerator compartment.

If you have stored eggs in the refrigerator, keep them there; do not take them out and leave them in the external environment. At this point, the high external temperature will cause tiny water droplets to condense on the shell and seep into the egg, reducing its antibacterial ability and causing it to spoil faster.
If a refrigerator is not available, store eggs in a cool place to prevent spoilage.
Egg Storage Time
Eggs stored in the refrigerator should only be kept for 3 to 5 weeks. Eggs taken out of the refrigerator should be used within 2 hours; if left longer, they will spoil.
Only buy eggs stored in a cool place; check to ensure the eggs are not cracked or dirty; ensure the eggs are not expired; only choose to buy quarantined eggs.
Identifying Bleached Chicken Eggs

To sell eggs at a higher price, many sellers use acetic acid (found in lemons and vinegar) to bleach the color of industrial chicken eggs to make them look like local (ta) chicken eggs. To distinguish them, observe carefully: Industrial eggs are larger, weighing 55-60g, while local eggs are smaller, weighing only around 45g.

Bleached eggs have a slightly pinkish-white color, and the shell is rough, looking as if it is covered with a layer of white dust, not shiny and overly clean. In contrast, real local chicken eggs have a natural white color and may have some dirt sticking to the shell.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Frying Fish Without Breaking or Crumbling
mon_an.mo_ta: Do you know the tips for frying fish without it breaking or crumbling? Today, we will introduce these small tips for frying fish: – Clean the fish, marinate with spices, and pat dry before frying.
cac_buoc: Heat the pan first, then pour in the oil or fat, and add the fish after one minute.

After the pan has heated up, you can use a slice of raw ginger to rub firmly against the bottom and sides of the pan, then pour in the oil to fry the fish. The oil and raw ginger create a slippery film between the fish skin and the pan, preventing the skin from sticking.
If frying fish that has been marinated in salt, you must wash the fish thoroughly before putting it in the pan to prevent it from sticking and breaking.
When frying fish, do not use a flame that is too high, as this causes fresh fish to lose water quickly and makes the skin more likely to stick.

mon_an.ten: Effective Tips for Frying Tofu Without Sticking
mon_an.mo_ta: Fried tofu is a familiar dish, but making it golden, crispy, and not burnt is an art. Let's look at these great tips for frying tofu without sticking! Please refer to the following.
cac_buoc: Fried tofu is a simple, rustic dish loved by many, especially during cool weather. There is nothing better than enjoying hot, golden, crispy pieces of tofu dipped in a bowl of sweet and sour fish sauce.

However, sometimes frying tofu causes difficulties for home cooks, such as the tofu breaking, sticking to the pan, or being burnt on the outside while the inside is undercooked. Therefore, to make frying tofu easier, you can refer to the simple tips below.
The frying pan must be clean

If using a regular pan instead of a non-stick pan to fry tofu, you need to scrub it very clean before frying. Note: do not use a steel wool pad to scrub as it will scratch the pan, making the tofu stick even more easily. Just pour in hot water, and the old food will soften and peel off, then wash it thoroughly.
Drain the tofu or put it in the freezer before frying

Before frying tofu, you should cut it and let it drain completely. Alternatively, use a kitchen towel or paper to pat the tofu dry. Frying wet tofu not only causes oil splatters but also makes it stick to the pan more.

Alternatively, before frying, put the whole block of tofu in the freezer for 30 minutes, then take it out and cut it into small pieces. This tip helps the tofu become crispy and airy, keeps the pieces square and beautiful, and prevents them from breaking in the pan.
Preventing sticking while frying
Apply a little vinegar and coat the surface of the pan evenly after the pan is hot. Then add the oil, wait for the oil to boil, and drop the tofu in; the tofu will not stick to the pan.
Additionally, you can avoid sticking by frying an egg first after the oil is hot, then frying the tofu; the tofu will certainly no longer stick to the pan.
Frying the tofu

When starting to fry the tofu, you must ensure the oil is hot enough. Since it is not a non-stick pan, you can heat the pan until very hot before adding the oil (or fat), wait a bit longer, and then add the tofu; the tofu will be golden brown and won't stick.
Note: the oil in the pan should cover at least 1/4 to 1/3 of the tofu piece, and you should not wait until the oil is smoking hot as this will cause the tofu to burn quickly.
Do not let the tofu pieces touch each other, as they will be harder to remove. Additionally, since the oil is already quite hot, you should only fry over medium heat so the tofu doesn't burn.

To ensure the oil temperature in the pan is always even, you should only fry a moderate amount of tofu. Do not put too much tofu in the pan at once, as it lowers the oil temperature and the tofu will not cook evenly.

If the tofu happens to stick to the pan during frying, do not panic or rush to remove it, as this will break the tofu. You can turn off the stove, tilt the oil to one side, and wait for the pan to cool; the tofu will release itself and be much easier to remove.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Frying Crispy Golden Spring Rolls for a Perfect Tet Meal
mon_an.mo_ta: Fried spring rolls (nem rán) are an indispensable dish in Tet feasts. To have the most golden, crispy, and delicious spring rolls for these days, check out the frying tips below!
cac_buoc: Fried spring rolls are one of the traditional dishes for Tet. However, not everyone knows how to make them delicious and golden-crispy without burning, or how to freeze them for use throughout the Tet holiday.
Therefore, you can refer to the tips below for perfectly delicious spring rolls:
The Filling

When making the filling, note to use just enough eggs so the filling is neither too dry nor too wet. If the filling is dry, the spring rolls won't be tasty and lack the necessary softness. If the filling is too wet, the wrappers will easily burst during frying.
How to Wrap

When wrapping the spring rolls, be careful not to wrap them too tightly. This will cause the filling to expand slightly during frying, which tears the rice paper and causes the filling to spill out. Wrap them just enough; a slightly loose wrap is also fine.
Refrigerate Before Frying

Many experienced cooks share that spring rolls should not be fried immediately after wrapping. Instead, place them in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes to let them firm up and dry, which makes them very crispy when fried.
How to Make Spring Rolls Crispy
You can mix a bowl of diluted sugar water and brush it onto the unfried spring rolls. This will give the rolls a deep golden color and a crispy texture.

Alternatively, you can use a vinegar solution to brush on the rice paper. Take ½ bowl of water, add about 1 tbsp of rice vinegar, and stir well. Use this mixture to soften the rice paper while wrapping; it helps the spring rolls become crispier and look better when fried.
Frying the Spring Rolls
Method 1: Double Frying

After wrapping, fry the spring rolls in two stages. For the first time, heat the oil over low heat and fry the rolls until lightly cooked, then remove and place them on paper towels. After the first round, you can use fresh oil and fry them again until fully cooked; the crust will be golden and beautifully crispy.
Method 2: Deep Frying
With this method, the spring rolls will cook faster and achieve an even golden color on all sides. To save oil, you can use a deep-bottomed pan or a small saucepan for frying.
Method 3: Adding Lime Juice
When adding oil to the pan, add a few drops of lime juice. This prevents oil splatters and helps the spring rolls fry up crispy.
Freezing Spring Rolls Before Tet
If you don't have much time, you can wrap the spring rolls a few days before Tet and freeze them. During Tet, take out what you need each day to fry. Freezing spring rolls is not difficult.

After wrapping, place the spring rolls on a wide tray. Note: keep the rolls separated and put them in the freezer for about 40 minutes until they harden. Then, arrange the rolls into airtight containers. This prevents them from sticking together. When needed, take them directly from the freezer to the frying pan.
With this freezing method, you can keep the spring rolls for 2 weeks.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Cutting Onions Without Crying
mon_an.mo_ta: Cutting onions often makes you cry due to the juices they release. Today, we will introduce several very useful tips for cutting onions without tears that you should know.
cac_buoc: How to cut onions without crying
Step 1: Use a sharp knife

Cutting and slicing onions with a very sharp stainless steel knife dipped in water before starting will significantly reduce eye irritation. If cutting a large amount of onions, dip the knife in water frequently.
Step 2: Cut onions under water
Cutting onions under water or under a running tap also helps significantly because the water dissolves the sulfur compounds before they can reach your eyes.
Step 3: Use a potato
Rub a slice of fresh potato on both sides of the knife, then cut onions or chilies freely without worrying about stinging eyes.
Step 4: Chill the onions

Chilled onion cells react more slowly when cut. Therefore, place the onions in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes before cutting and peeling, or put them in the freezer for 10-15 minutes (depending on the size of the bulb).
Step 5: Don't use your hands

If the recipe requires finely chopped onions, simply put them in a food processor instead of cutting them by hand. Do not over-process the onions and wait for the onion vapors to settle before opening the lid.
Step 6: Use a candle
Light a candle very close to your cutting board when slicing onions so the heat can draw away the sulfur from the onion.
Step 7: Place a bowl of water nearby
You can also keep a bowl of cold water nearby and dip the knife into it frequently while cutting.
Step 8: Turn on a fan
Turn on a fan in the same direction you are sitting to blow away the onion droplets released during cutting. This method will help limit eye irritation.
Step 9: Chew continuously
Chew gum or any food in your mouth. This encourages you to breathe through your mouth, thereby absorbing the tiny droplets before they fly up to your eyes.
Step 10: Leave the root intact
Do you cut off both ends of the onion before slicing? You shouldn't! Try leaving the root end until the very last because sulfur compounds are more concentrated near the root.
Step 11: Limit exposure of the cut surfaces

Whether dicing or cutting into wedges, always cut the onion in half and place both flat sides down on the cutting board so the unpeeled part faces up. Once cut, move the pieces into a bowl and set them aside. This will limit eye irritation.
Step 12: Hold a piece of bread in your mouth

There is a small tip: if you hold a slice of bread (or any food) in your mouth while cutting onions, you won't cry. This tip stems from the idea that if you do something that forces you to breathe through your mouth, your nose will be less irritated and you will shed fewer tears.
Step 13: Cut the ends under water
Contrary to the method above, cut both ends of the onion under water. After that, you can slice the onion freely without worrying about crying.
Step 14: Vinegar

Spray the cutting board with a 50/50 mixture of vinegar and water, as vinegar has the ability to stop the sulfur reaction. If the mixture is not effective, try spraying pure vinegar on the board. However, this may affect the flavor of the cooked onions.
Step 15: Prep in bulk

If you frequently use onions for cooking, you can cut a large batch at once and store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator for later use. This saves time and reduces the number of times you have to deal with stinging eyes.
Step 16: Wear protective eyewear
To protect your eyes from the attack of onion vapors, you can wear protective glasses. Swimming goggles or gardening glasses both work, as long as they seal around your eyes.

Additionally, to wash the onion smell off your hands, you can rub your hands with dry salt, lemon juice, rub them against a stainless steel spoon, or rinse them under water before washing again with soap.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Beautiful Lotus Flower Plate Decoration
mon_an.mo_ta: Plate decoration is not just about simple food arrangement; it is an art to create a wonderful culinary experience. In the world of food styling, the lotus flower decoration tip has become a notable trend. With its delicate beauty and symbolism, the lotus image on a plate brings elegance and attraction. Let's explore tips for beautiful lotus flower plate decoration! Decorating a plate in the shape of a lotus is an exciting idea to create a highlight for the meal. Read these tips to learn how to carve and arrange ingredients delicately, creating unique and impressive culinary artworks.
cac_buoc: Step 1:

First, to decorate the plate with a beautiful lotus shape, use a knife to gently remove the green rind of the watermelon. Be careful and gentle, trying to take the whole piece of rind while keeping it thin and even. Note that the thinner and flatter the rind, the softer the lotus leaf will look when carved.
Step 2:

Next, to carve soft and lovely lotus leaves, use a pencil to sketch the leaf shapes first. Then, use the tip of a sharp knife to cut along the sketched outlines. Once the lotus leaves are separated from the rind, use the tip of the knife to make diagonal incisions on both sides to create the leaf veins. Refine them to look better, then soak all the lotus leaves in clean water.
With the remaining watermelon rind, you can carve additional small details for decoration such as lotus stamens, grass leaves, duckweed...

To create the lotus flower, cut the carrot into thin round slices. Lotus flowers have both irregular and regular petals; for symmetrical petals, just draw one petal first and overlap it onto another piece to create a matching symmetrical petal. For small lotus petals, you can draw them according to the size needed to fit the decorative plate.
To carve a fish, you should also sketch the shape on the carrot first to get a beautiful form. Then, use the tip of a sharp knife to carve according to the drawing.
Step 3:

When presenting on the plate, place the decoration on one side to leave space for the food. The principle is to arrange the lotus leaves first, creating a natural overlap that isn't too stiff or ostentatious. Once the leaves and stems are fixed, arrange the flowers to create balance.

Gently arrange each petal to form the shape of a lotus flower. You can add the stamen to the center when the lotus is in bloom. Arrange additional small duckweed, grass leaves, and two swimming fish to create a vivid picture on the plate.
Here are some plate decoration samples you can refer to:
Notes for lotus flower plate decoration

Choose the right type of watermelon: To get thin and flat rind, choose a watermelon with a thin skin that isn't too hard. The rind needs to be a vibrant green to provide a good background for the lotus shape.

Use appropriate tools: To remove the watermelon rind and carve the lotus leaves, use a paring knife and a sharp-tipped knife. This helps you work gently and accurately, avoiding damage to the rind or leaves.

Carve soft lotus leaves: When carving lotus leaves from the rind, sketch them first with a pencil to define the shape and then carve along the outlines. Remember to create the leaf veins by making diagonal incisions with the knife tip. This helps create a natural and soft shape for the lotus leaves.

Create beautiful lotus flowers: When carving lotus flowers from carrots, sketch first to define the shape and then use the knife to carve. For symmetrical petals, simply draw one petal and stack them to create other symmetrical petals. This helps create a beautiful and balanced lotus flower shape.

Arrange meticulously: When presenting on the plate, arrange the lotus leaves meticulously and naturally. Ensure the leaves overlap harmoniously and are not too stiff. Then, arrange the lotus flowers and other small details like stamens, duckweed, grass, or fish to create a vivid overall picture on the plate.
Utilize colors: Use the natural colors of watermelon and carrot to create highlights for the decoration. Ensure the color patches are distributed reasonably to create balance and harmony.
Perform carefully: Lotus flower plate decoration requires meticulousness and precision. Perform carefully and patiently to achieve the best results.
Conclusion

Decorating a plate in a lotus shape not only brings an attractive meal but also creates a unique work of art. By applying the above tips, you can create beautiful and impressive decorative plates that everyone will remember. Express your creativity to create wonderful culinary experiences for everyone to enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: Today, we would like to continue introducing meat preparation tips to you. Meat preparation tips.
cac_buoc: Old, tough meat can be tenderized if massaged with a little lemon juice and allowed to soak before frying. Meat will soften during the cooking process if a little vinegar is added (1-2 tablespoons of vinegar per 1 kg of meat).

Roasted meat will stay tender when basted with hot water or hot broth. Cold water will make the meat dry and tough. To prevent meat from burning while roasting, place a small pot of water in the oven; the steam will keep the meat from burning.

Steaks and cutlets will be tender if rubbed with a mixture of vinegar and cooking oil before frying. Additionally, all connective tissue and gristle should be removed so they maintain their required shape.
Meat will be juicy if blanched in boiling water before cooking and then simmered over low heat.
When mincing or pounding meat, use a wooden cutting board dipped in warm water. Do not add egg whites to minced meat patties, as this will cause the patties to fall apart and become dry.

Fried liver should not be marinated or seasoned with salt beforehand to keep it tender; it will taste better if soaked in milk for 2-3 hours before frying. The liver membrane can be easily removed after placing it in hot water for a couple of minutes.
Boiled sausages or blood sausages will not burst if pricked in a few places with a needle or a sharpened toothpick. These dishes will taste better if steamed or fried.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for Delicious Grilled Meat – Grilled meat has long been a favorite for many people. Making delicious grilled meat is not difficult, but sometimes we tend to let it get dry. The secrets below will help you have a perfectly grilled meat dish. These tips will introduce you to several tricks as well as delicious meat marinade recipes.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Marinating time

Home cooks often underestimate and spend too little time marinating meat, so the dish does not fully absorb the spices. Therefore, changing the marinating time is one of the tips for delicious grilled meat.

Normally, home cooks only marinate for about 30 - 60 minutes, which is too short. You should marinate longer; the best marinating time is from 6 - 8 hours, but leaving it that long may cause the spices to degrade due to prolonged exposure to air. Therefore, marinating for about 2 - 4 hours will make the meat flavorful while reducing harmful factors.
Step 2: Marinade spices

To marinate meat well, the spices are extremely important. As mentioned above, some types of spices will degrade when marinated for a long time, such as MSG; therefore, to make the meat dish tastier and more nutritious, you can skip the MSG.
You can refer to the following spices to marinate meat; this is also one of the *Tips for Delicious Grilled Meat*:

Use the following spices: crushed shallots, minced garlic, honey, oyster sauce, sesame oil (if available, it will make the meat more fragrant), cooking oil, black pepper, fish sauce, sugar, seasoning powder, coconut water, and baking soda.

Note: Coconut water and baking soda will make the meat very tender when marinated. You should use granulated sugar for marinating; the meat will not burn as easily when grilled compared to using rock sugar.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for Choosing Fresh Lemons – In the hot summer, a glass of fresh lemonade or iced milk lime is very delicious, but do you know the tips for choosing fresh lemons without preservatives? Tips for choosing fresh lemons for deliciousness and food safety.
cac_buoc: Fresh lemons serve as a refreshing drink, an ingredient for fragrant sweet and sour dipping sauces that aren't as harsh as vinegar, and they are also effective for removing stains. However, currently on the market, fresh lemons are often sprayed with many types of preservatives and anti-mold agents, which are very harmful to consumers. This article will provide you with some tips to distinguish between good fresh lemons and those sprayed with chemicals.
When you lightly press or scratch the lemon peel and see oil spray out with a fragrant scent, this is a quality lemon that has not been soaked in chemicals.
Choose lemons that feel heavy for their size, have a bright color, and are medium-sized. Medium-sized lemons that feel firm and heavy are usually better and juicier than large, light ones.

Choose lemons with smooth, thin skin, without lumps or rough patches, and avoid those that are dull green or pale yellow. Smooth-skinned lemons usually contain more vitamins than lumpy ones. Lemons with dull or pale yellow colors are those that were harvested a long time ago, which will make your cooking less delicious and affect your health.

Do not choose lemons with a pungent smell: Fruits containing chemicals often have a pungent, unpleasant odor because they were brought to market before the withdrawal period after spraying was over. You can check by putting the lemons in a plastic bag, tying it for a moment, then opening it to smell. If there are residual chemicals, there will be a slightly pungent smell.

Check the origin of the lemons. A safe cultivation process is the decisive factor in ensuring lemons are not contaminated. Therefore, you should choose fruit with a clear origin (when buying at the supermarket) or ask the seller. This is especially important if you use the lemon zest for baking or direct consumption.

Above are some tips for choosing fresh lemons to ensure health for home cooks and the whole family. However, above all, you should choose to buy lemons from trusted wholesalers or retailers where the origin is more guaranteed.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Choosing and Preparing Duck
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for Choosing and Preparing Duck – This article provides tips for choosing and preparing duck so that you can enjoy delicious duck dishes. Learn how to cook delicious meals with these tips for choosing and preparing duck.
cac_buoc: Summer is the season for delicious duck dishes like duck braised with dracontomelon, duck with bamboo shoots, etc. Therefore, choosing good ducks that are not too fatty, have sweet tender meat, and do not smell gamey is a top priority for home cooks.
1. How to choose duck:
In cooking, female ducks are preferred because their meat is much softer and sweeter than male ducks. Additionally, duck meat is divided into many types, each with its own way of selection.

Grass duck (Vịt cỏ): Gray-brown feathers, smaller than common ducks or Muscovy ducks; this is the type most commonly sold at markets and supermarkets. Grass duck meat is not greasy because it has little fat, soft bones, and sweet, tender meat. Grass duck is great for braising, ginger-braised, porridge, or soup.

Muscovy duck (Vịt xiêm): Blue-black feathers, large size about 3-4.5kg. Muscovy duck has firm meat, is very lean, and tastes delicious. Compared to other ducks, Muscovy duck is more expensive and suitable for dishes that require long cooking times like double-steaming, cooking with fermented bean curd, "fake dog meat" style, braising, stewing... For duck porridge, Muscovy duck is the best.

Common duck (Vịt ta): White feathers, large size about 3 kg. This type is commonly sold at markets and supermarkets. Common duck is fatty with thick, sweet meat; it is not as good for porridge as Muscovy duck, but if making "cháo cối" (where the duck is straw-singed, marinated, then cooked), then an egg-laying duck is very good. Since common ducks are large and fatty, if you like meat that has both fat and thick lean portions, choose this one. Common duck is used for braising with ginger or lemongrass, cooking with fermented bean curd, bamboo shoots, soup, grilling...
2. Tips for preparing duck

To make plucking easier, after bleeding the duck, dip it immediately into cold water so the water soaks through the body. Then, heat water for blanching. The water should only be at a light simmer (rolling boils will tear the skin) before putting the duck in to soak evenly. If the wing feathers pull out easily, remove the duck and clean the feathers. Pluck in the direction of growth, pressing your hand close to the skin.
When cleaning the duck, cut off the oil gland at the tail because this is a scent gland; if you aren't used to it, it will smell very gamey.

Small tip: To prevent the duck from having a gamey smell, use crushed ginger or wine to rub all over the body, then rinse with clean water or diluted salt water. For dishes where the duck is chopped up, you can briefly blanch the pieces in boiling water and rinse with cold water to remove any remaining odor.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Preserving Vitamin A During Cooking
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for Preserving Vitamin A During Cooking – Vitamins are easily lost during food preparation, especially Vitamin A. This article will provide a few tips to limit the loss of Vitamin A during cooking. To cook without losing nutrients beneficial for health, especially Vitamin A, please refer to the following article:
cac_buoc: Studies show that washed vegetables stored in the refrigerator spoil quickly, while if left outside for a day, the amount of Vitamin A decreases by 26%. To keep vitamins at the highest level, home cooks need to work quickly when preparing vegetables. Wash vegetables before chopping, and cook them immediately after preparation. There are many ways to cook vegetables, but steaming is the method that helps retain the most Vitamin A. It is best to wash vegetables when you buy them and store them in a well-ventilated place.

Besides steaming, stir-frying also helps retain vitamins in vegetables better, especially Vitamins A and C. However, for stir-fried dishes, you need to use high heat and toss quickly, then eat while hot, because if prepared in advance and then reheated, up to 90% of the vitamins are lost.

A very important task before preparing vegetables to avoid the risk of food poisoning is to wash each stalk individually in a large basin of water, or wash them under running water to remove dirt, parasites, worm eggs, and toxic chemicals remaining on the vegetables.

Note: When boiling vegetables, add a little salt to the water and keep the lid closed. A little salt helps maintain the green color of the vegetables, while a closed lid minimizes vitamin loss to about 15%; opening the lid will cause a 32% loss.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Quick and Clean House Cleaning for Tet
mon_an.mo_ta: Cleaning the house always takes a lot of time and effort. Below are some tips to help you clean faster, cleaner, and without too much effort.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Discard unnecessary items

This is the top priority task to help your home become tidy. If your family has many small items, you can arrange them neatly in one corner. Items that are no longer usable or useful should be thrown away or given to those who need them.
Step 2: Clean tables and chairs

For fabric or velvet upholstered sofas, you can dilute alcohol, use a brush to clean, and then dry. If there are stains on the sofa surface, use a cloth dampened with a mixture of baking soda and clean water to wipe.
If the furniture is made of wood, you can use a clean rag dipped in fresh milk to wipe, then wipe again with clean water.
Step 3: Clean the refrigerator
To clean the outside of the refrigerator, use a soft cloth with a little toothpaste.

For the inside, to limit odors, simply place thin slices of lemon or a piece of bread inside. This is an extremely effective deodorizing method. When wiping the inside, you can use baking soda and water.
Step 4: Clean the kitchen

For kitchen countertops, you can use a slice of cucumber or carrot to rub on them and then wipe with clean water. For greasy sinks, you should clean them after every use so your sink is always sparkling. You can use hot water combined with dish soap.
Step 5: Clean carpets

You can use a vacuum cleaner to clean carpets. If gum is stuck to the carpet, use a plastic bag to wrap some ice cubes and place them on top; once the gum hardens, you can remove it easily. If the carpet is wet from soda or tea, sprinkle baking soda on it and then use a vacuum to clean.
Step 6: Clean tea sets and dishes

To clean tea sets for Tet, add a little vinegar to the dishwater. This method not only removes grease and stains but also helps dishes look brighter and cleaner. Besides vinegar, you can use lemon as a substitute for great results.
Step 7: Clean mirrors and glass doors
For windows with lots of glass or mirrors in the house, instead of using detergents, use vinegar to wipe them clean.
Step 8: Clean the microwave

To clean the microwave, use water with about a tablespoon of vinegar in a small bowl and place it inside. Next, set the temperature to medium-high for about 5 minutes and then wipe as usual. You can also sprinkle a little salt inside, turn it on, and once the oven cools, use a warm sponge to wipe it clean.
Step 9: Clean the bathroom

To clean the bathroom, tidy up and remove old bottles, empty toothpaste tubes, toilet paper rolls... Then, use a cloth soaked in vinegar to wipe the toilet, sink... Close the bathroom door for about 20-30 minutes, then return to scrub with a brush; the stains will be easily removed.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Removing Burnt Food Odors
mon_an.mo_ta: The tips shared below will help you remove burnt food odors, bringing back delicious and healthy meals.
cac_buoc: How to remove burnt food odors
Let the food cool completely
When you detect a burnt smell, turn off the stove immediately. Then, use oven mitts to lift the hot pot off the stove so the food doesn't burn further.
You can use a wet towel to cover the pot or pan containing the burnt food until the towel cools completely. This is a secret to help take away the smoke and burnt smell lingering on the food.
Remove the burnt parts
For grilled dishes, the only way to save them is to use scissors to cut off the over-burnt parts that are no longer edible and utilize the remaining parts.

For fried dishes, quickly remove the food from the oil and discard all the old burnt oil; wash and dry the pan. The over-burnt parts should also be cut off; the rest depends on the doneness of the food to decide whether to re-fry or not.

For braised dishes, quickly pick out the usable parts; do not be greedy and take too much, including parts near the burnt areas. If the burnt smell is still strong, you can take the food out, rinse it with clean water, pat dry, place in a new pot, and re-season.

For soups and stews: Use a spoon to skim off the unburnt liquid and transfer it to another pot, avoiding heavy movements or scooping too deep into the burnt part to ensure the smallest burnt bits do not stick to the spoon.
Add water
For foods with a firm and hard texture like meat, fish, vegetables... rinse the burnt food under the tap to clean off all the burnt bits still clinging to the food.
Dry the food
After rinsing with water, you need to dry the wet food or green vegetables by using paper towels to absorb excess water.
Add sauce and spices

Start cooking the food that has been freed from the burnt layers again and add plenty of sauce. You should combine chicken with tomato sauces, or use butter sauce for fish dishes. Add spices to the dish: salt, pepper, and others according to your preference. For soups or stews, you can hide the burnt smell and bitter taste by adding bacon to the dish.
With just a little ingenuity and variation in processing, you can remove the burnt smell of food and make the meal tastier!

mon_an.mo_ta: To boil meat perfectly, you always need your own secrets. We will share with you cool tips to help you have fresh, delicious, and attractive boiled meat dishes.
cac_buoc: How to boil pork

First, wash the meat thoroughly under the tap, then drop the pork into a pot of water with a little salt and a few drops of vinegar. After boiling for 3 minutes, remove the meat and wash it clean; this method helps the meat have a beautiful white color.

Then, boil another pot of water, add dried shallots or a bit of white wine, and boil until the meat is cooked. The aroma of the shallots or white wine will remove the gamey smell of the pork and make the dish tastier.
How to boil chicken

To boil chicken until just cooked, tender, and fragrant without the skin cracking, first place the cleaned chicken in a pot and pour cold water to submerge the body. Heat until it reaches a gentle simmer. Be careful not to let it boil vigorously, as the skin will easily crack. At this point, skim off the foam and let it simmer for about 7 - 8 minutes.

Next, grill 1 ginger root and 1 shallot, crush them, and add to the pot, then continue boiling. If it is a young chicken, boil for another 5 minutes; if it is slightly older, boil for another 10 minutes. Then, turn off the heat, cover with a lid, and soak the chicken in the water for another 5 minutes.

To check if the chicken is cooked, use a chopstick to pierce the meat; if it pierces easily and the juice that comes out is not pink, it is done. To make the skin crispy and golden, drop the chicken into very cold water immediately after removing it; once completely cool, take it out, drain, and you can brush a layer of chicken fat mixed with fresh turmeric on the skin.
How to boil duck or goose

First, clean the duck/goose and remove the odor by rubbing it with a little salt, ginger, and white wine both inside and out, then rinse and drain. Place the duck in a pot and pour enough water to submerge it so the meat stays white and doesn't turn dark.

Next, add a small piece of crushed ginger to the pot to prevent a gamey smell. Turn the heat to high until the water boils. Once boiling, use a spoon to skim off all the foam. Add a spoonful of soup powder and peeled grilled shallots to the pot, then cover. Turn the heat to low and simmer for about 25 - 30 minutes until the meat is cooked.
How to boil beef

The way to boil beef so it is fragrant and not tough or dry is to marinate the beef with ginger, lemongrass, cinnamon, star anise, and salt overnight or for 5-6 hours in the refrigerator before placing it in a pot of cold water to submerge the meat. Cook the beef over low heat for 20-30 minutes depending on the thickness.
When you can pierce it with a chopstick, the beef is cooked. However, you should limit piercing the meat multiple times to check.
How to boil chitterlings

To boil pork chitterlings so they are white, crispy, and not smelly, wait for the water to reach a rolling boil before dropping them in so they are just cooked and crunchy. Usually, the total time from putting them in the boiling water to taking them out is about 7-10 minutes (depending on the quantity).

Once cooked, remove the chitterlings and immediately drop them into a bowl of ice water with squeezed lemon, ensuring they are fully submerged. The sudden cooling combined with the acidity will help the chitterlings become white and crispy.
With these small tips, we hope you will have delicious, rich, and fragrant boiled meat slices.

mon_an.mo_ta: These useful tips will help you defrost food quickly while preserving its nutrients, ensuring your dishes remain delicious.
cac_buoc: 1. Defrost in the refrigerator

This is the safest way to defrost as it prevents bacteria from attacking the food. Method: Move the food from the freezer to the refrigerator compartment. However, this method is quite time-consuming and can take a whole day. It is suitable if you plan to cook something the next day; simply leave the food in the fridge overnight and take it out when you are ready to prep. An advantage of this method is that if you decide not to cook it, you can safely return it to the freezer without hygiene concerns.
Note: To prevent liquid from the defrosting process from leaking into the fridge, you should wrap the food in a plastic bag or place it in a glass bowl.
2. Defrosting food properly with cold water

To defrost food faster, take the frozen food directly from the freezer and pour a little water over the bag. This method is quicker and limits the loss of nutrients. However, you must ensure the food does not come into direct contact with the water and must be submerged in cold water. Submerging food in hot water or direct contact with water creates a favorable environment for bacteria to grow, which is unsafe. Note that you should change the water every 30 minutes and do not soak the food for too long in cold water to ensure the defrosting temperature prevents bacterial invasion while retaining nutrients. This way, you can shorten the defrosting process to 1-2 hours.
3. Add salt and ginger to preserve nutrients during defrosting

To retain the nutrients in the food while soaking in cold water to defrost, you can add a tablespoon of salt or some crushed ginger. This helps meat, fish, or other frozen foods retain more nutrients and look fresher.
4. Tips for using defrosted food correctly
You do not need to defrost food completely before cooking; this prevents the natural juices from being lost and allows them to soak into the sauce or accompanying ingredients during cooking.
It is best to cook the food immediately after defrosting and cut large pieces of meat for processing.
You should not defrost food in the microwave because the food will be cooked on the outside while remaining raw on the inside, losing its natural sweetness when cooked.

Another small tip to defrost meat extremely quickly and safely at home: use two aluminum pots. Place one pot upside down, fill the other with water, and place the meat to be defrosted between the two pots. Your meat will be defrosted in just 5 minutes.
With the tips shared above, we hope you can defrost food faster while still preserving its nutritional value.

mon_an.ten: Handy Kitchen Hacks for Home Cooks
mon_an.mo_ta: Great kitchen hacks for home cooks to handle various situations in the kitchen. Explore these tips to improve your cooking skills.
cac_buoc: Preserving the color of food
Fruits and vegetables such as apples, pears, and potatoes often turn brown after peeling. To prevent this, soak them in diluted salt water. This reduces oxidation and maintains their beautiful color.
Fixing over-sweetened food
In cooking, it is common to over-season. Let's learn some handy hacks for when you accidentally add too much sweetness.
If you season a dish too sweet, you can add a little salt or apple cider vinegar. Your dish will be more balanced and carry the characteristic aroma of apple cider vinegar.
Fixing salty food

For dishes that are too salty, you can add sugar or apple cider vinegar. They will help significantly reduce the saltiness. If these two ingredients are not available, you can also use a slice of potato; potatoes are excellent at absorbing excess salt from a dish.
Tips for boiling delicious corn

For boiled corn, unlike other boiled vegetables, adding salt will make the corn tough. Instead, use a little sugar. This will make the corn taste sweeter, softer, and more fragrant, while also helping it cook faster.
Reducing fat
Sometimes we find dishes too greasy but don't know how to reduce the excess oil. Here are some handy hacks for home cooks:
Drop a few ice cubes into the pot of soup; the excess grease will cling to the surface of the ice. Quickly remove the ice cubes before they melt too much.

Cut a few pieces of plastic wrap, crumple them up, and stir gently on the surface of the dish. The grease will stick to the plastic wrap and come right out. However, do not apply this to boiling hot dishes; it is best when the food is slightly warm.
Place a few chicory leaves on the surface of the cooking soup or stew. The chicory will absorb the excess fat.
Wait for the dish to cool completely, then place it in the refrigerator. After a few hours, the excess oil and fat on the surface will solidify, and you can easily scoop it off.

mon_an.ten: Effective Tips to Quickly Remove Burnt Smells from Food
mon_an.mo_ta: In the kitchen, no matter how skilled you are, accidents like burnt food can happen. It can be difficult to remove the burnt smell spreading through the kitchen. Here are some great tips to handle these situations! Effective tips to quickly remove burnt smells from food:
cac_buoc: When you detect burnt food, turn off the stove immediately, then use oven mitts to remove the pot or pan from the heat to stop it from burning further. Place it in a cool, ventilated area and put a wet towel over the top of the pot or pan; wait until the pot cools completely, and the unpleasant burnt smell will subside. Additionally, open all windows, turn on the exhaust fan, and use the range hood to prevent the kitchen from smelling like burnt food.
For burnt grilled items like grilled patties, meat, or fish, you can use scissors or a knife to trim away the charred edges and keep the edible parts.

For braised or stewed dishes where the burn is usually at the bottom, do not waste it by throwing it all away. Save the edible part by using a ladle to scoop the top portion into another pot. For dishes with broth, discard the liquid, take the edible parts and rinse them briefly with cold water, then you can choose to cook them again depending on how well-done the food is.
A small tip to handle the burnt smell in braised dishes is to add a few pieces of bread or some potato batons; they can absorb the burnt odor from the food.

For fried or stir-fried items, if the cooking oil has a burnt smell, you should discard it and not use it again. The main component of cooking oil is fat; at excessively high temperatures, these fats denature, which is harmful to the body and ruins the flavor of your food.
