When reheating food, you can add extra seasonings like onion, garlic, pepper, tomato sauce, butter, or bacon. These ingredients have strong characteristic flavors that can mask other odors, thereby reducing the burnt smell of the food.

A small tip to keep your kitchen smelling fresh and remove burnt odors quickly is to keep a handful of tangerine peels or dry tea leaves in a dry spot in the kitchen. Tangerine peels and dry tea are very effective at absorbing odors. Alternatively, you can use clove water: boil cloves in a pot of water and leave it in the kitchen for 10-30 minutes. The burnt smell will vanish faster. You can also use lemon-scented spray around the kitchen to mask the odor.
Note:
Limit marinating food with sugar or seasoning powder when frying or pan-searing. These seasonings burn easily and stick to the surface, causing the outside to burn while the inside remains raw.
Use a timer for dishes that require long cooking times.
Stay calm when handling burnt food to avoid burning your hands.

For pots and pans with burnt food, after processing the food, you must scrub them thoroughly, boil them with water, and rinse with cold water to ensure no burnt residue remains to affect the next dish.
Place burnt food in a plastic bag, tie it tightly, and put it in the trash so the smell does not spread.

mon_an.mo_ta: Not only a healthy beverage, tea also has many other uses in the kitchen and daily life. Some very useful tea hacks include: deodorizing, absorbing moisture, tenderizing meat, and more. Refer to these tea hacks for more useful knowledge!
cac_buoc: Useful tea hacks:

Absorbing moisture: After drying used tea dregs, place them in small cloth bags and put them in high-humidity areas like kitchen cabinets or wardrobes. The tea dregs will absorb excess moisture, provide a gentle fragrance, and help prevent mold.

Deodorizing the refrigerator: To deodorize the fridge, place some dried tea dregs or dry tea leaves in the back corner. Tea is quite effective at deodorizing and killing bacteria, helping your fridge stay clean and fresh.

Repelling flies and mosquitoes: Simply burn a little dry tea in the house, and insects like flies, mosquitoes, ants, and cockroaches will stay away. The scent of tea leaves not only provides a pleasant aroma but also repels insects effectively. This is a great way to keep a tidy kitchen. You will no longer worry about cockroaches or ants running around the kitchen ruining things!

Tenderizing tough meat: No matter how tough the meat is, it will soften if you marinate it in black tea. Method: Pour 4 tbsp of black tea into a cup of warm water, steep for 5 minutes, then strain. Pour this tea into half a cup of brown sugar and stir to dissolve. Season the meat with salt, pepper, onion, and garlic powder in a pot with a lid. Pour the tea and sugar mixture over the seasoned meat and simmer on low heat until the meat is tender.

Deodorizing new cutting boards and wooden items: New cutting boards and wooden utensils often have an unpleasant varnish smell. Simply use tea water to wipe them down a few times, and the varnish smell will disappear completely.
Other useful hacks:

Improving sleep: According to traditional Chinese medicine, using pillows stuffed with tea dregs can help lower blood pressure, overcome insomnia, and soothe headaches. However, tea dregs in a pillow can quickly become damp from sweat. Therefore, you should regularly sun-dry these pillows to prevent mold growth.
Cleaning carpets: Spread damp tea dregs over the surface of dirty carpets before vacuuming. The tea dregs will absorb dust and dirt trapped in the carpet.

Making fertilizer: Soak tea leaves in water for about two days, then strain out the dregs and use the tea water to water your plants. This is considered a very good fertilizer due to the nutrients in the tea. Do not use the dregs directly as they can attract pests and insects.
Foot soak: Tea water is one of the secrets to eliminating foot odor. Brew a very strong pot of tea and soak your feet while the water is still warm.
Preventing acne: To soothe active acne, simply crush green tea leaves and apply them to the affected area, then rinse with water. Green tea has antibacterial properties that help prevent acne.

mon_an.ten: Tips to Quickly and Effectively Reduce Saltiness in Dried Fish
mon_an.mo_ta: In daily Vietnamese cuisine, dishes like dried fish and dried shrimp are very popular. However, to preserve these foods for a long time, they are often heavily salted. Here are some tips to reduce the saltiness of dried fish.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Soak dried fish in diluted salt water

You might think soaking salty fish in salt water makes it saltier, but that is not the case. The salt concentration in the diluted salt water is lower than in the dried fish, causing the salt in the fish to diffuse into the water. Soak the dried fish in diluted salt water for 30 minutes, remove, and soak again in fresh diluted salt water for another 30 minutes. The saltiness will decrease noticeably.
Step 2: Soak dried fish in diluted lemon water

Soaking in lemon water significantly reduces the saltiness of dried fish; however, it can make the fish sour, affecting your dish. Therefore, make the lemon water very diluted! You can mix 1 bowl of water with 1/4 bowl of lemon juice and soak for 30 minutes.
Step 3: Soak dried fish in rice water
Rice water has many miraculous uses and is extremely cheap. After washing rice to cook, keep the rice water and soak the dried fish in it for about 30 minutes; the fish will become much less salty.
Step 4: Marinate dried fish with sweet and sour seasonings
For sweet and sour dried fish dishes, you should marinate the fish beforehand with sugar, honey, lemon, or vinegar to reduce the saltiness and make it more flavorful during cooking.
Above are a few tips to reduce the saltiness of dried fish; you can also apply these to dried shrimp or similar salty dried foods.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Making Perfect Fried Shallots
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for making perfect fried shallots – Hacks for making fried shallots for dishes like steamed rice rolls and salads to make them more fragrant and delicious.
cac_buoc: Fragrant fried shallots have long been an indispensable topping for many dishes. Making good fried shallots requires tips from choosing the shallots to the cooking process and storage.
Choose shallots with brown skins that feel firm and are not damaged, sprouted, or rotten. Peel the shallots, wash them, and let them dry completely.

Usually, slicing 1-2 shallots won't make your eyes sting, but for the large quantity needed for fried shallots, it is best to soak them in ice water for 30 minutes before slicing them very thinly. Every 2-3 shallots, rinse the knife once and do not wipe it dry to prevent your eyes from stinging.
Next, spread the shallots out to air dry slightly; if there is no sun, drying them in a cool, ventilated place is fine.

Add cooking oil to a pan. Once the oil is hot, add the shallots so they are completely submerged in oil. To save oil, you should use a thick pot with a moderate diameter. During the frying process, do not stir too much to avoid breaking them; just stir gently occasionally.

Fry until the shallots turn a light golden color, then use a mesh strainer to remove them onto paper towels. Note: do not wait until they are fully browned because they will continue to cook while hot on the plate; they will reach a perfect golden brown once cooled. Wait until they are completely cool before storing in an airtight jar for later use.

mon_an.ten: Essential Kitchen Hacks You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: When cooking, you will often encounter situations where the dish doesn't turn out as expected. Below are essential kitchen hacks you should know for better meals.
cac_buoc: 1. How to handle greasy dishes

If you accidentally add too much oil, your dish will be difficult to eat and easily becomes cloying, but throwing it away is wasteful. Follow this method to remove excess grease: Drop an ice cube into the pot. Once the fat solidifies on the surface, simply use a spoon to scoop it out. It's that simple. This will make your dish less greasy and much lighter.
2. Fruits that should not be refrigerated

Normally, we keep food fresh by putting it in the fridge. However, note that you should not store the following fruits this way: oranges, apples, pears, bananas, tomatoes, avocados, and peppers. Keep these fruits in a cool, ventilated place and do not buy too many at once, as they will lose their freshness and nutrients over time.
3. Preventing salt from clumping

If salt is stored for a long time or not properly, it can easily clump. Don't worry; this small tip will solve the problem: Put a few grains of rice into a small cloth or mesh bag and place it in the salt container. Rice is excellent at absorbing moisture and will keep the salt dry and free-flowing. Your salt will stay perfectly dry and won't become watery.
4. Tip for keeping bread fresh longer

Bread is difficult to preserve; if not eaten immediately, it becomes stale, chewy, or hard. This method will help keep bread fresh longer: Take a plastic bag and a washed, dried stalk of celery. Place both the bread and the celery in the bag and tie it tightly. Since celery does not have a strong scent, it won't affect the flavor of the bread but will keep it fresh.
5. How to fix salty soup

If your soup is too salty because you over-seasoned it, it is easy to fix. The simplest way is to take a potato, wash and peel it, then add it to the soup. Potatoes are high in starch and absorb salt very well. If you don't have a potato, put a handful of rice in a cheesecloth or mesh bag and drop it into the soup; rice works similarly to potatoes as its high starch content quickly absorbs the saltiness.
These are kitchen hacks to help home cooks fix mistakes in processing and preserving food. Apply these small tips for yourself and your family to enjoy delicious meals!

mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for identifying safe food help you buy the freshest ingredients by recognizing which foods contain preservatives, pesticides, etc., for healthier and more delicious meals.
cac_buoc: This article provides ways to identify food that uses preservatives or growth stimulants so you can avoid unsafe products and learn tips for identifying safe food.

For vegetables: Currently, green vegetables are often sprayed with pesticides or preservatives to keep them fresh longer. If you see leaves that look younger than normal, are dark green, brittle, and have almost no insect holes, these are likely vegetables that have been over-fertilized or sprayed with pesticides without ensuring the proper withdrawal period. Consuming these over time will bring toxins into your body.

For fruits: If the surface of the fruit is very shiny and it stays fresh for a long time without rotting, these are fruits treated with pesticides to kill fungi and bacteria for preservation. Specifically for jackfruit and durian: If the fruit is ripe but the segments lack the characteristic aroma, these were likely harvested green and injected with chemicals to ripen them quickly.

For fish: Rivers and lakes are facing pollution, so farmed fish is more common than wild-caught fish. However, farmed fish meat is not as firm or sweet as wild fish, and farmers sometimes use antibiotics. These fish are often weak, the meat is bland, and they spoil quickly. When cooked, the meat shrinks significantly.

Bean sprouts: Although they have a short harvest time, to increase profits, some sellers mix sprouts with numerous growth chemicals overnight. If the sprouts are white, thick, plump, brittle, and have almost no roots, they have been treated with water-retention chemicals and root-killers. Despite the harmful chemicals, these sprouts often look very attractive to shoppers.

For pork: If the meat is almost entirely lean with no fat and has a dark red color like beef, it likely comes from pigs treated with growth stimulants containing corticoids. Consuming food with corticoids can cause metabolic disorders and bladder cancer.

Glass noodles, rice vermicelli, and phở noodles: Normally, these rice-based products should be an off-white color and not overly brittle or chewy. If they look clearer than usual, the manufacturer may have used bleaching chemicals. If these noodles are left overnight at room temperature and do not spoil, preservatives (mainly formalin) were likely added. Consuming these can damage the mucous membranes of the stomach and esophagus.

mon_an.ten: Tips to Distinguish Between Korean and Chinese Enoki Mushrooms
mon_an.mo_ta: At major wholesale markets, enoki mushrooms labeled as imported from Korea are sold extensively. However, most of these packages do not print packaging or expiration dates. While the packaging states they must be stored at 1-5°C to be safe, they are often sold in the open at temperatures over 30°C. Mr. Vu Oanh, a representative of Hung Phat Green Technology Company (Biovegi brand), stated: "Currently, enoki mushrooms in Vietnam have many distributors, each with their own sources mainly from Korea and China. Since this mushroom is difficult to grow, domestic production cannot meet demand. Daily consumption can reach several tons, while Vietnamese facilities only produce 10-20kg." Here is how to distinguish between Korean and Chinese mushrooms!
cac_buoc: To avoid buying Chinese enoki mushrooms, according to Mr. Vu Oanh, consumers can rely on the following information to distinguish between those imported from China and Korea:

Origin information on the packaging: The quality of the packaging and the plastic material of Korean enoki mushrooms feels soft to the touch, with clear printing and bright colors. In contrast, Chinese packaging is stiffer and cloudier.
Information about the distributor and importer is printed fully and clearly on the packaging. Consumers can distinguish them by checking the barcode: 880 is Korea, while 690 to 695 is China.
Visually, Korean enoki mushrooms have an ivory-white color rather than the pure white of Chinese enoki mushrooms.
We hope you find this information useful for choosing high-quality, safe mushrooms!

mon_an.ten: Tips for Extending Food Shelf Life
mon_an.mo_ta: Tips for extending food shelf life will help you preserve food longer and save costs. Below are some tips to help you cook more economically while maintaining nutritional value.
cac_buoc: Tips for extending the shelf life of Meat
Using vacuum bags will help you preserve meat much longer in the freezer for later use. You no longer have to worry about wasteful disposal.
Honey

When buying honey in the supermarket, we often see an expiration date. However, for honey, you can temporarily ignore it because honey can be kept much longer. If the honey crystallizes, simply heat it up to melt the sugar and you can continue using it for a long time.
Tips for extending the shelf life of Nuts and Seeds
Nuts and seeds like peanuts, beans, and dried lotus seeds are usually kept well for a few months, but you can keep them for up to a year by packaging and storing them in the refrigerator.
Spices and dried herbs

Perform a small test to see if they are still usable by smelling them. If the dried herbs have faded in color but the scent is still strong when you squeeze or crush them in your palm, they are still usable. Store them in a cool, dry place in airtight containers to preserve them for when needed.

mon_an.mo_ta: Salt Hacks – Salt is not just a common seasoning for meals; it also has many unexpected uses. These salt hacks will help you prepare more delicious and diverse dishes.
cac_buoc: Prevent meat and cakes from sticking to the grill

Whenever you grill meat or bake cakes, it can be frustrating when they stick to the grate. To fix this, dip a cloth in salt water and wipe the grill grate; the meat or cakes will no longer stick while cooking.
Extend the shelf life of cheese

For cheese, simply wrap it in a cloth dampened with salt water before placing it in the refrigerator. This method significantly increases the preservation time for fresh milk and cheese. However, to prevent the cheese from becoming too salty, use a very diluted salt solution.
Boil eggs faster
Add a little salt to the boiling water; your eggs will cook faster and be much easier to peel.
Remove onion and garlic smells from hands
Soak your hands in salt water or vinegar to completely eliminate the smell of onions or garlic lingering on your skin. This is one of the most effective salt hacks.
Check egg freshness

Eggs are a staple in every household, so choosing fresh ones improves the quality of your meals. Simply add 2 tbsp of salt to a glass of water and drop the egg in. If it is fresh, the egg will sink; if it is old, it will float on the surface.
Clean vegetables and prevent browning in fresh produce

Certain fruits and vegetables like apples, pears, and potatoes oxidize and turn brown quickly after peeling. To prevent this, soak them in diluted salt water; they will retain their natural color for your family meals.
Before preparing fresh vegetables, soak them in cold water mixed with salt for about 15 minutes, then rinse under running water. This method helps wash away dirt and sand while also killing bacteria.

mon_an.mo_ta: Continuing our series on kitchen hacks, today we introduce some tips for preparing dishes from fish, poultry, and birds. First, for fish dishes, please note:
cac_buoc: Fish scales are easier to clean if you soak the fish in cold water mixed with a little vinegar (2 tbsp per 1 liter of water).
Frozen fish should only be thawed by soaking in cold water to preserve its natural sweetness.
The muddy pond smell of fish will disappear if you soak the cleaned fish in water mixed with a little vinegar, pepper, and bay leaves for about 1 hour.
Fish will taste better if soaked in milk for about an hour after cleaning. Then, season with salt and cook.
The fishy or unpleasant odor of certain fish will vanish if you add a few pieces of potato to the pan while frying.
Tips for cooking and preparing fish dishes
For poultry and birds:
Pluck the feathers immediately after slaughtering.
Before frying an old chicken, boil it first, then coat it with dry breadcrumbs and brush with heavy cream before frying.
To keep the chicken skin clean and white, you can use alcohol to lightly singe it after plucking.
To make poultry meat delicious and tender, rub the inside and outside with lemon juice or vinegar before cooking or frying.
Geese should be dry-plucked; the meat will taste better.
Tips for preparing poultry and birds

mon_an.mo_ta: Mulberry syrup is a delicious refreshing drink for the summer. Besides its refreshing effect, it has many useful health benefits. We will guide you through some mulberry syrup hacks for your health.
cac_buoc: Some medicinal remedies from mulberry syrup
1. Refreshment and treating constipation
Drink 2 glasses of mulberry juice per day to clear heat and quench thirst.
With 3 glasses of mulberry juice per day, the high Vitamin C content will effectively treat constipation.
2. Stimulate appetite, improve sleep, and boost health
Drink 1-2 glasses of mulberry juice before meals to stimulate digestion and improve appetite and overall health.
Mulberry-infused water is a very healthy fruit drink.
After dinner, drinking a glass of mulberry juice will help you fall asleep faster and enjoy a deeper sleep.
3. Relieve muscle and joint pain
Regularly drink three glasses of mulberry juice a day (morning, noon, and night) to treat muscle and joint aches.
Promote rosy skin, blood circulation, and regular menstruation
Regularly drink 2 glasses of mulberry juice a day in the morning and at noon.
Drink continuously for 3 months to see rosy skin, improved blood circulation, and regular menstruation.
4. Reduce sore throat
Wash 500g of mulberries and press them into juice.
Use the mulberry juice to gargle (for 3 to 5 days) to treat mouth and throat pain.
5. Treat burns
Select fresh, ripe mulberries that are not bruised and wash them thoroughly.
Press the mulberries for juice, then apply, wash, or use as a compress on the burn wound.

mon_an.mo_ta: Please refer to these collected tips and knowledge about potatoes below:
cac_buoc: How to prevent potatoes from discoloring

After potatoes are peeled and sliced or left whole, they will turn gray-brown if exposed to air for a while due to oxidation. Therefore, after peeling, place them immediately in clean water and cook them promptly.
If a gray color appears during cooking, add a little vinegar to the pot; the gray color will gradually turn back to white.
Methods for stir-frying and cooking potatoes

When stir-frying or cooking potatoes, use heat gradually to avoid the outside being mushy while the inside is still hard. For whole potatoes, wash and boil them with the skin on, then dip them in room-temperature water for a moment to make peeling easier. When stir-frying, it is not always necessary to peel them; just washing them thoroughly is enough, as the part closest to the skin contains the most nutrients. However, you must remove any green patches or sprouts to avoid poisoning.

Besides stir-frying, frying, and stewing, there are many other ways to prepare potatoes. Here is a simple yet delicious method: When boiled potatoes are cooked but not yet fully cooled, mash them thoroughly, add a little milk or butter, and mix well for a soft, delicious dish. If you have time, beat in a raw egg, add flour, pepper, and salt, then shape into balls and drop them into boiling oil, stirring until they turn dark golden. This dish is fluffy, crispy, and very fragrant.

mon_an.mo_ta: 1. How to keep fresh milk from forming a skin: Fresh milk contains lactic acid which causes a skin to form if left from morning to afternoon. To prevent this, add a little salt to the milk bottle to neutralize the lactic acid.
cac_buoc: 2. How to remove the gamey smell from beef
Roast a piece of ginger, scrape off the charred skin, crush it finely, and rub it over the surface of the meat. This will eliminate the unpleasant smell of beef.
3. How to keep bread fresh
Place the bread in a clean plastic bag and add a fresh stalk of celery. This will keep the bread fresh and flavorful for several days.
4. How to keep sponge cake fresh

To keep a sponge cake fresh for several days, place it in an airtight container along with a slice of bread. If the bread slice becomes dry and hard, replace it with a new one. You can also use a piece of jujube instead of bread for the same effect.
5. Method to enhance the aroma of cooking oil
Pour cooking oil (peanut oil, soybean oil) into a pot, increase the heat, add a little Sichuan pepper and star anise, then let it cool down. This makes the oil much more fragrant.
6. Method for preserving peanuts

Dry the peanuts and spread them out to cool completely. Place them in a plastic bag with a small packet of Sichuan pepper, tie it tightly, and store in a cool, dry, dark place. This way, peanuts can be kept for over 2 years.
7. Keep cucumbers fresh for several days
Place the cucumbers in a bowl of water. Ensure the stem end is facing down and submerged about 1/3 of the way. Change the water once a day.

mon_an.ten: Effective Deodorizing and Heat Relief Tips
mon_an.mo_ta: 1. How to remove garlic breath: After eating garlic, your mouth and breath often smell strongly of it. We suggest the following methods to eliminate the odor:
cac_buoc: Crush a few cloves and mix them with the garlic; the garlic smell will disappear.
After eating garlic, have some peanuts for dessert; the garlic smell will go away.
Chew on some dry tea leaves or a piece of apple; the garlic smell will also vanish.
2. Remove grease odors from pots and pans

After stir-frying, even if you have washed the pot, boiling water in it may still smell like grease. If you are boiling water in such a pot, drop a plain bamboo chopstick (not a painted one) into the water to remove the smell.
3. How to remove odors from a cutting board
Soak the cutting board in rice water mixed with a little salt, scrub it thoroughly, then rinse with hot water to eliminate the smell.
4. How to relieve the burn from eating chili
The best way is to put a little salt in your mouth; hold it there without swallowing. Wait a few minutes, then rinse your mouth with water; the burning sensation will disappear.
5. Prevent eye irritation when cutting onions, garlic, or chilies
Before you plan to chop onions, chilies, or garlic, soak your knife in cold water (the colder the better); this will reduce the pungency and prevent stinging eyes.

mon_an.mo_ta: Avoiding certain things while cooking will make your dishes more delicious and preserve essential nutritional values. This article provides housewives with some tips on what to avoid in the kitchen.
cac_buoc: Things to avoid when cooking
Do not fry cold cuts, ham, or Chinese sausages because these foods contain ammonium nitrate salts; frying them can create carcinogenic substances.

Do not boil eggs for too long: Eggs are rich and creamy when just cooked through. Boiling them for too long creates a substance that is difficult to absorb and reduces the nutritional value of the egg.

Do not add vinegar when stir-frying vegetables because the chlorophyll in the vegetables will react with the acid in the vinegar, turning the vegetables yellow. The dish will lose its visual appeal and nutritional value.

*Things to avoid when cooking:* Do not marinate duck meat with spices too early. Early marinating causes the proteins in the meat to toughen and the fibers to contract, making it less tasty. A helpful tip is that the ideal marinating time for duck is 1 hour.
Do not render lard over high heat because it will cause the fat to develop an unpleasant smell, which is harmful to health, especially the digestive system, trachea, and esophagus.

Do not let the pan get so hot that it smokes before stir-frying vegetables, as this destroys the bonds in the vegetables and can cause stomach irritation, ulcers, or heartburn. During the stir-frying process, the tip is to use high heat to keep the vegetables green and crunchy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Food is the main source of energy and the foundation of the complex human body. The metabolic process requires a regular supply of food, specifically high-nutrition food. Food intake also needs to be balanced; eating too much rich food can cause diseases, while a poor diet is even more dangerous. Furthermore, food must be presented beautifully and attractively to create an "appetite" for everyone. This reflects good health and aids digestion. When one "loses their appetite," even the most delicious food is hard to swallow, so preparing food to stimulate the appetite becomes a true science and art. Cooking requires "skill."
cac_buoc: Common dishes are divided into hot and cold dishes. Hot dishes include soups, porridge, meat, fish, tea, etc., while cold dishes include raw vegetables and appetizers. The temperature for hot dishes is typically 55-65°C. Do not eat at higher temperatures as it can damage the mouth and internal organs. Cold dishes should be close to room temperature. Do not eat too many very cold items, as it slows digestion and can cause stomach aches or sore throats.

The energy value of food is measured in calories (one calorie is the heat energy needed to raise one liter of water by 1°C). High-calorie foods are not necessarily good if consumed in excess, as they can lead to obesity or early atherosclerosis. These include animal/vegetable fats and sugars. Foods like grains, meat, and fish have medium calorie values, while vegetables, lean fish, and skim milk are low-calorie. Low-calorie foods are recommended for people over 40 or those with sedentary lifestyles. Scientists show that a sedentary person (bedridden) needs 1700 calories/day, a mental worker needs 3000 calories, a heavy manual laborer needs 3500-4500 calories, and an athlete or extreme laborer needs 4500-5000 calories. While we can calculate exact calories, in daily life, a general understanding is sufficient. Finally, follow the wisdom of our ancestors: "cut your coat according to your cloth," meaning eat according to your budget and physical needs; excess in anything, including eating, is never beneficial.

mon_an.ten: Potato Preparation Hacks You Might Not Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Potato hacks that not everyone knows. Today we would like to introduce to you: Potato preparation tips that not everyone is aware of.
cac_buoc: For salads, boil potatoes with the skin on, let them cool slightly, then peel and slice while still warm. If you want boiled potatoes to have a bright white color, add a little vinegar to the cooking water. Potatoes will taste better if you add a few cloves of garlic and 1 bay leaf per 1 kg of potatoes to the water. Potatoes should be cooked over low heat to soften evenly; ensure pieces are cut uniformly. High heat will make the outside mushy while the inside remains hard and unappetizing.

Mashed potatoes will be fluffy and smooth if you add a little butter and milk, then whip them while still hot. If you add cold milk, the product will turn a dull gray. Mashed potatoes are best when the potatoes are steamed. Most importantly, do not use new (young) potatoes for mashing. Leftover mashed potatoes can be made into patties by adding eggs, dry breadcrumbs, and pepper, then frying until golden.

When frying potatoes, ensure the fat or oil is very hot and only add salt once the potatoes have browned; adding salt earlier will cause them to release water, losing their color and shape. Before frying, drain well or pat the potatoes dry.

Dark spots on old potatoes can be removed by adding a little vinegar to the cooking water (1 tbsp vinegar per 1 kg of potatoes). When roasting potatoes (in an oven, for example), use a needle or fork to prick holes in the skin so they don't burst.

Use a stainless steel knife to peel or slice potatoes. Peeled potatoes kept without water can be stored for no more than 1 hour if placed in a pot covered with a clean, damp towel. Newly harvested potatoes are easy to peel if you soak them in cold water for about 5 minutes.

mon_an.ten: How to Season Like a Professional Chef
mon_an.mo_ta: Seasoning like a professional chef – No matter how delicious a dish is or how beautiful its color, it cannot be truly great without the right seasoning. Is seasoning like a professional chef difficult? Let's learn how to season with these hacks! Season like a pro to treat your whole family.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Start seasoning like a professional chef with these basic seasonings:
Fish sauce:

Fish sauce has a characteristic aroma but its flavor changes easily during cooking. Here is when to add it: For porridge, soups, or stir-fries, only season when the dish is already cooked. For braised dishes, marinate with other spices first; if you need the extra aroma of fish sauce, add it at the very end. Do not marinate with fish sauce for more than 30 minutes as the dish will lose its flavor.
MSG (Monosodium Glutamate):

MSG enhances the flavor of a dish, but if you don't know how to use it, it can be unhealthy. MSG should not be used for marinating and should not be added over high heat, as it can decompose into harmful substances. The hack is to only add MSG when the food is cooked, just before or after turning off the heat.
Salt (or seasoning salt):

This is the most basic seasoning for all dishes, making them savory and delicious. The timing depends on the dish. For soups, cook for a while to let the sweetness from the meat or fish release before adding salt. For braised or fried dishes, marinate the food with salt before cooking to preserve the sweetness of the meat or fish. When boiling food, add salt to the water as soon as it boils before adding vegetables or meat; this keeps vegetables green and prevents meat from darkening. You can refer to more tips on boiling meat.
Step 2: Continue seasoning like a professional chef with these other common seasonings:
Seasoning powder (Hạt nêm):

Seasoning powder is a newer seasoning but is used by many families. It has a salty, meaty flavor and can be used for both marinating and cooking. Do not add seasoning powder after the dish is cooked because it will not dissolve.
Sugar:

Sugar provides sweetness and makes dishes much easier to eat, but it burns easily at high temperatures. Do not add sugar when the food is almost done because it takes time to dissolve, which can affect the taste and make the dish sweeter than intended. For braised dishes, marinate the food with sugar first. For soups and stir-fries, you can add sugar while cooking, but remember to add it after the salt to maintain the natural sweetness of the ingredients.
Vinegar:
Vinegar is acidic and can ruin many dishes if added at the wrong time during stir-frying. Depending on the dish, add it at the beginning or after cooking is finished.
Black pepper:

Pepper is fragrant and mildly spicy, but it loses its aroma at high temperatures. Furthermore, marinating with pepper is not always beneficial for health. The hack for pepper is to add it when the food is just cooked or sprinkle it on top when serving; this keeps the pepper fragrant and delicious.

mon_an.mo_ta: Bean sprouts, including both mung bean and soybean sprouts, are a popular dish. Today, we will guide you on how to sprout bean sprouts quickly at home!
cac_buoc: Construct a pot using dry, clean straw or hay about 5cm thick, 45-65 cm high, and 60 cm in diameter. Wrap the outside with thick paper (other wrapping materials can be used as long as they retain heat).
Place 2 layers of thin plastic film inside the straw pot, and install a drainage tube at the bottom.

Soak the beans in warm water for about 5h; use 50°C water for mung beans and 35°C water for soybeans. Afterward, remove and let them sit in a basin for about 3h before pouring them into the straw pot. Spread them evenly, cover tightly, and wrap another layer on the outside for insulation.
Water the beans 5 times a day (use 30°C water for mung beans and 25°C water for soybeans).

After more than 70h for mung beans or 60h for soybeans, the sprouts can grow 6-8cm long. Mung bean sprouts 4-7cm long are fresh, tender, without leaves or root hairs, and contain the highest Vitamin C content.

mon_an.ten: Benefits of Tea for Healthy and Beautiful Skin
mon_an.mo_ta: Tea is an easy-to-find ingredient with many health benefits. Regular use of tea water will help you achieve healthy, beautiful skin and a balanced body!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Sun protection:

In summer, to combat the harmful effects of sunlight that cause tanning and skin damage, apply tea-soaked gauze to exposed skin areas like the face, neck, and arms before going out. Tea water acts as an excellent natural sunscreen.
Step 2: Acne treatment:

Green tea water has antibacterial properties that remove sebum and dirt that clog pores—the main cause of acne. Therefore, washing your face regularly with green tea water will help you achieve bright skin and reduce acne effectively.
Step 3: Effective skin care:
To make your skin bright and smooth, infuse green tea with mineral water and a little sugar. Use a soft gauze soaked in this solution to wipe your face in the morning and at night before bed.
Step 4: Skin whitening and fading dark spots:
Mix green tea with rose water and a little fruit vinegar, then gently pat it onto your face to nourish, whiten, and fade dark spots.
Step 5: Skin rejuvenation and anti-aging:
Antioxidants in green tea are proven to prevent signs of aging from both inside and out. This means green tea helps restore youthful skin by increasing elasticity and effectively reducing wrinkles.
Simply mix a little strong green tea with honey at a 2:1 ratio, then apply the mixture evenly to your face. Leave it for 15 minutes before rinsing with cool water. Perform this 2 times/week.

Alternatively, boil 1 tsp of dried green tea buds with 25 ml of water for 2-3 minutes, then strain. Soak a soft gauze in the tea water and apply it to your face morning and night to give your skin a bright, healthy tan. You can store this solution at room temperature for 1 day or in the refrigerator for 2 days.
Step 6: Preventing skin tanning

Boil 1 tsp of green tea buds with 25ml of water, steep for 40 minutes, then strain for the clear liquid. Once cooled, use a soft gauze to apply it to your face and neck every morning and night before bed. This method prevents your face from tanning in the sun.
Step 7: Softening skin:
Mix 100g of honey with 2 tsp of tea water. Use a soft gauze to apply the solution to your face for 10-15 minutes, then rinse with clean water. Do this once daily for desired results.
Step 8: Lightening dark circles around the eyes:

Green tea is very effective in reducing swelling and dark circles by constricting blood vessels under the eyes. It also contains small amounts of caffeine and tannins, which help reduce fluid in tissues and tighten the skin around the eyes. This prevents wrinkles and sagging, making the area visibly brighter.
The method is simple: soak cotton pads in strong tea, chill them in the refrigerator, and then place them over your eyes. This will help clear away the tired look in your eyes.
Step 9: Shrinking pores
Catechins in green tea are one of the best remedies for shrinking pores and increasing skin elasticity.
You can follow these steps: wash your face and steam it or apply a warm towel to open the pores, then apply chilled green tea water to the skin and rinse with water.
Step 10: Effective anti-wrinkle cream

Boil 1 tsp of tea with 50ml of water, steep for 40 minutes, strain, and let cool. Use a soft gauze to apply the tea water to your face and neck morning and night before bed. Besides nourishing the skin, this is especially beneficial for middle-aged women showing signs of aging and early wrinkles. For oily skin, add a few drops of lemon juice. This therapy nourishes, erases wrinkles, and tightens pores.

To erase wrinkles for dry skin, use a solution made from 2 tsp of honey, 1 tbsp of strong tea, 2 tbsp of rice flour paste, and 1-2 tbsp of boiled, cooled water. Apply an even layer to the face, cover with soft paper or a wet towel for 15-20 minutes, then rinse with cool water.

Mix 1 tbsp of rice flour with strong tea to form a smooth paste, then mix with an egg yolk. Apply to the face for 15-20 minutes, then rinse with warm water. Use this once a week to gradually fade wrinkles.
Step 11: Exfoliation:

Green tea extracts help soften and refresh the skin by naturally and safely exfoliating dead cells. You can mix cooled green tea water with warm bath water. Soak and massage for about 5 minutes before rinsing with clean water.
Notes when using green tea:
If you don't have much time, simply drinking 1 cup of green tea every morning is also very beneficial.
Green tea has strong cleansing properties, so you should only wash with it 1-2 times/week to avoid drying out your skin!

mon_an.mo_ta: Coconut oil is a compound with many uses in beauty and daily life. We will provide you with useful information about the benefits of coconut oil so you can apply them!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Composition of pure coconut oil:
Pure coconut oil includes main components such as saturated fatty acids, lauric acid, fatty acid derivatives, Vitamin E, Vitamin K, and minerals like iron, calcium, and magnesium.
The saturated fats in coconut oil help prevent the combination of free radicals in the body, limiting oxidation and preventing cancer.
Lauric acid is a highly antibacterial compound, common in breast milk, which helps increase a child's resistance.
A significant amount of linoleic acid in coconut oil also helps prevent hair loss and speeds up wound healing.
Vitamins and minerals in coconut oil help increase the body's anti-aging capabilities and beautify the skin.
Step 2: Benefits of coconut oil:
Coconut oil is wonderful for beauty: the essential oils keep the skin moisturized while strengthening tissue connections for healthy skin and reduced wrinkles.

Coconut oil is good for dieting: studies show it helps women reduce belly fat; it is easy to digest and suppresses appetite. Saturated fats in coconut oil convert into energy for body activities, so you don't need to consume too many calories.

Coconut oil supports digestion: For those with digestive issues or bloating, adding coconut oil to their daily diet is recommended because its fatty acids have antibacterial properties against Candida or parasites that cause poor digestion.
Additionally, you can use coconut oil for exfoliation, as a hair conditioner to darken hair, as an anti-chapping balm, or as a deodorant.
Step 3: How to use coconut oil effectively:
Use coconut oil to remove makeup: if you run out of makeup remover, use a cotton ball soaked in coconut oil to wipe your face, then wash with a facial cleanser for clean skin without damage.
For acne-prone skin after popping a pimple, use a cotton swab with a little coconut oil to dab the spot to reduce redness and prevent scarring.
Treating cracked heels: soak your feet in warm salt water for 30 minutes, scrub away dead skin, rinse, dry, and apply a layer of coconut oil overnight.
Applying coconut oil to dark spots also helps them heal faster.

Mix 2 tbsp of coconut oil with 1 cup of finely ground coffee. After bathing, apply this mixture to the skin, massage for 5 minutes, and rinse. This is popular for whitening, fading brown spots, and smoothing skin.

Apply a coconut oil mask for firm, smooth skin: mix 1 tbsp of coconut oil with 2 tbsp of unsweetened yogurt, or a 2:1:1 ratio of coconut oil, fresh lemon juice, and white sugar. Apply to the face for 20-30 minutes.

Use coconut oil to repair damaged hair: for split ends, trim the ends, apply coconut oil to the hair, wrap in a warm towel for 15 minutes, then wash with low-lather shampoo and dry with a soft towel. Note: do not apply coconut oil directly to the scalp while washing as it makes hair greasy.
In cold weather, apply coconut oil to lips and skin to reduce dryness and chapping.
Rinsing your mouth with coconut oil (oil pulling) helps achieve white teeth and fresh breath due to its antiseptic properties.
You can also use coconut oil for cooking; it does not break down at high temperatures, making it very safe.

mon_an.ten: Amazing Benefits of Apple Cider Vinegar
mon_an.mo_ta: Apple cider vinegar is a familiar solution for many families due to its useful benefits. We will share the wonderful uses that apple cider vinegar can provide.
cac_buoc: Characteristics of apple cider vinegar:
Apple cider vinegar is made from fresh apples and is beneficial for health due to its 4-8% acetic acid content, which aids digestion.
The main component of apple cider vinegar is water.
Natural liquid apple cider vinegar has a short shelf life, so it is now also available as a powdered extract with a longer shelf life.
Benefits of apple cider vinegar:
Detoxifying the liver: if your liver is at risk of damage from excessive alcohol, mix 1 tbsp of apple cider vinegar with 1 cup of warm water and drink it early in the morning to detoxify.
Softening clothes: to limit the use of chemical fabric softeners, add ½ cup of apple cider vinegar to the laundry water to make fabrics and clothes softer.
Using apple cider vinegar for baking: Many cakes with apple cider vinegar have a wonderful flavor and a fluffier texture, making them healthier.

Treating dandruff: dandruff will no longer be a worry if you dilute 1 part apple cider vinegar with 2 parts water and use this mixture to wash your hair; dandruff will decrease significantly, and your hair will become shinier.

Deodorizing hands: when cooking fish, seafood, garlic, or onions, your hands will have an unpleasant smell. Wash your hands with 1-2 tsp of apple cider vinegar, then rinse with cold water to remove the odor.
Apple cider vinegar is also great for brightening the face: use a damp cotton pad with a little vinegar, apply it to the face for 10 minutes, then rinse with water.
For sunburned skin, add a little apple cider vinegar to your bathwater and soak for at least 10 minutes; your skin will visibly brighten after a week.
Rinsing your mouth with apple cider vinegar after brushing also helps whiten teeth as the weak acid can break down plaque and kill bacteria.
Soak a cotton ball in apple cider vinegar and place it directly on a wart to prevent it from recurring after it heals.
Using apple cider vinegar to bleach or clean objects is a small tip you should apply daily.
Apple cider vinegar is also excellent for weight loss; you can drink 1-2 tsp mixed with 150ml of water 2-3 times a day.
Notes when using apple cider vinegar:
You can use green apples or Tao Meo apples to make apple cider vinegar.
During the process, a film (mother) may form; this is normal, so do not worry.
Apple cider vinegar toner exfoliates and brightens skin well but makes skin sun-sensitive in summer, so only use it in the evening.

mon_an.mo_ta: When cooking, homemakers often unintentionally make mistakes that should be avoided. These directly or indirectly affect food quality and family health. Let's explore what to avoid!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Do not overheat oil

When cooking, people often pour oil into the pan and do other tasks while waiting for it to heat up. Some even wait for the oil to smoke before adding food. This is not good as it gives the oil an unpleasant taste, destroys its antioxidants, and forms harmful compounds.
Therefore, do not wait for the oil to get too hot; add food when the oil starts to heat up to avoid losing nutrients and harming your health.
Step 2: Do not overcrowd the pan

Cooking requires patience. If you try to stir-fry quickly by overcrowding the pan, the food will become soft and cook unevenly. This results in bacteria not being fully destroyed by the heat, which can lead to pathogens developing in the body.
Step 3: Do not over-stir the food

We often stir or whisk food constantly to prevent burning, but over-stirring can be detrimental. It not only reduces nutritional value but also makes the food mushy and unappealing, which can affect your appetite and health.
Step 4: Do not wash meat in the sink
Washing meat in the sink might seem harmless, but while the meat gets clean, dirt and bacteria stick to the sink, multiply, and spread to dishes if not cleaned thoroughly.
Step 5: Do not use non-stick pans at high heat

High temperatures can cause non-stick pans to release PFCs (perfluorocarbons) in the form of fumes. Studies show PFCs are linked to liver damage and developmental issues. Check the best operating temperature for your pan before cooking.
Step 6: Do not use metal utensils on non-stick pans
Using metal utensils on a non-stick surface is a bad idea. You might scratch the surface, leading to the ingestion of the PFC coating. Use wooden or high-heat rubber utensils to ensure safety.

mon_an.ten: Dos and Don'ts of Refrigerator Food Storage
mon_an.mo_ta: To have delicious, nutritious meals, food needs to be kept fresh and intact. These dos and don'ts of refrigerator storage will provide you with tips to preserve food better!
cac_buoc: Don'ts when storing food in the refrigerator

Do not leave food containers uncovered. Many people put plates, bowls, or pots of leftovers directly into the fridge without a lid or wrap. This causes moisture to evaporate, affecting the flavor of other foods and drying out the leftovers. It also allows bacteria to grow, causing unpleasant odors.

Do not mix raw and cooked foods in the same compartment. Raw food that hasn't been processed is not hygienically safe; if placed with cooked food, the latter can be contaminated by bacteria. Cooked foods also have distinct aromas that can be affected, reducing their storage life.
Do not overfill the refrigerator. This prevents cold air from circulating, leading to insufficient temperatures for proper preservation.

Do not store eggs on the refrigerator door. The door is the warmest part of the fridge. It is better to keep eggs in their original cardboard carton on the upper shelves to prevent them from spoiling quickly.
Do not use plastic water bottles in the fridge, especially in summer. Harmful chemicals like dioxins, bisphenol, and phthalates can leach from the plastic into the water.

Do not refrigerate certain foods like potatoes, coffee, onions, garlic, or bread. These foods lose their aroma, decrease in quality, and cause odors for other items. Bread dries out and loses its flavor quickly in the fridge.
Do not wash raw vegetables before refrigerating. This makes them mushy and accelerates the decomposition of nearby foods.
To preserve food in the best way, apply these measures:
Put leftovers in airtight containers or wrap them with plastic wrap. Cooked food should be cooled and refrigerated within 2 hours of cooking.
Raw food should be washed and placed in bags or airtight containers before refrigerating. Fresh meat and fish should be stored in the freezer.

Store vegetables and fruits like cabbage, cauliflower, carrots, grapes, apples, and pears at about 0°C and 95% humidity. For tomatoes, cucumbers, watermelon, and green onions, store at 4-8°C with 90-95% humidity. Pumpkin, sweet potatoes, and bananas should be kept at 10-15°C and 60-70% humidity.
Ensure refrigerator compartments are clear so cold air can circulate via convection.
Separate ripe fruits from others, as ripe fruits stimulate the ripening process of nearby produce, reducing storage time.
Limit opening the refrigerator for too long. Decide what you need before opening, as keeping it open raises the temperature and allows bacteria to multiply.
Use metal containers instead of plastic for storage. Plastic has poor cold absorption, wasting energy and taking longer to cool.
Every two weeks, give the refrigerator a rest by turning the temperature to 'off' for 15-30 minutes before restarting.
Clean the refrigerator weekly.

mon_an.ten: Egg Cooking Tips and Useful Kitchen Hacks
mon_an.mo_ta: Eggs are a common ingredient. Here are some great kitchen tips for preparing and cooking eggs: To separate yolks from whites easily, crack the egg into a paper funnel; the white will flow down while the yolk remains in the funnel.
cac_buoc: Do not whisk egg whites and yolks in aluminum basins to avoid the eggs turning gray; use ceramic or porcelain instead.
Egg whites will whisk into stiff peaks better if you add a little powdered sugar or a few drops of lemon juice. They should also be cold, free of any yolk, and the bowl and whisk must be grease-free.
Eggs will not crack or burst while boiling if you add a little salt to the water or place an inverted bowl at the bottom of the pot.
Great tips for chicken eggs
Other miscellaneous kitchen tips:
Bread should be kept in clean cloth or plastic bags to stay soft and delicious. Do not store white and brown bread together, or the white bread will lose its quality.
Before slicing bread, warm it over a flame for a minute or two.
Discolored cooking oil will become clear again if you add a little salt (1 tsp of salt per 1 liter of oil).
Onions will be less pungent if rinsed with cold water.

mon_an.ten: Foods You Should Never Reheat Multiple Times
mon_an.mo_ta: Below are 6 types of food you should not reheat multiple times to preserve their nutritional value and prevent health issues.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Eggs

Whether boiled or fried, you should not reheat eggs as it can be harmful to your health. Eggs are high in calcium, nutrients, and vitamins; when reheated, especially at high temperatures in a microwave, the yolk can turn toxic.
Bacteria can thrive at temperatures between 4°C and 62°C, spoiling food and making you sick. If you have leftovers, it is best to use them in sandwiches, salads, or discard them.
Step 2: Cooking oil

You have likely been told not to reuse oil. Oil used for frying loses its stability and its structure breaks down. Specifically, when oil is heated above 190°C, it accumulates toxins that increase low-density lipoprotein (LDL)—the bad cholesterol.

Additionally, oils like grapeseed, walnut, avocado, and hazelnut have low smoke points and can smell rancid when reheated. Avoid using these for high-heat cooking or frying. Reheating dishes made with these oils at high temperatures can turn them into dangerous fats.
Step 3: Potatoes

Not all potato dishes are problematic when reheated; it depends on how you store them after cooking. Potatoes are an ideal environment for Clostridium botulinum—the bacteria that causes food poisoning. Storing them at room temperature without rapid cooling promotes the growth of harmful bacteria.
Step 4: Leftover rice
Rice is often left over after meals. Families usually store it in the fridge and reheat it. However, this is a mistake to avoid as it can damage the stomach.
Leftover rice can be dangerous when reheated or reused because bacteria can multiply if the rice is not stored correctly or kept for too long. Reheating rice increases the risk of food poisoning.
Step 5: Chicken

Chicken is an ideal environment for E. coli and Salmonella, which cause diarrhea and food poisoning. Furthermore, reheating chicken changes its protein structure, which can lead to digestive problems. If you have leftover chicken, eat it cold or repurpose it into other dishes instead of reheating.
Step 6: Beets, celery, and spinach
When reheating these vegetables, their nitrate content converts into nitrites due to bacterial action. Consuming many nitrite-rich foods increases the risk of cancer.

mon_an.ten: Common Cooking Mistakes You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: With the common processing errors listed below, we hope you can avoid them to create more delicious and beautiful dishes.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Mixing

Except for dishes that require fast and vigorous mixing until smooth, you should knead or mix at an appropriate level for each dish. For salads, mix gently to avoid crushing the vegetables, which ruins the appearance.
Step 2: Over-stirring

A stew will look much better and more attractive if you stop over-stirring it. Monitor the temperature accurately and garnish beautifully so that once it comes out of the oven and cools slightly, you have an appealing dish like a Casserole.
Step 3: Slicing meat

Imagine you are cutting a steak; look at the surface and you will see fibers running along it. Cut across these fibers (against the grain) to prevent the meat from crumbling and to make the slices tender and appetizing. Identify the grain before slicing to ensure the meat isn't tough.
Step 4: Using dull knives
It is very frustrating to use a dull knife. It makes the food look messy and is extremely inconvenient during preparation and cutting.
Step 5: Putting wet food into the pan

For most dishes, you should not leave food wet when putting it in the pan; however, for specific items like fried fish, this is sometimes necessary to prevent oil splattering. Generally, you should pat food dry before cooking to avoid splatters or the food becoming soggy.
Step 6: Insufficient seasoning

Don't fear salt; sprinkle it in to make the dish savory and flavorful. In reality, a moderate amount of salt won't make the dish salty but will enhance the flavor. Add a little at a time and taste to ensure it's perfect.
Step 7: Not tasting
Taste your food throughout the cooking process to adjust seasonings and find ways to improve the preparation.
Step 8: Not reading the recipe
Many people cook by instinct without following the provided recipe. To ensure success, take the time to read the recipe first.
Step 9: Adding ingredients at the wrong time
If you don't identify which ingredients need to cook longer and which cook quickly, mixing them all at once will result in a dish that is half-cooked and half-raw, losing its flavor.
Step 10: Fear of heat
For example, to get a perfect golden-brown crust on beef, let the pan get hot before adding oil, wait for the oil to heat up, and then add the meat.
By avoiding these common mistakes, you will create more delicious and visually appealing meals.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cantaloupe is a favorite fruit for many, but not everyone knows all its benefits. We will list 20 amazing benefits of this fruit for you!
cac_buoc: Cantaloupe is a favorite fruit for many, but not everyone knows all its benefits. Here are 20 benefits that cantaloupe provides:

4. *Prevent heart disease:* Being rich in potassium, it reduces the risk of cardiovascular diseases like heart attack and stroke. It also contains adenosine, which has effective blood-thinning properties.
5. *Control diabetes:* This is considered a miracle cure for diabetic patients due to its effect on controlling blood sugar levels.
6. *Boost the immune system:* Cantaloupe contains plenty of Vitamin C, which stimulates the formation of white blood cells to fight infections.

12. *Prevent dehydration:* Cantaloupe contains a high amount of water, helping to resolve cases like fainting due to dehydration.
13. *Prevent kidney stones:* The oxykine in cantaloupe helps eliminate kidney stones and cleanses the kidneys due to its high water content.

mon_an.ten: Common Beef Cooking Mistakes to Avoid
mon_an.mo_ta: Essential tips for achieving the perfect beef dish. Check out these common mistakes to avoid when cooking beef!
cac_buoc: Below are 9 common mistakes when cooking beef, as pointed out by Executive Chef Billy Olivia of Delmonico's (established in 1837), one of Wall Street's most beloved steakhouse restaurants.
1. Grilling beef immediately after taking it out of the refrigerator
Most of us do this without realizing it makes the beef tough because the outside overcooks while the inside remains raw.
2. Placing beef in a pan or oven that hasn't been sufficiently preheated
When the oven or pan hasn't reached the required temperature, the beef needs to cook longer, leading to a loss of nutrients and a dull "gray" color that looks unappetizing.
3. Not seasoning or seasoning the meat unevenly
Some people only lightly season or only season one side. This prevents the meat from being fully infused with flavor and makes it much less delicious.
Executive Chef Billy Olivia also revealed his secret: season both sides of the meat evenly with a mixture of table salt, sea salt, and a blend of 7 different finely ground peppercorns.
4. Grilling beef over heat for too long
Naturally, you don't want your fresh, delicious beef to turn from golden brown to burnt and dry, losing all its flavor and nutrition.
5. Piercing the beef with a fork while grilling to check for doneness
Piercing the meat with a knife or fork while cooking allows the juices and seasonings to escape. This significantly reduces the flavor and quality of the beef.
6. Flipping the meat on the stove more than once

This is particularly detrimental when pan-searing a steak separately from its sauce, or when there is no final step to add moisture. You should only place the meat in a preheated pan and flip it once the bottom has turned a caramelized golden brown. Flipping too many times before the meat is properly seared causes uneven cooking and allows the nutritious juices and internal flavors to leak out. 7. Pressing the meat down onto the pan
Avoid doing this so that the fats, nutrients, and seasonings inside the meat aren't squeezed out, which would diminish the dish's flavor.
8. Eating the beef immediately after grilling
We often want to eat beef right after it comes off the grill, but this isn't ideal!
Letting the grilled beef rest for about 10–15 minutes before enjoying it is the perfect amount of time for the meat to become most flavorful and tender.
9. Forgetting to sprinkle seasoning before serving
Since many seasonings are lost during the cooking process, sprinkling a little extra salt or seasoning onto the beef for a bolder flavor before eating is absolutely essential.
How to choose good beef:
Choose meat that is bright red (not dark red). The meat should be dry and smooth with small fibers.
When pressed with a finger, the meat should be elastic and not sticky or slimy.
The meat should have a mild beefy aroma, not the pungent smell of beef fat.
If you prefer tender beef, choose meat from a young calf. Veal or young beef is usually lighter in color than older beef, with a fine grain and white fat rather than yellow.

mon_an.ten: Important Notes When Using Brown Rice
mon_an.mo_ta: In Traditional Chinese Medicine, as with all living things and humans, matter is structured according to a suitable yin-yang ratio. Each of our cells and organs, as well as our metabolic processes and the interaction of yin and yang, maintain the body's vital activities. 13 benefits of brown rice.
cac_buoc: 9 benefits of aloe vera

From this perspective, the process of living, consuming, and producing energy is also the movement of yin and yang. During this process, yin and yang are constantly changing, rising and falling, waxing and waning. However, this process must ensure the body remains balanced, helping to achieve equilibrium so that yin does not overwhelm yang and vice versa.

Not just with brown rice and sesame salt, even foods considered most nutritious never satisfy all nutritional needs on their own. Therefore, the diet must be diverse and changed frequently. A body that maintains yin-yang balance is healthy and comfortable. Conversely, an imbalance will lead to discomfort, weakness, or illness, depending on the severity.

It must be acknowledged that this is an effective method. However, application must be guided by a physician and adapted to the specific conditions of each individual and time period, rather than eating brown rice unscientifically.
Most of us know that brown rice and sesame salt have many benefits and certain effects on some illnesses.

On the other hand, we must face the fact that brown rice and sesame salt only satisfy a certain number of nutritional needs and are only effective for certain types of diseases. Furthermore, brown rice and sesame salt cannot satisfy all nutritional requirements, nor can they cure all illnesses.
For this reason, the National Institute of Nutrition recommends eating a sufficient quantity and a balance of nutrients from about 10 to 15 types of food per day.
In other words, a diverse and constantly changing diet is the most correct and scientific way to eat.
We do not oppose eating brown rice and sesame salt; however, we oppose extreme use, specifically the dogma of eating only brown rice and sesame salt without any other food.

For patients with long-term physical weakness (and even for healthy, normal people), eating purely brown rice and sesame salt for a long time can be harmful or at least make the body more severely debilitated due to the lack of other nutrients not found in brown rice and sesame salt.
For illnesses caused by lack of food, malnutrition, or those not caused by yin-yang imbalance or toxin accumulation, the brown rice and sesame salt method is inappropriate.
Therefore, the elderly, the weak, and the malnourished must be cautious and consult a physician before applying the brown rice and sesame salt diet.

mon_an.ten: Useful Tips for Using Lemon Peels
mon_an.mo_ta: These small tips for using lemon peels will help you a lot in cleaning stains, especially for kitchen utensils!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cleaning grease and dirt:

Kitchen grease and grime are extremely difficult to clean without detergents, but detergents often contain toxic chemicals and can be expensive. With just the peel of a squeezed half-lemon, this is no longer a concern.

Simply use the lemon peel with a little salt to scrub the greasy or grimy areas of the stove, then wipe clean with a cloth. However, some surfaces like marble may be sensitive to acid, so you should not use lemon on them.
Step 2: Refreshing cutting boards:

Wash the cutting board with water, then use the lemon peel to scrub the surface. Let it sit for a few seconds for the lemon to disinfect the board, then rinse. Your cutting board will not only be sparkling clean but will also have a light fragrance, eliminating lingering food odors.
Step 3: Deterring insects:

Insects like ants often appear in the kitchen wherever food is kept, which can be frustrating. You might not know that insects are very afraid of the acid in lemons. You can place lemon peels at thresholds, holes, or anywhere insects might enter to effectively repel them.
Step 4: Cleaning stains on coffee mugs and teapots:

Mugs, glasses, and teapots used for tea and coffee will develop yellow stains over time. The solution is to slice lemon peels, put them in the pot, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat. Let it sit for 1 hour before washing the pot clean.
For cups and mugs, add salt, ice, and lemon peels, scrub thoroughly, and then rinse with water.
Step 5: Cleaning the microwave:

Place sliced lemon peels in a bowl of water and microwave on high for about 5 minutes until the water boils and steam condenses on the walls. Then, remove the bowl and wipe away the dirt on the walls and ceiling of the microwave.
Step 6: Deodorizing trash:

Trash stored in the house for just a few hours can start to smell unpleasant. To keep your kitchen fresh, simply put lemon peels into the trash bag after use; slicing the peels makes them even more effective.
Step 7: Polishing copper and steel, and preventing rust:
Cut a lemon in half, soak it in salt, toothpaste, or soda water, and scrub the object to be polished. Let it sit for about 10 minutes, then rinse with water and buff dry.
Step 8: Humidifying and scenting the kitchen air:
In winter, you can place lemon peels in a pot of water and simmer on the stove. Leave the lid off so the steam can escape, creating moisture and a pleasant scent for your small kitchen.
Step 9: Preventing brown sugar from clumping:
Brown sugar left out will clump. Placing a lemon peel in the package with the sugar will help absorb moisture and prevent clumping, while also giving it a special aroma.
Hopefully, these small tips will be helpful to you in the kitchen!

mon_an.mo_ta: Great tips for preserving vegetables – Homemakers often have the habit of buying many vegetables at once to stock up. However, not everyone knows how to store them correctly to maintain the nutritional value of fresh produce. These tips will show you how!
cac_buoc: Great tips for preserving vegetables
1. Keep vegetables with dirty skins

Vegetables with dirty skins like potatoes, carrots, or artichokes will be better preserved and maintain their nutritional value thanks to the layer of soil on their skins. Do not wash them before storing; leave them as they are and keep them in a cool, dry place. You can keep potatoes for a month without worrying about them spoiling.
2. Avoid pre-prepping

Pre-prepped vegetables, such as those with the roots trimmed or old parts removed, usually spoil faster than if you leave the whole bunch intact. According to researchers, cutting and picking vegetables before storage allows bacteria to multiply faster (except when removing pest-damaged or rotten leaves).
3. Remove pest-damaged or rotten leaves

To keep vegetables fresh longer when refrigerated or kept in a cool place, you should pluck off any pest-damaged, wilted, or rotten parts. Keeping these parts will affect the rest of the vegetables, causing them to spoil faster.
4. Store in the dark
Another secret for preserving potatoes and vegetables that adapt well to the dark is to wrap them in newspaper or black/dark-colored plastic bags. This helps them last longer and prevents sprouting.
5. Choose the right refrigerator temperature

Most vegetables cannot withstand temperatures that are too cold. Keep the refrigerator at a moderate cold level, and your vegetables will stay fresh longer. This is one of the great tips for preserving vegetables.
6. Tips for preserving bananas and tomatoes

These are two types of fruit that ripen quickly and will affect the ripening speed of other fruits kept near them. Store bananas in paper bags or, more simply, keep them away from other fruits, especially soft-fleshed ones like avocados and mangoes.
Tomatoes should not be kept in temperatures that are too cold, as they will lose their flavor and nutrients. Ensure you are storing tomatoes in a cool place where the temperature is not too low.

mon_an.ten: Common Seafood Preparation Mistakes to Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Seafood in general is considered a precious food source, providing natural protein and calcium to help the body stay healthy and resilient. Seafood is often rich in beneficial nutrients like magnesium and zinc. However, misconceptions during preparation, storage, and consumption can turn these nutritious foods into toxins, affecting health and potentially causing food poisoning. In recent years, cases of poisoning from eating raw or undercooked seafood have been increasing. This is the result of consumer misconceptions. Let's learn about common mistakes when preparing seafood!
cac_buoc: Things to know

All types of seafood contain bacteria capable of causing diarrhea; these bacteria multiply rapidly once the seafood is caught and increase even more if left unprocessed for a long time. As the bacteria act, they produce toxins that accumulate in the seafood meat. These toxins cannot be destroyed by any cooking method.

Many people believe that seafood must be eaten raw to be nutritious, such as raw oysters, shrimp ceviche, or squid salad. In reality, there is no scientific evidence proving that eating these types of seafood raw is more nutritious than eating them cooked.

Eating raw seafood also makes the intestinal tract susceptible to parasites and worms. According to nutritional research, in prepared seafood salads containing all the seasonings, 85% of liver fluke larvae still survive.
In crabs grilled until the shell is golden, 65% of lung fluke larvae remain; in crabs grilled until the shell is charred, 23.3% of larvae still survive.
Prevention measures
The first rule when eating seafood is to choose fresh items; spoiled, dead seafood or anything with an unusual smell must be discarded entirely.

Give up the habit of eating raw or undercooked meat, fish, and seafood that is only "cooked" by squeezing lime juice without heat. Using lime, vinegar, or blanching in boiling water only sears the surface of the food without fully cooking the entire piece of meat. While this method ensures minimal nutrient loss, the user is at risk of parasitic infection or food poisoning.

In the past, the environment was cleaner, and seafood at estuaries and coasts was not yet contaminated with too many toxins. Today, the safety of water and seafood sources is at an alarming level. Therefore, when preparing seafood, carefully remove inedible parts, wash thoroughly, and cook completely.

Seafood that is not processed immediately should be stored in the refrigerator. Do not mix raw seafood with cooked seafood. When defrosting, leave the seafood in the refrigerator compartment overnight. If needed immediately, you can rinse it under cold running water or use a microwave. Do not defrost by soaking in warm water or leaving it at room temperature.
Let's protect your family and yourself from the risks of seafood poisoning caused by daily eating habits!

mon_an.ten: Common Mistakes When Using Dish Soap
mon_an.mo_ta: Common mistakes when using dish soap in daily cleaning not only cause toxic substances to cling to dishes but also affect the user's health. These handy tips will point out incorrect habits when using dish soap that could impact those cooking for the whole family.
cac_buoc: According to scientists, the use of detergents always affects the user's health to a certain extent. To prevent unnecessary harm while using dish soap, these tips will highlight common mistakes to keep in mind.
Soaking dishes for too long in dish soap

After eating or cooking, there are many stubborn stains that stick to the dishes no matter how you wash them. Do not soak them in diluted dish soap because the toxic substances in the detergent will soak directly into the dishes. This happens even faster with kitchen tools made of wood or bamboo.
Rinsing dishes too quickly after washing

Dish soap contains many toxic chemicals; if you only rinse briefly with water, it is difficult to wash these substances away. Therefore, the only way to clean off these chemicals is to rinse very thoroughly, 2 to 3 times in a basin of clean water after washing.
Using too much dish soap in one go

When you see that kitchen tools are too dirty, you might use a lot of dish soap, thinking they will get clean faster. In reality, they do not get clean any faster than when using a moderate amount. The "side effect" is that it becomes very difficult to rinse off all the chemicals, and the residue will leach into food when the tool is reused.
Using laundry detergent or soap powder to wash dishes

When using laundry powder to wash food containers, chemicals can remain during the washing and rinsing process, posing many risks of causing hepatitis, stomach, and gallbladder diseases, and reducing the body's resistance...
Pouring dish soap directly onto dishes

This is one of the fastest ways for toxic substances to cling directly and most heavily to dishes. This method is both wasteful and allows a large amount of toxins to soak into the dishes, making it likely that chemicals will remain on the surface for a long time. When reused to hold food, the remaining chemicals will leach into the food and enter the body, causing illness over time.
Buying dish soap of unknown origin or counterfeit goods

While all types of dish soap contain toxic substances, counterfeit or low-quality types have higher toxic levels because they are mixed with cheap chemicals and the chemical components are not tested. Long-term use will harm the user's health.
How to use dish soap properly:
Step 1: Use an amount of dish soap appropriate for the number of dishes. In winter, dishes should be washed with warm water mixed with dish soap to dissolve grease and clean more effectively.

Step 2: For dishes and kitchen tools that are too dirty or have stubborn stains, soak them in clean water or hot water for 1 hour before washing. For stains like soot or tarnish, you should use steel wool and a bit of sand. It will be very clean.
Step 3: After washing with dish soap, rinse with clean water 2 - 3 times, scrubbing thoroughly by hand.

mon_an.ten: Common Mistakes When Eating Beef That Harm Your Health
mon_an.mo_ta: Beef is a highly nutritious food that frequently appears in every family's menu. However, eating too much or based solely on preference can sometimes become a "poison" that harms your health. Please refer to some notes when using beef!
cac_buoc: Beef has a very rich nutritional content that can strengthen immunity, provide energy for cells, and build muscle. Delicious beef is rich in protein, contains vitamin B12, zinc, and also contains Cytocilin – a fat-burning substance. However, beef contains high cholesterol levels and can cause dangerous health conditions if you eat too much or eat it incorrectly.
Do not eat rare beef

Currently, farming, slaughtering, and transportation are sometimes not guaranteed, so meat is easily contaminated with bacteria. To ensure health and avoid the fear of parasites or tapeworms entering the body, you should give up the habit of eating rare or undercooked beef. It is necessary to eat cooked food, drink boiled water, and choose carefully from clear origins before processing.
Do not eat at night

Beef is significantly richer in iron than other foods. Iron is very beneficial for health because it transports oxygen to muscles through red blood cells, helping the body feel full of energy. Iron also has a great effect on liver function, promoting the liver to work better and more efficiently without getting tired.

However, if you eat beef at night, it means you have loaded a large amount of iron into your body while the liver needs to rest. This will interfere with the liver's biological clock, leading to abnormally high blood sugar levels. If this situation occurs frequently, you will face a high risk of diabetes.
Do not eat with seafood

Beef and seafood should not be combined because their nutritional components can react with each other. Beef contains a lot of phosphorus, which is necessary for bone formation, while seafood is rich in calcium and magnesium. Therefore, when using these two types of food together, it will create salt precipitation. This form of salt not only hinders phosphorus absorption but also reduces the rate of calcium absorption.
Do not eat while treating melasma or freckles

Beef contains a lot of protein that is good for the body. However, if you have melasma, using this food will cause the melasma to spread faster. Therefore, if you are suffering from melasma or freckles, you should not use beef to limit the spread of the pigmented skin area.

mon_an.ten: Nutritional Mistakes Mothers Should Stop Immediately
mon_an.mo_ta: Despite always focusing on supplementing nutrition for their children, mothers sometimes still make some basic mistakes. Below are some nutritional mistakes that mothers should stop immediately to ensure their children always develop healthily!
cac_buoc: Nutritional mistakes mothers should stop immediately
Step 1: Adding fish sauce or salt to food for children under 1 year old
For children under 1 year old, fish sauce and salt should not be added to food because the child's kidney function is still very weak and can only eliminate 1 gram of salt/day.

Mothers do not need to add salt when feeding children porridge, even when cooked with meat, fish, or shrimp, and should not add sugar to weaning meals because eating too much sugar can lead to obesity.
Step 2: Eating a lot of pig's trotter porridge to produce milk

Family members often pressure postpartum mothers to eat a lot of food such as pig's trotters, various porridges, and rice high in starch to produce milk for the baby. But in fact, the amount of milk secreted does not entirely depend on eating a lot; the most important thing is that you must breastfeed frequently and correctly, get enough sleep, and have a comfortable spirit.

The milk secretion mechanism depends heavily on neurological factors. When the baby suckles, it stimulates the nerve endings in the nipple, creating a nerve flow to the posterior lobe of the pituitary gland to secrete 2 hormones: Prolactin and oxytocin.

Prolactin stimulates the mammary glands to produce milk, while oxytocin stimulates the smooth muscles of the mammary glands to secrete milk. Therefore, if you do not breastfeed or use breast pumps, you will not have milk even if you eat a lot.

If mothers are already overweight, they should not eat too much, especially starchy foods. You should eat nutrient-rich foods such as unsweetened milk, non-sweet fruits, plenty of green vegetables, and if necessary, supplement with functional foods that provide micronutrients, then your milk quality will be very good.
Just note that you need to supplement plenty of water and eat liquid-based foods such as porridge, soup, milk...
Step 3: The truth about pineapple and watermelon
All types of fruit are good for health; no fruit causes "internal heat" (if eaten in moderate amounts). If you eat too much pineapple, it can lead to heat and mouth sores.

As for watermelon, it does not cause heat at all but is also very good for health. Watermelon contains a lot of water, full of vitamins and minerals, and there is no worry about weight gain like other sweet fruits.
Step 4: Drinking milk without accompanying food in the morning

In the morning, some children, because they are reluctant to eat, only have the habit of drinking a glass of milk and eating nothing else. This is the reason why they feel hungry quickly. If they only drink milk, the milk will not stay long in the stomach, leading to poor absorption of the protein in the milk.
