In the morning, before drinking milk, children should eat a small amount of starch such as a small bowl of porridge or soup, a slice of bread, or biscuits is best.
Step 5: The misconception that shrimp meat has a lot of calcium

Many people mistakenly believe that eating shrimp ensures plenty of calcium. And mostly, people peel off all the shells and claws, eating only the shrimp meat. But in fact, the amount of calcium is mainly in the claws and shells, while the shrimp meat mainly provides protein.

Children also only need protein supplements depending on their age. If children are given too much protein, it is not good and can lead to digestive disorders, diarrhea, constipation, or being overweight and obese. If you want to provide calcium for the body, you can choose small shrimp to eat the whole shell.
Step 6: Defrosting yogurt for children in the microwave

Fresh milk can be put in the microwave to defrost (meaning to make it less cold). As for yogurt, it should not be put in the microwave. If you accidentally overdo it and the temperature goes above 60 degrees, the beneficial bacteria in the yogurt may die. At that point, eating yogurt no longer has any effect.
The best way to warm up yogurt is to leave it at room temperature for 10-15 minutes or soak it in warm water at about 50 degrees.
Step 7: Eating charred grilled or braised food

Grilled and braised food, especially when the fat is charred, will have an attractive aroma. However, that aroma comes from aromatic cyclic carbon compounds that can cause cancer. Therefore, you should not eat too much grilled food. Ideally, you should not eat it more than 1-2 times a month.

mon_an.ten: Amazing Benefits of Bananas You Should Know
mon_an.mo_ta: Bananas are a very healthy fruit because they provide many calories and other nutrients. Below are the amazing uses of bananas that you should know!
cac_buoc: 1. Characteristics of bananas:
Bananas contain a large amount of protein and a large amount of carbohydrates; when ripe, these components will convert into sugar, creating the sweet taste and aroma of the banana.
Ripe bananas also contain many other components such as glucose, lactose, maltose, galactose, and starch.
Bananas are also a fruit containing many necessary vitamins such as vitamins A, C, E, and essential amino acids, so it can be affirmed that bananas are a very healthy fruit.
2. Health benefits of bananas:

Eating bananas helps improve memory: Perhaps this benefit of bananas is most widely known; bananas contain Potassium, which enhances brain activity, allowing us to work more effectively and stay more alert. In addition, the amount of vitamin B in bananas also helps support the nervous system after stressful work.
Eating bananas supports the digestive system: Thanks to the high fiber content in bananas, intestinal activity will be enhanced, preventing constipation or stomach problems.

Eating bananas provides energy for the body: Thanks to the relatively high sugar content in bananas, you can eat ripe bananas to provide immediate energy for the body; therefore, bananas are indispensable in the diets of athletes. A scientific study has shown that 2 bananas will provide enough energy for 90 minutes of strenuous exercise.
Eating bananas is good for people with anemia: Bananas have a very high iron content, so when eating bananas, more hemoglobin will be produced, providing more blood to nourish the body.

Eating bananas can help stabilize your psychology: For people with psychological problems or mood swings, you should follow the advice to eat 1 banana a day to supplement the amino acid Tryptophan, an essential amino acid for producing serotonin, a hormone that helps regulate psychology and improve your mood.
3. Benefits of bananas in beauty:

Eating bananas helps you maintain your body shape: When eating bananas, the sugar level in the body will be balanced, thereby reducing the possibility of obesity and contributing to maintaining a slim body shape.
Using bananas to create hair and skin masks will give you long, black, smooth hair and even, bright, firm skin.
4. Notes when eating bananas:

You should only eat a maximum of 3 bananas per day: Scientists in the UK and Italy have simultaneously pointed out that eating too many bananas will harm your health; it is best to only eat 3 bananas per day to ensure an adequate supply of potassium for the body and reduce the risk of stroke.

Eating too many bananas can lead to headaches because bananas contain a lot of tyramine and phenylethylamine, which dilate blood vessels. Usually, the amount of tyramine will be higher in ripe bananas, so the longer a banana is ripe, the easier it is to cause a headache.

In addition, eating too many bananas over a period of time can cause nervous system inhibition with symptoms such as: drowsiness, nausea, and dizziness because the amount of potassium and tryptophan supplied to the body is too large.

mon_an.mo_ta: Being overweight is currently very common among many people, especially women. To have good health and a beautiful body, women should have a reasonable diet, and the 10 appetite-suppressing foods below will help women have more methods to reduce weight!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peanuts

Peanuts help increase the production of the hormone cholecystokinin, which can naturally suppress appetite. Research by experts at the University of California (USA) also shows that eating these nuts, or any tree nuts, can also help stabilize blood sugar levels and reduce bad cholesterol (LDL).
Step 2: Eggs
The protein content in eggs helps you feel full longer. Protein can prevent sudden spikes in blood sugar levels, which can minimize appetite.
Step 3: Lean beef
The amino acid leucine in high-protein foods like beef, fish, and dairy products helps burn fat while maintaining muscle elasticity. It also helps reduce appetite.

In principle, to lose weight, the total amount of calories taken into the body must be less than the amount of calories consumed. However, the most common trouble that dieters face is the inability to control gnawing hunger. To solve this problem, dieters need to choose "healthy" foods for their weight loss goals. These are foods that not only provide many useful nutrients for the body and contain few calories but also have the effect of curbing appetite.
Step 4: Apples

Apples contain very few calories and fat. The ability of apples to curb appetite comes from their abundant fiber content. Fiber helps you feel full for a long time because it expands the stomach. As a result, you need less food to satisfy hunger while preventing overeating. This fruit also contains natural sugars that help maintain healthy blood sugar levels. This has the effect of preventing the body from digesting too much starch.

If you eat 3 small pears or apples a day, you will lose more weight than those who do not eat apples. Furthermore, blood glucose levels in people who eat apples or pears will decrease significantly compared to those who do not.
Step 5: Oatmeal

Oatmeal is also a fiber-rich food, containing useful starch (which is consumed slowly). In addition, oatmeal is also an ideal choice for diabetic patients because it helps lower the glycemic index. You can use this flour for breakfasts accompanied by low-fat milk and some flaxseeds.
Step 6: Water

If an appetite appears while the body truly has no need for energy, drink water to fill the stomach. Water - a calorie-free drink - is perhaps the best choice to master the appetite for those following a weight loss plan. Pay attention to drinking water regularly throughout the day and whenever you feel hungry to trick the brain into thinking the stomach is full. A recent research result in people following a low-calorie diet showed that those who drank 2 glasses of water before each meal lost 7 kg within 12 weeks compared to 5 kg in those who did not drink water before eating.
Step 7: Green tea

This is a drink famous for its antioxidant capacity. However, green tea also has the ability to stimulate the release of hormones that help control or limit appetite. The ability of green tea is shown in promoting deception, creating a false sense of fullness, increasing the metabolic rate, preventing fat digestion, and enhancing energy for the body. They are also foods that help burn fat (can consume up to 43% of fat).
Step 8: Soup

People following a diet are advised to eat at least 2 low-calorie soup meals. Soup curbs appetite thanks to its high water content and supports weight loss because it contains very few calories. Soups made from broth and vegetable soups are the healthiest choices.
Step 9: Salad

Not only a delicious dish, but salad is also a great choice for an appetizer before the main meal because it will help you fill your stomach and not overeat. The abundant fiber in the salad will delay glucose from entering the vessels. This helps you not feel hungry too quickly. A study published in the journal of the American Dietetic Association concluded that women who ate a salad containing about 100 calories before dinner reduced their calorie consumption by 12% throughout the meal.
Step 10: Dark chocolate

In the list of 10 foods that help master appetite just mentioned, dark chocolate will perhaps surprise many people with its "anti-weight gain" ability. However, if used only in a small, moderate amount, dark chocolate is a great food for health. The bitter taste of this pure chocolate can help curb appetite. Some studies have pointed out that the antioxidants in dark chocolate will act as appetite suppressants, helping with weight loss and blood sugar control. However, the point to note is that you should only use this sweet food at a limited level.

mon_an.ten: Foods to Avoid Combining with Eggs
mon_an.mo_ta: Although eggs are very good for your health, combining them with certain foods can be harmful to the body. Here are the foods you should not eat with eggs.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Tea

Many people have the habit of drinking tea after eating eggs to reduce the unpleasant smell, unaware that this is very harmful to health. The tannic acid in tea leaves combines with the protein in eggs to form a tannic acid protein compound that slows down intestinal peristalsis, prolonging the time stool is stored in the intestines. This is a culprit for constipation and increases the risk of accumulating harmful substances in the body.
Step 2: Soy milk:

Both soy milk and eggs are nutritious foods, so people often have the habit of eating eggs with soy milk in the morning. However, the protein in eggs combines with the trypsin in soy milk, hindering the process of breaking down and absorbing protein in the body.
Additionally, soy milk contains many nutrients such as protein, fat, sugar, vitamins, and minerals... which can be lost when combined with eggs.
Step 3: Sugar:

After eggs are cooked, the amino acids in eggs and sugar combine to form Glycosyl lysine – which breaks down the amino acid components in the eggs. Furthermore, this compound is difficult to absorb, toxic, and can cause blood clotting, posing a danger to the body.
Combining these two foods also makes it difficult for the body to absorb nutrients, negatively affecting human health.
Step 4: Persimmons:
Eating persimmons after eating eggs can easily lead to food poisoning and may even cause acute gastritis, with main symptoms such as nausea, diarrhea, and abdominal pain.

If you accidentally eat persimmons after eggs, you should immediately drink a glass of diluted salt water (200 ml of water and 20 g of salt). If you do not feel like vomiting after drinking, you can drink it multiple times to vomit out all the harmful substances. Alternatively, you can use crushed fresh ginger mixed with warm water to drink. If necessary, you can also take a laxative to eliminate toxins as quickly as possible. If they were consumed a long time ago, use a purgative to quickly push the toxins out of the body.
Step 5: Garlic:

Many people like to use garlic instead of shallots when preparing eggs, but few know that when garlic is over-fried or charred, it creates a very toxic substance when combined with eggs. Therefore, we should not eat eggs with garlic.
Step 6: Goose, rabbit, and turtle meat:

Rabbit, goose, and turtle meat have a "cold" nature. Eggs also belong to this food group, and both contain certain biologically active substances. When eaten together, they cause a reaction that stimulates the digestive tract, leading to diarrhea.

Additionally, eating eggs at the same time as turtle meat can lead to food poisoning. This is especially true for people who are fatigued or have a cold. It may also be unsuitable for pregnant women or those with poor digestion.
Step 7: Pig brain:
Consuming eggs with pig brain will increase blood cholesterol, which can easily cause a sudden spike in blood pressure, potentially leading to death.
Step 8: Anti-inflammatory medicine:

People with intestinal diseases or diarrhea should especially avoid taking medicine immediately after eating eggs. Because eggs have a high protein content, they increase the burden on the stomach, affecting the effectiveness of the medicine. Other inflammatory diseases such as respiratory or urinary tract infections do not significantly affect the absorption of the medicine.

mon_an.ten: 4 Delicious Dipping Sauces for Boiled Chicken
mon_an.mo_ta: Save these 4 delicious dipping sauce recipes for boiled chicken now to help your family enjoy a more flavorful and savory meal!
cac_buoc: Many people are often subjective or oversimplify the process of making dipping sauce. For example, boiled chicken is often served with just fish sauce or seasoning powder... However, this simplification makes the dish much less attractive.

Making dipping sauce is not difficult; it just takes a little time and effort. Each dish needs its own dipping sauce recipe, but some dishes have multiple ways to prepare the sauce. After making a delicious bowl of dipping sauce a few times, you will surely stop thinking that dipping sauce is... just for dipping.
Chili Lime Salt
Preparation: 1 lime; 1 tbsp white salt, 1/2 tbsp sugar, and 1/3 tsp MSG (optional), 3 lime leaves, 1 red chili, 1 lime zester.

*Method:* Mix the salt, sugar, and MSG thoroughly. Then, use the zester to grate the green outer peel (the lime zest contains essential oils and provides the main aroma of the lime, so do not skip it).

Next, wash the lime leaves and fresh chili, then julienne and finely mince them. Mix these ingredients into the salt plate, squeeze in the lime juice, and stir well until the salt and lime juice dissolve and blend together.
Add the lime leaves and chili, and you have a fragrant and attractive plate of chili lime salt. The deliciousness of boiled chicken depends significantly on the dipping spices.
Fish Sauce Dip

Ingredients include one ladle of good fish sauce, 1/4 tsp MSG (optional), 1/4 tsp black pepper, a few thin chili slices, and julienned lime leaves. Pour the fish sauce into a bowl and stir in the MSG until dissolved. Then add the pepper and sliced chili. When eating, sprinkle a bit of julienned lime leaves on top!
Seasoning Powder Dip

Ingredients include seasoning powder, black pepper, lime (or calamansi), and chili. Put the seasoning powder in a bowl and squeeze in the lime (or calamansi) juice. Gently remove the seeds. Add sliced chili and pepper to taste. You can also sprinkle in julienned lime leaves for a very fragrant and attractive dip.
Chicken Blood Dip

Ingredients include one tbsp seasoning powder, half a tsp black pepper, fresh chili, half a lime, and some boiled chicken blood. Finely mash the boiled blood, then add the seasoning powder, pepper, and sliced chili and mix well. Finally, squeeze in the lime juice and mix gently.

mon_an.ten: Distinguishing Chuối Tây and Chuối Tiêu: Shape, Color, and Flavor
mon_an.mo_ta: Can you distinguish between all types of bananas? Do you know which is Chuối Tây and which is Chuối Tiêu? If not, read the guide below! General overview of Chuối Tây and Chuối Tiêu.
cac_buoc: 1. Chuối Tây
Chuối Tây, also known as Apple banana or Cavendish in some contexts, is a popular type of banana on the market. It originated from the Atlantic region and is widely grown worldwide.
2. Chuối Tiêu
Chuối Tiêu, also known as Taiwanese banana, is a smaller type of banana originating from Taiwan.
It has small fruits, yellow-green or yellow in color, and has a sweet but slightly tart taste.
Distinguishing Chuối Tây and Chuối Tiêu through shape, color, and flavor
1. Chuối Tiêu:

Chuối Tiêu is loved by many people. It is known that Chuối Tiêu is usually divided into two types: dwarf and tall. A notable feature of this banana is its long, crescent-curved shape. When unripe, the skin is dark green, and when ripe, it turns an attractive yellow.

To identify a riper and sweeter Chuối Tiêu, you can look at the appearance. When black spots appear on the skin and the flesh is yellow, the banana will have a deep sweet flavor. The flesh of Chuối Tiêu is very soft and fragrant, providing a refreshing sensation when eaten.

You can eat Chuối Tiêu both green and ripe. Green Chuối Tiêu has a characteristic astringent taste; you can slice it to eat with raw vegetables or use it in dishes like fish braised with bananas, eel simmered with bananas, and many others. As for ripe Chuối Tiêu, you can eat it directly, make banana smoothies, banana ice cream, banana cakes, and many other delicious dishes.

Thus, Chuối Tiêu not only has a characteristic flavor but is also versatile in use, from raw dishes to desserts. Enjoy the wonderful flavors that Chuối Tiêu brings by exploring its diversity in cuisine.
Chuối Tiêu
2. Chuối Tây:

Chuối Tây is a small-sized banana, easily distinguished by its characteristic shape. The fruit is thick in the middle, tapered at both ends, has a long stem, and the skin has three distinct ridges. Usually, when Chuối Tây is ripe, the skin becomes thicker and light yellow, while the flesh is white.

The flavor of Chuối Tây is very special and appealing. The flesh is chewy and firm, offering a balanced sweet taste with a hint of acidity. This makes Chuối Tây a delicious and interesting choice that you can eat a lot of without getting bored, thanks to its diverse and attractive flavor.

With such unique characteristics, Chuối Tây is not just an ordinary fruit but also brings a unique and interesting culinary experience. Enjoy the characteristic flavor of Chuối Tây and discover the richness it brings to your cooking!
Chuối Tây

mon_an.ten: How to Prevent Sliced Lotus Root from Discoloring
mon_an.mo_ta: When preparing lotus root, follow these tips to prevent it from changing color:
cac_buoc: Slice into thin pieces.
Dip into boiling water for a moment and remove immediately.
Add a little salt to soak for a while.
Then rinse again with clean water.

Add vinegar, minced ginger, MSG, and sesame oil; mix well for a very crunchy salad. Alternatively, you can put it in a pan and stir-fry, tossing a few times, add a little salt and MSG, then remove from the heat immediately. Doing this will keep the lotus root white, crunchy, and delicious.
When stir-frying lotus root, if it seems too dry, you can add a little water; the dish will be whiter and softer.

mon_an.ten: Tips for Quickly Tenderizing Stewed Chicken, Duck, and Goose
mon_an.mo_ta: If you don't know how to stew chicken, duck, or goose so they soften quickly, refer to these cooking tips: Methods for tenderizing chicken.
cac_buoc: Before slaughtering the chicken, pour a tablespoon of vinegar into its mouth and wait a few minutes before processing. This chicken meat will become tender and delicious quickly when stewed.
Alternatively, add 3-4 hawthorn berries or a few potatoes when stewing an old chicken; the meat will also soften quickly.
Before stewing, stir-fry the chicken (whole) with aromatic vinegar, then put it in to stew; it will soften very fast.

You can also use a pressure cooker at setting 5 to stew old chicken; the meat softens quickly without losing its aroma. Then transfer it to a clay pot and simmer for about half an hour; the meat will be delicious and save fuel. This method can also be used for duck and goose.
Methods for tenderizing duck
The following methods apply only to duck:
Drop a few metal screws into the pot to cook together; the duck meat will soften quickly.
Take a small piece of pig pancreas, chop it up, and add it to the pot with the duck; the meat will soften quickly and have a delicious aroma.
Methods for tenderizing goose
For goose meat, you can pick cherry leaves, wash them, and drop them into the pot to stew or cook with the meat; it will soften very quickly.

mon_an.mo_ta: Here are 3 ways to cook mung beans: – Wash the beans, drain them dry, and pour them into boiling water. The water only needs to cover the beans by one finger joint. When the water in the pot is almost dry, pour in more boiling water, then cover tightly and cook for several dozen minutes; the beans will be soft without changing color.
cac_buoc: Wash the beans and put them into a thermos, pour in boiling water, close the lid tightly, and after about 3-4 hours, the beans will be soft and expanded. Then pour them into a pot to cook; they will soften very quickly.
Stir-fry the beans in a cast-iron pot (or pan) for about 10 minutes before cooking; the beans will also soften quickly.

mon_an.mo_ta: Defrost food quickly and safely with simple tips that can limit numerous harmful agents, as food is very susceptible to bacterial contamination during the defrosting process if not done correctly. Proper defrosting is not difficult if we know how. Defrosting food is just as important as cooking it.
cac_buoc: Modern homemakers have many ways to defrost food; however, many methods are unscientific and affect the nutrients in the food. Here are 2 defrosting methods that homemakers should use:
Defrosting with cold water
This is a fast defrosting method; you just need to run cold water over the frozen food bag or submerge the entire sealed bag in a basin of clean water.

The advantage of this method is that it defrosts food quickly and safely, but you must always keep an eye on the food. The food must be packed in a tightly sealed plastic bag so that water does not touch the meat directly. Do not use hot water, as it can heat the outer layer of the meat to a temperature favorable for bacterial growth. Every 30 minutes, you need to change the water to ensure it stays cold enough.
If defrosting fish, you should add a little crushed fresh ginger or salt to the water; the fish meat will taste better.
Defrosting in the refrigerator

Compared to water defrosting, refrigerator defrosting is safer against bacteria but takes a very long time to melt the ice. With this method, you must move the food from the freezer to the fridge compartment overnight for it to be ready by the next morning.

Poultry, fish, and ground meat defrosted this way can be safely kept in the refrigerator for another 1-2 days before cooking. This is also a fast and safe way to defrost food. Another advantage is that if you decide not to cook the defrosted meat, you can safely move it back to the freezer to refreeze.
Once food has been defrosted, it should not be put back in the freezer to refreeze (unless defrosted in the fridge), as this can easily generate harmful bacteria for the user.

mon_an.ten: Guide to Ripening Fruit Quickly and Removing Astringency
cac_buoc: In fruit processing, a common issue we face is waiting for fruit to ripen naturally and removing unacceptable astringency. However, there are several simple methods to ripen fruit quickly and effectively remove the astringent taste. Let's explore the methods and steps to enjoy these attractive fruits!
1. Using paper bags to ripen fruit faster

Paper bags, a common material for food storage, can be a useful tool to make fruit ripen faster. Every fruit naturally produces ethylene gas, a substance that stimulates the ripening process. By placing the fruit in a paper bag and tying the mouth slightly loose, the ethylene gas cannot escape and will act on the fruit, making it ripen faster.

For best results, ensure the paper bag is dry, keep it out of direct sunlight, and leave the fruit at room temperature. Once the fruit is ripe enough, move it to the refrigerator to stop the ripening process.
2. Using cotton cloth to ripen fruit faster

To use cotton cloth to ripen fruit faster, prepare a clean, soft cotton towel or linen cloth. Spread the towel out and place soft fruits like peaches, plums, or thin-skinned fruits on the towel, ensuring the stem side is facing down. Leave some space between the fruits so they do not touch each other.

Then, use another towel to cover the fruit or use the same towel if it is large enough to wrap all the fruit. By wrapping the fruit in cloth and waiting until they become soft or fragrant, you can get them ready to enjoy.
3. Placing fruit in the rice bin

The rice bin is another option to ripen fruit faster. Rice has a good ability to retain ethylene gas; therefore, placing fruit in the rice bin will help them ripen faster than leaving them on the table or in paper or plastic bags.

To perform this method, ensure you bury the fruit deep into the rice, which will speed up the ripening process. However, this method should only be applied to fruits that are almost fully ripe or that you want to eat the next day.
4. Using ripe apples or bananas

To make fruit ripen faster, after placing them in a paper or plastic bag, you can add a ripe apple or banana to the bag. Apples and bananas are two types of fruit that release more ethylene than others; therefore, they will stimulate a faster ripening process for the other fruits in the same bag.
Note:
These methods can be applied to fruits such as avocados, papayas, bananas, sapodillas, cantaloupes, mangoes, peaches, pears, plums, pineapples, tomatoes, and custard apples.
However, do not apply these methods to apples, blueberries, cherries, grapes, pomegranates, strawberries, raspberries, watermelons, oranges, lemons, limes, tangerines, and grapefruits.
These fruits are usually best when ripened on the tree, so after buying them, they should be kept in the refrigerator to avoid waste if they ripen too quickly before you can eat them.
Specifically for crunchy persimmons (hồng ngâm), if you want to make them ripen faster, you need to soak them in basins of plain water.
Above are the ways to ripen fruit quickly and remove astringency. By utilizing these methods, you will have the opportunity to enjoy sweet, ripe, and fresh fruits.

mon_an.ten: 5 Simple Steps to Remove Pesticides from Vegetables
mon_an.mo_ta: Homemakers are finding it increasingly difficult to choose vegetables, as many pesticides and preservative chemicals are used today. So how can we reduce the amount of pesticides on vegetables? These tips will provide 5 simple ways to help clean pesticides from your produce.
cac_buoc: 5 Simple Steps to Remove Pesticides from Vegetables

Vegetables and fruits often have high levels of pesticides and preservative chemicals because they attract many pests. Furthermore, vegetables usually only stay fresh for a short time. Therefore, to keep them looking fresh, they are often sprayed with many pesticides and preservatives.
These substances are very toxic when ingested, bringing many bad consequences to consumers. These tips will provide a few ways to help you wash away these dangerous chemicals.
1. Wash vegetables with a 5% salt water solution.
2. Cucumbers, apples, etc., are fruits with high residue levels; for your health, wash them thoroughly and peel them before eating!

3. High temperatures can also decompose pesticides. Therefore, for some heat-resistant vegetables like bean sprouts, cauliflower, celery... you should blanch them for 2 minutes in boiling water. This will significantly reduce the pesticide amount, and during the cooking process, the remaining pesticides will be fully decomposed.
4. Sunlight also has the effect of decomposing organic mercury and organic chlorine on vegetables. Leave vegetables under the sun for 5 minutes, and most of these two substances will evaporate.
5. Soak vegetables in clean water for 5 - 10 minutes before washing, or use rice water to soak fruits first. The purpose of this is to neutralize the harmful substances in the produce.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 1: Cooking Oil and Lard
mon_an.mo_ta: – Meat products should use peanut oil: Peanut oil has a fragrance that can eliminate the fishy or gamey smell in various meats. You can drizzle some heated peanut oil over steamed fish. Using lard makes the fish less fragrant and creates a greasy, fatty smell. If stir-frying marinated beef, you can add a little peanut oil before putting it on the stove.
cac_buoc: When stir-frying or cooking vegetables, you should use lard: This is because lard makes the vegetables glossy, smooth, and fragrant.
For noodles and glass noodles, you can use a combination of peanut oil and lard: The food will have the aroma of peanuts and the richness of lard.
*Sesame oil should only be used for dishes with fishy or pungent smells:* Only use sesame oil for 1-2 dishes in a meal, and use only a small amount after the dish is cooked.

*Vegetable oils:* Soybean oil, corn oil, sesame oil, cottonseed oil, peanut oil... contain many fatty acids that can reduce blood pressure and cholesterol levels in the blood, while providing essential fatty acids for the body. But if used in excessively high amounts, they will cause reverse effects, negatively impacting the body, especially the blood and blood vessels.

When using cooking oil, pay attention to the appropriate timing. When processing ingredients, you need to add other spices first, then add the oil; this ensures the solubility of the spices. You can add oil when the food is cooked but still on the stove, then remove it immediately; this makes the dish more fragrant and glossy, but it can make the food harder to digest and affect health.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 2: Determining Oil and Fat Temperature
mon_an.mo_ta: The temperature of oil or fat significantly affects the flavor and color of a dish after it is removed from the heat. The concept of "levels" is often used to measure the heat of oil or fat. Typically, each level corresponds to about 25-30°C. The levels can be divided as follows: *Level 1-2:* A few small bubbles of oil or fat slowly rise from the bottom of the pot.
cac_buoc: *Level 3-4:* The surface of the oil begins to ripple in waves, but no oil smoke has risen yet.
*Level 5-6:* The wave-like movements become stronger, with very intense movement in the center compared to the edges; oil smoke begins to rise.
*Level 7-8:* The oil surface begins to look calm again, a lot of oil smoke rises, and there is a bubbling sound when stirred with a ladle.
*Level 9:* The oil smoke is thick and rises even faster.

Oil temperature requirements vary for each dish. For frying, the fat should be kept at Level 7-8 to ensure the dish is "crispy on the outside and tender on the inside." If using oil or fat only to lubricate the food, the temperature should be at Level 4-5; if you want the food to be more seared, use Level 8 or higher with a short heating time so the food is crispy outside while remaining soft inside. Home cooking methods cannot be exactly like those in restaurants; generally, the amount of oil used at home is less and the heat source is weaker than in restaurants; therefore, the temperature of oil or fat in home cooking needs to be higher than in restaurants.
*Note:* Eating food stir-fried or fried in oil at high temperatures is not beneficial for your health.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 3: Tips for Using Oil, Fat, and Cooking
mon_an.mo_ta: Preventing oil and fat from splattering – Sprinkle a little salt into the fat before heating to prevent oil from splattering when adding food to be fried; this avoids burns and neutralizes Aspergillus flavus toxins remaining in the oil or fat.
cac_buoc: Preventing oil and fat from overflowing

When stir-frying vegetables that release a lot of water, the volume of the oil or fat will increase and may cause it to overflow. Simply drop a few Sichuan peppercorns into the oil and it will quickly subside.
Rendering lard
When rendering lard, keep the heat low. Determine the flame level: it is correct when the fire does not produce blue smoke.
Pour a little filtered water into the pot before rendering the fat; this prevents the residue in the fat from burning, maintains a delicious aroma, and makes the lard whiter and more plentiful.
Choosing the right time to add salt while cooking

Add salt at the appropriate time when stir-frying vegetables: For root vegetables (parts that grow underground), add salt a bit earlier so it can penetrate the vegetables. For cabbage, cauliflower, melons, and beans, add it later; if added too early, the water and nutrients in the vegetables will be released, making them mushy and flavorless, and increasing cooking time. It is best to add salt when the vegetables are just cooked through.
Choosing the right time to add soy sauce

Using soy sauce when stir-frying vegetables can give them a sour smell because a portion of the sugar in the soy sauce decomposes when heated, releasing a sour taste. You can "fix" this by adding a little sugar. However, it is best to remove the pan from the heat immediately after drizzling the soy sauce.
Fixing the dish when too much vinegar is added

Add an appropriate amount of sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) and stir well if you accidentally pour too much vinegar into the dish. The sodium bicarbonate will neutralize the acetic acid in the vinegar and reduce the sourness.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 4: How to Use MSG
mon_an.mo_ta: The best way to use MSG is to add it after the soup or vegetables have been ladled into a bowl. Doing this makes the dish more delicious and ensures it is not harmful to the body. MSG contains 13% sodium; using excessive amounts increases the risk for people with conditions such as high blood pressure, kidney disease, or heart disease. Therefore, a person weighing 50 kg should not consume more than 6 g of MSG per day.
cac_buoc: MSG only takes effect after it is dissolved in food. Therefore, for freshly stir-fried vegetables, ladle them into a bowl, pour out a little of the vegetable juice, dissolve the MSG in it, and then pour it back into the large bowl of vegetables and mix well. Do not use a small spoon or pour it into your hand to sprinkle it over. For salads, cold mixed vegetables, or dry hot vegetables, you can dissolve the MSG in a little boiling water before pouring it over the vegetables and mixing well.

MSG is very difficult to dissolve in foods with high acidity (such as pickles). In foods with high alkalinity (such as salted eggs), it will produce a pungent, sour taste. Therefore, it is best not to use MSG with highly acidic or alkaline foods.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 5: Seasoning Order and Water Secrets in Stir-frying and Frying
mon_an.mo_ta: In cooking, seasoning appropriately is not enough; you must also know the order of adding ingredients—which spice goes in first and which goes in last. The basic principle is: ingredients with weak absorption should be added first, and those with strong absorption should be added later. For example, if stir-frying a dish that requires sugar, add the sugar first, followed by salt, vinegar, soy sauce or fish sauce, and finally MSG. *Note:* Seasonings without a distinct aroma like salt and sugar can withstand heat during long cooking times; however, those with characteristic aromas like vinegar, soy sauce, and fish sauce cannot withstand it and the scent will evaporate. Secrets of using water when stir-frying and frying.
cac_buoc: Many readers likely know that when stir-frying sliced or minced meat, besides skill in slicing and seasoning with soy sauce, fish sauce, salt, onions, ginger, and starch, adding a precise amount of water will make the dish tastier. Quickly add the meat and stir well with chopsticks when the fat in the pot has reached the required temperature. At that point, you should also add a little water and an appropriate vegetable, stir-frying until cooked. This helps control and compensate for the water in the meat that evaporates under high heat; at the same time, the meat will become tender and more delicious.

Soak peanuts in water to let them plump up slightly, then drain them before adding them to a pot of boiling fat that completely covers the peanuts. When they are almost cooked, reduce the heat and wait until they are crispy. Remove them, add sugar and salt, and you're done. Stir-fried peanuts will be fragrant, crispy, larger, with the skins intact and a glossier appearance than dry-roasted or stir-fried peanuts. This method can also be applied to soybeans.

When you want to fry steamed bread, slice it, dip it completely in water, lift it out and let it drain for a moment, then quickly drop it into a pan of hot fat and fry. The slices will be golden brown, crispy on the outside but soft inside, fragrant, and will absorb very little fat. Do not soak all the bread slices at once; soak them as you fry to prevent the bread from becoming mushy.

Using a ratio of 500g of cooking fat to 1,500g of boiling water, wait until the water surface is calm again and there are no bubbles rising. Then you can add the ingredients to be fried; this is more effective than frying with fat alone.

mon_an.ten: Using Spices Part 6: Three Useful Tips
mon_an.mo_ta: "Fixing" clumped white sugar: When white sugar clumps together, cut a few pieces of jujube and put them in, then pour everything into a glass jar and seal it tightly for a while; the sugar will naturally separate back to its original state.
cac_buoc: How to dissolve clumped rock sugar

If rock sugar forms into very large clumps that are difficult to break, hang a 100W light bulb very close to the rock sugar so the heat radiates onto it. Turn the clumps over evenly; after 1-2 minutes, you can easily break them apart by hand.
How to crush garlic without it splattering

Use a piece of soft cloth that fits tightly over the mouth of the mortar and wrap it around the handle of the pestle. When crushing, the cloth acts as a mobile lid to prevent the garlic from splattering out.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chili is a very good spice and is loved by many people; however, not everyone knows how to use chili correctly. This article will introduce you to the best ways to preserve and use chili peppers!
cac_buoc: Tips for using chili peppers correctly:

How to keep and preserve chili peppers: Fresh chilies can be placed in a plastic bag and kept in the refrigerator for up to 2 weeks. Dried chilies can be stored at room temperature, away from damp areas and direct sunlight, for about 4 months. Additionally, you can use a knife to slit the chili and remove the seeds, soak it in warm boiled water, and then dry it. When eating, just soak it in warm water again and the chili will be as fresh as the original. Another way to preserve chilies for a long time is to put them in the freezer. After buying chilies, remove the stems, wash them clean, then put them in a sealed container and place them in the freezer. When eating, just take them out and rinse with water; the chili will soften again. According to some people's experience, this method can keep chilies for a very long time without spoiling.

Chilies should be cooked before eating: Chilies are processed in many ways—they can be ground, pickled with garlic, or eaten fresh because the nutrients will be more abundant. However, it is best to cook chilies before eating. This is because chilies contain a lot of capsaicin, which can irritate the oral and digestive mucosa. Once boiled in water, the digestive irritation of the chili will decrease.

Adding seasonings to chili: Chilies are spicy, hot, and slightly sour. When you add seasonings to chili, such as garlic, bamboo shoots, or vinegar, you will eat less chili and harmonize it with many other spices. This helps you consume chili in a healthier way.
People who should not eat chili:

People with cardiovascular and cerebrovascular diseases, high blood pressure, or chronic bronchitis should not eat spicy food because the capsaicin in chili will increase blood circulation, making the heart beat faster. People with these diseases who eat a lot of spicy food over a long period may suffer from acute heart failure.
People with chronic gastritis or stomach ulcers should not eat chili because it can cause mucosal edema and increase gastric motility, affecting the recovery of digestive function.
People with chronic cholecystitis or gallstones will find that chili stimulates more stomach acid secretion, making gallbladder-related diseases more serious.

People with hemorrhoids must absolutely avoid eating a lot of spicy food as it can cause anal abscesses. Additionally, chili causes constipation and makes hemorrhoids more serious and harder to treat.

People with pink eye or keratitis will find that eating chili makes these conditions worse. Pregnant women and those who have just given birth should avoid eating a lot of spicy food as it can affect the baby through breastfeeding.

mon_an.mo_ta: Using microgreens correctly – Currently, most vegetables contain some level of pesticides or preservatives, so homemakers are switching to growing and eating microgreens. Home-grown vegetables are not only clean but also contain many good nutrients for women. A few tips below will help you use microgreens more correctly for healthier meals.
cac_buoc: You can currently grow microgreens yourself or buy them at supermarkets and clean vegetable stores.

For home-grown microgreens, using them correctly is not difficult; since they are home-grown, the quality is guaranteed to be clean and fresh. However, you should harvest them as soon as they reach the right size; if the greens get too old, they will no longer be delicious.

For store-bought microgreens, you should still be careful because they might have been fertilized to grow plumper and extend the harvest time. Therefore, you should wash these types of microgreens very thoroughly. Then, soak them in a diluted salt water solution to clean off bacteria and fertilizer.

Note that microgreens are very delicate and easily bruised. Therefore, during the washing process, you should be gentle and use a very diluted salt solution; if the solution is too concentrated, it can make the greens salty. Use microgreens correctly to make the dish delicious.

Microgreens are very suitable for dishes such as salads, oil and vinegar dressings, or eaten raw. Because microgreens are cooling and easy to eat, they are great for mixed salads. For stir-fried or cooked dishes, pay special attention because microgreens are very soft and cook quickly. If you are not careful, the greens can become mushy and lose their nutrients.
Microgreens should be eaten within the day and not kept for long. However, you can also put them in a sealed container in the refrigerator at 5°C to keep them for an additional 2-3 days.

mon_an.mo_ta: I notice that during Tet, a lot of food is used and often not finished, which is very wasteful. Furthermore, Tet is a time for feasting; if you don't prepare and pre-process the ingredients, it takes a lot of time and you won't be able to enjoy yourself with everyone. Today, I would like to share a few tips for efficient food use during Tet to help you cook faster, more conveniently, and avoid food waste. Wish you a prosperous New Year with your family and loved ones! Happy New Year!
cac_buoc: Prepare cooking ingredients in advance:
Offerings must be fresh; do not use leftovers for offerings. Offering rice must also be freshly cooked, and the pot must be washed clean before cooking.
Prepare spring rolls (nem) before Tet and freeze them. When it's time to eat, take them out, wrap them in an extra layer of rice paper, and re-fry them; they will be both crispy and beautiful.
Clean and pre-process vegetables and fruits for 2-3 days before Tet, and keep them cold in plastic containers; just take them out to use at mealtime.
Plan the menu in advance for each day and each meal to avoid repeating dishes or having too many or too few dishes.
Pickled and fermented dishes should be prepared many days before Tet.

Dishes to avoid: Avoid dishes that should not be eaten on the first day of the New Year, such as squid or balut (trứng lộn)... (my mother says to abstain, though I like those dishes a lot; it's best to avoid them to prevent being scolded by grandparents! :D)

Prepare appetizers: You should prepare snacks for drinking before Tet, such as fermented pork (nem chua), beef soaked in fish sauce, pork shank soaked in fish sauce, or pig ears soaked in vinegar. Homemade items are both hygienic and just as delicious as those from the store!
Utilize leftovers: Make food for breakfast or snacks by using leftovers such as:
Chicken: Cook rice noodle soup (bún thang), glass noodles, phở, or porridge...
Vietnamese ham and sausages: Eat with hot sticky rice or cook with rice noodles...
Bánh chưng: Fry until golden; it's best eaten with pickles!
Additionally, I find the decoration stage very important. A feast that is both delicious and beautiful will surely be admired by everyone!
Above is what I know; you can share other recipes for everyone to refer to. Wish you a prosperous New Year!

mon_an.ten: Using Black Garlic Correctly for Maximum Benefits
mon_an.mo_ta: Black garlic is considered a miracle cure that can treat many diseases and is popular in many places, especially South Korea and Japan. However, not everyone knows how to use black garlic effectively. You can refer to the way to use black garlic to learn more useful information!
cac_buoc: Black garlic:

It is garlic fermented over a long period of about 45 days under precise temperature and humidity conditions. In South Korea and Japan, black garlic is widely used as a health-enhancing food. Black garlic has very high antioxidant properties and is considered capable of prolonging youth. In recent years, black garlic has become known to many for its miraculous health benefits, thanks to a nutrient content many times higher than regular garlic, most notably its anti-cancer and antioxidant properties.

Black garlic is actually a product of fermenting fresh garlic under appropriate conditions; it is black, chewy, has almost no unpleasant odor, and has a sweet taste similar to fruit. When eating, users only need to peel the outer layer. Black garlic can be preserved for a longer time than regular garlic.
Main benefits of black garlic:

Enhances immunity: Black garlic is proven to have antioxidant properties twice as high as regular garlic, which can slow down the body's aging process while protecting the body from damage caused by free radicals.

Anti-inflammatory and anti-infective: Black garlic contains S-allylcysteine, which supports the absorption of allicin, strongly promoting the body's self-defense against invading bacteria, viruses, and infections.
Reduces blood cholesterol: Black garlic contains S-allylcysteine and a derivative of the amino acid cysteine, which can effectively reduce blood cholesterol.

Prevents and supports cancer treatment: Organic sulfur compounds and tetrahydro-beta-carboline derivatives formed during fermentation have strong free radical scavenging activity and higher lipid peroxidation inhibition than regular garlic.
Improves blood circulation and liver function: Black garlic helps blood circulation become regular and continuous, helping to eliminate toxins and protect liver function more effectively.
How to use black garlic reasonably?
To help consumers easily use black garlic correctly every day to exploit its health benefits, we have 3 choices:
Option 1: Peel and eat raw directly, 3-5 cloves/day; for the elderly, 1-2 cloves/day.
Option 2: Drink black garlic soaked in wine, 10-20ml/day.
Option 3: Use black garlic to prepare dishes according to personal preference.
Notes to know when using black garlic:
However, while using black garlic, you should also note a few issues:
First: Only use black garlic with a clear origin and food safety quality inspection.
Second: Use black garlic according to the allowed quantity; do not use too much as it will have the opposite effect.
Third: Preserve black garlic correctly; keep it in a cool, dry place, avoiding direct contact with sunlight.
Above are some things to know about black garlic that I have collected. You can refer to many other useful tips and delicious dishes!

mon_an.ten: Benefits of the Basket Plant in Treating Coughs
mon_an.mo_ta: As we know, the basket plant (Callisia fragrans) has many benefits, treating back pain, skin diseases, stomach diseases, diabetes, cardiovascular diseases, and even coughs. This illness often appears when the weather turns cold, especially in winter for young children when playing makes them forget to keep their bodies warm. Treating a sore throat with basket plant leaves.
cac_buoc: Benefits of the basket plant in treating coughs
Below are a few ways to use basket plant leaves to treat a cough.

Method 1: Use 50g of basket plant leaves, wash them, then crush them in a mortar and squeeze out the juice. Mix the juice with 5 drops of banana vinegar and drink it regularly every day. Drink for about 5 days, then stop for 5 days before continuing. Drinking continuously like this for a month will cure coughs caused by sore throats, bronchitis, and many stomach, liver, kidney, or gallstone diseases, as well as being very effective for the common cold.

Method 2: Choose a few fresh basket plant leaves and wash them, then add a few grains of salt and wrap the leaf like a betel quid. Chew and hold the pulp in your mouth, swallowing the juice. Use this about 2 to 3 times a day, 2 to 3 leaves each time. Using this for about a month will show a reduction in sore throat symptoms such as a dry cough, sore throat, and loss of voice.
If used regularly, it can even treat chronic sore throats.
How to treat a dry cough with basket plant leaves

Coughing is a common ailment in the elderly and children. Children in the house often get a dry cough in the cold winter; at this time, you can crush basket plant leaves, chew them thoroughly, swallow the juice, and discard the pulp. Chew 3 times a day before meals; doing this for about 3 to 4 days will completely stop the dry cough. Adults can also apply this method with similar effectiveness.
Above are the common ways used to treat coughs. Not only for coughs, but you can also apply this in other cases, using a dosage suitable for your body's condition to bring effectiveness.

Nevertheless, besides the benefits that the basket plant brings, this medicine can also cause side effects in people with weakened immune systems who are prone to allergies. Therefore, everyone needs to be cautious or, best of all, consult a doctor carefully before using the basket plant to treat their illness.

mon_an.mo_ta: Heart-Shaped Boiled Eggs – A clever tip to add variety to your boiled eggs for decorating dishes or lunch boxes. Here is a guide on how to make heart-shaped eggs.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare all the necessary ingredients and tools.
Step 2: Fold the cardboard in half lengthwise, place the peeled egg in the center, then place the chopstick on top of the egg.
Step 3: While the boiled egg is still warm, place it in the center of the cardboard. Use rubber bands to secure both ends as shown (remember the egg must be warm, otherwise it will break easily).
Step 4: The chopstick acts as a press to create a deep indentation. This is why the egg must be warm; if it's cold, pressing it will cause it to crack.
Step 5: After 10-15 minutes, remove the chopstick and cardboard. Looking from one end of the egg, you will see the heart shape. Slice the egg in half crosswise to get two heart halves.
Source: Ngoi sao

mon_an.ten: 5 Simple and Delicious Ways to Boil Soft-Boiled Eggs
mon_an.mo_ta: Soft-boiled eggs with runny yolks and tender whites are an attractive and nutritious dish. From simple steps to refined techniques, you will find a recipe that suits your preference and cooking skills. Read on to discover 5 simple and delicious ways to boil soft-boiled eggs! I. Preparation
thoi_gian: Timing is crucial for soft-boiled eggs; even a 1-minute difference can lead to failure.
cac_buoc: You can use chicken eggs (or duck eggs, as preferred) for this dish.
Next, prepare the seasoning – vinegar.
Use a pot with a lid, a slotted spoon, and a sharp pin.
II. 5 simple and easy ways to boil soft-boiled eggs
1. Traditional soft-boiled egg method
To prepare this, you will need the following ingredients:
1 chicken egg.
500ml filtered water.
Here is the process:
Step 1: Wash the egg with water to remove any surface dirt.
Step 2: Use a small pot, place the egg inside, and pour in enough water to submerge the egg.
Step 3: Bring the pot to a boil. The cooking time varies depending on your desired level of doneness. Generally, once the water boils, you should cook the egg for about 6 minutes.
Step 4: When the time is up, prepare a bowl of cold water, remove the egg, and soak it for 2-3 minutes before peeling.
Step 5: When you enjoy the egg, you will immediately taste the soft, creamy yolk. It has no fishy smell and is exceptionally appealing.
Soft-boiled egg: 4-5 minutes (runny yolk, soft white).
Hard-boiled egg: 9-12 minutes (both yolk and white are firm).
Choose the cooking time that fits your preference and turn off the heat once the desired doneness is reached.
2. Boiling eggs with an electric kettle
Ingredients to prepare:
Over 1 liter of filtered water.
The process is as follows:
Step 1: First, pour water into the kettle and carefully place the rack inside.
Step 2: Place the eggs into the kettle and close the lid tightly.
Step 3: Wait for about 3 minutes, then remove the eggs and immediately soak them in ice water.
Step 4: Peel the eggs and enjoy the sweet flavor of the runny yolk combined with an indescribable smoothness.
Enjoy the wonderful flavor of these boiled eggs and savor this special dish.
3. How to boil eggs in the microwave
Ingredients to prepare:
The process:
Step 1: Place the egg in a ceramic bowl and ensure it is completely submerged in water (this prevents the egg from exploding).
Step 2: Add a pinch of salt to the bowl and microwave on high for about 7 minutes.
Step 3: Once finished, remove the egg from the microwave and place it in cold water or serve immediately while hot.
Step 4: A unique feature of this method is the egg's chewy texture and a subtle hint of salt, creating a unique combination.
Enjoy the boiled egg using this method and experience the special flavor it brings.
4. How to boil soft-boiled eggs with vinegar
Ingredients to prepare:
1200ml filtered water.
Step 1: Wash the egg and use a pin to prick a small hole at the large end (this helps the egg release air).
Step 2: Prepare a small pot with a thick bottom and boil 500ml of filtered water.
Step 3: Add 2 tbsp of vinegar to the boiling water and reduce to low heat.
Step 4: Place the egg in the pot and boil for about 6 minutes (remember to cover with a lid and let it sit for an additional 3 minutes).
Step 5: Remove the egg immediately and soak it in a bowl of cold water for 2 minutes.
Step 6: Peel the egg and experience the rich flavor of the yolk.
Enjoy the boiled egg using this method and feel the special flavor of the smooth, soft yolk.
5. How to boil soft-boiled eggs in a rice cooker
Step 1: Place the egg in the rice cooker and pour in enough water to submerge half of the egg.
Step 2: Close the lid and turn on the "Cook" mode.
Step 3: Wait until the rice cooker switches to "Keep Warm" mode, then remove the egg immediately and soak it in a bowl of cold water for 3 minutes.
Step 4: Peel the egg and enjoy the delicious, rich flavor of the boiled yolk.
Enjoy the special flavor that soft-boiled eggs from this process bring.
III. Notes when boiling soft-boiled eggs
Here are important notes to ensure perfect success when boiling soft-boiled eggs:
Choose eggs that are not cracked and ensure they are clean.
To prevent the eggs from breaking, boil them in gently simmering water.
Peel the eggs gently without applying too much pressure to keep the soft-boiled egg intact.
IV. How to choose fresh eggs
When buying commercial chicken eggs, note the following to ensure you select fresh, high-quality eggs:
Choose eggs with a fresh, uniform deep orange color, without pale hues or brown spots.
Check the surface of the egg by touching it. If it feels slightly rough and grainy, these are signs of a fresh egg. Conversely, a smooth surface may indicate the egg is old.
Shake the egg near your ear and listen. If there is no sound, it is a sign of a fresh egg and you should buy it. If there is a loud sloshing sound, the egg may be old.
These tips will help you choose fresh and high-quality commercial chicken eggs when shopping.

mon_an.mo_ta: What does a 7-day meal plan for diabetics include? Let's find out in the article below! Diabetes is a chronic disease that develops silently. It affects daily life and can lead to dangerous complications in the eyes, heart, feet, hands, and kidneys if the patient does not establish a scientific diet. However, choosing food and planning a daily menu is not easy for many. Limited food choices and balancing energy while ensuring nutrition can be a headache. You can refer to this 7-day meal plan for diabetic patients in the post below.
cac_buoc: Nutritional principles to remember for diabetic patients
Principle 1: Diverse nutrition

A diverse and complete diet from many food sources will provide enough necessary nutrients for the body to function normally. For diabetic patients, especially children, maintaining a full and diverse diet is important to ensure comprehensive mental and intellectual health development.
Usually, a balanced diet must include all the following groups: carbohydrates, protein, fats, fiber, and minerals to protect the patient's health:

Protein: Protein should account for about 15-20% of energy intake (equivalent to 0.8g/kg/day for adults) and supports the development of body cells and tissues. However, for patients with kidney issues, protein intake needs adjustment.

Fats (lipids): Total energy from fat should be around 25% of the diet and should not exceed 30%. Limit saturated fats (animal fats) as they can cause arterial blockage. Instead, consume unsaturated fats, such as sesame oil, soybean oil, sunflower oil, etc., to provide energy and absorb certain vitamins.

Carbohydrates: Energy from carbohydrates should reach 50-60% of total energy. Priority should be given to complex carbohydrates like grains and tubers, while limiting simple sugars and high-sugar foods (cakes, candies, soft drinks, etc.).
Principle 2: Maintain 3 main meals

It is necessary to maintain 3 stable main meals in the daily diet. For those with stable weight and good blood sugar control, there is no need for extra snacks or splitting meals. Patients should only have snacks when they are very active or at risk of hypoglycemia, which can be dangerous, such as elderly patients, those with severe cardiovascular complications, kidney failure, or those using Insulin. Whether to have a snack or not should be carefully considered.
Eating 3 full meals a day, combined with light snacks, will help avoid the above risks and maintain stable blood glucose levels.
Principle 3: Increase fiber

Fiber plays an important role in treating diabetes because it helps control sugar, fat, and blood pressure levels. High-fiber foods like green vegetables and certain fruits stay in the stomach longer, slowing digestion and the absorption of sugar into the blood.
The recommended fiber intake for an adult is 20-50g per day.
Principle 4: Use healthy cooking methods

Simple cooking methods help preserve the nutritional content of food. Therefore, healthy cooking methods usually involve fewer steps and limited seasoning, prioritizing natural spices. Here are the principles to note:
Use cooking methods like boiling, steaming, or stewing to limit fat usage, instead of pan-searing or deep-frying. Use natural spices and limit sugar.
Avoid using high-carbohydrate foods like cornstarch or wheat flour to prepare dishes.

Nutritional principles for diabetic patients are established to guide the diet and remind patients how to care for and improve their health. In addition to following nutritional principles, diabetic patients must adhere to treatment protocols to maintain stable blood sugar, increase treatment effectiveness, and limit potential complications.
Notes when planning nutrition for meals
1. Breakfast
A diabetic's breakfast should include carbohydrates, naturally ripe fruits, and protein. You can choose a bowl of glass noodles, phở, noodles, sweet potatoes, or whole grains.
2. Lunch

For lunch, you need to increase fiber from vegetables like lettuce, red peppers, corn, black beans, whole grains, etc. Supplement protein from lean pork loin or skinless chicken. Additionally, include foods rich in vitamins, omega-3, and magnesium.
3. Dinner

For dinner, you should eat less than at lunch and breakfast and choose easily digestible foods. For protein, you can choose salmon or tofu. Other nutrients like antioxidants, magnesium, vitamins, and fiber can come from asparagus, broccoli, peas, and tomatoes.

A small note for diabetic patients is that main meals should be eaten in moderation; do not eat until overly full. If you feel hungry 1-2 hours after eating, you can have a light snack with some fruit or vegetables. Foods with a low glycemic index are highly recommended. These include green vegetables, grains, and fruits; specifically, you must limit oily fried foods and stimulants.
Sample one-week menu for diabetic patients

mon_an.ten: What is Included in a Meal Plan for High Cholesterol?
mon_an.mo_ta: To prevent high blood lipids (cholesterol) and its complications, a scientific diet and proper abstinence are indispensable. Many foods are harmful and increase blood fat, but many are beneficial for health and help reduce excess fat in the blood, such as apples, salmon, or common carp. People with high blood lipids need to strictly control their diet, eating foods with low cholesterol content such as green vegetables, soy-based foods, or lean pork loin. Pay special attention to green vegetables rich in fiber, as they help reduce cholesterol absorption.
cac_buoc: => To overcome high blood cholesterol, diet is the number one priority.
I. How important is the menu for people with high blood lipids?

High blood lipids is an abnormal lipid condition in the body, including increased levels of low-density lipoprotein (LDL) cholesterol, triglycerides, and total blood cholesterol, along with decreased high-density lipoprotein (HDL) cholesterol.

There are many common causes of high blood lipids, such as obesity, smoking, physical inactivity, excessive alcohol consumption, and an unbalanced diet, especially the overconsumption of foods containing saturated fats.

Research has shown that the type and amount of fat we consume through our diet can affect blood cholesterol levels, leading to increased total and LDL cholesterol, and an increased risk of heart disease.

Oily, fried foods and fatty meats are very high in fat. Conversely, milk, eggs, and some other meats have less fat and cholesterol. Fat can be found in both plant and animal foods, while cholesterol only appears in animal-sourced foods. Some foods are high in both fat and cholesterol (like fried eggs), high in fat but low in cholesterol (like peanut butter and butter), low in fat and high in cholesterol (like shrimp), or low in both (like fruit).
II. People with high blood lipids should avoid eating foods containing fat

To reduce blood cholesterol levels, the diet should limit fat intake to only 30% of calories and avoid animal fats like lard and beef fat. These foods contain saturated fats that clog arteries. Avoid using palm oil and coconut oil; not just the oils themselves, but also their presence in non-dairy creamers, coffee, cakes, and other products.
Limit consumption of foods like animal butter, cakes, pastries, french fries, fast food, and industrially processed foods, as well as foods containing trans fatty acids.
Replace them with vegetable oils such as canola oil, olive oil, corn oil, safflower oil, soybean oil, or sunflower oil, as these oils have cholesterol-lowering effects.
Increase fish consumption to absorb omega-3 fatty acids, which protect the heart, while limiting red meat.

Increase fiber intake in every meal, especially soluble fiber. Foods rich in soluble fiber like legumes, brown rice, barley, and fruits like apples, pears, guavas, plums, oranges, and grapefruit help reduce the amount of fat and cholesterol absorbed into the body.
Ensure adequate folic acid consumption, because if this acid level is too low, homocysteine levels will rise, increasing the risk of heart disease.
III. What does a menu for people with high blood lipids include?
1. Green vegetables and fresh fruit

Green vegetables and fresh fruit are the main sources of fiber, which limits cholesterol absorption. Leafy greens like spinach and kale have been proven by research to lower LDL cholesterol levels and prevent plaque buildup in arteries.

Fruit, especially those rich in fiber, also helps lower bad cholesterol. Fiber supports cholesterol reduction by binding with good cholesterol and removing it from the body through waste. Soluble fiber also helps you feel full longer, supporting weight loss and maintenance.
2. Bean sprouts

Bean sprouts are a healthy source of protein and vitamins that treat many types of diseases. Bean sprouts are low in calories, fat-free, nutrient-dense, and have many health benefits, including improving metabolism and regulating cholesterol levels.
One study showed that consuming bean sprouts can lower bad cholesterol and increase good cholesterol in people with type 2 diabetes.
3. Grains and nutritious nuts
Eating whole grains and nuts (especially oats and barley) helps reduce blood cholesterol and prevents heart disease in adults.

Research shows that eating more whole grains (at least 2.5 servings per day) is associated with a lower risk of cardiovascular disease. Another study with postmenopausal women showed that 6 servings of whole grains per week help protect against cardiovascular disease.

Nuts like almonds, walnuts, macadamias, pecans, and legumes like lentils and peas are good protein sources to replace unhealthy meats. Nuts contain fiber and healthy fats that effectively improve cholesterol.
4. Foods rich in plant sterols and stanols
Vegetable oils like olive oil, peanut oil, canola oil, and soybean oil.
Grains containing plant sterols and stanols like oats, barley, corn, and brown rice.
Seeds and nuts like flaxseeds, chia seeds, sunflower seeds, and walnuts.
Tree nuts like almonds, macadamias, and pecans.
IV. Some notes on nutrition for people with high blood lipids
1. Patients with high blood lipids should:
Eat plenty of vegetables and fresh, low-sugar fruits; eat whole fruits rather than juicing them.
Eat plenty of garlic.
Have at least 3 days a week eating fish or legumes instead of meat.

Avoid foods with high cholesterol content such as: pig brain, fat, chicken skin, duck skin, egg yolks, pork trotters, beef tendons, etc.
Avoid alcohol (one glass of red wine per day can be good for blood vessels).
Avoid smoking.

Bean sprouts – Help eliminate bad cholesterol.
Apples – Absorb excess cholesterol.

V. Ways to prevent and stop high blood lipids:
Eat moderately, eat at the right time, in the right portions, and eat less in the evening.

Limit fried, stir-fried dishes with lots of oil; avoid fast food; limit salt and high-protein foods.

cac_buoc: I. Nutritional Guidelines for Gout Patients
Step 1: Key Considerations for Gout Patients
Drink 2–2.5 liters of water daily; mineral water is best.
Supplement with green vegetables, naturally ripe fruits, and whole grains.
Limit protein intake to a moderate level: Total meat and fish should be under 150g/day. You can use this conversion guide: 100g meat = 180g tofu = 70g peanuts = 100g fish = 100g shrimp.
For Acute Gout Patients:
Protein: 15% of total daily energy; choose sources like eggs, milk, peanuts, and cheese.
Fats – Sugars: 65% of total energy; choose polyunsaturated plant-based fats.
Avoid fast-growing vegetables like bamboo shoots, bean sprouts, and asparagus.
For Chronic Gout Patients:
Chronic gout patients must strictly limit foods high in purines and protein. Animal protein and legumes should not exceed 100g per day. Refer to these three purine groups (per 100g of food):
Group I (0–50mg): Non-fast-growing vegetables, vegetables not in Group II, dairy products, eggs, cooking oil, tea, coffee, etc.
Group II (50–150mg): Poultry, red meat, whole grains, legumes, cauliflower, asparagus, mushrooms, kale, spinach.
Group III (150–1000mg): Organ meats, wild game or free-range animals (e.g., wild boar, rabbit), fermented foods, cod roe, caviar, seafood like scallops, herring, anchovies, lobster, beer, etc.

Additionally, gout patients should eat pumpkin, winter melon, watermelon, adzuki beans, pears, apples, grapes, soybeans, and cow's milk. These are low-purine, diuretic, and heat-clearing foods that support treatment.

mon_an.mo_ta: Saving gas properly with the following tips will help you save a significant amount of fuel. Do you know how to save gas correctly? Proper gas-saving techniques not only reduce fuel costs but also help you prepare fragrant, delicious meals.
cac_buoc: Clean the gas stove regularly

Many families do not clean their gas stoves after cooking, allowing residue to build up and clog the gas ports. Over time, this causes the flame to shrink, requiring more gas to cook. Wiping down the stove at the end of the day keeps it clean and prevents the gas lines from becoming blocked.
Choose the right cookware

Different dishes require different cooking times and heat levels. Therefore, choosing pots and pans that suit each dish will help you save gas properly. For example, use a thin pan for stir-fries; similarly, for stews, choosing a pressure cooker will save a lot of time and gas.
Use moderate heat

Adjust the heat according to the dish you are cooking. However, a general rule is not to let the flame exceed the base of the pot. This wastes gas and disperses the heat, which can even melt the handles of stainless steel pots.
Stay focused while cooking

This tip seems simple but is often the hardest to follow because it is easy to get distracted while boiling water or simmering porridge. Frequent distractions lead to excessive fuel consumption and can sometimes even ruin the dish.

mon_an.ten: Health and Beauty Benefits of Bananas
mon_an.mo_ta: Bananas are a familiar fruit to all of us. We know many of their benefits, such as boosting the immune system and preventing muscle cramps. However, there are many other health and beauty benefits of bananas that you might not know yet. Let's explore these benefits together. Health and beauty benefits of bananas 1
cac_buoc: Characteristics of bananas:
Bananas contain a large amount of protein and carbohydrates; as they ripen, these components convert into sugars, creating the sweetness and aroma of the fruit.
Ripe bananas also contain other components such as glucose, lactose, maltose, galactose, and starch.
Bananas are also rich in essential vitamins such as vitamins A, C, and E, as well as essential amino acids.
Health benefits of bananas:

Boosts memory: Bananas contain potassium, which enhances brain function, helping us work more effectively and stay alert. Additionally, the vitamin B in bananas supports the nervous system after stressful work.
Supports the digestive system: Thanks to the high fiber content in bananas, intestinal activity is enhanced, preventing constipation and other stomach issues.

Provides energy: Due to the high sugar content, you can eat ripe bananas to provide instant energy to the body, which is why bananas are essential in an athlete's diet. A scientific study has shown that just 2 bananas provide enough energy for 90 minutes of strenuous exercise.
Good for anemia: Bananas have a very high iron content, which helps produce more hemoglobin and increases the blood supply to the body.

Stabilizes mood: For those with psychological issues or mood swings, it is recommended to eat 1 banana a day to supplement the amino acid Tryptophan. This is an essential amino acid for producing serotonin, a hormone that helps regulate mood and improve your state of mind.
Beauty benefits of bananas:
Maintains physique: Eating bananas helps balance blood sugar levels, which reduces the risk of obesity and helps maintain a slim figure.
Hair and skin care: Using bananas to create hair and skin masks will give you long, shiny black hair and bright, smooth, firm skin.
Precautions when eating bananas:
You should only eat a maximum of 3 bananas per day to ensure an adequate supply of potassium and reduce the risk of stroke.

Eating too many bananas can lead to headaches because they contain tyramine and phenylethylamine, which dilate blood vessels. Tyramine levels are usually higher in very ripe bananas, so the longer they ripen, the more likely they are to cause headaches.

Additionally, eating too many bananas over a period of time can suppress the nervous system, causing symptoms such as drowsiness, nausea, and dizziness due to the excessive supply of potassium and tryptophan.

mon_an.mo_ta: Solanum procumbens (Cà gai leo) is known by many names such as climbing nightshade, thorny vine, or star-shaped nightshade. Its scientific name is Solanum hainanense – Hance Solanaceae. Here are the physical characteristics of this plant.
cac_buoc: Solanum procumbens is a perennial climbing shrub. It typically clings to other plants or crawls along the ground, and its branches can grow quite long.
The stems are smooth and woody, branching out extensively. The branches are covered in thick, star-shaped downy hairs, and along the length of the stem are closely spaced, pale yellow curved thorns.

The leaves are oval and slightly elongated with irregular lobes. The upper surface has small thorns, while the underside is covered in fine, soft white hairs. The leaves grow alternately along the stem.
Regarding the flowers, they grow in cymes from the leaf axils. Each cluster usually contains 5 to 7 pale purple blossoms.

The ripe berries are spherical and succulent. They are dark green when young and turn a very eye-catching bright red when ripe. The seeds are yellow and flat, similar in shape to chili or tomato seeds.
The growing season is short, from April to May, while the fruiting season lasts a bit longer, from July to September.
Distribution

The plant adapts well to various environments but is commonly found in hilly and mountainous regions with cooler climates, primarily in the Northern mountainous provinces, Central provinces, and some parts of the South.

The roots contain starch and various chemical compounds such as alkaloids and glycoalkaloids, which are excellent for protecting liver cells. They help inhibit and neutralize hepatitis viruses, prevent cirrhosis, and are used to treat liver-related diseases.
Uses of Solanum Procumbens

In folk medicine, this plant is highly effective for patients with liver conditions. In the past, before modern medicine was widely available, people with liver issues like jaundice, yellowing of the eyes, acne, or rashes would brew this plant as a daily tea for treatment. It also has many other therapeutic uses.

mon_an.mo_ta: Garlic is an essential spice in every family meal. Many dishes lose their appeal without it; furthermore, garlic is a medicinal herb that can treat various ailments. Let's explore some useful tips regarding garlic and what you need to know.
cac_buoc: Garlic tips for food preparation
To make a dish more fragrant, you should mince the garlic or use a garlic press instead of slicing it. Slicing is only suitable for finished dishes, briefly stir-fried and placed on top for garnish.
If you are in a hurry and don't have time to peel garlic, simply leave the skin on and crush it; the skin will then come off quickly and cleanly.

When sautéing garlic, avoid adding it to a pan that is too hot. It is best to add garlic when the oil is not yet hot; as the garlic heats up with the pan, it will release more oils and make the dish more fragrant.

Many people dislike garlic because of its pungent smell. You can mellow the flavor by cooking it longer in the dish. For salads or dipping sauces, you can blanch the garlic in boiling water before mincing it. These two methods will significantly soften the garlic's pungency.

If your hands smell like garlic after cooking, wash them with a little lemon juice; or even simpler - rub your hands against the bottom of a stainless steel spoon under running water for a while to completely eliminate the odor.
Tips for selecting and storing garlic
Choose garlic with a tight outer skin that has not yet sprouted.
Store garlic in a cool, dry place. Damp environments can cause garlic to sprout or turn dark and spoil.
If the weather is too humid, you can peel the garlic in advance, put it in an airtight container, and store it in the refrigerator for up to 5 weeks.
If the garlic sprouts, you can still use it, but remember to cut off the sprout as it can be toxic to the body.

mon_an.mo_ta: While bean sprouts are delicious and nutritious, store-bought ones often carry the risk of being treated with toxic chemicals. You can make your own sprouts at home without a machine using these simple materials.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Plump mung beans, no hollow or pest-damaged seeds to ensure germination - 100 g
Plastic basket with a base at least 2 cm high - 1 piece
1 large handkerchief or 2-3 small handkerchiefs - tool
cac_buoc: Wash the mung beans 2-3 times with water to remove dirt and dust. Soak them in warm water (38°C) for 8-12 hours so the seeds can absorb enough moisture. When the seeds have enough water, you will see a tiny sprout peeking out from the tip. At that point, gently drain the water and rinse the beans under a light stream of cold water.
Next, dampen the handkerchiefs with water. Line the bottom of the high-based plastic basket with a handkerchief. Spread the mung beans evenly over the handkerchief.

Soak the large cotton towel in water, fold it into four, and place it over the layer of mung beans in the basket. The cotton towel and handkerchief will maintain moisture from both top and bottom, ensuring the air around the seeds remains humid, creating ideal conditions for germination.

Place the basket in a cool, airy spot away from direct sunlight. Rinse with water about 20 times a day (by pouring water through the towel). Regularly check the growth to prevent the beans from rotting or failing to sprout. Your sprouts should be ready for harvest around the 4th day.
Gently lift the handkerchief, remove the bean sprouts from the surface, and rinse them with water.

mon_an.mo_ta: Dishes with tofu are usually very refreshing and appetizing. Try this variation of stir-fried tofu with bean sprouts for a light and simple meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, soy sauce, vegetarian seasoning powder
cac_buoc: Let's cook this Stir-fried Tofu with Bean Sprouts for a light and easy meal:
Step 1: Wash the tofu and cut into large, long strips. Drain well so it doesn't splatter when frying. After frying, let it cool and then slice into smaller strips to prevent them from breaking.
Step 2: Wash the king oyster mushrooms and slice into bite-sized pieces. Wash the bean sprouts and drain. Peel the carrot, wash, and julienne. Wash the cilantro and drain.
