Prepare the coating: Crack 1 egg and take the white. Mix the egg white with 2 tbsp cornstarch.
Coat the ribs: Add the cornstarch and egg white mixture to the bowl of ribs. Mix well so the coating covers the ribs evenly.
A small tip: Marinating the meat with egg white and cornstarch helps the ribs turn a beautiful golden color and become crispier when fried.

Fry the ribs: Place a pan on the stove and add cooking oil. Wait until the oil is hot, then place the coated ribs into the pan and fry over medium heat. Fry until the ribs are golden brown and the edges are crispy. Then, remove the ribs from the pan and drain the oil.
3. Simmer the ribs
Pour out most of the oil from the pan, leaving a little to sauté the garlic until fragrant.

Add 10g minced horn chili and the entire pre-mixed sauce into the pan. Next, pour 50ml of filtered water into the sauce bowl, swirl to rinse, and pour into the pan. Cook the sauce until the mixture boils and thickens slightly.
Simmer the ribs over low heat for about 5 minutes until the sauce becomes thick and syrupy and the ribs are evenly glazed. Then, turn off the heat.
Arrange the ribs on a plate and garnish to create a beautiful dish.
4. Finished product

The sweet and sour pork ribs are easy to make with simple and easy-to-find ingredients. However, the flavor is incredibly delicious and attractive, making you want to eat more. Each piece of ribs is infused with flavor, combined with the sweet and sour sauce, creating a wonderful taste sensation when eaten with rice.
Notes for making sweet and sour ribs
Choose fresh ribs: Ensure you choose ribs with a bright color, soft meat, and no foul odor. Fresh ribs will make the dish tastier.
Marinate evenly: When marinating, ensure you rub the spices onto every side of the ribs. Marinate for 15-20 minutes for the ribs to absorb the flavor.
Coat the ribs evenly: Before frying, ensure the coating is spread evenly over each piece of ribs. This helps create a crispy crust and attractive color.
Fry correctly: When frying, use medium heat to ensure the ribs are evenly golden and crispy. Check the ribs frequently so they don't overcook and become dry.

Make the sauce to taste: Ensure the ratio of ingredients in the sauce like sugar, fish sauce, vinegar, and water suits your family's palate. You can adjust the sourness and sweetness to your preference.

Simmer to the right consistency: When adding the ribs to the sauce, simmer over low heat for about 5 minutes so the ribs are evenly glazed and the sauce thickens. Ensure not to cook too long to prevent the ribs from becoming too soft and losing their crispiness.
How to choose good pork ribs
1. Choosing good pork ribs
Fresh ribs usually have a light pink color and are elastic when pressed. Choose ribs without any stale odor.
Choose ribs with small, flat bones. This type of ribs has more meat than large, round bones and fewer bones overall.
For soup dishes, choose ribs with both lean meat and fat. This will make the meat soft, fragrant, and richer in flavor.
Avoid choosing ribs with a foul smell, pale green meat, slimy texture, or lack of elasticity when pressed.
2. How to clean pork and remove odors
You can use white wine, ginger, salt, lemon, or vinegar to rub onto the meat. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes and then rinse thoroughly with water.
Additionally, during marination, you can roast a shallot, peel it, crush it, and mix it with the meat. This helps deodorize effectively.
By following these tips for choosing and preparing pork, you will have fresh ingredients without any unpleasant odors for your dishes.

mon_an.mo_ta: Not only providing many beneficial vitamins for health, this pink grapefruit jelly is also a snack that you can "eat forever without getting fat"!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Pink grapefruit - 1 (you can substitute with other types; choose thin-skinned, smooth, large-pored, and heavy fruit)
Sugar - 30g (if you want to lose weight effectively, do not use sugar)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, peel the grapefruit and separate the segments. Note to remove all the pith and white fibers so the final product is not bitter.
Step 2:
Soak the gelatin leaf in cold water for about 10 minutes. In hot weather, you should place this bowl of water in the refrigerator.
Step 3:
While waiting for the gelatin to soften, dissolve the sugar in the water and grapefruit juice.
Step 4:
Carefully arrange the grapefruit segments beautifully in glass cups or molds as desired.
Step 5:
Squeeze the excess water from the gelatin, then melt it in the microwave or over a double boiler.
Step 6:
Next, stir the melted gelatin into the sugar water from step 3, then pour the mixture into the grapefruit jelly molds.
Place the jelly molds in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour until the jelly is completely set. Once set, remove the jelly from the molds and decorate beautifully.
This is a jelly you can eat a lot of without worrying about weight gain, and it provides many vitamins for the body!

mon_an.mo_ta: Potato-wrapped shrimp is a perfect dish in both quality and presentation. It features a harmonious blend of sweet shrimp, savory pork paste, and the nutty aroma of potatoes. The shrimp are encased in golden, crispy potato strands, making the dish incredibly appealing. The method is not too difficult or time-consuming, making it a smart choice for your family's weekend meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, pepper, cooking oil, chili sauce - to taste
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Peel the potatoes and divide them into two parts.
Cut one potato into chunks and boil until tender.

Shred the other potato into thin strands; try to make the strands as long as possible. Blanch the potato strands in boiling water and then quickly submerge them in cold water. This makes the potato soft and easy to wrap without turning brown.
Wash the shrimp, peel off the shells, remove the dark veins from the back, and drain well.
Step 2: Execution
Once the boiled potatoes are cooked, mash them until very smooth.
Next, mix the mashed potatoes with cornstarch, raw pork paste, a bit of salt, and pepper. If the mixture is too thick, add a little water. Stir the mixture until it is smooth and pliable.
Take a shrimp and spread a portion of the potato mixture evenly over its body. Remember to leave the tail exposed.
Finally, take the potato strands and wrap them evenly over the potato mixture on the shrimp's body.
Next, place a pan on the stove and add enough oil to completely submerge the shrimp; this ensures the potatoes are crispy and not overly greasy.
Drop each shrimp into the oil to fry. Remember to flip them frequently so they cook evenly and turn golden on all sides. When the shrimp have a beautiful golden color, remove them and drain the oil.
Place the shrimp on paper towels to absorb any excess oil.
Finally, arrange the shrimp on a plate and decorate as you like.
Dipping sauce: You can use garlic chili fish sauce, chili sauce, or mayonnaise.
Notes

When frying the shrimp, remember to remove them as soon as they turn a bright golden color because the ingredients cook very quickly. If fried for too long, the potatoes will become hard and chewy, affecting the taste.
Buy very fresh shrimp that are still swimming; avoid buying pre-peeled, frozen, or iced shrimp.
Choose fresh, firm potatoes with a nice yellow color, no soft spots, and no green patches.
The raw pork paste is optional, but adding it definitely makes the dish tastier.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Delicious Tomato Scrambled Eggs
mon_an.mo_ta: This dish is simple, easy to make, and quick for when you are busy. Tomato scrambled eggs served with hot rice are wonderful. Please refer to our recipe below!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Cut the tomato into small pieces.
Step 2: Crack the eggs into a bowl, add salt, pepper, sesame oil, and cooking wine.
Step 3: Beat the eggs well. Heat the cooking oil, pour in the eggs, stir briefly, then remove to a bowl.
Step 4: Add more oil to the pan, add the tomatoes and a pinch of sugar. Stir-fry until the tomatoes are soft.
Step 5: Return the eggs to the pan along with the chopped scallions and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Step 6: Season to taste, then serve the tomato scrambled eggs on a plate with hot rice!

mon_an.ten: Delicious Pumpkin Soup with Shrimp and Pork Ribs
mon_an.mo_ta: Pumpkin soup with shrimp and pork ribs is a suitable dish for young children, providing full nutrients and a flavor that kids love. You can make this for your baby and the whole family to enjoy. Check out the recipe below!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the ribs, cut into bite-sized pieces, and blanch in boiling water. Wash the shrimp, peel, remove the heads, and devein.
Step 2:
Peel the pumpkin, remove the seeds, wash, and cut into slices about 1 cm thick. Use flower or star molds to shape the pumpkin pieces.
Clean and finely chop the scallions and culantro.
Step 3:
Place the pork ribs in a pot with 750 ml of broth and cook over medium heat for about 20 minutes until the ribs are tender. Skim off the foam to keep the broth clear.
Add the shrimp and pumpkin to the pot and cook for 3-5 minutes until done. Season with seasoning powder, salt, and pepper to taste.
Turn off the heat, add the scallions and culantro, and stir well.
Step 4:
Ladle the pumpkin, shrimp, and meat soup into a bowl and serve warm for the baby.

mon_an.ten: Pigeon Porridge with Lotus Seeds and Mung Beans
mon_an.mo_ta: Discover how to cook delicious pigeon porridge with lotus seeds and mung beans for babies and pregnant women. A nutritious dish, rich in nutrients and perfect for this stage.
thoi_gian: Cooking tips for moms on how to cook nutritious pigeon porridge for babies. Pigeon meat has the effect of tonifying the liver and kidneys, strengthening the spleen and stomach, benefiting qi and blood, and detoxifying. The meat is used as a remedy for cases of emaciation, weakness, malnutrition, and poor health. Pigeon meat is neutral in nature, contains a lot of protein, lipids, calcium, phosphorus, iron, mineral salts, and vitamins; therefore, it is a good food for the elderly, children, the sick, and especially for postpartum women. The recipe for pigeon porridge with lotus seeds and mung beans is as follows:
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Black pepper - 1 small tsp of ground pepper
cac_buoc: Step 1: Process the pigeon
Dispatch the pigeon; if you are afraid, you can cover its nose or submerge its head in water, or tape the nose shut, etc.
Pluck the feathers clean; pigeon feathers are very easy to pluck dry, so do not dip in boiling water like chicken.
Skewer the pigeon and singe it over a flame to burn off fine down feathers and create an aroma.

Wash off dirt and burnt feathers, then eviscerate; you can use scissors. Be careful not to break the intestines, which would soil the cavity. Cut around the vent and open it up, then use the tip of the scissors to cut the throat and pull out the crop.

Discard the intestines, crop, lungs, etc. Only keep the gizzard, heart, liver, and eggs. When eviscerating, do not soil the meat so the body does not need to be washed again, preserving nutrients. Clean the giblets like you would for a chicken. Scrub the gizzard and heart with salt and wash multiple times.

Filter the meat from the thighs and breast and set aside; mince it and discard the feet (as they can make the porridge smell gamey). Marinate with pepper, seasoning salt, and a little fish sauce for aroma.
Step 2: Simmer the porridge
Wash the rice, lotus seeds, and mung beans to remove dust and grit.

Put the glutinous rice, plain rice, mung beans, lotus seeds, and pigeon bones into a pot with about 1 liter of water. Cover tightly and simmer over low heat for about 15 minutes until the porridge is soft.
Step 3: Sauté the pigeon meat
While waiting for the porridge to soften, sauté the marinated pigeon meat from Step 1.
Place a pan on the stove, add olive oil, sauté the minced shallots until fragrant, then add the pigeon meat and stir-fry until just cooked.
Step 4: Cook the porridge

When the porridge is soft, add 1/2 of the pigeon meat to the pot and boil for another 5-7 minutes so the porridge absorbs the meat flavor. You can also keep the other 1/2 of the meat to add to the bowl when eating.
Once the porridge is done, remove the bones. Take out the cooked lotus seeds, mash or crush them, then stir them back into the porridge.
Finally, season with fish sauce, ladle the porridge into a bowl, and top with the remaining pigeon meat for presentation.
Secrets for a delicious pigeon porridge:
Choose a squab (ra ràng) because as the elders say, "Squab is at its fattest and sweetest." A squab (just starting to grow feathers) is the most tender and ideal for a baby's porridge.
Do not bleed the pigeon like a chicken or duck because pigeon blood is very nutritious.
Do not process the pigeon with boiling water; pluck the feathers while dry as they come off easily.

After plucking, you must singe it to clean the down and create a characteristic aroma. In the past, people used dry straw. This gives the skin an attractive amber color and makes the meat very fragrant. In the city, you can use a skewer and grill it over the stove or charcoal.
If you have bone broth, you can use it to simmer the porridge for extra richness. However, if not, plain water is fine as the pigeon bones will release sweetness and nutrients.

Depending on the texture your baby can eat, prepare the ingredients accordingly. For weaning babies, you can blend the finished porridge. For older kids, you can crack the rice and mung beans to the desired size before simmering.
Similarly, you can replace pigeon with spotted dove or quail to change the menu.
If cooking for adults, instead of mincing the meat, you can leave the pigeon whole to simmer with the porridge, then serve in a bowl topped with scallions and Vietnamese coriander.
How to choose fresh ingredients
Buying fresh pigeon
To ensure you get the best squab, choose birds about 15 days old. These have soft, thick, fatty meat and are highly nutritious.
To identify a squab, look for birds about the size of a fist with sparse down feathers, with thicker feathers only on the wings and back.
When buying, press under the wing. If the meat is thick, it is fresh. Also, the breast meat should feel soft when pressed.
If buying pre-processed pigeon, avoid those with pale blue skin and choose those with rosy skin to ensure quality.
Buying mung beans
Choose mung beans with a bright green color, firm seeds, no signs of pests, and a characteristic aroma. Good mung beans have a white dot on the belly, are plump, and have no unusual black spots.
Buying creamy lotus seeds

For quality, choose freshly picked lotus seeds still attached to the pod. Good seeds are usually mature, fragrant, and creamy, not hard. They should be ivory white or deep yellow, plump, and uniform in color.

When buying dried lotus seeds, ensure the packaging is intact with no discoloration. Prioritize hand-processed seeds that are easy to peel. These contain no harmful preservatives and do not affect the flavor of the dish.

mon_an.ten: Nutritious Chicken and Mung Bean Porridge
cac_buoc: Delicious and nutritious chicken and mung bean porridge is a familiar Vietnamese recipe. Want to discover how to cook it perfectly? Gather your ingredients and start showing off your skills with this wonderful dish. We will explore the details and steps in the article below!
I. Traditional Chicken and Mung Bean Porridge Recipe
1. Ingredients
500 g chicken meat
50 g plain rice
50 g glutinous rice
50 g mung beans
5 purple shallots
1 stalk scallion/cilantro
1/2 tbsp turmeric powder
1/2 tbsp seasoning salt
A little seasoning: Salt, pepper, and seasoning powder
2. Preparation
2.1. Prepare the ingredients
Clean the chicken: Remove any remaining feathers and wash the chicken with diluted salt water to make it clean and odorless. Rinse several times, drain, and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Prepare aromatics: Peel and wash the shallots. Clean and finely chop the scallions and cilantro.
Marinate the chicken: Place the chicken in a bowl. Add 1 tbsp seasoning powder, 1/2 tbsp seasoning salt, 1/3 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tbsp turmeric powder. Mix well and marinate for 10 minutes.
2.2. Boil the chicken
Bring 1 liter of water to a boil. Add the shallots.
Place the marinated chicken in the pot, cover, and cook over medium heat for about 20 minutes.
Remove the chicken once it is cooked.
Tip: To keep the chicken firm and tasty, do not simmer it with the porridge to avoid making the meat mushy. Remove it once cooked.
2.3. Cook the porridge
Before cooking, soak the mung beans in water for about 2 hours, then wash clean.

After removing the chicken, add 50 g plain rice, 50 g glutinous rice, and 50 g washed mung beans to the pot. Cover tightly and simmer over medium heat for about 30 minutes until the ingredients are soft.
Next, return the chicken to the pot and cook for another 15 minutes over medium heat until both the chicken and porridge are completely soft.
Before turning off the heat, season to taste.
When serving, ladle the porridge into a bowl and add chopped scallions, cilantro, and pepper. The chicken mung bean porridge is ready to enjoy.
2.4. Finished product
The porridge is hot, fragrant, with tender sweet chicken and a delicate shallot flavor. A bowl of this porridge on a windy day feels wonderful.
Show your cooking talent by making this pot of porridge for the whole family. Good luck and enjoy!
II. Chicken and Mung Bean Porridge with Minced Pork
Glutinous rice: 100 g
Plain rice: 30 g
Mung beans: 50 g
Pork bones: 200 g
Ground pork: 100 g
Shallot: 1 bulb
2. Preparation for Minced Pork version
2.1. Prepare the ingredients
Glutinous and plain rice: Wash and soak in water for 30 minutes to soften before cooking.
Mung beans: Soak in water for 45-60 minutes to soften. Rinse and drain.

Pork bones: Wash and blanch in boiling water to remove odors and impurities. Then, add 1-1.5 liters of water to a pot to simmer the bones. Do not cover the pot during simmering to prevent the broth from becoming cloudy.
Ground pork: Put 100 g ground pork in a small bowl, add 1/3 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp seasoning powder, 1/3 tsp pepper, and 1/2 tsp fish sauce. Mix well to marinate.
Shallot: Peel and mince 1 shallot. Place a pan on the stove, add 1 tbsp oil, then add the shallot and sauté until fragrant. Add the marinated pork and stir-fry until firm. Turn off the heat.
Scallions and perilla leaves: Clean and chop finely. Wash the bean sprouts and drain.
2.2. Cook the porridge
When the bone broth boils, add the prepared rice and mung beans to the pot. Simmer over low heat so the bones release their sweetness.
During cooking, skim off any foam. Continue simmering until the porridge is soft and thick, then turn off the heat.
2.3 Finished product:
Ladle the porridge into a bowl, then top with scallions, perilla leaves, and minced pork. Now you can enjoy the delicious porridge.
III. Restaurant-Style Chicken and Mung Bean Porridge
Chicken thighs: 2 pieces (or other parts)
Rice: 1 bowl (rice bowl)
Peeled mung beans: 50 g
A little Vietnamese coriander (rau răm)
Bean sprouts: A little
Cooking oil: 1 tbsp
Seasonings
2.1. Prepare the chicken
You can buy pre-processed chicken to save time, but if you want to do it yourself, buy fresh chicken.
To remove the odor from the thighs, rub salt directly onto the skin. Remove any remaining feathers and wash with water several times. Drain in a basket.
Prepare other ingredients:
Vietnamese coriander: Pick off wilted leaves, wash, and drain.
Bean sprouts: Soak in diluted salt water for 10 minutes, rinse, and drain.
Shallots: Peel, wash, and slice thinly.
Rice: Wash 1 bowl of rice twice to remove dust. Soak in water for 15 minutes before use.
Mung beans: Wash the mung beans and soak in water for 15 minutes before cooking.
You have finished preparing the ingredients for the porridge.
2.2. Boil the chicken
Place a pot on the stove, add 1 tbsp oil and sliced shallots to sauté until fragrant.
Pour 1 liter of water into the pot and bring to a boil.
Once the water boils, add the 2 chicken leg quarters and boil for 20-30 minutes.
Use medium heat and skim off the foam. Flip the chicken every 10 minutes to ensure even cooking.
To check if the chicken is done, pierce the thigh with a chopstick. If no red juice runs out, it is cooked. Remove to a plate and let cool.
2.3. Cook the porridge with mung beans
After removing the chicken, add the soaked rice and mung beans to the pot.
Add 1 tsp seasoning powder and 1 tbsp salt to taste.
Cook the porridge over medium heat for about 30 minutes. Stir every 5-10 minutes to ensure even cooking and prevent burning at the bottom.
Adjust the consistency by adding water and re-seasoning to your preference.
Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces once cooled. Place some bean sprouts at the bottom of a bowl, ladle in the porridge, and top with Vietnamese coriander and ground pepper.
2.4. Completion

After completing these steps, you have a delicious and attractive portion of chicken mung bean porridge. The rice grains are perfectly bloomed and fragrant. The sweetness of the broth, the creaminess of the mung beans, and the slight heat from the pepper create a wonderful dish.
The harmonious combination of porridge with firm, chewy chicken creates a special flavor profile. No one can resist this wonderful taste!
Read more: How to cook delicious chicken and shiitake mushroom porridge

mon_an.ten: Chicken and Lotus Seed Congee Recipe
cac_buoc: Chicken and lotus seed congee is a familiar dish, but cooking it quickly and making it delicious is not always easy. From selecting the chicken and lotus seeds to the scallions and herbs, every ingredient in this dish is meticulously chosen to create a perfect bowl of congee. Let's explore how to make delicious chicken and lotus seed congee in the article below!
I. Instructions for making delicious chicken and lotus seed congee
1. Ingredients
1 chicken drumstick (about 150 – 200g)
100g white rice
100g lotus seeds (type of your choice)
50g mung beans
1/4 carrot
4 shallots
1 sprig of cilantro
2 scallions
2 tbsp cooking oil
Common seasonings: salt, seasoning powder, sugar (to taste)
2. Cooking steps
2.1. Prepare and boil the chicken
Rub the chicken with salt (or lemon juice) to clean and remove odors, then rinse thoroughly several times.
Next, remove the skin and boil the chicken in boiling water over high heat for about 15 minutes until fully cooked. Then, shred the meat and discard the bones.
2.2. How to clean chicken and remove odors
Use salt, lemon, or ginger to clean and deodorize the chicken, then rinse with water several times.
Blanching the chicken in a mixture of rice wine and ginger is also very effective for deodorizing.
2.3. Prepare other ingredients
Wash the lotus seeds, remove any damaged ones, and soak in water for about 30 minutes until softened.
Wash the rice and mung beans, then soak in water for about 30 minutes until they expand.
Wash and grate the carrot. Peel and thinly slice the shallots, then fry until fragrant.
Wash and thinly slice the scallions and cilantro.
2.4. Cook the congee
Place a pot of water on the stove over high heat. Add the rice and mung beans, then simmer for about 15 minutes until the rice grains bloom. Done.

Next, add the lotus seeds and carrots to the pot and simmer for another 15 minutes. Season with 1 tsp sugar and 1 tsp seasoning powder, then add the fried shallots. Stir well and boil for another 5 minutes.
Finally, adjust the seasoning to taste. Ladle the congee into small bowls and top with the shredded chicken and scallions.
II. How to cook black chicken and lotus seed congee like a pro
1. Ingredients
3 tbsp rice
1 tbsp brown rice
300g black chicken (1 small bird)
50g lotus seeds (fresh or dried)
1 tbsp skin-on mung beans
1 sprig of scallion
1 sprig of cilantro
Seasonings
2.1. Prepare the black chicken
To save time, you can ask the seller to clean the black chicken for you. Once home, simply rub the surface with salt and rinse with water.
Prepare other ingredients:
For fresh lotus seeds: peel, remove the lotus embryo, and wash thoroughly to avoid bitterness.
For dried lotus seeds: soak in water for about 2 hours so they expand evenly and don't stay hard.
Wash the brown rice, mung beans, and white rice 2-3 times, then drain.
Trim the roots of the scallions and cilantro, wash, and finely chop.
2.2. Cook the congee
Place the brown rice, mung beans, white rice, black chicken, and 800ml water into a pressure cooker. Cook on high heat for 8–10 minutes until the congee and chicken are tender, then remove from heat.
Seasoning:
Add 1 tsp seasoning powder, 1/2 tsp MSG, and 1/2 tsp salt to the pot. Stir well to dissolve, then adjust the seasoning to taste.
2.3. Garnish and finish
Ladle the congee into a bowl, garnish with chopped scallions, cilantro, and a bit of ground pepper. That's the final step.

The finished black chicken and lotus seed congee will have an enticing aroma from the chicken broth. When eating, you will taste the sweet, tender chicken meat perfectly blended with sweet lotus seeds and nutty mung beans.
The congee is soft and sweet, seasoned just right. Topped with some fragrant fried shallots, it's simply unbeatable, isn't it?
Read more: How to cook delicious chicken and straw mushroom congee
III. How to buy fresh ingredients
1. For live black chicken
When buying black chicken, choose healthy, active birds. The feathers should be smooth and shiny. There should be no discharge from the eyes or nose.
Avoid buying birds that look lethargic, with drooping tails or slow movement. Ruffled feathers or signs of dampness on the head are indicators of illness.
2. For pre-processed black chicken
When buying pre-processed black chicken, choose birds that are compact and firm. The breast should be small, and the skin should be a glossy black.
Good black chicken will have fresh meat without any unpleasant odor. When pressed, the meat should be firm and elastic.
Avoid buying black chicken meat that is mushy, slimy, deformed, or sunken.
For peace of mind, buy black chicken from reputable poultry vendors at the market or in supermarkets.
3. For fresh lotus seeds
When buying fresh lotus seeds, choose those still in the pod. Select large, vibrant green pods. Freshly harvested pods will taste better and sweeter.
Avoid buying pods that are too old, dark in color, or nearly withered, as the seeds inside will be difficult to peel.
4. For dried lotus seeds

When buying dried lotus seeds, choose those with an off-white color and a small, uniform size. If possible, buy hand-processed dried lotus seeds that you can select by hand at the market. These contain no preservatives, preserving their full flavor and aroma when cooked.
If buying pre-packaged dried lotus seeds, choose bags originating from Northern provinces like Hung Yen, Ha Tay, Ha Nam; Western provinces like Dong Thap; or Central provinces like Hue.
To ensure safety, buy dried lotus seeds from large grocery stores and reputable supermarkets.
Avoid buying dried lotus seeds that show signs of mold, feel soft to the touch, or have an unpleasant odor.

mon_an.ten: The Best Baby Clam Porridge for Babies - A Northern Vietnamese Specialty
mon_an.mo_ta: Baby clams are a nutrient-rich food, high in calcium to help babies grow strong. Join us in learning how to cook this unique baby clam porridge to diversify your child's menu. Discover the best traditional Northern-style baby clam porridge recipe. This detailed guide on ingredients and the cooking process will help your baby enjoy a nutritious and flavorful meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cooking oil or olive oil - as needed
cac_buoc: 1. The Best Baby Clam Porridge Recipe for Babies
Step 1: Clean and boil the clams
Soak the clams in water with a bit of salt and chili to release all the grit. Boil the clams until cooked, adding a few grains of salt to the water. Step 2:

Shuck the meat from each clam or swirl them in water to separate the meat quickly. Clean the clam meat and rinse it with the clam broth to remove any fishiness. Mince the clam meat so it is easy for the baby to eat without any gritty texture.
Step 3: Sauté the clam meat
Sauté the shallots until fragrant, then add the clam meat and sauté with a bit of high-quality fish sauce. Remove to a bowl.
Step 4: Prepare the rice for the porridge
Mix the glutinous rice and jasmine rice, soak for about 10 minutes to soften, then crush them in a mortar until small.
Wash the dill and mince or blend it finely so the baby can eat it without choking. Use only the leaves, as the tough stems are difficult for babies to consume.
Step 5: Cook the porridge

Pour the clam broth into a pot, add the crushed rice, and simmer for about 15 minutes on low heat until the rice is soft. While cooking, let the porridge boil and do not stir with chopsticks or a spoon. Stirring can cause the porridge to burn at the bottom and prevent the rice from softening properly.

Once the porridge is cooked, use chopsticks to whisk it until smooth. Add the sautéed clam meat, bring to a boil again, then add the dill and remove from the heat. Serve the porridge in a bowl and feed it to the baby while warm.
2. How to make Baby Clam Porridge with Mung Beans
Ingredients Preparation
100g shucked baby clam meat
1 cup rice (rice bowl)
100g whole mung beans (with skin)
1/2 cup glutinous rice (rice bowl)
A little Vietnamese coriander
A little cilantro
2 shallots
4 stalks green onion
5 cloves garlic
1/2 onion
1 ginger root
2 tbsp sugar
1 tsp salt
3 tbsp fish sauce
3 tbsp cooking oil
1 tsp seasoning powder
Ingredient Pre-processing

Wash the mung beans and soak them in water for 2 hours until soft. Wash and finely chop the Vietnamese coriander, green onions, and cilantro. Mince the garlic and shallots. Slice 1/2 of the ginger root and mince the other 1/2.
Sauté the clams

Place a pan on the stove and add 2 tbsp of cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add the shallots and garlic and sauté until fragrant. Next, add the clams and minced ginger to the pan, then season with 1/2 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp seasoning powder. Stir gently so the clams absorb the spices, then turn off the heat.
Cook the porridge
Mix 1 cup of jasmine rice and 1/2 cup of glutinous rice together. Wash the rice and toast it in a pot with a little oil until the grains become glossy.

After toasting, once the rice turns golden, add 700ml of warm water and the prepared mung beans to the pot. Season the porridge with 2 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp seasoning powder, 3 tbsp fish sauce, and 1/2 onion.

Add 1/2 of the sautéed clams into the porridge and mix well. Set the remaining clams aside in a bowl to serve as a topping. Ladle the porridge into a bowl, add some green onions, Vietnamese coriander, and julienned ginger. Now, you can enjoy the delicious clam porridge.
This fragrant and delicious mung bean clam porridge will surely satisfy your family. The soft, nutty mung beans combined with the savory clam meat create a wonderful flavor.
Notes when cooking clam porridge for babies

Ensure the use of fresh and safe ingredients: Choose fresh, high-quality clams and ensure that the mung beans and vegetables used are fresh. Limit the use of ingredients containing preservatives and artificial coloring.
Follow correct ratios and preparation methods: Adhere to the exact ratios and preparation steps as instructed to ensure food quality and safety.
Control the temperature: Ensure the clam porridge is cooked at a sufficiently high temperature to kill bacteria and ensure food safety.
Pay attention to the size and softness of the food: Mung beans and clam meat should be cooked until soft but not too mushy. Ensure the porridge consistency is suitable for the baby to digest easily.

Check the temperature and food condition: Before feeding the baby, check the temperature of the porridge to ensure it is at a safe level. Carefully check the clam meat to ensure there are no shell fragments or other hard substances that could be dangerous for the baby.

mon_an.ten: Pork and Tofu Porridge for Baby Weaning
mon_an.mo_ta: When starting the weaning stage, pork and tofu porridge is a perfect dish for babies to explore new foods. This is a nutritious porridge providing protein from pork and calcium from tofu. Let's learn how to cook pork and tofu porridge for your baby! Detailed instructions on how to cook pork and tofu porridge for weaning. A nutritious and easy-to-make dish that provides protein and calcium for babies.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients

Start by peeling the pumpkin, washing it, and dicing it before steaming until tender. Once the pumpkin is cooked, mash it with 1/3 bowl of water. Wash the silken tofu, boil it, and mash until smooth. For the glutinous rice, ensure it is washed thoroughly before use.

Wash the pork after purchasing, then mince it. Next, marinate the pork with ½ tbsp of minced shallots and ½ tbsp of seasoning powder; let the meat absorb the flavors for about 15 minutes. For the tomato, wash and remove the seeds, then dice into small cubes.
Step 2: Processing
In a pot, add the rice and 250ml of water with a rice-to-water ratio of 1:8. Simmer over low heat and stir well so the porridge becomes soft and smooth, avoiding any clumping.

On the stove, heat a pan and add 1 tbsp of cooking oil. Sauté ½ tbsp of minced shallots until fragrant, then add the tomatoes and marinated meat to stir-fry. When the meat is cooked and fragrant and the tomatoes are soft, turn off the heat.

Then, add the sautéed tomato and meat mixture into the white porridge pot and stir well. Season according to the baby's taste and simmer until the porridge comes back to a boil. Sprinkle a little chopped cilantro to enhance the aroma. Turn off the heat, add 1 tbsp of cooking oil to the porridge, then remove the porridge from the pot and let it cool before feeding the baby.
Notes when cooking pork and tofu porridge
Choose fresh ingredients: Ensure the pork, tofu, and other components are fresh with no signs of spoilage.
Wash ingredients thoroughly: Before use, wash the pork, tofu, and other ingredients to remove dirt and bacteria.
Mince and cook thoroughly: Mince the pork and tofu into small pieces for easy eating. Ensure everything is cooked thoroughly to make the dish easy to digest and avoid the risk of infection.
Use clean filtered water: When cooking porridge, use clean filtered water to ensure quality and safety for the baby.
Check the temperature before feeding: Before giving the porridge to the baby, check its temperature to ensure it is not too hot and is safe for the baby.
Do not use spicy seasonings: Avoid using spicy seasonings, pepper, or other strong spices in the baby's porridge to avoid irritating the baby's digestive tract.
Store properly: If there is leftover porridge, store it in a food-safe container in the refrigerator and use it within 24 hours.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Delicious Pork and Katuk Porridge for Babies
mon_an.mo_ta: Pork and katuk porridge is a simple yet highly nutritious dish for babies, featuring fresh, tender pork and fiber-rich green katuk leaves. The ingredients blend together in a delicious, fragrant, and nutritious bowl of porridge. Mothers, please add this simple and tasty porridge recipe to your collection!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - Soup powder, fish sauce, MSG, seasoning powder
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the lean pork and mince it together with the scallion whites, then marinate the meat with a little fish sauce and seasoning powder.
Step 2: Pick the katuk leaves, discarding any damaged or old leaves, then wash them and rub them thoroughly so they are not scratchy when eaten. After draining the katuk, mince it finely.
Step 3: Place the pot of white porridge on the stove and add the marinated meat to stir in.
Step 4: Next, add the minced katuk and season to taste.
Step 5: Finally, add baby cooking oil to the porridge pot and remove from the heat!
Scoop the porridge into a bowl, let it cool slightly, and then feed the baby.

mon_an.ten: Pork Heart Porridge for Baby Weaning
mon_an.mo_ta: Pork heart is known as a food that provides many nutrients for the human body, especially for babies. We would like to introduce the recipe for pork heart porridge for baby weaning. Let's check out the recipe!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - fish sauce, salt/soup powder, seasoning powder/MSG, pepper, chili sauce or fresh chili, fried shallots
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients
First, mix the non-glutinous and glutinous rice together, and rinse briefly to remove dust. Place the rice in a bowl and soak in warm water for about 30 minutes.
Peel the onions; halve 2 onions and dice 1 onion.
Peel and wash the carrots, then dice them.
Wash the fresh mushrooms and slice into bite-sized pieces (do not slice too small as they will shrink when cooked); I like keeping them in pieces for a crunchy texture.
Peel the ginger; slice one part thinly to add to the porridge pot, and crush and mince the other part to marinate the pork heart.
Trim the roots of the green onions and cilantro, wash, and chop finely.
Wash the pork heart and slice thinly. Marinate with ½ tsp salt + ½ tsp seasoning powder + ¼ tsp pepper + ½ tsp minced ginger + 1–2 tsp minced shallots for about 30 minutes to absorb the flavors.

Wash the pork tail bones and chop into small pieces. Place in a pot, cover with water, add 1 tsp salt, and blanch to remove impurities. Boil for about 1 minute, then drain the bones and rinse off any foam; discard this first boiling water.
Step 2: Cooking
I use a rice cooker, which is very convenient and saves a lot of time!

Place the blanched and cleaned bones into the pot, add 2 liters of water + 2 tsp salt/soup powder + 2 halved onions + sliced ginger. Bring to a boil and skim off any foam again. Add the soaked rice and stir gently. Close the lid and bring to a boil.
Note: While simmering the porridge, prepare the vegetables as mentioned in the preparation step. Multitasking will save time.

When it boils, remember to use a wooden spoon to stir the rice and bones well; otherwise, the rice at the bottom will stick and burn. After boiling, switch the rice cooker to "Warm" mode for about 30 minutes, then stir again with the wooden spoon and switch back to "Cook" to bring it to a boil again. Then switch back to "Warm" for another 30 minutes, and the porridge will be ready.

Occasionally use a wooden spoon to stir until the porridge becomes thick and smooth. Add more boiling water if needed to reach your desired consistency. Remove and discard the onion pieces and ginger slices. Add all the diced onions and carrots, bring to a boil, and keep on "Warm" for about 5 minutes until soft. At this point, add all the fresh mushrooms, close the lid, and switch back to "Cook" to boil. When the mushrooms are just cooked and release their sweetness, add all the marinated pork heart to the pot, stir well, and close the lid. Once it boils, open the lid, add the green onions and cilantro, and stir one last time. Add 1 tsp seasoning powder or ½ tsp MSG and stir. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Avoid boiling for too long or the pork heart (or kidney) will become tough and lose its tender sweetness.

When eating, grind a little pepper and chili powder (if desired) for aroma. Sprinkle some fried shallots on top for a wonderful fragrance. If you like it spicy, add a bit of chili sauce or fresh chili. Serve hot for the best taste.

The porridge is thick due to the glutinous rice and has the fragrance of rice, onions, ginger, and cilantro, with a hint of heat from the pepper. Especially, the pork heart is just cooked, tender, and sweet, not chewy. A bowl of this porridge warms the stomach on a cold day. The diced onions simmered until soft add sweetness, as do the carrots, which also provide an eye-catching color.
Notes:
If anyone in the family has an open wound, do not add glutinous rice to the porridge.

If there are children, you should stew the bones with onions and vegetables first to get a sweet broth for cooking the porridge. Avoid cooking the tail bones directly in the porridge as I did, to prevent bone fragments.

mon_an.mo_ta: In this article, we will explore a traditional and flavorful dish – delicious and nutritious duck and mung bean congee. This congee not only offers a wonderful taste but also brings sweetness and nutrition to the body. With the perfect combination of savory duck meat and creamy mung beans, this dish is sure to captivate anyone who tries it. Let's continue to discover how to cook this delicious and nutritious duck and mung bean congee in the guide below! Cook this flavorful congee with simple instructions. Enjoy the natural sweetness from the duck broth, the aroma of scallions, cilantro, and pepper. The tender duck meat blends perfectly with the mung beans to create a wonderful flavor. This congee is a perfect choice for a family meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, MSG, pepper, sugar, fish sauce - seasonings
Bean sprouts, basil, rice paddy herb - fresh herbs for serving
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare and boil the duck
To save time, choose pre-cleaned duck. To remove any odor, wash the duck with diluted salt water and rinse several times with clean water.

Next, pour 3 liters of water into a pot and add the duck, cover, and bring to a boil over high heat. Boil over medium heat until the water boils, then simmer for another 15-20 minutes until the duck meat is tender.
After that, remove the meat and let it cool completely, then chop the duck into bite-sized pieces. Soak the mung beans in water for about 1 hour, then drain.
For the rice, soak in water for about 2 hours, then rinse 2-3 times and drain.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the scallions. For the bean sprouts, pick out any bean skins, wash with water, and drain. Finally, finely chop the scallions for use.
2. Prepare the seasoning sauce
Start by peeling the ginger, washing it, and slicing it thinly. Next, place the ginger and 2 sliced chilies into a mortar and grind into a paste, then transfer this mixture to a bowl.

Then, add 1/2 tsp MSG, 1/2 tsp seasoning powder, 2 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp fish sauce to the bowl. Stir well to dissolve the mixture and ensure all ingredients are combined. Taste and adjust the seasoning to suit your preference.
3. Cook the congee

Bring the duck boiling water back to a boil. Once the water is boiling, add the soaked mung beans and rice to the pot. Next, add the seasoning mixture of 1/2 tbsp salt and 1/2 tsp MSG. Cover the pot and simmer for about 10-15 minutes, then open the lid and stir gently.
Continue cooking the congee over medium heat for another 20-25 minutes until the rice is soft and broken down. Adjust the seasoning to taste, then turn off the heat.

Before serving, place some bean sprouts in a bowl, then ladle the congee on top. Sprinkle with some chopped scallions and add the duck meat. Finally, sprinkle with a bit of ground pepper and you have completed the delicious duck and mung bean congee.
4. Finished product
With just 2 simple steps, you will have a delicious, authentic, and nutritious bowl of duck congee to treat your family.

The duck congee features natural sweetness from the duck broth, along with the light aroma of scallions, cilantro, and pepper. The duck meat is tender with a natural chewiness, blending with the rich flavor of the fish sauce, adding to the dish's appeal.
How to choose fresh duck for mung bean congee
1. For live ducks
When choosing, select ducks with smooth, shiny feathers, no pinfeathers on the inner skin, and even, long outer feathers.

To ensure the duck is delicious, meaty, and easy to pluck, feel the duck's breast. If the breast feels full, the skin on the neck and belly is thick, and the wings cross over each other, those are good signs.
Avoid choosing ducks with ruffled feathers, a foul odor, or a lethargic appearance. This may indicate the duck is sick and not suitable for consumption.
2. For pre-cleaned ducks
When buying pre-cleaned duck, choose those with pale yellow skin and even color. When pressing the meat, it should be firm and have good elasticity.

Avoid choosing ducks that have been sitting for a long time, as they often have a very dark color or bruises. If the meat feels soft, has a foul smell, or has liquid leaking out, you should avoid buying it as these are bad signs.

mon_an.ten: Northern Braised Frog with Green Bananas and Tofu
cac_buoc: Braised frog with green bananas and tofu – a natural specialty of the Northern Delta region, with a rustic, familiar yet incredibly attractive flavor. The harmony between the sweetness and chewiness of wild frog meat, the starchiness of green bananas, and the softness of tofu, combined with the characteristic aroma of various spices, is truly rich and unforgettable. This is truly an unforgettable culinary experience! Let's explore how to make braised frog with bananas and tofu!
I. Traditional braised frog with bananas
1. Prepare ingredients
600g cleaned frog meat
2 green bananas
200g pork belly
2 blocks fried tofu
Perilla leaves
1 turmeric root
2 shallots
2. Prepare ingredients
2.1. Ingredient Preparation

Start by rubbing the frog with salt after buying, then rinse 2-3 times with water to remove impurities. Cut the frog into bite-sized pieces, then marinate with minced turmeric, 1 tsp seasoning powder, and ½ tsp MSG.
Wash the pork and slice thinly.
Fry the tofu and cut into small pieces.
Peel the green bananas, slice thinly, and soak in a bowl of diluted salt water for about 20 minutes. After soaking, rinse the bananas and drain.
Soaking bananas in salt water prevents them from browning and helps clean the sap.
Additional Preparation:
Wash the perilla leaves and chop finely.
Peel the shallots and slice thinly.
2.2. Fry the tofu
If using white tofu, fry until golden. If buying pre-fried tofu, fry it again to make it crispier and more fragrant.
Place a pan on the stove, add cooking oil and wait until hot, then drop the cut tofu in and fry until golden brown and crispy, then remove to a plate.
2.3. Sear the meat
Using the same pan, add the pork belly and sear until the edges are browned and crispy, then remove to a plate.
2.4. Cook the braised frog with bananas and tofu

Place a pot on the stove, add oil and shallots and sauté until fragrant, then add the marinated frog and stir-fry until the meat firms up. Next, add the green bananas and stir-fry together. You can add a bit of fish sauce to enhance the flavor. After stir-frying for about 5 minutes, add about 300ml of water to the pot and bring to a boil over high heat.

Once boiling, reduce to low heat and simmer until the bananas are soft. Check by poking a banana; if soft, add the tofu and meat, stir well, and simmer for another 5 minutes. Finally, turn off the heat and add perilla leaves before serving. The Northern braised frog with bananas and tofu is now complete.
II. Braised frog with bananas and tofu (Alternative method)
1. Prepare ingredients
Frogs: 4 whole
Tofu: 3 blocks
Green bananas: 2 fruits
Small fresh turmeric: 1 root
Shallot: 1 bulb
Dry garlic: 1 bulb
Fresh chili: 1 fruit
Piper lolot leaf: 1 leaf
Small perilla: 1 bunch
Fermented rice (mẻ): 2 tbsp
Common seasonings (oil, seasoning powder, fish sauce, salt, MSG): a little
Cooking oil: 1 tbsp
Fish sauce: 1/2 tbsp
Common seasonings (salt, seasoning powder, MSG): a little
Prepare ingredients for braised frog with bananas and tofu
Frog meat:
Wash and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Marinate with minced chili, minced fresh turmeric, seasoning powder, pepper, and fish sauce; mix well.
Green bananas:
Peel and cut into small pieces.
Soak in salt water for about 15 minutes to prevent browning.
Tofu:
Fry until golden brown.
3. Stir-fry the frog meat
Heat oil in a pan, sauté minced shallot and garlic.
Stir-fry the frog meat until golden and fragrant, then add the green bananas.
4. Braise the frog meat
Pour the fermented rice liquid (strained) into the pan with the frog meat.
Transfer the frog, bananas, and liquid to another pot, cook over low heat for about 15 minutes until the bananas are soft.
5: Completion
Add finely chopped perilla leaves, stir briefly, and turn off the heat.
Ensure the dish has a rich flavor, a slightly thickened golden broth, delicious pork belly, soft bananas, and savory frog meat.
III. How to choose good frog meat
To choose good frog meat, keep the following in mind:
Timing: Choose wild frogs from September onwards as this is when they are meatiest and most nutritious.
Size and state: Prioritize large, plump frogs with yellow skin. Choose live ones with slender heads, clear muscle definition, bright eyes, and white or yellowish bellies.
Types to avoid: Do not buy farmed frogs or frozen processed frogs as this meat is often bland and lacks the characteristic flavor and aroma of fresh wild frogs.

The above passage specifies the factors to note when choosing frog meat to ensure the best quality and flavor for your dish. If you need more information or have other requests, please let us know. 1. Choose wild frogs from September onwards as this is when they are meatiest and most nutritious.

mon_an.ten: Chicken Wings in Tomato Sauce for Kids
mon_an.mo_ta: Chicken wings in tomato sauce for kids – making rice more delicious for the little ones, bringing joy to the whole family. Cooking guide for delicious Chicken Wings in Tomato Sauce for kids.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Honey, garlic, salt, sugar, pepper, oyster sauce, scallions
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the chicken wings:
Cut the chicken wings in half, blanch briefly in boiling water, and score a few lines so the wings absorb the spices. Wash and drain.
Marinate the wings with 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, 1 tbsp honey, and a little pepper; mix well and marinate for 2 - 3 hours for deep flavor.
Step 2: After marinating, coat the chicken wings with an even layer of tapioca starch.
Step 3: Fry the chicken wings until golden and cooked through, then remove to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil.
Step 4:
Sauté garlic in a pan with oil, then add ketchup and oyster sauce to the pan, bring to a boil, and season with a little sugar and filtered water.
Add the chicken wings to the pan, simmer until the sauce thickens, then serve the chicken wings in tomato sauce on a plate and enjoy hot with rice.
Source: Ngoi sao

mon_an.mo_ta: Fried dishes always have a surprising appeal for every family, especially for young children. If your child doesn't like eating corn, this easy-to-make crispy corn fritter recipe will help them enjoy it more. The fritters are fragrant with corn, featuring a light sweetness blended with the savory taste of shrimp and chicken.
cac_buoc: Let's start the daily delicious cooking guide with crispy corn fritters!

Step 1: Debone the chicken thigh and remove the skin, then cut into small pieces. Peel the shrimp, remove the black vein on the back, and wash. Place the chicken and shrimp in a blender and mince. Then add shallots, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tbsp sugar, and pepper; blend together until fragrant.
Step 2: Transfer the minced meat mixture to a bowl, add the corn kernels and cornstarch so the mixture binds together well.
Step 3: Divide the corn and meat mixture into equal portions and form into 1cm thick patties. Coat with a layer of breadcrumbs.
Step 4: Place a deep pan on the stove, add cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add each corn patty and fry until golden brown on both sides, then remove. Place in a basket to drain the oil.
Step 5: Present the easy-to-make crispy corn fritters on a plate. Serve hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: Pumpkin has long been known as a nutritious food with plenty of fiber and vitamin A, which is very beneficial for a baby's health and digestive system. Mothers, try this delicious and attractive scallop and pumpkin congee to change up your baby's menu using this recipe.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pumpkin

We will use the pumpkin itself to present the congee for a more attractive look. Therefore, keep the pumpkin skin intact, wash it thoroughly, then use a sharp knife to cut across about 1/3 of the way down from the stem. Use a sharp knife or spoon to scoop out the pumpkin flesh so that the outer shell remains intact. We will use this pumpkin as a bowl to hold the congee. Place the whole pumpkin (including the cut stem part) into a pot of boiling water and boil for about 5 minutes so the inner layer is just cooked and loses its raw smell, then remove and soak immediately in cold water and drain.
For the scooped-out flesh, remove seeds and fibers, and cut into small pieces (if necessary).
Step 2: Cook the congee
Rinse the rice thoroughly, place in a pot, add water (if you have bone broth, use it for better flavor), bring to a boil, then lower the heat so the rice softens.
Step 3: Briefly stir-fry the cleaned tiger prawns and scallops with turmeric powder and seasoning powder to taste.

Step 4: When the congee is almost cooked, add the pumpkin pieces from Step 1 and continue simmering until the pumpkin is soft. Then add the tiger prawns and scallops and simmer further. Season the congee with salt, fish sauce, and seasoning powder to taste, then sprinkle with chopped scallions, stir well, and turn off the heat.
Step 5: Presentation
Ladle the congee into the prepared pumpkin bowl, top with a few pieces of pumpkin and some chopped scallions for decoration.

With this unique presentation, the scallop and pumpkin congee will surely attract children at first sight. This congee, with its main ingredients of pumpkin, rice, scallops, and tiger prawns, helps supplement starch, vitamin A, fiber, protein, and essential nutrients for your baby's development.
A few tips for mothers to have the best pumpkin and scallop congee for their babies:

Although pumpkin is already very sweet and the congee is delicious on its own, you can prepare bone broth to cook the congee to add more nutrition. Bone broth simmered from chicken or pork bones is best. Avoid using beef bones as they will overpower the aroma of the pumpkin.
You can mix a little glutinous rice with the aromatic rice to make the congee more fragrant and flavorful.
You can also refer to the delicious chicken congee recipe to continuously vary the menu and avoid boredom for your children.

mon_an.ten: Shrimp and Mushroom Congee for Kids
mon_an.mo_ta: Shrimp and mushroom congee for kids – Learn to cook a new congee dish for your baby with simple ingredients that are high in nutrients, which will surely be very good for your little one. An easy-to-make dish for kids who are picky about congee, helping to change their palate.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, seasoning powder, cilantro, scallions, shallots, pepper
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the shrimp first: Peel the shrimp, remove the black vein on the back, rinse with diluted salt water, pat dry, then coarsely crush. Marinate the shrimp with minced shallots, a little salt, and a bit of pepper; mix well and marinate for about 20 minutes.
Step 2: Soak the glutinous rice in cold water for about 2 hours, then rinse and drain. Rinse the aromatic rice and drain. Heat a pan and toast both types of rice until the grains are dry and firm.
Step 3: Trim the mushroom stems, wash, and soak in diluted salt water for 15 minutes. Then remove to a basket to drain in preparation for the shrimp and mushroom congee.
Step 4: Put the glutinous rice, aromatic rice, cold water, and a little salt into a pot. Bring to a boil over low heat until the rice grains are soft.
Step 5: Heat a pot, add cooking oil, sauté shallots until fragrant, then add the shrimp and stir-fry until cooked.

Step 6: Once the rice is soft, add the stir-fried shrimp and continue simmering for 15 minutes. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Then add the mushrooms and cook for 3-5 minutes until the mushrooms are thoroughly cooked.
Step 7: Turn off the heat, sprinkle some cilantro and scallions into the pot, ladle into a bowl, sprinkle a little pepper on top, and serve hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: Clam congee is a nutritious dish that helps clear heat and detoxify the body. Let's cook this delicious clam congee with coconut milk according to the recipe. With this method, you will have a fragrant, thick, and creamy congee to serve with pepper, chili fish sauce, fried shallots, or fried dough sticks as desired. Additionally, you can cook clam congee to change the menu for children (just omit the chili and use little to no pepper).
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients:

Peel shallots, wash, slice, and fry until golden; set aside. Wash the clams, soak in diluted salt water with a few chili slices, and cover tightly so the clams spit out all the sand. Rinse the rice and drain. Wash the mustard greens and shred finely. Wash and chop the scallions. Knead the shredded coconut with hot water to extract 1/2 bowl of thick coconut cream and 1/2 bowl of thin coconut milk.
Step 2: Cook the congee:

Place the rice and broth into a pot, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the rice grains have fully bloomed. Add the 1/2 bowl of thin coconut milk and bring back to a boil, then add the clams and stir until they are cooked. Adjust the seasoning to taste, add a little oil, the thick coconut cream, chopped scallions, and perilla leaves; stir well and turn off the heat.
Step 3: Presentation:
Place the shredded mustard greens in a bowl and ladle the hot congee over them. When eating, stir well so the greens cook. You can add chili and fried shallots if desired. Serve hot.
Some secrets for a delicious clam congee:

To make the congee creamy and thick, you don't need to toast the rice before cooking. Start cooking the rice in cold water. Bring to a boil then lower the heat, and do not add seasonings until the rice is soft. If you season too early, the rice will stay hard and won't soften properly.

If you prefer more flavorful clams, you can boil them first, remove the meat, wash it, and then marinate with pepper, minced shallots, and fish sauce. Sauté minced shallots until fragrant, then briefly stir-fry the clams and set aside. Use the clam boiling water to cook the congee for better flavor. However, adding clams directly to the congee is also delicious and saves time. If adding directly, remember to soak the clams thoroughly to remove all sand.
Since clams are naturally salty, you should leave the seasoning as the final step to avoid making the congee too salty.

I find eating clam congee with shredded spicy mustard greens very delicious. This is a tip learned from seafood restaurants in Da Nang. Every shop there serves congee with a plate of shredded mustard greens. It's a perfect match. Give it a try!

mon_an.ten: Minced Pork and Egg Congee for Recovery
mon_an.mo_ta: Minced pork and egg congee is nutritious and delicious for both adults and children. Served with scallions and perilla, it is also known as recovery congee, an extremely effective dish for treating colds. Let's learn how to cook this delicious congee with this recipe.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Preparation
Blanch and wash the pork, then mince it. Marinate the pork with some white scallion parts, 1 minced shallot, pepper, seasoning powder, and fish sauce for 15 minutes.
Wash and finely chop the scallions, perilla, and cilantro.
Rinse the rice and drain.
Step 2: Cook the congee

Place the rice and water in a pot, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the rice blooms and the congee thickens. During the cooking process, occasionally add a little cold water to help the rice soften faster.

While waiting for the congee, put 1 bowl of water and 1 tbsp rice vinegar into a small pot. Crack the eggs and gently drop each one into the pot so the white wraps around the yolk. Poach until the egg is slightly set but the yolk is still runny. When the egg floats slightly, turn off the heat, remove the eggs, and rinse immediately with cold water. Peel off some of the white on one side for a better appearance. Set aside.
Place a pan on the stove, sauté minced shallots until fragrant, then add the pork and stir-fry until cooked and crumbly.

When the congee is soft and bloomed, add the stir-fried pork and stir well. You can add a little more water if the congee is too thick. Cook until the congee reaches the desired consistency, then add some scallions and turn off the heat.
Step 3: Presentation
Place chopped perilla and scallions in a bowl. Ladle the hot congee on top, gently place an egg on the congee, and sprinkle with more scallions and cilantro for decoration. Serve hot.
Tips for cooking delicious congee:
Start cooking the rice in cold water. Do not season until the rice is soft. Add cold water to the pot during cooking to help the rice soften faster.

Add vinegar to the egg poaching water to prevent the eggs from breaking. Only poach until the eggs are just set with a runny yolk for the best taste. Usually, when the egg floats, it's ready and must be removed and rinsed with cold water immediately. This stops the cooking process and makes it easier to trim the whites. This presentation looks much better. (In the past, my mother used to put the egg directly into the congee pot or crack it into the bowl and pour hot congee over it, which is also delicious! :P)

mon_an.ten: Delicious Chicken and Shiitake Mushroom Congee
cac_buoc: Chicken congee is a familiar dish that many people love. Not only is it delicious, but it is also rich in nutrients beneficial for health. If you are wondering how to prepare chicken for a dish suitable for both adults and children, chicken congee is an unmissable choice. Let's find out how to cook chicken congee in this article!
I. Guide to making whole chicken congee
1. Prepare ingredients
1 chicken (about 2.3 kg)
300g aromatic rice
300g fresh shiitake mushrooms (or straw mushrooms)
4 scallion stalks
4 cilantro stalks
5g Vietnamese coriander (rau răm)
5g ginger
4 garlic cloves
5 shallots
1 tbsp fried shallots
½ tsp turmeric powder
Seasonings: salt, sugar, rock sugar, pepper, seasoning powder, MSG, fish sauce
2. Prepare ingredients
Peel the shallots; cut 3 in half and mince the rest.
Mince the garlic.
Cut the white part of the scallions into 3cm lengths; finely chop the green parts.
Finely chop the cilantro.
Clean the Vietnamese coriander, wash thoroughly, and chop finely.
Wash the mushrooms and cut in half.
Wash the ginger and slice.
Rinse the rice and drain.
3. Boil the chicken
Mix ½ tsp turmeric powder with 1 tbsp hot oil; stir well to brush onto the chicken skin for a beautiful golden color.
When preparing the chicken, first rub a layer of salt and lemon on the outside and inside, then rinse several times. Remove the claws and the oil gland at the tail.

To boil the chicken, place it in a pot with 4 liters of water, shallots, and ginger. Heat the water to about 50°C before adding the chicken. Add 1 tbsp salt and 20g rock sugar to the water. Simmer on low heat after it boils, skim the foam, and cook for another 15-20 minutes. Once the chicken is cooked, turn off the heat and steep for 15 minutes.
After steeping, remove the chicken and soak in cold water. Remove the shallots and ginger from the broth. If the broth has evaporated too much, add cold water to reach 4 liters.
Remove the chicken from the cold water, brush the turmeric oil mixture onto the skin, then shred or chop into bite-sized pieces.
4. Toast the rice

To toast the rice, first place a pan on the stove and add 2 tbsp cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add some minced shallots and sauté until fragrant. Then, pour the rice into the pan and stir-fry over medium heat for about 6 minutes until the rice is firm and turns opaque white, then turn off the heat.
5. Sauté the mushrooms

To sauté the mushrooms, place a pan on the stove and add 1 tbsp cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add minced shallots and sauté until fragrant, then add the mushrooms. Season with 1 tsp seasoning powder and 3 tbsp water. Stir-fry until the seasonings dissolve, then turn off the heat.

To cook the best chicken congee, after the rice has bloomed in the chicken broth for about 30 minutes, add the sautéed mushrooms. Season with 1 tbsp seasoning powder, 1/3 tbsp salt, ½ tbsp sugar, and 1/3 tbsp MSG; stir well. Finally, add scallions and pepper, then turn off the heat.

After ladling the congee into a bowl, you can garnish with scallions, cilantro, and fried shallots. Enjoy this delicious congee with the chicken meat, Vietnamese coriander, and seasonings like salt, pepper, and lime.
II. Chicken and Malabar spinach congee (for babies)
Chicken thigh meat: 30 g
Malabar spinach: 20 g
White congee: 1.5 bowls
Salt: 1/4 tsp
Seasoning powder: 1/2 tsp
Baby cooking oil: 1 tsp
2. How to prepare chicken and Malabar spinach congee
2.1. Prepare the chicken
Place a pot on the stove, add 200ml water and the cleaned chicken thigh to boil until cooked through.
Then, use a knife to separate the meat from the bone and mince finely.
2.2. Prepare the Malabar spinach
Wash the Malabar spinach, cut into pieces, and place in a blender with 30ml water to puree.
2.3. Cook the congee
Heat a pot on the stove, add 1.5 bowls of congee and 2 bowls of water to dilute, cook over medium heat.
Add 1/4 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp seasoning powder to the congee when it boils.
When the congee boils, add the minced chicken, stirring well for about 3 – 5 minutes.
After the congee boils again, add the pureed Malabar spinach, stir for 3 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Pour the congee into a bowl and add 1 tsp baby cooking oil, stir well before serving.

You have just finished a delicious and nutritious bowl of chicken and Malabar spinach congee for your baby. This combination of white congee, sweet tender chicken, and fresh Malabar spinach promises a new culinary experience for your little one.
III. Notes for making delicious and nutritious chicken congee
To avoid odors, remove the oil gland at the tail before preparation.
Boiling the chicken starting from warm water (about 50°C) helps prevent a fishy smell and keeps the skin from cracking.
When adding water to boil, ensure the chicken is submerged with the back facing up so that thick parts like the breast and thighs are evenly cooked and the skin doesn't crack.
Steeping the chicken in the water after boiling helps it cook through to the bone without leaving blood.
Using aromatic or glutinous rice will provide a better flavor.
You can use chicken fat to make oil for toasting the rice, which makes it more fragrant; when cooked, the rice grains will bloom without becoming mushy or overly gloopy.
After steeping for enough time, remove the chicken and soak in cold water to make the skin crispier.
You can also shred the chicken and mix it into a salad to serve with the congee.
IV. How to buy fresh chicken
Choose chicken with bright yellow skin, no bruises or blood clots, and the meat should be pinkish-red.
When pressing lightly on the meat, if it feels firm and elastic, it is fresh. Conversely, if you see deep indentations, or if it feels mushy, leaky, and has a foul smell, avoid buying it.
When cooking congee for babies, choose the chicken breast as it is rich in protein, contains many nutrients, and the meat is soft, making it easier for babies to eat.

mon_an.mo_ta: The harmonious combination of chicken and tofu creates a very delicious taste that isn't as heavy as other types of chicken balls. Let's get into the kitchen and make these crispy chicken and tofu balls!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Remove the bones and skin, then cut the chicken into small pieces.
Step 2: Finely chop the tofu and onion.
Step 3: Place the chicken, onion, tofu, egg yolk, flour, and a little salt into a blender and process until very smooth.
Step 4: Place the chicken mixture in the refrigerator for about 20 minutes. This step will make it easier to shape the balls!
Step 5: One by one, roll the chicken mixture into small balls and then coat them in breadcrumbs. If you don't like round shapes, you can shape them into long sticks like cheese sticks.
Step 6: Heat oil in a pan and fry the balls until golden brown. You should use a fair amount of oil so the chicken balls are evenly rounded.
Step 7: Remove the chicken balls and place them on paper towels for about 2 minutes to drain excess oil before enjoying.

mon_an.ten: Simple and Delicious Stir-Fried Egg Noodles
mon_an.mo_ta: Change up your family menu with these stir-fried egg noodles to keep your meals exciting. Check out these simple and delicious ways to make stir-fried egg noodles in the content below! Enjoy a tasty meal with this guide to making flavorful stir-fried egg noodles. Discover how to make delicious stir-fried egg noodles today and enjoy a wonderful lunch or dinner.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 15ml hoisin sauce; 10ml soy sauce; 1.5g salt; 7.5ml cooking wine; 1 pinch pepper; 240g egg noodles (stir-fry type); 45ml cooking oil; 1 stalk green onion, chopped
cac_buoc: 1. Stir-fried Noodles with Egg and Sausage
Ingredients
2 packs instant noodles
2 delicious smoked IKA sausages
1-2 eggs
100g choy sum
Shallots
Garlic
Seasonings: fish sauce, seasoning powder, ground pepper
Instructions
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Wash the Malabar spinach, cut in half or into 5cm segments.
Peel and wash the shallots and garlic, then mince them.
Remove the plastic wrap from the sausages, then cut into 3 equal parts and score them for a nice appearance.
Step 2: Boil the instant noodles
Unpack the noodles and place them in a large bowl.

Boil water in a pot, then pour the boiling water to submerge the noodles. Soak for about 7-8 minutes until the noodles are just soft. Drain well. Note: do not soak for too long to avoid the noodles becoming too soft and mushy.

Note: Do not soak the noodles for too long because if the strands get too big, they will break when stir-fried. It is best to soak only until the strands are soft, still chewy, and not clumped together.
Step 3: Make the fried egg
Place a pan on the stove and add a little cooking oil. When the oil is hot, crack an egg into the pan.

Add a little water to the pan and cover with a lid to create steam, helping the egg cook evenly on both sides without flipping. This will create a thin layer of white covering the egg, preventing the yolk from drying out or breaking.
Wait until the egg reaches your desired doneness (usually a runny yolk is better), then turn off the heat and remove the egg to a plate.
Step 4: How to stir-fry noodles with sausage
Place a pan over heat and add a little oil. Wait until the oil is hot, then add the minced shallots and garlic and sauté until fragrant.
Next, add the sausages to the pan and stir-fry until they look slightly firm.
Then, add the vegetables and continue to stir-fry together. Toss the ingredients evenly, ensuring the noodles are also stir-fried well. Handle gently to avoid breaking or crushing the noodles.
Add a little fish sauce or soy sauce to the pan to stir-fry together and season to taste.
Step 5: Presentation and enjoyment
When the noodle strands are firm, chewy, smooth, and not sticky, remove the stir-fried noodles, vegetables, and sausages to a plate.
Finally, place the fried egg on top. You can sprinkle some toasted white sesame seeds on top for a beautiful look.
2. Stir-fried Noodles with Egg and Tomato
Ingredients
3 tomatoes
2 eggs
100g egg noodles
1 stalk green onion
2 tbsp ketchup
1 tbsp sesame oil
1/2 tsp minced ginger
1/2 tbsp cooking oil
2 tbsp soy sauce
1/2 tsp pepper
1/2 tsp brown sugar
Ingredient preparation
Clean the tomatoes, then cut them into small slices to cook faster.
Clean and chop the green onions. Then, crack the eggs into a bowl and beat them.
Fry the eggs

In a pan, add about 1/2 tbsp cooking oil. Place the pan over medium heat and wait for the oil to get hot. Then, add the eggs to the pan and stir well. Cook and stir until the eggs are cooked through and no longer wet. Once the eggs are dry and cooked, remove from the pan and set aside.
Stir-fry tomatoes with eggs
Turn on medium heat and add the tomatoes to the pan. Add 1/2 tsp minced ginger and 1 tbsp sesame oil to the pan. Stir well until the tomatoes are cooked.
Next, add 2 tbsp ketchup and 2 tbsp soy sauce to the pan. Stir the ingredients well.
Then, add about 500ml water to the pan. Continue to cook until the water boils, then add the fried eggs back into the pan. Stir well to combine the mixture.
Season with 1/2 tsp pepper and 1/2 tsp brown sugar. You can adjust the seasonings to suit your family's taste.
Crack the remaining egg into a bowl, beat it, then pour it into the pan. Stir constantly while cooking so the egg cooks evenly. When the mixture boils again, turn off the heat.
How to blanch the noodles
Place a large pot of water over high heat and bring to a boil. Add about 1 liter of water to the pot to blanch the noodles without them sticking together.
When the water is boiling, add the noodles to the pot and blanch for 2 to 3 minutes, depending on the type of noodles (refer to the instructions on the noodle packaging).
Complete the blanching process.
Presentation and enjoyment
Take the cooked tomato egg broth and pour it into a bowl.
Add the blanched noodles to the bowl and sprinkle some green onions on top.
The dish is now complete, and you can enjoy the egg noodles with tomato broth and green onions.
3. Stir-fried Egg Noodles with Fried Egg and Greens
Ingredients
200g stir-fry noodles
1 onion
2 garlic cloves
1 bunch of greens (spinach, bok choy, or any greens of your choice)
2 tbsp cooking oil
2 tbsp fish sauce
1 tbsp soy sauce
1/2 tsp sugar
Pepper, salt (to taste)
Instructions
Prepare ingredients: Wash the greens and chop them. Mince the garlic and onion.

Fry the egg: Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well. In a pan, add 1 tbsp cooking oil and heat it up. When the oil is hot, pour the eggs into the pan and stir well until the eggs are cooked and set. Once the eggs are cooked, remove to a plate and set aside.
Stir-fry the greens: In the same pan used to fry the eggs, add 1 tbsp cooking oil and heat it up. Then, add the minced garlic and onion to the pan, sauté until fragrant.
Add the greens: Next, add the prepared greens to the pan. Stir-fry the greens for about 2-3 minutes until they are soft but still retain their crunch.

Stir-fry the noodles: Push the greens to one side of the pan, add 1 tbsp cooking oil to the empty space. Then, add the stir-fry noodles to the pan and stir-fry with the oil and greens. Stir the noodles and other ingredients well for about 2-3 minutes, until the noodles are soft and evenly stir-fried.
Mix fish sauce and soy sauce: In a small bowl, combine 2 tbsp fish sauce and 1 tbsp soy sauce. Mix well until the ingredients are blended.

Add seasonings and egg: Pour the fish sauce and soy sauce mixture into the noodle pan. Next, add sugar, pepper, and salt (if needed) to adjust the taste. Stir well so the seasonings penetrate the noodles and greens. Finally, add the prepared fried eggs to the pan and stir well.

Presentation and enjoyment: Place the stir-fried egg noodles with greens on a plate and decorate as desired. You can enjoy the stir-fried egg noodles while they are still hot, served with fish sauce or soy sauce to enhance the flavor.
4. Crispy Egg Stir-fried Noodles
1/2 red onion
1/2 carrot
1/2 cabbage
1/2 green radish
1/2 bok choy
Prepare ingredients: Wash the vegetables and cut them into bite-sized pieces. Mince the garlic, onion, and red onion.

Crispy egg: Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat well. In a pan, add 1 tbsp cooking oil and heat it up. When the oil is hot, pour the eggs into the pan and mix well to form a thin, crispy layer. When the eggs are cooked and golden brown, remove to a plate and set aside.
Stir-fry vegetables: In the same pan used to fry the eggs, add 1 tbsp cooking oil and heat it up. Then, add the minced garlic, onion, and red onion to the pan, sauté until fragrant.
Add vegetables and carrots: Next, add the carrots and cabbage to the pan. Stir-fry for about 2-3 minutes until the vegetables and carrots are soft.

Stir-fry the noodles: Push the vegetables and carrots to one side of the pan, add 1 tbsp cooking oil to the empty space. Then, add the stir-fry noodles to the pan and stir-fry with the oil and vegetables. Stir the noodles and other ingredients well for about 2-3 minutes, until the noodles are soft and evenly stir-fried.
Mix fish sauce and soy sauce: In a small bowl, combine 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 tsp sugar. Mix well until the ingredients are blended.

Add seasonings and crispy egg: Pour the fish sauce and soy sauce mixture into the noodle pan. Next, add pepper and salt (if needed) to adjust the taste. Stir well so the seasonings penetrate the noodles and vegetables. Finally, add the prepared crispy eggs to the stir-fried noodles and stir well.

Presentation and enjoyment: Place the crispy egg stir-fried noodles on a plate and decorate as desired. You can enjoy the stir-fried egg noodles while they are still hot for the best crispy egg texture.
5. Simple Stir-fried Egg Noodle Recipe
Step 1: In a small bowl, mix honey, hoisin, soy sauce, sesame oil, salt, wine, and white pepper. Set aside.
Step 2: Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the noodles. Blanch for 2-3 minutes, then rinse the noodles under cold water so they don't stick together.

Step 3: Heat a pan then add 15ml oil, swirl the pan so the oil spreads evenly. Add the noodles to the pan, stir well for about 5 minutes until the noodles turn a deep golden color (about 4-5 minutes).

Step 4: Add another 15ml of cooking oil around the pan and stir gently. Then, lower the heat to medium and add the remaining oil along with the sauce mixture. Stir the noodles for another 3 minutes, then add some green onions and toasted sesame seeds, then turn off the heat.
Conclusion:

The guide to making stir-fried egg noodles offers a delicious and flavorful dish. The combination of stir-fried noodles, eggs, and greens creates a wonderful pairing. The noodles are stir-fried until fragrant and soft, blending with the crispy fried eggs. This dish is not only delicious but also meets the body's nutritional needs. With simple instructions, you can hand-make these stir-fried egg noodles and enjoy a tasty meal at home.

mon_an.ten: Crispy Fried Chicken and Mushroom Patties
mon_an.mo_ta: If you are wondering what to cook for the family tonight, why not try making crispy fried chicken and mushrooms? This dish is a blend of delicious chicken, soft and sweet fresh mushrooms, rich butter, and a crispy breadcrumb crust. These crispy fried chicken and mushroom patties will help moms win over the whole family, especially the kids. Let's learn how to make this delicious dish!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Wash the chicken and let it drain. If the meat pieces are too large and thick, you can cut them into small bite-sized pieces so the chicken cooks quickly without becoming mushy.
Next, wash the fresh mushrooms and cut them into small pieces.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and beat them.
Step 2: Implementation steps
First, put the chicken in a pot and add enough water to submerge the meat. Then, place the pot on the stove and boil until the chicken is cooked.
When the chicken is cooked, take it out to cool slightly, then shred or finely chop the meat.
Then, put the butter in a pot and melt it.
Next, add 200g of flour to the butter pot. Use a spoon to stir well so the flour doesn't clump and the mixture is even.
Then, add ½ tsp salt, 1 tsp pepper, and the milk to the flour pot.
Add the unsweetened fresh milk slowly to the flour pot to avoid making the dough too runny. Be sure to stir constantly and thoroughly to obtain a very smooth, somewhat thick flour mixture.
After the mixture is well combined, add the fresh mushrooms and shredded chicken to the flour pot. Continue to mix very well so that the flour and ingredients are blended together.

Then, transfer the flour, mushroom, and chicken mixture into a plastic container, smoothing the surface. Cover the mouth of the container tightly with plastic wrap and place the container in the refrigerator for about 1.5 to 2 hours.
