Making Giò Lụa is quite simple, isn't it? It takes a little time, but in return, you have a wonderful dish for your family's daily meals, especially during Tet.
You can also boil this roll, but steaming is best!
It's absolutely delicious served with Gac sticky rice or mung bean sticky rice!

mon_an.ten: Secrets to Delicious Beef Hot Pot for Tet
mon_an.mo_ta: Tet is an occasion for the whole family to reunite and gather together. It would be wonderful to cook a beef hot pot for everyone to enjoy, wouldn't it?
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Mustard greens, chrysanthemum greens, celery - as much as you like
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the pork bones and cut into large chunks. Bring water to a boil, add the bones, and once it boils vigorously, discard the water. Add fresh cold water and simmer to make the broth.
Step 2:
Thinly slice the beef across the grain and marinate with minced ginger and seasoning.
Remove the stems from the tomatoes and cut into wedges.
Cut the tofu into bite-sized squares. Pick and wash the mustard greens, chrysanthemum greens, and celery; keep them separate and cut into 15cm lengths for easy eating.
Sauté the scallions until fragrant.
Step 3:

When ready to eat, pour the broth into the hot pot, add the hot pot seasoning packet, and adjust the seasoning to taste. You can add satay if desired. Arrange all prepared items on plates on the table.
When the broth runs low, add more broth as needed.
After adding the ingredients, you can add some noodles to the pot for a more filling meal.

mon_an.ten: Chả Đùm – Savory Southern Vietnamese Steamed Meatballs
mon_an.mo_ta: Chả đùm is a unique and familiar dish for people in Southern Vietnam. This dish is often prepared for holidays, especially the Lunar New Year (Tet). Chả đùm has a delicious and attractive flavor, characterized by a thin outer layer of rich caul fat combined with a diverse, flavorful filling. This is a rustic dish deeply connected to the lifestyle and cultural traditions of Southerners. Let's learn how to make delicious Chả đùm! Discover how to make this wonderful dish; the enticing flavors of this traditional Vietnamese food will make you want to eat it immediately. Enjoy the exciting experience of blending wonderful ingredients in every bite of Chả đùm.
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the ingredients
Boil the peas: Place a pot on the stove and boil 50g of peas for 3-4 minutes until the water boils, then remove and let cool.
Wash and soak the caul fat: Wash 50g of caul fat multiple times with salt water, then soak it in water mixed with a little wine to remove odors.
Soak glass noodles and wood ear mushrooms: Soak 20g of glass noodles and 20g of wood ear mushrooms in warm water until expanded, then use a knife to cut them into small strands.
Tear and soak the bread: Tear 100g of dense white bread into small pieces, then soak in 220ml of unsweetened fresh milk and mash finely.

Mix the filling: Combine 100g ground beef, 200g ground pork, 1 tbsp broth powder, and 1/2 tbsp sugar and mix well. Next, add 1 egg, wood ear mushrooms, glass noodles, boiled peas, 50g roasted peanuts, 100g fried garlic, and 10g crushed peppercorns, then mix well by hand.
These preparation steps will ensure all ingredients are ready for cooking the delicious Chả đùm.
2. Process the Chả đùm
Line the bowl with caul fat: Spread the caul fat evenly over the surface of a deep bowl or ramekin.

Wrap the meat with caul fat: Divide the meat mixture into 4 portions. Place each portion into a bowl lined with caul fat. Press the meat down firmly, then wrap the edges of the caul fat over it. Note: Press firmly to ensure the meat binds together for a beautiful round shape.
Repeat the process: Repeat the steps until all the meat mixture is used.
This way, you will have round, firm meatballs with good cohesion, ready for the next step.
3. Steam the Chả đùm
Steam the meatballs: Place the wrapped meatballs into a steamer. Steam for about 15 minutes.
Invert onto a plate: Once cooked, remove from the steamer by inverting the bowl onto a plate.
Garnish: Use a knife to make light cuts on the surface. Then, sprinkle with some scallion oil, roasted peanuts, and cilantro to add flavor and make the dish look more attractive.
Note:
If you cannot find caul fat, you can grease the bowl with lard before adding the meat mixture to steam.
You can also omit the bread for a fluffier texture that retains the meat's dryness better.
Chả đùm can be served with shrimp crackers or rice crackers, creating a perfect combination of crunchy texture and savory flavor.
III. Some notes when making Chả đùm
Choose fresh ground meat: Use fresh ground meat with both lean and fat for a rich, delicious taste.
Prepare wood ear mushrooms: They must be soaked until expanded and cleaned thoroughly before use.
Mix the filling evenly: When mixing, do so thoroughly so all ingredients are well combined.
Steam until just cooked: Steam until just done; do not overcook to avoid drying out the meat.
Add other ingredients: Depending on preference, you can add other ingredients like peas or shiitake mushrooms to enrich the flavor.
Following these steps will help you create a delicious Chả đùm with a signature rich and savory taste.
IV. Ways to enjoy Chả đùm more deliciously
1. Wrapped in rice paper
Wrap a piece of Chả đùm in rice paper with fresh herbs, and serve with sweet and sour fish sauce and chili sauce.
This is an excellent way to eat it.
2. As a sandwich filling
You can slice the Chả đùm thinly and use it as a filling for Bánh mì.
This is delicious, convenient, and perfect for breakfast or a snack.
3. Mixed in a salad
You can cut the Chả đùm into small pieces and toss them with a vegetable salad.
This is both delicious and nutritious, very suitable for those on a diet.

mon_an.mo_ta: Salt-cured pork trotter is a traditional dish in Vietnamese culinary culture, carrying deep traditional flavors and family warmth. With just a few simple ingredients like pork trotter, salt, pepper, and marinade, you can create a delicious dish for Tet. Refer to the salt-cured pork trotter recipe below! This guide makes it easy to prepare for a cozy Tet holiday. Start cooking and enjoy these culinary moments during Tet!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Grill Mates Hickory BBQ Smoked Seasoning - 1 bottle (available at supermarkets)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pork trotter
To clean the hair on the trotter, use tweezers or a razor to completely remove any stiff hairs. Then, wash the trotter thoroughly with diluted salt water.
When making salt-cured pork trotter, choosing large, fresh trotters is important. Specifically, remove all the bones so the meat absorbs the salt easily and is convenient for tying.
Use bamboo strings or kitchen twine to wrap the trotter tightly, ensuring it is neat and attractive.
Step 2: Prepare the spices

Place a pan on the stove over low heat. Once the pan is warm, add 10g Mac Khen seeds, 10g Sichuan peppercorns, 20g white peppercorns, 1 star anise, 1 black cardamom, and 3 Doi seeds. Toast these spices for about 30 seconds until fragrant, then turn off the heat and let cool.
Once the spices have cooled, put them in a dry grinder and grind into a fine powder. Transfer the spice mixture to a dry bowl.
Note: If the meat floats too much above the water, you can use a small bowl to press it down to ensure the entire piece is marinated.
Step 3: Marinate the meat

Place the pork trotter in a basin, then add 30g minced lemongrass, 20g minced garlic, 1/2 tsp ginger powder, 1 tbsp fish sauce, and 1 tsp MSG. Next, add the toasted spice mixture from the previous step.
Use your hands to rub the spices evenly over the meat, ensuring it is covered both inside and out. Marinate for at least 2 hours to let the flavors penetrate.
Step 4: Shaping and brining the trotter
Place a pot on the stove with 2 liters of water and 2 tbsp of salt. Stir over high heat until the salt is completely dissolved. Bring to a boil, then turn off the heat and let the brine cool.
After the meat is marinated, use a spoon to scrape off the excess marinade sticking to the meat. Flip the meat so the skin side is facing out.
Next, use a mesh netting to slowly wrap the trotter, starting from the small end and pulling up until the meat is completely encased. Tie off both ends.
Bring a pot of water to a boil and hold the trotter just above the surface. Use a ladle to pour boiling water over the trotter until the skin becomes uniformly firm.
Place the trotter in a large container and pour the cooled brine over it until completely submerged. Cover and store in the refrigerator to brine for 24 hours.
Step 5: Steaming the trotter
After 24 hours, remove the trotter from the brine and let it drain in a basket.

Take a pot and cut a piece of aluminum foil the size of the pot's bottom. Place the foil in the pot, then pour 100g of rice onto the foil. Next, add 100g salt, 50g sugar, 10g Sichuan pepper powder, and 10g whole peppercorns on top of the rice. Turn on the heat and stir until the ingredients begin to release smoke and aroma.
Place a steamer rack into the hot pot and line the bottom of the rack with 5 stalks of lemongrass. Place the trotter on the rack and cover with a lid. Steam over low heat for 1 hour.

Turn off the heat and let the trotter cool naturally with the lid still on. Then, place the trotter on a plate in front of a fan or in a breezy spot to dry the skin. Once the skin is dry, place the trotter in a plastic container and seal tightly. Store in the refrigerator for 1 day before using.
Step 6: Finishing the delicious salt-cured trotter
Once the meat is tender and cooked, remove it and let it cool slightly in a basket. Then, place the meat in a plastic container and put it in the freezer for about 3-4 hours to firm up.
Once the meat is firm, use a sharp knife to slice it into thin, round pieces. Slice it so that every piece looks mouth-watering and irresistible.

mon_an.ten: Chè Kho (Mung Bean Pudding) for Year-End Offerings
mon_an.mo_ta: Chè kho is a familiar dessert used in rituals for offering to Buddha or ancestors in Vietnam. It is often served on the Full Moon, the first day of the lunar month, or during Tet for worship ceremonies. Today, we will guide you through a simple way to cook Chè Kho for offerings, so you can personally make this meaningful dessert. Enjoy the traditional flavor and bring joy to important holidays with this fragrant mung bean pudding.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Soak the peeled mung beans for about 4-5 hours until they expand and soften (alternatively, you can soak them in warm water).
Step 2: Wash the beans again and steam them in a steamer with a pinch of salt until cooked.
Step 3: While the beans are still hot, use a ladle to mash them until soft and fluffy.
Step 4: Pass the mashed beans through a sieve once more to ensure they are perfectly smooth.
Step 5: Toast the white sesame seeds until golden.
Step 6: Dissolve 150g of sugar in a little water and bring to a boil.
Step 7: Add the mung beans and stir constantly. Stir continuously so the pudding doesn't burn.
Step 8: When the water has evaporated and the beans and sugar syrup have thickened into a paste, turn off the heat. Transfer the pudding to a mold and sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top.
Notes for making Chè Kho:
Choose quality mung beans: Select fresh mung beans with uniform seeds and no damage. Check carefully before buying to avoid old beans that are hard to cook.
Soak the beans: Before cooking, soak the mung beans for 3-4 hours to soften them. This helps them cook evenly and reduces cooking time.
Cook for the right amount of time: When cooking the beans, ensure they are soft but still hold their shape. Overcooking will make them mushy and lose their natural nuttiness.

Add sugar and coconut milk: Once the beans are cooked, add sugar and coconut milk to enhance the flavor and sweetness. Add gradually and stir well to ensure the sugar dissolves and the mixture is homogeneous.
Check the sweetness: Before turning off the heat, taste the pudding. If necessary, add more sugar or coconut milk to adjust the sweetness to your liking.
Shaping the pudding: Once the pudding has cooled and firmed up, you can use a knife to cut it into attractive shapes for better presentation.
How to choose good ingredients:
1. How to buy mung beans
Choose medium, uniform beans: Mung bean seeds should be medium-sized and uniform, not too large or too small.
Check color and firmness: Choose beans with a beautiful yellow color, shiny and plump. When held, they should feel firm.
Avoid faulty beans: Avoid beans with strange colors, broken seeds, or mold. The beans should not be infested by weevils. Such beans can ruin the flavor of the dish.
2. How to store Chè Kho
Wait for it to cool completely: Before storing, wait for the pudding to cool completely to avoid condensation and moisture.
Place in a sealed jar: Use a jar or container with a tight lid. Ensure the container is completely dry and clean before adding the pudding.
Store in the refrigerator: Chè Kho can be stored in the refrigerator to extend its shelf life. Place the jar in the cold compartment and seal tightly to avoid absorbing odors from other foods.
Avoid contact with air: Keep the jar tightly closed to prevent air contact, which can cause the pudding to lose moisture and quality.
Use quickly: Chè Kho is best when consumed within 3-5 days after cooking. Prioritize eating it within this timeframe for the best flavor.

mon_an.ten: 3 Ways to Make Flavorful Fish Sauce Fried Chicken
cac_buoc: Fish sauce fried chicken is a popular and well-loved dish. With its delicious and rich flavor, the chicken is thoroughly infused with fish sauce, creating a perfect combination. Below are 3 ways to make fish sauce fried chicken for your reference.
I. Garlic Butter Fish Sauce Fried Chicken
1. Ingredients
1kg chicken
1 tub of butter
1 pack of crispy frying flour
1 large garlic bulb
5-7 fresh chilies
2 tomatoes
2 cucumbers
2. Cooking Steps
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Wash the chicken and cut into bite-sized pieces. Marinate the chicken with a little salt, parboil it, then remove and drain well.
Wash the chilies and garlic, then finely mince or grind them.
Wash the tomatoes and cucumbers. Soak the cucumbers in salt water or ice water for about 30 minutes to make them crispier. Then, remove and slice thinly to serve with the chicken.
Step 2: Marinate the chicken

Mix the chicken with 5 tsp fish sauce, 3 tsp sugar, and 1 tbsp seasoning powder. Once well mixed, sprinkle with a little crispy frying flour and stir well so the chicken is coated with seasonings and flour.
Step 3: Fry the chicken
Heat 200 ml of cooking oil in a pot or pan. Drop each marinated piece of chicken into the oil.

Fry the chicken over medium heat until golden brown. For extra crispiness, increase the heat and continue frying until crispy. Once done, remove the chicken from the oil and drain on a rack or paper towels.
Next, you can enjoy the crispy fish sauce fried chicken with the prepared chilies, garlic, tomatoes, and cucumbers.
Step 4: Make the garlic butter fish sauce glaze
Heat a pan. Add the butter and melt it.
Add the minced garlic and chilies from Step 1 to the pan, along with 20 ml fish sauce and 5 tsp sugar. Stir well until the mixture thickens.
Next, add the fried chicken to the pan and toss well. Cook for a short time so the mixture coats the chicken completely. Then, turn off the heat and remove the pan.
Finished product:
This wonderful garlic butter fish sauce fried chicken can be enjoyed with fresh greens like lettuce, tomatoes, cucumbers, or any other vegetables you like.
II. Traditional Fish Sauce Fried Chicken
Chicken wings: 4-5 wings.
Garlic: 2 bulbs
Ginger and fresh chili: 1 piece/fruit each
White wine and sea salt
Seasonings: fish sauce, MSG, black pepper, and cooking oil.
2. Preparation steps
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Peel and crush the garlic. Peel and mince the ginger.

After buying the chicken, use white wine and sea salt to rub the meat and remove any odors. Rinse the meat to remove the smell of wine and salt, then chop into bite-sized pieces or leave whole as desired. Marinate the chicken with 1-2 tbsp fish sauce, ½ tsp black pepper, ½ tsp MSG, 1 tbsp cooking oil, and a bit of ginger for about 15 minutes.
Step 2: Processing

Place a pan on the stove and add a moderate amount of cooking oil. Wait for the oil to heat up, then drop each piece of chicken in and fry until the meat is cooked through, crispy, and golden brown. Then, drain the chicken.

Using the same pan, add garlic, 1 tbsp fish sauce, and 1 tbsp sugar. Sauté until the garlic is fragrant and golden. Then, put the fried chicken back into the pan, toss quickly over high heat, and adjust the seasoning to taste. Just before turning off the heat, add the chilies.
Serve the chicken on a plate and garnish with lettuce, a few tomato slices, and some cilantro on top. The dish is complete.
III. Air Fryer Fish Sauce Chicken Wings
Chicken wings: 500g
Tomato: 1
Lemon: a little
Lettuce: a little
Minced chili: 1 tsp
Minced garlic: 1 tsp
Minced shallots: 1 tsp
Cooking oil: 1 tbsp
Fish sauce: 2 tbsp
Common seasonings: a little (can include sugar, seasoning powder, MSG)
2. Steps to make the chicken wings
2.1. Prepare the chicken wings
Wash the chicken wings with salt and lemon. Then, rinse with clean water and drain in a basket. Next, cut the wings into 2 pieces at the joint.
Tips for cleaning chicken wings and removing odors:

To remove odors and impurities, after rubbing the wings with salt, you can use a mixture of wine and sliced ginger. Use your hands to lightly crush and massage the meat again. Then, rinse the wings and wait for them to drain.
Alternatively, you can add lemon to water and soak the wings for about 15-20 minutes. Then, remove the wings, rinse with cold water, and drain.
2.2. Marinate the chicken

Mix the chicken wings with 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp minced chili, 1 tsp minced garlic, 1 tsp minced shallots, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp MSG, 1 tsp seasoning powder, and 1/2 tbsp cooking oil. Ensure the wings are evenly coated in this mixture.
2.3. Fry the chicken wings
Before frying, brush a thin layer of oil onto the surface of the air fryer basket. Preheat the air fryer at 180°C for about 3-5 minutes.
Arrange all the wings in the basket and fry the first side at 200°C for about 15-20 minutes.

After about 20 minutes, open the air fryer and flip the chicken pieces. Continue frying for another 10 minutes to ensure the wings are evenly cooked. Arrange the fried chicken on a plate and it's ready to enjoy.
Air frying chicken wings with fish sauce not only saves time but also reduces the steps compared to traditional frying methods.
IV. Notes when making fish sauce fried chicken

Ensure the wings are dry: Before marinating and frying, make sure the wings are washed and completely drained. Excess water can cause oil splatters when frying and prevent the chicken from becoming crispy.

Marinate evenly: Mix the fish sauce and other seasonings well to marinate the wings. Ensure the seasonings penetrate the meat by kneading and massaging gently. Let the wings marinate in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes for better flavor absorption.

Use appropriate temperature and time: When frying, adjust the temperature and time according to the instructions for your fryer or air fryer. This ensures the chicken is cooked through, crispy, and not burnt.

Manage the frying oil: If using a deep fryer, pay attention to the oil level and follow the manufacturer's instructions. Ensure the oil is deep enough to submerge the wings, but not too full to avoid overflowing when the food is added.
V. How to choose fresh chicken
Choose chicken with a dry surface: Select pieces of chicken that have a dry surface with no signs of moisture. This indicates the meat is fresh and recently slaughtered.
Check the elasticity: When pressed, fresh meat will retain its elasticity and quickly return to its original shape. If the meat stays soft and deformed for too long, it is a sign it's not fresh.
Observe the color: Fresh chicken usually has a light yellow, bright color. Avoid buying pieces that are pale white or slightly greyish, as this may be a sign of chemical treatment.
Check the smell: Fresh chicken has a characteristic raw meat smell, with no strange or foul odors. Smell the meat to check before buying.
Avoid mushy chicken: If the chicken feels mushy to the touch, it may be a sign that the meat has spoiled and should not be purchased.

mon_an.ten: Western Vietnamese Style Lemongrass Braised Chicken
mon_an.mo_ta: We all know that chicken and lemongrass are healthy foods, so we would like to introduce this delicious lemongrass braised chicken recipe. Please refer to the method below. Western Vietnamese Style Lemongrass Braised Chicken - Enjoy the characteristic flavors of the Mekong Delta with this attractive and tasty dish. Discover the recipe and secrets to creating a rich, delicious traditional meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Chicken thighs - 300g, washed and cut into bite-sized pieces
Lemongrass - 4 stalks (2 thinly sliced, 2 left whole and smashed)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Add a little cooking oil to a pan, add the lemongrass, ginger, and garlic, and sauté until fragrant.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for a while until the meat firms up, then season to taste.
Step 2:
Once the chicken is firm, pour 1 bowl of water into the pot. When the water boils, turn the heat to low and simmer until the chicken is tender.
When the lemongrass braised chicken is soft, serve in a bowl and enjoy!
How to choose fresh ingredients
How to choose fresh white radishes
Choose medium-sized white radishes that are tapered towards the tail. Radishes that are too fat at the tail often have a bland taste.
Choose radishes with the roots and leaves still attached, ensuring the leaves are fresh as this indicates they were recently harvested.
Avoid buying radishes with rotten stems while the skin is still glossy, as they may have been injected with preservatives.
Identify Chinese radishes to avoid: very smooth, shiny skin, pure white color, quite large size, fat body, and no leaves or roots.
How to choose fresh straw mushrooms
Choose straw mushrooms that are still in the bud stage, unopened, fresh, and slightly round or cylindrical in shape.
Choose mushrooms of moderate, uniform size.
Straw mushrooms that are black or grey are usually tastier than white ones.
When touched and lightly squeezed, the mushrooms should be firm. Fresh mushrooms have a characteristic natural aroma and no strange foul odors.
How to buy fresh chicken
Choose chicken with pinkish-red skin, no bruises or blood clots. Avoid chickens with dark, dull skin, as they may have died before being sold.
Prioritize chickens with a compact body, light yellow, thin, smooth skin with high elasticity. The chicken should have darker yellow streaks in areas like the breast, wings, and back.
Press on the thigh or breast to check if the chicken has been injected with water. If the chicken feels mushy, slippery, or deforms, do not buy it.
When buying frozen chicken, purchase from reputable supermarkets or food stores to ensure product quality.
How to prepare chicken without odors
Pluck out any stiff black feathers on the skin, cut off the oil gland and fat, and wash away any remaining blood inside the cavity.
Use smashed ginger and a little white wine to rub the chicken body for about 10 minutes, then rinse thoroughly with water.
You can wash the chicken in salt water and rinse under cold running water to remove stubborn impurities.
Absolutely do not soak the chicken in salt water to clean it, as soaking will make the meat become mushy and develop a fishy smell.

mon_an.ten: Super Tender Steamed Chicken with Scallions
mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed chicken with scallions is a simple and easy-to-make dish, yet it offers a special delicious flavor. After steaming, the chicken becomes fragrant, with glossy golden skin and a touch of green from the scallions, creating a very eye-catching meal. Let's discover how to make super tender and flavorful whole steamed chicken with scallions!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients

A key factor in making delicious steamed chicken with scallions without odors is thorough preparation. First, to remove the chicken's odor, use sea salt to rub the surface for about 5 - 10 minutes, then rinse several times with water. Next, use a knife to make a few slashes on the meat surface and let it drain.

To create a rich flavor, marinate the chicken with seasonings. Mix 1 tsp salt or seasoning salt, 2 tsp sugar, 1 tsp seasoning powder, and 1/2 tsp ground pepper. Rub the seasonings all over the chicken, then place it in the refrigerator for 15 - 30 minutes to let the flavors penetrate.

Peel the fresh lemongrass, remove the base and top, wash, and shred into small strips. Peel the ginger, wash, and slice. Soak dried shiitake mushrooms in warm water for about 10 - 15 minutes until soft, then wash to remove dirt. Finally, squeeze dry and carve the mushrooms into flower shapes.
Step 2: Steam the chicken

Place a pot on the stove with about 600ml of water and bring to a boil over high heat. When the water boils, spread a layer of lemongrass on the steamer tray and place the chicken on top. Steam the chicken for about 15 minutes over medium heat. After this time, check if the chicken is nearly cooked. If it is, lower the heat and add the ginger and shiitake mushrooms to the tray. Continue steaming for another 10 to 15 minutes.

Finally, add the green onions to the tray and steam for 5 more minutes. Then, turn off the heat. Remove the chicken from the steamer and chop into bite-sized pieces. Arrange the chicken on a plate while still hot.
Step 3: Finished product

This method is simple but results in a golden, fresh, and irresistibly sweet chicken dish. The flavor harmoniously combines the rich aroma of the chicken with the characteristic scents of scallions, lemongrass, and ginger, creating something new yet very rustic.
How to buy fresh ingredients
1. Tips for choosing good chicken
To ensure the steamed chicken is delicious and firm, choose live chicken to process rather than pre-processed frozen chicken. Here are some tips for choosing live chicken:
Choose similar sizes: If two chickens are of similar size, choose the heavier one. Its meat will be firmer.
Check the beak: Choose a chicken with a sharp, shiny beak that is not slimy. The beak is an important indicator of the chicken's health.

Observe the shape and state: Choose a chicken with a straight, slender, uniform body and no signs of scratches or broken claws. Especially avoid chickens with red spots or strange colored spots on their legs.
Check skin elasticity: When touching the skin, if it feels elastic and the meat is firm and not mushy, it is a sign of a fresh chicken.
Remember to apply these tips when buying live chicken to ensure quality and taste for your dish.
2.2. Tips for choosing green onions
For this dish, choose green onions with intact roots and plump bulbs, no scratches, bright colors, and a characteristic pungent aroma.
Avoid buying wilted or slimy green onions, or those with yellowing bulbs and unusual odors. These signs indicate the onions are old and may affect the dish's flavor.
2.3. Tips for choosing shiitake mushrooms
Whether using fresh or dried shiitake mushrooms, both work well for this recipe.

When choosing dried mushrooms, select those with a uniform golden-brown color, firm stems, and a characteristic aroma. For fresh mushrooms, choose those with moderately large, tightly closed caps that look beautiful and are not slimy.
Absolutely do not choose fresh shiitake mushrooms that are dark brown, as they might be a poisonous variety.
Limit buying mushrooms with bruises, wrinkled caps, or sliminess to ensure quality.
Notes when making steamed chicken with scallions
Choose fresh chicken: Select fresh chicken with plump, pink meat and no odor. Fresh chicken will be more tender and delicious.

Seasoning and marinating time: Marinate the chicken with salt, pepper, minced garlic, and seasonings to your taste. Let it marinate in the fridge for 2 to 4 hours or overnight to let the flavors penetrate and tenderize the meat.
Steam for the right time: Place the chicken in the steamer and cook for about 15-20 minutes per kilogram. Check the meat to ensure it is cooked through but not overcooked, so it remains tender.
Boil the water correctly: Boil the water over high heat first, then reduce to low or medium. This helps the chicken steam gently without overheating.

Add fresh aromatics: Add the scallions, ginger, and shiitake mushrooms when the chicken is nearly done to enhance the flavor and aroma. Scallions and ginger provide freshness, while shiitake mushrooms add a characteristic fragrance.

mon_an.ten: Mouth-watering Boneless Chicken Stuffed with Ham
mon_an.mo_ta: This Lunar New Year, try making this delicious and unique boneless chicken stuffed with ham to make your holiday meal more attractive! Discover the recipe for mouth-watering boneless chicken stuffed with ham – a unique and appealing dish you shouldn't miss. When you cut into the soft chicken, you'll find savory ham stuffed inside. Let's get started and show off your skills to enjoy this wonderful and creative flavor!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - seasoning powder, sugar, pepper, fish sauce.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients - Debone the chicken
After buying the chicken, rub the entire bird with a mixture of 1 tbsp sugar and 1 tsp salt.
Next, rinse the chicken with water and pat dry with a towel.
Place the chicken breast-side down, use a knife to carefully cut a straight line down the back skin. Then, use the tip of the knife to separate the skin on both sides from the meat.

When you reach the end of the thigh bone, use the knife to cut the tendons, then flip the skin back, keeping the knife between the bone and skin, moving around to separate them. This ensures the skin in this area doesn't tear.
Continue deboning the skin from areas where it sticks tightly to the bone, using the knife gently and slowly to separate the skin without tearing it.
For the wings, use the knife to expose the wing bone joint, then grasp each bone and pull firmly. Next, cut to separate the skin and bone.
After separating the skin from the meat, proceed to cut the lean meat away from the bones, taking care not to include any tendons.
Note:
Be very careful when deboning to avoid tearing the skin and ensure the dish looks good.
If you find it difficult to separate skin in areas with tendons or tight skin, use small nicks with the knife to make the process easier.
Step 2: Marinate the chicken meat
In a bowl, add 2 tbsp fish sauce, 4 tbsp cold water, 2 tbsp cooking oil, 2 tbsp tapioca starch, 2 tsp sugar, 1.5 tsp baking powder, and 2 tsp garlic powder.
Stir well to combine the seasonings. Depending on your taste, you can adjust the sugar, MSG, or seasoning powder.
Step 3: Grind and mix the chicken paste
Divide the chicken meat into 4 equal parts to grind them sequentially.

Place each part of the chicken into a blender, cover, and blend for 30 seconds. Then, transfer the ground chicken into the seasoning bowl. Once all the chicken is ground and in the bowl, mix well so the meat absorbs the seasonings evenly.
Next, divide the ground chicken mixture into 4 equal parts again and grind for a second time. After each grind, place the meat from the blender into a separate bowl.
Once the 4th part is ground and in the bowl, grease a spoon with oil and start mashing/spreading the meat about 50 times to create a bouncy texture.
Step 4: Stuff the chicken
For the ham (jambon), start by cutting it into slices approximately 1/3 the size of a palm thick.
Next, cut each slice into strips about twice as long as a palm's thickness and 1/3 of a palm wide.
Place the ground chicken mixture, raw pork paste, and ham into a large bowl, then use your hands (wearing gloves) to knead and combine these three ingredients.
Next, proceed to stuff the mixture into the chicken skin. It's best to stuff the wings and thighs first, then the rest of the body.
Finally, use a needle and thread to sew the chicken skin shut to keep the stuffing in shape.
Step 5: Steam the roll

Place the chicken in a steamer. Set the heat to medium and ensure the temperature inside the pot stays around 158°F (70°C). Steam the chicken for 2 hours 30 minutes to ensure it is cooked evenly from the outside in.
Afterward, place the chicken on a cutting board and use scissors or a knife to remove the thread. Then, slice the chicken into bite-sized pieces and prepare to serve.

The boneless chicken stuffed with ham, combined with the golden crispy skin, provides an attractive texture. The internal paste layer is finished with a firm texture and beautiful appearance, creating a unique and impressive combination.
When serving, just slice it like a traditional pork roll (giò).
And that's it, the delicious and attractive boneless chicken stuffed with ham is complete!
Although the deboning process is a bit elaborate and requires skill and meticulousness, you will have a wonderful dish for your family and guests during the Lunar New Year.
This dish is best enjoyed with pepper fish sauce, chili sauce, or pickled onions!
How to choose fresh raw pork paste
You should choose raw pork paste that is packaged securely, carefully, and airtight to ensure it is clean and safe from dust.
When buying packaged pork paste, pay attention to the expiration date and ensure the manufacturer is reputable. The paste inside should be a uniform light pink color with a smooth texture.
Avoid buying pork paste that shows visible meat fibers or fat chunks due to poor grinding. If there is an unusual odor, it may be a sign that the paste has expired and should not be used.

mon_an.ten: Five-Color Pork Roll for Kitchen Gods' Day
mon_an.mo_ta: Five-color pork roll is a very suitable dish for Lunar New Year or Kitchen Gods' Day meals. With its delicious flavor and eye-catching colors, it will make your family's meal tray much more attractive!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, sugar, fish sauce, pepper, seasoning powder - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients for the five-color roll
Wash the pork ear with wine and salt to reduce the odor.
Wash the pork belly with water.
Peel the carrot, wash, drain, and julienne into strips about 5-6 cm long.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms in hot water until expanded, wash, and mince.
Clean the green onions, removing roots and wilted leaves, then wash and mince.
Peel the shallots, wash, and mince.
Wash each banana leaf thoroughly and let them drain.
Step 2: Steps to make the five-color pork roll
First, boil the cleaned pork ear until cooked, let it cool, and slice thinly.
Boil the pork belly until cooked and slice thinly. When boiling the belly and ear, you can add a little seasoning salt and MSG for better flavor.
Next, crack the eggs into a bowl, add a little salt, pepper, and minced green onions, and whisk well. Then, fry the eggs into moderately thick sheets.

After that, put all the ground lean meat, pork ear, pork belly, wood ear mushrooms, carrots, and shallots into a large bowl. Add a little salt, pepper, 2 tbsp fish sauce, seasoning powder, and sugar, then mix everything well. Let it marinate for about 30 minutes so the ingredients absorb the seasonings. Remember to stir occasionally.
Separate the salted egg yolks, wash them thoroughly with wine, then steam for about 5 minutes and let them cool.
Start wrapping. Layer about 2-3 pieces of banana leaves on top of each other. Spread an egg sheet on top, then scoop the meat mixture onto it and spread it out evenly.
Finally, arrange the salted egg yolks on top, along the length of the leaf.
Carefully roll the egg sheet up, wrapping the meat filling tightly, then roll the banana leaves around it. Ensure you roll it very tightly, then secure with string.
Finally, fold the two ends of the banana leaves and tie them securely with string.
Next, boil the roll. Pour enough water to submerge the roll and boil for about 40-50 minutes until cooked. When done, remove and let it drain.
When serving, peel off the leaves and slice into rounds or small wedges like regular pork rolls.
Notes for a delicious five-color pork roll
If you want to check if the meat mixture is seasoned to your taste, you can cook a small bit in the oven/microwave and taste it.
You can steam or bake the salted egg yolks for about 5 minutes. If you don't like salted eggs, you can omit them, but you must wrap the roll very tightly.
You can divide the ingredients to make 2 smaller rolls.

mon_an.mo_ta: Discover the guide to making delicious head cheese, so you can enjoy it with your family on special holidays. These secrets and methods will help you show off your cooking skills and conquer the palate of every diner. Explore the recipe for head cheese in the article below! I. Traditional Delicious Head Cheese Recipe
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the ingredients
1 kg raw pork (Ear/ Snout/ Tongue/ Lean meat if you don't like fat)
5 shallots
1 ginger root
3 fresh lemon slices
100 gr wood ear mushrooms
100 gr shiitake mushrooms
Banana leaves as needed
A little cooking oil
2 tbsp premium fish sauce
1 tbsp sea salt
1 tsp black pepper
1 tsp sugar/seasoning powder
100 gr ice cubes
2. How to process head cheese
2.1. Prepare the ingredients
After buying the pork ear, snout, and tongue, rub them with 1 tbsp sea salt and wash thoroughly, removing any hair.

Boil water in a pot, add the meat along with some ginger and a few shallots to parboil. Shallots and ginger will help remove the meat's odor. When the meat is cooked through, remove it into a bowl of ice water and add a few lemon slices to make the meat white and crispy, then cut into small pieces.
Trim the roots of the wood ear mushrooms, soak them in cold water along with the shiitake mushrooms for about 15 minutes until soft. Then, wash and julienne for use.
2.2. Make the head cheese
First, marinate the sliced meat with pepper, sugar, seasoning powder (1 tsp each), and 2 tbsp good fish sauce. Let the meat absorb the seasonings for about 30 minutes.
Heat a pan, add a little cooking oil, and stir-fry the meat with the mushrooms over high heat, tossing constantly until cooked.
Line a mold with banana leaves, then gradually place the stir-fried meat into the mold, using the screw to press it down firmly.

Note: The tighter the roll is pressed, the more delicious and durable it will be. After pressing, let the roll cool outside. About 1 day later, remove from the mold and store in the refrigerator to enjoy gradually.
The roll can be stored in the refrigerator for about 1 week, depending on your storage method. When serving, cut into rounds and then into bite-sized pieces.
2.3. Completion

The head cheese and ear roll offer a crunchy texture from the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms, along with firm meat after being tightly pressed. When tasting, you will immediately feel the spicy and tingly flavor, fragrant and lingering on the tongue.
To fully enjoy the flavor, head cheese is often served with pickled mustard greens, pickled onions, and dipped in good fish sauce mixed with a little ground pepper or a few fresh chili slices.
II. Northern Style Stir-fried Pork Roll (Giò Xào)
200 gr pork leg meat
200 gr pork tongue
150 gr pork ear
150 gr pork snout
200 gr wood ear mushrooms
2 tbsp onion and garlic juice
1 tbsp crushed white peppercorns
1 kg banana leaves
Some string and plastic bags
2. Cooking steps

First, clean the hair on the ears and snout, then wash the pork leg meat thoroughly several times to ensure cleanliness, then drain. The tongue also needs to be washed, then soaked in boiling water mixed with a little white wine, then removed and washed again and drained.
Soak wood ear mushrooms in warm water until expanded, then drain and cut into small strips. Then, marinate the mushrooms with minced onion and garlic juice, ½ tsp seasoning powder, and 1 tsp pepper.
2.2. Boil the meat
Boil water in a large pot, add the meat and cook until about 80% done. Then, remove the meat and immediately soak in cold water to drain. Next, cut the meat into thin but uniform slices.
2.3. Stir-fry the meat

Start by heating a pan with 2 tbsp cooking oil. Add the meat to the pan and stir-fry for about 2 minutes. Then, season the pan with 1/2 tbsp salt, 1 tbsp ground pepper, 1 tbsp minced onion and garlic juice, 1 tbsp coarsely crushed pepper, 1 tbsp fish sauce, and 1/2 tbsp seasoning powder.
When the meat starts to firm up, add the wood ear mushrooms to the pan and stir-fry for another 3 minutes until the mushrooms are cooked. Once the mushrooms are thoroughly cooked, turn off the heat.
2.4. Wrap the head cheese
Place banana leaves on a tray, then put the meat into a plastic bag, wrap tightly, and tie firmly. Let the head cheese cool before placing it in the refrigerator to set.
When presenting for enjoyment, you can cut the head cheese into bite-sized pieces and serve with soy sauce or chili sauce for dipping.

The finished head cheese will have a pink color mixed with a bit of red from the set fat, interspersed with the brown of the mushrooms. When eating, the piece will bring a crunchy, sweet, rich flavor, fragrant with meat, mushrooms, and pepper.
Tips for success:
Characteristic of Northern cuisine, do not add sugar to the mixture when making head cheese.
Large pork ears are often old with hard cartilage. To make the head cheese more attractive with just the right crunch, choose medium-sized pork ears.
III. How to choose fresh ingredients
1. Pork head
To choose a fresh pork head, select one of moderate size, with bright pink bones and a characteristic aroma.
Avoid buying frozen pork heads, those with bruises on the skin, or unusual odors, as they may be old or spoiled.
2. Pork leg
When choosing pork leg, prioritize the front leg, as the meat here is usually softer and sweeter than the hind leg.
Good pork leg has firm muscle fibers, a light pink color, dry meat, and when pressed lightly, the meat will be slightly sticky and elastic.
Avoid choosing legs that are too large, pale in color, or have a foul odor, as these are signs of old meat that won't be sweet or fragrant.
3. Pork tongue
When choosing pork tongue, select pieces of moderate size, around 1.5kg, to ensure they are fragrant and tender when processed.
Fresh pork tongue usually has a bright red or pink color, and the part near the throat is a uniform white.
Avoid choosing tongues with strange smells, bruises, or ulcers on the surface, as these may be signs of a diseased pig.

mon_an.mo_ta: When mentioning chicken stew, we immediately think of a nutritious and healthy dish. Now, instead of the familiar chicken stew, we can vary it with some potatoes to make the dish less heavy. Let's go to the kitchen and make this nutritious chicken and potato stew for your whole family.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Soy sauce, cooking oil, seasoning powder, fish sauce - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1:

Wash the chicken thighs or wings with salt, chop into small bite-sized pieces, and place in a bowl to marinate with 1 tsp seasoning powder. Let it sit for 10 minutes to absorb the seasonings for a richer stew.
Peel the potatoes thoroughly and cut into 4cm square pieces.
Step 2:
Place a pan on the stove to heat, add cooking oil, and wait for it to boil. Then, add the chicken and fry until the meat firms up and turns golden.
Next, add the potatoes and briefly stir-fry with the chicken, adding more seasoning powder and fish sauce to make the dish more flavorful.
Step 3:
Add 1 large bowl of boiling water and smashed ginger to the pot with the chicken and potatoes. Once it boils, turn the heat to low and simmer for about 15 minutes.

By then, the dish will be tender and delicious. Before removing from the stove, drizzle 1 tbsp of soy sauce for fragrance and a beautiful golden color, then stir well. Finally, sprinkle chopped green onions on top for aroma and color.
What are you waiting for? Serve it in a bowl and eat while hot for the best taste!
Good luck and enjoy your meal!

mon_an.ten: Delicious Spicy Braised Chicken for Cold Days
mon_an.mo_ta: Spicy braised chicken is a very attractive dish because of the fresh, tender chicken simmered in a wonderful, flavorful sauce. When eating, each piece of chicken melts in the mouth, providing a mild spicy and delicious sensation. This dish is usually eaten with hot rice and is especially suitable for cold winter days.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients for the spicy braised chicken.
Wash the chicken thighs with cold water and drain.
Peel the potatoes and carrots, wash with water, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
Peel the onion, wash, and slice thinly.
Take the white part of the green onions, wash, and mince.
Step 2: Steps to make the spicy braised chicken.
To make the spicy braised chicken, first place a pot on the stove, fill it halfway with water, and boil over high heat.
When the water boils, drop the chicken thighs in to blanch for about 5-10 minutes to clean off impurities and reduce the odor.
When the meat looks slightly firm, remove the chicken and immediately rinse with cold water to keep the meat firm.

Next, take a bowl to mix the sauce. Add all the sauce ingredients: garlic, soy sauce, gochujang, liquid sweetener, salt, sesame oil, and pepper into the bowl and stir well until combined so the sauce is flavorful and not clumped.
After mixing the sauce, prepare a medium-sized pot on the stove and add a little cooking oil to heat.
When the oil is hot, add the potatoes and carrots and stir-fry briefly until firm.
When the potatoes and carrots are slightly firm, arrange the chicken thighs on top of them.
Next, pour the sauce mixture over the top, making sure to spread it evenly over the chicken.

Stir the mixture so the sauce incorporates into all ingredients, especially the chicken. Then, cover the pot tightly and turn the heat to high until it boils vigorously. Then, turn the heat down to low and cook until the potatoes and carrots are tender. You can check if they are cooked by using a chopstick to split a piece of potato or carrot. If it splits easily, they are done; otherwise, cook a bit longer.
Afterward, open the lid, add the onion to the pot, and cook for another 5 minutes before turning off the heat.
Finally, serve the chicken thighs along with the potatoes and carrots on a plate, drizzle the sauce over them, and sprinkle with chopped green onions.
Tips for a delicious spicy braised chicken
Besides chicken thighs, you can use other parts of the chicken for this dish, but thighs are the best choice.
If you cannot eat raw onions, you can add them to the pot while braising, stir well, then turn off the heat and serve with rice or bread.
If you cannot find liquid sweetener, you can substitute it with sugar, coconut caramel sauce, or a combination of sugar and oyster sauce to create a sweet replacement sauce.

mon_an.ten: Easy and Flavorful Fried Ribs with Garlic and Chili
mon_an.mo_ta: Fried ribs with garlic and chili are very easy to make with simple ingredients that you can buy at any market or supermarket. Below we will guide you through the simplest recipe so you can easily execute it.
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash and peel the garlic, then mince. Clean the green onions and chop finely. Wash and mince the chili (you can keep or remove the seeds depending on your family's spice preference).

Wash the ribs and drain, then cut into pieces about 5cm long. Mix with the seasoning mixture: fish sauce + pepper + sugar + seasoning powder. Let it sit for 15 minutes to let the meat absorb the flavors.
Step 2:
Coat the ribs evenly in tapioca starch or cornstarch so that when fried, they are golden and crispy without splattering oil.
Step 3:
Place a pan on the stove, add oil, and wait for it to heat up. Add the ribs and fry until they are light golden, then remove to a plate.

Place another pan on the stove, wait for the oil to heat up, then add the garlic and green onions and sauté until fragrant. Add the fried ribs back into the pan and toss quickly over medium heat. Adjust the seasoning to taste. Toss for about 3 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Step 4:
Serve the ribs on a plate and garnish as desired.
We hope this simple cooking guide will help you create an interesting new dish for your beloved family.

mon_an.mo_ta: Green peas are no longer strange to us in daily meals, but transforming them into a Tet jam (candied treat) to serve guests is wonderful! We invite you to make candied green peas according to the instructions below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 300g fresh or dried green peas (or canned)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the green peas and soak in diluted salt water for 30 minutes. After soaking, blanch the peas in boiling water and let them sit for 5 minutes.
Step 2: Remove the green peas and place them in a basket to drain.
Step 3: Next, place the peas in a suitable bowl and marinate with sugar for 2-3 hours so the sugar penetrates deep into the peas.

Step 4: After marinating, start cooking them into candy. Place the peas and the melted sugar mixture into a pan on the stove. When the sugar water boils, lower the heat to the minimum and stir continuously until the sugar crystallizes into powder (you can lift the pan above the flame and toss it so the sugar crystallizes faster and the peas dry quicker).

Step 5: The crystallized sugar coats each green pea, creating a delicious and nutritious candied green pea treat. Place the candied peas in a basket to dry completely, then store in an airtight glass jar.
Good luck and enjoy your candied green peas!

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried chayote with pork is a traditional Vietnamese dish that offers a harmonious combination of the natural sweetness of fresh chayote and the savory richness of pork. With a simple method and easy-to-find ingredients, you can make this delicious dish at home. Let's explore how to make this attractive stir-fried chayote with pork and enjoy this wonderful meal! This guide shows you how to make stir-fried chayote with pork at home, featuring the sweetness of chayote and the savory flavor of pork. A traditional Vietnamese dish that is easy to prepare and very appealing.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Shallots, green onions, cooking oil, seasonings - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Prepare the pork:
Wash the pork belly with water, then soak it in diluted salt water for 10 minutes. Rinse again with clean water, drain, and slice into bite-sized pieces.
Prepare other ingredients:
Celery: Remove the roots and wilted leaves, wash thoroughly, and cut into sections about 2 finger-lengths long.
Shallots and garlic: Peel, crush, and mince.
Carrot: Peel, wash, and cut into thin slices, then julienne.
Chayote: Peel, soak in a bowl of water to avoid sap stickiness. Rinse with clean water, drain, and cut into slices, then julienne.
Step 2: Cooking
Stir-fry the pork:
First, place a pan on the stove over medium heat. Add 2 tbsp of cooking oil and heat it up. When the oil is hot, add the minced shallots and garlic and sauté until fragrant.

Once the shallots and garlic are golden brown, remove them to a small bowl, keeping the oil in the pan. Next, add the pork belly to the pan and stir-fry for about 5 minutes until the meat is firm and the skin starts to crackle.
Add the chayote and carrots to the pan and stir-fry together. Season with 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp MSG, 1/3 tsp pepper, and 1 tsp oyster sauce. Stir-fry well for about 10 minutes.
When the chayote and carrots are cooked, adjust the seasoning to taste. Add the celery to the pan and stir-fry for about 30 seconds, then turn off the heat.
Presentation:

Arrange the stir-fried chayote on a plate and sprinkle the fried shallots and garlic on top. Add a bit of pepper to enhance the flavor. The stir-fried chayote with pork belly will have eye-catching colors, with a balance between the fresh green of the chayote and the reddish-orange of the carrots. The pork belly is delicious and flavorful.
Enjoy:
It is best enjoyed with hot steamed rice. You can also choose this as a side dish for a party with friends. To enhance the flavor, you can prepare a small bowl of chili garlic soy sauce for dipping.

mon_an.ten: Fried Pork Ribs with Lemongrass and Chili
mon_an.mo_ta: Discover fried pork ribs with lemongrass and chili – an exciting alternative to traditional sweet and sour ribs. This dish is especially good for finishing off a whole pot of rice. If you're wondering what to eat today, try this simple recipe to create these "divine" fried pork ribs. Explore how to make delicious fried pork ribs with lemongrass and chili to create an attractive, flavorful, and rice-consuming dish. Start with detailed instructions and simple steps to perform this dish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Tools - Pot, pan, cutting board, Inomata container, super sharp knife
Seasonings - Cooking oil, sesame oil, oyster sauce, sugar, salt, seasoning powder, fish sauce, chili sauce, tomato paste
Other ingredients - Minced lemongrass, minced shallots, minced garlic, minced chili
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pork ribs
Wash the pork ribs with diluted salt water.
Boil 1 liter of water and add 1/4 tbsp salt, 20g ginger, and 20g shallots.
Blanch the pork ribs in boiling water to clean them and remove any odors.
Step 2: Fry the pork ribs
When the water boils again, remove the ribs and rinse them with water, then drain.
Coat the ribs with a thin layer of crispy frying flour on all sides.
Fry the ribs in hot oil until they are golden and crispy.
Remove the ribs and drain the excess oil.
Step 3: Sauté the ribs
In a pan, add 2 tbsp cooking oil and sauté 2 tbsp minced garlic and shallots with 3 tbsp minced lemongrass until golden and fragrant.

Next, add 1/2 tbsp seasoning powder, 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1/2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp chili sauce, 1 tbsp tomato paste, and 1/2 tbsp sesame oil to the pan. Stir well to combine the seasonings.
Then, pour 300ml of fresh coconut water into the pan and bring to a boil. When the water boils, add the fried pork ribs and toss well so the ribs are evenly coated with the sauce.
Cook the ribs for 30 minutes. Finally, add 1 tbsp minced lemongrass and 1 tbsp minced chili to enhance the aroma of the dish.
Wait for the ribs to absorb the seasonings and become fragrant, then it's finished.
Finished Product

The marinated fried ribs with lemongrass and chili are attractive with the characteristic aroma of lemongrass. Each crispy rib is bursting with sweet and salty flavors and a hint of heat from the lemongrass and chili, combined with the rich taste of coconut water to create an exciting experience. Just one bite and you won't be able to resist.
III. Notes when making fried pork ribs with lemongrass and chili
Tips for choosing fresh pork ribs: Fresh pork ribs have light pink meat, good elasticity, and no strange or foul odors.
Choose ribs with small, flat bones, as these have more meat and fewer bones than ribs with large, round bones.
Additionally, to ensure family health, use tools like Inomata containers, manufactured by a genuine Japanese brand, during the ingredient preparation process.
IV. How to choose fresh pork ribs
For a better dish, choose young pork ribs with little fat and plenty of lean meat, or pork chops.
When buying pork ribs at traditional markets, go early in the morning for more fresh options.
Choose rib pieces that are light pink and elastic when pressed. Avoid ribs that are dark or pale, feel slimy to the touch, or have a foul smell.

Choose flat and small ribs, as they usually have more meat. However, do not choose ribs that are too small, as this may indicate the pig was underweight, the meat won't be as good, and health standards might not be guaranteed.

A tip to make the dish tastier: when frying the ribs, use low heat so the meat absorbs the seasonings evenly. When the ribs are cooked and evenly golden, turn off the heat and remove them. This helps reduce oil absorption compared to turning off the heat before the ribs are fully cooked due to sudden temperature changes.

When frying, ensure the ribs are light golden (you can test by lightly piercing with a spoon; the meat should no longer be red and just cooked through). This helps the ribs stay tender and more delicious.

mon_an.ten: Stewed Pork Ribs in Black Bean Sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: As the name suggests, the main ingredients for this dish are pork ribs and black beans. The method is extremely simple, making it a wonderful dish to treat the whole family for a late-day meal!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - 60ml soy sauce, 60ml dark soy sauce, 45ml oyster sauce
cac_buoc: Step 1:
First, combine the sake, black bean sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, and soy sauce, then stir well.
Step 2:
Add a bowl of warm water to create the stewing sauce for the ribs.
Step 3:
In a pan with hot oil, lightly fry the ribs until they are browned on both sides.
Step 4:
Using the same pan used to fry the ribs, add 2 tbsp of cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add the crushed garlic, green onions, and ground chili and sauté until fragrant.
Step 5:
Next, pour in the prepared sauce mixture. Cover and simmer over low heat until the sauce just begins to boil.
Step 6:
When the sauce starts bubbling, add the fried ribs, cover, and stew for about 1-2 hours.
Step 7:
After 2 hours of stewing, your ribs will look like this!
When eating, place the ribs on a plate and drizzle the stewing sauce over the top.

mon_an.mo_ta: Five-color braised pork ribs is an attractive dish that appeals to diners not only because of its colors but also its delicious flavor, with savory ribs blended with the aroma of spices. Let's get into the kitchen and make this delicious dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fresh chili, ginger, garlic, green onions - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the ribs and marinate them with salt, pepper, and soy sauce for about 15-20 minutes so the ribs absorb the seasonings and won't be bland when eaten.
Step 2: Next, place a pan on the stove. Sauté the garlic, then add the ribs and stir well until the ribs are cooked and turn slightly brown.
Step 3: Then, add enough water to just cover the meat, add soy sauce and caramel sauce, then cover and simmer for about 20 minutes until the sauce reduces and thickens.
Step 4: In this step, wash the onion, garlic, and peppers, then dice the onion, garlic, and peppers into bite-sized pieces.
In another pan, sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant, then add the two types of bell peppers and fresh chili.

Step 5: Finally, stir well until the ingredients are fully cooked, then add both the ribs and the sauce. Toss well so the ingredients are evenly mixed and coated in sauce, then turn off the heat. Before serving, you can add a bit of black pepper to enhance the flavor.
Note:
Before frying the ribs, you should marinate them for at least 15 minutes so they absorb the seasonings; otherwise, the ribs will be very bland and lack flavor.
When frying the ribs, remember to flip all sides so they cook evenly and have a beautiful exterior without burning.
This rib dish is very suitable to eat with hot rice, especially during winter.

The finished five-color braised ribs have eye-catching colors from the green of the vegetables, the bright red or yellow of the bell peppers, the purple of the onion, and the golden brown of the fresh ribs. The dish is attractive and flavorful without being greasy. Make this delicious dish to treat your family and friends!
How to choose and store ribs:

For dishes like sweet and sour stir-fry, braising, or frying... you should choose lean ribs with little or no fat. Ribs with cartilage (young ribs) are very delicious. For these dishes, loin ribs are the best choice.
For soups, porridge, or noodle dishes: choose ribs with both lean meat and fat so they are tender, fragrant, and rich when eaten.
For pork chops (cốt lết), choose pieces with thick loin and little fat for tender and delicious meat. Pork chops are best for grilling, frying, roasting, simmering, or smoking.
You should go to the market early to buy the freshest and most delicious pork ribs. Going late often means the good pieces are sold out, or the ribs might become stale due to the weather.

Additionally, note that you should buy ribs (or other fresh ingredients) last after buying vegetables and fruits to minimize the time the ribs are kept in plastic bags, as they can become stale and harmful substances from the bag can seep into the meat.
When you bring the ribs home, take them out of the bag and cook them immediately. If not, wash them, put them in an airtight container or zipper bag, and store them in the refrigerator.

mon_an.mo_ta: This Tet, let's learn how to make pork belly soaked in vinegar to treat your family and guests! The dish is very easy to make and absolutely delicious!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: A few star anise, a few coriander seeds.
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Keep the ginger skin on and slice it. - Roast the ginger, star anise, and coriander seeds until slightly charred and fragrant.
Step 2:
Place the ginger, star anise, and coriander seeds into a non-absorbent paper bag or a phở spice infuser. Tie the mouth of the bag with thread.
Step 3:
Wash the pork belly, rub salt onto the meat, let it sit for about 15 minutes, then rinse thoroughly.
Step 4:
Place the meat in a pot of water, bring to a boil, and blanch for about 3 minutes to firm up the skin.
Step 5:

Place the meat in a pot, add the spice bag, season with a teaspoon of salt, and boil for about 20-25 minutes depending on the size of the meat. Turn off the heat and cover tightly to let the meat finish cooking.
Step 6:

Dissolve sugar in filtered water and bring to a boil to melt the sugar. Once cooled, add vinegar and fish sauce. Season for a sweet and sour, salty taste, using a ratio of 1 part water : 1 part sugar : 2 parts vinegar : 1 part fish sauce. You can adjust the amount of vinegar to your preference.
Step 7:

Once the meat has cooled, remove it and place it in a clean glass jar. Pour in the prepared vinegar mixture, add whole chilies and some peeled garlic cloves. Store in a cool place for about 3-4 days before use.
Step 8:
After the meat has marinated, use scissors to cut the thread, use a knife to slice into thin bite-sized pieces, and serve with fresh herbs, rice vermicelli, and rice paper rolls, or eat with rice.
It's so easy to have a delicious pork belly soaked in vinegar dish to treat your family and guests this Tet!

mon_an.mo_ta: Instructions for making a delicious, simple stir-fried beef with bean sprouts dish suitable for family meals. This dish not only brings great flavor but is also easy to make and saves cooking time. The article below provides a detailed recipe for you to make stir-fried beef with bean sprouts at home. Stir-fried beef with bean sprouts - A delicious dish with rich flavors. Fragrant, tender beef combined with fresh bean sprouts creates a nutritious and ideal meal. Discover the recipe and method for delicious stir-fried beef with bean sprouts at home!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - Sugar, MSG, salt, seasoning powder
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the meat
Soak the beef: Soak the beef in diluted salt water for about 10 minutes to clean and deodorize it. Then, remove the meat and rinse several times with water until the odor is gone, then drain.
Cut the meat: To make the beef easy to stir-fry and tender, cut the beef across the grain into thin bite-sized slices.
Here are ways to prepare beef for stir-frying with bean sprouts to ensure it is clean and odorless:
Method 1: Use ginger: Roast a small knob of ginger, then scrape off the outer skin and crush it. Rub it all over the beef, then rinse with water.
Method 2: Use white wine: Soak the beef in white wine for about 15 minutes, then rinse under cold water.
Method 3: Use boiling water: Bring a pot of water to a boil, then blanch the beef for about 3 minutes. Remove and rinse under cold water.
Method 4: Use shallots: Roast a shallot until dry, then peel and crush it. Marinate this shallot with the beef.
2. Prepare other ingredients
Green onions: Wash the green onions and slice them thinly.
Garlic: Peel the garlic, crush, and mince.
Shallots: Peel the shallots and mince them.
Chili: Take 2 chilies and slice them to make dipping sauce; keep the remaining 3 whole for stir-frying.
Bean sprouts: Wash the bean sprouts and drain.
3. Marinate the meat

Marinate the beef: Place the beef on a plate, then add 2 tsp MSG, 1 tsp seasoning powder, 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, and 1 tbsp fish sauce. Use a spoon to mix well so the meat absorbs the seasonings. Marinate for about 10 - 15 minutes.
4. Stir-fry beef with bean sprouts

Add 1 tbsp cooking oil, minced garlic, and shallots to a pan. Sauté until fragrant, then add the marinated beef to the pan. Stir-fry for about 5 minutes over medium heat until the beef is about 80% cooked, then remove to a plate.

Turn on the heat and add 1 tbsp cooking oil and the bean sprouts to the pan. Stir-fry for about 2 minutes over medium heat until the bean sprouts slightly wilt. Then, add 1/2 tsp MSG, 1/3 tsp seasoning powder, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tbsp sugar, and 1/2 tbsp fish sauce to the pan. Lower the heat and add the beef back in, tossing for about 3 minutes until the sprouts are cooked. Next, add the 3 whole chilies and green onions, then turn off the heat.
Prepare the dipping sauce: Place the 2 sliced chilies and 3 tbsp soy sauce in a small bowl, mix well to have a delicious dipping sauce ready to serve.

When finished, the stir-fried beef with bean sprouts will have a savory, delicious flavor and the natural sweetness of the beef, combined with the tender and easy-to-eat bean sprouts. This is truly a wonderful nutritious stir-fry for the whole family to enjoy!
How to choose fresh beef
1. How to buy fresh beef
Color: Fresh beef is usually bright red, possibly with some light pink patches. Avoid buying meat that is gray, brown, or shows signs of spoilage.
Check fat and tendons: Fresh beef usually has white, even fat, without yellow patches or strange colors. Tendons should also be white or slightly translucent.
Check the smell: The smell of beef must be fresh and characteristic, without any foul odor. If you sense an unpleasant or strange smell, the meat may be spoiled.
Check elasticity: Fresh beef usually has good elasticity. When pressing the meat with a finger, it should feel sticky and return to its original shape quickly.
Hopefully, this information helps you choose fresh and safe beef for your meals.
2. How to buy bean sprouts
Clean bean sprouts usually have many long roots and inconsistent sizes, often being elongated with curved stems. The surface of the sprouts should not be shiny.
Avoid buying sprouts with unusual lengths or stems that are too large and round, as well as short roots. These types of sprouts may have been soaked in chemicals.
By following these criteria, you can find clean and safe bean sprouts to use in your dishes.

mon_an.mo_ta: Instead of the familiar boiled chicken, transforming it into jellied chicken will surely delight your whole family with this new dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 15g gelatin powder (available at baking supply stores)
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Soak the mushrooms in warm water for 10 minutes, then rinse thoroughly. Peel the carrots and cut them into flower shapes for a nice presentation.
Step 2:
Chop the chicken into bite-sized pieces, then rinse with salt water and drain. Place the meat in a pot and marinate with 4 tbsp seasoning powder; let it sit for 10 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Step 3:
Pour 2l of water into the pot with the chicken and place on the stove over high heat. During cooking, remember to skim the foam frequently so the broth doesn't become cloudy.
Step 4:
Place a pan on the stove, add 1 tbsp cooking oil, and lightly sauté the mushrooms. This step is to remove the pungent smell of the mushrooms.
Add the mushrooms and carrots to the chicken pot. At this stage, the water has started to reduce, so cook over low heat. Cook for another 20 minutes.
Step 5:

After 20 minutes, place 15g of gelatin in a bowl, add 2 tbsp of the hot chicken broth, and mix well until the gelatin dissolves. Pour the gelatin into the meat pot, turn off the heat, and stir well with a spoon.
Step 6:
Ladle the chicken into individual bowls, let cool, and place in the refrigerator to use gradually during Tet.
Unlike jellied pork which sets from fat, jellied chicken made with gelatin helps reduce cholesterol significantly!
This style of making jellied meat is very suitable for girls who want to lose weight but still want to eat well during this Tet holiday.
When eating, serve the jellied chicken on a plate, add some pickled mustard greens and a bowl of soy sauce; it's extremely good with hot rice!

mon_an.mo_ta: Coconut fried shrimp attracts diners not only with its appealing color but also with the savory taste of the shrimp, the richness of the coconut, and a bit of crispiness and chewiness that creates an irresistible dish. Today we will guide you on how to make this delicious dish!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the shrimp and remove the vein, then add a little salt, pepper, and wine. Let it marinate for 15 minutes to absorb the seasonings and reduce the fishy smell.
Step 2: Wash the broccoli and cut into small florets. Blanch in boiling water for about 2 minutes until the broccoli is tender.
Step 3: Roll the shrimp in breadcrumbs and cornstarch, then place in a pan of hot oil and fry over medium heat for about 2-3 minutes. When the outer crust turns golden, remove them.
Step 4: Place the shrimp on paper towels to drain the oil.
Step 5: Add coconut milk and sugar to a pan, stir constantly over medium heat until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Step 6: Finally, add the shrimp and mayonnaise to the pan, toss gently for a few minutes so the shrimp is coated in the sauce.

mon_an.ten: How to Boil Pork to be Tender and Sweet
mon_an.mo_ta: Boiled pork is a common dish in every family, but not every cook knows how to boil pork to be delicious and crispy. Let's get into the kitchen and learn how to boil pork perfectly!
cac_buoc: Place the meat in a pot and pour in enough cold water to cover the meat by 2-3 cm. Bring to a boil over high heat for 1 minute, then remove. Discard this first boiling water, wash the meat and the pot, then add the meat and fresh water and bring to a boil again.

Turn the heat to high to boil the water, then drop sliced shallots into the pot. Then, sequentially add 1 tsp seasoning salt, ½ tsp MSG, and ½ tsp sugar to the boiling pot. Lower the heat to a simmer.
The boiling time depends on whether your piece of meat is small or large.
Some mistakes that make boiled pork less delicious
1. Not pre-processing the meat
Many people have the habit of boiling meat without performing pre-processing steps. However, this can cause the meat to cook unevenly, with the outside soft while the inside is still red.

To ensure the boiled meat is evenly cooked, perform these pre-processing steps. Before boiling, scrape off the hair on the skin and wash thoroughly. Then, use lemon and sea salt to rub onto the meat and rinse again. Lemon and salt not only help deodorize effectively but also provide citric acid and vitamin C, making the meat more fragrant and fresher.
By correctly performing the pre-processing steps before boiling, you will ensure the meat is evenly cooked, preserving the flavor and quality of the food.
Choosing the pork cut and appropriate boiling method

Each dish requires choosing the right pork cut. For boiled pork, you should choose the lower belly (interwoven lean and fat, soft and connected) or pork leg, or crispy shoulder meat with interwoven lean and fat to enhance the flavor.

If using lean meat (tenderloin) for boiling, soak the meat beforehand in a diluted salt and sugar solution at a 4-5% ratio (500 ml water mixed with 20-25g salt and 20-25g sugar). Then, wash the meat before starting the boiling process.
This method is called brine liquid and is often used by Western chefs when boiling chicken breast. This method helps the meat retain moisture, making it tender, sweet, and not dry.
By choosing the right pork cut and applying the brine liquid method, you will have delicious, tender, and flavorful boiled pork.
2. Boiling meat starting with cold water

Instead of putting meat in a pot with cold water from the start and turning on the stove, many cooks should apply the method of adding meat when the water is boiling. When the water is boiling, the skin and outer muscle fibers will contract, keeping the protein inside from escaping, helping the boiled meat be naturally sweeter.

After adding the meat to boiling water, lower the heat and boil until just cooked, usually taking about 15 minutes. You can test by piercing the meat; if no pink juice flows out, the meat is evenly cooked. Then, turn off the stove and cover the lid to soak the meat in the water, which helps the meat absorb water and become juicier.

By following these steps, you will have sweet, tender boiled meat without it being red inside or having dark skin, and the meat fibers will not be dry. This is the secret to enjoying boiled meat with great flavor and high quality.
3. Adding cold water while boiling on high heat

Some people often turn up the heat and add cold water while boiling to make the meat cook faster. However, they don't realize that high temperatures cook the outside while the inside remains red. Furthermore, the rapid evaporation of water in the pot reduces the amount of broth, so they add cold water to continue boiling.

According to nutritionists, meat and bones contain a lot of protein and fat. When cold water is added during the boiling process, the sudden drop in temperature causes protein and fat to precipitate. This leads to the meat's pores contracting, creating conditions for bacteria to attack and reducing the natural sweet flavor of the meat.
4. Boiling meat for too long

Some people also have the habit of boiling meat for too long and too thoroughly, intending to make the meat completely cooked and no longer red inside. However, this causes the dish to become dry and bland. Furthermore, according to health experts, when meat is boiled for too long, the nutrients in the meat escape into the broth and the protein is destroyed. Some substances even have the potential to become toxic, affecting the flavor of the dish and not being good for health.
To ensure the best quality and flavor for boiled meat, follow proper boiling methods and avoid the above habits.
How to choose delicious pork
Regarding color

To ensure quality, choose fresh pork pieces with bright colors. Good meat is usually light pink or light red, and the fat will be white or slightly ivory. When cutting vertically with a knife, the meat will be slightly firm, the surface will be dry, and the skin will be soft. These are signs of fresh meat.
Avoid choosing meat with strange, pale, or too dark colors. If the meat surface is glossy and feels slightly slimy to the touch, absolutely do not buy it.
Regarding smell
Good meat will have a characteristic pork aroma that is not unpleasant. This meat smell does not have a fishy or pungent odor.
If the meat already has a strange, fishy, or foul smell, it is a sign that the meat is spoiled and should not be used.
Choose meat with a characteristic aroma, without strange or foul odors, to ensure the best quality and flavor for the dish.
Regarding elasticity

To check elasticity, you can press your hand into the meat. If the meat has good elasticity, after withdrawing your hand, the meat will return to its original shape without a depression. This is a sign of fresh meat. When touched, the meat fibers will be firm, not too hard nor mushy, and no slimy fluid will flow out.
Regarding the fat and skin layer

Pigs raised under normal conditions will have a fat layer about 1.5 – 2 finger-lengths thick. You can easily observe the thick fat and skin layer as a simple characteristic to identify pork that hasn't been force-fed for weight.
Choose pork pieces with distinct structures between meat and fat, but still firmly attached to each other. When touched, you should find it difficult to separate the meat and fat.
Avoid choosing pieces where the fat and lean meat are detached. When touched, if yellow fluid flows out, it is a sign the pig was raised with lean-meat agents and should not be bought.
Some tips to help boil pork white and not dry
Boiling meat to be white
Method 1:
Before boiling the meat, blanch it in a mixture of water, vinegar, and salt for about 3 minutes. Then, rinse the meat with clean water.
Next, boil the meat in cold water until tender.
Method 2:
When the meat is cooked, add 2 tsp of vinegar or white wine to the pot.
Turn off the stove and leave the meat in the pot for about 1 – 2 minutes, then remove.
Soak the meat in a bowl of ice water for about 15 – 20 minutes to make the meat firm and prevent it from darkening.
Boiling white meat without it being dry
To avoid the meat becoming dry after boiling, there are some points to note:
Ensure not to boil the meat too thoroughly, letting the juices inside escape.
Check the boiling time by piercing the meat with a chopstick. If the chopstick pierces through easily, the meat is cooked.
If the juice from the meat is still pink, cook for another 5 minutes and check again.
With these ways of boiling white meat, you will have tender, delicious meat that is not dry. Adjust the boiling time to suit the amount and size of the meat pieces.

mon_an.mo_ta: Making a delicious jar of pickled shallots is not difficult; you just need to choose even, good shallots and have the best pickling method to own a delicious jar for this Tet! Let's learn how to make this delicious dish! "Fatty meat, pickled shallots, red couplets / Neu tree, firecrackers, green banh chung." Pickled shallots are an indispensable dish during the traditional Tet holiday of the Vietnamese people, used as an accompaniment to bánh chưng or rich, high-protein dishes. The mild sourness, slight spiciness, and aroma of pickled shallots help enhance the flavor of other dishes and stimulate better digestion. Choosing ingredients is a very important step; to have a delicious jar, you should choose white shallots, which will be more fragrant and less pungent, and take less time to ripen than purple shallots.
cac_buoc: Step 1: After buying the shallots, peel off the dirty brown outer skin, cut the roots, and soak in rice water mixed with a little salt overnight.
Step 2: Discard the rice water and soak the shallots again in salt water (slightly salty) for 1 day to make them crispy and white.
Step 3: Rinse the shallots thoroughly with diluted salt water and drain before putting them into the pickling jar.
Step 4: Peel the sugar cane, split into 4, cut into short pieces about half a finger long, and place at the bottom of the glass jar or ceramic crock.

Step 5: Prepare a slightly strong salt water solution, you can add vinegar. Arrange the shallots in the jar or crock, pour the salt water to cover them, then use a clean ceramic plate to press down on the shallots so they don't float above the water. Use a clean, heavy object to place on the plate to compress the pickled shallots.

Step 6: Store in a cool place. When eating, use clean chopsticks to take the shallots out, rinse with cooled boiled water or diluted salt water, then peel off the old outer layer to get the white, tender part of the pickled shallot to eat.

Note: The above pickling recipe only applies when you want to keep the shallots for a long time, making them sour and removing the spiciness and pungency. To have pickled shallots ready for Tet with the current cold weather, you should pickle them 1 month or more in advance.
How to choose fresh shallots
Choose shallots with a beautiful green outer skin, not wilted, cracked, or showing signs of rot. The outer skin should be smooth and without black spots.
