Get close to the shallots and smell their aroma. Fresh shallots usually have a fresh, light, and characteristic scent. Avoid choosing shallots with an unpleasant smell or signs of spoilage.
When touching the shallots, they should feel firm and not overly soft. Moderate hardness indicates fresh and good shallots.
Check the cut part of the shallot. If this part has a bright color, without signs of being dry or wilted, then that shallot is fresh and of good quality.
If possible, buy shallots from reputable stores, local markets, or trustworthy gardens. This helps ensure the shallots were harvested and stored correctly.
Usually, fresh and delicious shallots are available in spring and summer. Therefore, choose to buy shallots during this time to ensure the best quality and flavor.
Notes on making and storing pickled shallots
1. Notes when pickling shallots

To make delicious pickled shallots, you need to adjust the amount of salt and sugar just right. If the ratio is incorrect, the shallots cannot ferment. If there is too much salt or sugar, the shallots will become too salty or too sweet and hard to eat.
Using warm salt water for pickling will help the fermentation process happen faster. Additionally, you can place the jar of pickled shallots under sunlight to speed up fermentation.
To avoid white foam forming during fermentation, ensure the glass jar has been sterilized and dried before pouring the brine in. This helps prevent white foam from appearing on the pickled shallots.
To ensure the shallots ferment evenly, you can use a plastic grate (or bamboo sticks) placed on top of the shallots to ensure they are submerged evenly in the brine.
When enjoying pickled shallots, use clean tools to take them out, and avoid stirring too much as this can quickly create a white film, spoiling the shallots.
2. Storage
If you don't use them all, you can keep the jar of pickled shallots in the refrigerator to slow down the fermentation process.
To store pickled shallots, after completion, you can keep them in a cool place and use them within 5 – 7 days. If kept in the refrigerator, pickled shallots can be stored for about 1 month.
When enjoying pickled shallots, use clean tools to take them out and avoid stirring much; this ensures the long-term preservation of the pickled shallots.

mon_an.ten: Homemade Mixed Vegetable and Pork Rib Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Mixed vegetable and pork rib soup is a delicious traditional dish, bringing together the rich flavors of young ribs and various vegetables. This is a staple of Vietnamese cuisine, known for being both savory and nutritious. Want to enjoy a perfect bowl of soup at home? Let us guide you through this simple and tasty recipe. Discover how to cook this flavorful mixed vegetable and pork rib soup at home with detailed instructions on preparation, seasoning, and the simmering process. Enjoy this traditional, flavor-packed soup with your family every day.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the pork ribs and place them in a pot, covering them with water. When the water begins to simmer and foam rises, reduce the heat to low and skim the foam for about 10 minutes until the broth is clear and sweet without any odors. (Washing the ribs beforehand also helps remove odors). Sauté the ribs with fish sauce to absorb the flavor, then add water to the pot. The longer you simmer on low heat, the sweeter the broth will be.
Step 2: Soak the shiitake mushrooms until soft, trim the stems, and add them to the pot for aroma and flavor.
Step 3: Peel the carrots, potatoes, and chayote; cut the broccoli into bite-sized pieces.
Step 4: Once the broth is flavorful, season with salt and seasoning powder to taste. Add the potatoes first, followed by the carrots after a while, and then the chayote. Cover and cook for a bit.
Step 5: When the potatoes are almost cooked, add the broccoli and cook for 2 to 3 minutes. Turn off the heat and ladle into a bowl to serve hot.
How to choose fresh ingredients for mixed vegetable and pork rib soup
To select fresh ingredients for this soup, keep these important notes in mind:
Ribs: Choose young ribs with a bright pink color, elastic meat, and no unpleasant odor. If possible, choose ribs with some white fat, as it adds flavor and richness to the soup.

Vegetables: Choose fresh vegetables that are not wilted, bruised, or showing signs of decay. Carrots should be bright in color, potatoes should have no dark spots, and mushrooms should be free of mold.
Aromatics: Choose fresh shallots, garlic, and ginger that are not wilted, dried out, or sprouted.
Fresh herbs: If you want to add fresh herbs to the soup, choose bright green, unwilted leaves. Wash them thoroughly before use.
Seasonings: Choose high-quality salt, sugar, and fish sauce with no strange odors.
Purchase ingredients from reliable sources such as local markets, grocery stores, or farms to ensure the freshness and safety of your soup.

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Luffa with Chicken Giblets and Bean Sprouts
mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried luffa with chicken giblets is a familiar dish in Vietnamese family meals. This dish is popular because it is simple to prepare, uses easy-to-find ingredients, and tastes delicious, catering to many people's palates. Let's get into the kitchen to make this tasty dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Shallots, green onions, cooking oil - ingredients
Fish sauce, seasoning powder, MSG, pepper - seasonings
cac_buoc: Peel the fragrant luffa, wash, and slice into bite-sized pieces about 2cm thick.
Clean the chicken giblets thoroughly by rubbing them with salt and vinegar to remove odors and slime, then slice thinly.
Wash the bean sprouts and drain well.
Peel and mince the shallots.
Trim the roots of the green onions, wash, and cut into 3cm lengths.

Heat oil in a pan. Once hot, sauté the minced shallots until fragrant. Add the chicken giblets and a bit of seasoning powder, stir-frying until cooked. Next, add the bean sprouts and luffa, stirring constantly so they cook evenly. Season to taste. When the luffa and sprouts are cooked, add the green onions, toss, and turn off the heat.
Transfer the stir-fried luffa and chicken giblets to a plate, sprinkle with a bit of pepper, and garnish as desired.

mon_an.mo_ta: Learn how to cook this delicious and comforting Vietnamese braised pork, perfect for a cozy dinner on chilly days.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Pork - 500g (choose pork belly for a soft and fragrant result)
cac_buoc: Prepare the meat: Clean the pork, blanch it briefly in boiling water, then remove and cut into square pieces. Marinate with crushed and minced shallots, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 tsp seasoning powder for about 15 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Make the caramel sauce: Heat a little oil in a pan, add about 3 tbsp sugar, and cook until the sugar melts and turns an amber color. Add a little water and stir until the caramel is fully dissolved.
Braise the pork: Add the marinated meat to the pan, pour in enough water to just cover the surface, and bring to a boil. Reduce to low heat and simmer until the meat is tender.

After about 30 minutes, the liquid will gradually reduce and thicken, and the meat will turn a beautiful amber brown. Season again to taste (add sugar, fish sauce, or salt if needed), then sprinkle with black pepper and green onions (optional) and turn off the heat. Serve on a plate and enjoy hot with steamed rice or sticky rice.
Here is the final braised pork dish. It looks delicious, doesn't it?

I prefer using pork belly for this dish as it becomes soft, fragrant, and rich without being too greasy or dry. You should choose lower pork belly with thin skin, a thin fat layer, and plenty of meat where the layers are well-attached. However, if you don't like fat, you can switch to pork rump.

mon_an.ten: Northern-style Combination Dried Pig Skin Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Combination dried pig skin soup is a signature dish of Northern Vietnam, traditionally served at weddings, family gatherings, and especially during the Lunar New Year (Tet). The soup is visually stunning with the red of carrots, green of broccoli and peas, translucent white of dried pig skin, deep brown of shiitake mushrooms, and yellow of fish cakes. However, it is the delicate, sweet broth that makes this dish unforgettable. With Tet approaching, let's cook this traditional soup for the whole family. This recipe combines meat, seafood, and fresh vegetables for an authentic flavor.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Dried pig skin and other supplementary meats. Quantities are approximate at 100g each; adjust as needed.
Pork meatballs (mọc) - 100g (you can buy raw pork paste, mix with minced wood ear mushrooms, and stuff into shiitake mushrooms)
Rice wine - 1 cup (to deodorize the pig skin)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the broth.

Bring water to a boil, blanch the bones, then rinse with cold water. Wash 1/2 piece of ginger, keep the skin on, char it until golden, and crush it. Add the ginger to the pot with the bones and water to simmer for the broth. Remember to skim the foam while cooking to keep the broth clear.
Step 2: Prepare the ingredients
While the broth is simmering, prepare the other ingredients as follows.
Soak the dried pig skin in rice water until it expands and turns white. Rub it with ginger, rice wine, and salt to remove any odors, then rinse with ginger water. Drain well.

Peel and devein the shrimp, then butterfly them or grind into a paste. Season and stuff the shrimp paste into shiitake mushrooms to make meatballs. Clean the chicken and pork heart, slice thinly, and marinate with salt, pepper, shallots, and minced garlic. Sauté all these ingredients with the pig skin until just cooked through.

Wash the vegetables, carve them into flowers or cut into bite-sized pieces. Blanch them in boiling water and immediately shock them in cold water to preserve their green color. Whisk the egg, fry it into a thin sheet, and shred it. Soak the shiitake mushrooms until soft and clean them.
Step 3: Cook the soup

Once the ingredients and broth are ready, add each type of vegetable to the broth first. Cook until just tender, then remove and set aside. Next, cook the meats, shrimp, and heart one by one until just done, then remove and set aside for a beautiful presentation. Season the broth to taste, add green onions and coriander, then turn off the heat.
Step 4: Presentation

Take a bowl and layer the meat and vegetables at the bottom. Place a layer of dried pig skin on top and garnish with the other ingredients for a colorful look: red carrots, green broccoli and peas, pink shrimp, yellow fish cakes, and brown mushrooms. If serving immediately, pour the hot broth from Step 3 into the bowl. If not serving right away, arrange the ingredients in the bowl and pour boiling broth over them just before eating. Garnish with more green onions and coriander and serve hot.

This concludes the guide for authentic Northern-style combination dried pig skin soup for Tet. Through this process, you have learned to create a clear, delicious broth and how to marinate meats to infuse them with flavor. The final step of decorating with shrimp, coriander, and ground pepper adds the signature touch to this festive dish.

mon_an.ten: Dried Bamboo Shoot and Pork Trotter Soup
mon_an.mo_ta: Every year, my mother prepares a variety of foods for Tet. I always help by prepping ingredients for traditional dishes, starting with papaya, kohlrabi, and carrots for pickles, then shallots, and finally prepping the bamboo shoots for this rich and savory pork trotter or pork rib soup.
thoi_gian: Cooking dried bamboo shoot soup with pork trotters or ribs takes some time because you must dedicate a significant amount of time to prepping the dried bamboo. However, the final result—a bowl of golden, fragrant, and rich soup that is never greasy—is well worth the effort. Depending on the type of bamboo, prep can take from 2-3 days to a week. My family usually preps a large batch and stores it in the fridge for later use. Let's prepare the ingredients and make this dish together.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Dried bamboo shoots - 200g (Any type works, but 'tongue' bamboo shoots are best for their thickness and golden color)
Pork trotter - 1 piece (include both the hoof and the leg meat; can be replaced with ribs)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the bamboo shoots

Soak the dried bamboo shoots in water to soften. My family uses rice water from every meal to soak the bamboo, changing the water twice a day. Rinse the bamboo, boil it in a pot, then drain and rinse again. Repeat this process several times until the boiling water is no longer dark yellow and the strong bamboo smell is gone. The bamboo should turn a pleasant straw-yellow color. This prep can take 2 days to a week depending on the bamboo and the weather.
After boiling, drain the bamboo, rinse with cold water, and cut into bite-sized pieces or shred into strips.
Step 2:

Clean the pork trotter and marinate with spices to taste. Place a pot on the stove, sauté minced shallots until fragrant, then add the trotter and lightly sauté until the spices are absorbed. Add enough water, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer until the trotter is tender.
Step 3:

While waiting for the trotter to soften, soak the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms until they expand, then rinse and trim the stems. Keep the shiitake mushrooms whole and cut the wood ear mushrooms into bite-sized pieces.
Separate the white parts of the green onions and shred them. Wash the green parts and the sawtooth herb, then cut into sections.
Step 4:

Heat a pan, sauté minced shallots until fragrant, then add the bamboo shoots and sauté with spices. You can add a little broth from the trotter pot to help the bamboo absorb the flavors (especially if the bamboo is dry). Then, add the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms to sauté together.
Step 5:

Add the sautéed bamboo and mushrooms from Step 4 into the pot of simmering pork trotters. Continue cooking until both the bamboo and trotters are tender. Season again to taste, then add the shredded white onions, green onions, and sawtooth herb before turning off the heat.
Ladle the soup into a bowl and serve hot.

This fragrant, rich, and nutritious soup is a favorite for many people from the North. Its golden color and wonderful aroma make it an essential part of the Tet menu. You can enjoy it hot with rice vermicelli or steamed rice, accompanied by pickled vegetables or pickled onions.

If you don't like pork trotters, you can use pork ribs instead. Choose loin ribs for more meat and better flavor. While some people dislike cartilage ribs, my family loves them; buying loin ribs with plenty of cartilage for this soup is absolutely delicious and very appetizing.

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Pork Kidneys with Mixed Vegetables for Lunar New Year
mon_an.mo_ta: To prepare a truly special meal for Lunar New Year, stir-fried pork kidneys with mixed vegetables is an excellent choice. The harmonious combination of tender pork kidneys and fresh vegetables will bring a unique culinary experience to your family gathering. Stir-frying mixed kidneys is not only simple but also quick and easy. Today, let's learn how to make this traditional dish that conquers the palate and brings joy to the family during the holidays.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Celery, leeks, and green onions - 1 bunch
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the ingredients

Pork kidneys: Selecting fresh and delicious kidneys can be quite difficult as they are a sensitive organ. When buying, try pressing the kidney. If it has good elasticity and a light reddish-purple exterior, that is a good sign.

Pork heart: Pork heart is a delicious ingredient and is also quite expensive compared to other types of offal. However, it is very nutritious and often used to cook porridge for young children. When choosing to buy pork heart, touch and feel it. Ensure the heart has no issues.
Carrots: Choose bright red carrots without black spots on the skin or blemishes. It is best to buy carrots with the roots still attached.
Onions and celery: Choose fresh onions and celery with no signs of spoilage.
Shiitake mushrooms: You can buy shiitake mushrooms at dried goods stores or choose to buy them in the supermarket to ensure quality.
Shallots: Avoid buying shallots that are blackened, moldy, or too dry due to poor storage.
Cooking oil: If possible, choose to use olive oil for the health benefits of you and your family.
Seasoning powder, oyster sauce, MSG: Use these seasonings to flavor the dish according to your family's taste.
2. Tips for cleaning pork heart and kidneys
Method 1: Water soaking method
First, peel off the outer membrane of the heart and kidneys, then cut them in half to remove all blood and impurities inside. Next, rinse the heart and kidneys thoroughly.
Next, soak the heart and kidneys in water for about 30 hours. Use sea salt when washing to remove impurities.
Then, rinse the heart and kidneys several times with water.
Bring water to a boil and add the cleaned heart and kidneys; blanch them and add a little white wine to remove any odor.
Method 2: Vinegar soaking method
Clean the heart and kidneys, then divide them into 4 parts.
Place the heart and kidneys in a soaking bowl and soak in a mixture of water and white vinegar for about 30 minutes.
Next, blanch the heart and kidneys in boiling water for about 5-10 minutes to remove the odor.
Method 3: Using flour
Clean the pork heart and kidneys, then divide them into 4 parts. Roll each part through flour several times.
Then, use your hands to rub firmly so the flour forms a thick paste on the surface of the heart and kidneys.
Doing this for about 10 minutes will help remove the odor of the pork heart and kidneys.
3. Cooking the stir-fried pork kidneys

In a pan over the stove, pour in oil and sauté the garlic until fragrant. Next, add the heart and kidneys to the pan and stir-fry until cooked. Then, remove the heart and kidneys and set aside on a separate plate.
Add carrots, garlic, straw mushrooms, onions, and baby corn to the pan and stir-fry until cooked. During the stir-frying process, season to taste to suit your family's preference.
Next, return the stir-fried heart and kidneys to the pan and toss well until the vegetables and meat are evenly combined. Stir for about 3 minutes and then turn off the heat.

This stir-fried pork kidney dish will be wonderful when enjoyed with hot rice, bringing an irresistible rich flavor. To make the dish more attractive, you can garnish it with a little cilantro and ground pepper.

mon_an.mo_ta: When you bite into a hot piece of chả cốm, you will feel the rich sweetness of the meat, the chewy fragrance of the green rice inside, and the crispy texture of the outer crust. The unique flavor of chả cốm has become an iconic symbol of the culinary talent of the capital city. Let's refer to the recipe for this delicious and flavorful chả cốm!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, cooking oil, pepper - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: For this easy-to-make dish, put the ground pork, raw pork paste, green rice, and fish sauce (add pepper if desired) into a bowl and mix well.

Step 2: Use food preparation gloves to place the mixed green rice and meat mixture into your palm to shape the chả cốm into flat patties, about the size of your palm, or round shapes as you prefer. Shape and place the newly formed chả cốm onto a clean lotus leaf, one by one until finished.

Step 3: Arrange the patties alternately on a steaming rack and steam for 15 minutes. If lotus leaves are not available, you can substitute them with banana leaves. Steaming the patties in leaves will make the dish more fragrant. However, if you don't have any, you can still steam them without leaves.
Step 4: Brush annatto oil onto each patty and then fry them to create color and increase the appeal of the patties.
Step 5: Drain the oil, then slice the chả cốm and arrange them on a plate to serve hot or eat with other dishes.
Source: Collected

mon_an.ten: Simple and Crunchy Pickled Daikon in Fish Sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: Pickled daikon in fish sauce is a harmonious blend of various spices, creating an irresistible flavor. Preparing this dish is quite simple; with just a little time, you will have a delicious side dish ready. Let's explore how to make pickled daikon in fish sauce in the article below! I. Instructions for making delicious pickled daikon in fish sauce
cac_buoc: 1. Ingredients
1 kg fresh daikon radish
1 head of garlic
3 chili peppers
100ml fish sauce
150g sugar
3 tbsp salt
2. Cooking Steps
Step 1: Preparation
Select 1 kg of fresh, firm daikon radishes. Do not peel; trim both ends, wash thoroughly, and cut into finger-sized strips to speed up the drying process.
Marinate the daikon with 3 tbsp of salt for about 1 hour, then rinse with water to reduce saltiness. Squeeze dry and sun-dry for about 1 day until the daikon is dry and ready for the next step.
Mince the chilies and garlic.
Step 2: Boiling the Fish Sauce
Boil 250ml of filtered water in a pot, add 150g sugar and 100ml fish sauce. Stir well and simmer until the sugar dissolves and the sauce boils. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
Step 3: Pickling the Daikon
Mix the daikon with garlic and chilies, then place in a glass jar. Pour in the fish sauce and press the daikon down with a spoon. Seal the lid tightly.
Pickle for 2-3 days before serving.
Step 4: Serving
Arrange the daikon on a plate and serve with bánh tét or hot rice to enjoy the wonderful flavor.
The pickled daikon pieces offer a rich, savory flavor that stimulates the palate. This dish is not only delicious but also healthy, perfect for the Lunar New Year (Tết).
II. Instructions for Sweet and Salty Pickled Daikon
Daikon radish: 500g
Garlic: 5 cloves
Chilies: 3
Fish sauce: 50ml
Sugar: 80g
Salt: 1 tbsp
Filtered water: 125ml
2. Step-by-step Instructions
2.1. Ingredient Preparation
Trim the ends of the daikon and wash several times. Cut into strips about 3 finger-joints long and 1/3 finger-joint thick.
Wash the garlic, peel, and slice thinly. Wash the chilies, remove stems, and slice diagonally.
2.2. Marinating and Drying
Place the daikon in a basin, add 1 tbsp of salt, and toss to coat evenly.
Marinate for about 1 hour, tossing a few times to ensure even absorption.
After 1 hour, rinse the daikon several times to reduce saltiness and squeeze dry.
Spread the daikon on a tray and sun-dry for about 1 day until dry but still soft.
2.3. Preparing the Fish Sauce
In a pot, combine 50ml fish sauce, 80g sugar, and 125ml filtered water over medium heat.
Simmer until the sugar dissolves and the sauce boils, then continue for another 2 minutes. Turn off the heat and let it cool.
2.4. Pickling the Daikon
Mix the dried daikon, sliced garlic, and chilies on a plate.
Pack the daikon, garlic, and chilies into a glass jar. Pour in the cooled fish sauce, seal tightly, and pickle for 2 days.
2.5. Final Result
The pickled daikon has a rich aroma of fish sauce, the spiciness of garlic and chili, combined with a crunchy texture and balanced sweet-salty flavor.
Perfect when paired with bánh tét or bánh chưng during Tết, or simply with hot rice.
Conclusion:
This dish promises a special culinary experience—crunchy yet soft, rich in fish sauce flavor, and spicy from garlic and chili. Try this combination now to feel the excellence of traditional flavors.
III. How to Choose Fresh Ingredients
Fresh daikon is identified by a smooth surface, few roots, a firm feel when squeezed, and a characteristic aroma.
Choose medium-sized radishes that feel heavy, as they are less likely to be hollow inside. Radishes that are neither too young nor too old will yield the best flavor after pickling.
Avoid radishes with soft surfaces or unpleasant odors, as these are signs of rot. Careful selection ensures a delicious and safe dish.
IV. Tips for Success
When preparing the daikon, just wash the skin thoroughly; there is no need to peel it.
When simmering the fish sauce and sugar, use low heat to help them blend better.
Letting the fish sauce mixture cool for a day before using helps the pickles last longer without spoiling. This preserves the dish better and maintains its flavor over time.

mon_an.ten: Authentic Steamed Chicken with Mustard Greens Recipe
mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed chicken with mustard greens is a rich and delicious traditional dish. When the fragrant, sweet chicken blends with the fresh taste of mustard greens, the dish becomes truly irresistible. Discover this simple recipe to make for your family! Enjoy authentic steamed chicken with mustard greens with this simple recipe. Fresh chicken combined with crisp mustard greens and delicate seasonings creates a traditional dish that is both savory and appealing.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings: Sugar, black pepper, oyster sauce, sesame oil, soy sauce, seasoning powder.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Preparation
Soak the chicken in diluted salt water for 5 minutes, then rinse several times with cold water to clean.
Place the chicken in a pot of cold water. Add peeled onion and green onions, then boil for 30-35 minutes.
Wash the mustard greens to remove dirt and discard any wilted parts. Trim the stems, keeping only the leaves.
Peel the carrots and rinse several times with cold water.

To carve carrots into flowers: cut into small sections and mark 5 points to create a regular pentagonal cylinder. From each vertex, make a C-shaped cut toward the core, remove the excess, and slice into bite-sized flower shapes.
Step 2: Cooking
Once the chicken is cooked, remove it to a basin to cool slightly, then shred the meat into thin, bite-sized pieces.
Blanch the mustard greens and carrots in the chicken broth. Remove and immediately place them in an ice bath to keep them crunchy and vibrant green.
Season the shredded chicken with 1 tsp seasoning powder, 1/2 tsp pepper, 1/2 tsp MSG, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/4 tsp salt, and 1 tsp minced garlic. Mix well.
Prepare a large steaming bowl. Arrange the mustard green stems crosswise at the bottom, then fill half the bowl with the seasoned chicken.
Press down gently to even out the chicken. Cover with another layer of greens and add the remaining chicken.
Prepare a steamer. Once the water boils, steam the chicken for 10 minutes.

Heat a pan with 2 tbsp cooking oil and 1 tsp minced garlic. When the garlic turns golden, add 2 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 1/2 tsp pepper, and 6 tbsp chicken broth. Stir and simmer for 2-3 minutes until the sauce thickens.
After steaming for 10 minutes, add 2 tbsp of the oyster sauce mixture and steam for another 5 minutes until fully cooked. Remove from the steamer; the dish is ready.
Alternative presentation for Steamed Chicken with Mustard Greens:
It looks appetizing, doesn't it? Delicious and nutritious for the whole family!

mon_an.ten: Northern Vietnamese Fried Spring Rolls (Bánh Đa Nem) Recipe
mon_an.mo_ta: Northern-style fried spring rolls, served hot with herbs and sweet and sour dipping sauce, are always a favorite. While a familiar dish in Vietnamese daily life, do you know how to make them with the authentic Northern flavor—crispy on the outside and tender on the inside? Follow this guide to make perfect Northern bánh đa nem! Detailed instructions to create savory and attractive spring rolls for daily meals or special occasions. Enjoy these wonderful spring rolls with exquisite flavor alongside family and friends.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green onions, cilantro, wood ear mushrooms, shiitake mushrooms
Seasonings, black pepper, rice paper wrappers (bánh đa nem)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Preparation
Soak shiitake and wood ear mushrooms in warm water for 15 minutes to soften. Rinse, trim the stems, and mince.
Rub the pork with salt, rinse, then mince or grind and place in a bowl.
Peel and devein the shrimp, rinse, and mince.
Soak glass noodles in warm water for 15 minutes to soften. Drain and cut into 5cm lengths.
Beat the egg in a bowl. Peel and mince the shallots and garlic separately.
Mince the chilies.
Peel, wash, and shred the carrots. Peel, wash, and dice the onion.
Wash the green onions and cilantro, trim the roots, and chop finely.
Step 2: Preparing the Filling

In a large bowl, combine the ground pork, shrimp, glass noodles, shiitake mushrooms, wood ear mushrooms, carrots, onion, green onions, cilantro, and beaten egg. Add 1 tsp salt, 2 tsp seasoning powder, 1 tsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp MSG, 1 tbsp minced shallots, and a pinch of ground pepper. Mix thoroughly. Refrigerate and marinate for about 30 minutes.
Step 3: Wrapping the Spring Rolls

Lay a rice paper wrapper on a clean tray or cutting board. Lightly dampen with water to soften it and prevent cracking. Place a sufficient amount of filling in the center. Fold in the two sides and roll up tightly. Repeat until all filling is used.
Step 4: Frying

Heat 500ml of cooking oil in a pan. Once the oil is hot, gently add the spring rolls and fry over low heat to ensure the filling cooks through. When the rolls are golden brown and crispy on all sides, remove them to a tray lined with paper towels.
Secrets to Authentic Bánh Đa Nem
Do not add the egg to the filling too early; if left too long, the mixture will become watery.
Avoid rolling too tightly; the filling expands during frying, which can cause the wrapper to burst.
For extra crispiness, deep-fry the rolls; the faster they fry, the crispier they become.
Avoid using high heat, as it can burn the wrappers.
If not serving immediately, fry them once until lightly cooked. When ready to eat, fry again until golden brown for a better flavor.
Making and enjoying bánh đa nem is a way to experience and preserve traditional culinary heritage. These fragrant spring rolls are a great choice for family gatherings. Good luck and enjoy!

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Snow Peas with Shrimp and Pork
mon_an.mo_ta: A simple stir-fry served with white rice featuring mushrooms, crunchy snow peas, and sweet shrimp, bringing a refreshing vegetable taste and nutrition from the shrimp to your meal. This wonderful dish is a must-try for every family. A simple stir-fry served with white rice featuring mushrooms, crunchy snow peas, and sweet shrimp, bringing a refreshing vegetable taste and nutrition from the shrimp to your meal. This wonderful dish is a must-try for every family.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green onions, salt, fish sauce, seasoning powder, black pepper - seasonings
cac_buoc: Step 1: Trim the roots of the shimeji mushrooms, wash with diluted salt water, and place in a basket to drain.
Remove the stringy fibers from the snow peas and wash thoroughly.
Wash the green onions and chop finely.
Step 2: Peel and devein the shrimp, then coarsely crush them.
Step 3: Heat two teaspoons of cooking oil, sauté the garlic until fragrant, and stir-fry the shrimp until cooked.

Step 4: Add the snow peas and stir-fry quickly over high heat. After about 3 minutes, add the mushrooms, season with one teaspoon of salt, one teaspoon of fish sauce, and half a teaspoon of seasoning powder, then toss well.

Step 5: Stir-fry for about 7 - 10 minutes, adjust the seasoning to your taste, turn off the heat, and sprinkle with a bit of black pepper and chopped green onions. Transfer to a plate and serve as a stir-fried dish with rice.
Enjoy your meal, everyone!

mon_an.mo_ta: Dưa món is an indispensable dish during the traditional Lunar New Year (Tet). Every year, my mother makes dưa món for Tet to serve with bánh chưng, thit đông, giò xào, or cold cuts. Each crunchy piece of pickle, with its perfect balance of sour, spicy, salty, and sweet flavors, along with pickled onions, will help balance the richness of Tet holiday meals.
cac_buoc: Peel and wash all ingredients, then slice them into 3-5mm thick pieces. You can cut them into strips or carve them into flower shapes as desired, then sun-dry them until withered. If there is no sun, you can put them in the oven at the lowest temperature setting to dry.

In the past, about a month before Tet, my mother would start preparing the ingredients for dưa món, sun-drying them for several days. You can prepare the ingredients in the summer, dry them (when the sun is strong, they dry faster), and save them until Tet to make the pickles.
Nowadays, things are much simpler; you can buy pre-prepared pickling ingredients at the supermarket to skip this preparation step.
Here I am using pre-dried ingredients, so before making the pickles, soak them in cold water to soften slightly and to wash away any dust accumulated during the drying process.
Bring water to a boil and blanch the ingredients for about 10-20 seconds.
Then remove them and immediately place them in a bowl of cold water, soak, wash again, and squeeze firmly to drain all water.
In a pot, combine fish sauce, sugar, and water in a ratio of 3 sugar: 2 fish sauce: 1/2 water. Stir to dissolve, bring to a boil, then turn off the heat. Let the fish sauce mixture cool completely.
Place the ingredients into a jar, pour in the cooled fish sauce mixture, and use a bamboo or plastic weight to keep the ingredients submerged. Let it marinate for about 5-7 days before eating.

When serving, arrange the dưa món on a plate. You can adjust the flavor to your liking (or mix the pickles with a bit of vinegar, garlic, and re-season). Serve with bánh chưng, thịt đông, or giò xào for a delicious Tet meal that isn't greasy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cơm rượu nếp is an indispensable dish during the Tết Đoan Ngọ festival in many regions of our country. Let's learn how to make this traditional dish! This is a dish to be savored and should not replace breakfast; do not eat it on an empty stomach and do not eat too much because fermented rice naturally contains a certain amount of alcohol. Although it is not as strong as regular wine, eating too much can make you tipsy, and eating it while hungry can cause stomach discomfort.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the glutinous rice and drain.
Step 2: Steam the glutinous rice or cook it like regular rice.
Step 3: Spread the rice onto a large tray, thinning it out so it cools quickly.
Step 4: Remove all the husks from the yeast balls by rubbing them together, then grind the yeast into a fine powder.

Step 5: Sift the yeast onto the warm rice: Sift half over the top surface of the rice, then flip it over and sift the rest before mixing. (This is done because glutinous rice is very sticky and difficult to mix evenly with yeast).
Step 6: Roll the rice into small balls.
Step 7: Poke several small holes in the bottom of the zip-lock bag and place the rice balls inside.

Step 8: Place the bag of rice into a ceramic pot. Place a bamboo rack inside the pot so that as the rice ferments, the liquid from the bottom of the bag will drip down, preventing the rice from becoming too pungent.
Step 9: The product will be ready in about 3-5 days.
Finished product requirements: The rice should have a strong aroma of glutinous rice, feel soft and well-fermented, with a bit of liquid at the bottom of the jar.
Notes:
The rice usually used is fragrant, sticky rice, or best of all, nếp nương or nếp cái hoa vàng.
When spreading the rice on the tray, ensure it is even to help the yeast mix more thoroughly.
When choosing yeast for rice or wine, absolutely do not use Chinese yeast as consuming it can lead to headaches or poisoning...

mon_an.mo_ta: Tet holiday dishes are often high in protein and can easily become overwhelming. Therefore, a sweet and sour dish is the perfect choice to balance the palate for a more enjoyable Tet. Let's learn how to make dưa củ kiệu! Choose medium-sized leek bulbs, not too large or too small. Drying them sufficiently in the sun will result in crunchy, fragrant pickles.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Slaked lime, wood ash - 1 bowl each
cac_buoc: Mix the wood ash with water, let it settle, and collect the clear water, discarding the sediment. Clean the leek bulbs and soak them in the ash water overnight to reduce the pungency, then rinse thoroughly with cold water.
Dissolve the alum in water, soak the leeks for about 4 hours, rinse well, and drain.
Mix the slaked lime into water, take the clear water, and soak the leeks for another 2 hours.
Remove the leeks, drain, and sun-dry for 1 day.
Dissolve sugar and salt in vinegar, bring to a boil, and let cool.
Wash the chilies and cut as desired. Peel the garlic and cut in half.
Arrange the leeks, garlic, and chilies in a jar, pour the vinegar mixture over to submerge them, and leave for 10 days before use.

mon_an.ten: Dried Bamboo Shoot Soup with Pork Trotters
mon_an.mo_ta: Dried bamboo shoot soup with pork trotters is a familiar dish to Vietnamese people, especially during the Lunar New Year. This delicious dish, made with easy-to-find ingredients and a simple method, attracts diners with its tender, flavorful pork and well-simmered, crunchy dried bamboo shoots. Let us share the secret to cooking this wonderful dish perfectly!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare ingredients

Wash the dried bamboo shoots thoroughly, soak for about 2 days until they expand, then shred or slice them. If you don't have time, soak them for at least 4-5 hours before cooking to make them softer and tastier.
Wash the pork trotter and bones, then chop into bite-sized pieces. Blanch the bones once in boiling water to remove odors and impurities.
Wash the onion bulbs and slice them into strips.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms until expanded, rinse with clean water, and slice into bite-sized pieces.
Peel, wash, and mince the shallots.
Step 2: Steps to make delicious dried bamboo shoot soup with pork trotters
First, boil the bamboo shoots in cold water several times until the water is clear and the bamboo is soft. Then rinse the bamboo with cold water.

Next, sauté the minced shallots in oil until fragrant, then add the bamboo shoots and wood ear mushrooms to stir-fry. Add a little salt and fish sauce so they absorb the seasoning. You should stir-fry them thoroughly so they are well-seasoned and partially cooked. Add the bamboo first, then the wood ear mushrooms.
Place the pork trotter and bones into a large pot, stir-fry briefly with fish sauce and a bit of MSG until seasoned, then pour in water and simmer for about 30 minutes until tender.

Next, add the stir-fried bamboo and wood ear mushrooms to the pot with the trotters and bones. Continue cooking until the bamboo is soft and the trotters are tender. While simmering, you can add some salt and MSG to make the broth sweet and savory. Simmer for about 45 minutes so the bamboo is tender and not tough, and the trotters are soft and easy to eat.
Finally, adjust the seasoning to taste, turn off the heat, ladle the soup into a bowl, top with some sliced onions, and enjoy this wonderful soup.
Notes
Dried bamboo shoots should be soaked for at least 4-5 hours to fully expand so they soften faster when cooking.
Remember to clean the pork trotters thoroughly before cooking.
When simmering the bones and trotters, be sure to skim off any foam to keep the broth clear and fragrant. If you want a more aromatic broth, you can add a small piece of cinnamon.

How to choose good pork trotters: You should buy the hind legs, which have smaller bones, more meat, and thinner skin. Choose firm meat that isn't flabby, weighing about 500-600g. Avoid oversized trotters from lean pigs, as they take longer to cook and the meat isn't as good.

How to choose good dried bamboo shoots: Buy bamboo that is light brownish-yellow and still retains its characteristic aroma. Choose bamboo shoots that are evenly yellow without fibers, which indicates young bamboo. There are usually 4 types: măng trúc, măng nứa, măng vầu, and măng lưỡi lợn.
Măng trúc is small and pointed, crunchy and sweet. Măng nứa and măng vầu are softer. These three types are usually used for stir-frying or soup.
Măng lưỡi lợn is the thick bulb part, sliced and dried; when cooked, it is cut into tongue-shaped pieces and usually stewed with pork or trotters for feasts.

mon_an.mo_ta: Fragrant and attractive chicken patties with an eye-catching color. When enjoyed, you will find the chicken tender and flavorful, paired with the crunchy texture of shiitake mushrooms. Serving these chicken patties with rice vermicelli is an excellent choice. Refer to our recipe below to make these delicious and unique chicken patties! We hope this helps you create a wonderful dish to treat your loved ones.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning powder, cooking oil, black pepper - seasoning
cac_buoc: How to make chicken patties for 2-3 servings:
Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Wash the chicken and mince it.
Peel, wash, and finely mince the onion.
Wash the shiitake mushrooms, soak in hot water until fully expanded, then rinse again thoroughly. Drain and mince the mushrooms.
Peel, wash, drain, and mince the garlic.
Step 2: Cooking steps
First, heat a bit of oil in a pan. Once the oil is hot, sauté the garlic until fragrant.
Next, add the onion and stir well, then add the shiitake mushrooms and a bit of seasoning powder. Stir-fry for 3 more minutes and turn off the heat.
Mix the minced chicken with 3 tbsp of tapioca starch and black pepper. Add the sautéed mushroom mixture and mix thoroughly until all ingredients are well combined.
Shape the chicken mixture into equal-sized small patties and set them aside on a tray.

Once the patties are ready, heat oil in a pan. When the oil is hot, fry the patties. Remember to flip them to ensure both sides are evenly cooked and golden brown. Do not use high heat, as it may leave the inside raw and the outside burnt.
Once cooked, remove the patties and place them on paper towels to drain excess oil. Serve on a plate and enjoy with sweet and sour fish sauce or chili sauce.
Notes for delicious chicken patties
For extra flavor, you can marinate the chicken with a bit of ginger and lemongrass.
Serve with cucumber, cilantro, or lettuce to balance the flavors.
Depending on your preference, you can enjoy the patties with chili sauce or sweet and sour fish sauce, though the latter is usually the best pairing.

Dipping sauce recipe: Mix 1 part sugar + 1/2 part vinegar + 1/2 part lime juice + 1 part fish sauce + 3-4 parts water (adjust to taste). You can use chicken broth or fresh stock instead of water for a special touch. Prepare sliced or minced chili. Peel and crush garlic, then soak it in vinegar and lime juice before adding to the fish sauce for a better look and flavor.

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Bean Sprouts with Chicken Giblets
mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried bean sprouts with chicken giblets is a very familiar dish in Vietnam. It is simple in both ingredients and preparation but remains extremely delicious and nutritious, providing essential nutrients for the body. Let's cook this dish!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - Cooking oil, MSG, salt, fish sauce
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Wash the chicken liver and gizzards, then rub with salt to remove any odors.
Slice the liver thinly. Score the gizzards in a chrysanthemum pattern so they stay tender and crunchy when stir-fried.
Marinate the liver and gizzards with seasoning and MSG.
Step 2:
Wash the bean sprouts and drain well.
Peel and thinly slice the shallot. Wash and chop the green onions.
Step 3:
Heat oil in a pan and sauté half of the sliced shallots until fragrant.
Add the gizzards and liver. Stir-fry over high heat quickly so they stay crunchy and tender without becoming tough, then remove to a plate.
Step 4:

Heat more oil in the pan and sauté the remaining shallots. Add the bean sprouts and stir-fry over high heat. Season to taste, then return the liver, gizzards, and green onions to the pan and toss well.
Transfer the stir-fried bean sprouts and giblets to a plate, garnish with cilantro, and serve hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: Five-color meatloaf is a dish that is both familiar and unique, using common ingredients prepared in a new way to create a delicious meal. It features crunchy pork ear, wood ear mushrooms, carrots, flavorful lean meat, and the light saltiness of salted egg yolks, all blending together perfectly. Head to the kitchen and try making this wonderful dish for the upcoming Lunar New Year!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, sugar, fish sauce, black pepper, seasoning powder - seasoning
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Peel and wash the carrot, then julienne into 5-6 cm strips. You can use a peeler for speed.
Soak wood ear mushrooms until soft, wash, and slice into strips.
Wash and thinly slice the green onions.
Peel, wash, and mince the shallots.
Wash the banana leaves thoroughly and let them dry.
Clean the pork ear with white wine and salt to remove odors and ensure a crunchy texture.
Wash the pork belly with water.
Step 2: Making the five-color meatloaf
Boil the cleaned pork ear until cooked, let it cool, and slice thinly.
Boil the pork belly until cooked and slice thinly.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add a bit of salt, black pepper, and chopped green onions. Whisk well.
Fry the egg mixture into medium-thick sheets.

In a large bowl, combine the ground pork shoulder, sliced pork ear, pork belly, wood ear mushrooms, carrots, and minced shallots. Add a bit of salt, black pepper, 2 tbsp fish sauce, seasoning powder, and sugar. Mix well and marinate for 30 minutes.
Separate the salted egg yolks, rinse with white wine, and steam for about 5 minutes. Let them cool.
Wrapping: Layer 2-3 banana leaves. Place an egg sheet on top.
Spread the meat mixture evenly over the egg sheet, then arrange the salted egg yolks in a line along the length.
Carefully roll the egg sheet to encase the filling tightly. Then roll the banana leaves, ensuring a very tight wrap so the filling stays intact. Secure with string.
Fold the two ends of the banana leaves and tie securely with string.
Boil the meatloaf in a pot of water (fully submerged) for 40-50 minutes. Once cooked, remove and drain.
To serve, peel off the leaves, slice into rounds, and enjoy with hot rice.
Tips for a delicious five-color meatloaf
To check the seasoning, cook a small piece of the meat mixture in the oven or a pan and taste it to adjust the seasoning if needed.
For the salted egg yolks, you can steam or bake them for 5 minutes to set the outer layer.
If you prefer smaller loaves, divide the ingredients to make two smaller rolls.

mon_an.ten: Beef Stew with Ginger and Lemongrass
mon_an.mo_ta: Beef stew with ginger and lemongrass is a delicious dish perfect for cold winter weather. It attracts diners with the fragrance of lemongrass and ginger, along with tender, flavorful beef. Let's get into the kitchen and learn how to make this nutritious dish for the family!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, sugar, seasoning powder, salt, pepper - seasoning
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients:
Wash the beef and cut into 2x2 cm cubes.
Peel the ginger, wash, and julienne.
Peel, wash, and mince the shallot.
Wash the lemongrass, cut into sections, and split lengthwise.
Steps for delicious beef stew:
Step 1:
Heat a bit of oil in a pot. Sauté the minced shallots, then add the ginger and lemongrass. Stir well.
Add the beef and stir-fry with the aromatics.
Step 2: Seasoning
Add 3 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, and a bit of seasoning powder. Mix well, cover the pot, and simmer over low heat to let the meat absorb the flavors.
Cook until the beef is seared and the surface tightens. Add enough water to just cover the meat and bring to a boil. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Step 3:
Continue simmering over low heat until the liquid reduces and thickens, and the beef is tender. Turn off the heat, plate, and serve.
Tips for delicious beef stew with ginger and lemongrass
Always simmer over low heat until the beef is tender and the sauce is slightly thickened.
This dish pairs perfectly with hot rice or bread!
How to choose good beef:
Identifying quality beef:
The meat should be bright red with fine fibers, a distinct beefy aroma, and pale yellow fat.
Dark red meat with deep yellow fat and large fibers indicates an older, tougher animal.
Dark red meat with white fat and a slightly fishy smell is likely buffalo meat.
Check for parasites: they look like rice grains embedded in the muscle fibers and can be easily removed with a knife tip, unlike tendons which are attached.
How to remove beef odors:
To remove odors, char a piece of ginger, peel the burnt skin, crush it, and rub it onto the beef. Rinse with water.
Add a bit of salt to help tenderize. For tough cuts like shank or ribs, adding a piece of pineapple, an ice cube, or an aluminum spoon to the pot can speed up the process.
Pay attention to color: buy fresh red beef, not dark red. Fat should be yellow and firm, not soft.
Look at the grain: choose fine, soft fibers over large, tough ones.
Finally, the meat should not be sticky to the touch and should have no unpleasant odor.

mon_an.mo_ta: Candied carrots with eye-catching colors, a unique delicious flavor, moderate sweetness, and high nutritional value will give you a great appetite. Today's article will guide you on how to make soft candied carrots to welcome guests during the Lunar New Year.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel, wash, and drain the carrots, then shred them.
Step 2: You can further mince or blend the shredded carrots, then squeeze out excess liquid.
Macerate the carrots with sugar until the sugar dissolves and the carrots are well-soaked.
In a non-stick pan, combine the sugared carrots, lime juice, and orange juice. Simmer over medium heat.
Step 3: After boiling for 10 minutes, reduce to low heat and stir occasionally until the syrup thickens.
Step 4: Add honey and continue to simmer until the mixture becomes very thick and sticky. Turn off the heat.
Step 5: Scoop small portions onto a lightly oiled tray. Once cooled, roll into balls and coat with desiccated coconut.
Tips for delicious soft candied carrots
Store the finished candies in an airtight jar with a desiccant pack or keep them in the refrigerator.
How to choose good carrots:
Carrots are highly nutritious. You can use them for many dishes and drinks.
Choose bright-colored, firm, straight, and smooth carrots.
If the greens are attached, they should be fresh and not wilted.
The smaller the core, the sweeter the carrot; those with thick shoulders or many greens at the base often have large, bland cores.
Avoid oversized carrots as they can be fibrous and less sweet. Smaller carrots are usually more tender and flavorful.
Avoid soft, bruised, wilted, or overly misshapen carrots.
Storage tips:
Do not wash before refrigerating, as moisture causes rot.
Store in a cool, dry place; they can stay fresh for up to 3 weeks.
Remove greens before refrigerating. Wrap in a cloth and store in the crisper drawer for longevity.
Trim any green parts before storing. Wrap in cloth and keep in the fridge.
Do not cut carrots before storing; only wash and cut right before use.
If carrots soften at room temperature, crisp them up in an ice water bath.
Use within 1-2 weeks for maximum nutritional value.
These colorful, delicious, and nutritious soft candied carrots are a delightful treat.

mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little time in the kitchen and familiar ingredients, this simple recipe will give you a delicious, well-seasoned five-color head cheese. It has a signature crunchy texture that is sure to delight anyone who tries it.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - salt, seasoning powder, fish sauce, sugar, black pepper
Wood ear mushrooms - a few pieces
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pig ear, meat, and vegetables

Clean the pig ear by rubbing it with a bit of rice wine and salt, then rinse with water to remove any odor. Place the ear in a pot of water and boil until cooked. Once cooked, remove and soak in ice water to maintain crunchiness. When cooled, slice into small pieces.
Rinse the pork belly and boil until cooked. Remove, let cool, and slice into small pieces.
Soak the wood ear mushrooms in warm water until expanded. Trim the stems, rinse, and julienne.
Peel and rinse the carrot, then julienne it like the wood ear mushrooms.
Peel and rinse the shallot, then slice thinly.
Crack the chicken eggs into a bowl. Add finely chopped green onions, 1 tsp of salt, and pepper. Whisk well and fry in a pan until cooked.
Step 2: Mix the filling

In a large bowl, combine the pig ear, pork belly, carrot, shallot, wood ear mushrooms, and ground pork. Add seasonings: pepper, 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt, ½ tsp seasoning powder, and 1 tsp white sugar. Mix well and marinate for about 30 minutes to allow the flavors to penetrate.
Step 3: Wrap the head cheese
Separate the salted duck egg yolks. Place them in a bowl with a little rice wine and steam for about 5 minutes until cooked.
Rinse the banana leaves and wipe them dry.

Layer 2-3 banana leaves on top of each other. Place the fried egg sheet on top, then spoon the meat filling into the center. Spread it evenly and arrange the 3 salted egg yolks along the length of the meat.
Roll the head cheese tightly and secure it firmly with string.
Step 4: Boil the head cheese
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Submerge both rolls in the water and boil for 40 to 50 minutes until cooked. Remove and place in a basket to drain.
Finally, let the head cheese cool down. Use a knife to slice it into thin rounds, arrange on a plate, garnish, and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little effort, you can make these delicious candied cherry tomatoes. They feature a glossy red color, a light fragrance, and a unique taste that brings a refreshing sensation. Let's make this treat using the guide below.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Soaking liquid - 1 tsp food-grade lime powder mixed with 1 liter of cold water
cac_buoc: Step 1: Rinse the cherry tomatoes and drain. Use the tip of a knife to make 4-6 even vertical slits along the body of each tomato. Gently press them flat to remove the seeds and create a 5-petal flower shape.

Step 2: Mix the lime powder and water. Let it sit for 10 minutes to settle, then decant the clear lime water. Soak the tomatoes in this clear lime water for 5-6 hours. Remove the tomatoes and rinse each one thoroughly under cold water several times.
Step 3: Combine the prepared tomatoes, sugar, lemon juice, and salt in a bowl. Mix well and let sit for a few hours until the sugar dissolves.
Step 4: Once the sugar has dissolved, pour the tomatoes and the syrup into a small non-stick pan. Simmer over low heat, occasionally stirring gently so the tomatoes absorb the sugar evenly.
When the syrup becomes thick and viscous, turn off the heat.
Step 5: Arrange the tomatoes on a rack and place in a cool area or under the sun and wind to dry before storing in a jar.
Once the *candied cherry tomatoes* are dry, place them in a jar to preserve and enjoy during the Lunar New Year.
Tips for delicious candied cherry tomatoes
You can adjust the amount of sugar to suit your family's taste.
How to choose good tomatoes:

Choosing safe tomatoes by color: Safe tomatoes are naturally ripened without stimulants. Look for tomatoes with glossy skin and a deep red color. If you look closely, you can see tiny specks under the skin.

Choose firm tomatoes: Naturally ripened tomatoes will feel slightly soft when touched. When cut in half, you will see yellowish-white seeds and a red, soft, slightly mealy pulp. Chemically ripened tomatoes feel hard on the outside, and when cut, the seeds are green and the pulp is hard. Avoid bruised, mushy, or spoiled tomatoes.

Choose tomatoes with fresh green stems: The stem is a good indicator of safety. If the stem is fresh, green, and still firmly attached to the ripened fruit when pulled gently, it is naturally ripened.

Additionally, you can tell during cooking. Naturally ripened tomatoes soften quickly, are fragrant, and turn bright red. Chemically ripened ones take a long time to soften, have a pale color, and lack fragrance.

mon_an.mo_ta: These pineapple jam balls are visually appealing with a unique sweet and sour flavor. The combination of pineapple, sugar, and honey creates a delicate sweetness and gentle acidity. Let's get cooking!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Peel the pineapple and remove the eyes. Finely chop the pineapple and drain some of the juice. Alternatively, you can dice it and pulse in a blender, but do not over-blend. Once chopped or blended, squeeze out the juice but do not make it too dry.
Step 2: Combine the pineapple, salt, and sugar in a pot or non-stick pan and mix well.
Step 3: Let it sit for about 1 hour for the sugar to dissolve and penetrate the pineapple.
Step 4: Place the pan on the stove and simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes.

Step 5: Lower the heat and continue to simmer until the jam starts to become sticky. Add the lemon juice and honey, then simmer for another 10-15 minutes until the jam thickens significantly. Turn off the heat.
Step 6: Let the jam cool slightly, then roll into small balls and roll them through a bowl of white sugar.
Finally, arrange the chewy pineapple jam balls on a plate and enjoy.
Tips for delicious pineapple jam
Store the jam in a glass jar in a cool place.
If you don't like sugar coating, you can roll the balls in shredded coconut for a beautiful look.
How to choose a good pineapple:

*Color:* This is the first thing to look for. The base of the fruit indicates sweetness. If the pineapple is bright yellow from the stem to the base, or has a few green spots, it is ripe and sweet. An even yellow color means higher sweetness. If it has dark brown or reddish-gold spots, it is overripe. Avoid green pineapples as they are unripe and won't ripen after picking.
Shape: Short, rounded pineapples have more flesh than long, cylindrical ones.
Eyes: Choose fruits with large, sparse eyes so that you have more flesh after peeling.
Aroma: Check the base of the fruit. It should smell sweet and fresh. Little to no smell means it's not ripe. A fermented, vinegary, or overly sweet smell indicates it is overripe.

Touch: Overripe pineapples will be soft and the skin may be wrinkled. Fresh, ripe pineapples are neither too hard nor too soft; the skin should not dent when pressed. Mold, leaking juice, or cracks are signs of spoilage.
The crown should be fresh and green. Overripe fruits often have dry, brown crowns with falling leaves.

mon_an.ten: Sweet and Sour Pickled Pig Ears
cac_buoc: A signature flavor of the Lunar New Year is sweet and sour pickled pig ears. The perfect balance of sweet and sour helps cut through the richness of traditional holiday dishes. Today, we will share various ways to make this irresistible dish.
I. Traditional Sweet and Sour Pickled Pig Ears
1. Ingredients
2 pig ears
½ cup garlic
½ cup shallots
50 grams salt
350 grams sugar
Rice vinegar
1 small knob of ginger
2. Instructions
2.1. Prepare the pig ears

After purchasing, clean the pig ears and boil until tender. To clean, shave the hair thoroughly and wash both inside and out with warm water. To remove odors and whiten the ears, wash with a mixture of salt and rice vinegar before rinsing with clean water.
Once cleaned and drained, boil the ears until tender. You can add crushed ginger and 1 tsp of salt to the boiling water to reduce the odor.
When the ears are tender, remove and immediately soak in ice water for 15-20 minutes to make them crunchier.
2.2. Cook the sweet and sour brine
To make the brine, boil the sugar, salt, and 400ml vinegar in a pot. Once the sugar and salt have dissolved, stir gently and turn off the heat to cool.
Prepare the chilies by slicing half and crushing the other half. Thinly slice the garlic and shallots.
2.3. Pickle the pig ears
Next, slice the pig ears into thin, bite-sized pieces, keeping the tendons intact to enjoy the crunchy texture.

Mix the garlic, shallots, chilies, and pig ears with the brine in a bowl, then transfer everything to a container. Use a glass jar and ensure it is dry to prevent spoilage. Store in the refrigerator for 2-3 days before serving.
II. Pickled Pig Ears with Lemongrass and Chili
Pig ears: use the cartilage part from 1 ear
Lemongrass: 4 stalks
Chili: 1 piece
Garlic: 6 cloves
Kumquats: 7 pieces
2. Instructions
To make the brine, boil water with vinegar, sugar, and fish sauce for 5-10 minutes. Season it slightly strong, then turn off the heat to cool.
Boil the cleaned pig ears with garlic and lemongrass for about 20 minutes to remove odors. After boiling, remove and soak in ice water for 10 minutes.
Slice the pig ears into 0.5 cm thick pieces. Thinly slice the lemongrass lengthwise. Cut the kumquats into three rounds (remove seeds to avoid bitterness). Thinly slice the garlic and chilies.
Arrange the pig ears, lemongrass, kumquats, garlic, and chilies in a clean plastic or glass jar. Toss gently. Pour the cooled or slightly warm brine into the jar until fully submerged.
Finally, store the jar in the refrigerator for half a day or a full day before enjoying.
III. Pickled Pig Ears with Sweet and Sour Radish
Pig ears: 2 pieces
Carrots: 2 pieces
White radishes: 2 pieces
Lemongrass: 2 stalks
Ginger: 1 knob
Rice vinegar: 300 ml
Filtered water: 100 ml
Salt: 50 grams
MSG: 1 tsp
Garlic: 4 cloves
Shallots: 4 bulbs
2.1. Boil the pig ears
Clean the pig ears by shaving the hair, rubbing with salt and lemon, then rinsing. Cut the lemongrass in half and crush it; slice the ginger.
Bring water to a boil, add the ginger, lemongrass, a tablespoon of salt, and the pig ears. Boil for 20 minutes. Remove and place in an ice bath.
2.2. Prepare the pickling liquid
Combine 300ml rice vinegar, 100ml water, 350g sugar, 50g salt, and 1 tsp MSG in a pot. Bring to a boil and let cool. Peel and slice the carrots and radishes into bite-sized pieces.

Diagonally slice the horn chilies; leave half of the bird's eye chilies whole and split the other half to remove seeds. Peel and slice the garlic and shallots. Once the pig ears are cooled, slice them into strips along the tendon.

To pickle, once the vinegar-sugar mixture has cooled, combine all ingredients and mix well. Pour into a clean jar, arrange neatly, add green peppercorns, seal tightly, and refrigerate for 1-2 days. It can be stored for up to 2 weeks.
These pickled pig ears are often served with boiled shrimp, shrimp crackers, Vietnamese coriander, fried shallots, and sweet fish sauce, or enjoyed on their own.
IV. How to choose pig ears for a crunchy texture
The pig ear is made of cartilage covered by a thin layer of skin.
It is an essential ingredient for head cheese (giò thủ) and popular in salads, rice paper rolls, or pickling. Its appeal comes from the fatty, chewy, and crunchy texture.
To choose good pig ears, careful observation is key. Select ears that are bright white, firm, elastic to the touch, and free of any foul or strange odors.

While many people hesitate to make this at home due to hygiene concerns, buying from a reliable source and preparing it yourself ensures safety. Remember these cleaning and boiling tips to remove odors and maintain crunchiness for a more appealing dish.

mon_an.ten: Glass Noodle Soup with Chicken Giblets
mon_an.mo_ta: A familiar and essential dish on the Lunar New Year table is glass noodle soup with chicken giblets. With the aroma of shiitake mushrooms, the chewy-crunchy texture of chicken gizzards, and a savory broth, this dish will enhance your family meal!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Chicken giblets (can include unlaid eggs) - 2 sets
Wood ear and shiitake mushrooms - 100 gr
Shallots, fresh onions, cilantro, Vietnamese coriander - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: Soak the glass noodles in water until softened.
Step 2: Soak the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms in water until expanded. Rinse the wood ear and trim the stems off the shiitake mushrooms.
Step 3: Clean and finely chop the Vietnamese coriander and green onions.
Step 4: Thinly julienne the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms.
Step 5: Clean the chicken giblets, slice into bite-sized pieces, and marinate with a little seasoning.
Step 6: Drain the soaked glass noodles, rinse, and cut into manageable lengths.
Step 7: Stir-fry the marinated giblets with the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms until cooked.

Step 8: Bring the bone broth to a boil and season to taste. Blanch the glass noodles in the broth, then transfer to a bowl. Top with the stir-fried giblets and herbs, then pour the hot broth over the noodles.
Enjoy your meal!

mon_an.mo_ta: "Fatty meat, pickled shallots, red couplets / Ritual poles, firecrackers, green bánh chưng." Vietnamese culinary culture has long been summarized in these simple verses passed down through generations. A traditional Tet cannot be complete without fatty meat, bánh chưng, and especially a bowl of pickled shallots. These fragrant, sour, and crunchy shallots reduce the richness of heavy dishes and stimulate the appetite when eaten with traditional Tet foods like jellied meat or bamboo shoot stew.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Shallots - 1kg (Choose according to preference. Young shallots are less pungent and pickle faster. Mature shallots are more fragrant but take longer to pickle)
Salt - As needed (about 70-100g, or to taste; do not use too little or they will spoil)
Vinegar - 2 tbsp (can be replaced with white wine)
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the shallots
Trim the roots and remove the green tops.
Rinse thoroughly and drain.
Step 2: Prepare the brine
Add salt and sugar to the water, bring to a boil, strain any residue, and let cool. When the water is still slightly warm, add the vinegar or wine.
Step 3: Pickling

Clean a glass jar and wipe it dry. Place the drained shallots into the jar and pour the brine in until fully submerged. Use a bamboo grate and a weight to keep the shallots submerged (if they float, they will develop a film and spoil). Seal tightly. They are usually ready in about 10 days. However, if the weather is very cold, it may take 10-15 days.
Note: When the shallots are sour enough, you should move them to a milder brine to keep them longer and prevent them from becoming mushy. You can also store them in the refrigerator.
Step 4: Presentation

Pickled shallots can be eaten immediately, but they are even better if you peel the outer layer, trim the ends, sprinkle with a little chili powder, and toss with a dash of fish sauce for a richer flavor.
It's so simple to make this signature Tet dish. Start making your traditional pickled shallots today!
If you prefer sweet shallots that aren't pungent, you can try the sweet pickling tip.

mon_an.mo_ta: When winter arrives, especially during Tet, jellied meat (aspic) becomes a favorite dish. Usually made from pork hock and skin with mushrooms, you can change things up this year with chicken! Chicken aspic is a signature winter and Tet dish. Discover this simple and delicious recipe.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Gelatin - 4-5 sheets (used here for convenience in cold weather; you can use pork skin instead)
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare ingredients

Place a pot on the stove with 1/2 liter of water, 300g pork skin, 1 tsp salt, and 2-3 ginger slices. Bring to a boil. After 10 minutes, remove the pork skin and drain. Keep the boiling liquid to use as broth for the aspic.
Once the pork skin has cooled, cut it into small, bite-sized pieces. Rinse the chicken with diluted salt water and chop into small serving pieces.
Soak shiitake mushrooms in hot water for 20 minutes until expanded, then rinse and chop.
Boil the wood ear mushrooms briefly, rinse, and chop.
2. Stir-fry the chicken
Marinate the chicken with 1 tsp ground pepper and 2 tsp oyster sauce for 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Sauté 1 tsp minced shallots until fragrant, then add the chicken. Stir-fry for 5 minutes.
Add the pork skin, wood ear, and shiitake mushrooms. Stir-fry for another 5 minutes until the skin firms up. Pour in the broth, reduce heat to low, and simmer for 10 minutes.
Season with 1 tsp seasoning powder and stir. Continue simmering for another 10 minutes so the flavors penetrate the meat.
3. Molding
Place the chicken and mushrooms into a bowl, then pour the broth over until nearly full. Let it cool, then refrigerate for at least 3 hours or preferably overnight.

Once set, enjoy this nutritious dish. The clear jelly allows you to see the ingredients inside. You will taste the sweetness of the chicken, the fragrance of shiitake, the crunch of pork skin, and the texture of wood ear mushrooms.
Notes for making chicken aspic
Choose fresh chicken: Ensure the chicken is fresh for the best taste and safety.
Proper preparation: Clean the chicken well and remove unwanted parts. Chop into small pieces for even cooking.
Marinating: Season according to your taste using salt, pepper, garlic, or shallots.
Boiling: Ensure the water is boiling before adding meat to ensure food safety.
Combine ingredients: Adding mushrooms and pork skin enhances the flavor and texture.
Broth: Use the chicken boiling water as the base for the aspic to retain nutrients and flavor.
Setting time: Refrigerate for at least 3 hours or overnight to allow the flavors to meld and the jelly to set firmly.
How to choose quality ingredients
1. Choosing pork skin
Selection: Choose skin from the loin or shoulder area. This part is crunchier than other areas.
Thickness: Look for thick, flat, large pieces for easier preparation.
Color: Good skin should be pinkish, not too white, and free of bruises or odors. It should be elastic when pressed.
2. Choosing mushrooms
For wood ear mushrooms:
Selection: Choose large, thick ears with few small mushrooms at the base.
Color: Good wood ear is dark amber on top and milky coffee-colored underneath.
Avoid: Do not buy mushrooms that are too black, as they may become mushy when soaked and lack crunch.

mon_an.mo_ta: If you are used to boiled, fried, or braised chicken, try this variation for a completely different flavor. These chicken spring rolls (nem gà) are not only visually appealing but also nutritious, adding a fresh touch to your Tet holiday meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Chili paste (sa tế), soy sauce, cornstarch, fish sauce - 1 tsp each
cac_buoc: Step 1: Rinse the chicken and finely dice.
Step 2: Peel and mince the garlic and ginger.
Step 3: Rinse the lemongrass, remove the tough outer layers, and mince.
Step 4: Rinse the bell pepper and finely dice.
Step 5: Rinse the mustard leaves and julienne.
Step 6: Combine all prepared ingredients in a large bowl.
Step 7: Add 1 tsp chili paste, soy sauce, fish sauce, cornstarch, and the juice of 1/3 of a lemon. Add the diced chicken, mix thoroughly, and marinate for 15-30 minutes.
Step 8: Heat oil in a pan and stir-fry the chicken mixture until cooked.

Step 9: Transfer the chicken to a plate, squeeze in a little lemon juice, add the julienned mustard leaves and one egg yolk. Mix well and let cool slightly. You can add 1 tsp of sugar if you prefer a sweeter filling.
Step 10: Lay out a sheet of rice paper, add the chicken filling, and roll tightly and evenly.
Step 11: Repeat until the filling is gone. Heat oil in a pan and fry the rolls over medium heat (since the filling is already cooked) until the wrapper is golden and crispy.
Step 12: Remove the rolls and place on paper towels to drain excess oil. Arrange on a plate and serve hot with sweet and sour dipping sauce.

mon_an.mo_ta: Nem Nắm Hải Hậu is a specialty of Nam Dinh province. This dish is indispensable for holidays, weddings, or family gatherings. It is easy to make with simple ingredients. Let's try it!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fig leaves, polyscias fruticosa leaves (đinh lăng), chili, MSG, salt, lemon - as needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: Separate the skin and the lean meat from the pork ham. Rinse and boil until cooked, then remove and let cool. (Note: The skin cooks faster, so remove it 2-3 minutes after the water boils).

Step 2: Once cooled, julienne the skin into thin strips and finely mince the lean meat. Place them in a pot. Mix thoroughly with minced garlic and roasted rice powder. Add a small amount of sugar, MSG, and salt (be careful not to over-salt as it will be dipped in fish sauce later).
Step 3: Squeeze the mixture into firm, small balls and arrange on a plate.
Preparing the dipping sauce
Take 1/3 cup of water, add 1 tbsp sugar, and stir until dissolved.
Add 2 tbsp fish sauce to the bowl.
Add minced garlic, chili, and the juice of half a lemon.

To eat, take a small piece of Nem Nắm, wrap it in a fig leaf and a polyscias leaf, and dip it into the sauce. This dish can also be served with rice vermicelli rolls for a delicious and beautiful meal.

mon_an.mo_ta: A guide to making delicious chicken phở to refresh your palate during Tet. According to Vietnamese tradition, boiled chicken brings luck in the New Year, making it a staple for New Year's Eve and the first day of Tet. While boiled chicken with lemon-pepper salt is classic, eating it for days can become tiring. This recipe transforms leftover or fresh chicken into a refreshing noodle soup. Northern-style phở gà is simple, using chicken, cinnamon, star anise, cilantro, scallions, and ginger. Let's try this family recipe.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Chicken - 1/2 or 1 whole chicken depending on serving size
cac_buoc: Step 1: Boil the chicken
You can use leftover boiled chicken from offerings, but here are the steps for fresh chicken:

Clean the chicken, rub with salt, and rinse. Place in a pot with cold water, a pinch of salt, crushed ginger, and shallots. Bring to a boil, then simmer on low for 10-15 minutes to prevent the skin from tearing. Flip the chicken for even cooking.

Turn off the heat and let the chicken soak in the pot for a while to finish cooking, then remove. Submerge in ice water to make the skin firm and crunchy. You can brush the skin with chicken fat rendered with turmeric for a beautiful yellow color.
Step 2: Shred the chicken
Once cooled, debone the chicken. Set the bones, head, feet, and neck aside. Shred or slice the meat into bite-sized pieces.
Step 3: Cook the broth
Put the bones back into the chicken boiling water (you can add pork bones for more sweetness if desired).

Char the ginger and shallots over a flame until fragrant, peel, and crush. Toast the cinnamon, star anise, and coriander seeds until fragrant. Place them in a spice bag with the ginger and shallots and drop into the broth. Simmer for 15-20 minutes, then season with salt and seasoning powder to taste.
Tip: In Southern Vietnam, people prefer a sweeter broth; you can add a bit of rock sugar.
Step 4: Blanch the noodles
Blanch the phở noodles in boiling water and drain. If using fresh large sheets, cut them into strands before blanching. If using dried noodles, boil until tender.
Step 5: Presentation
Place the noodles in a bowl. Top with thinly sliced onions (optional), chopped green onions, cilantro, sawtooth herb, and the white parts of the scallions (slivered).
Tip: In the South, phở is often served with bean sprouts and herbs, while the North usually doesn't. Add greens according to your preference.
Step 6: Pour the hot broth over the noodles and enjoy your delicious phở gà.
Source: candycancook.com
Phở gà is nutritious yet light. It's perfect for breakfast or a main meal. On a cold day, a bowl of hot phở with a squeeze of lemon and some fried dough sticks (quẩy) is unbeatable!

mon_an.mo_ta: Apples are excellent for your health, offering anti-aging benefits and helping to prevent cardiovascular diseases. The acids in apples help combat obesity, while the fiber aids digestion. Apples are widely loved for their delicious flavor and versatility. Today, we share the secret to making Warm Winter Apple Cider, a healthy drink that puts a twist on a familiar favorite. You can make this in large batches and store it to enjoy gradually!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Mix all the ingredients together and simmer for about 10 minutes, or keep on low heat to stay warm.
Step 2:
Pour into glasses and garnish with a slice of orange, lemon, or a cinnamon stick. Serve while warm.
Allow to cool, then pour the Warm Winter Apple Cider into a clean glass bottle, seal tightly, and store in a cool place.
Source: ST

mon_an.ten: Sweet and Sour Pickled Pig Ears for Tet
mon_an.mo_ta: Every year, my mother makes this dish for Tet, and my father and brother absolutely love it. After getting married, I asked for her secret recipe to make it for my in-laws, and now my father-in-law and husband are huge fans too. I often make these pickled pig ears as a drinking snack for them; it pairs perfectly. Now, this dish is an indispensable part of our family's Tet holiday. I noticed online that some people sell these for quite a high price, so I'm sharing this delicious and affordable homemade version. Give it a try!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Glass jar - Used for pickling; remember to choose one with a lid
Pig ears - Quantity as desired; I usually make 2-3 at a time to eat gradually
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the pig ears

Clean the pig ears thoroughly. I usually blanch them in boiling water, then remove and scrape them clean. Rub with salt and lemon to remove any odors. Place the ears in a pot and boil until cooked through. Remove and immediately submerge in a bowl of cold water mixed with a little vinegar until completely cooled. This keeps the ears white and crunchy.
Step 2: Prepare the sweet and sour pickling liquid.
Use the water used to soak the ears, skim off any fat, and boil it with sugar, vinegar, and fish sauce. Add sliced garlic, then let the liquid cool completely.
Step 3: Pickle the pig ears
Place the cooked pig ears from Step 1 into a clean, dry glass jar. Pour the cooled pickling liquid from Step 2 over them until fully submerged. Add fresh chilies (sliced or whole) and sliced garlic.
Step 4: Presentation and Storage
Use bamboo slats to press the ears down so they stay submerged (if you don't have slats, a small plate or bowl works too). Cover tightly and let sit for 3-5 days.

When serving, slice the ears into thin strips and arrange on a plate. It can be served with fresh herbs or enjoyed as a drinking snack. The remaining pig ears can be stored in the refrigerator for 2-3 weeks.
Each thin slice of pickled pig ear is sweet, sour, and fragrant with vinegar, garlic, fish sauce, and a kick of chili. You can easily present it beautifully as shown in the image.
After finishing the ears, don't discard the pickling liquid. Since it's made with good fish sauce and balanced flavors, you can use it as a dipping sauce for spring rolls or bún chả.

mon_an.ten: Creative Ways to Prepare Bánh Chưng After Tet
mon_an.mo_ta: If you have leftover bánh chưng after Tet, transform it into this incredibly delicious and attractive sweet potato-wrapped fried bánh chưng! You will surely love it.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Combine coconut milk, water, tapioca starch, and sugar in a pot. Stir well and cook over low heat until the mixture boils and thickens.
Step 2: Finely chop the scallions (about 1/2 bowl). Heat 1/3 bowl of cooking oil until smoking hot, then pour it over the scallions to make scallion oil.
Step 3: Peel and dice the sweet potato, boil until tender, then drain.
Add 1/2 tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar, and 1 tsp scallion oil to the potatoes.
Wear plastic gloves and mash the potatoes until smooth and well-seasoned.
Step 4: Roast the peanuts, peel, and crush them. Slice the bánh chưng and steam until soft.

Step 5: Place the softened bánh chưng into a plastic bag. Dampen a clean towel, wring it dry, and wrap it around the bag. Knead the bánh chưng like bread dough until the glutinous rice forms a smooth, pliable mass.
Step 6: Prepare a clean sheet of plastic wrap. Flatten the rice dough on the plastic into a rectangular shape.
Step 7: Spread the mashed sweet potato over the rice, then roll it up and deep-fry until golden brown. Once the rice is crispy and golden, remove and place on paper towels.

Use scissors to cut the roll into small squares. Drizzle with the coconut sauce, then the scallion oil, and finally the crushed peanuts. If you don't like coconut milk, you can substitute it with chili sauce.

mon_an.mo_ta: Check out this recipe for delicious chicken aspic to serve your family during the upcoming Tet holidays!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings: A dash of fish sauce, seasoning powder, MSG
cac_buoc: Required ingredients:
Step 1: Wash the chicken and drain. Debone the chicken and set the bones aside; cut the meat into bite-sized pieces.
