Industrial layer chickens look similar to free-range chickens, so distinguish them carefully. Free-range skin is pale yellow, darker only on the breast, wings, and back, while industrial chickens are white or uniformly yellow (possibly from toxic dyes).
To identify dyed chicken, observe if the skin is yellow but the fat underneath is white; this indicates chemical dyeing.
Free-range skin is thin, smooth, and elastic. Choose fresh-looking chicken with no odors or
antibiotic smells, and no bruises or blood clots on the skin.
Avoid chickens with dark, dull skin, as they may have died before being slaughtered.
To avoid water-injected chicken, press suspected areas (thighs, breast); if mushy, slippery, or deformed, do not buy it. Injected water is often mixed with borax (according to some shop owners).
Live chicken
When choosing live chicken, observe the following:
The chicken should be healthy and active. The comb should be bright red, eyes alert, and feathers shiny and smooth
The beak should be sharp with no discharge.
The legs should be straight and slender; the skin should be evenly yellow and shiny

mon_an.mo_ta: This chili lime grilled chicken is visually appealing with its beautiful golden-brown skin, tender and flavorful meat, and a wonderful aroma.
cac_buoc: How to make Chili Lime Grilled Chicken Step 1:
Clean the chicken thighs with salt to remove any odors, then rinse thoroughly with water. Once drained, place them in a baking dish. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and marinate for about 10 minutes.
Step 2:
In a small bowl, squeeze the lime juice. Add olive oil, garlic, chili powder, and chili sauce. Stir well until the ingredients are fully combined.
Step 3:
Use a small spoon to pour the marinade over each chicken thigh until they are well coated. If there is any leftover sauce, pour it directly into the baking dish.
Step 4:
Once the sauce is added, cover the baking dish with foil and refrigerate for 2 hours to allow the flavors to penetrate the meat.
Step 5:
Preheat the oven to 190°C. Bake for 1 hour. When the chicken is cooked through and has a beautiful golden-brown color, remove it and serve on a plate. Enjoy with rice and vegetables.
Notes for a delicious grilled chicken dish
This chili lime grilled chicken is visually appealing with its beautiful golden-brown skin, tender and flavorful meat, and a wonderful aroma.
How to choose good chicken:
Live chicken

To buy healthy, disease-free chickens, avoid those with pale or purple combs, lethargic behavior, runny beaks, dull eyes, drooping wings, or a tired appearance with their heads constantly tucked down.

Additionally, do not choose chickens with wrinkled skin, thin bodies, bony breasts, or frayed feathers. Specifically, avoid chickens with cold, dry feet; a pale or red anus; or those with discharge or droppings around the vent, as these are signs of illness.
Only choose chickens that look healthy and active. The comb should be bright red, and the eyes should be alert. Feathers should be shiny and smooth against the body.
The crop should not feel too full or too empty. Observe the droppings (should be firm), the comb should be upright, the breast firm, and there should be no wheezing sounds.
Pre-processed chicken
Local free-range chickens (gà ta) usually have a compact, firm body and a narrow breast.

Egg-laying chickens can look similar, so distinguish them carefully. Local chicken skin is pale yellow, only darker on the breast, wings, and back, while industrial egg-layers are often white or yellow all over (possibly due to harmful dyes).
The skin should be thin and highly elastic. Choose meat that looks fresh, without any foul or antibiotic smell, and no bruises or blood clots on the skin.
To avoid water-injected chicken, press on areas like the thighs or breast; if it feels mushy, slippery, or deforms easily, avoid it.

mon_an.ten: Coconut Heart Salad with Shrimp and Pork
mon_an.mo_ta: Coconut heart salad with shrimp and pork is a unique dish that will surely delight you from the first bite. This salad features eye-catching colors, delicious flavors, fresh shrimp and pork, crunchy coconut heart, and a savory dressing that provides a wonderful dining experience.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - fish sauce, salt, sugar, vinegar, cooking oil
cac_buoc: How to make Coconut Heart Salad with Shrimp and Pork
Step 1:
Choose the tender part of the coconut heart, discard the tough parts, and slice thinly. Soak in cold water, then rinse and drain well.
Step 2:

Wash the pork belly and boil it with a bit of seasoning until cooked, then slice thinly. You can add a grilled shallot and a few shiitake mushrooms to the boiling water to make the meat more fragrant.
Trim the whiskers off the shrimp and wash them with a bit of rice wine to remove the fishy smell. Rinse with water, boil until cooked, and peel, leaving the tails intact for presentation.
Step 3:
Peel and wash the onion, slice thinly, and soak in a mixture of vinegar and sugar to remove the pungency while maintaining its crunch.
Step 4:
Wash the cucumber and soak it in salt water. Rinse again, drain, cut in half, and slice diagonally.
Peel the carrot, wash, and julienne.
Remove the roots and tough stems from the Vietnamese coriander and cilantro, wash the tender parts, and chop finely.
Step 5:
Roast the peanuts, peel, and crush them slightly.
Peel, wash, and mince the garlic.
Wash and slice the chilies.
Cut the lime and squeeze for juice.
Peel and wash the shallots, drain, slice thinly, and fry until golden and fragrant.
Step 6:

Prepare the dressing: In a small bowl, combine 1.5 tbsp fish sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp lime juice, minced garlic, and chili. Adjust the ratio according to the type of fish sauce and your taste. Stir until the sugar is completely dissolved.
Step 7:

In a large bowl, combine the coconut heart, carrot, cucumber, and onion. Slowly pour in 2/3 of the dressing and toss well. Let it sit for 5 minutes to absorb the flavors. Add the shrimp, pork, and the remaining dressing, then toss again and adjust seasoning to taste.
Step 8:
Finally, transfer the salad to a plate and top with chopped herbs, roasted peanuts, and fried shallots.
Notes for a fresh and delicious coconut heart salad
How to choose fresh shrimp:
Check the shrimp tail

To determine freshness, stretch the shrimp out and hold it up to the light to check the space between the shell segments and the meat. Wider gaps indicate the shrimp is not fresh, as it may have been cooked too long or frozen for a long time.
Avoid slimy shrimp

Do not buy shrimp that feel slimy. These shrimp often curl into a circle rather than lying straight. To check, run your finger over the shell from front to back and vice versa. If it feels gritty or sticky, do not buy them.
Shrimp legs
Check if the legs are still firmly attached to the body; the meat should be firm. Avoid shrimp with legs that have turned black, as this is a sign they are no longer fresh.

mon_an.ten: Pork Stomach and Lotus Root Salad
mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little time in the kitchen and simple ingredients, you can make this delicious, unique, and refreshing pork stomach and lotus root salad. Its crunchy texture and vibrant flavors will surely satisfy your palate.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green onions, Vietnamese coriander - a little
Seasoning - Fish sauce, sugar, garlic, chili, vinegar or white wine
cac_buoc: HOW TO MAKE PORK STOMACH AND LOTUS ROOT SALAD

Step 1: Clean the pork stomach thoroughly using vinegar or white wine to remove odors. Boil the stomach in water with 1 tbsp of salt. Once cooked, remove and soak in a bowl of ice water to keep it white and crunchy. Finally, drain and slice thinly into bite-sized pieces.
Step 2: Peel and wash the carrot. Slice the onion and chili into thin strips about 3-4 cm long.
Step 3: Wash the lotus roots, cut into 3-4 cm segments, and split them in half. Soak the lotus roots in cool boiled water with a few slices of lime and a pinch of salt.

Step 4: Peel and slice the carrot and onion into bite-sized pieces. Julienne the bell peppers into 2-3 cm strips. Bring a pot of water to a boil and blanch the lotus roots and carrots very briefly; remove them immediately to keep them crunchy. Drain and place in a clean bowl.
Step 5: Prepare the dressing: Mix 3 tbsp fish sauce, 5 tbsp lime juice, and 3 tbsp sugar in a bowl with minced garlic and chili. Stir well (adjust the ratio to suit your taste).

Step 6: Combine the pork stomach with the lotus roots, carrots, and onions. Slowly pour the dressing over the mixture. Toss gently, then add chopped Vietnamese coriander and toss once more. (Mix the ingredients 10-15 minutes before serving to ensure the vegetables stay crunchy).
Finally, plate the salad and enjoy immediately.
How to choose good pork stomach:
Choose stomach from healthy pigs: This is the most important safety factor. Buy from a trusted source, avoid frozen products, and ensure there is no unpleasant odor.

Visual check: A good stomach should have an even color without any abnormalities or spots. Naturally, the back of the stomach is light brown (turning darker when boiled), and the inside is creamy white with a protective membrane. Once cleaned, it should appear bright white.
Check the thickness: A stomach about 2-3 cm thick is ideal. It will be crunchy and fragrant when eaten. This usually comes from large, healthy pigs and will provide the best culinary experience.

With just a little time in the kitchen and simple ingredients, you can make this delicious, unique, and refreshing pork stomach and lotus root salad. Its crunchy texture and vibrant flavors will surely satisfy your palate.

mon_an.ten: Pork Tongue Salad with Sour Bamboo Shoots
mon_an.mo_ta: Pork tongue salad with spicy and sour bamboo shoots is a unique dish that will captivate you from the very first bite. With eye-catching colors, crunchy pork tongue infused with seasonings, and the crisp texture of sour bamboo shoots and vegetables, this dish offers a truly appetizing experience.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, 2 tbsp high-quality fish sauce, 2 tbsp lime juice or vinegar, and a little salt
cac_buoc: How to make pork tongue salad with spicy and sour bamboo shoots
Step 1:

Choosing pork tongue: When buying, choose fresh ones with a thick, round tongue, bright color, and a white throat area without blood clots. After purchasing, lightly rinse the tongue. Boil a pot of water until simmering, then add the tongue and blanch for about 5 minutes before turning off the heat. Remove the tongue and immediately rinse under cold running water.

Next, use a knife to thoroughly scrape off the white membrane on the tongue, as this layer carries a strong odor and will make the tongue smell if left on after boiling. Scrape the throat area and both sides of the tongue, then rinse under running water and drain.

Then, use half a lime to squeeze out the juice and rub the tongue thoroughly with grain salt to remove any remaining odor and whiten the tongue. Rub well and rinse 1-2 times under running water, then drain to prepare for cooking.

Once the tongue is cleaned, boil it with a few slices of crushed ginger until cooked through. Add a little salt to make the meat firmer and tastier. When the tongue is cooked, remove it and soak immediately in ice water, then slice thinly.
Step 2:
Peel the garlic and bird's eye chilies, wash them, and mince finely.

Prepare the dressing: Combine 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sugar, and 2 tbsp fish sauce in a small bowl, stirring until the sugar dissolves. Then, add the minced garlic and chili. Mix the dressing with a few tablespoons of lime juice or vinegar, adjusting to taste. For this dish, the dressing should be spicy to be truly delicious.
Step 3:
Pick the culantro and Vietnamese coriander, removing the roots and wilted leaves. Wash thoroughly, drain, and roughly chop.
Peel the onion, wash it, and slice it horizontally or vertically. If you cannot eat raw onions, you can quickly blanch them in boiling water.
Peel the carrot, wash it, and slice or shred it into bite-sized matchsticks.
Step 4:
Roast the white sesame seeds and peanuts until golden brown.
After roasting the peanuts, let them cool slightly, then rub off the skins and split them in half.
Step 5:
Next, mix the pork tongue, sour bamboo shoots, onion, carrot, Vietnamese coriander, culantro, and the prepared dressing together. Adjust the seasoning to taste.
Finally, arrange the salad on a plate and sprinkle the roasted sesame seeds and peanuts on top to enhance the flavor and appeal.

Pork tongue salad with spicy and sour bamboo shoots is a unique dish that will captivate you from the very first bite. With eye-catching colors, crunchy pork tongue infused with seasonings, and the crisp texture of sour bamboo shoots and vegetables, this dish offers a truly appetizing experience.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried kimchi with tofu features hot, delicious, and nutritious tofu pieces paired with crunchy kimchi and fresh pork, providing a delightful dining experience.
cac_buoc: How to make stir-fried kimchi with tofu:
Step 1: Prepare kimchi and onion:
First, cut 250g of kimchi into bite-sized pieces.
Next, peel and wash the onion, then cut it in half and slice thinly.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the green onions, wash them, and cut into 2-3cm segments.
Step 2: Marinate the pork:
Mix 2 tbsp chili powder with 3 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp minced garlic, 1 tsp minced ginger, 2 tsp sugar, ½ tsp pepper, and 1 tbsp rice wine. Stir well until all ingredients are combined.
Add the sliced pork to the marinade and mix well to coat. Let the pork marinate for 15-20 minutes so the flavors penetrate deeply, making the meat tastier.
Step 3: Stir-fry the kimchi:

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Once hot, add the marinated pork and stir-fry for 3 minutes over medium heat. Then, add the kimchi and stir-fry over medium heat for 4 minutes. Stir until the kimchi and meat are slightly dry.
Step 4: Finishing:

Once the meat and kimchi have firmed up, add the onion and green onions and stir-fry for another 2 minutes or until the pork is fully cooked. Turn off the heat and add 1 tsp sesame seeds and 1 tsp sesame oil, tossing well to combine.
Step 5: Blanch the tofu:
Boil about 2-3 cups of water in a pot, then add ½ tsp salt and the tofu. Blanch the tofu for 3 minutes. If the tofu is already clean, you can skip this step.
Step 6: Cut the tofu:
Cut the tofu into rectangular pieces approximately 3cm x 4cm x 1cm. You can use other sizes, but keep the thickness around 1cm. If possible, keep the tofu warm until serving.
Step 7: Plating:
Place the kimchi on a plate and arrange the tofu pieces around it. You can sprinkle some white sesame seeds on top for garnish and enjoy.
Tips for delicious stir-fried kimchi with tofu
For the pork, choose the shoulder or belly cut. You can use beef instead, but pork is the ideal pairing for kimchi.
You can use other types of alcohol, but do not omit it, as it helps the marinade create a better flavor for the meat.
You can microwave the tofu for 2-3 minutes instead of boiling it. Alternatively, you can steam the tofu.
For a vegetarian version, omit the pork and increase the amount of kimchi.
This stir-fried kimchi with tofu dish is visually appealing with fresh kimchi, well-seasoned pork that is tender yet slightly crisp on the outside, offering a wonderful taste for everyone.

mon_an.mo_ta: With just a little time in the kitchen and familiar ingredients, you can make delicious crispy fried stuffed pork intestines to treat your family and friends. The dish features a crispy outer skin and a savory, rich meat filling. Serve it with chili sauce or sweet and sour dipping sauce for a delightful meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - Seasoning salt, cooking oil, pepper, MSG, oyster sauce
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the pork intestines thoroughly upon purchase and drain. (You should use vinegar or lime to wash the intestines and remove any fishy odor).
Step 2: Soak the wood ear and shiitake mushrooms in cold water until fully expanded. Trim the stems, wash thoroughly, and mince.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the green onions, wash, and mince.
Step 3: Peel the carrots, wash, shred, and mince.
Roast the peanuts, let them cool, and remove the skins.
In a bowl, combine the minced pork, mushrooms, and green onions. Season with ½ tsp seasoning salt, 1 tsp pepper, 1 tbsp oyster sauce, 1 tsp MSG, and ½ tbsp fish sauce.
Step 4: Mix well by hand until the ingredients are thoroughly combined into a uniform mixture.
Step 5: Use a funnel or a plastic bottle cap to stuff the meat mixture into the intestines. Stuff evenly (not too tightly) until all ingredients are used, then tie the ends with string.
Step 6: Place the stuffed intestines in a steamer and steam over boiling water.

Step 7: Once the intestines are cooked, prick them with a toothpick to release excess liquid. Cut into sections and fry until golden brown. Remember to turn them frequently so they cook evenly and develop an attractive color.
Step 8: Finally, slice the intestines into bite-sized pieces and arrange them on a plate. Serve with chili sauce or sweet and sour fish sauce.
Tips for delicious stuffed pork intestines
How to choose good pork intestines:

You should buy small, round, pinkish intestines; these are the best quality. Small intestines can sometimes be bitter, so choose small ones with firm, round tubes and milky white fluid inside. Intestines with large diameters, thin walls, or yellow fluid inside are usually old, chewy, and prone to bitterness.
After buying, turn them inside out and wipe away the mucus, or pump water through them to flush out the slime quickly and cleanly.
To remove the odor, use lime juice or vinegar to rub the intestines. Then rinse with salt water to disinfect and clean them once more.
Next, quickly blanch the intestines in hot water so they firm up slightly, then wipe them clean one last time.
How to boil intestines to keep them white and crunchy

When boiling, add a few crushed grilled shallots to the pot. Once the water boils, drop the intestines in. When cooked, remove and soak them in a bowl of diluted vinegar water to keep them white and crunchy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chả ốc is a rich and savory dish that has become a popular choice in Vietnamese cuisine. With the unique flavor of sea snails and a delicate blend of spices, this dish not only captivates food lovers but also adds variety and appeal to any feast. Let's explore how to cook delicious snail patties! Here is a detailed guide to making chả ốc at home, from preparation to cooking.
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the apple snails

Soak the apple snails in rice water for 2-3 hours to make them release slime, adding a sliced chili to speed up the process. Then, wash the snails under a strong stream of water and use a brush to scrub the slime off the shells and mouths.
Next, boil the snails in a pot over high heat for about 7-10 minutes with 3 stalks of cut lemongrass and 1/2 a crushed ginger bulb.
Once the snails open their mouths after about 10 minutes, extract the meat using a sharp tool. Wash the snail meat with diluted salt water mixed with a bit of vinegar, then rinse with clean water.
Finally, drain the cleaned snail meat in a basket, then put it in a blender and mince it.
Soak shiitake mushrooms in warm water for about 10 minutes until soft, then wash them. You can mince the mushrooms with a knife or use a blender.
After buying the pork, soak it in diluted salt water, then rinse with clean water. Mince the pork using a blender or a knife.
Mince the shallots and green onions after removing the roots and skins. Wash the remaining lemongrass stalks after removing the old outer leaves.
2. Mix the snail patty mixture
Combine the minced snail meat, minced pork, pork paste, minced shiitake mushrooms, green onions, and shallots. Add 20g of potato starch and mix well until all ingredients are fully incorporated.
Next, marinate the mixture with: 1 tsp fish sauce, 1/2 tsp seasoning powder, 1/3 tsp MSG, and 1/2 tsp ground pepper (or whole peppercorns).
Mix the snail patty mixture until it is soft and pliable, then let it rest for 5-10 minutes to absorb the seasonings.
3. Shaping and steaming

After washing the lemongrass, separate the leaves and cut them into short segments (about the length of an index finger) to line the snail mouths. Use a spoon to stuff half of the mixture into the snail shells until full. With the remaining half, you can form them into round balls and flatten them into thin patties.
Once the shells are stuffed, arrange the snails and the flattened patties in a steamer. Place the pot on the stove and steam for about 5-10 minutes.
When the surface of the patties has firmed up, mix 3 tbsp egg yolk with 3 tbsp water and stir well.
Next, use a brush to smoothly coat the inside of the snail mouths and the surface of the patties to create an attractive golden color. Steam for another 5 minutes until fully cooked.
4. Prepare the dipping sauce
In a bowl, combine the following: 1 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp sugar, 5 tbsp water, 1/2 tbsp lime juice, and minced garlic.
If desired, add 1/2 tbsp ginger juice or 1/2 a minced ginger bulb for aroma, and 1 minced chili. For a spicier kick, add a few chili slices.

The result is a plate of fragrant apple snail patties with a crunchy, chewy texture, paired with a light sweet and sour dipping sauce, creating a special and attractive flavor. You can enjoy chả ốc with steamed rice, fresh rice vermicelli, or raw vegetables to enhance the experience.
Tips for delicious snail patties

How to choose good snails: Choose fat snails with the operculum (trapdoor) located close to the outside. When still, the snail body often pokes out and retracts quickly when touched. Snails with the operculum deep inside are thin or have been kept too long and are not tasty, or may even be dead.
How to clean snails thoroughly:
1. Soak in rice water: Use rice water to soak the snails for 2-3 hours; they will release slime and dirt into the water as slimy crumbs. Then just rinse the snails several times with clean water.
2. Soak with a knife: Drop a small metal knife into the soaking water. The smell of the metal in the water stimulates the snails to release mud and dirt faster and more thoroughly.

3. For a quick but effective soak, you can also soak snails in water mixed with vinegar and minced fresh chili for a few hours. However, snails soaked this way should be cooked immediately to maintain freshness.

4. For stuffed snails, do not break the apex (tail) of the shell, as the sweet juices will leak out during steaming. Use a small knife to gently pry the mouth open, use a chopstick to push the snail inward for a moment, then shake the snail vigorously.
5. The snail will fall out. Discard the muddy part at the end. Take the remaining meat, rub it thoroughly with vinegar, and rinse with cold water until clean.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chicken has long been a staple for Vietnamese people, from boiled chicken to ginger-braised chicken. To diversify your family meals, today we will guide you through making sesame chicken stir-fry. This dish features the aroma of sesame, the savory taste of seasonings, and the sweetness of chicken. It is perfect when served with a bowl of hot rice after a hard day's work. Let's start learning how to cook this delicious sesame chicken.
cac_buoc: Learn how to cook delicious sesame chicken stir-fry now:
Step 1: Prepare a mixture of honey, minced garlic, and soy sauce.
Step 2: Add the sesame seeds and sesame oil to the mixture above and stir well with a whisk.
Step 3: Dice the onion and bell peppers. Wash the chicken and marinate with salt and pepper for a while to enhance the flavor.
Step 4: Whisk the egg whites with cornstarch in a bowl. Then, add the marinated chicken to this mixture and toss to coat evenly.
We are halfway through making this delicious sesame chicken stir-fry, let's continue!
Step 5: Place a pan on the stove and wait until hot, then add a little oil. Sauté the bell peppers and onion over medium heat until softened, then remove to a plate.
Step 6: Add the chicken to the pan and stir-fry until it turns golden brown.
Step 7: Once the chicken is golden brown, add the sautéed bell peppers and onion back into the pan.
Step 8: Finally, pour in the mixture from Step 2. Cook until the liquid in the pan boils, then reduce the heat and stir-fry for another 1-2 minutes until finished.

mon_an.mo_ta: The sweet and sour taste of tamarind sauce, combined with a hint of heat from chili and ginger and the crunchy texture of well-seasoned squid, creates an irresistible dish. With just a little time in the kitchen, you can prepare this delicious meal for your family and friends!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - seasoning powder, fish sauce, salt, pepper, sugar, cooking oil
cac_buoc: How to make Sweet and Sour Tamarind Squid
Step 1: Soak the sweet tamarind in hot water until soft, then press through a sieve to collect the pulp.
Peel and wash the ginger; julienne 2/3 of it and mince the remaining 1/3.
Peel, wash, and mince the garlic.
Wash and slice the chilies.

Step 2: Clean the squid and peel off the light purple outer skin. Rub the squid briefly with half of the minced ginger and a little white wine to remove any fishy odor. Drain and cut the squid into bite-sized pieces.

Step 3: Marinate the squid with a little seasoning powder, pepper, the remaining minced ginger, and half of the tamarind pulp. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for about 15 minutes to let the flavors absorb.
Step 4: Place a pan over heat and add cooking oil. Once the oil is very hot, sear the squid briefly, then remove and set aside.

Step 5: Drain most of the excess oil from the pan, leaving about 1 tablespoon. Sauté the minced garlic until fragrant. Once the garlic is golden, add the remaining tamarind pulp, fish sauce, sugar, and chili. Season to taste and simmer for 1-2 minutes until the sauce thickens.

Step 6: When the sauce has thickened and tastes right, return the fried squid to the pan. Toss well so the sauce coats the squid evenly. Turn off the heat, transfer to a plate, garnish with the julienned ginger, and enjoy.
How to choose fresh squid
Check the color
For fresh squid, the brown parts should be deep brown rather than pale, and the white parts should be as opaque as milk. Both colors should have a bright, glossy sheen.
Feel the firmness

Press your finger into the body of the squid. Fresh squid is usually firm with high elasticity, meaning it quickly returns to its original shape after you release your finger. If it is not fresh, the flesh will feel soft or flabby and won't bounce back quickly.
Observe the eyes

Checking the eyes is a very effective method. Fresh squid usually has very bright, clear eyes where you can clearly see the pupils. If the squid is no longer fresh, the eyes will be blurry and cloudy.
Check the tentacles

Flip the tentacles over to check the suckers. If the suckers are intact and firmly attached to the tentacles, the squid is very fresh. If they are falling off, the squid is no longer good. Additionally, fresh squid has firm tentacles, while stale squid will feel soft and mushy.

mon_an.mo_ta: This beef and kimchi salad features tender beef, well-absorbed seasonings, slightly spicy kimchi, and crunchy pickled greens. Served with hot rice, it's a dish that will make your rice cooker empty in no time!
cac_buoc: Wash the beef and boil it in a pot of lightly salted water until cooked. Remove and submerge in a bowl of cooled boiled water. Drain and slice into thin, bite-sized pieces.
Squeeze the excess liquid from the kimchi and cut into short, bite-sized pieces.
Rinse the pickled mustard greens with cooled boiled water, then squeeze very dry to reduce the saltiness. Cut into bite-sized pieces.
Peel and trim the onion, wash it, then slice thinly. Soak the slices in vinegar to reduce the pungency and make them crunchier.
Wash the chilies, remove the seeds, and mince.
Trim the roots and wilted leaves from the culantro, wash, and chop finely.

Next, combine all ingredients including beef, kimchi, pickled greens, culantro, and chili in a bowl and toss well. Season to taste. Note: Since kimchi and pickled greens are already salty, you may not need much extra seasoning if you prefer a milder taste.
Add the vinegar-soaked onions and mix well. Let the salad sit for 10 minutes to allow the flavors to meld.
Finally, arrange the salad on a plate, decorate as desired, sprinkle with sesame seeds, and enjoy.
How to choose good beef

When buying, choose meat that is bright red (not too dark) with small fibers. It should be dry, fine-grained, firm, and not sticky to the touch. Yellow fat indicates the meat will be tender and rich. Young beef has white fat and very fine-grained, tender meat. Old beef has large, dark red fibers and grayish fat; it is tough and takes a long time to cook. Meat from a heifer is generally better than from a bull. If you can find young heifer beef (bò tơ), it is the best choice for its tenderness, white fat, and fine grain.
Beef that is pale green or has white spots between the fibers may be infected with parasites or cysts. Do not buy meat that has an unpleasant odor.
Distinguishing buffalo from beef
You can identify buffalo meat immediately: it is usually a pale pinkish-red with large fibers and a deep purple-red hue, but the fat is whiter than beef fat.
For this salad, you can use tenderloin or shank, but we recommend beef shank for a sweeter taste and a more interesting, slightly chewy texture.
How to use beef for different dishes
For stir-fries: Use fillet or tenderloin. When stir-fried, the meat will be tender without being tough.

For stews (beef stew, beef cooked in beer, etc.): Choose cuts with tendons or connective tissue such as shank, tendon, oxtail, or thigh for the best results. When cooking stews, add ingredients like garlic, ginger, cinnamon bark, and cloves to make the dish more fragrant, less greasy, and more nutritious.
For grilling: Use fillet or brisket with a bit of fat; it will be more flavorful and delicious when grilled.
This beef and kimchi salad is excellent served with rice or as an appetizer. Good luck with this dish!

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy fermented pork belly features fresh, flavorful meat with a crunchy skin. Served with sweet and sour chili sauce and a side of pickles, this dish offers a unique tang that enhances the flavor without being greasy!
cac_buoc: Step 1: Clean the scallions and cilantro by removing the roots and wilted leaves. Wash thoroughly and drain.
Peel the shallots and garlic, wash, and drain.
Next, place the prepared aromatics and pepper into a mortar and pound into a fine paste.
Step 2: Place the cooked sticky rice in the mortar and pound until soft and sticky.
Step 3: Wash the pork belly with salt to remove any odors, then rinse again with water. Drain and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Step 4: Place the meat in a bowl with the seasonings and the pounded paste. Wear gloves and mix well until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Next, put this mixture into a plastic bag, tie it tightly, and store it in the refrigerator overnight to allow the meat to develop a slightly sour fermented flavor.
Step 5: Once the meat has fermented, heat oil in a pan. When the oil is slightly hot, add the meat and fry over medium heat.

Step 6: While frying, remember to flip the meat frequently so it becomes evenly golden brown and crispy with an attractive color. Before removing to a plate, place the meat on paper towels to reduce excess grease.
Finally, arrange the meat on a plate and enjoy with sweet and sour chili sauce and some pickles to enhance the flavor!
How to choose good pork

Fresh pork: The exterior has a dry film and the surface is slightly firm. The cut surface is bright pink, the skin is soft, the meat fibers are firm, and it has good elasticity (when pressed with a finger, it leaves no mark). The fat is bright, firm, and has a characteristic aroma. Joint surfaces are smooth and clear, and the synovial fluid is transparent. The marrow clings tightly to the bone cavity and is elastic.

Stale pork: The exterior starts to feel slimy or very slimy (depending on the level of spoilage), the cut surface is slightly wet, and elasticity is poor (pressing with a finger leaves a persistent indentation). The fat is dark, less firm, and has a rancid smell. Joint surfaces are slimy, and the synovial fluid is cloudy. The marrow easily detaches from the bone and is dark or brown.
Old pork or sow meat: The meat fibers are loose, dark red, and the skin is thick.

Diseased pork: The meat fibers are loose, the fat is yellow and may contain opaque white grains. There are small spots in the liver or kidneys. The skin may have round or oval hemorrhagic patches. The skin might not be intact or may have carved-out areas (where abscesses or hemorrhages were removed).

Avoid buying pork that is too old or too young. Only buy medium-aged pork with a pink color and thin skin. There are two types of lean meat: tenderloin and rump. Tenderloin is tastier and sweet when cooked, but if overcooked, it becomes fibrous and dry. Rump meat is softer.
For pork hock, choose the hind leg as it has more meat and softer skin.
If buying pork fat to render into lard, choose large leaf fat that is slightly pinkish-white.

With just a little time in the kitchen and easy-to-find ingredients, you can make this delicious and unique roasted pork dish. Served with pickles to prevent greasiness, it provides a wonderful dining experience.

mon_an.mo_ta: Beer-braised duck features an attractive color and a delicious aroma. The meat is tender and deeply infused with spices, providing a delightful experience for anyone who tastes it.
cac_buoc: Preparing ingredients for mixed beer-braised duck:

Rub the duck meat with salt and lemon to remove odors, then rinse thoroughly with water. Remember to peel the skin off the duck's tongue and feet. Once cleaned and drained, chop the duck into bite-sized pieces.
Peel, wash, and mince the garlic. Clean the scallions, remove roots and wilted leaves, then chop finely.
Wash the king oyster mushrooms and cut them into small pieces.
Cut the green and red chilies into large, bite-sized pieces.
Steps to make unique beer-braised duck
Step 1: First, mix 15ml of cooking wine with a small bowl of clean water and soak the duck meat for 20 minutes. Then, remove the meat and let it drain.
Step 2: Next, heat oil in a pan and sauté the garlic and scallions until fragrant.
Add the duck meat and stir-fry until the meat is firm and the juices have evaporated.

Step 3: Add the star anise, soy sauce, and sugar. Stir until the meat turns a golden brown color, then pour in the beer. Once the beer boils, reduce to low heat and simmer for about 15 minutes so the duck absorbs the seasonings.
Add the mushrooms and continue to simmer for 10 minutes.
Step 4: Season with salt and other spices to taste, then add the bell peppers. Increase to high heat and stir until the peppers are soft, then turn off the heat. Serve in a bowl and enjoy.
Notes for a delicious beer-braised duck
When simmering, you should wait until the beer smell has completely evaporated before turning off the heat.
Braising with beer helps the duck meat become softer, more fragrant, and gives it a unique flavor.

How to choose good duck: When buying, choose mature and fat ducks with round breasts, thick neck and belly skin, and full feathers (the tips of the two wings should just cross each other). These ducks are easier and faster to pluck.
Avoid choosing young ducks as the meat will be soft and not firm, and it takes a lot of time to pluck the downy feathers. Young ducks have large, soft bills. Older ducks have smaller, hard bills.

Ducks that have laid many eggs also have quite fragrant meat; these ducks have a sagging lower belly. Unlike chicken, when eating duck, it is better to choose a male duck as the meat is tastier than the female.
To check if a duck is healthy, check the vent; if it is clean and not smeared with droppings, the duck is not sick.
In general, choosing a duck is not too difficult; choose one that is just mature—neither too young nor too old—to ensure a delicious dish and easy preparation.
How to remove duck odor:

To prevent the duck from smelling, rub it with a bit of salt, pepper, crushed ginger, and optionally some white wine before processing. Let it sit for 30 minutes, then rinse and drain. When boiling, add a piece of crushed ginger to the pot. This will eliminate the odor and keep your duck dish fragrant and attractive.
The above guide shares how to make Beer-Braised Duck. If you have any questions while reading, please contact us. Our chef will answer your questions in detail to help you create the best dish!

mon_an.ten: How to Cook Simple Spicy and Sour Seafood Mushroom Hotpot
mon_an.mo_ta: Seafood mushroom hotpot is a familiar dish, especially for weekend gatherings with friends or family. The cooking process is not very complicated, and any home cook can prepare this meal to ensure it is both hygienic and healthy. Today, we will guide you through making a spicy and sour seafood mushroom hotpot. Enjoy a rich meal with the wonderful flavors of mushrooms and seafood combined with an attractive spicy and sour broth. This article provides detailed, easy-to-follow steps so you can cook this delicious hotpot at home.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Culantro, rice paddy herb, dill - for serving
Water spinach, mustard greens, onion (or other vegetables as preferred) - for serving
Rice vermicelli or fresh noodles (as preferred) - for serving
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the pork marrow bones, blanch them in boiling water to remove impurities, then rinse again. Chop into sections, place in a pot with water, and simmer to make the broth.

Step 2: Wash the shrimp and drain. Wash the squid and cut into bite-sized pieces, then arrange on a plate. Soak the clams in rice water to remove sand. Clean and wash the accompanying vegetables and drain. Soak the dried shiitake mushrooms until soft, then wash.
Step 3: Cut the tomatoes into wedges and sauté them in hot oil to create a colorful base.
Step 4: Once the broth is ready, add the sautéed tomatoes and shiitake mushrooms to create color and enhance the flavor. Add a little sour tamarind to the pot for a refreshing tartness.
Step 5: Season the broth, add sliced pineapple along with rice paddy herb, culantro, and dill. Simmer to extract the flavor and aroma for the hotpot.

Step 6: Wash the tofu and cut into bite-sized pieces. Once the broth is finished, transfer it to a mini gas stove or induction cooker. Dip the vegetables, tofu, and seafood into the boiling broth and enjoy the spicy, sour, and sweet flavors of the mushrooms, seafood, and bone broth.
This can be eaten with rice vermicelli or fresh noodles; both are delicious.
Wishing everyone a tasty weekend with this dish!
What vegetables should be eaten with seafood mushroom hotpot?
1. Water spinach is excellent for seafood hotpot
Water spinach is a great choice for seafood hotpot. For a crunchier texture, you can remove some of the leaves and use mostly the stems.
Note that water spinach can have a slightly acrid taste in winter, but in summer, it is sweeter and fresher. Therefore, use water spinach for hotpot in the summer!
2. Kale – The king of vegetables
Kale is considered the king of vegetables. It contains many vitamins and minerals beneficial for health. Kale is often used raw, in smoothies, or stir-fried.
Additionally, kale is very suitable for dipping in hotpot, especially Thai seafood hotpot. You will experience a delicious flavor and a light sweetness that blends perfectly with the broth.
3. Spinach
Spinach is rich in vitamin C and iron, offering many health benefits.
Spinach can be used in seafood hotpot. However, this vegetable can be hard to find at traditional markets; you can look for it in large supermarkets.
4. Bean sprouts – Crunchy and sweet in seafood hotpot

Bean sprouts have a crunchy, sweet taste and are very suitable for hotpot. They contain many vitamins and minerals that stimulate digestion and help cool the body. This helps you feel more comfortable when enjoying spicy and sour Thai seafood hotpot.
5. Shredded banana blossom – An indispensable vegetable for seafood hotpot
Shredded banana blossom is an essential vegetable for seafood hotpot. It has a slightly acrid taste and a sweet aftertaste that pairs perfectly with Thai seafood hotpot.

Furthermore, this vegetable aids digestion and prevents bloating. An important note is to soak the shredded banana blossom in salt water after cutting to keep it fresh and prevent it from turning brown.
6. Water celery – A popular choice for seafood hotpot
Water celery is a popular vegetable used for dipping in hotpot, especially seafood hotpot.
Water celery contains many vitamins and nutrients. It has a characteristic aroma and is very suitable when combined with seafood like shrimp and crab to eliminate fishy odors.
7. Napa cabbage – A common choice for seafood hotpot
Napa cabbage is a common vegetable used in various hotpot dishes. This vegetable has a mild flavor, which helps highlight the taste of the Thai seafood broth.
Another notable point is that napa cabbage contains many anti-cancer substances, can reduce harmful fats, and supports the recovery process after alcohol consumption.
8. Okra – A delicious addition to seafood hotpot

Okra often appears in grilled or stir-fried dishes. However, it is also very suitable for Thai seafood hotpot. When blanched until just cooked, okra provides a crunchy texture. If you have tried this vegetable before, you certainly won't skip it when eating hotpot.
9. Mustard greens – Reduces fishy odors in seafood hotpot

Mustard greens are an excellent choice for seafood hotpot, especially for reducing fishy smells. This vegetable has a slightly pungent and bitter taste, which effectively helps balance the richness of the meal.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried chicken gizzards with onions is a savory and flavorful dish, often prepared for family gatherings or special occasions. Featuring tender chicken gizzards combined with sweet, aromatic onions, this dish offers a unique and appealing taste. Let's learn how to make this traditional, rich dish to enjoy with your loved ones. This guide provides a step-by-step approach to creating a delicious meal perfect for any festive table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Scallions, salt, chili powder, fish sauce, sugar - As needed
Annatto oil and garlic - As needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients
Peel the onion, wash it, and slice it thinly lengthwise.
Peel the garlic, wash it, crush it, and mince it finely.
Trim the roots off the scallions, wash them, and cut them into 2-inch lengths.
Step 2: Prepare the liver and gizzards
To remove odors and clean the liver and gizzards, soak them in diluted salt water for about 15 minutes. Then, rinse thoroughly and slice into small pieces.
Here are several ways to clean liver and gizzards to ensure they are fresh and odorless:
Method 1: Rub the liver and gizzards with salt (or lemon juice, vinegar) for about 5 minutes, then rinse thoroughly under running water.
Method 2: Soak the liver and gizzards in diluted salt water (or diluted white wine) for about 10 minutes, then rinse 2-3 times with clean water and drain.
Method 3: Another way to remove odors is to soak them in fresh milk for about 10 minutes after washing with salt, then rinse again before cooking.
Step 3: Marinate

Place the liver and gizzards in a bowl. Add the minced garlic, 1/2 tsp MSG, 1/2 tbsp soy sauce, and 1/2 tbsp oyster sauce, then mix well. Let them marinate in this mixture for about 15 minutes to absorb the flavors.
Step 4: Stir-fry the liver and gizzards
Heat 2 tbsp of cooking oil in a pan. Add the marinated liver and gizzards and stir-fry over high heat for about 1 minute, then reduce the heat to medium.
Next, add the onions, 1/2 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp MSG, 1 tsp seasoning powder, 1/3 tsp salt, and 1/2 tsp ground pepper to the pan. Continue stir-frying over medium heat for about 3 minutes.
To prevent burning, add 3 tbsp of filtered water to the pan during the stir-frying process.
Finally, add the scallions and stir-fry for another 30 seconds. Turn off the heat and transfer the dish to a plate.
Step 5: Finished product

Stir-fried chicken gizzards with onions is a harmonious blend of crunchy, sweet onions, chewy gizzards, and rich, tender liver. The delicious and bold flavor of this stir-fry makes it a perfect accompaniment to steamed white rice for daily meals.
Notes for cleaning chicken gizzards and liver
Choose fresh organs: Select fresh chicken gizzards and liver to ensure quality and avoid spoilage.
Clean thoroughly: Before starting, rinse the organs under cold water to remove dirt and impurities.
Clean the liver and membranes: Use a sharp knife to clean the liver and the outer membrane of the gizzards. Carefully separate the liver and remove the membranes.
Check the liver: After cleaning, check for any remaining blood vessels or clots. If found, clean further by rinsing or trimming them off.
Handling and storage: If not using immediately, store the organs in the refrigerator to ensure food safety. Use within 1-2 days for the best freshness.
Personal hygiene: Ensure personal hygiene by washing your hands thoroughly after handling the organs or using any tools.

mon_an.ten: Chicken Glass Noodle Salad with Bean Sprouts – A Weight Loss Recipe
mon_an.mo_ta: Chicken glass noodle salad with bean sprouts is a delicious and appealing dish for those on a weight loss journey. With chicken and fresh green vegetables as the main ingredients, this dish not only keeps you full for longer but also provides essential nutrients. Discover how to make this salad to enjoy its refreshing flavor. This guide offers simple steps to create a healthy, tasty meal with fresh greens and savory seasonings.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Cilantro, mint, Vietnamese coriander - a little of each
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the ingredients
Step 1: Prepare the chicken
Rinse the chicken under cold water and remove any unwanted parts.
Slice the chicken into thin pieces, either long strips or squares as preferred.
Step 2: Prepare the dry glass noodles
Bring a large pot of water to a boil.
Add the dry glass noodles to the boiling water and blanch briefly until soft yet chewy.
Once cooked, rinse the noodles with cold water and drain well.
Step 3: Prepare the peanuts
Roast the peanuts in a dry pan until they are golden pink and fragrant.
Place the roasted peanuts on a paper towel to absorb excess oil and let them cool. Then, crush them into small pieces.
Step 4: Prepare the herbs and vegetables
Rinse the cilantro, mint, and Vietnamese coriander under cold water.
Chop the herbs into small pieces to be used as seasoning.
Wash the bean sprouts thoroughly, then blanch them in chicken broth until slightly softened.
Step 5: Prepare the dressing
In a small bowl, combine the sugar, lemon juice, fish sauce, soy sauce, and pepper.
Stir well until the sugar is completely dissolved and the mixture is smooth.
After completing these preparation steps, you can proceed to assemble the salad.
2. Processing

1. Place the chicken in a pot and boil until cooked with shiitake mushrooms, ginger, and a bit of seasoning powder. Once the chicken is cooked, remove it, let it cool, and shred it into bite-sized pieces.
2. Using the existing chicken broth, add the washed glass noodles (cut into 5-7cm lengths) and cook until tender, then remove and drain.
3. After washing, blanch the bean sprouts in the chicken broth to maintain their crunch. Pick the herbs to remove roots and wilted leaves, wash them, and chop finely.
4. Take the roasted and peeled peanuts and lightly crush them with a knife.

5. In a bowl, mix the sugar, lemon juice, fish sauce, soy sauce, chicken broth, and pepper. Once well combined, put all the prepared ingredients into a large bowl, pour the dressing over slowly, and toss well. Taste and adjust the seasoning to your preference.
6. Finally, arrange the chicken glass noodle salad on a plate and enjoy.
Tips for a delicious chicken glass noodle salad
For more meat, choose chicken breast or thighs.
After boiling the chicken, set aside 2 bowls of broth before using the rest to blanch the bean sprouts.
How to choose good chicken:
Pre-slaughtered chicken:
1. Local chicken (gà ta) is usually compact, firm, with a narrow breast.

2. Be careful to distinguish it from industrial egg-laying hens. Local chicken skin is pale yellow, only darker at the breast, wings, and back, while industrial hens are often white or yellow all over (possibly due to dyes).
3. To check for dyes, observe if the skin is yellow but the fat underneath is white; if so, it has been chemically dyed.
4. Local chicken skin is thin, smooth, and elastic. Choose fresh-looking meat with no foul or antibiotic smell, and no bruises or blood clots on the skin.
5. Avoid dark-colored meat, as this indicates the chicken died before being processed.
6. To avoid water-injected chicken, press on the thighs or breast; if it feels spongy, slippery, or deformed, do not buy it.
Live chicken:

1. The chicken should look healthy and active. The comb should be bright red, eyes alert, and feathers shiny and sleek. The beak should be sharp with no discharge. Legs should be straight and slender with bright yellow skin.

2. Part the feathers to check for thin, soft, shiny skin with yellow patches under the breast and wings. You should be able to see the meat and blood vessels under the wing skin as there is little fat.
3. The vent should be pinkish, active, and dry with no abnormal discharge or droppings.
4. Check under the wings; a small red dot surrounded by a blackish bruise indicates water injection.
Notes for processing chicken for this dish
1. Pre-slaughtered chicken
Local chicken is typically compact and firm with a narrow breast.
Distinguish it from industrial hens. Local chicken skin is pale yellow with darker spots on the breast and back, whereas industrial hens may have unnaturally uniform white or yellow skin.
If the skin is yellow but the fat is white, it is likely dyed.
The skin should be thin and elastic. Meat should be fresh without odors or bruises.
Press the meat to check for water injection; avoid any that feels mushy or slippery.
2. Live chicken
Look for healthy, agile birds with bright red combs and clear eyes. Feathers should be smooth and close to the body. The beak should be clean.
Legs should be thin and straight with shiny yellow skin.
The skin should be thin and soft, allowing you to see the meat underneath.
The vent should be healthy, pink, and dry.
Check for injection marks under the wings; a red dot or dark bruising indicates the bird has been tampered with.

mon_an.mo_ta: Korean mixed glass noodles (Japchae) – with this simple cooking method, you will have an incredibly attractive dish. This guide shows you how to make simple Korean Japchae at home. Enjoy a delicious, rich dish with the characteristic flavors of Korean cuisine right in your own kitchen.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Soy sauce, sesame oil, toasted sesame seeds
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the bell peppers and carrots. Peel the carrots and julienne them. Seed the bell peppers and julienne them. Stir-fry them with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Step 2: Trim the roots of the enoki mushrooms, shake off any dirt, and soak in diluted salt water for 15 minutes, then rinse with clean water. Stir-fry these with sesame oil and soy sauce as well.
Step 3: Peel the onion, wash it, and slice it into wedges. Stir-fry with soy sauce and sesame oil to complete the flavor profile of the Japchae.
Step 4: Wash the greens, cut them into bite-sized pieces, and stir-fry with soy sauce and sesame oil.
Step 5: Stir-fry the beef with some chopped scallions, soy sauce, and sesame oil until the flavors are absorbed.
Step 6: Blanch the glass noodles in boiling water until just cooked—not too mushy or too chewy. Rinse under cold water to firm up the strands. This is key to a good Japchae.

Step 7: Mix all the ingredients together: bell peppers, carrots, onions, enoki mushrooms, beef, greens, and noodles. Season again with soy sauce to taste. Sprinkle toasted sesame seeds on top to finish the dish.
Notes for making Korean Japchae
Choose fresh ingredients: Use fresh glass noodles and high-quality vegetables, meat, or seafood to ensure the best flavor.
Ensure hygiene: Wash your hands and all cooking tools before starting. Keep the workspace clean and process ingredients under sanitary conditions.
Balance the flavors: Choose appropriate seasonings and sauces to create a unique, balanced taste. Taste and adjust according to your personal preference.
Proper cooking time: Monitor the cooking time for the noodles and other components to ensure they are neither too soft nor too hard. Keep the noodles slightly chewy.
Garnish: Before serving, garnish the dish with scallions, fried shallots, sesame seeds, or roasted peanuts to enhance both flavor and appearance.
Proper storage: If there are leftovers, store them in an airtight container in the refrigerator and consume within 1-2 days for food safety.
How to buy the best ingredients for Japchae
How to buy fresh beef
Color and surface: Choose beef that is bright red with a dry surface. The meat should have natural moisture but not be overly wet. Fresh beef should have streaks of creamy white fat throughout.
Texture: Prioritize meat with a clear structure and interlocking fibers. This ensures the meat is tender and has a good mouthfeel.
Avoid bad signs: Do not buy meat that is pale, dark, or has a slimy surface. Fresh beef should not have an unpleasant odor.
Choosing fresh greens
Color and surface: Fresh greens should be vibrant green with smooth leaves and a sleek surface.
Weight and smell: They should feel heavy for their size, have no strange odors, and feel fresh and crisp to the touch.
Avoid bad signs: Avoid greens that are pale, have dark spots on the stems or leaves, or are crushed.
Choosing good carrots
Color and surface: Choose carrots that are bright orange with a smooth, shiny surface.
Stems and body: Prioritize carrots with fresh green stems still firmly attached to the body. This indicates they were recently harvested.
Avoid bad signs: Do not buy carrots that are rotten, crushed, or have abnormal black spots on the surface.
Following these tips will help you select fresh, chemical-free vegetables and carrots for a high-quality meal for your family.

mon_an.ten: Savory Stir-Fried Glass Noodles with Shrimp
mon_an.mo_ta: With this stir-fried glass noodle and shrimp dish, it only takes 20 minutes to complete a meal to treat your family. Check out our recipe below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning - Soy sauce, vinegar, chili sauce, salt, white pepper
cac_buoc: Grate the ginger and cut the scallions into long segments. Soak the glass noodles in water until soft.
Wash the shrimp, peel, and devein them, then rinse again and drain. Marinate the shrimp with pepper and salt, then stir-fry in a hot pan with oil until just cooked. Remove and set aside.
Step 1: Briefly stir-fry the peas, scallions, and ginger to make the dish more fragrant.
Step 2: Add the glass noodles, soy sauce, vinegar, and chili sauce.
Step 3: Finally, add the shrimp back in, toss everything together for about 1 minute, then turn off the heat. Serve on a plate and enjoy while hot.

mon_an.ten: Sweet Potato Wrapped Shrimp and Pork
mon_an.mo_ta: This easy-to-make sweet potato wrapped shrimp and pork dish is perfect for chilly winter days. The sweetness of the potato combined with the savory shrimp and pork filling is a perfect match for a satisfying lunch. Detailed daily cooking instructions are provided below!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt, seasoning powder, fish sauce, pepper, shallots
cac_buoc: Start making the sweet potato wrapped shrimp and pork:

Step 1: Wash the sweet potatoes to remove dirt, peel, and cut into pieces. Bring a pot of water to a boil and cook until the potatoes are tender. Remove and drain, then mash finely. Use the hot potato water to soak the wood ear mushrooms until expanded, then wash, trim the roots, and chop finely.

Step 2: Peel and devein the shrimp, wash, drain, and dice. In a bowl, mix the minced pork, wood ear mushrooms, shrimp, and minced shallots. Add a bit of pepper, 1 tsp salt, 1/2 tsp seasoning powder, and 2 tsp fish sauce. Mix well to marinate.
Step 3: Add the mashed sweet potato to the meat bowl and mix well. Add a little tapioca starch so the mixture binds together and doesn't feel dry when eaten.
Step 4: Take the mixture and roll it into small, bite-sized balls.
Step 5: Roll each ball through the all-purpose flour.
Step 6: Next, roll the balls through the beaten egg. Place the breadcrumbs on another plate and roll the balls in them until coated.
Step 7: Heat a deep pan with a generous amount of oil. When the oil is hot, fry the balls until golden brown and cooked through, then remove.

mon_an.mo_ta: If you are familiar with traditional fried fish cakes, these crispy breaded fish cakes will add variety to your family's daily menu.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fish sauce, salt, seasoning powder, pepper, chili sauce
cac_buoc: Learn to cook delicious crispy breaded fish cakes:

Step 1: Wash the fish thoroughly to remove any fishy smell. Mix the fish with tapioca starch, minced shallots, 2 tsp fish sauce, 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp seasoning powder, and a bit of pepper. Mix well, then put the fish into a blender and grind until smooth.
Step 2: Use a spoon to scoop the fish paste into your hand and shape into flat discs about 1 cm thick. Roll each piece through the all-purpose flour.
Step 3: Beat the egg. Dip each fish cake into the egg wash, then roll it in the breadcrumbs.

Step 4: Pour oil into a pan. When hot, drop the fish cakes in and fry until golden brown on all sides. Once cooked, quickly remove them to a plate lined with paper towels to prevent them from becoming greasy.

mon_an.mo_ta: Roasted duck spring rolls are made from flavorful pieces of roasted duck and healthy, crispy tofu skin. Learn how to make this dish, which is perfect for a relaxing weekend with the family. It doesn't take much time but results in a delicious treat for everyone.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning powder, sugar, salt, sesame seeds
cac_buoc: Let's start learning how to make roasted duck spring rolls!
Step 1: Wash the celery, bamboo shoots, and carrots, then julienne them. Slice the roasted duck into bite-sized pieces.
Step 2: Place a pan over medium heat and stir-fry the bamboo shoots first.
Step 3: Add the celery and carrots to the pan and stir well. Add a bit of oyster sauce to make the vegetables more fragrant.
Step 4: When the vegetables are nearly cooked, add the roasted duck and stir-fry together. Season with a little salt and pepper for aroma and taste.
You're halfway through this easy recipe! Let's keep going!
Step 5: Soak the tofu skin in water until soft and pliable. Place the stir-fried filling from step 4 onto the skin and roll tightly like a spring roll.
Step 6: Line a baking tray with foil, arrange the rolls on top, and bake for 10 minutes at 120°C. Occasionally check the rolls during baking to ensure they don't burn.
Ta-da! The roasted duck spring rolls are finished! Let's enjoy!

mon_an.mo_ta: Honey-glazed grilled buffalo ribs are a delicious, attractive, and flavorful dish. Combining the tenderness of buffalo ribs with the sweet aroma of honey, this dish offers a wonderful culinary experience. Discover the detailed method to enjoy this excellent dish right at home! This guide provides precise steps and fresh ingredients for a perfect result.
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ribs
After purchasing the ribs, wash them with salt water, blanch them in boiling water, and drain. You can leave the ribs whole or cut them into 5-7cm lengths.
Step 2: Mix the marinade
In a bowl, combine 3 tbsp honey, 2 tbsp fish sauce, 1 tbsp MSG, 1 tbsp lemon juice, 2 tbsp annatto oil, 1 tbsp minced garlic and chili, and a little pepper. Stir well to create the marinade.
Wear gloves and rub the marinade evenly over the ribs. Let them marinate for about 30 minutes to absorb the flavors. After marinating, place the ribs on a grill rack.
Step 3: Grill the ribs
Preheat the oven to 150°C for 5 minutes before putting the ribs in.

Once the ribs are in, increase the temperature to 200°C for 10 minutes, then lower it to 170°C and grill for another 15 minutes. During the process, take the ribs out and brush the remaining marinade over the surface to prevent drying and create a beautiful shine.
When the ribs are cooked, place them on a plate, garnish with side vegetables, and enjoy.
You can also use an air fryer with a similar method if you don't have an oven.
Notes for marinating buffalo ribs with honey
When marinating buffalo ribs with honey, keep these important points in mind for a delicious and safe meal:
Choose quality honey: Use pure honey without additives or preservatives. Fresh honey provides a special flavor.
Ensure fresh ribs: Select fresh buffalo ribs with no odor and store them properly to avoid bacteria.
Marinate evenly: Ensure the honey and other seasonings are well-mixed and thoroughly coat the ribs. Massage gently to help the flavors penetrate.
Marinating time: Marinate for 30 minutes to 2 hours for the best flavor profile.
Safe storage: To prevent bacterial growth, marinate the ribs in the refrigerator and do not leave them out too long before grilling.
Baste the ribs: Periodically brush the marinade onto the surface while grilling to keep them moist and add a glossy finish.
Correct temperature: Follow the recommended temperatures and times to achieve a golden-brown, tender finish while preserving the natural flavor.
Following these tips will help you create a delicious and safe honey-grilled buffalo rib dish for family and friends.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried squid with curry – An easy-to-make dish for a relaxing drink with friends. Learn how to cook this flavorful curry squid.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning powder, fish sauce, sugar, cooking oil
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the squid: Clean the squid, peel off the skin, score in a diamond pattern, and cut into bite-sized pieces or rings as desired.
Step 2: Marinate the squid with 2 tbsp curry oil, minced shallot, a bit of seasoning powder, and sugar. Let it sit for about 15 minutes to absorb the flavors.

Step 3: Heat a pan with 2 tbsp cooking oil and sauté the minced garlic until fragrant. Add the minced lemongrass and chilies. When the lemongrass is golden and aromatic, add the marinated squid and stir-fry continuously over high heat until cooked. Season with a little fish sauce to taste. Serve the dish hot on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Make this delicious stir-fried squid with baby corn using our recipe. The squid is perfectly seasoned with a spicy kick from satay, and hints of ginger and scallions. The baby corn and carrots are incredibly sweet and crunchy. This dish works great as a snack or served with steamed rice!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning: Salt, fish sauce, pepper - As needed
cac_buoc: Step 1: Prepare the ingredients

Clean the squid, remove the innards and skin, then use a sharp knife to lightly score the surface in a diamond pattern. Cut into bite-sized pieces about 2 finger-joints long. Marinate the squid with minced shallot, garlic, pepper, satay, and fish sauce.
Wash the horn chili; slice half into diamond shapes and mince the other half. Crush the bird's eye chilies. Cut the scallions into lengths matching the squid pieces.
Slice the baby corn diagonally, blanch quickly in boiling water, then remove and drain immediately.
Prepare the sauce mixture: 1 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp chili sauce, and 1 tbsp fish sauce.
Step 2: Cook the dish
Heat a pan and add cooking oil to coat the surface. Sauté the ginger and minced shallot/garlic until fragrant. Add the squid and stir-fry until firm, then remove to a plate.

In the same pan, add the baby corn and carrots and stir-fry until cooked, then return the squid to the pan. Pour in the prepared sauce mixture and toss well. Add the minced horn chili, bird's eye chilies, and scallions. Adjust the seasoning to taste and turn off the heat. Sprinkle with a little pepper for aroma, transfer to a plate, and garnish with cilantro.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried bitter melon with pork is an excellent dish for those looking to maintain a healthy diet. The characteristic bitterness of the melon combined with savory pork creates a unique and delicious pairing. This dish is not only tasty but also health-conscious; bitter melon is low in calories and sugar, helping to manage blood sugar levels. With a simple preparation method and easy-to-find ingredients, this is a delightful choice for your daily meals. A familiar staple in many households, it features tender pork and crisp bitter melon, where the sweetness of the meat balances the slight bitterness of the melon, topped with the aroma of green onions for a wonderful dining experience.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasoning powder, black pepper, fish sauce, cooking oil - to taste
cac_buoc: 1. Prepare the ingredients
Start by cleaning the pork tenderloin by rinsing it with diluted salt water. Then, slice the meat into bite-sized pieces and marinate with 1 tsp salt, 1 tsp cooking oil, and 1 tsp black pepper.
For the bitter melon, cut off both ends, split lengthwise, and remove the inner pith and seeds. Slice the melon into thin pieces.
Peel and crush the shallots, then mince them for use in the dish.
2. Traditional Stir-fried Bitter Melon with Pork

Add 2 tbsp of cooking oil to a pan. Once the oil is hot, sauté the minced shallots until fragrant, then add the pork and stir well. Stir-fry until the meat firms up and turns a nice golden color, then remove to a bowl.

Next, add the bitter melon to the pan and season with 1 tsp seasoning powder. Stir-fry until the color deepens and it is slightly cooked. Add the pork back into the pan and stir-fry together for about 1 minute, tossing evenly.
If desired, add chopped green onions to enhance the presentation. Once finished, turn off the heat and serve.

The final result should be bitter melon that is perfectly cooked—not too soft and without a harsh raw smell. The pork should be evenly cooked and savory. This dish is best enjoyed with steamed white rice.
3. Japanese-style Stir-fried Bitter Melon with Pork
Pour 2 tbsp of cooking oil into a pan and heat it up. Add the pork and stir-fry for 3-5 minutes until cooked through.
Next, add the bitter melon, mirin, and soy sauce to the pan, stir-frying with the meat for about 2 minutes.
Add the tofu to the pan and gently toss for about 2 minutes. Then, pour in the beaten eggs and stir until the eggs are evenly scrambled and mixed with the other ingredients. Turn off the heat.

Finally, plate the stir-fry and sprinkle some bonito flakes on top for garnish. This step not only makes the dish more attractive but also brings out the natural aroma of soy sauce and mirin. The combination of bitter melon, egg, and meat creates a sweet and appealing flavor.
4. Stir-fried Bitter Melon with Minced Pork and Egg

Sauté the minced white parts of the green onions until fragrant, then add the minced pork to the pan. Season with black pepper and salt, stir-frying until the meat is cooked, then remove to a separate plate.
Sauté more green onion whites and add the bitter melon to the pan, stir-frying until cooked. Add the pork back in and stir-fry with the melon for about 1 minute.
Pour in the eggs and stir-fry until the eggs are cooked and well-blended with the ingredients. Once the eggs are set, turn off the heat.
Finally, serve the bitter melon, pork, and egg on a plate, then sprinkle with a bit of black pepper and cilantro for garnish.
The final result is a dish of stir-fried bitter melon with minced pork and egg that offers a gentle sweetness. This should be enjoyed while hot, and it pairs perfectly with rice.

mon_an.mo_ta: Simple Mulberry Jam – It is the season for deep red, fragrant, and delicious mulberries. Make this simple mulberry jam to use in various treats like mulberry ice cream or mulberry sponge cake.
cac_buoc: Let's start making this simple and easy mulberry jam!
Step 1:
Wash the mulberries thoroughly, remove the stems, and discard any unripe berries. Soak them in water for about 30 minutes, then drain in a colander.
Marinate the mulberries with granulated sugar for 1 hour. Note: When soaking or marinating mulberries, use a plastic or enameled bowl; avoid metal containers as the acidity can cause oxidation.
Step 2: Add the lemon juice, filtered water, and all the maltose syrup into the pot with the mulberries. Simmer over low heat, stirring constantly until the mixture becomes thick and syrupy.
Step 3: The simmering process for this simple mulberry jam can take up to 40 minutes depending on the heat level or whether you want the jam to be very soft or keep the berries whole.
Step 4: Wait about 2 hours for the jam to cool completely before transferring it to airtight jars. The jam can be kept for 1 month at room temperature or longer if refrigerated.

mon_an.mo_ta: Thai Noodle Salad – A delicious daily dish with the characteristic mild sourness and spicy kick of Thai cuisine that will surely delight you. Here is how to make this attractive Thai Noodle Salad.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Finely chopped chili, minced garlic, and minced ginger. Mix these with 2 tbsp soy sauce and 1 tsp lime juice (adjust the sourness to your preference).
cac_buoc: Step 1: Wash the chicken breast and roast it in the oven until cooked (if you don't have an oven, you can pan-fry it until golden). Then, slice it into small pieces.

Step 2: Bring water to a boil, add the noodles and cook until just tender. Drain and rinse several times with clean water, then let dry. Heat some oil, toss the noodles briefly, then turn off the heat. Next, stir-fry the carrots and cabbage until just cooked.

Step 3: Use a small basin to mix the salad ingredients first: combine the lettuce, herbs, green onions, fish mint, carrots, cabbage, and chicken, tossing well with olive oil. Finally, add the noodles, pour the sauce over, and mix thoroughly. Adjust seasoning to taste.
Step 4: When serving this delicious dish, you can prepare an extra bowl of chili garlic fish sauce for dipping if desired.
Source: Ngoi sao

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy Fried Noodles with Vegetables – An easy-to-eat dish featuring crunchy noodle nests topped with sweet, crisp vegetables. Besides vegetables, you can also combine this with fried or stir-fried meat for a delicious meal. Learn how to cook this tasty Crispy Fried Noodle dish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green onions, garlic, cornstarch, sesame oil
cac_buoc: Step 1: Clean all the vegetables and slice them into bite-sized pieces suitable for your family members.

Step 2: Place the beef in the freezer for 10 minutes, then take it out, wash, and slice into bite-sized pieces; partially frozen beef is easier to slice thinly. Marinate the beef with cornstarch, soy sauce, and sesame oil for about 15 minutes.

Step 3: Soak the noodles in boiling water for about 1 minute, then drain. In a pan with hot oil, fry the noodles until they become crispy. Once crispy, remove the noodles to a plate lined with paper towels to absorb excess oil.

Step 4: In another pan, stir-fry the broccoli, snow peas, and baby corn. When the broccoli starts to turn deep green, add the straw mushrooms and bamboo shoots. Once everything is fully cooked, remove to a separate plate. Sauté the minced garlic and onions, then quickly stir-fry the beef. Add the vegetables back in and toss quickly.
Step 5: Place the crispy noodles on a plate, top with the vegetables and beef, and enjoy while hot. If you prefer a vegetarian version, you can omit the beef.
Source: Kenh14

mon_an.ten: Spicy and Sour Mixed Flower Crab Hot Pot
mon_an.mo_ta: This weekend, let's learn how to cook a delicious spicy and sour mixed flower crab hot pot to change up the family meal. With this recipe, you will have a sweet, rich, and flavorful hot pot. Let's get started. Discover how to make this mixed crab hot pot at home. With a unique flavor profile, this dish combines the sweetness of the crab, the spiciness of the spices, and the aroma of various mixed ingredients. Enjoy a bold, attractive hot pot with a variety of crabs and a spice blend that creates a wonderful culinary experience.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green vegetables - As desired (can use sponge gourd, Malabar spinach, water spinach, mustard greens, etc.)
Rice vermicelli, glass noodles, or flat rice noodles - As needed
cac_buoc: I. How to cook delicious spicy and sour mixed flower crab hot pot
1. Cook the broth.

Wash the pork bones, blanch in boiling water, then rinse again to remove impurities. Place in a pot with water, bring to a boil, and skim off the foam for a clear broth. Cover and simmer to extract the sweetness from the bones.
Heat oil in a pan, sauté minced shallots, crushed green peppercorns, lemongrass segments, and sliced galangal. Add the sliced pineapple and the bone broth.
2. Prepare the ingredients
While the broth is simmering, prepare the remaining ingredients.
Wash the crabs, remove the shell and the apron, clean out the mud inside, then cut each crab in half.
Pick the young parts of the vegetables, wash thoroughly, drain, and cut into segments.
Clean the mushrooms and trim the stems. Cut a cross on the caps of the straw mushrooms for decoration. Slice the king oyster mushrooms.
3. Assemble the hot pot
Pour the broth into the hot pot, add wedged tomatoes, crabs, and mushrooms, and bring to a boil. Adjust seasoning to taste.
During cooking, the crabs and mushrooms will release their sweetness into the bone broth, making it incredibly flavorful. Add vegetables as you eat.
II. How to make Flower Crab Hot Pot with Green Peppercorns
1. Ingredients
100g king oyster mushrooms
100g oyster mushrooms
100g straw mushrooms
50g green peppercorns
4 shallots
1 sponge gourd
500g Malabar spinach
500g fresh rice vermicelli
800g live flower crabs
2 tbsp fish sauce
2 tbsp cooking oil
Seasonings: salt, sugar, seasoning powder, and pepper (to taste)
2. Processing the Green Peppercorn Crab
Prepare the ingredients
Wash the crabs and split them in half. Remove the apron and mud, then rinse again to remove any odor. If the crabs are large, cut them into smaller pieces.
Straw and king oyster mushrooms: Trim the stems, soak in diluted salt water to clean, then drain.
Oyster mushrooms: Trim the stems, rinse with water, and drain. Do not soak in salt water to avoid losing nutrients.
Sponge gourd: Peel, wash, and slice diagonally.
Malabar spinach: Trim the roots, remove damaged leaves, wash, and drain.
Shallots: Peel, wash, and slice thinly.
Green peppercorns: Wash and crush.
Note: When crushing green peppercorns, put them in a plastic bag to prevent them from flying out.
Cook the hot pot
Boil 1.5 liters of water in a pot. While waiting, heat a pan with 3 tbsp of oil. Sauté the shallots until fragrant.
When the shallots turn golden, add the crushed green peppercorns and sauté quickly until fragrant, then turn off the heat.
Once the water boils, pour the shallot and peppercorn mixture into the pot. Lower the heat and add seasoning powder, salt, and sugar to taste.
Add the straw mushrooms and prepared crabs to the pot and cook until done. The crabs will be cooked after about 5-10 minutes.
Once the mushrooms and crabs are cooked, add the sponge gourd, king oyster mushrooms, oyster mushrooms, and Malabar spinach. Serve with fresh rice vermicelli.
III. How to cook Kimchi Flower Crab Hot Pot
1. Ingredients for Kimchi Crab Hot Pot
1kg fresh clams
300g baby beef shank
500g napa cabbage kimchi
200g enoki mushrooms
1 small white radish
1 block of soft tofu
500g chrysanthemum greens
Seasonings: a little (as needed)
2. Prepare the ingredients
Wash the crabs and split them in half. Remove the apron and mud, then rinse again. Cut in half if too large.
Soak clams in rice water for 45 minutes to remove sand, then rinse. Wash the beef shank with salt water and slice thinly.
Peel the radish, wash, and cut into chunks. Clean the chrysanthemum greens, keeping about 10cm of the stems, and wash.
Trim the enoki mushrooms, wash, and tear into small clusters.
Cut the tofu into bite-sized pieces and blanch in boiling water to make them firmer.
Cut the kimchi into bite-sized segments.
Place a pot on the stove and boil 1.5 liters of water with the radish to make a sweet broth. Season with seasoning powder, salt, and sugar to taste.
Add the kimchi and bring back to a boil (keep the kimchi juice to add to the broth for extra flavor). Stir in 1 tbsp of fish sauce and adjust seasonings.
Add the crabs and clams first as they take longer to cook (about 5-10 minutes). When eating, add the beef, mushrooms, vegetables, and tofu.
Once the beef is cooked, serve with rice vermicelli, radish, kimchi, and green onions.

The hot pot features the spicy, warm flavor of kimchi blended with the fresh sweetness of clams and crabs. You can dip the ingredients in soy sauce for extra richness. Add fresh chilies to the soy sauce if you prefer more heat.
Notes for a delicious mixed crab hot pot:
Sauté the shallots, galangal, and lemongrass before adding the broth to make it more fragrant. Add pineapple for a gentle sourness that complements the sweet broth.
When adding mushrooms, boil for at least 10 minutes to ensure they are fully cooked for digestive safety.
Crab can be dipped in salt, pepper, and lime juice, with a bit of wasabi. Seafood with wasabi is the best combination.

mon_an.mo_ta: With easy-to-find ingredients and a simple method, you can create a delicious, savory, and unforgettable dish of stuffed eggplant in tomato sauce! In today's article, we will guide you through making this super tasty sweet and sour stuffed eggplant. Please take a look!
cac_buoc: Step 1:
Mix the minced meat thoroughly with some chopped green onions, minced ginger, 1 egg, and a pinch of salt.
Step 2:
Slice the eggplant into rounds about 8mm thick, then butterfly each round (slice through the middle but do not cut all the way through).
Step 3:
Stuff the meat mixture into the center of each eggplant slice.
Step 4:
Mix 3/4 of the cornstarch with the remaining egg, then dip each stuffed eggplant piece into the mixture.
Step 5:
Heat oil in a pan and fry the eggplant until golden brown. Place the fried eggplant on paper towels to drain excess oil.
Step 6:

Mix the minced ginger, chili, and green onions with 3 tbsp soy sauce, 2 tbsp sugar, 1 tbsp vinegar, 1 tbsp sesame oil, 1 tbsp water, and the remaining cornstarch. Pour this into a pan and simmer gently. When the mixture thickens, add the eggplant and toss quickly over high heat for 1-2 minutes. Done!
If done skillfully, the eggplant will be very crispy!
The dish looks very attractive, doesn't it!
If you cannot eat spicy food, replace the chili with tomato sauce!

mon_an.ten: Steamed Chicken with Lemongrass and Lime Leaves
mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed chicken with lemongrass is a favorite for many families, featuring chicken steamed to perfection—tender, juicy, lightly seasoned, and infused with the deep aroma of lemongrass, lime leaves, and ginger. Just a little time in the kitchen and you'll have a wonderful dish to treat your family and friends!
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Seasonings - rock salt, fine salt, pepper, MSG, seasoning powder, cooking oil, shallots
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients for the steamed chicken:
Peel the shallots, wash, and mince them.
Trim the lemongrass, wash, and mince one half; crush the other half and cut into 3cm segments.
Peel or scrape the ginger, wash, and mince one half; julienne the other half.
Wash the lime leaves; finely shred one half and leave the other half whole.
Wash the horn chilies and slice them.
Clean the chicken, setting the giblets aside.
