Trim the roots of the enoki mushrooms, wash well, drain, and arrange on a plate. - Thinly slice the white part of the lemongrass to marinate the fish; cut the tougher upper part into 5-6 cm lengths and split them lengthwise to add to the hotpot broth. - Peel and crush the garlic, letting it sit for 15 minutes before use. Wash the vegetables, drain well, and arrange on a large platter. Cut the rice vermicelli into bite-sized portions and place on a plate.
Step 2: Prepare the hotpot broth

Cut the marrow bones into large pieces, wash thoroughly, and blanch once in boiling water to remove impurities and odors. Place them in a pot to simmer. When the water boils, add the fish head and bones. Simmer for about 45 minutes. Before turning off the heat, season with salt and seasoning powder to taste. Remove the bones and strain the broth for clarity. If the broth is cloudy, whisk an egg white and stir it into the cooled broth; bring to a simmer while stirring so the impurities bind to the egg, then skim it off.
Sauté half of the minced garlic and lemongrass in oil with 1 tbsp of sate sauce, then add this mixture to the broth.
Step 3: Make the dipping sauce
There are two ways to prepare the dipping sauce, depending on your preference:
Option 1: Mix 2 tbsp of salt, sliced fresh chilies, and 1 tbsp of lime juice together.
Option 2: Pour premium fish sauce into a small bowl and add minced garlic and fresh chilies.
Step 4: Finishing

When ready to eat, pour the broth into the hotpot, bring to a boil, and add the shiitake mushrooms and 1 tsp of sate sauce. Follow with the seafood, and finally the vegetables and enoki mushrooms. Once the vegetables are blanched and the seafood is cooked, remove and enjoy! This seafood hotpot is perfect for chilly days. The sweetness of the bone and seafood broth pairs perfectly with the spicy kick of lemongrass and chili. Wishing you a warm and happy day!

mon_an.ten: Baby Napa Cabbage in Superior Broth
mon_an.mo_ta: This baby napa cabbage dish features a sweet, clear broth and tender greens, making it a perfect light vegetable dish for those on a diet. Baby napa cabbage is rich in vitamins and fiber, low in fat, and low in calories. Adding century egg and luncheon meat enhances the flavor without making the meal feel heavy. With moderate difficulty, it's beginner-friendly, taking only about 20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Enoki mushrooms - 10 g (optional, skip if preferred 😂)
Luncheon meat (can be substituted with sausage)
cac_buoc: Wash the baby napa cabbage, slice lengthwise, and then cut into sections.
Cut 3 g of green onions into short lengths. Slice 10 g of garlic. Finely slice 10 g of ginger.
Dice the century egg and the luncheon meat (or sausage) into 1 cm cubes.
Wash the enoki mushrooms and separate the strands.
Bring water to a boil, blanch the baby napa cabbage for about ten seconds, then remove.
Heat a wok, coat with oil, discard the excess, then add a small amount of fresh oil.
Lower the heat and sauté the green onions, ginger, and garlic until fragrant.
Pour in about 300 g of water (enough to just cover the cabbage), then add the cabbage, enoki mushrooms, and luncheon meat.
Season with oyster sauce, sugar, salt, and MSG, then bring to a boil.
Cook for 3 minutes. Once boiling, transfer to a plate: arrange the cabbage first, place the century egg on top, and pour the broth over.
My photography skills are limited, but the taste is excellent!

mon_an.mo_ta: Qianlong Cabbage is a classic Beijing-style salad: tender napa cabbage hearts hand-torn and tossed in a thick, sweet and sour sesame dressing. It is crisp, refreshing, and intensely flavorful. Rich in vitamins and fiber, while the ground sesame provides healthy fats and calcium. This dish requires no stir-frying or cooking—simply mix the sauce and toss. It's very beginner-friendly and usually takes only 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 2 people.
Aged black vinegar - 45 ml (approx. 3 tbsp, vinegar to sesame paste ratio approx. 3:2)
cac_buoc: Use only the tender inner leaves of the napa cabbage (the yellow parts). Remove the tough stems and tear the leaves by hand into pieces about half the size of your palm. **Do not use a knife** (torn edges allow the sauce to cling better).
Wash the torn leaves and dry them thoroughly; any remaining water will prevent the sauce from sticking.

Place 30 g of sesame paste in a bowl. **First, pour in 45 ml of black vinegar**, stirring in one direction to gradually thin the paste until it *flows in a thin stream* (do not stir back and forth, as this can cause the oil to separate).

Add 5 g of sugar to the sesame sauce and stir well; then add 1 g of salt and stir; finally, add 5 ml of sesame oil and stir (add seasonings one by one, stirring each in while checking the consistency).
Drizzle the prepared sesame sauce over the cabbage leaves and toss gently by hand until every leaf is coated.
Sprinkle with toasted white sesame seeds and serve. If time permits, **let it sit for 5 minutes** to absorb the flavors before eating.
The key is to ensure the cabbage is completely dry; wet leaves won't hold the sauce, making the dish bland.
When mixing the sauce, always use the vinegar to "loosen" the sesame paste first before adding other ingredients. Never pour everything in at once.
Zhenjiang vinegar is preferred for its color and acidity; avoid rice vinegar (too mild) or white vinegar (too sharp and pale).
This recipe uses a vinegar-sugar base; for a rounder, richer flavor, you can replace half the sugar with honey.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cold Wood Ear Mushroom Salad: Since pantry staples often include dried goods, wood ear mushrooms are a healthy choice, and this salad preparation is relatively simple.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Dried wood ear mushrooms: 20 g / Fresh: 120 g
cac_buoc: Rehydrate the dried wood ear mushrooms in about 400 ml of water for 45 minutes (skip this if using fresh).
Trim the woody stems off the hydrated mushrooms (as shown in photos 4, 5, 6) and wash thoroughly.
Bring a pot of water to a boil. Add the mushrooms and boil on high heat for 1.5-2 minutes.
Mince the garlic and chilies and place them in a medium to large bowl. Add the salt, sugar, light soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, and wasabi in the quantities listed above.
Drain the mushrooms well and add them to the bowl with the dressing.
Toss thoroughly and serve on a plate.
Adjust the seasonings to your taste; the wasabi can be omitted if preferred.
The salad tastes better if left to cool and marinate for about 15 minutes.

mon_an.ten: Romaine Lettuce Salad with Sesame Dressing
mon_an.mo_ta: A refreshing, non-greasy home-style salad: the rich nuttiness of sesame sauce coats crisp romaine lettuce, creating a stimulating blend of sour, sweet, salty, and fragrant flavors. Lettuce provides vitamins and fiber, while sesame sauce adds calcium and healthy fats. It's very easy to make—just cut and toss. From prep to table in about ten minutes, perfect for beginners and busy schedules.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 1-2 people.
1 head of romaine lettuce (approx. 200 g) * number of servings
5 ml soy sauce * number of servings
10 ml sesame paste * number of servings
5 ml sesame oil * number of servings
10 ml oyster sauce * number of servings
cac_buoc: Crush and mince the garlic.
In a bowl, combine the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame paste, sesame oil, sugar, oyster sauce, and minced garlic. Whisk until smooth.
Cut the lettuce into sections, each no longer than 4 cm.
Place the lettuce in a large basin, pour the dressing over it, and toss thoroughly.
Sesame paste can be substituted with peanut butter.
Ensure the sesame sauce is mixed very thoroughly with the lettuce for the best flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: A crisp and refreshing home-style salad: the celtuce stem becomes crunchier after salting, with a mild spicy kick that makes it a great appetizer. It is rich in vitamins and fiber and low in calories. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about twenty minutes from prep to table. It tastes even better when chilled.
cac_buoc: Peel the celtuce and cut into small batons. Cut the radish into batons as well. Place them in a large bowl, toss with salt, and let sit for 10 minutes.
Rinse the salted vegetables with water 1-2 times.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the vegetables, and cook for 1 minute. Drain well and place in a large bowl.
Heat oil in a pan, sauté the ginger, garlic, and chilies for 30-45 seconds, then pour the hot oil and aromatics over the celtuce.
Toss thoroughly and serve on a plate.
The radish is optional, used mainly for color.
Once plated, you can add light soy sauce, sugar, aromatic vinegar, or sesame seeds to taste for more depth.
The size of the batons is up to you, but ensure the celtuce is peeled thoroughly, otherwise the crunchiness will be affected.
Chilling the salad before serving yields even better results.

mon_an.mo_ta: A refreshing and easy-to-eat cold dish, rich in plant protein and calcium, low in fat, and healthy. It's quick to make, usually taking a beginner only 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 1 person.
cac_buoc: Cut the tofu into 2 cm cubes and set aside.
Pour 500 ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the tofu and boil for **1-2 minutes** to remove the raw soy smell and firm up the texture.
Remove the tofu, drain well, place in a bowl, and set aside.
Wash and finely chop the green onions; set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic; set aside.
In a clean small bowl, combine 15 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml sesame oil, 5 ml vinegar (optional), and 2 g white sugar (optional).
Add the minced garlic.
Stir well until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is combined.
Drizzle the sauce evenly over the tofu.
Garnish with the chopped green onions.
If desired, drizzle with 5 ml of chili oil (optional).
Gently toss with chopsticks or a spoon and serve.
When making this salad, use firm or extra-firm tofu as it holds its shape better and has a nicer bite.
For a milder flavor, omit the vinegar and chili oil.
The sauce ratios can be adjusted to your preference.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cold Enoki Mushroom Salad is a simple, quick appetizer: crunchy, tender, and slippery with a savory, slightly sour taste. Enoki mushrooms are rich in fiber and vitamins and low in calories. The process only involves blanching and seasoning, making it very beginner-friendly and quick to prepare when busy. Takes about 10 minutes from prep to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 1 person.
cac_buoc: Trim the roots off the enoki mushrooms, wash with water, and set aside.
Wash and finely chop the green onions; set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic; set aside.
Pour 1000 ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the enoki mushrooms and cook for **1-2 minutes** until softened.
Remove the mushrooms, drain well, place in a large bowl, and set aside.
In another clean small bowl, combine 15 ml light soy sauce, 10 ml vinegar, 3 g white sugar (optional), and 5 ml sesame oil (optional).
Add the minced garlic.
Stir well until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is combined.
Drizzle the sauce evenly over the enoki mushrooms.
Garnish with the chopped green onions.
If desired, drizzle with 5 ml of chili oil (optional).
Gently toss with chopsticks and serve.
Do not blanch the enoki mushrooms for too long to maintain their crunch.
The sauce ratios can be adjusted to your preference.
If you don't like spicy food, omit the chili oil.

mon_an.mo_ta: A refreshing home-style appetizer: crunchy cucumbers with a pleasant sour aroma. Cucumbers are high in water and vitamins, helping to cool the body and hydrate the skin. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly: just smash, season, and marinate for 15 minutes. The whole process takes about 20 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 1 person.
Vinegar - 7.5 ml + 4 ml * number of servings
Soy sauce - 5 ml + 2.5 ml * number of servings
Salt - 0.4 g + 0.2 g * number of servings
Sesame oil - 5 ml + 2 ml * number of servings
cac_buoc: Use a knife to smash the cucumbers flat, then chop them into 3 cm pieces.
Place the chopped cucumbers in a bowl.
Crush and mince the garlic.
Add 5 g of white sugar to the bowl, toss well, and marinate for 15 minutes (marinating with sugar results in better flavor, better color, and prevents wilting).
Add the vinegar, soy sauce, salt, oyster sauce, and garlic to the bowl; mix well.
Add the sesame oil and toss again.
Sometimes the ends of the cucumber can be bitter; wash them well, trim the ends, and taste to be sure.
You can eat it immediately or prepare it in advance and keep it in the fridge (not the freezer).
If refrigerating, cover tightly with plastic wrap and consume within 8 hours, otherwise the cucumber will over-marinate and lose its crunch.
Peeling the cucumber is recommended for a better texture.

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Cabbage with Egg and Glass Noodles
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a savory and fresh home-style stir-fry: crunchy shredded cabbage pairs with chewy glass noodles and fluffy eggs for a rich variety of textures. Cabbage is rich in vitamins and fiber, eggs provide quality protein, and carrots add extra nutrition for a balanced meal. The glass noodles need soaking, so there are a few steps, but the technique is straightforward. It's a slight challenge for beginners. Takes about 1 hour 20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt - 2 g, Light soy sauce - 15 ml, Dark soy sauce - 10 ml, Oyster sauce - 10 ml
Green onion - half a stalk, Garlic - 2 cloves, Dried chilies - 5 pieces
cac_buoc: Shred the carrot and cabbage; set aside.
Soak the glass noodles in cold water for 1 hour, then place them in a pot and pour boiling water over them. Cook until softened, then drain and set aside.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add salt, and whisk for 15 seconds.
Finely chop the green onion, garlic, and chilies; set aside.
Heat oil in a wok, pour in the eggs, scramble until cooked, then remove and set aside.
Add more oil to the wok, then sauté the green onion, garlic, and dried chilies for 8 seconds.
Add the shredded carrot and cabbage; stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the glass noodles.
Season with 15 ml light soy sauce, 10 ml dark soy sauce, 10 ml oyster sauce, and 2 g salt.
Add the cooked eggs back into the wok and stir-fry for about 15 seconds.
Remove from the heat and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic Indian vegetarian home-style dish characterized by its dry, fragrant, and golden appearance with bold spices. Featuring soft potatoes and slightly charred cauliflower, it carries the authentic flavors of North India. Rich in fiber and Vitamin C, it offers balanced nutrition. The recipe is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 25 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2-3 people.
2 potatoes (about 250g), peeled and cut into 2cm chunks
1 head of cauliflower (about 300g), broken into small florets
8g fresh ginger, grated into a paste
cac_buoc: Peel the potatoes and cut them into 2cm chunks.
Break the cauliflower into uniform small florets; use a knife to cut down any larger pieces.
Add 30ml of cooking oil to a pan and heat over medium heat.
Once the oil is hot, add 3g of cumin seeds and fry until the *cumin seeds darken and become fragrant* (about 10 seconds, be careful not to burn them).
Add the chopped onion and sauté until *translucent and slightly golden* (about 3-4 minutes).
Add the ginger, garlic, and green chili, and sauté for 1 minute.
Add the chopped tomato and sauté until *soft and mushy* (about 2-3 minutes).
Add 3g turmeric powder, 3g red chili powder, 5g coriander powder, and 5g salt.
Sauté for 1 minute to allow the spices to blend with the vegetables.
Add the potatoes and sauté for 2 minutes so the spices evenly coat the surface.
Add the cauliflower florets and gently toss to combine.
Cover with a lid, turn the heat to medium-low, and **simmer for 12-15 minutes**. During this time, open and stir every 3-4 minutes to prevent sticking.
When the *potatoes can be easily pierced with a chopstick and the cauliflower is slightly charred*, sprinkle in 3g of garam masala.
Sauté for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat, garnish with cilantro leaves, and serve.
This is a dry-style dish; no water is needed. If it seems too dry and sticks to the pan, you can add a very small amount of water (about 15-30ml), but do not add too much.
Do not cut the potatoes too small, or they will break apart during sautéing.
Slightly charred edges on the cauliflower are normal and actually enhance the flavor.
Aloo Gobi became widely known in the West thanks to the 2001 British comedy film "Bend It Like Beckham."
This dish can be served with naan, roti, or rice.

mon_an.mo_ta: This North Indian vegetarian dish features grated bottle gourd mixed with chickpea flour, formed into dumplings, fried until crispy, and then simmered in a savory tomato-onion curry sauce. It is crispy on the outside, soft on the inside, and rich with aromatic spices. Bottle gourd is cooling, while chickpea flour provides plant-based protein and fiber, making it a satisfying and balanced meal. While it involves several steps for frying and sauce-making, it is not difficult if followed in order. The entire process takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2-3 people.
4 cloves garlic (about 12g), grated into a paste
cac_buoc: Prepare the dumplings
Peel the bottle gourd and use a grater to shred it into fine strips.
Use your hands to squeeze the water out of the shredded gourd; *squeeze as dry as possible*, otherwise the dumplings will not hold their shape when fried.
Add 80g chickpea flour, 3g salt, 3g red chili powder, and 3g coriander powder to the squeezed gourd.
Mix thoroughly by hand and knead into a dough that doesn't stick to your hands.
Shape the mixture into small balls about 3cm in diameter and set aside.
Pour 500ml of oil into a deep pot and heat over medium heat to about 170°C (test by dropping a small piece of dough; if it rises quickly and bubbles, it's ready).
Fry the dumplings in batches for **4-5 minutes** until the *surface is golden and crispy*.
Once fried, place the dumplings on paper towels to drain excess oil and set aside.
Prepare the sauce
Add 30ml of oil to a pan and heat over medium heat for 10 seconds.
Add the chopped onions and sauté until they *turn golden brown* (about 5-7 minutes).
Add the ginger and garlic paste and sauté for 1 minute until *fragrant*.
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until *completely soft and the oil separates* (about 5 minutes).
Add 3g turmeric powder, 5g red chili powder, 5g coriander powder, 3g cumin powder, and 5g salt.
Sauté for 2 minutes to blend the spices with the tomatoes.
Pour in 200ml of water, stir well, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and **simmer for 5 minutes**.
Gently drop the fried dumplings into the sauce and **simmer on low heat for 3-5 minutes** to let them absorb the flavors.
Sprinkle with 3g garam masala and the minced green chili.
Turn off the heat, garnish with cilantro, and serve.
Squeezing the water out of the gourd is the key step; too much moisture will cause the dumplings to fall apart.
Do not simmer the dumplings in the sauce for too long, or they will lose their crispness and become mushy.
In India, this dish is often served with naan or steamed white rice (Chawal).
The word "Kofta" originates from Persian/Arabic, meaning "ground or pounded," and is popular across South Asia and the Middle East.

mon_an.ten: Di San Xian (Eggplant, Potato, and Green Pepper)
mon_an.mo_ta: Di San Xian is a classic Northeast Chinese home-style dish: tender eggplant, savory potatoes, and crunchy peppers tossed in a fresh, salty sauce that pairs perfectly with rice. This combination of ingredients provides plenty of vitamins and fiber, with potatoes offering satisfying starchy energy. This dish requires frying and quick stir-frying, demanding some technical skill; beginners may need extra practice. The entire process takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: This recipe is enough for 2-4 people.
Calculate the ratio of ingredients based on the conditions above.
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients
Wash the potatoes, eggplant, and peppers.
Peel the potatoes.
Cut the eggplant and potatoes into irregular bite-sized chunks, about 15g each.
Tear the peppers by hand along the grain into pieces about 25% larger than the potatoes and eggplant.
Try to wipe any water off the surface of the peppers to prevent oil splattering during frying. Use paper towels or air-dry for half an hour.
Cut scallions into 0.5cm pieces (5g total). Mince 15g of garlic and divide into two 7.5g portions. Mince 5g of ginger.
In a small bowl, combine 10ml light soy sauce, 10g sugar, 8g starch, and 80ml water. Stir well to make the sauce and set aside.
Flash-fry the vegetables
Heat a pan and add 150ml of oil.
Fry the potatoes for 3-4 minutes until golden brown and easily pierced with a chopstick.
Remove the potatoes and keep the oil in the pan.
Fry the eggplant for 2-3 minutes until about 70% cooked; the eggplant should be soft, slightly charred on the edges, and have released some oil.
Remove the eggplant and keep the oil. (There may be no oil left.)
If there is no oil left in the pan, add another 15ml.
Fry the peppers for about 15 seconds; remove immediately when the skin starts to wrinkle. Drain and discard the oil from the pan.
Final stir-fry
Reheat the pan and add 15ml of fresh oil.
Add 5g scallions, 5g ginger, and 7.5g garlic; sauté over medium-low heat until fragrant.
Add 15ml doubanjiang (spicy bean paste). Lower the heat and sauté until the oil turns red and the paste is fragrant.
Pour in the sauce mixture. Immediately turn to high heat and stir quickly to prevent burning! The sauce will bubble and thicken in about 10 seconds.
Immediately add all the prepared potatoes, eggplant, and peppers.
Stir-fry for 20 seconds so the thickened sauce evenly coats the ingredients.
Turn off the heat and stir in the remaining 7.5g of garlic. Toss well and serve.
It is perfectly normal for there to be more sugar than starch. The starch here provides no flavor; it is only used as a physical thickener.
Eggplant will shrink to about 1/4 of its volume after frying, so don't be surprised if the amount looks much smaller than when you started.
Adding peppers to the pan may cause significant splattering. Use the pan lid as a shield and add the peppers carefully.

mon_an.mo_ta: Home-style Egg Tofu is a quick stir-fry that is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside: a golden crust envelops silky egg tofu, combined with green peppers, carrots, and seasonal vegetables. It can be adjusted to be savory or sweet and sour. Made primarily from eggs, egg tofu is rich in high-quality protein, while the addition of wood ear mushrooms and vegetables ensures balanced nutrition. It requires some pan-searing technique but is moderately easy for beginners. The whole process takes about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2 people.
30g wood ear mushrooms (about 10g dry, soaked until expanded)
2g salt (if using chicken powder, reduce to 0.5g or omit)
cac_buoc: Slice the carrots, thinly slice the peppers, and mince the onion and garlic.
Open the egg tofu packaging and cut into cylinders about 1cm thick.
Place the tapioca starch on a flat plate to prepare for coating the tofu.
Gently place the tofu on the starch, coating both sides and the edges evenly; ensure the layer is not too thick.
Heat 150ml of oil in a non-stick pan (the oil should cover more than half the height of the tofu). Flip and fry when the edges turn golden.
Once both sides are golden, remove and place on a clean plate; set aside.
Add 10-15ml of oil to a wok or pan, sauté the onion and garlic until fragrant, then add the green peppers, carrots, sausage, and wood ear mushrooms.
Add the oyster sauce, light soy sauce, salt, chicken powder, sugar, and ketchup.
Gently toss until the colors are evenly distributed.
Do not let the fried tofu sit for too long; have all your other ingredients ready beforehand.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Diced Lotus Root is a quick vegetarian home-style dish: the lotus root is refreshingly crunchy and tender, with a savory flavor and a hint of spice that goes great with rice. Lotus root is rich in fiber and vitamins, helping to clear heat and hydrate the body. The method is simple, requiring only attention to blanching and seasoning, making it easy for kitchen novices. The whole process takes about 20 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Cut the scallion and bird's eye chilies into small pieces and set aside.
Peel the lotus root, cut into small cubes (no larger than 3cm), and soak in water to prevent oxidation and browning; set aside.
Add 500ml of cold water to a wok and bring to a boil.
Blanch the lotus root in the boiling water for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Discard the water, heat the pan until dry, and add 10-15ml of cooking oil.
When the oil is hot, sauté the scallion and chilies until fragrant.
Add the prepared lotus root to the pan and stir-fry over high heat.
Add the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Stir-fry for 2 minutes and serve.
When choosing lotus root, look for golden-brown skin with thick, white flesh. Avoid any that are bruised or have an unusual odor.
Try to avoid using iron cookware, as it can cause the lotus root to turn black.

mon_an.mo_ta: Dry-pot Cauliflower is a Hunan-style home dish: the cauliflower is crunchy and fragrant, paired with crispy, rendered pork belly and a mild spicy kick. Cauliflower is rich in Vitamin C and fiber, while the pork belly adds protein and energy. The difficulty is moderate, requiring careful draining after blanching and rendering the fat from the pork. It is suitable for beginners with some basic cooking experience. Takes about 40 minutes from prep to serving.
cac_buoc: Place the cauliflower head-down and soak in light salt water for 20 minutes. Rinse well and use a small knife to break into small florets.
Blanch in boiling water for 1 minute, remove immediately and rinse with cold water until completely cooled; drain well and set aside.
Thinly slice the pork belly. Cut the white parts of the garlic/scallion and crush them with the side of a knife. Cut the red chilies into sections.
Heat the pan and add oil. When hot, sauté the white parts of the scallion until fragrant.
Add the pork belly to the pan and sauté over medium heat until the surface changes color. Continue sautéing for a while to render the fat from the pork.
Add the red chili sections and cauliflower; toss a few times.
Add 10ml of light soy sauce.
Add 5g of white sugar, turn to high heat, and stir-fry continuously for 1 minute.
Cut the garlic greens into sections, add them to the pan, toss a few times, then turn off the heat. Cover and let it steam for 1 minute before serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: Hand-torn Cabbage is a classic Hunan dish that is sour, spicy, and refreshingly crunchy. The cabbage is tender yet crisp, and the pork belly is rendered until fragrant but not greasy—a perfect appetizer. Cabbage is rich in Vitamin C and fiber, while pork belly provides protein and energy. It requires high-heat stir-frying, which can be a bit challenging for beginners, but following the steps ensures success. Takes about 20 minutes from prep to serving.
cac_buoc: Halve the cabbage and remove the white core in the center [see Figure 1].
Tear the cabbage by hand into pieces. Place in a bowl with 2g of salt, wash thoroughly, and drain [see Figure 2].
Prepare the ginger slices, garlic, chilies, and leek; set aside [see Figure 3].
Slice the pork belly, rinse with water, and set aside.
Heat 30ml of oil in a pan. Stir-fry the cabbage over high heat for 1 minute, then add 3g of salt. Continue stir-frying for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Heat another 30ml of oil in the pan and stir-fry the pork belly over high heat for 1 minute.
Add the ginger slices and other aromatics; sauté for 1 minute.
Return the cabbage to the pan, then season with black vinegar, cooking wine, and chicken powder. Continue stir-frying over high heat for 2 minutes, then serve.
In step 5, the stir-frying time should be adjusted based on the actual situation; usually, stir-fry until the cabbage is about 70% cooked (when it has released some moisture and softened).
In step 5, adding salt helps retain the cabbage's moisture while adding a bit of flavor.
In the final step, the stir-frying time can be adjusted flexibly according to the actual heat and personal taste.

mon_an.mo_ta: Caramelized Potatoes is a classic Shandong (Lu) dish. The final product is golden and glossy with long, thin sugar threads. It is crispy on the outside, fluffy on the inside, and delightfully sweet. Potatoes provide starch and Vitamin C for a quick energy boost. This dish has a certain level of difficulty; beginners must watch the heat carefully when melting the sugar to prevent crystallization or burning. Expect it to take about 30 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 300ml cooking oil (enough to let the potatoes float)
120g white sugar (plenty of sugar is needed to create a thick syrup for the threading effect)
cac_buoc: Peel the potatoes and cut them into uniform small chunks. Toss with dry starch (do not add water) until the surface is well-coated.
Heat the oil in a pan. Add the potatoes and fry slowly, tossing occasionally for 5-7 minutes until a chopstick can pierce through them.
Remove the potatoes and place them in a large bowl; set aside.
Add water and white sugar to the pan. Stir slowly in one direction until the sugar turns a golden brown syrup.
Return the potatoes to the pan, toss for 30 seconds to coat, and remove from heat.
Arrange the potatoes on a plate and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Do not over-fry the potatoes, or they will lose their shape when caramelized and plated, affecting the presentation.
Excess cooking oil can be collected back into a bottle for future use.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Corn with Pine Nuts is a quick home-style dish with a light, sweet, and crunchy flavor. The pine nuts are rich and crispy, while the corn is sweet and tender—a widely loved Northern Chinese family favorite. The combination provides fiber, unsaturated fats, and vitamins for balanced nutrition. The method is simple and easy for beginners, usually taking only about fifteen minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 200g corn kernels (canned sweet corn or fresh boiled corn)
cac_buoc: Blanch the corn kernels and diced carrots for 1 minute, then drain.
Heat the pan, add oil, and briefly sauté the carrots before adding the corn kernels.
Add the white sugar and salt; stir-fry evenly.
Mix the water and starch to make a slurry. Pour it into the pan and stir quickly until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the roasted pine nuts and toss to combine.
Remove from heat and serve.
Dry-roasting the pine nuts over low heat until lightly golden and fragrant before starting will make them taste better.
When using canned corn, drain it thoroughly first to prevent too much liquid in the pan.
Do not use excessively high heat to avoid burning the pan or the pine nuts.

mon_an.mo_ta: A flavorful snack that is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside with a savory, aromatic finish. It has the dry-crisp texture often found in Sichuan restaurants, revealing the natural sweetness of the corn with every bite. Corn provides starch and fiber, while sesame adds healthy fats and Vitamin E. This dish has several steps but simple techniques; it just requires patience in drying and coating the corn. Very beginner-friendly. Takes about 30 minutes from thawing to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: This portion size is equivalent to a standard serving at a Sichuan restaurant.
Starch (enough to coat the kernels, about 40-70g)
cac_buoc: Thaw the corn kernels: soak in warm water for 15 minutes or boil in water for 5 minutes.
Take a tray (Box A), line it with paper towels, and pour in the thawed corn.
Shake, shake, shake! - until the paper towels are completely soaked.
Take a second tray (Box B), line it with fresh paper towels, and transfer all the corn from Box A to Box B.
Shake, shake, shake! - until these paper towels are also soaked.
Repeat this process several times until no visible water droplets remain on the corn, though it should still be damp.
Pour in plenty of starch, enough to completely cover the corn kernels.
Shake, shake, shake! - until the starch thoroughly coats every kernel.
Turn on the heat, place the pan, and add oil—try to coat the bottom evenly but don't use too much.
When the oil is about 80% hot, add the starch-coated corn.
Fry over medium heat for 30 seconds without stirring, otherwise the coating will fall off.
Gently stir-fry for 3 minutes, then remove from heat.
The most important step: sprinkle with 3g of salt and pepper seasoning and the sesame seeds!
Your fragrant "Salt and Pepper Corn" is now ready.
Don't bother shucking fresh corn by hand; you can buy "pre-shucked corn kernels" from grocery apps and thaw them with warm water.
If thawing with boiling water is too slow, just cook them in the boiling water! (But never cook the corn inside the bag; tear a small hole first).

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Green Beans with Minced Pork and Olive Paste
mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Green Beans with Minced Pork and Olive Paste is a classic Teochew-style home-cooked dish, featuring a savory, aromatic, and crunchy-yet-tender texture that pairs perfectly with rice. Green beans are rich in fiber and vitamins, combined with minced pork for high-quality protein, while the olive paste (Gan Lan Cai) provides a unique savory umami. The steps are clear and beginner-friendly; just ensure the beans are thoroughly cooked. Total time from preparation to serving is about thirty minutes.
cac_buoc: Wash the green beans, remove the tough strings, and dice them into uniform pieces; set aside.
Crush and mince the garlic; set aside.
Dice the bird's eye chili into uniform pieces; set aside.
Remove the skin from the pork belly and mince the meat; set aside.

Heat the wok and swirl in 20ml of oil to coat; pour out the hot oil and replace it with 10ml of room-temperature oil—this is the legendary "hot wok, cold oil" technique used to prevent the minced pork from sticking.

If you don't have a container for room-temperature oil, you can skip the coating step; simply add oil to the wok, add the minced pork immediately, and sauté over low heat for two minutes to render the fat.
Once the pork is fragrant, add the minced garlic, olive paste, and chili; stir-fry until aromatic.
Add the green beans and stir-fry over medium heat for at least 5 minutes; you must ensure the beans are **thoroughly cooked** to avoid potential food poisoning.
When the beans are cooked through, drizzle 2ml of soy sauce around the edges of the wok, then add 2g salt, 1g chicken powder, 1g pepper, and 0.5g sugar.
Toss well to combine the seasonings.
Remove from the wok and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Water-Oil Braised Leafy Greens is a simple and quick home-style side dish: using boiling water with a few drops of oil and seasoning to make the leaves tender and glossy. This method is both refreshing and lightly fragrant. It helps increase the absorption of fat-soluble vitamins, making it more nutritious than eating raw vegetables. The difficulty is low and very beginner-friendly; it usually takes only 10 minutes from washing to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Water-rich leafy greens (they may look like a lot during prep, but the volume reduces quickly when heated).
cac_buoc: Wash the vegetables thoroughly.
Pour 150ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil. (The water does not need to fully submerge the vegetables.)
Add 3g of salt.
(Optional) Add 3ml of oyster sauce.
Add 2ml of cooking oil.
Add the vegetables, toss slightly, then cover and braise for 1 minute.
Scoop onto a plate.
If you are unsure about the saltiness, start with less salt and taste before serving to decide if more is needed.
You can use chicken broth or bone broth instead of water for better flavor.
Do not braise for too long.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a savory, rice-enhancing Hunan-style quick dish: sour, spicy, fresh, and aromatic. The eggs have crispy edges and a soft, porous texture that soaks up the rich sauce, making it very appetizing. Eggs provide high-quality protein and lecithin, while the fragrant vinegar further stimulates the appetite. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about ten minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Do not beat the eggs; crack them directly into a bowl and set aside.
Cut the scallions into 3cm lengths.
Place the garlic cloves and bird's eye chilies into a garlic mincer and grind finely.
In a small bowl, combine the fragrant vinegar, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, white sugar, and a splash of water; stir well to make the sweet and sour sauce.
When the oil is hot, pour in the eggs. Once the eggs have set, break them into large pieces with a spatula, add the minced garlic and chili, then pour in the sweet and sour sauce.
Reduce the sauce over high heat; just before serving, toss in the scallions and it's done.
In my experience, using pure brewed Lao Heng He fragrant vinegar with no additives provides the best flavor; the vinegar aroma is the soul of this dish.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Eggs with Onions is a savory and aromatic home-style dish: soft, silky eggs paired with sweet onions make it a national favorite for pairing with rice. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and vitamins, while onions provide fiber and antioxidants, making this a nutritionally balanced quick meal. The method is extremely simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 5 minutes from prep to serving.
cac_buoc: Crack the eggs into a large bowl, add the sliced onions and salt, then whisk for 60 seconds.
Heat oil in a pan, pour in the egg mixture, and fry one side for 30-45 seconds. Flip and continue to stir-fry for 2-3 minutes, then drizzle with cooking wine and remove from the pan.
Serve the eggs on a plate and garnish with chopped scallions.

mon_an.mo_ta: A common home-style vegetarian dish that is crunchy, tender, and refreshing. Rich in vitamin C and fiber. The method is simple and quick; beginners usually only need 15 minutes to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 2 people (as a side dish).
cac_buoc: Wash the cauliflower, use a knife or your hands to break it into small florets, and slice the large stems; set aside.
Peel and slice the garlic; set aside.
Pour 1000 ml of drinking water into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the cauliflower florets and cook for **2-3 minutes** until the color lightens and they become slightly tender.
Remove the blanched cauliflower and drain well; set aside.
Heat a wok, add 15 ml of cooking oil, and heat over high heat.
Add the sliced garlic and sauté quickly until fragrant.
Add the blanched cauliflower, switch to medium-high heat, and stir-fry quickly for about **2 minutes** to heat evenly.
Add 3 g of salt and continue to stir-fry well.
Drizzle 50 ml of drinking water around the edges of the wok, cover with a lid, and braise for **1 minute** so the cauliflower cooks through and absorbs the flavor.
Open the lid, give it a quick final toss, and serve.
Blanching the cauliflower first shortens the stir-fry time and ensures it cooks evenly.
The stir-fry time can be adjusted based on your preferred texture. If you like it crunchier, shorten the time.

mon_an.mo_ta: A home-style steamed dish that preserves the original flavor, natural sweetness, and nutrients of the pumpkin. It is soft, sticky, and sweet, suitable as both a dessert or a staple starch. Pumpkin is rich in β-carotene and fiber, which are good for vision and gut health. Extremely simple to make, even for beginners; it takes only 15-20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1-2 people.
cac_buoc: Wash the pumpkin skin, then remove the pulp and seeds.
Cut the pumpkin into slices about 2 cm thick; set aside.
Pour 1000 ml of drinking water into the steamer.
Arrange the pumpkin slices evenly on a plate.
Once the water in the steamer is boiling, place the plate of pumpkin inside.
Cover and steam over high heat for **15-20 minutes**, until the pumpkin is soft and can be easily pierced with a chopstick.
Turn off the heat and carefully remove the plate.
Different varieties of pumpkin vary in sweetness and starchiness. Mature pumpkins are usually sweeter and fluffier.
Pumpkin skin is nutritious; you can steam it with the skin on if preferred, but be sure to wash it thoroughly.
Steaming time depends on the size and thickness of the slices and the variety of pumpkin. Testing with a chopstick is the best way to check for doneness.

mon_an.ten: Steamed and Stir-fried Potatoes and Carrots
mon_an.mo_ta: This potato and carrot dish uses the "steam first, stir-fry later" method, resulting in distinct, soft, and savory shreds. Potatoes and carrots are rich in potassium and β-carotene, providing balanced nutrition. The process is simple and quick, making it easy for beginners; it takes only 20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Li Dai Chu brand stir-fry seasoning 1/2 teaspoon
Li Dai Chu brand meat-flavor seasoning 1/2 teaspoon
cac_buoc: Shred the carrots and potatoes finely (you can use a julienne peeler).

Toss the carrot and potato shreds with flour (the carrots should look like small sausages and the potatoes like noodles; each shred should be distinct and fall separately when picked up with dry hands).
**Loosen the mixture** of potato and carrot shreds and steam in an electric steamer for **5** minutes (or for 5 minutes over high heat in a regular steamer once the steam rises).
**Note: Do not cover the lid immediately at the start; leave it uncovered until steam is generated, then cover (this prevents sticking).**
Turn the heat to high; after 15 seconds, add the scallions and sauté until fragrant. Stir-fry for 40 seconds, then add the steamed potato and carrot shreds and toss.
After 20 seconds, add the Li Dai Chu stir-fry seasoning, followed by the meat-flavor seasoning, then the salt, and finally the MSG. Stir briefly, then turn off the heat and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Silky Scrambled Eggs is a classic home-style dish: the eggs are soft and smooth with a rich egg aroma and a hint of milk. Eggs are high in quality protein and vitamins, making them nutritious and easy to digest. The method is very friendly for beginners to master; it takes only about 5 minutes from prep to serving, making it an ideal choice for a quick energy boost when busy.
cac_buoc: Add the milk and 5ml of oil to the eggs, whisk well, and set aside.
Heat a non-stick pan over high heat for about 30 seconds, then add 5ml of oil.
Heat for 30 seconds, then switch to low heat and pour in the egg mixture.
Let it sit in the pan for 5 seconds, then use a spatula to gently push the eggs from the edges toward the center.
Stir-fry until the eggs are mostly set, then turn off the heat and serve on a plate.
Finally, you can sprinkle with a bit of black pepper or salt to season according to your taste.

mon_an.mo_ta: This home-style stir-fried eggplant is soft and flavorful with a rich savory sauce aroma, enhanced by the fragrance of star anise. Eggplant is rich in fiber, vitamin P, and potassium, which help protect cardiovascular health. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, using a quick high-heat stir-fry technique. It takes about twenty minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1-2 people.
Star anise = number of servings * 1 petal
Dried shrimp = number of servings * half a handful (adult male hand)
Minced pork = number of servings * 50 g
Soy sauce = number of servings * 40 ml
> Note: Oil and soy sauce are also mentioned in the steps; refer to them to determine the exact amounts needed.
cac_buoc: Wash the eggplants and cut them into two sections (crosswise). Cut each section into diamond-shaped pieces and place them in a bowl; set aside.
Wash the scallions and chop them; set aside on the cutting board.
Break the star anise into small pieces; set aside on the cutting board.
If using minced pork, first use 10 ml of oil (15 ml if using lean pork) and stir-fry over medium heat until it changes color (about 1 minute), then scoop out and set aside.
Turn on the stove and heat the wok until all water has evaporated.
Pour in the cooking oil, using enough to double the depth needed to cover the bottom (more oil is fine, but do not use too little).
When the oil is about 60% hot, add the optional ingredients: star anise, dried shrimp, and scallions.
If you don't have optional ingredients like star anise, heat the oil until it is 90% hot.
When the oil reaches 90% heat, pour the eggplant from the bowl into the wok and toss with a spatula.

Stir-fry for about 40 seconds, hold the spatula parallel to the wok, and pour the soy sauce onto the spatula. Use about 2.5 spatula-fulls per person (it's better to have slightly less soy sauce than too much, as it can become too salty).
When the eggplant is halfway softened (about 1 minute later), add the previously cooked minced pork and toss quickly to combine.
If using sugar and vinegar, add them now.
Continue to stir-fry.
Wait until all the eggplant in the wok has changed color and softened, then remove from the pan.
Because of the soy sauce, this dish does not need extra salt. Taste before serving; if it's not salty enough, add a pinch of salt, and increase the soy sauce next time.
If you used dried shrimp, you can reduce the amount of soy sauce as desired.
Keep the heat on high throughout the stir-frying process.
Remember! Absolutely do not add water, or it will become boiled eggplant and won't taste good; therefore, it's better to have too much oil than too little.
If your home stove doesn't get significantly hotter after reaching 70% heat, you can proceed to the next step without waiting for 90% heat.
Add the sugar and vinegar at the very end and stir-fry for 20 seconds before serving to prevent the vinegar's acidity from evaporating too early.

mon_an.mo_ta: A refreshing and easy-to-eat home-style vegetarian dish that is crunchy, tender, savory, and fresh with a sweet finish. Green vegetables are rich in vitamins and fiber, aiding digestion. The method is extremely simple and can be done by anyone; it takes only about 10 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Cooking oil 10-15ml (enough to coat the bottom of the pan)
cac_buoc: Separate the vegetables into small stalks, wash thoroughly with water, and set aside.
Mince the garlic and set aside.
Heat the pan over medium or high heat, then add 10-15ml of cooking oil. Wait 30 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Add the prepared vegetables to the pan and stir-fry until they soften (about 1 minute).
Add the minced garlic.

Pour in the calculated amount of clean water (the water level should evenly moisten or almost submerge the vegetables), add the salt (2g * number of servings), and continue to stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Finally, add the white sugar, turn the heat to low, cover with a lid, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Scoop onto a plate.
Adding white sugar helps keep the vegetables looking greener.

mon_an.mo_ta: The blooming onion is a classic American-style appetizer: a whole onion is cut so it stays connected at the base, then battered and fried until the "petals" naturally open like a golden flower. It features a crispy exterior and a sweet interior, making it a perfect snack for gatherings when paired with a dipping sauce. The difficulty lies in selecting the right ingredients, knife skills, and oil temperature: the onion must be large and sweet, cutting too deep will cause the petals to fall off, insufficient battering prevents a crispy crust, and oil that is too hot will burn the exterior. Total time from prep to serving is about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the number of servings. One portion is enough for 2 people, calculated as follows:
120g low-gluten flour (40g of which is used for the first dredging)
1200ml cooking oil (for frying, actual loss is about 80ml)
cac_buoc: Cutting the flower
Peel the dry outer skin of the yellow onion, cut off 5mm of the top, and keep the root base intact.
Place the knife at the top and cut vertically down toward the root, stopping 1cm before the base so the root remains connected.
Similarly, make a cut every 45 degrees for a total of 16 cuts, dividing the onion into 16 petals.
Flip the onion over with the root facing up, and make an additional cut between every two petals in the same manner (8 more cuts).
Soaking
Place the cut onion into ice water with the root facing up and soak for 20 minutes.
After soaking, remove and let drain with the root facing up for 5 minutes.
Battering
Take 40g of low-gluten flour and sprinkle it evenly between the petals, separating them as you go so the inner surfaces are coated with dry flour.
Mix the remaining 80g of low-gluten flour, 40g cornstarch, 2g chili powder, 1g black pepper powder, and 3g salt; set aside.
Mix 1 egg with 100ml ice water and whisk for 30 seconds until well combined; set aside.
Dip the onion into the egg mixture with the root facing up, flipping it 3 times to ensure both sides of every petal are coated.
Place the onion into the flour mixture with the root facing up. Use your hands to scoop and sprinkle flour from the center outward into the gaps between petals; flip 3 times.
Lift the onion and shake off excess flour. Check the base of the petals for any bare spots; sprinkle more flour mixture on those areas.
Let it rest for 2 minutes to allow the flour to hydrate; the exterior should have an even layer of white flour.
Frying
Pour 1200ml of cooking oil into a deep pot and heat over medium heat to 170°C.
Place the onion into the oil with the root facing down; the oil will bubble vigorously.
Maintain the temperature between 165°C - 175°C and fry for 3 minutes. Meanwhile, use a slotted spoon to continuously ladle hot oil over the top of the onion.
Flip the onion over with the root facing up and fry for another 2 minutes.
When the petals are golden brown and the crust has hardened, remove it. The onion is ready when it floats and the petals are fully bloomed.
Place on a slotted spoon to drain for 2 minutes.
Plating
Place the onion on a plate with the root facing down so the petals naturally spread out.
Place 30ml of dipping sauce in the center (ketchup, mayonnaise, or honey mustard all work well).
Use yellow onions (sweet onions) and choose large ones; red onions are too pungent, white onions are too watery, and small onions have petals that are too thin and break easily.
When cutting the onion, you can place two chopsticks on either side of the bulb; stop when the knife hits the chopsticks to avoid cutting through the root.
Soaking in ice water helps the petals become crisp and bloom naturally; do not skip this step.
Insufficient battering is the leading cause of failure; any inner petal surfaces not coated with flour will become soft and soggy after frying.
Use a deep pot instead of a flat pan so the oil covers the whole onion; otherwise, the top petals will not cook properly.
If the oil is above 180°C, the exterior will burn before the inside is cooked; keep it below 180°C throughout.
If you don't have a kitchen thermometer, insert a chopstick into the oil; when many small, dense bubbles form around it, the temperature is about 170°C.
For the dipping sauce, you can refer to the garlic soy sauce recipe.

mon_an.mo_ta: This fragrant grilled eggplant is charred on the outside and soft on the inside. The spicy aroma of cumin and minced garlic melts into the tender eggplant flesh, easily recreating the flavor of street-side BBQ at home. Eggplant is rich in vitamin P and anthocyanins, which help protect the cardiovascular system and act as antioxidants. This recipe uses an oven but has clear steps, allowing beginners to finish in about half an hour—perfect for a quick, rice-pairing dish for family gatherings.
cac_buoc: Combine the soy sauce, cumin, salt, minced garlic, and chopped chili in a bowl; mix well and set aside.
Wash the eggplant and pat the surface dry with paper towels.
Use a fork to prick 4-8 holes on one side of the eggplant.
Apply 15-25ml of cooking oil evenly over the entire surface of the eggplant.
Set the oven to 200°C (convection mode, high heat) and preheat for 2 minutes.
Place the eggplant on the middle or top rack of the oven and bake for 12-15 minutes (until the surface wrinkles and it can be pressed down 0.3-0.5cm deep).
Remove the eggplant and use a knife to make a longitudinal slit down the center, stopping 1-1.5cm from the ends.
Use a small knife or fork to gently loosen the flesh inside the slit.
Gently pull the slit open and pour in the sauce prepared in step one.
Return the eggplant to the oven at 200°C and bake for 4-7 minutes.
Remove from the oven and turn off the power.
The final result is just like the grilled eggplant from the BBQ stalls downstairs—so fragrant!
**Note:**
If the surface is wet, not oiled enough, or not pricked with a fork, the **eggplant may explode during baking**.
**Improvement tip:**
For the first slit, you can cut the eggplant completely in half, score the flesh, and then apply the sauce.

mon_an.ten: Blanched Choy Sum with Soy Sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: This classic Cantonese dish uses the blanching technique: a quick dip in boiling water preserves the natural sweetness and crunch of the choy sum, especially the crisp stems. Rich in vitamin C and fiber, low in fat and calories, it is perfect for those seeking a healthy diet. The method is very simple, with an estimated difficulty of two stars; beginners can usually finish it in 15 minutes, making it an ideal choice for a quick vegetable side dish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The following amount is enough for two people, or one person if eaten with rice.
cac_buoc: Wash the choy sum and **remove the tough or old ends**. You can also use a knife to **peel the outer skin of the stems** if they are tough; this makes the inside taste better, but be careful with the blanching time so they stay crunchy.
Mince the garlic; if you have onion, you can add a little minced onion as well.

Prepare the "soul" sauce: mix 5g light soy sauce, 5g oyster sauce, 3g sugar, and 100ml water (half a bowl). > Adding a little starch will help the sauce coat the greens better and intensify the flavor, though some Cantonese purists might find it unusual.
Bring 500ml of water to a boil with 5g salt and 10g cooking oil.
Place the stems into the boiling water first and blanch for 1 minute until they turn deep green. Then submerge the whole plant and blanch for another 1 minute. Remove and arrange on a plate.

In a separate small pot, pour in the prepared sauce and bring to a simmer over low heat. Add half of the minced garlic, some julienned ginger, and minced chili. Alternatively: heat oil in the pot first, sauté the minced garlic and onion until fragrant, then add the sauce and chili and bring to a boil.

Reduce the sauce slightly until thickened. After it boils for about ten seconds, pour it directly over the choy sum. You don't need too much sauce, but the minced garlic is essential—don't skimp on it.
Always choose the freshest choy sum! Fresh! Fresh!
Make sure to add oil and salt to the blanching water.

mon_an.mo_ta: Century egg with silken tofu is a refreshing and appetizing cold salad: chewy, smooth century eggs paired with silken tofu that melts in your mouth. The savory, fragrant, and slightly sour flavor makes it a great accompaniment to rice. Tofu is rich in high-quality plant protein and calcium, while century eggs provide iron, vitamin A, and other nutrients. The process is nearly effortless, easy for beginners, and takes only about 5 minutes from prep to table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the number of servings. One portion is enough for 1 person.
cac_buoc: First, peel the century eggs and cut them into quarters.
Cut the silken tofu into cubes or slices and place them in the center of the plate.
Mix the light soy sauce, sugar, vinegar, sesame oil, and chili oil to make the sauce, then pour it over the dish.
Finally, optionally garnish with crushed peanuts, chopped scallions, and cilantro.
Blanching the tofu briefly beforehand can help remove the raw soy bean smell.
When cutting the century eggs, you can wipe a little sesame oil on the knife to prevent sticking.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic summer cold dish—sweet, sour, and refreshing. It is very simple to make. Tomatoes are rich in vitamin C and help stimulate the appetite. Beginners can easily master this; the entire process (including chilling) takes about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Use a knife to score a cross on the skin of the tomatoes.
Pierce the stem end with a chopstick and rotate it over a gas flame for 10 seconds (or blanch in boiling water for 30 seconds) until the skin starts to curl.
Peel the tomatoes completely.
Cut the tomatoes into eight wedges (cutting with the grain helps retain more juice), remove the stem ends, and set aside.
Once all are cut, arrange a layer of tomatoes evenly on a plate.
Sprinkle with white sugar, then repeat the layers until all tomatoes are used.
Place in the refrigerator to chill for 10 minutes.
The dish is ready—nutritious, delicious, sweet, and sour. It's a great way to cool down in summer and cleanse the palate.
Please be careful when using the knife during the process.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a savory, home-style stir-fry with a rich soy flavor. The yardlong beans are tender and well-seasoned, with a fresh spicy kick that goes perfectly with rice. Rich in fiber and vitamins, it aids digestion. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 20 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: Due to the nature of the ingredients, this recipe serves 2 people.
cac_buoc: Finely chop the scallions and mince the garlic; set aside.
Mix the light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, and salt to make a sauce; set aside.
Slice the bird's eye chilies into rings; set aside.
String the yardlong beans and cut them at a 45° angle into *4-10cm* segments; set aside.
Heat oil (10ml - 15ml) in a wok. When the oil starts to smoke, add the scallions and chilies, stir-frying until fragrant.
Add the yardlong beans and stir-fry for *30 seconds*.
Pour in the sauce and stir-fry over high heat for *2 minutes*.
Pour in 150ml of water.
Turn the heat down to medium-low, cover, and braise for 8-10 minutes.
Add the minced garlic and remove from the heat.
Cutting the beans requires some knife skill; if you are not comfortable, you can use scissors.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised winter melon is a glossy, savory, and tender vegetarian dish. It is a popular Chinese-style braised dish that is soft and flavorful. Winter melon is high in water content, fiber, and vitamin C, offering cooling properties and aiding in reducing swelling. Combined with simple seasonings, it is both nutritious and easy to digest. This dish is beginner-friendly with clear steps, requiring about 25 minutes.
cac_buoc: Peel the winter melon and cut into small cubes no larger than 2cm.
Heat oil in a pan, add the winter melon, and pan-fry slowly for 2 minutes until the surface turns golden.
Remove the winter melon and place in a large bowl; set aside.
Using the remaining oil in the pan, add the minced ginger, light soy sauce, and oyster sauce; sauté for 15 seconds.
Return the winter melon to the pan, stir-fry for 30 seconds, then pour in boiling water until the melon is submerged. Cook over high heat for 10 minutes.
Add the dark soy sauce for color and continue cooking until the melon is very soft (a chopstick should slide through easily).
Add the chicken bouillon powder, cooking wine, and scallions. Stir for 30 seconds, then transfer the winter melon to a serving bowl.
Keep the remaining sauce in the pan, pour in a starch slurry (starch mixed with water), bring to a boil to thicken, and pour the sauce over the winter melon.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised eggplant is a rich, savory, and satisfying home-style dish: tender eggplant pieces soaked in a thick sauce, combined with bell peppers and tomatoes for a balanced sweet and sour taste. The eggplant is fried until fragrant but not greasy. This dish involves coating the eggplant in batter and then slow-braising it. While it has several steps, beginners can succeed by paying attention to the details. It takes about 45 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the number of servings. One portion is enough for 2 people.
Flour = number of green eggplants * 150 grams
Soy sauce = number of eggplants * 7 grams (rounded up)
cac_buoc: Wash the green eggplants, green pepper, tomato, onion, and large scallion.
Slice the scallion into 5mm rings, peel and crush the garlic, cut the tomato into 6cm cubes, and cut the green pepper and onion into 5g pieces.
Cut the eggplant into diamond shapes (first cut into 2cm thick slices, then into 2cm strips, and finally cut diagonally into pieces).
Pour the flour into a bowl, gradually add a little water, and whisk into a thick batter.
Add the starch and 30 grams of water; mix well.
Crack the egg into the bowl, add (flour / 20) grams of salt, and whisk well.
Add the eggplant pieces to the batter and stir so every side is coated.

Heat a wok over high heat, add 500ml of oil. When a thin wisp of smoke appears, turn the heat to low. Use chopsticks to add the eggplant pieces one by one. Once all are in, turn the heat to medium. Fry until golden brown, then remove and drain the oil.
Add (servings * 5) g of oil to the wok. Add the garlic and scallion rings, sauté for 15 seconds. Add the green pepper and sauté for 30 seconds, then add the tomato and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the fried eggplant and enough water so the level is 0.8 times the height of the ingredients.
Add the soy sauce and (servings * 3) g of salt.
Wait until the sauce thickens (water level is about 0.2-0.3 times the height of the ingredients). Remove the lid, serve the dish, and turn off the heat.
Note for steps 4-6:
Must be performed in order, otherwise it will be a disaster...

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy pan-fried tofu is crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside, with a perfectly balanced savory-sweet sauce. It is a quick and satisfying dish. Tofu is rich in plant protein and calcium, while eggs provide high-quality protein. Patience is needed to fry the crust to a golden crisp, but the steps are clear and easy for beginners. The whole process takes about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 1 block firm tofu (buy 1.25 units * number of people)
50 g cornstarch * number of tofu blocks
cac_buoc: Whisk the eggs into a liquid; set aside.
Prepare the sauce (20g light soy sauce + 10g oyster sauce + 5g dark soy sauce + 10g sugar + 10g cornstarch + 200ml water).
Cut the firm tofu into slices (personal suggestion: 5 slices per person, 1.2cm thick).
Place cornstarch on a plate. Dredge each tofu slice in starch, then dip into the egg wash; set aside.
Heat a pan and add 18ml of cooking oil. Wait 10 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Place the egg-coated tofu slices evenly in the pan, covering the bottom. Fry over low heat until golden, then flip.
When both sides are golden, pour in the sauce so each piece of tofu is submerged. Cook over high heat for 3 minutes until the sauce thickens.
Turn off the heat.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a crisp and refreshing cold salad. The crunchiness of the celery blends with the chewiness of the Agrocybe mushrooms for a rich texture. High in vitamins and minerals, it is both nutritious and appetizing. The method is very simple and easy for beginners to master, taking about 30 minutes from prep to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the number of servings. One portion is enough for 1-2 people.
1 jar Min Xing brand Agrocybe mushrooms (Tea Tree mushrooms)
250-300g celery (tender celery about 30cm tall is recommended; otherwise, use mountain celery or regular celery but blanch until just cooked)
cac_buoc: (Skip if using tender celery) Boil a kettle of water; set aside.
Wash the fresh tender celery or regular celery and remove any yellow leaves; set aside.

(Skip if using tender celery) Pluck the celery leaves and set them aside in a bowl. Use a knife to shred the stalks into 2-3mm wide strips; this helps them cook faster and more evenly for a crispier texture.
Cut the tender celery into 4cm segments; set aside.
(Skip if using tender celery) Place a pot on the stove, pour in the boiling water, and wait for it to bubble.

(Skip if using tender celery) Add the shredded celery to the pot and blanch for about 20 seconds, then add the leaves. After 5 seconds, turn off the heat, remove everything, and soak in cold water; set aside.
Place the blanched celery or tender celery in a bowl. Sprinkle with salt, sesame oil, oyster sauce, and the prepared Wei Ji Xian soy sauce; mix well.
Add the Agrocybe mushrooms to the bowl and toss to combine.
Arrange on a plate.
Ready to serve.
The water level must cover the celery during blanching.
If the celery leaves are too old or tough, they can be discarded.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Eggplant and Potatoes is a classic Northeast Chinese home-style stew. It is soft, savory, and fragrant with a hint of chili and garlic—a perfect dish to pair with rice. Eggplant is rich in anthocyanins and fiber, while potatoes provide starch and vitamin C. Combined with protein from pork, this dish is nutritionally balanced and satisfying. The process is simple but requires good heat control during stir-frying and reducing the sauce, making it a moderate challenge for beginners. Total time from preparation to serving is about 45 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 2-3 people.
Eggplant = x number of servings * 1 piece (approx. 150g each)
Potatoes = x number of servings * 1 tuber (approx. 150g each)
Meat = x number of servings * 180 grams
Soy sauce = x number of servings * 15 milliliters
Salt = x number of servings * 5 grams
Chili = 50 grams (used for seasoning; use this amount regardless of the number of people)
Garlic = 3 cloves (used for seasoning; use this amount regardless of the number of people. Note: 3 small cloves, **not 3 whole bulbs**)
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the conditions above.
cac_buoc: Wash the eggplant, potatoes, and chilies; peel and crush the garlic.
Cut the eggplant and potatoes into roughly 6 cm chunks, chop the chilies into 5g pieces, and slice the meat into 3 cm strips.
Turn on the stove, heat the pan, and add x number of servings * 13 milliliters of oil.
When a thin wisp of smoke rises from the oil, add the chilies.
Once the chili fragrance is released, immediately add the meat and stir-fry with a spatula for 30 seconds.
Add the potatoes and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the eggplant and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the soy sauce and salt, then continue stir-frying for 5 minutes.
Add water until the level reaches 0.9 times the height of the ingredients in the pan, then cover with a lid.
Wait until the water level reduces to 0.1 times the height of the ingredients, then open the lid, add the garlic, stir well, and turn off the heat.
Note for steps 5-7: if the bottom of the pan becomes dry (no oil or water left), add 5 milliliters of water and continue stir-frying.

mon_an.mo_ta: Pan-fried Lettuce Leaf Pancakes are a quick and simple home-style snack—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, with the fresh aroma of lettuce leaves. Lettuce leaves are rich in vitamins and fiber, and combined with eggs, they provide high-quality protein for balanced nutrition. The process requires no complex techniques—just mix and fry both sides. It is very beginner-friendly, taking only about 10 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Finely chop the lettuce leaves, then mix with eggs, starch, light soy sauce, and chicken powder; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, pour in the lettuce mixture, and spread it evenly across the surface.
Fry the first side for 120 seconds, flip and fry the other side for another 60 seconds, then remove from the pan.
Lettuce leaves are chosen because they are commonly found in vegetable packs; however, they can be substituted with chives or similar greens.
Blanching lettuce leaves for a cold salad can result in a bitter taste, which is why they are prepared as pan-fried pancakes instead.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Spinach with Eggs is a light and easy-to-eat home-style dish. The spinach is tender and the eggs are fragrant and fresh—a popular flavor enjoyed across many regions. Spinach is rich in iron, folic acid, and vitamins, while eggs provide high-quality protein and lecithin, helping to nourish the blood and boost physical health. The entire process is simple and perfect for beginners, taking only about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Trim the spinach roots, wash thoroughly, place in a basket, and blanch in boiling water.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk well.
Heat the pan and add 10ml of oil.
When the oil is hot, pour in the beaten eggs and stir-fry over medium heat for 15 seconds to form a thin omelet, then use the spatula to cut it into small pieces.
Turn off the heat, remove the egg pieces to a plate, and do not wash the pan.
Turn the stove back on, add 5ml of oil, and when hot, add the spinach. Stir-fry over high heat for 15 seconds, then add the egg pieces back in and toss well.
Add 5g of salt and 100ml of water, then stir-fry over high heat for 10 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, this dish features a rich scallion aroma and a savory, slightly spicy flavor. Tofu is rich in plant protein and calcium, and when combined with green chilies and scallions, it provides balanced nutrition. The difficulty is moderate; the key is to pan-fry the tofu slowly over low heat. Beginners can succeed by patiently following the steps. The entire process takes about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 1 person.
White tofu blocks = x number of servings * 0.8 (rounded up).
Chicken bouillon powder = x number of servings * 1.5g.
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the conditions above and adjust to taste.
cac_buoc: Wash the tofu. Cut into slices about 5 mm thick and place on a plate.
Wash the scallions, trim the roots, chop finely, and set aside.
Wash the chilies, split them open, remove the seeds, and cut into 1cm * 1cm pieces; set aside.
Heat the pan and add x number of servings * 9ml of oil.
Once the oil is in the pan, coat the bottom evenly, arrange the tofu slices in a single layer, and fry over low heat until golden, then flip.
When both sides are golden, remove to a plate and set aside.
Add enough oil to coat the bottom of the pan, add the chilies, and stir-fry over high heat, pressing down with a spatula for 3 minutes.
Add the tofu back in, toss, then add salt and chicken powder. Stir-fry over medium heat for 1 minute, then pour in 10 ml of water and reduce the sauce over high heat.
Before serving, sprinkle with the chopped scallions and transfer to a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Celery with Garlic is a crisp and refreshing vegetarian home-style dish with a bold garlic aroma. Celery is rich in fiber, vitamin K, and potassium. The soul of this dish is its "crunch"—stir-fry over high heat for just half a minute before serving to keep it crispy and juicy. It takes only about 10 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Remove most of the celery leaves, keeping only a few young ones. If the stalks are thick, split them lengthwise for uniformity, then cut into segments no longer than 5 cm (about the length of a thumb; too long and they are hard to swallow).
Mince the garlic and set aside.
Before adding the celery to the pan, drain it as thoroughly as possible; the drier, the better.
Heat the wok, add 15 ml of lard, and once the lard is hot, sprinkle in 2 g of salt first.
Add the minced garlic and sauté over low heat for 10 seconds until fragrant.
**Switch to high heat**, toss in the celery segments, stir-fry quickly for **30 seconds**, and remove from the pan immediately.
Standard for serving: the celery should look **half-cooked**, jade green in color, and not yet wilted to maintain maximum crunch.
Fragrant celery (the thin-stalked variety) is best for its crisp and tender texture. Regular celery works too, but thick stalks must be split lengthwise.
**Quick stir-frying over high heat is key**; the time from adding the celery to removing it should not exceed 1 minute. Overcooking makes it soft and lose its crunch.
Ensure the celery is well-drained before cooking; excess water will lower the pan temperature and "boil" the celery instead of stir-frying it.
Stir-frying with lard is more fragrant than oil, but cooking oil can be used as a substitute.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Water Spinach with Garlic is a crisp, refreshing, and garlicky dish, typical of Sichuan-style small stir-fries. Water spinach is rich in fiber, vitamins, and calcium, which helps stimulate digestion. The method is very simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Wash the water spinach, remove bruised leaves or tough stems, and cut into 2 or 3 equal segments (to prevent them from being too long to stir-fry).
First, add a little oil to the pan and heat until it lightly smokes. Swirl the pan so the hot oil coats the sides, then pour in the remaining oil (the "hot pan, cold oil" technique).
Add the minced garlic and sauté over low heat for 10 to 15 seconds until fragrant.

Quickly add all the water spinach, **turn the heat to high**, and use a spatula in one hand and chopsticks in the other to toss the spinach continuously **until it softens and turns a vibrant green**.
Once softened, put down the chopsticks and use the spatula to quickly stir-fry for 15-20 seconds to ensure even heating, then sprinkle in 2 g salt, 3 g sugar, and 8 ml light soy sauce.
Continue stir-frying over high heat for 10 seconds, then remove from the pan.
Try to choose fresh, young water spinach; otherwise, the result may be tough.
The amount of water spinach should be determined by your pan size; it is recommended not to exceed one panful to prevent leaves from falling out during tossing.
You must **use high heat** when stir-frying water spinach so it softens quickly while remaining crisp; high heat also helps release the aroma of the light soy sauce.

mon_an.mo_ta: This home-style vegetable dish stands out with its bold garlic aroma and simple seasoning. The broccoli is blanched until tender-crisp, making it light and fresh. Rich in vitamin C, fiber, and antioxidants, it is a quick and nutritious vegetarian dish. The process is easy to master for beginners, usually taking about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Cut the broccoli into small florets and wash thoroughly.
Peel and mince the garlic; set aside.
Pour 1000 ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the broccoli and **cook for 2-3 minutes** over high heat until it turns jade green and tender.
Remove the cooked broccoli, drain well, arrange on a plate, and set aside.
Heat a pan and add 10 ml of cooking oil. When the oil is hot, add the minced garlic and sauté over low heat until fragrant.
Add 10 ml light soy sauce, 5 ml oyster sauce, 2 g white sugar, and 30 ml water.
Bring the sauce in the pan to a boil.
Pour the cooked garlic sauce evenly over the broccoli on the plate.
Do not exceed the recommended blanching time to avoid affecting the broccoli's crunch and nutritional value.
If you prefer a crunchier texture, shorten the blanching time.

mon_an.mo_ta: Kabayaki Eggplant is a sweet and savory home-style dish with a soft, tender texture. It adopts the Japanese Kabayaki flavor profile but uses Chinese braising and pan-frying techniques. Eggplant is rich in fiber and vitamins, helping to clear heat and promote circulation. The difficulty is moderate and requires some patience; expect it to take about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The amount of oil depends on the type of pan used:
Non-stick pan: oil should form droplets and be spread to cover the area of the eggplant.
Cast iron pan: oil should be spread to just cover the bottom of the pan.
1 long eggplant, narrow at the top and wider at the bottom (Note: do not use Zhejiang or round eggplants).
cac_buoc: Peel the eggplant and cut crosswise into two segments.
Steam for 5 minutes.
Slice lengthwise but do not cut all the way through; make 2-3 shallow scores on each inner side so it can be flattened out.
Pan-fry until both sides are golden.
Pour the Kabayaki sauce over the eggplant until it reaches 1/2 the height of the eggplant.

Fry until the bottom side takes on color, then flip and reduce the sauce; if the sauce doesn't thicken, add a starch slurry (ratio of starch to water from 1:4 to 1:10 depending on the sauce consistency).
Drizzle the remaining Kabayaki sauce over the eggplant.
Remove from the pan and serve.
This "Kabayaki" version is actually quite Chinese; traditional Japanese Kabayaki is grilled.
The soul of the dish is the Kabayaki sauce; you can also use store-bought sauce.
If the dish feels too rich, garnish with 2-5 mm chopped scallions for color and balance.
When making other eggplant dishes (like Fish-Fragrant or Soy-Braised), Zhejiang eggplants are highly recommended for their thin skin and slender shape.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tiger-skin Green Peppers is a classic home-style side dish. The skin is slightly charred and wrinkled, while the texture is soft yet crisp. It features a savory, fresh, and sweet-and-sour flavor that is very appetizing. Green peppers are rich in vitamin C and fiber, boosting immunity and digestion. The process is straightforward; once you master the pressing technique and heat control, it is easy for beginners. Usually ready in 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green peppers 5 pieces, 10-15cm long is ideal
cac_buoc: Remove the stems from the green peppers and wash under running water.
Cut the peppers into long strips; on average, slice each pepper lengthwise into 3-4 strips.
Peel and mince the garlic into 2mm cubes.
`Seasoning 1`: Pour 20ml of oil into a small bowl and add the minced garlic.
`Seasoning 2`: Combine white sugar, light soy sauce, vinegar, and salt in a bowl (or similar container) and stir well.
Pour `Seasoning 1` into the pan and heat until 50% hot, then add the green peppers in a single layer without overlapping.
