Use a spatula to continuously press down on the peppers, flipping them when appropriate.
Sauté for about 2 minutes; when the pepper skins appear wrinkled and charred (tiger-skin effect), pour in `Seasoning 2`.
Increase the heat and continue stir-frying for 30 seconds, then remove from the pan and serve.

mon_an.ten: Stir-fried Triple Mushrooms in Oyster Sauce
mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Triple Mushrooms in Oyster Sauce is a fresh, silky, and quick home-style stir-fry. The mushrooms are thoroughly infused with oyster sauce, resulting in a tender and slightly chewy texture with a hint of spice. Rich in plant protein, fiber, and vitamins, and paired with broccoli for balanced nutrition. The method is simple and easy for beginners to master, taking about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Trim the dirty roots off the seafood and white beech mushrooms and separate the clusters.
Slice the shiitake mushrooms (0.5-1 cm thick; slightly thicker slices provide a better chew).
In a small bowl, mix the starch with 50ml of water until smooth and no lumps remain (this is your starch slurry); set aside.
Bring water to a boil, add the broccoli, blanch for 3 minutes, then remove to a bowl and set aside.
Clean the pot and boil fresh water with 5 g of salt; add all the mushrooms and blanch for 1 minute.
After 1 minute, remove the mushrooms and drain well.
Heat oil in a pan; when small bubbles appear, add the minced ginger, bird's eye chili, and bell pepper, and sauté for 30 seconds.
Add the three types of mushrooms, then add light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and chicken powder. Toss well, then pour in the starch slurry.
Cook over medium heat until the sauce thickens, then add the cooking wine and chopped scallions before removing from the pan.
Garnish with the blanched broccoli.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried lettuce with oyster sauce is a refreshing and crisp home-style dish: tender-crunchy lettuce drizzled with a garlicky oyster sauce that perfectly balances savory and sweet. This quick vegetarian dish is popular in both Cantonese and Sichuan restaurants. Rich in vitamins and fiber to aid digestion, the recipe is very beginner-friendly, taking only about 15 minutes from washing the greens to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The portion size for this recipe is equivalent to a standard serving at a Sichuan restaurant
cac_buoc: Wash the lettuce thoroughly and remove any bruised leaves.
Heat a pot with 1 L of fresh water. Add 2 ml - 3 ml of cooking oil and 0.5 g of salt, then wait for the water to boil.
Once boiling, add the lettuce and blanch **each leaf** for 10 seconds.
Remove the lettuce, drain well, and arrange on a plate.
Prepare the sauce: in a bowl, combine 10 ml light soy sauce, 6-8 ml oyster sauce, 0.5 g salt, and 1 g white sugar. Add 10-15 ml of fresh water and stir well.
Reheat the pan and add 5-8 ml of cooking oil. Once the oil is hot, add the minced garlic.
When the garlic becomes fragrant, pour in the prepared sauce. Bring to a boil and turn off the heat immediately.
**Drizzle** the sauce evenly over the lettuce.
This dish is rich in vitamins and simple to make, offering a refreshing taste that is gentle on the body.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic Chinese home-style dish with a sweet and sour appetite-whetting flavor. Silky scrambled eggs wrap around soft, juicy tomatoes to create a timeless comfort food. Eggs provide high-quality protein while tomatoes are rich in Vitamin C and lycopene, making it a balanced and easily absorbed meal. With simple steps and accessible ingredients, it is perfect for beginners and takes only 15 minutes from prep to plate.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 1 person.
Eggs = 1.5 * x number of servings, rounded up
Cooking oil = 4ml * x number of eggs
Chopped green onions = 0-10g * x number of servings
cac_buoc: Wash the tomatoes.
Optional: Peel the tomatoes by blanching them in boiling water, then transferring them to cold water to slip the skins off.
Remove the stems and cut the tomatoes into small chunks (no larger than 4cm). These are your `tomato chunks`.
Crack the eggs into a bowl, add `1g * x number of servings` of salt, and whisk well. This is your `egg wash`. You may add 1ml of vinegar to the eggs to remove any fishy scent and make them fluffier.
Heat the pan and add the cooking oil.
When the oil is hot, pour in the `egg wash`. Stir-fry until the eggs set into curds and turn slightly golden. These are your `soft-scrambled eggs`.
Turn off the heat. Remove the `soft-scrambled eggs` to a plate and turn the heat back on. Note: Do not wash the pan.
Add the `tomato chunks` to the pan. Use a spatula to press and stir for 20 seconds, or until the tomatoes soften and break down.
Return the `soft-scrambled eggs` to the pan and toss well. You may add 10ml of ketchup and 50ml of water if you prefer more sauce. You can also add cooked meats or other ingredients at this stage.
Add the remaining salt, sugar (optional, if you prefer a sweeter taste), and chopped green onions (optional). Toss to combine.
Turn off the heat and serve.
This dish has many variations depending on personal preference, including but not limited to:
Quick method:
Add the `tomato chunks` directly into the pan with the `soft-scrambled eggs` and stir-fry together until the tomatoes are soft.
Continue from step 10.
Replace "salt" with "two drops of light soy sauce".

mon_an.mo_ta: A light and fresh home-style thickened soup that is sweet, sour, and silky smooth. Tomatoes provide Vitamin C and lycopene, while eggs and tofu offer high-quality protein for a balanced, easy-to-digest meal. The process is simple—just chop, sauté, and simmer—making it easy for beginners to master in about 15 minutes.
cac_buoc: Small dice the tomato, whisk the egg in a bowl, and cube the tofu; set aside.
Heat oil in a pan, add the ginger slice, and after 5 seconds, add the tomatoes and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour the boiling water into the pan. Once the broth boils, add the whisked egg and cubed tofu after 60 seconds.
When the soup returns to a boil, pour in the starch slurry (starch mixed with a little water) and stir in one direction for two rotations.
Add the chicken bouillon, salt, and green onions. Serve after 30 seconds.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried zucchini with eggs is a refreshing and easy home-style dish: succulent zucchini paired with fluffy scrambled eggs. Adding tomatoes provides a sweet and sour note that makes it very appetizing with rice. Eggs provide protein and lecithin, while zucchini is high in Vitamin C and fiber. The process is simple and beginner-friendly, usually taking only 15 minutes from prep to table.
cac_buoc: Wash the tomato and cut into small pieces; set aside.
Wash the zucchini and cut into diamond shapes (approx. 4cm per side); set aside.
Crack three eggs into a bowl and whisk until well combined; set aside.
Heat the pan and add 5ml - 10ml of cooking oil.
Pour in the eggs and stir constantly until they set into curds. Use the spatula to break them into smaller pieces, then remove to a bowl and set aside.
Add another 5ml - 10ml of oil to the pan, add the tomatoes, and sauté until soft.
Add the zucchini and toss well. Add 6g of salt, reduce to low heat, and **wait for 4 - 5 minutes**.
Add the reserved eggs back into the pan and stir-fry on medium heat for 15 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Edamame with salted plums is a sweet and sour home-style snack that is refreshing and tender with a natural fruity aroma from the plums. Edamame is rich in plant protein and fiber, helping to boost energy and promote digestion. The method is very simple and easy for beginners, taking only 35 to 45 minutes in total.
cac_buoc: Dissolve the salt in fresh water and soak the edamame for 15 minutes.
Pour in boiling water, add the edamame and salted plums, and cook for 20-30 minutes.
Remove from the pot and enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic home-style dish that is hot, sour, and incredibly crunchy. With its bright colors, it is a favorite quick stir-fry. Potatoes provide starch and potassium, while chilies are rich in Vitamin C to stimulate the appetite. The steps are clear and simple, making it very beginner-friendly with a total time of about 20 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 240g potatoes (shredded as thinly and long as possible)
cac_buoc: Peel the potatoes and cut into thin shreds (or use a mandoline/grater).
Rinse the potato shreds in fresh water to remove excess starch, then blanch them for 10 seconds. Drain and set aside.
Finely chop the green onion; crush and mince the garlic (divide into two equal portions and set aside); cut dried chilies into short segments; shred the green and red chilies.
Heat the pan over low heat with oil. Sauté half of the green onions (white parts), half of the minced garlic, and the dried chilies until fragrant.
Add the green and red chili shreds and toss briefly, then add the potato shreds and stir-fry until they change color (becoming slightly translucent).
Add 5ml light soy sauce, 10ml black vinegar, the remaining minced garlic, and 2g salt. Toss quickly to combine.
Before serving, sprinkle with the remaining green onions, toss well, and arrange on a plate.
You must rinse the potato shreds thoroughly to remove starch, otherwise they will stick together.
After adding the second half of the garlic and salt, serve quickly to preserve the garlic aroma and the potato's crunch.

mon_an.ten: Japanese Tofu and Enoki Mushroom Pot
mon_an.mo_ta: This Japanese tofu and enoki mushroom pot is a savory, umami-rich dish that goes perfectly with rice. The tofu is crispy on the outside and soft inside, while the enoki mushrooms are silky and flavorful. Enoki mushrooms are rich in amino acids and fiber, and Japanese egg tofu provides high-quality protein. This dish has simple steps that beginners can easily master in about 30 minutes.
cac_buoc: Slice the egg tofu into rounds. Pan-fry over low heat until both sides are golden, then remove and set aside.
Mince the garlic. Prepare the sauce by mixing light soy sauce, oyster sauce, dark soy sauce, sugar, and 100ml water; set aside.

Heat oil in a pan. When hot, sauté the chilies and minced garlic until fragrant. Add the enoki mushrooms first and sauté until soft. Layer the fried tofu evenly on top of the mushrooms. Pour in the sauce from step 2, simmer for 5 minutes, then turn to high heat to reduce the sauce.
The enoki mushrooms must be sautéed until soft first.
Try not to stir the tofu too much as it breaks easily.

mon_an.mo_ta: Golden Coin Eggs is a Hunan-style home dish that is crispy on the outside and tender on the inside. Savory and slightly spicy, the golden fried egg slices resemble ancient coins, symbolizing good luck. Combined with green and red chilies, it is rich in protein and vitamins. The difficulty is moderate, but with a little practice, beginners can finish this rice-pairing dish in about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Place eggs in a pot of cold water. Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and cook for 8 minutes.
Run under cold tap water to cool, then peel.
Mince the garlic (pieces no larger than 1 mm). Finely dice the long peppers and bird's eye chilies (approx. 2-3 mm).
Cut each hard-boiled egg crosswise into 4 even slices.
If using starch, coat each egg slice and shake off the excess.
Add 25 ml of oil to the pan (use 20 ml if not using starch) and add the egg slices.
Fry until the edges are slightly charred and golden, then add another 10 ml of oil and flip.
Once the second side is golden, add the long peppers, bird's eye chilies, and minced garlic. Fry for about one minute, then flip.
Add the doubanjiang and fry for a few dozen seconds, then flip.
Mix the light soy sauce, oyster sauce, and sugar to make a sauce. Gently toss the pan to coat, then serve.
The original recipe suggests 15 g of bird's eye chili; if you prefer less heat, reduce to 6 g or remove the seeds.
A non-stick pan is recommended. If using one, you can reduce the initial oil by 5 ml.
Ensure the eggs are fully set before peeling.
Do not stir too vigorously or the eggs will fall apart.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a rustic Northwest-style stew: tender yardlong beans, fluffy potatoes, and a rich tomato base that is savory and slightly tart. It is high in fiber, vitamins, and starch for a balanced meal. The method is extremely simple, the ingredient amounts are flexible, and it is nearly impossible to fail, making it very beginner-friendly. Ready in about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: Due to the nature of the ingredients, this recipe is portioned for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Finely chop the green onion, mince the garlic, and julienne the ginger; set aside.
String the yardlong beans and cut into 2-10cm segments; set aside.
Peel the potato and cut into 1cm³ cubes; set aside.
Peel the tomato and cut into 1cm³ pieces; set aside.
De-seed the peppers and cut into 0.15cm wide strips; set aside.
Heat 10ml - 15ml of oil in a pan. When the oil starts to smoke, add the onion, ginger, and garlic. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the yardlong beans and stir-fry until they change color (from bright green to jade green).
Add the potatoes and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Pour in hot water (just enough to cover the vegetables). Cover and simmer until the potatoes are *soft* (test with a chopstick).
Add the tomatoes, salt, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, five-spice powder, and peppers. Simmer until the tomatoes release their juices (stir occasionally to prevent sticking).
Add the chopped cilantro and serve.
After adding the tomatoes and continuing to simmer, stir occasionally to prevent the bottom from burning.

mon_an.ten: Smashed Green Peppers with Century Eggs
mon_an.mo_ta: Smashed green peppers with century eggs is a rustic home-style cold dish that looks simple but packs a punch. The smoky aroma of charred green peppers blends with the creamy richness of century eggs for a spicy, tangy appetizer perfect for summer. Century eggs provide protein and minerals, green peppers offer Vitamin C, and garlic boosts the appetite. The process is straightforward and easy for beginners, taking only 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green onion (approx. 10cm, preferably the green part)
cac_buoc: Wash the green peppers, remove the stems, slice open one side, and remove the seeds. Press them flat on the cutting board and set aside (you must remove the seeds to prevent them from popping in the pan).
Cut the green onion into 0.5cm segments; set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic; set aside.
Peel the century eggs; set aside.
Cut the bird's eye chilies into 5-10mm segments; set aside.
Heat the pan and add 10ml - 20ml of cooking oil.
Add all the green peppers. Reduce to low heat to maintain the pan's temperature and fry until the peppers are soft (test by piercing with a chopstick).
Turn off the heat. Place the century eggs and fried peppers into a small metal bowl.
Method 1: If you have a rolling pin and the noise won't disturb neighbors, use the end of the pin to smash the eggs and peppers in the bowl until well combined (optional).
Method 2: Use your hands to tear the peppers into 0.5cm strips and use a fork to mash the century eggs (optional).
Add the bird's eye chilies.
Add the light soy sauce, black vinegar, white sugar, sesame oil, and all other reserved ingredients.
Mix thoroughly and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried chives with eggs is a classic family dish. The chives are aromatic, and the eggs are soft and fresh. It is simple to make and highly nutritious. Chives are rich in vitamins and fiber, while eggs provide high-quality protein. This dish uses easily accessible ingredients and is especially suitable for beginners, taking only about 10 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 1 person.
Cooking oil = 10ml * x number of servings
cac_buoc: Wash the chives and drain well.
Cut the chives into small segments about 3cm long, referred to as `chive segments`.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk well; this is the `beaten eggs`.
Heat the pan and add cooking oil.
When the oil is hot, pour in the `beaten eggs` and stir-fry quickly until the eggs set into clumps. Remove and set aside; these are the `scrambled eggs`.
Add another 5ml of cooking oil to the pan, add the `chive segments`, and stir-fry quickly over high heat for 30 seconds.
Add the `scrambled eggs` back into the pan and toss well.
Add salt and toss well.
Turn off the heat and serve.
This dish emphasizes quick stir-frying over high heat; overcooking chives makes them lose their aroma and crisp-tender texture.
If you prefer softer chives, you can extend the stir-frying time slightly.

mon_an.ten: Stir-Fried Cucumber with Egg and Sausage
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a refreshing and quick Chinese-style home stir-fry with a savory and fresh taste. The cucumbers are crisp-tender, the eggs are soft, and the sausage adds a lovely aroma. Eggs provide high-quality protein, cucumbers are rich in vitamins and water, and the sausage enhances the flavor, making for a nutritionally balanced meal. The steps are simple and clear with very low difficulty, making it very beginner-friendly. The entire process takes only about 10 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Wash the cucumber and slice into half-moons; set aside.
Slice the sausage into half-moons; set aside.
Finely chop the red chili (optional); set aside.
Crack the eggs into a bowl and whisk well; this is the `beaten eggs`.
Pour 5ml of cooking oil into a hot pan.
When the oil is hot, reduce to low heat, pour in the `beaten eggs`, and use chopsticks to scramble until the eggs set and turn slightly golden. These are the `soft-cooked eggs`; remove and set aside.
**No need to wash the pan**; pour 5ml of cooking oil into the pan, add the cucumber slices, and **stir-fry over high heat for 1 minute**.
Add the `soft-cooked eggs` back to the pan, season with 2g salt and 3ml light soy sauce, then immediately add the sausage slices and chopped chili (optional) and toss well.
Turn off the heat and serve.
Since sausage is already salty, it should be added after seasoning so it doesn't absorb extra salt.

mon_an.mo_ta: Microwave steamed eggs is a simple and quick home dish that is silky and delicate, making it perfect for a late-night snack or a quick side. Eggs are rich in high-quality protein and vitamins, providing essential nutrients, while dried krill adds calcium. This dish is very beginner-friendly as it doesn't require heat control skills. The entire process, from whisking and seasoning to taking it out, takes only about 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 1 person.
10 dried krill * x number of servings (optional)
5g green onions * x number of servings (optional)
cac_buoc: Crack the eggs into a microwave-safe ceramic bowl and whisk until smooth.
Add water and salt, then stir well.
Add the dried krill to the bowl and stir to ensure they are distributed and not clumped together.
Finely chop the green onions (approx. 0.6±3mm) and stir them into the bowl.
Place the bowl in the microwave. Cover with plastic wrap or a microwave-safe ceramic lid (Note: do not seal tightly; leave a gap for air to escape) and cook for 2 minutes (500W).
Carefully remove the wrap or lid, then continue to cook for another 2 minutes.
If your microwave does not have a turntable, manually rotate the bowl 180 degrees halfway through to ensure even heating.
Add the sesame oil.
Carefully remove the bowl from the microwave (it will be very hot).
If using soy sauce, simply ensure it is drizzled thinly and evenly over the surface of the steamed eggs.
Enjoy your steamed eggs.
One egg is approximately 50±5g. If using different sized eggs, adjust the water ratio accordingly.
Ensure the eggs are thoroughly whisked, otherwise they may pop slightly during cooking.
The egg and water mixture should not exceed 2/3 of the bowl's capacity to prevent overflowing.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a silky home-style steamed egg dish made quickly using a steamer oven. The texture can be adjusted: less water makes it firmer, while more water makes it softer. It is rich in high-quality protein and nutrients, making it easy to digest. The difficulty is moderate; beginners can master it with a little attention. It takes only about 15 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 6ml light soy sauce / seasoned soy sauce (optional for seasoning)
cac_buoc: Crack an egg into a bowl and whisk well.

Add purified water at 60°C to the bowl at a volume of 1.0-1.5 times the volume of the egg, and stir well. Within the correct range, less water results in a firmer texture, while more water results in a softer texture. Note: outside this range, too little water feels overly tough, and too much water makes it too thin.
Add 1g of salt. Salt plays an important role in enhancing the base flavor and helping the egg set.
Add 5ml of cooking oil.
Strain the beaten egg mixture and remove any surface bubbles (optional, but if not strained, the steamed eggs will have air pockets and won't look as smooth).
Ensure the steamer oven has enough water (if unsure, fill the water tray).
Place the thoroughly stirred egg bowl into the steamer.
Set to **100°C** and steam for **10 minutes**.
Open the steamer (Note: steam will rush out immediately, so open it slowly).
Remove from the steamer (you can add light soy sauce for seasoning).
Enjoy.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a simple and quick home-style steamed dish that is silky like jelly and perfectly savory. It often appears on breakfast tables or as a side dish. Eggs provide high-quality protein and lecithin, which are easy to digest. It is very beginner-friendly; with just a few simple steps, you can steam a smooth egg custard in about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 8ml light soy sauce / seasoned soy sauce
cac_buoc: Crack two eggs into a bowl and whisk well.
Add 3g of salt. Salt is essential for the base flavor and for helping the custard set.

Add 2ml of white vinegar to remove the eggy smell (optional). Rice vinegar also works, but its color may darken the eggs. You can also use cooking wine, which removes the smell without the acidity of vinegar.
Add purified water at 70°C to the bowl at a volume of 1-1.5 times the volume of the eggs, and stir well. A 1:1 ratio makes the eggs firmer, while a 1:1.5 ratio makes them softer.
Strain the beaten egg mixture and remove any surface bubbles (optional, but if not strained, the surface will have air pockets).

Pour 300-500ml of water into any pot. Once the water boils, place the bowl of beaten eggs inside. The bowl must be covered with a lid, an inverted plate, or plastic wrap to prevent condensation from dripping in, which causes a 'honeycomb' texture.
Steaming steps (choose one of two):
Steam over **medium heat** for **10 minutes**, then turn off the heat and let it sit for **5 minutes**.

Steam over **high heat** for **5 minutes**, keeping the water boiling constantly. Every **2 minutes**, lift the lid to release steam; if the lid is opened too late, the eggs will develop air pockets; if opened too early or too often, the steaming time will need to be extended.
How to tell if it's done? Shake the bowl; if the eggs are no longer liquid and have a firm, jelly-like bounce, they are ready.
Remove from the pot.
Add sesame oil and light soy sauce before serving. You can also use rattan pepper oil instead of sesame oil for a refreshing numbing sensation.
This is a basic recipe; you can enhance it by adding sausage, minced meat, or dried krill to enrich the flavor.

mon_an.mo_ta: A simple and easy-to-make home-style therapeutic drink available in sweet or savory versions. It is silky and smooth, often used as a folk remedy to soothe the throat. Rich in high-quality protein and lecithin, it is easy to digest and can relieve throat dryness and irritation. The method is extremely simple—beginners can do it after seeing it once. It takes only about 5 minutes from boiling the water to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 1 person.
5 - 10 g white sugar (for the sweet version)
cac_buoc: Crack the egg into a bowl.
Using chopsticks or a whisk, beat the egg in one direction until the white and yolk are completely combined and the color is uniform (this takes about 1 - 2 minutes).
Add the sugar or salt to the egg and stir briefly to combine.
Prepare 100°C water that has just reached a rolling boil.
**While quickly stirring the egg in the bowl with chopsticks, pour the boiling water in a thin, steady stream**. Ensure the boiling water mixes thoroughly with the egg.
Continue stirring for a moment until the egg is completely cooked, forming uniform light-yellow egg ribbons.
To prevent potential Salmonella bacteria from raw eggs, it is highly recommended to use 100°C water that has just boiled to cook the egg instantly.

mon_an.mo_ta: Duck simmered with beer results in a rich sauce and tender, flavorful meat with a subtle hint of beer. It is a unique home-style dish. Duck meat is nutritious, rich in protein, B vitamins, and minerals, and becomes very flavorful when braised with beer. Although there are several steps, the process is not complicated; beginners can usually finish it in about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Duck meat (half a duck, 1 kg, chopped into small pieces by the butcher)
2 green chilies, 1 red chili (10cm to 15cm long) (cut into 2cm segments or slices)
4 cloves garlic, crushed and set aside
3cm fresh ginger, crushed and set aside
3 bird's eye chilies, cut in half (optional)
2 leeks, cut into segments and set aside
2 large green onions, 1 cut into segments, 1 kept whole
2 black cardamoms, crushed and seeds removed
cac_buoc: Blanch the duck to remove the gamey smell and impurities.
Rinse the duck meat once and place it in a pot.
Pour in enough water to cover the duck.
Add 20 ml cooking wine.
Add the whole green onion.
Add 2cm of crushed fresh ginger.
Turn on the heat and bring to a rolling boil.
Skim off the foam.
Remove the duck meat, rinse with clean water, and set aside.
Start cooking.
Wash and heat the pan, then add 60ml peanut oil.
When the oil reaches 60°C, add a pinch of Sichuan peppercorns (about 30 seeds).
Add the duck meat and stir-fry for 4 minutes; at the 2-minute mark, add all the dry spices; at the 3-minute mark, add all the aromatic base ingredients (ginger, garlic, bird's eye chilies).
Pour in 1000 ml of beer.

Braise the duck for 30 minutes; at the 10-minute mark, add salt (3g), light soy sauce (10ml), and dark soy sauce (5ml); at the 20-minute mark, add the green and red chili segments; at the 29-minute mark, add the leeks and green onion segments and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Serve.
While cooking, monitor the liquid level; if it falls below 2/3 of the ingredients, add more hot water or beer.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a savory and aromatic Hunan-style stir-fry that is a perfect 'rice-puller.' The richness of the pork belly, the softness of the eggs, and the fresh aroma of green peppers blend together for a complex flavor profile. Pork and eggs provide high-quality protein, while green peppers add Vitamin C for balanced nutrition. The difficulty is moderate; pay attention to the heat when stir-frying and the order of seasoning. Beginners can master this with a little practice. Preparation takes 7 minutes, cooking takes 10 minutes, for a total of about 17 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. This recipe serves 1-2 people.
cac_buoc: Preparation: Slice the pork, ideally separating the fat from the lean parts. Cut the green chilies and bird's eye chili into segments. Mince the garlic slices and julienne the ginger. Crack the eggs into a small bowl and whisk well.
Once prepared, start cooking. Add oil to the pan over low heat. When the oil is hot, pour in the eggs and scramble until just cooked. Return them to the small bowl and set aside.
Add a little more oil to the pan over low heat. When the pan is hot, add the fatty pork slices to render the fat.
When the fatty pork turns golden, increase to medium heat and add the lean pork slices to stir-fry together.
Once all the lean pork has changed color, add the julienned ginger, minced garlic, and Doubanjiang. Stir-fry until the meat is evenly colored.
Add the green and red chilies and the scrambled eggs, then add the soy sauce and sugar. Continue stir-frying until the green chilies are just cooked but still crisp.
Remove from the pan and serve!
If you used a lot of oil for the initial egg scrambling, you may not need to add more oil when stir-frying the pork.

mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed Chicken with Winter Melon is a refreshing dish: the winter melon slices at the bottom soak up the chicken juices, cordyceps flowers add a fresh flavor, and the chicken is tender and smooth. It is low in calories, high in protein, and simple to make. It takes about 35 minutes from preparation to serving, making it an ideal everyday family meal.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: 30g cordyceps flowers (washed and soaked until soft)
cac_buoc: Chop the chicken into pieces. Add julienned ginger, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, and cooking oil. Massage well and marinate for 20 minutes.
Line the bottom of a plate with the thinly sliced winter melon.
Layer the soaked cordyceps flowers over the winter melon.
Place the marinated chicken on top of the cordyceps flowers.
Bring water to a boil in a steamer. Once the steam rises, steam for 15 minutes, then remove and serve.
Thinly slicing the winter melon helps it cook faster and absorb more flavor from the chicken juices.
Placing the cordyceps flowers between the melon and the chicken allows their fresh flavor to permeate from top to bottom.

mon_an.ten: Steamed Winter Melon Stuffed with Meat
mon_an.mo_ta: Steamed Winter Melon Stuffed with Meat is a home-style dish that combines meat and vegetables. It is tender, fresh, and smooth, with the savory meat filling blending perfectly with the sweet, light winter melon. Minced pork provides high-quality protein and essential amino acids, while winter melon helps clear heat and provides hydration. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, requiring only a little practice with the rolling technique. It takes about 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is sufficient for 2 people.
1 egg (optional; some may find it slightly eggy)
25g starch slurry (25g starch mixed with 50ml water)
Minced ginger and scallion (3-4 slices ginger about 30g, plus the white part of the green onion above)
cac_buoc: Peel the winter melon and cut into slices 25cm long and 3cm thick.
Place the sliced winter melon in a bowl, add 15g of salt, rub evenly, and let sit for 10 minutes.
While the melon sits, in another bowl, combine the minced pork, minced ginger and scallion, 5g salt, 5g starch, ground pepper, and light soy sauce.
Use chopsticks to stir the pork mixture clockwise until the ingredients are thoroughly combined and the color is uniform (about 2 minutes).
Rinse the marinated winter melon (which will have softened) with clean water three times.
Take a slice of winter melon, roll it up, and stuff it with the meat filling.
Place the rolls on a plate, arranging them tightly around the edge.
Crack an egg into the center of the circle.
Place in a regular steamer. Once the water boils, cover and steam for 15 minutes.
Open the lid and remove the plate.
Pour the juices from the plate into a pan. Add the starch slurry and 50ml of clean water. Bring to a boil.
Drizzle the thickened sauce over the stuffed winter melon.
When removing the plate from the steamer, be very careful as it will be extremely hot.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic dish from the salt-mining chefs of Zigong, Sichuan: spicy, numbing, dry, and fragrant. The rabbit meat is firm and chewy, starting with a spicy kick followed by a fresh, long-lasting aftertaste. Rabbit meat is high in protein, low in fat, and rich in lecithin and amino acids, making it nutritious and easy to digest. The process involves handling various aromatic spices and strict heat control, which can be challenging for beginners. It takes about 1.5 hours from preparation to stir-frying, but the flavor improves significantly if left overnight, making it well worth the wait.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt = weight of rabbit in jin * 2g (1 jin = 500g)
MSG = weight of rabbit in jin * 1g
Oyster sauce = weight of rabbit in jin * 5g
Cooking wine = weight of rabbit in jin * 10g
Oil = weight of rabbit in jin * 0.9 ～ 1 liter
Garlic = weight of rabbit in jin * half a bulb
Total scallions/large leeks/onions = weight of rabbit in jin * 15g
Dried chilies = total volume of cut dried chilies equal to the volume of rabbit meat
Sichuan green peppercorns = 1 small bowl (full) per 1.5kg of rabbit meat
Star anise = weight of rabbit in jin * 1 piece
Cinnamon = weight of rabbit in jin * 1 thumb-sized piece
Bay leaves = weight of rabbit in jin * 5 leaves
Sand ginger (kaempferia galanga) = weight of rabbit in jin * 1 soybean-sized piece
White cardamom = weight of rabbit in jin * 2 seeds
Fennel seeds = weight of rabbit in jin * 15g
White sesame seeds = weight of rabbit in jin * 25g
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the intended amount of meat.
cac_buoc: Peel and mince the garlic and ginger and set aside; rinse the star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves, sand ginger, white cardamom, and fennel seeds and set aside.
Use scissors to cut the dried chilies into 2cm sections, rinse, and set aside.
Wash the scallions/leeks/onions; cut the onions into small pieces.
Chop the rabbit into 2cm pieces, season with salt, cooking wine, and MSG, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat oil in a wok; when the oil is 40% hot (medium-low), add the scallions/leeks/onions and stir-fry until fragrant. Once they turn slightly charred, remove and discard them.

Turn the heat to high to increase the oil temperature; when it reaches 80% hot, add the rabbit meat. Switch to medium-low heat during frying and cook until the rabbit is slightly golden and charred, then remove the meat.

Increase the oil temperature again, then add the dried chilies, green peppercorns, star anise, cinnamon, bay leaves, sand ginger, white cardamom, and fennel seeds; switch to low heat and fry until the chili sections are crispy.
Return the rabbit to the wok, add the oyster sauce, and stir-fry for a few minutes.
Turn off the heat, add the garlic, ginger, and white sesame seeds, and toss well.
Let it sit overnight for the flavors to fully penetrate.
Note for step 6: The oil must completely submerge the rabbit; add more oil if necessary.
Note for step 7: Chilies burn very easily and will turn black; this happens quickly, so you must use low heat. Generally, wait until the steam subsides before adding the rabbit back in.

mon_an.ten: Shredded Cold Chicken Salad (Liangban Ke Ti)
mon_an.mo_ta: A low-oil, low-calorie home-style cold dish. The shredded chicken is tender and flavorful, while the sesame oil and aromatic vinegar create a refreshing, slightly numbing, and tangy taste—perfect for cutting through the summer heat. Chicken breast is rich in high-quality protein and low in fat. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 30 minutes from start to finish.
cac_buoc: Slice the ginger and set aside.
Pour 4 liters of water into a pot.
Add the chicken breast and ginger slices.
Add 20ml of cooking wine.
Turn the heat to high and bring to a boil without a lid.
Once boiling, turn the heat to medium and skim off the foam with a spoon.
Continue to cook for **5-7** minutes; 5 minutes for fresh meat, 7 minutes for frozen meat.
The size of the chicken breast affects the cooking time; pierce the chicken with a chopstick—if it goes through easily, it is cooked. If not, extend the cooking time.
Rinse and soak the chicken in room-temperature boiled water until it cools down.
Shred the chicken into small strips along the grain.
Prepare a bowl.
Add the sesame oil, light soy sauce, aromatic vinegar, white sugar, and salt to the bowl.
Stir the sauce until the sugar and salt are mostly dissolved.
Pour the sauce over the shredded chicken and toss well.
This dish was made during quarantine with available ingredients; if possible, add cilantro or scallions for extra flavor. Chili oil can be added for those who like it spicy.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic Chinese braised dish with tender, flavorful meat and a rich aroma. The braising liquid (master brine) can be reused and becomes more fragrant over time. It is perfect as a cold appetizer, a snack with drinks, or a side dish. Rich in quality protein and vitamins with balanced nutrition. It requires some patience, but the steps are clear and beginner-friendly. Soaking to remove blood, making caramel color, and pressure cooking takes about 1 hour, followed by an overnight soak to fully develop the flavor. Slice and serve the next day.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 2-3 people.
Water as needed (must cover all the meat)
cac_buoc: It is recommended to review the instructions for making caramel color first.
Soak the beef shank in cold water for at least 3 hours to remove the blood.
Prepare the braising liquid.
Make the caramel color: add 30g of white sugar to a pan, heat over low heat until melted and brown, then add 150ml of hot water and stir well. Set aside.
Cut the onion into pieces, crush the ginger and garlic, and break the dried chilies in half. Set aside.
Fill a pot with enough water, add the spice pouch, onion, ginger, garlic, and dried chilies, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add 15ml each of soybean paste, doubanjiang, oyster sauce, and red fermented bean curd, then stir well.
Pour in the prepared caramel color and mix well.
Add 120ml of light soy sauce and 60ml of dark soy sauce, then stir well.
Add 10-15g of salt to season.
Pour in 1 can of beer (330ml) and bring back to a boil.
Braise the beef.
Blanch the beef shank in a separate pot for 2-3 minutes, remove, and rinse off the scum with hot water.
Place the blanched beef into the boiling braising liquid, ensuring the liquid covers all the meat.
Close the pressure cooker lid; once it reaches pressure, cook for 25-30 minutes.
After cooking, do not open the lid; keep it warm and let it cool naturally, soaking overnight for better flavor.
Remove the braised meat and place it in the refrigerator to firm up.
Slice before serving; can be eaten directly or used in a cold salad.
Storing the braising liquid.

To reuse: after each use, strain the liquid to remove all solids, bring to a boil to sterilize, let cool, and store in the fridge or freezer. When using again, replenish spices according to the original ratio. (Adjust water based on the remaining liquid.)
If stored correctly, the master brine can last a long time and improves with age.
**Important Note**: if braising vegetarian items, set aside a portion of the liquid to use separately; liquid used for vegetarian items should not be reused.
Cold salad dressing.

Mix minced garlic, chopped scallions, white sesame seeds, and chili powder in a 1:1:1:1 ratio. Add fresh bird's eye chilies to taste. Heat vegetable oil with a bit of sesame oil or prickly ash oil and pour it over the spices in stages. Add 10ml each of light soy sauce, vinegar, and oyster sauce, 5ml of sugar, and a pinch of MSG/chicken powder. Finally, add 15ml of the braising liquid and mix well.
When making a cold salad, you can add sides like smashed cucumbers, wood ear mushrooms, fried peanuts, or cilantro.
You can also set aside some braising liquid to make beef noodles; use it as a broth for blanched noodles and add your favorite vegetables.

mon_an.mo_ta: Mouth-Watering Chicken is a classic Sichuan cold dish: chilled, tender chicken coated in bright red chili oil, offering a spicy, numbing, fresh, and fragrant taste that is perfect as a summer appetizer. The chicken provides high-quality protein, while the crushed peanuts and aromatics add energy and depth. The difficulty is medium; pay attention to the heat when boiling the chicken and seasoning the chili oil. Suitable for those with some cooking experience. Total time is approximately 1.5 hours including boiling, cooling, and saucing.
cac_buoc: Slice the ginger; set aside 1 scallion stalk and 15 Sichuan peppercorns.
Wash the chicken, place it in a pot, cover with water, add the ginger slices, scallion, and peppercorns, and bring to a boil over high heat.
Once boiling, reduce to medium-low heat for 20 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Remove the chicken and place it in ice water until completely cold.
Remove the chicken, chop into pieces, and arrange on a plate. Set aside.
Heat a pan over low heat and toast the peanuts until the skins crack. (Stir constantly to prevent burning.)
Cut the remaining scallion into sections, mince the garlic, and peel and crush the toasted peanuts. Set aside 15 peppercorns.
Heat oil in a pan, add the scallion sections, peppercorns, and half of the minced garlic. Stir-fry until fragrant.
When the oil is 80% hot, turn off the heat and strain the hot oil.
Pour the hot oil into a bowl with the chili powder, stir, and strain to get clear red chili oil.
Add the remaining minced garlic, light soy sauce, vinegar, salt, MSG, sugar, sesame oil, and Sichuan pepper powder to the chili oil. Mix well and let cool.
Sprinkle the crushed peanuts over the chicken, pour the chili oil sauce over the top, and garnish with cilantro. Serve.
A second method for Mouth-Watering Chicken will be updated later.

mon_an.mo_ta: Coca-Cola chicken wings feature a glossy red glaze and tender meat with a perfect sweet and savory balance. It is a popular creative dish for family meals. The wings provide quality protein and fat, and cooking them in cola makes the meat exceptionally tender. The process requires mastering the heat during frying and sauce reduction, which is slightly challenging for beginners but achievable by following the steps. Total time is about 40 minutes.
cac_buoc: Place the wings in a pot and cover with cold water. Add 1 slice of ginger and 10-20ml of cooking wine. Bring to a boil over high heat (about 2 minutes), skim off the foam, and drain. This step is for frozen wings; if using fresh wings, simply score them and marinate directly with light soy sauce.
Remove the wings and score them twice on each side with a knife. Marinate with about 10g of light soy sauce for 10 minutes (ensure the surface is well-coated).

Place a pan over low heat with a little oil, sauté the remaining ginger slices first, then add the marinated wings. Fry until golden, then flip (until both sides are golden). Use a spatula to toss the wings and ginger 4-5 times to prevent sticking.
Once the wings are golden, pour in the cola until covered. Bring to a boil over high heat and skim off any dark foam (blood residue). Add the scallion knot.
Seasoning: add 2g of salt, 10g of white sugar, and 3g of light soy sauce (you can use 3g of dark soy sauce instead for a deeper color).
When the scallion knot turns yellow, remove it along with the ginger slices. Switch to medium heat and continue to simmer the wings.
When the cola becomes syrupy and forms threads, lower the heat so the sauce coats the wings tightly. Remove from heat and plate.
Sautéing the ginger first helps prevent the wings from sticking to the pan.
Do not use high heat during the final reduction to avoid a bitter taste.
This dish is primarily sweet in flavor.

mon_an.ten: Taiwanese Braised Pork Rice (Lu Rou Fan)
mon_an.mo_ta: Taiwanese Braised Pork Rice is a fragrant staple of Taiwanese home cooking. The hand-cut pork strips are tender and flavorful, coated in an amber-colored glossy sauce that is incredibly rich when drizzled over hot rice. It is high in quality protein, collagen, and carbohydrates for a quick energy boost. The method is very beginner-friendly; once the ingredients are prepared and the heat is managed, the process takes about 1.5 hours, with only 30 minutes of active cooking and the rest left to a slow simmer.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. The following is for 2-3 people.
cac_buoc: Cut the pork belly (with skin) into thin strips: 0.7cm (length) x 0.7cm (width) x 2.5cm (height).
Mince the shallots and garlic and set aside.
Hard-boil the eggs, peel them, and lightly score the whites (to help absorb flavor). Set aside.
Heat a wok over **high heat**, add 15ml of oil, and swirl to coat the bottom. The oil prevents the pork from sticking initially. Wait 5 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Add the pork strips and stir-fry until the meat turns slightly white, then drizzle 10ml of rice wine around the edge of the wok. Continue stir-frying until the pork begins to render its fat.
Add the minced shallots and stir-fry for 1 minute until the aroma of fried shallots is released.
Add the minced garlic and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Push the pork to one side, add the rock sugar and cook until melted and bubbling into a caramel, then toss the pork to coat evenly.
Add the light soy sauce and stir-fry until fragrant.

Drizzle in 25ml of rice wine, add water to cover the pork, then add the white pepper, five-spice powder, star anise, bay leaves, and boiled eggs. Once boiling, reduce to low heat and braise for 1 hour. Note: soy sauce saltiness varies; taste during braising—if too sweet, add soy sauce; if too salty, add a little sugar or water. Stir every 15 minutes to prevent sticking. If it looks too dry, add 100ml of water.
After 1 hour, turn the heat to high and reduce the sauce until thickened and glossy with an amber color.
Once finished, scoop a bowl of rice, drizzle the tender braised pork over it, add a braised egg, and enjoy.

Regarding cutting the pork belly: place the pork skin-side up. The skin surface is the length and width, and the vertical direction is the height. The goal is to have thin strips with alternating layers of fat and lean meat. (Note: strips must be thin to braise into a melt-in-the-mouth texture.)
Tips for cutting pork belly:
If the pork is **fresh**, place it in the **freezer for 30 minutes** before cutting.
If the pork is **frozen**, let it sit at **room temperature for 30 minutes** before cutting.
Use quick, light strokes to slice through the meat easily while preserving the layered structure.

mon_an.ten: Cantonese Sweet and Sour Pork (Gu Lu Rou)
mon_an.mo_ta: Gu Lu Rou is a classic Cantonese home-style dish: sweet, sour, and appetizing with a crispy exterior and tender interior. The fruity sweetness of the pineapple makes the meat refreshing and less greasy. Pork provides quality protein, while bell peppers and pineapple add vitamins and fiber. The challenge lies in controlling the heat while frying the meat, which can be tricky for beginners, but following the steps ensures success. From marinating to serving, the process takes about 40 minutes—a perfect, flavorful meal for the family.
cac_buoc: Wash the pork shoulder (100g), pat dry with paper towels, and cut into pieces slightly smaller than the desired final size.
Marinate the pork with salt (1/2 tsp) for 20 minutes.
Chop the green bell pepper (25g).
Cut the pineapple slices (75g) into bite-sized pieces.

In a bowl, combine the ketchup (4 tbsp), white vinegar (2 tsp), minced garlic (1 tbsp), light soy sauce (1/2 tsp), cornstarch (2 1/2 tsp), sugar (2 tbsp), salt (1/4 tsp), and water (200ml). Mix well to make the sauce.
Dredge the pork pieces in cornstarch (6 tbsp).
Heat oil (500ml) in a pan over medium heat.
Add the pork pieces and fry over medium heat for 5 minutes, then remove.
Return the pork to the pan and double-fry over high heat for 1 minute.
In a clean pan, add 1 tsp of oil and the sauce mixture; simmer over medium heat for 3 minutes.
Add the bell pepper and pineapple, and cook over high heat for 2 minutes.
Toss the fried pork pieces with the sauce until evenly coated. Serve.
For a more layered texture, you can add an egg to the cornstarch coating for extra crispness and aroma.

mon_an.mo_ta: Curry Beef Slices is a rich and satisfying home-style dish. The spicy aroma of curry blends with the savory fat of the beef slices, combined with potatoes, carrots, and other vegetables for a soft, hearty texture. It is rich in protein, vitamins, and calcium, providing a balanced meat-and-vegetable meal. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, usually taking only 40 minutes to serve—perfect for meal prepping.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 2 people.
Fatty beef slices 300g (add more if preferred)
cac_buoc: Slice the onion; cut the carrot and potato into chunks. Set aside.
Bring a pot of water to a boil, add the beef slices, skim off the scum, then drain and set aside.
Heat a pan, add 10ml - 15ml of oil, and **wait 10 seconds for the oil to heat up**.
Add the onion and stir-fry until soft and translucent.
Add the potatoes and carrots and **stir-fry for 2 minutes**.
Add cold water until the ingredients are just submerged.
Add the bay leaf and curry cubes, cover with a lid, and **once boiling, lower the heat and simmer until the potatoes and carrots are tender (test with a chopstick)**.
Add the beef slices and milk, cover, and simmer for another 2-3 minutes. Serve. (Stir gently to avoid breaking the beef slices.)
The curry cubes do not need to be crushed; just add them whole.
Stir occasionally during cooking to ensure the seasoning is evenly distributed.

mon_an.mo_ta: Shangzhou Braised Pork is a traditional dish from Shang County, Shaanxi. It features a reddish-pink color and a soft texture that is rich but not greasy, carrying the unique fresh aroma of Shangzhou dried ferns. The pork provides quality protein and fat, while the ferns add fiber and micronutrients. This dish involves a complex process requiring both knife skills and heat control, making it suitable for experienced cooks. The entire process takes about 2.5 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Per serving: amount for two people
cac_buoc: Scrape and wash the pork, boil until 60% cooked (turns white), remove, and while still hot, brush the skin with honey and vinegar.

Heat the lard in a wok over high heat until 80% hot (approx. 200°C, heavy blue smoke, oil surface is still). Place the pork in skin-side down and fry until golden red. Remove and soak in the cooled pork boiling liquid until softened. Place on a cutting board and slice into pieces 10cm long and 0.6cm thick, keeping the skin side down. Arrange neatly in a steaming bowl.
Cut 5g of large scallion into 2.4cm sections and the other 5g into 2.4cm diagonal slices. Peel and wash the ginger; slice 1.5g and mince 5g. Cut the egg crepe into 2.4cm isosceles triangles.

Boil the dried ferns until soft, remove old stems and impurities, wash, and cut into 3cm sections. Place in a bowl, add 5ml soy sauce, 1g salt, and 10ml lard; mix well and spread over the pork slices. In a small bowl, mix 100ml chicken broth, 5ml soy sauce, 0.5g salt, and 15ml cooking wine; pour into the steaming bowl. Add the ginger slices, scallion sections, and star anise. Steam over high heat for 30 minutes, then reduce to low heat and steam for another 1.5 hours. Once tender, remove and discard the ginger, scallion, and star anise. Strain and reserve the steaming liquid, then invert the pork onto a deep serving plate.

In a wok, combine 100ml chicken broth with the reserved steaming liquid and bring to a boil over high heat. Add the minced ginger, sliced scallions, and MSG; stir well. Add the egg crepe triangles, drizzle with sesame oil, and pour the sauce over the pork. Serve.
Shangzhou ferns are a local specialty; if unavailable, they can be replaced with other types of dried edible ferns.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a home-style dish with a unique flavor: the duck meat is fragrant, fresh, and tender, with a subtle hint of beer. It is warming without being overpowering and aromatic without being greasy. Duck is rich in protein, and the beer helps remove gaminess while enhancing the aroma, making the dish even more savory. The method is beginner-friendly, taking about 1 hour from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Chop the duck into 3cm pieces. Place in a pot of cold water with ginger slices and cooking wine. Blanch, then remove and drain. Set aside.
Heat a wok, add about 100ml of oil, and wait for it to shimmer over high heat. Add the duck and stir-fry until it changes color.
When the duck has completely changed color (turning white), push it to one side of the wok. Add the doubanjiang and rock sugar; stir-fry over low heat until fragrant and the sugar has caramelized.
Add the cloves, star anise, bay leaves, dried chilies, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, and garlic. Stir-fry until the aromatics are released.
Pour in the beer until the duck is submerged. Add salt and chicken powder, then simmer over medium heat for 30 minutes (cook for an extra 5 minutes if you prefer it softer).
Remove from heat and arrange on a plate. Serve and enjoy.
Ensure there is enough beer to completely cover the duck; a light, crisp beer works best.

mon_an.mo_ta: Hui Guo Rou is a famous traditional Sichuan dish. The main ingredient is pork leg meat or pork belly. The finished product has a glossy red color, with the fatty parts slightly curled and translucent, while the lean parts are fragrant and tender without being dry. It tastes rich but not greasy, savory, fresh, and slightly spicy, with a combined aroma of leeks and doubanjiang (fermented bean paste). Pork is rich in high-quality protein and essential fatty acids; combined with red and green peppers and leeks, it provides essential vitamins. This dish involves several steps, including boiling, slicing, and stir-frying, requiring some control over the heat and knife skills. However, by following the process, even beginners can succeed. The entire process takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Pork belly: 0.5 kg for men / 0.3 kg for women (authentic Hui Guo Rou uses 'secondary hind leg' meat, which is firm with a good fat-to-lean ratio)
Red and green chilies (choose according to spice tolerance, 0-30g) *Note: thick-fleshed bell peppers are not recommended
cac_buoc: Phase 1: Processing the pork belly

Heat the pan and press the pork belly skin-side down firmly against the pan to sear the skin. This step treats the pores on the pigskin (or ask the butcher to singe the skin when buying; if you don't mind the pores, you can skip this).
Use a steel wool scrubber to scrub the skin clean until the blackened carbonized parts are completely removed; otherwise, it will taste bitter.
Place the pork belly in a pot, pour in cold water just to cover, add ginger slices, cooking wine, and scallions (tie the 2 stalks into a knot).
Turn on high heat. When the water boils, skim off the foam and continue cooking for 15 minutes, until the lean part can be easily pierced with a chopstick.
Processing side ingredients
Slice the red and green chilies into rounds.
Cut the leeks into sections.
Thinly slice the ginger into small pieces.
Pre-mix 5ml of doubanjiang and 5ml of light soy sauce.
Phase 2: Processing the pork belly
Remove the cooked pork belly and place it in cold water to cool down.
Wipe the water off the pork, then cut into 2mm thin slices with the fat on top and lean on the bottom (slicing too thick makes it less tasty and very greasy).
Start stir-frying (Note: this step **requires fast handling, be careful not to burn the pan**)
Heat the pan and add a thin layer of oil to coat it.
Add the pork belly and stir-fry until the fat becomes translucent and the slices curl slightly (called "lamp bowl shape"); hind leg meat gives the best effect.
Pour in the doubanjiang-soy sauce mixture and 5g of MSG, then toss for 15 seconds.
Add the chili rounds and ginger slices, then add the remaining 5ml of doubanjiang and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the leeks and stir-fry for 60 seconds.
Serve.
Simplified Version
Choose frozen pork belly left at room temperature for 0.5 hours or fresh pork belly chilled in the fridge for 1 hour, then cut into 2-5mm thin slices.
Turn on medium heat, add the chilies to the pan and dry-fry for 30-45 seconds, then remove.
Heat the pan, add a thin layer of oil to coat it, and stir-fry the ginger slices for 15 seconds.
Add the pork belly, tossing every 10 seconds until the pork turns golden brown (the longer you fry, the firmer the pork becomes).
Add the previously dry-fried chilies, 10ml of doubanjiang, and light soy sauce to season, then continue stir-frying for 60 seconds.
Add the leek sections and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Serve.
If you don't like leeks, you can swap them for onions or other vegetables, but pay attention to the cooking time; vegetables should be stir-fried beforehand or they may stay half-raw.
If the pork pieces are large, they can be cut into 5cm squares; cook the pork belly until a chopstick can pierce the skin with slight pressure.
Soaking the pork in cold water after boiling makes the meat firmer.
Wiping the pork dry is essential to prevent oil splattering and burns during stir-frying.
Remember not to cut the pork too thick, or it will be very greasy.

mon_an.mo_ta: The ribs are fall-off-the-bone tender, and the potatoes are soft, fluffy, and infused with flavor. The sauce is rich, slightly sweet, and mildly spicy—a classic Northern Chinese home-style braised dish. It is rich in protein, calcium, and starch for balanced nutrition. It is slightly difficult, requiring mastery of the sugar-coloring technique and heat control, but the steps are clear so beginners can try. The whole process takes about 1.5 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: The parameters below are the exact configuration for a standard serving of 2-3 people.
Ginger = 30g (divided into two parts: 15g for blanching, 15g for stir-frying)
Scallions = 25g (divided into two parts: 15g tied in a knot, 10g finely chopped)
Cooking wine = 25ml (divided into two parts: 15ml for blanching, 10ml for stir-frying)
Salt = 3g (used for seasoning during the final reduction)
cac_buoc: Initial prep: cutting ingredients and preventing oxidation

**Process the potatoes:** Peel 300g of potatoes and cut into irregular chunks. **Immediately soak them in a bowl of clean water** after cutting to isolate them from oxygen and prevent the surface from turning black; set aside.
**Process the aromatics:** Thinly slice all 30g of ginger (divide into two 15g portions). Process 25g of scallions: tie 15g into a knot and finely chop the remaining 10g; set aside.
Initial prep: spice packaging and parallel tasks

**Prepare the sauce bowl (one-time use):** Take a small bowl, add 10ml light soy sauce, 5ml dark soy sauce, 5ml oyster sauce, and 5ml soybean paste. Mix well and place within reach of the stove; set aside.

**Prepare the aromatic spice plate (one-time use):** Take a small plate, add 5g dried chilies, 1g star anise (1-2 petals), 1g Sichuan peppercorns (about 10 grains), 1g cinnamon (one small piece), and the 15g of sliced ginger; set aside.
**Start the parallel water boiling process:** Turn on the electric kettle to boil 700ml of water. (Ensure the boiling water is ready exactly when the stir-frying is done).
Preliminary processing: blanching the ribs and draining

**Cold water blanch:** Place 750g of spare ribs in a pot of cold water, add the scallion knot, 15g ginger slices, and 15ml cooking wine. Bring to a boil over high heat, then keep boiling for 2 minutes to force out the blood foam.
**Hot rinse, avoid cold:** Remove the ribs and **must use hot water** to rinse off any remaining foam on the surface (cold water will cause the meat to contract sharply and become tough).

**Absolute draining (preventing oil splatter):** The cleaned ribs **must be thoroughly patted dry with paper towels**. Place them on a plate next to the wok; set aside (this prevents violent splattering when adding them to the high-temperature sugar base).
Main stir-fry: caramelizing and aromatics (intensive phase)
**Caramelize the sugar:** Heat the pan with 20ml of oil. Add 10g of white sugar and stir constantly over medium-low heat. Cook until the sugar melts, bubbles, and turns a reddish-brown caramel color.
**Sear for color:** Quickly add the 750g of thoroughly dried ribs and switch to medium-high heat. Fry for 2-3 minutes until both sides of the ribs are slightly golden and evenly coated in caramel.

**First aromatics:** Push the ribs to the side to create a small space in the pan, then **pour in the 【aromatic spice plate】**. Use the hot oil at the bottom to fry for about 10 seconds to release the oil-soluble fragrance of the spices.

**First seasoning:** Drizzle the remaining 10ml of cooking wine along the edge of the hot pan to create a 'wok hei' aroma. Immediately **pour in the 【sauce bowl】**, stir-fry for about 30 seconds until the sauce completely coats the ribs and releases a rich savory aroma.
Braising and reduction: coating and serving

**Add water for long braising:** By now the kettle has boiled; pour in 700ml of boiling water (the water must cover the ribs) and bring to a boil over high heat. Then cover, turn to low heat, and simmer continuously for 40 minutes.

**Add potatoes:** After 40 minutes, open the lid, drain the 300g of soaked potatoes, and add them to the pan. Cover again and continue simmering over low heat for 15-20 minutes, until a chopstick can easily pierce the potatoes.

**Season and reduce:** Open the lid and add 3g of salt (taste the sauce now and adjust slightly to your preference). Switch to high heat and start stirring to reduce the sauce, which takes about 3-5 minutes. Stop when the sauce is thick and clings evenly to the ribs and potatoes.
**Garnish and serve:** Transfer to a plate and sprinkle the 10g of prepared chopped scallions evenly over the top to garnish.

mon_an.ten: New Orleans Style Roasted Chicken Drumsticks
mon_an.mo_ta: New Orleans style roasted chicken drumsticks are simple and easy to make, rich in protein and iron. It takes about 3 hours in total, with about 20 minutes of active prep time.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One portion is enough for 1 person.
Chicken drumsticks (large leg quarters) 2 pieces (each weighing about 200g, total about 400g)
New Orleans style chicken wing seasoning 15 - 20 g
cac_buoc: Thaw the chicken drumsticks and wash them clean.
Score the drumsticks: on the thickest part of each drumstick, use a small knife to make 4-6 deep parallel cuts; the deeper the cuts, the better the flavor penetration.
Take a pot, **add 15 - 20 g New Orleans chicken wing seasoning powder, 5 g salt, and ≥30 mL water**.
Add the scored chicken drumsticks to the pot and mix well.
Place the pot in the refrigerator to **marinate for 2 - 4 hours**; the longer the time, the deeper the flavor.
Line a baking tray with aluminum foil, remove the chicken, and place them skin-side down (do not tear the foil). **Discard the remaining liquid in the pot.**
Place in the upper-middle rack of the oven and roast with the following settings: _**Top 230 ℃, Bottom 230 ℃, top and bottom heat, timer for 20 minutes**_
Remove from the oven and pour the rendered fat from the tray into a large bowl; set aside. (Do not tear the foil)
Flip all the chicken drumsticks over.
Place in the upper rack of the oven and roast with the following settings: _**Top 150 ℃, Bottom 230 ℃, top and bottom heat, timer for 20 minutes**_
Remove from the oven and pour the rendered fat from the tray into the large bowl; set aside. (Do not tear the foil)
Place in the upper rack of the oven and roast with the following settings: _**Top 60 ℃, Bottom 60 ℃, top and bottom heat, timer for 15-20 minutes**_
Remove from the oven and pour the rendered fat from the tray into the large bowl; set aside. (Do not tear the foil)
Take a small bowl and **mix the fat from the large bowl with soy sauce at a volume ratio of 10:1 to 2:1**. The more soy sauce, the saltier it will be; adjust to your personal taste.

Hold the base of the drumstick and dip it into the liquid in the small bowl; you can use paper towels or gloves to stay clean. You can now enjoy the New Orleans roasted chicken directly from the foil on the tray. If the liquid in the small bowl runs out, repeat the previous step.
You can take the chicken out to mix it once or twice during the marinating process. Do not marinate for an excessively long time.
This guide is based on an oven with a **25 L capacity and 1400 W power**.
If your oven power is lower or higher than this, you can appropriately extend or shorten the timer, but ensure the chicken is fully cooked.

mon_an.mo_ta: Bacon Mac and Cheese is a classic American comfort dish. It is rich, creamy, and smooth, with cheese coating the chewy macaroni, combined with fragrant, salty, and satisfying crispy bacon. It is rich in protein and calcium, but quite high in calories and fat, so it is recommended as an occasional treat. It requires some patience; mastering the basic white sauce and heat control can be a bit challenging for beginners. Overall difficulty is medium. If not baking, it takes about 30 minutes to serve; if baking, extra time is needed for preheating and roasting, totaling about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2 people.
Cheese 40-55g, plus an extra 25g if baking, shredded
cac_buoc: Grate the cheese into small shreds.
Slice the onion.
Boil the macaroni in slightly salted water for 6 minutes.
**Medium heat**
Add butter to the pan and wait for it to melt.
Add the onion.
When the onion softens, add the garlic.
When the garlic is fragrant, add the meat and wait for 5 seconds.
**Low heat**
Add the milk in four additions, stirring for 5 seconds after each addition before adding the next.
Add the flour and stir very thoroughly.
Add the cheese and stir until well combined.
Mix the macaroni with the cheese sauce.
If you do not plan to bake it, you can eat it immediately.
**Baking:**
Preheat the oven to 180°C.
Sprinkle an additional 50g of cheese over the macaroni.
Once the oven reaches 180°C, put the macaroni in.
Bake until the surface is golden brown, about 24 minutes.
This dish is quite indulgent, containing about 1300 kcal and 80g of fat; it is not recommended for frequent consumption.

mon_an.mo_ta: Ginger Chicken is a savory Hunan dish that goes perfectly with rice. The chicken is dry-fried until fragrant and infused with flavor, featuring a bold ginger aroma that is spicy but not overwhelming. Chicken provides high-quality protein, while fresh ginger helps dispel cold and stimulates the appetite. The method is simple and easy for beginners to master. From marinating to serving takes about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Chicken = half a bird (preferably free-range, approx. 650g)
Cooking oil = 50ml (preferably tea seed oil, otherwise use rapeseed oil)
Thai chilies = 0-5 pieces (0-50g) (adjust to spice level)
Beauty peppers (Meirenjiao) = 0-5 pieces (0-50g) (can substitute with Thai chilies)
cac_buoc: Chop the chicken into small 1cm pieces as much as possible, wash and drain, then marinate with light soy sauce and cooking wine for 30 minutes.
First, heat a large wok until it starts to smoke slightly, add the oil, and wait 5 seconds.
Add the ginger slices and switch to medium heat, stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 minutes until the water evaporates and the chicken fat is rendered.
Add the chopped chilies and garlic cloves, then add salt and dark soy sauce; continue stir-frying for 30 seconds.
Pour in the beer, cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 2 minutes.
Turn to high heat to reduce the sauce, then transfer to a plate and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Ginger Scallion Chicken is a classic Cantonese home-style dish: the chicken is tender and juicy, with a bold ginger and scallion aroma, perfectly savory and fresh—a real rice-killer. Chicken drumsticks provide high-quality protein, while ginger and scallions help warm the stomach and stimulate the appetite. The process mainly involves steaming and hand-shredding; the steps are clear and quite easy for beginners. From prep to finish takes about 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One portion is enough for 2 people.
Salt-baked chicken powder (diem cuc ke phan) 5g
cac_buoc: Wash the four chicken drumsticks and place them in a bowl.
Add the salt-baked chicken powder and 5ml of oil to the bowl, then mix well.
Let the chicken marinate for 15 minutes; meanwhile, prepare the steamer and bring the water to a boil.
After marinating, place the chicken in the steamer once the water is boiling and steam for 20 minutes.
Depending on preference, cut the ginger into 1) minced ginger, 2) ginger matchsticks, or 3) finely diced ginger.
Cut the scallion into small 0.5cm sections.
Place the ginger and scallion into a dipping bowl, then add salt and sugar.
Pour the remaining oil into a separate pan and heat until it is about 60-70% hot.
Drizzle the hot oil over the ginger and scallion bowl.
Once the chicken is steamed, shred it into strips; no need to shred too finely, about 1cm wide is fine.
Drizzle the ginger-scallion oil over the shredded chicken, mix well, and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Cumin Beef is a spicy, fragrant, and tender home-style stir-fry: the bold cumin aroma blends perfectly with the silky texture of the beef and the crunch of green peppers. Beef is rich in high-quality protein and easily absorbed iron; combined with green peppers for extra vitamins, it is nutritionally balanced. It requires some knife skills and heat control, making it suitable for those with some cooking experience. Including marinating and prep, the whole process takes about 45 minutes to get on the table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Green pepper amount: 2 pieces per person, 100g each
Thai chili amount: 3 pieces per person, 5g each
Light soy sauce amount: 20ml per person
Scallion amount: 1 stalk per person, 20g each
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the above conditions and adjust to taste.
cac_buoc: First, finely chop the Thai chilies and grind the cumin seeds in a mortar until they are coarse grains; this helps the flavor penetrate better. If short on time, you can skip the grinding.
Remove the stems and seeds from the green peppers (keep seeds if you like it spicy), then slice into strips. Cut the scallions into sections.
Thaw the beef beforehand, rinse with water, drain or pat dry with paper towels, then slice the beef against the grain.
Marinate the beef: add light soy sauce, starch, and oil; mix well and let sit for 30 minutes. You can also refer to a marinating guide for techniques.
Heat the pan with oil, add the scallions to sauté until fragrant, then add the marinated beef and stir-fry.
When the beef changes color, sprinkle the cumin and chili mixture evenly and stir-fry until cooked.
Add the green pepper strips; when they are just cooked through, add the salt.
Stir-fry on high heat 🔥 for 1 minute, then turn off the heat and toss for another 30 seconds to ensure even heating before serving.

mon_an.mo_ta: This famous Sichuan dish is characterized by its 'lychee' flavor (sweet and sour with a hint of scorched chili), featuring a mild tang and sweetness mixed with the aroma of dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns. The diced chicken is tender and smooth, while the peanuts are crunchy and fragrant, creating rich layers of flavor. It is rich in high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids, making it a perfect appetizer. The recipe is divided into simple and advanced versions, making it beginner-friendly; just plan ahead for the marinating time. From prep to serving takes about 1.5 hours.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: This dish defaults to a single-person portion, but is enough for two; theoretically, for more people, just multiply the ingredients.
Dried chilies (or Erjingtiao chilies) = 10g (if using Erjingtiao, about 4 pieces)
Chili oil (hot oil poured over flakes) = 5g
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the above conditions and adjust to taste.
cac_buoc: Simplified Version

Use scissors to debone the chicken drumstick, flatten the meat with the back of a knife, cut into strips, then into 1.5cm cubes. Soak in clean water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside (if using chicken breast, dice directly and follow the next steps).

Place the green leaves of the scallion and 5g of ginger slices in a bowl, pour in 50g of boiling water and set aside; cut the white part of the scallion into 1.5cm rounds and set aside; microwave the peanuts on high for 5 minutes to dry them out and set aside.

Add 2g salt, 5g dark soy sauce, 15g cooking wine, and 15g starch to the diced chicken and stir until slightly dry; gradually add some of the scallion-ginger water, stirring until the chicken becomes sticky; cover with plastic wrap and marinate in the fridge for 1 hour.

Cut the dried chilies into sections; heat a pan on high, then turn to low; add the dried chilies and toast until slightly scorched, then remove and set aside; toast the Sichuan peppercorns until fragrant, then remove and set aside.

Switch to high heat, add 20g vegetable oil; when it reaches 70% heat (bubbles form around a bamboo chopstick), add the chicken cubes. Fry until the top starts to turn white, flip with a spatula, fry for 30 seconds, then toss evenly.
Add the scallion rounds and stir-fry, then add the remaining scallion-ginger water (if less than 100g, add a little hot water - it must be hot); cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 2 minutes.
Switch to high heat, add the roasted peanuts, dried chilies, and Sichuan peppercorns; add 2g chicken powder, 5g aromatic vinegar, and 2g white sugar; toss well.
Mix 10g starch with 50g clean water to make a slurry, pour into the pan, toss evenly, and reduce the sauce to your desired consistency.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with 10g sesame oil, and serve.

Slightly more complex but more attractive version. Compared to the simple version, this encourages using Erjingtiao chilies and raw peanuts, and adding celtuce to enhance the crunch of the peanuts and the tenderness of the chicken.
Peel the celtuce and cut into 1cm cubes; set aside.
Cut the Erjingtiao chilies into 1cm sections.
Use scissors to debone the chicken drumstick, flatten the meat with the back of a knife, cut into strips, then into 1.5cm cubes. Soak in clean water for 10 minutes, then drain and set aside.
Place the green leaves of the scallion and 5g of ginger slices in a bowl, pour in 50g of boiling water and set aside; cut the white part of the scallion into 1.5cm rounds and set aside.

Add 2g salt, 5g dark soy sauce, 15g cooking wine, and 15g starch to the diced chicken and stir until slightly dry; gradually add some of the scallion-ginger water, stirring until the chicken becomes sticky; cover with plastic wrap and marinate in the fridge for 1 hour.
Switch to medium heat, add 20g vegetable oil, add raw peanuts and stir-fry until the surface is slightly scorched; remove the peanuts but leave the oil in the pan.
Continue heating; when it reaches 70% heat, add the chicken cubes and doubanjiang; stir-fry for about 1 minute.
Add the diced celtuce and continue stir-fry for 1 minute.

Add the scallion rounds and stir-fry, then add the remaining scallion-ginger water (if less than 100g, add a little hot water - it must be hot); add the Erjingtiao chili sections; cover and simmer over medium-low heat for 2 minutes.
Switch to high heat, add the peanuts and Sichuan peppercorns; add 2g chicken powder, 5g aromatic vinegar, and 2g white sugar; toss well.
Mix 10g starch with 50g clean water to make a slurry, pour into the pan, toss evenly, and reduce the sauce to your desired consistency.
Turn off the heat, drizzle with 10g sesame oil and 5g chili oil, toss for 10 seconds, and serve.
Adjust chili amount to taste; remove seeds if you prefer less heat.

mon_an.mo_ta: Xiao Chao Rou is a classic Hunan home-style dish that is spicy, fragrant, and perfect with rice. The pork belly slices are fried until the edges are slightly crispy and fragrant but not greasy, then stir-fried with fresh chilies, fermented black beans (douchi), and doubanjiang to create a rich savory aroma. It is rich in high-quality protein and fats, while the chilies provide plenty of Vitamin C, helping to stimulate the appetite and warm the body. The difficulty is medium, suitable for beginners with some experience; pay attention to marinating the meat and controlling the heat. From prep to serving takes about 1 hour, including 30 minutes of marinating and 15 minutes of stir-frying.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Fermented black beans (douchi) 10g, adjust ±5g to taste
Doubanjiang (fermented bean paste) 10g, adjust ±5g to taste
cac_buoc: Slice the pork belly.
Place the pork in a container, add starch, dark soy sauce, and salt; mix well and marinate for half an hour.
Cut the scallion into sections.
Slice the bird's eye chilies and Thai chilies diagonally.
Heat the pan and pour in the oil.
When the oil is hot, add the pork belly and stir-fry. Once it changes color, remove and set aside.
Add garlic to the pan and sauté until fragrant, then add the fermented black beans and stir-fry evenly.
Add the doubanjiang and stir-fry evenly.
Add the previously fried pork belly back into the pan and continue to stir-fry evenly.
Add the bird's eye chilies, Thai chilies, and scallion sections; stir-fry for 40 seconds.
Serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: This stir-fried chicken liver dish features a bold garlic aroma, a tender texture, and a hint of toasted cumin—a flavorful home-style stir-fry. Chicken liver is rich in iron, Vitamin A, and high-quality protein, helping to nourish the blood and improve eyesight. The process requires mastering the blanching technique to remove gaminess, which is a bit challenging for beginners. From prep to serving takes about forty minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make.
One portion is enough for 2 people.
Leeks (about 200g, add more if you like)
Large scallion 150g (divided into two parts: 100g cut into sections, 50g sliced)
Ginger 120g (divided into two parts: 70g sliced, 50g finely diced)
cac_buoc: Wash the chicken livers and set aside.
Wash the leeks, cut into sections, and set aside.
Wash the large scallion; cut 100g into sections and slice the remaining 50g; set aside.
Wash the ginger; slice 70g and finely dice the remaining 50g; set aside.

Step one: Blanching. Place the cleaned chicken livers in a pot, cover with cold water, and add the 100g of scallion sections, 70g of ginger slices, and 30ml of cooking wine. Turn on high heat. When the water boils, turn to medium heat, skim off the foam, and **wait 5-10 minutes** before turning off the heat. Remove the livers, soak in cold water, and rinse clean. Once cleaned, slice them and set aside.

Step two: Stir-frying. Turn on medium heat. Add 30ml of oil to the pan and wait 10 seconds for it to heat up. Add the 50g of sliced scallion and 50g of diced ginger; sauté until fragrant. Once fragrant, add the sliced chicken livers and stir-fry until slightly golden. Add the leeks and stir-fry for 30 seconds. When they are just cooked through, turn to low heat. Add the seasonings: 5g salt, 5g chicken powder (or MSG), 5g thirteen-spice powder, 5g pepper powder, and 10g BBQ seasoning or cumin (optional). Switch to high heat and stir-fry quickly for 30 seconds to prevent burning, then turn off the heat. Transfer to a plate and garnish with 5g of sesame seeds if desired.
