mon_an.mo_ta: Chicken with shiitake mushrooms is a home-style dish using chicken thighs and shiitake mushrooms as main ingredients. After stir-frying and braising, the chicken becomes silky and tender, infused with the characteristic aroma of the mushrooms and a rich, savory sauce. It is a Cantonese favorite enjoyed by all ages. Chicken is rich in high-quality protein and amino acids, while shiitake mushrooms contain lentinan and fiber, which help boost immunity and promote digestion. This dish requires some knife skills and heat control, posing a slight challenge for beginners. The entire process takes about 1 hour.
cac_buoc: Rehydrate the dried shiitake mushrooms in warm water
Finely slice the ginger, cut the green onions into segments, and halve the garlic into small bits
Debone the chicken thighs (optional, but makes eating easier) and cut into small pieces
Quarter the rehydrated mushrooms and keep the soaking liquid; set aside
Blanch the chicken for 1 minute to remove scum and impurities
Add 15ml cooking wine, 15ml light soy sauce, 1.5g salt, and 15ml dark soy sauce to the chicken and mix well by hand
Heat oil to 30% heat (low-medium), stir-fry the chicken until golden, then scoop out and set aside
Keep the remaining oil in the pan, sauté the green onions, ginger, and garlic until fragrant, then add the mushrooms and stir-fry over high heat
After 20 seconds when the mushroom aroma is released, add the stir-fried chicken, the mushroom soaking liquid (all of it, **this is the "soul" step**), 15ml sugar, and 30ml light soy sauce
Switch to medium heat without a lid and simmer for 2 minutes to reduce the sauce. Drizzle with 5ml sesame oil, sprinkle with chopped green onions, turn off the heat, and serve
Deboning chicken thighs is quite complex; here is my personal experience for reference:
Place the chicken thigh flat on the cutting board, **bone facing directly toward you**, and make a deep cut from top to bottom, ensuring you reach the bone
Use your hands to push the meat to both sides
Use the tip of the knife to separate the meat from the bone
Flip the thigh, insert the knife close to the bone, and cut the connection points between the bone and meat
Use the tip of the knife to cut the final attachment point to finish

mon_an.mo_ta: Fragrant, spicy, and chewy, this is a popular home-style dish that goes perfectly with rice. Chicken feet are rich in collagen, which is good for the skin and strengthens tendons and bones. You need to trim the claws first; if using whole feet, deboning is required, which can be challenging for beginners, but patience will lead to success. From blanching and simmering to stir-frying for flavor, the process takes about 45 minutes.
cac_buoc: Trim the claws off the chicken feet. If using only the paws, cut them in half. If using whole feet, debone them. Rinse thoroughly with water.
Place the chicken feet in a pot of cold water with green onions, ginger, and cooking wine to blanch. Skim off the foam once it boils.
Add bay leaves, star anise, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce. Cover and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes.
Remove the chicken feet and set aside one bowl of the braising liquid.

Heat oil in a pan and sauté minced ginger, minced garlic, and bird's eye chilies over low heat. Add some chili powder if you prefer it spicier. Add light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, five-spice powder, and salt; stir-fry until the sauce is fragrant.
Add the chicken feet, season with a little salt, and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes. Pour in the braising liquid while stirring.

Add chicken bouillon powder to enhance the savory taste, toss in green onion segments, and remove from the pot. Note: If adding side dishes, do so after sautéing the aromatics and before adding the chicken feet.

mon_an.ten: Yu Xiang Shredded Pork (Fish-Fragrant Shredded Pork)
mon_an.mo_ta: Yu Xiang Shredded Pork is a classic Sichuan dish with a sweet, sour, and slightly spicy flavor. It features tender shredded pork with carrots, green peppers, and wood ear mushrooms for a rich texture. High in protein and vitamins, it offers balanced nutrition. This dish has a certain level of difficulty, requiring the preparation of the "fish-fragrant" sauce and precise heat control during stir-frying. Beginners are recommended to follow each step carefully. Estimated time is about 40 minutes (excluding wood ear mushroom soaking time).
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: This version is sized for 1-2 servings.
cac_buoc: Prepare the marinade and the savory sauce
Make the `marinade`: mix 5ml light soy sauce, 5ml cooking wine, 5g starch, 20ml water, and 1 egg white
Make the `aromatic sauce`: mix 5ml light soy sauce, 15ml vinegar, 10 grams white sugar, 1 gram salt, 5g starch, and 20ml water. Prepare the ingredients
Marinate the pork tenderloin in the `marinade` for 15-30 minutes. Ensure the meat is well coated.
Soak dried wood ear mushrooms for 4 hours, wash, and cut into small pieces.
Wash the green peppers, remove stems, and julienne.
Wash the carrots, julienne, and blanch them.
Finely mince the ginger and garlic.
Cut green onions into 5mm segments. Cook the ingredients
Heat the pan and add 15ml oil.
Add the marinated meat to the pan, quickly stir to separate until it turns white, then remove and set aside.
Heat the pan again and add 5ml oil.
Add all the `green onions`, `ginger`, `garlic`, and `doubanjiang` (bean paste).
Add all the `carrots`, stir-fry for 20 seconds, then add the green peppers and wood ear mushrooms; stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the `cooked meat`. Quickly stir-fry to combine. Do not stir-fry for more than 20 seconds.
Pour in the `aromatic sauce`. Quickly stir-fry to combine. Do not stir-fry for more than 15 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve on a plate.

mon_an.mo_ta: Yu Xiang Eggplant is a classic Sichuan home-style dish. It is sweet, sour, and slightly spicy, with soft eggplant that absorbs the sauce, making it an excellent companion for rice. Eggplant is rich in fiber and vitamins, and the addition of minced pork provides protein. The difficulty is medium, requiring mastery of eggplant frying and seasoning. Beginners can succeed with a little practice. It takes about 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each preparation, determine how many servings to make. One serving is enough for one person.
Green onions, ginger, garlic, bird's eye chilies (to taste)
cac_buoc: Cut the eggplant into batons.
Mince the pork, finely chop the green onions, ginger, and garlic, and dice the bird's eye chilies.
Prepare the fish-fragrant sauce: mix salt, MSG, sugar, light soy sauce, dark soy sauce, vinegar, and starch slurry in a bowl.

Pour 300ml oil into the pan and turn on low heat (low heat is easier to control). When the oil is 70% hot (about 40 seconds on low heat, with light smoke), fry the eggplant for two minutes until the edges are slightly golden, then remove. Excess oil can be scooped out for later use.
Keep 15-30ml oil in the pan, stir-fry the minced pork until it turns white, then remove.
Pour 15-30ml oil into the pan, sauté the doubanjiang, white parts of the green onions, ginger, and garlic until fragrant, then add the minced pork and stir-fry evenly.

Add 80-150ml water (estimated at 80% of the eggplant's height), add the eggplant and the sauce. Stir-fry over high heat to infuse the flavors and reduce the sauce. Finally, toss in the green onions and serve.
Eggplants can be peeled if preferred, and more minced pork can be added to taste.

mon_an.mo_ta: This spicy, fragrant, and silky tofu dish uses salted duck egg instead of traditional spicy bean paste. It offers a fresh, savory flavor with a hint of numbing heat and spice, making it an excellent appetizer that pairs perfectly with rice. Rich in high-quality protein and micronutrients like calcium and iron. Moderate difficulty, beginner-friendly, taking about 40 minutes in total.
cac_buoc: Mince the garlic and ginger; set aside.
Cut the bird's eye chilies into rings; set aside.
Mince the pork belly (skip if using pre-ground meat).
Add half of the salt and premium soy sauce to the minced meat, stir well, and set aside.

Carefully cut the salted egg in half lengthwise; remove the yolk (must be removed to avoid a fishy smell). Mash the remaining egg white into roughly 2mm * 2mm pieces (no need to be too fine); set aside.
Open the tofu packaging and use a paring knife to cut the tofu directly in the box into approximately 2.5cm * 3cm cubes; set aside.
Heat the pan and add 10ml - 15ml of cooking oil. Wait 10 seconds for the oil to heat up.
Reduce to low heat. Add the garlic, ginger, chili rings, Sichuan peppercorns, salted egg white, and chili garlic sauce. Sauté for 20 seconds until fragrant.
Increase to medium heat, add the minced meat, and stir-fry for about 1 minute until the meat changes color.
Reduce to low heat, add the tofu, and sprinkle the remaining salt and premium soy sauce evenly over the tofu.
Pour boiling water in from the side of the pan (to prevent the tofu from breaking) until it just covers the tofu.
Turn to high heat. Once the water boils, immediately switch to medium heat and wait for about 10 minutes.
When the liquid has reduced to 1/5 and the tofu surface has taken on color, turn off the heat and serve.
During this time, be sure to watch closely to prevent the pan from burning.

mon_an.ten: Mala Xiang Guo (Spicy Numbing Stir-fry Pot)
mon_an.mo_ta: A bold Sichuan family dish featuring a combination of vegetables, meat, and tofu products. It offers a satisfying spicy aroma and rich layers of flavor. The meat and vegetable combination provides high-quality protein and various vitamins for balanced nutrition. The steps are clear but require mastering blanching and heat control; it offers a slight challenge for beginners. Total time is about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Total green vegetables: 455g (including bok choy, romaine lettuce, and spinach, proportioned to your preference)
Total boneless meat: 430g (including pork, beef, chicken, fish balls, and sausages, proportioned to your preference)
In the above list, the proportions of vegetables, meat, tofu, and noodles are recommendations; feel free to adjust based on your preference.
cac_buoc: Bring a pot of water to a boil (enough to submerge the ingredients in steps 2-4).
Add the green vegetables to the boiling water, blanch for 5 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add the boneless meat to the boiling water, blanch for 4 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Add the Beijing spicy instant noodles to the boiling water, cook for 2 minutes, then remove and set aside.
Discard the boiling water, wipe the pan dry, add 105g of cooking oil, and heat on high for 30 seconds.
Add the Mala Xiang Guo seasoning and stir-fry for 20 seconds.
Add the dried chilies and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the blanched vegetables, switch to medium heat, and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the blanched meat and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the cooked instant noodles and toss with chopsticks for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and serve.
Heat level explanation:
High heat is typically around 240°C; for an induction cooker, the input power is about 2 kilowatts.
Medium heat is typically around 120°C; for an induction cooker, the input power is about 1.4 kilowatts.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic Indian curry featuring grilled chicken thighs simmered in a rich sauce of tomatoes, butter, and cream. The flavor is smooth and velvety, sweet and sour with a hint of spice, carrying the unique complex aroma of Indian spices. Chicken, yogurt, and cashews provide plenty of protein and healthy fats, while tomatoes and spices offer vitamins and antioxidants. Somewhat challenging to make, requiring heat control and spice balancing. Including marinating time, it takes about 1 hour and 45 minutes to complete.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 3-4 people.
500g chicken thighs (boneless, cut into large chunks)
5g red chili powder (preferably Kashmiri chili powder)
3g dried fenugreek leaves (kasuri methi), crushed by hand
cac_buoc: Marinate the chicken (1 hour in advance).
In a large bowl, mix the yogurt, grated ginger, grated garlic, chili powder, turmeric, salt, and lemon juice.
Add the chicken chunks and toss well to coat thoroughly.
Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for **at least 1 hour**. Pan-sear the chicken.
Pour 15ml of oil into a flat pan and heat over high heat.
Add the marinated chicken chunks to the pan (do not pour in the excess marinade).
Sear on high heat until *both sides are charred golden brown* (about 3 minutes per side); the chicken does not need to be fully cooked.
Remove and set aside. Prepare the sauce base.
Add the tomatoes, onion, cashews, ginger, garlic, and 100ml of water to the pan.
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and **cook for 15 minutes** until *all ingredients are very soft*.
Let it cool slightly, pour into a blender, and blend until *completely smooth*.
Pass the sauce through a sieve to remove any pulp, resulting in a silky sauce; set aside. Simmer.
Add 50g of butter to the pan and melt over medium heat.
Pour in the strained tomato sauce.
Add 5g chili powder, 5g coriander powder, 3g cumin powder, and 5g salt.
Sauté for **3-5 minutes** until the *sauce darkens and the oil separates*.
Add the seared chicken chunks and stir well.
Add 10g sugar (to balance the acidity of the tomatoes) and stir.
Pour in 100ml of light cream and stir well.
Simmer on low heat for **10-12 minutes** until the chicken is fully cooked and has absorbed the sauce.
Add 3g garam masala and 2g cardamom powder.
Sprinkle in 3g of dried fenugreek leaves (crush them by hand before adding).
Stir well and turn off the heat.
Serve on a plate; you can drizzle a little extra cream on top for garnish.
Dried fenugreek leaves (Kasuri Methi) are the key ingredient for this dish's unique herbal aroma. They can be found at Indian grocery stores or online.
Using Kashmiri chili powder gives a brighter red color with less heat. If unavailable, use half the amount of regular chili powder and add 3g of paprika.
Cashews help make the sauce thicker and smoother. If you have a nut allergy, replace them with an equal amount of light cream.
This dish is typically served with naan bread or basmati rice.
Butter Chicken is considered one of India's greatest contributions to world cuisine and is a staple on Indian restaurant menus globally.

mon_an.mo_ta: Braised Yellow Chicken is a homestyle dish using chicken thighs, shiitake mushrooms, and green peppers as main ingredients. It features a rich sauce and tender chicken with a savory-sweet flavor that pairs perfectly with rice. Rich in high-quality protein and mushroom polysaccharides. Caramelizing the sugar for color can be challenging, but it can be replaced with dark soy sauce. The overall difficulty is low, making it easy for beginners to master. Takes about 40 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Preparation.
Wash the chicken thighs and chop into **4cm** chunks.
Slice the ginger and cut the dried chilies into **small rings**.
Slice the shiitake mushrooms and cut the green peppers into long, thin **diagonal strips**. If using dried mushrooms, wash off the dust, soak overnight, and reserve the soaking water.
If using a potato, cut it into **bite-sized chunks** similar in size to the chicken. Stir-fry.

Caramelize the sugar: Add a base of oil to the pan; while the oil is still cool, add the white sugar (**this requires some skill; beginners can skip this, move to the chicken stir-fry step, and use dark soy sauce for color instead**).
Heat slowly over low heat until the oil temperature rises and the sugar melts and turns dark brown (stir constantly to avoid burning).
Quickly add the chicken chunks, switch to high heat, and stir-fry rapidly! Drizzle in the cooking wine and continue stir-frying for a moment.
Add the ginger slices and dried chilies.
Add the soy sauce and stir-fry evenly.
Pour in the mushroom soaking water or fresh water until the chicken is just submerged.
Add the sliced shiitake mushrooms, white pepper powder, salt, and potato.
After stirring well, cover and braise over medium-low heat for **15-20 minutes** (transfer to a clay pot if available).
Wait until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened (do not let the sauce dry out completely), then finally add the green peppers.
Add MSG (optional), stir well, and turn off the heat! The green peppers should be just cooked through; do not overcook them.

mon_an.mo_ta: A quick, refreshing, and tender homestyle dish with a savory flavor, garlic aroma, and a hint of spice. Rich in protein and vitamins, it helps clear heat and hydrate. Very beginner-friendly; success depends on heat control. Estimated cooking time is 25 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 1 person.
Bird's eye chili = 1 * number of servings
cac_buoc: Slice the lean pork into thin pieces, place in a bowl, add 10g of oil and the soy sauce, stir well, and marinate for 10 minutes.
Trim 5cm off both ends of the cucumber, then slice the rest diagonally into 0.5cm thick pieces.
Place the cucumber in a bowl, sprinkle with 8g of salt, stir well, and marinate for 5 minutes.
Peel and smash the garlic, then mince it; set aside.
Remove the stem from the bird's eye chili and cut into 0.5cm segments.
Heat the pan, add 40g of oil, and once the oil is smoking hot, add the minced garlic and chili; stir-fry 5 times.
Add the marinated pork and stir-fry until the meat changes color and is cooked through.
Add the cucumber and 2g of salt. Stir-fry over high heat for 30 seconds, then serve. If you cannot maintain high heat, the cucumber may stay raw; consider increasing the time to 50 seconds.

mon_an.mo_ta: Black pepper beef is a widely popular home-style stir-fry featuring a bold black pepper aroma and tender beef strips. Combined with sweet, crunchy onions and bell peppers, it offers a perfect balance of meat and vegetables that appeals to all ages. Rich in high-quality protein and iron, with vitamins from the peppers and onions, this dish is very beginner-friendly and typically takes less than an hour from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the intended number of servings. One serving is sufficient for 2-3 people.
Beef = x number of servings * 100g (adjust based on appetite and pan size)
Onion = x number of servings * 1/12 piece (e.g., for 3 people, use about 1/4 onion)
Bell pepper = x number of servings * 1/12 piece (e.g., for 3 people, use about 1/4 pepper)
Black pepper marinade = use the ratio specified on the product packaging
Black pepper powder = x number of servings * 1g (or sprinkle to taste)
Peanut oil = x number of servings * 10ml (oil amount varies by total volume; adjust proportionally if beef quantity changes)
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the above conditions.
cac_buoc: Cut the beef into strips, preferably under 8cm long, 5-10mm thick, and about 1cm wide (precision is not strictly required).
Marinate the beef with the marinade, mix well, and let it sit. Refer to the product instructions for quantity and time; you may marinate longer but do not shorten the time.
If using a liquid marinade, sprinkle a layer of black pepper powder three minutes before the marinating time ends, then add the starch, mix again, and let it sit for 20 minutes.
Turn on the heat, heat the pan, and add the peanut oil.
When a thin wisp of smoke rises from the oil, add the beef to the pan.

Turn the heat to medium-high and stir-fry for 2 minutes until the exterior of the beef changes color (no visible raw blood; if blood is still visible, it needs more time). Be careful of oil splatters.
Add the onions and bell peppers, then stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add salt, sprinkle another round of black pepper powder, and stir-fry for 30 seconds to mix well.
Once the onions have softened, turn off the heat, remove from the pan, and serve on a plate.

mon_an.ten: Guizhou Sausage with Baby Chinese Cabbage
mon_an.mo_ta: This dish is savory and fresh, combining the intense aroma of Guizhou-style sausage with the delicate sweetness of baby Chinese cabbage. It is a rare non-spicy flavor from Southwestern cuisine that appeals to everyone. Baby Chinese cabbage is rich in vitamins and fiber, which balances the protein and fat from the sausage. The process is extremely simple, requiring no complex heat control or extra seasoning. It takes only 15 minutes from start to finish, making it perfect for beginners and busy weekdays.
cac_buoc: Pour 750ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil.
Add the sausage and boil for 13 minutes.
Add the baby Chinese cabbage and cook for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat and remove the sausage and cabbage.
Cut the cabbage into sections and slice the sausage, then arrange them on a plate.
Depending on your pot size, ensure the water just covers the ingredients; it is better to have too much water than too little.
If you do not have a knife, the cabbage and sausage can be served whole.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a quick and simple Cantonese-style main dish. The rice is infused with the savory, aromatic fat of the Chinese sausage, paired with crisp-tender greens and carrots for a rich texture. It is nutritionally balanced with starch, protein, and various vitamins. Cooked entirely in the microwave, it is very beginner-friendly and takes only about 15 minutes to prepare.
cac_buoc: Rinse the rice and place it in a `rice bowl`, add 400ml of water, and **cover with a lid**.

Place in the microwave on high power for `6` minutes. While the rice is cooking, prepare the ingredients: slice the sausage, wash the greens, slice the carrots, and chop the scallions. Place the greens and carrots in a `greens bowl`, add 10ml of oil and 5g of salt. Mix 10ml of light soy sauce and 5ml of oil in a `small bowl`.
After 6 minutes, use a towel or heat-resistant gloves to remove the bowl; the rice should be about 80% cooked.
Layer the sausage slices over the rice and continue microwaving on high for `2` minutes.
Remove the rice, place the `greens bowl` in the microwave, and cook on high for `4-5` minutes.
Arrange the greens on top of the sausage rice and crack an egg over it. Depending on your preference, microwave on high for another `40-60` seconds.
Remove the rice; the main components are now done.
Place the `small bowl` in the microwave and heat on high for `30` seconds.
Drizzle the heated light soy sauce mixture over the rice and sprinkle with chopped scallions to finish.
Any leftover greens can be dipped in the sauce and eaten.

mon_an.mo_ta: Spaghetti Bolognese is a quick and easy Western home-style dish with a rich sauce and al dente noodles, perfect for busy weekdays. Minced meat and onions combined with ready-made pasta sauce provide a quick boost of protein and starch, while onions add fiber. The method is very beginner-friendly, involving only simple chopping and stir-frying. Once mastered, it can be served in 15 minutes, making it much more satisfying than instant noodles.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine the intended number of servings. One serving is enough for 2 people.
Onion, more than half (about 150g, usually double the weight of the meat)
cac_buoc: Fill a pot with water and bring to a boil, then add the spaghetti (cook for 6-12 minutes).
While the water is boiling, proceed with the following steps, but keep an eye on the pasta cooking time.
Finely dice the onion.
Pour oil into a pan and sauté the diced onions over medium heat.
Stir constantly, being careful not to burn the onions, until they become translucent.
Add the minced meat and continue to stir (break it apart) until the meat turns brown.
Add the pasta sauce and stir gently to combine.
Drain the cooked spaghetti and add it to the meat sauce, mixing well (or pour the sauce directly over the plated noodles).
Spaghetti comes in various thicknesses; check the cooking time on the packaging before boiling.
Note that pasta sauce is not the same as regular tomato ketchup. Ketchup is a condiment, while pasta sauce is a seasoned tomato base with different herbs and spices.

mon_an.mo_ta: Handmade dumplings (Sủi cảo) are a classic Chinese staple with thin skins and generous filling. They are fresh, juicy, and can be seasoned to taste. The pork filling provides high-quality protein and fat, while chives add vitamins and fiber. This dish is quite challenging for beginners as it requires mastering dough kneading, wrapper rolling, filling mixing, and temperature control. Total preparation time is approximately 3 hours.
cac_buoc: Prepare the wrappers.
Place all the flour into a mixing bowl.
Add the toasted sesame oil.
Make a small well in the center of the flour.
Add the water in 4-5 stages, mixing as you go, until slightly dry dough clumps form.
Stop adding water and use your hands to press the dough together.
Press the dough until it picks up all the flour from the sides of the bowl (the bowl and hands should be clean).
Place the dough on a work surface, cover it with the bowl, and let it rest for 45 minutes at room temperature (around 25°C).
After resting, roll the dough into a long log, fold it back, and roll it out again; repeat this 3 times.
Roll into a final long log and cut into 20 equal pieces. Roll each piece into a ball about 3-3.5cm in diameter.
Flatten each ball. Dust your hands, the surface, the rolling pin, and the dough with flour to prevent sticking.
Use a rolling pin to flatten the dough into a circle about 8cm in diameter and 2mm thick, with the center slightly thicker (3mm) than the edges. Prepare the filling.
Remove the skin from the pork, keeping some fat, and cut into small chunks.
Mince the pork finely using a knife (two knives are recommended) and place in a bowl.
Finely mince the ginger and scallions, add them to the meat, and mix well.
Wash the chives and cut them into pieces smaller than 3mm.
Mix the chives with the minced meat. Add 2ml each of oyster sauce, light soy sauce, and sesame oil. Add one egg white and mix well by hand.
Let the filling sit for 30 minutes before wrapping. Wrap the dumplings.
Place a wrapper in your left hand. Try to keep the side where the filling goes free of excess flour so it seals properly.
Use chopsticks in your right hand to place filling in the center (about half the diameter of the wrapper).
Fold the edges together and pinch firmly to seal. Pleating is optional for personal meals as long as the dumpling does not leak. Cook the dumplings.
Use a pot large enough for 20 dumplings, or cook in batches.
Boil water until the pot is about 3/4 full.
Once the water is at a rolling boil, add the dumplings and turn the heat to medium.
When the water boils again after adding the dumplings, pour 50ml of cold water along the side of the pot (repeat this step twice more).
After the third time the water boils and 50ml of cold water is added, wait for it to boil again, then turn the heat to low for 60 seconds before removing the dumplings.
Do not cover the pot while boiling. Adding cold water three times prevents the dumplings from breaking due to continuous vigorous boiling.
Optional additions and serving suggestions:
Consider adding the following:
Black vinegar 10ml
Ginger, small piece (50g)
Sesame oil 2 drops
Garlic/minced garlic 3 cloves per person
Serve with black vinegar (recommended: 10-20ml).
Mix shredded ginger with 20ml of black vinegar in a small bowl for a richer dipping sauce.
Add 1-3 drops of sesame oil to the black vinegar for the dipping sauce.
Add crushed minced garlic to the black vinegar for the dipping sauce. (Note: This will leave a garlic scent; skip or clean your palate if you have a meeting after the meal.)

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an upgraded version of fried rice with a variety of ingredients: fluffy, separate grains, silky eggs, combined with shrimp, luncheon meat, and diced vegetables for a distinct layered texture. It is a classic main dish of Huaiyang cuisine. Rich in high-quality protein, starch, and vitamins, it offers balanced nutrition. Although there are many steps, the process is intuitive and beginner-friendly; it just requires patience in prepping the ingredients. Estimated time is about 1 hour.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before each cooking session, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1-2 people.
Luncheon meat (Spam) 150g (Shanghai Maling Ham Luncheon Meat recommended, 340g per tin, use half a tin per batch)
cac_buoc: Dice the carrots into 0.2cm*0.2cm*0.2cm cubes, set aside
Dice the luncheon meat into 0.2cm*0.2cm*0.2cm cubes, set aside
Separate the white parts and green leaves of the green onion, cut each into 0.25-0.5cm small pieces, set aside separately
Crack the eggs into a bowl, whisk well, and set aside
Boil the carrots, peas, and corn until cooked, then remove and set aside (do not discard the water)
Boil the shrimp until cooked, remove and set aside (the water can be discarded)

Heat the pan and the oil; you can refer to stir-fry guides regarding the "hot pan, cold oil" technique. For the second oil pour, use 20-30ml of oil, wait for it to heat up, then slowly pour in the eggs (control the stream diameter from the bowl to about 0.5cm), do not stir
Once the eggs have set, remove them immediately and set aside
Add the luncheon meat, peas, carrots, corn, and shrimp to the pan and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes, then remove to a plate and set aside
Rinse the pan with water to remove any residue, ensuring the pan is clean (it can be oily but must be free of debris)
Heat the pan with oil (10ml), add the white parts of the green onion and sauté until fragrant

Reduce to low heat (if the oil is too hot, turn off the heat for 1-2 minutes), add the rice, use a spatula to quickly break up the rice and stir-fry, ensuring the rice is evenly coated in oil and the grains are separate
Pour the eggs back in, continue to break them up so they crumble and fully incorporate with the rice
Switch to high heat, add all other prepared ingredients, and stir-fry quickly for 1-2 minutes
Sprinkle in the salt and stir-fry until evenly mixed
Sprinkle in the green onion leaves and stir-fry for 1 minute
Turn off the heat and serve on a plate
It is normal for your arm to feel tired after finishing; consider it a good forearm workout
Supermarkets sell frozen mixed peas, carrots, and corn, which can be used to save time on dicing; brands like Pams Mixed Veges are very affordable and work well

mon_an.mo_ta: This pizza crust uses a low-temperature overnight fermentation method, resulting in a soft yet slightly chewy crust, perfect for home-style Western baking. It primarily provides starch and some healthy fats. The process is simple but requires patience for the dough to rise, making it beginner-friendly. From preparation to the end of baking, including the overnight cold fermentation, it takes about 10-14 hours, making it ideal to prepare a day in advance.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One 8-9 inch pizza requires about 125g of flour, which is enough for one person (sufficient for an adult male)
Flour : Water : Olive oil : Dry yeast : Salt : Sugar
To make 4 crusts at once, you will need:
cac_buoc: Use the prepared warm water to dissolve the dry yeast, stir gently, and set aside
Take the prepared flour and add the salt, olive oil, and white granulated sugar
Prepare to mix the water and flour, adding water while stirring until all the water is incorporated
Stir until no dry flour is visible
Place in a container about three times the size of the dough, seal tightly, and place in the refrigerator (4°C). **Wait 8-12 hours; usually, dough made the night before is ready by the next evening**
Observe the fermented dough; **it is ready when it has roughly doubled in size**
Remove the fermented dough, divide it into four equal parts, cover each with plastic wrap, and set aside
Sprinkle a generous amount of dry flour onto the cutting board to prepare for kneading
Since the dough is quite wet, it will be less sticky once coated in flour; no need for heavy kneading, just until the surface is slightly smooth
Use your hands to stretch or a rolling pin to flatten the dough; it doesn't have to be perfectly round, just ensure an even thickness that fits your oven
Line with parchment paper, place the crust on top, add your prepared toppings according to taste, and sprinkle with shredded cheese
Fruit Pizza: Oven top heat 180°C, bottom heat 220°C, bake for 16 minutes
Meat and Vegetable Pizza: Oven top heat 200°C, bottom heat 230°C, bake for 18 minutes
Drizzle with salad dressing or any sauce you like and enjoy~
Be sure to pay close attention to the water ratio
Oven quality varies; for the first time, observe how the heat affects the pizza
Unless specifically noted as low-gluten or high-gluten flour, standard all-purpose flour is generally used
Fruits that release a lot of water, such as watermelon or tangerines, should not be used as toppings

mon_an.mo_ta: Japanese Curry Rice is a rich, home-style Japanese dish using curry roux cubes, combined with potatoes, carrots, onions, and meat for a smooth, savory, and slightly sweet-spicy flavor. It is rich in protein, starch, and vitamins, providing ample energy. The overall method is not complicated, but it requires heat control and stirring techniques, suitable for those with a little cooking experience. It takes about 1 hour from prep to serving, and the flavor improves after being chilled.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The amount of ingredients is proportional to the curry; calculations are based on **half a box of House Foods curry roux (115g)**. Half a box makes about six bowls; curry tastes better after being chilled in the fridge, so don't worry about not finishing it alone.
cac_buoc: 1. Preparation
Trim the ends of the carrot, peel, and cut into rolling chunks (rangiri)
Peel the outer layer of the onions, remove the core, and cut into wedges
Peel the potatoes and cut into large chunks
Cut the meat into cubes
Peel the garlic, smash, and mince
Finely chop the curry roux cubes to increase surface area for faster melting. 2. Cooking Process
Heat the pan with oil, add the garlic and meat, **stir-fry quickly** until the *surface of the meat turns white*
Add the carrots and **stir-fry quickly** to heat evenly
Add the onions and **stir-fry quickly** until the onions *turn translucent*
Add the potatoes and continue to stir-fry until the potatoes *soften* (test with a chopstick)
Add enough water to fully cover the ingredients; once boiling, **wait 15 minutes**
Turn off the heat, add the curry roux, and stir
Wait for the curry to melt completely before turning the heat back on, then **stir slowly for 10 minutes** to prevent scorching
When the mixture reaches a *thickened consistency*, turn off the heat. 3. Reheating after chilling: For chilled curry, take out the portion needed, reheat, and pour over rice.
Microwave: 2-3 minutes on high for one serving
Stovetop: Add 50ml of water and **stir constantly** while reheating
Notes
Steps 1-6 can be done while waiting during steps 2-5; you can also use this time to boil some vegetables or fry an over-easy egg.
From step 2-5 to 2-6, monitor the boiling water level; if it falls below 2/3 of the ingredients, add hot water to submerge them again.

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic home-style Japanese rice bowl dish. Fatty beef slices and white onions are simmered in a sweet and savory sauce until flavorful. The meat is tender, the onions are sweet, and the sauce is aromatic. Beef provides high-quality protein and heme iron, while onions are rich in fiber and antioxidants. The preparation is not complex; beginners can easily complete it by following the steps. The cooking process takes about 30 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Ingredient amounts are proportional to the rice; calculations are based on **one cup of rice (160ml)**. This serves about two people; leftovers can be refrigerated, though they may not taste as fresh.
cac_buoc: 1. Preparation
Peel the outer layer of the onion, remove the core, and cut into wedges
Wash the green onions and cut into 0.5cm pieces
Heat a dry pan, add the white sesame seeds, and **toss the pan** to heat evenly until *lightly golden*
Blanch the beef slices for 1 minute, then remove and drain

Mix 40g `mirin` (or 30g `cooking wine`), 30g `soy sauce`, 20g `oyster sauce`, 5g `sugar`, and 5g `dark soy sauce` (optional, for color) in a bowl to make the `seasoning sauce` (you can place the bowl directly on an electronic scale for this). 2. Cooking Process
Heat the pan with oil, add the onions, and **stir-fry quickly** until the onions *turn translucent*
Reduce to low heat, add 250g of water (or dashi), turn the heat back to high, and **wait 3 minutes**
Add the beef and the `seasoning sauce`
**Stir all ingredients constantly** for **10 minutes** to prevent sticking
Turn off the heat
Scoop the beef and onions over rice (be sure to drizzle some sauce over the rice)
Garnish with chopped green onions and toasted sesame seeds; it's ready. 3. Reheating after chilling: For chilled gyudon, take out the portion needed, reheat, and pour over rice.
Microwave: 2-3 minutes on high for one serving
Stovetop: Add 50ml of water and **stir constantly** while reheating
Notes

If using high-quality beef, you can skip blanching to retain more beef flavor; the mirin will help remove any gaminess. Don't worry about the beef being undercooked; 10 minutes of simmering ensures it is done
If possible, add 15g of `sake` for better flavor

mon_an.mo_ta: Noodle soup is a versatile home-style main dish with a clear broth and smooth noodles that pairs well with various meats and vegetables. The flavor can be light or bold. It is rich in starch and high-quality protein; adding vegetables provides vitamins and fiber for a balanced, filling meal. The method is extremely simple, requiring no prior cooking experience. It usually takes about 30 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Noodle quantity: Equivalent to one pack of instant noodles per person, typically between 70-230g.
Cold water: Enough to submerge the noodles, usually between 200 - 400 ml
Vegetables: Volume roughly equal to the noodles
Note: The volume of leafy greens can be excluded from this estimate
cac_buoc: First, cut the vegetable ingredients into pieces no larger than 4cm for even cooking
If using raw meat, place it in cold water first, cover, and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam/scum from the surface, then turn off the heat and remove the parboiled meat; set aside
Bring water to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium heat

Add ingredients that take longer to cook into the pot (such as parboiled meat, shiitake mushrooms, etc.). To ensure they are cooked through, time for 10 minutes after the water returns to a boil; for particularly large chunks, add another 5 minutes.

Add the noodles to the pot, stir occasionally to ensure the noodles and broth are fully in contact, maintain a gentle boil, and cook for 5 minutes. If white foam forms after adding noodles, crack the lid or remove it to vent.
Add quick-cooking ingredients like leafy greens to the pot, stir to submerge them, and cook for 2-5 minutes
Turn off the heat, then add salt, pepper, sesame oil, or your preferred seasonings. Stir well and serve
The process can be adjusted according to your preference; experimenting often leads to pleasant surprises
If you are unsure about the amount of salt, add it in small increments to avoid over-salting

mon_an.mo_ta: Henan Steamed Noodles is a traditional family snack originating from Henan. The noodles are first steamed, then stir-fried, and steamed again to create a glossy, flavorful, and chewy texture. Pork belly and garlic sprouts provide protein and fiber, making this a nutritionally balanced main dish. While there are several steps, beginners can succeed by simply following the order. The total time from preparation to serving is approximately 40 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The quantities below are for 1 serving! Please adjust ingredients according to your needs.
cac_buoc: First Steaming
Fill the pot with 7 parts water; once boiling, place the steamer rack inside.
Spread the dried noodles evenly, drizzle with 5ml of oil and coat well, then steam for 15 minutes.
Remove the noodles and steamer rack, set aside, and discard the water in the pot. Prepare the vegetables.
Slice the pork belly into 2mm thick pieces.
Cut the garlic sprouts into 3cm sections.
Thinly slice the green onions (0.2cm).
Julienne the ginger into 1mm x 1mm x 3cm strips.
Crush the garlic on a cutting board and mince into 1mm pieces. Stir-frying.
Heat a wok until dry, then add 3ml of cooking oil.
Hold the handle and swirl the wok so the oil coats 2/3 of the surface.
Over medium heat, stir-fry the pork slices for 1 minute.
Add the green onions, ginger, garlic, and cooking wine; continue stir-frying for 1 minute.
Add the garlic sprout sections to the wok and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Season with dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, oyster sauce, salt, chicken bouillon, and thirteen-spice powder; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add 500ml of water to cover the vegetables and simmer for 1 minute.
Add the steamed noodles and stir constantly for 3 minutes; once the noodles are evenly colored, turn off the heat.
Transfer the mixed noodles and vegetables into a separate bowl. Second Steaming.
Refill the pot with 7 parts cold water, place the steamer rack, and spread the noodle mixture evenly on top.
Once the water boils, cook over high heat for 15 minutes, then remove from the pot.
Drizzle with 10g of sesame oil and serve.
Noodle thickness and texture:
Thin, round variety (most common in supermarkets, chewier).
Wide, flat variety (softer texture).

mon_an.ten: Tengzhou Vegetable Pancakes (Tengzhou Cai Jian Bing)
mon_an.mo_ta: Tengzhou Vegetable Pancake is a traditional snack from Tengzhou City, Shandong, created by Wang Niu Gao during the Qing Dynasty. It uses flour pancakes to wrap seasonal vegetables like Napa cabbage, vermicelli, and tofu, along with eggs and sausage, seasoned with oil and spices then pan-fried. The result is crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, savory and refreshing. Suitable as a main dish or breakfast, taking about 15 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 1 person.
Flour pancakes = x number of servings * 2 sheets
Napa cabbage = x number of servings * 100 g
Vermicelli (dry weight) = x number of servings * 50 g
Tofu = x number of servings * 80 g
Carrots = x number of servings * 50 g
Chives = x number of servings * 30 g (optional)
Sausage = x number of servings * 40 g (optional)
Cooking oil = x number of servings * 20 ml
Salt = x number of servings * 2 g
MSG = x number of servings * 1 g (optional)
Cumin powder = x number of servings * 2 g
Chili powder = x number of servings * 2 g (optional)
Black pepper powder = x number of servings * 1 g
cac_buoc: Soak the vermicelli in warm water for 10 minutes until soft, drain well, and cut into sections no longer than 5 cm; set aside.

Wash the Napa cabbage and shred into strips no wider than 1 cm; peel and julienne the carrots (< 1 cm); dice the tofu into small cubes (< 1 cm); wash and cut the chives into 1 cm sections. Place everything in a mixing bowl.
Add 15 ml oil, 2 g salt, 1 g MSG, 2 g cumin powder, 1 g black pepper, and 2 g chili powder to the bowl. Mix well with chopsticks until the vegetables are evenly coated; set aside.

Heat a flat pan (or griddle) over medium heat, add 5 ml oil, and swirl to coat. Crack the egg into the pan, break the yolk and white with a spatula, and fry into a thin round slightly smaller than the pancake.
Place one pancake flat onto the egg so they stick together, then flip them over (egg side facing up) and switch to low heat; keep ready.
Spread the vegetable mixture evenly over the pancake (egg side), leaving a 1 cm border at the edges to prevent spilling when folding.
Cover the vegetables with the second pancake and press gently with a spatula to bond the layers.
Cook over medium-low heat for 2 minutes until the bottom is lightly golden, then flip the entire pancake over and cook for another 2 minutes until the other side is golden and glossy.

Switch to the lowest heat and continue cooking for 1 minute until both sides are golden brown and the vegetables are fully cooked (you can check by inserting a chopstick; there should be no resistance from raw vegetables).
Turn off the heat, fold both sides of the pancake toward the center to form a rectangle about 10 cm wide, then use a spatula or knife to cut it in half and serve.
Vegetables can be substituted according to preference: spinach, pumpkin, radish, or shepherd's purse all work well; keep the total vegetable weight per serving around 300-350 g.
These pancakes are best eaten hot; they will soften and lose their crunch if left at room temperature for more than 30 minutes.
If you don't have a traditional griddle, a non-stick flat pan with a diameter of at least 28 cm will work; watch the heat carefully to avoid burning the pancake.
Flour pancakes can be store-bought; alternatively, mix 100 g flour with 150 ml water to make a thin batter and cook it in a flat pan.

mon_an.ten: Ham Rice Balls (Huo Tui Fan Tuan)
mon_an.mo_ta: A simple Japanese-style rice ball that is quick to make. Savory ham combines with salad dressing and seaweed for a rich texture that is very filling. High in starch, protein, and vitamins, it provides a quick energy boost. Extremely low difficulty, easy for beginners, taking only about 1 hour from cooking the rice to completion.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Place the rice and water in a rice cooker, start the cooking cycle, and wait until finished.
Place the frozen corn and peas in a pot, cover with water, bring to a boil, wait 2 minutes, then drain.
Cut the ham into 1cm cubes.
Meanwhile, heat 10ml of oil and stir-fry the ham until it takes on some color.
In a bowl, combine the rice, ham, seaweed flakes, peas, corn, and salad dressing; mix well.
Serve on a plate (if desired).
The amount of salad dressing can be adjusted to taste.
Feel free to experiment with different types of salad dressings.

mon_an.mo_ta: Stir-fried Starch Jelly is a specialty snack from the Shanxi and Shaanxi regions. It is smooth and tender in the mouth, savory and slightly spicy, with the aroma of garlic and bean paste. Mainly made from starch, it provides plenty of carbohydrates for a quick energy boost. Moderate difficulty, suitable for beginners with some basic skills; the entire process takes about 15 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The ingredients below are for one serving. Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for one person.
cac_buoc: Cut the starch jelly into mahjong-sized cubes.
Turn on low heat, heat the oil in a pan, and when slightly warm, sauté the minced garlic until fragrant, then add the bean paste and stir-fry until the oil turns red.
Add the starch jelly cubes to the pan and stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add light soy sauce for flavor and dark soy sauce for color; stir-fry evenly, then add the chili powder and continue to stir-fry.
Add the salt and thirteen-spice powder, then stir-fry for another 10 seconds.
Pour in the prepared mineral water, stir-fry for 10 more seconds until the sauce thickens, then turn off the heat and serve.
Garnish with chopped green onions to finish.
When choosing starch jelly, it is best to use those made from pea starch; if unavailable, sweet potato starch or other varieties will also work.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a Minnan-style main dish featuring soft and chewy rice cakes with the charred aroma of scallion oil—a filling, home-style meal. Made from rice flour, the cakes provide ample starch, while eggs and green vegetables add protein and vitamins for balanced nutrition. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 30 minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 1 person.
Rice cakes 250 g * x number of servings
Green onions 2 stalks * x number of servings
Salt 1-2g * x number of servings, to taste.
cac_buoc: Bring water to a boil in a pot and cook the rice cakes until tender. Place them in a bowl of water to prevent sticking, then drain and set aside.
Finely chop the green onions (separating the white parts from the green leaves); cut the green vegetables into small sections and set aside.
(Optional) Prepare scrambled eggs; refer to the Tomato Scrambled Eggs recipe.
Heat a pan and add 30ml of cooking oil.
Add the white parts of the green onions to the pan; once they turn golden brown and fragrant, pour out the scallion oil and set aside.
Reheat the pan and add 20ml of cooking oil.
Add all the side ingredients (eggs, green vegetables, etc.) and stir-fry evenly.
Drain the rice cakes and add them to the pan.
Add the soy sauce and salt, then stir-fry well.
Turn off the heat, add the reserved scallion oil, stir-fry to combine, and serve.
Side ingredients can be added according to personal preference, such as lean meat.
When boiling the rice cakes, remember to stir them to prevent sticking to the pot.

mon_an.mo_ta: This stir-fried spaghetti is tender and refreshing, combining fatty beef slices with a rich, savory sauce for a Western-style family main dish. Rich in starch and protein, it provides a quick energy boost. The recipe is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 30 minutes in total.
cac_buoc: Add 250g water / person.

Wait for the water to boil, add the pasta, and cook over medium heat for 15 - 20 minutes (this type of pasta is usually quite firm; it's best to taste it before draining—if the center is still hard, continue cooking).
Drain the pasta and set aside on a plate.
Heat the pan and add cooking oil. When the oil is medium-hot, add the pasta and stir-fry for one minute (if it's too dry, add a little water).
Add 10g tomato sauce, the fatty beef slices, and 2g salt, then continue to stir-fry for one minute.
Remove from the pan and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: These stir-fried instant noodles are chewy, savory, and flavorful—a quick family main dish that improves upon traditional noodle cooking. Combined with eggs and sausages, it provides a rich source of protein and energy. The method is simple; just pay attention to rinsing the noodles with cold water to maintain their chewiness. It's easy for beginners and takes about 15 minutes to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Calculate the ingredient ratios based on the above conditions.
cac_buoc: Prep the sausages.
Unwrap the sausages and cut into small 1cm wide pieces. Prep the noodles.
Add 1200 ml of water to the pot; in practice, just enough to submerge the noodle block. Bring to a full boil; do not add the noodles before the water boils.
Add the instant noodle block and cook for 45 seconds. Use chopsticks to loosen the noodles while cooking.
Once the noodles are loosened, turn off the heat immediately. Do not overcook!
Scoop out 80ml of the hot noodle water and set aside.
Drain the noodles and rinse under cold water.
Drain the noodles well. Do not soak them in water for long. Prep the seasoning.

Prepare a small bowl and squeeze in the instant noodle seasoning packets. Add the entire dried vegetable packet. Add the entire sauce packet. Add 50% - 80% of the powder packet (adding the whole powder packet will be very salty).
Pour the 80ml of hot noodle water from the previous step into the small bowl and stir well to make the seasoning sauce. Prep the eggs.
Take the calculated number of eggs and crack them into a small bowl. Do not add salt! (The eggs will eventually absorb the salt from the other ingredients in the pan).
Heat the pan for 20s, then add x number of servings * 8ml oil.
Add the prepared eggs. Stir-fry for about 20s until the eggs are set.
Remove the fried eggs and set aside. No need to wash the pan, though there usually won't be much oil left. Final step.
Reheat the pan for 20s, then add oil: x number of servings * 10ml.
Add the sausages prepared in step one. Stir-fry for 10 seconds.
Add the noodles from step two. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the seasoning sauce from step three. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add the fried eggs from step four. Stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve on a plate.
In Beijing, you might consider adding sesame sauce after plating. If the sesame sauce is too thick, dilute it with water at a 1:1 ratio.

You must rinse the noodles with cold water! Cold water immediately removes the gelatinized starch from the surface and stops the residual heat from cooking the inside. This is the core principle to ensure the noodles don't clump, don't stick to the pan, and stay chewy.
Another way to prep the noodles that also keeps them chewy. This extends the prep time, allowing you to prepare other side ingredients simultaneously:
Wash the noodles: soak the instant noodle block in cold water for 2 minutes until sufficiently hydrated, then drain (do not soak until soft).
Steam: place the wet noodle block in a steamer. Once the water boils, steam on high heat for 8 minutes. Remove and loosen the strands to set aside (steaming retains moisture and ensures chewiness).

mon_an.mo_ta: Dry Stir-fried Phở (Chow Fun) is a classic Cantonese snack known for its strong "wok hei," dry yet smooth texture, and soft, translucent, chewy noodles. Combined with shredded meat, bean sprouts, and shredded cucumber, it offers a rich variety of textures. It primarily provides carbohydrates and protein, while the added vegetables provide vitamins and fiber. This recipe is of medium difficulty; beginners can succeed by preparing all ingredients in advance. The entire process takes about 30 minutes from start to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Phở noodles: 250g per person (if a larger portion is needed, add 100g per person and round down).
Shredded cucumber: 30g per person; wheat gluten (mian jin): 30g per person; mung bean sprouts: 30g per person; beaten egg: 1 per person.
Smashed garlic: 2 cloves per person; green onion: 1 stalk per person.
Phở seasoning: 20g per person (or prepare your own stir-fry seasoning with 10g salt + 2g MSG + 3g cumin powder).
Dark soy sauce / Light soy sauce: 10ml / 15ml respectively for every 250g of phở noodles.
cac_buoc: Preparation
Finely chop the green onions (separate the white and green parts), smash the garlic, and set aside on the cutting board.
Whisk the eggs; take a small amount of egg white into one bowl and keep the rest in another bowl for later use.
Place the mung bean sprouts in a pot and cook over high heat for 60 seconds. Remove the sprouts, rinse with cold water, and set aside on a plate.
Cut the cucumber into shreds and set aside on a plate; you can place them with the bean sprouts.
Prepare the wheat gluten and place it on a separate plate.
Cut the meat into small strips; add the starch, the reserved egg white, and black pepper. Stir well in a clockwise direction.
Note: Store-bought liangpi often has oil on the surface; you can rinse it with tap water. Do the same for the wheat gluten.
Note: After rinsing the wheat gluten, use your hands to squeeze out most of the water (do not use excessive force). Heat the pan to stir-fry the meat.
Add cooking oil; once the pan is hot, pour the oil out.
Add the prepared meat and stir-fry until it changes color, then remove to a bowl and set aside. Stir-frying the phở
While the pan is still hot, add 20g of cooking oil (those with high blood pressure can reduce this amount), then add the white parts of the green onions and the garlic. Sauté until fragrant.
Add the phở noodles, drizzle with dark soy sauce for color, stir well, then add the stir-fry seasoning and continue to stir-fry.
When the phở noodles are nearly translucent, add the stir-fried meat strips and the wheat gluten. Add light soy sauce to enhance the flavor and stir-fry briefly twice.
Add the bean sprouts and shredded cucumber; stir-fry until the phở noodles are completely translucent.
Turn off the heat! Final step
Sprinkle with green onion leaves for garnish and lift the pan.
Transfer to a plate and enjoy your meal.
Personal tastes vary by region, weather, and time; please adjust the specific amount of seasoning to your preference. Chili can be added if desired.

mon_an.mo_ta: Chao Mo is a savory, fragrant, and crispy Northern Chinese home-style flour dish. Diced mantou (steamed buns) are stir-fried until golden brown—crispy on the outside and soft on the inside—with cumin and five-spice powder making the flavor even richer. It can be combined with eggs for protein and green onions for a fresh aroma and balanced nutrition. The difficulty is moderate, making it easy for beginners to master. It takes about 15 minutes to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Mantou (steamed buns): 2 pieces (day-old buns that are slightly firm work best)
Oil: 20ml (peanut oil or sesame oil is preferred)
Use the above proportions to calculate the ingredients you intend to use.
cac_buoc: Cut the mantou into small cubes or thin slices.
If using eggs, crack them into a bowl and whisk (you can add 1g each of salt and five-spice powder, or omit them and add during stir-frying).
Drizzle the egg over the mantou and toss to coat evenly; do not use too much egg.
Heat the pan over high heat and add cooking oil (if using a stainless steel pan and worried about sticking, you can add the oil first and heat until the oil is hot).
Add the diced mantou and stir-fry, tossing evenly.
Reduce to low heat and stir-fry until the mantou cubes are golden brown.
Add the salt, pepper, and five-spice powder.
Finally, add the chopped green onions and stir-fry a few more times.
Turn off the heat and serve.
During stir-frying, pay attention to heat control to avoid burning.
How to fix high heat: reduce the heat, add a little more oil, or drizzle a bit of water along the sides of the pan—be careful not to pour it all in one spot; it's best to scatter it.
Seasonings can be adjusted to your preference (e.g., Southern German seasoning).
If you like it extra crispy, you can use the lowest heat, stir-fry a bit longer, turn off the heat, and let it sit in the hot pan for a moment before serving.
Optional ingredients like minced garlic or green garlic can be added; sauté them separately before mixing in.

mon_an.mo_ta: Zha Jiang Mian is a traditional Beijing home-style noodle dish with a rich bean paste aroma, chewy noodles, and refreshing vegetable garnishes that balance the savory and sweet flavors. Nutrition primarily comes from the protein in the lean meat and vitamins from the vegetables, providing ample energy. The method is beginner-friendly; the estimated cooking time is about 30 minutes. Once mastered, the time can be shortened by preparing the vegetables and frying the sauce simultaneously.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Before starting, determine how many servings you intend to make. One serving is enough for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Shred the vegetable garnishes and set aside.
Finely chop the green onions. Heat oil in a pan, add the onions and meat, and stir-fry until the meat is fully cooked (no longer red).
Add the doubanjiang and sweet bean sauce; continue stir-frying until the mixture is **slightly thickened**. Scoop it out to get the *fried sauce*.
Prepare a large bowl of cold water and set aside.
Boil the noodles until cooked through (no white core remaining), then transfer them into the bowl of cold water from step 4.
Immediately drain the noodles and place them in a clean bowl.
Take the fried sauce from step 3 and pour it over the noodles; mix well. Then take the vegetable garnishes from step 1, add them to the bowl, and mix well.
Lean diced meat is recommended for better texture; it is best to buy and use it fresh.
*Fresh noodles* are recommended for this dish.
The key to delicious noodles is the chewiness. Do not choose very thin noodles like dragon beard noodles.
If you have the equipment (another pan) and are proficient, steps 2-3 and 1, 4, 5, 6 can be done simultaneously to save time.
The balance of salty and sweet depends on personal preference; you should experiment to find your optimal ratio of the two sauces.

mon_an.mo_ta: This home-style pan-fried flatbread features distinct layers with a crispy exterior and soft interior, boasting the toasted aroma of flour and oil. It is a staple on Northern Chinese dining tables, primarily providing carbohydrates and energy. While it requires some technique—especially when rolling the oil roux and shaping the dough—following these steps makes it accessible even for beginners. The process takes about 1 hour from kneading to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Note: This recipe is optimized for beginners and does not provide scaled versions.
cac_buoc: Place 400g of flour in a bowl. Use cold water to knead one half and hot water for the other half. Stir into flakes, then knead by hand into a smooth dough. Cover with plastic wrap and let it rest for 40 minutes.
With 10 minutes of resting time left, prepare the oil roux (refer to tips; a warm oil roux works best).
Do not knead the rested dough. Press it down lightly and cut it into four equal portions using one horizontal and one vertical cut.
Roll each portion into a ball, then flatten and roll into a circle roughly the size of your electric griddle. Take 1/4 of the oil roux and spread it evenly over the surface.
Make a cut from the center to the edge (the radius). Roll the dough from one edge into a cone shape, then pinch the bottom of the cone tightly to prevent the oil roux from leaking.
Press down on the tip of the cone to flatten it, then roll it out again into a circle roughly the size of the electric griddle (about 3mm thick).
Preheat the electric griddle and brush with oil. Place the flatbread in the pan, brush a little more oil on top to seal in moisture, and cover with the lid.
Sear on high heat for one minute, open the lid, flip the bread, and cook for another minute.
Repeat the process for the remaining portions and serve.

mon_an.mo_ta: Sesame flatbread is a well-known flour-based snack from Northern China. The exterior is coated in fragrant, crispy sesame seeds, while the inside is layered and fluffy. The flour provides carbohydrates, while the sesame seeds are rich in calcium and unsaturated fatty acids. Although the process involves kneading and making an oil roux, the steps are straightforward enough for beginners. It takes about 40 minutes from preparation to serving.
cac_buoc: Dough: Combine 300g flour, 3g dry yeast, 3g white sugar, 180g warm water, and 20g cooking oil. Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Oil roux: In a small bowl, mix 30g flour, 2g salt, 4g thirteen-spice powder, and 20g cooking oil. Set aside.

Shaping: Roll the dough into a rectangle and spread the prepared oil roux over it. Roll it up from one end and cut into 7 pieces. Fold each piece in half, use the space between your thumb and index finger to shape it into a ball, dip in water, then coat in white sesame seeds. Roll into small, round flatbreads.

Cooking: Preheat the electric griddle and add enough oil to coat the bottom. Place the flatbreads in the pan, brush a little oil on top, spread evenly, and cover. Select the 'large pancake' setting; remove from the pan when you hear the 'ding'.
If an electric griddle is unavailable, a flat frying pan can be used.
If you don't have sesame seeds, you can omit them; the bread will still be delicious.

mon_an.ten: Wuhan Hot Dry Noodles (Re Gan Mian)
mon_an.mo_ta: Hot Dry Noodles is one of the most iconic snacks of Wuhan, belonging to Hubei cuisine. The alkaline noodles are chewy and smooth, coated in a thick sesame sauce and topped with pickled long beans, dried radish, and minced meat for a savory, fragrant, and slightly spicy flavor. This dish provides carbohydrates and protein, and the sesame sauce is rich in calcium. It is quick and easy to make, taking only about 15 minutes from boiling the noodles to mixing.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Special alkaline noodles for Hot Dry Noodles (250g)
cac_buoc: Bring water to a boil, add the alkaline noodles, blanch for 25 seconds, then drain.
Sprinkle with salt, chicken bouillon powder, and pepper powder.
Dilute the sesame paste with 90ml of water, stir well, and pour over the noodles.
Add 5ml of soy sauce, 30ml of meat broth, and the garlic water.
Top with dried radish, minced meat, pickled long beans, and chopped scallions.
Mix thoroughly and serve immediately.
Add chili oil to taste.

mon_an.mo_ta: This Chicken Teriyaki Rice Bowl is a satisfying sweet and savory meal. The chicken thighs are pan-seared until fragrant and then simmered in a rich sauce until tender and flavorful. Chicken thighs provide high-quality protein, while broccoli and carrots add fiber and vitamins. While deboning the chicken requires a bit of technique, the overall process is simple enough for beginners. It takes about 30 minutes from prep to table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 1-2 people.
Honey 15ml (substitute: 20g white sugar + 5g cornstarch + 0.5ml lemon juice or vinegar)
cac_buoc: Place a chicken thigh skin-side down on the cutting board.
Use the tip of a knife to gently slice along the thigh bone from one end to the other.
Use your fingers or the back of the knife to slowly push the meat away from the bone. If you encounter tendons, cut them with the tip of the knife.
Once the meat is completely detached, hold one end of the bone, gently twist, and pull it out.
Repeat the steps to debone all chicken thighs.
Marinate the deboned chicken with black pepper powder, coarse black pepper, salt, and ginger slices for 5 minutes.
In a bowl, mix the cooking wine, light soy sauce, honey, dark soy sauce, and water.
Blanch the vegetables for 1-2 minutes until cooked, then set aside.
Heat 15ml of oil in a pan and sauté the smashed garlic until fragrant.
Place the chicken in the pan and fry over medium-low heat until both sides are golden brown. If the pan is too dry, add another 5-10ml of oil.
Pour in the prepared sauce, cover, and simmer over medium-low heat for 5-10 minutes until cooked through and the sauce has thickened and is bubbling.
Slice the chicken, arrange it on the rice with the vegetables, and drizzle the remaining sauce from the pan over the top.
If using the sugar and starch substitute, ensure they are completely dissolved before adding to the pan to prevent burning.
Stir every 3-5 minutes while simmering to prevent hot spots.
If the sauce bubbles vigorously, turns dark brown, or small caramel crystals appear at the edges, turn off the heat immediately.

mon_an.mo_ta: Instant noodles with egg is a quick and convenient meal that is smooth and savory, perfect for a fast fill-up anytime. It provides carbohydrates and protein for a quick energy boost. The method is extremely simple: boil water, cook the noodles, and drop in an egg. Even beginners can master this in about 10 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One serving can keep an adult full for about 3 to 4 hours.
Water 550ml-1000ml, depending on your pot. Use enough to fully submerge the noodles.
cac_buoc: First, bring the water to a boil (any heat level is fine; using hot water is faster).
Add the noodle block to the pot.
Add the seasoning packets included with the noodles.
Gently stir the noodles with chopsticks to dissolve the seasoning and ensure the noodles are fully submerged and heated.
Cover and wait about 1 minute until the water returns to a boil.
Crack the egg and add it to the pot.
Wait about 3 to 4 minutes until done.
The egg in this guide can be poached directly, or you can use a pre-boiled or soy-marinated egg.
Instant noodles can be purchased at any local convenience store.
Feel free to add other ingredients according to your preference, such as sausages, lettuce, shredded meat, spicy strips, dried fish, peeled shrimp, or chicken drumsticks.

mon_an.mo_ta: This simple, comforting Southern-style family dish features rice grains coated in melted lard, accented by the savory freshness of soy sauce and the delicate aroma of scallions. It is a reliable favorite for children who are picky eaters. It primarily provides quick carbohydrates and energy from fats, but is quite high in cholesterol and should not be eaten frequently. With no barriers to making it, even those who cannot cook at all can easily complete it; pre-cooked rice takes only a few minutes to mix into a fragrant main dish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Lard 15 g (reduce to 10 g if adding oyster sauce)
Light soy sauce 5 ml (reduce to 3 ml if adding oyster sauce)
Finely chopped scallions 0-12 g (5 g recommended initially)
cac_buoc: Spread the lard at the bottom of the bowl
Add the rice
Drizzle with soy sauce and oyster sauce
Sprinkle with chopped scallions and pork cracklings
Mix well
Recommended to serve with lean meat and vegetables for balanced nutrition
High in cholesterol; not recommended for frequent consumption

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a home-style dish combining Japanese steamed rice techniques. The rice is infused with the rich flavors of beef fat and salmon, resulting in a savory and fresh taste. Salmon provides high-quality protein and unsaturated fatty acids, while mushrooms add fiber. The process is extremely simple—just press a button on the rice cooker. It takes about 45 minutes from preparation to serving, making it perfect for beginners.
cac_buoc: Scale and debone the salmon
Finely chop the enoki and shiitake mushrooms
Wash the rice three times
Place the salmon, rice, and beef fat into the rice cooker
For a richer flavor, you can add an extra tablespoon of beef fat
Add water according to the rice cooker's scale
Set the rice cooker to the rice cooking mode and wait for 30 - 45 minutes

mon_an.mo_ta: This Japanese-style teriyaki chicken rice features a rich sweet and savory sauce, a slightly charred and crispy exterior, and a tender, juicy interior that pairs perfectly with rice. The chicken and eggs provide plenty of high-quality protein, though the amount of soy sauce and sugar is relatively high, making it suitable for an occasional treat. The method is simple: just mix the ingredients and let the air fryer do the work. It's easy for beginners and takes about 1 hour from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Ritz crackers (or other savory crackers) 16 pieces (48g)
cac_buoc: Mix the soy sauce, sugar, and vinegar together; stir well to make a sauce and set aside
In another bowl, combine the chicken, eggs, 1/2 of the sauce, and crushed Ritz crackers. Stir well
Line the air fryer with a foil bowl, add the meat mixture, and drizzle the remaining sauce evenly over the top
Air fry at **350°F (177°C)** for **40 minutes**. Best served with rice
When the exterior is *golden and crispy*, remove from the fryer, slice, and serve on a plate
For rice cooking, refer to Rice Cooker Steamed Rice or Stovetop Steamed Rice
Pay attention to the temperature while cooking to avoid burns.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a simple home-style staple; you can make soft, perfectly textured rice using just a regular pot. White rice primarily provides carbohydrates, quickly replenishing the body's energy. The method is extremely simple—beginners just need to monitor the heat throughout the process. It takes about 25 minutes from adding the rice to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Water: 2 times the volume of rice
cac_buoc: Wash the rice
Add the rice and water to the pot
Cook over high heat until the water boils
**Stir the bottom of the pot to prevent sticking**
Cover with a lid, turn to **low heat**, and simmer for 10-15 minutes (depending on preferred softness); do not open the lid during this time
Turn off the heat and let it sit for 5 minutes
Enjoy :)

mon_an.mo_ta: A basic staple everyone knows, featuring a pure rice aroma and a soft, chewy texture that can be adjusted to be firmer or moister by varying the water amount. Rich in starch, it provides quick energy and is suitable to accompany all kinds of dishes. The operation is extremely simple and easy for beginners; it takes about forty minutes from washing the rice to finishing the steaming process.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Typically, one person eats 100ml-200ml of rice.
The finger joint method (a precise way to determine rice-to-water ratio)
For long-grain rice: Add rice and water to the cooker; when your index finger touches the rice, the water should reach the first joint and 1/4 of the second joint (about 2.6 cm).
For short-grain rice: Add rice and water to the cooker; when your index finger touches the rice, the water should reach the first joint (about 2 cm).
Calculate the ingredient proportions based on the above conditions.
cac_buoc: Wash the rice
Add the rice and water to the rice cooker.
Plug in the rice cooker and start the cooking mode. Wait about 30 minutes.
Wait for the rice cooker to automatically switch to keep-warm mode.
Let the rice steam in the cooker for 10-15 minutes.
Fluff and serve the rice.
Technical Summary
Regardless of the container, the "finger joint method" can be used to cook delicious rice.
The amount of water can significantly affect the quality of a bowl of rice.
Long-grain rice is common in the South, while short-grain rice is common in the North; long-grain is slender, while short-grain is short and round.
Different rice varieties and water amounts will greatly impact the taste.
For more information, please refer to the user manual of your specific rice cooker.

mon_an.mo_ta: This North Indian home-style dish is a traditional staple of Punjab and Delhi. It features a rich, spicy tomato-onion sauce with red kidney beans simmered until soft and flavorful, served over warm rice for a filling meal. The beans are rich in protein, fiber, and micronutrients, offering balanced nutrition. The method is simple and beginner-friendly, taking about 40 minutes to cook, though dried beans require an 8-hour soak. It has a deep, comforting home-cooked flavor.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion serves 2-3 people.
Dried red kidney beans 200g (soaked for 8 hours)
cac_buoc: Preparation (8 hours prior)
Soak the dried red kidney beans in clean water for at least 8 hours (overnight); they will double in volume. Cook the beans
Drain the soaked beans

**Using a pressure cooker**: Add the beans and 600ml water, cover, and bring to high heat until pressurized. Reduce to medium heat and **pressure cook for 15-20 minutes** until the *beans can be easily mashed with a finger*
**Using a regular pot**: Add the beans and enough water, bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and **cook for 60-90 minutes** until the beans are completely soft
Once cooked, keep the cooking water and set aside. Sauté the curry
Heat 30ml of oil in a pan over medium heat
Add 2 bay leaves and fry until *fragrant* (about 10 seconds)
Add the chopped onions and sauté until *golden brown* (about 6-8 minutes)
Add the grated ginger and garlic, sauté for 1 minute
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until *completely softened and the oil separates* (about 5 minutes)
Add 3g turmeric, 5g red chili powder, 5g coriander powder, 3g cumin powder, and 6g salt
Sauté for 2 minutes to let the spices blend with the tomatoes
Pour the cooked beans and their cooking water into the pan
Add the green chili and stir well
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and **simmer for 15-20 minutes**
Meanwhile, use the back of a spatula to mash some of the beans to make the sauce *thick and creamy*
Add 3g garam masala and stir well
Turn off the heat and sprinkle with cilantro. Cook the rice
Wash the rice
Place in a rice cooker with 400ml water
Cook as usual. Serving
Serve the rice on a plate
Pour the kidney bean curry over or next to the rice
Can be served with an onion salad and lemon wedges
Red kidney beans must be thoroughly cooked before eating; undercooked beans contain phytohaemagglutinin (lectin), which can cause food poisoning.
In India, Rajma Chawal is considered the ultimate comfort food, similar in status to "braised pork over rice" in China.
For a richer taste, you can add 30ml of light cream.
Leftover kidney bean curry can be stored in the refrigerator for 3-4 days; the flavor often improves.

mon_an.ten: Old Friend Pork Rice Noodles (Lao You Fen)
mon_an.mo_ta: Old Friend pork rice noodles are sour, spicy, fresh, and fragrant. The smooth noodles carry the distinct, bold flavors of fermented black beans and sour bamboo shoots, a signature taste of Nanning. The pork provides high-quality protein, while the noodles offer quick energy. The overall difficulty is medium; pay attention to soaking the noodles beforehand. Once mastered, it takes about forty minutes to bring to the table.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Rice noodles (250g, remember to soak in 50°C warm water for 30 minutes)
Minced chili (15g after mincing, adjust to personal preference)
cac_buoc: Place all the pork in a bowl and season with cooking wine, salt, light soy sauce, starch, and pepper; set aside
Heat a dry pan (no oil), add all the sour bamboo shoots and stir-fry until the water evaporates, leaving a space in the center of the shoots
Add 10ml - 15ml of oil and all the garlic, minced chili, and fermented black beans into the center; stir-fry until fragrant
Add all the seasoned pork and another 10ml of light soy sauce; stir-fry for one minute
Add 5ml rice vinegar, 10ml light soy sauce, and 450ml water; bring to a boil
Once the water boils, add the soaked noodles and cook for another 3 minutes before transferring to a bowl
Remember, the noodles must be soaked to be delicious; if not soaked, the texture will be poor!

mon_an.mo_ta: A quick, spicy, and appetizing home-style noodle dish. The chewy noodles are coated in the spicy fermented black bean flavor of Lao Gan Ma sauce, with soy sauce enhancing the savory depth. Simple yet bold. As a main dish, it quickly replenishes carbohydrates and energy, while the capsaicin in the chili helps stimulate the appetite. With no barriers to entry, beginners can easily master it; it takes only about ten minutes from boiling water to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One serving is enough for 1 person.
Lao Gan Ma sauce 15ml * number of servings
cac_buoc: Bring water to a boil in a pot
Add the noodles evenly to the pot
Stir while cooking to prevent the noodles from sticking together
When you can lift a noodle with chopsticks and it slides off naturally, wait another 30 seconds then turn off the heat
Transfer the noodles to a bowl
Add the measured Lao Gan Ma and soy sauce
Use chopsticks to mix the noodles, Lao Gan Ma, and soy sauce thoroughly in the bowl
Serve

mon_an.mo_ta: This dish features a rich savory sauce, a perfect balance of salty and sweet, fragrant seared minced meat, and silky eggs. Served over hot rice, it is a very satisfying and quick home-style meal. Rich in high-quality protein and essential amino acids, it provides a quick energy boost. The method is simple and direct, easy for beginners, taking only about fifteen minutes from prep to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: One portion is for one person; for more people, increase proportionally but consider the pan's capacity.
cac_buoc: Cook the rice; typically use the measuring cup provided with the rice, one cup is 240g
Add 30ml of oil to the pan
Add the minced meat and pan-sear over medium heat until both sides are slightly charred
Crack the eggs into the pan (do not beat them) and cover with a lid
