Prepare the sauce: combine the dark soy sauce, light soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, and fried shallot oil in a bowl and stir well
Open the lid, pour the sauce into the pan, and wait for three minutes
Turn off the heat and slide the meat and eggs over the rice
Check for safety and enjoy your rice bowl
If you prefer a sweeter taste, increase the sugar by 10g
Please remember to turn off the gas appliance after cooking to avoid danger

mon_an.mo_ta: This home-style fried cake combines the savory flavor of cured pork (lap cheong/bacon) with the tenderness of eggplant. Crispy on the outside and soft on the inside, it is a rustic rice-flour-based staple. Rich in starch and high-quality protein, the eggplant also provides fiber and vitamins, creating a balanced meat-and-vegetable dish. The difficulty is medium, requiring control over the batter consistency and frying heat, but beginners can succeed by following the steps. Takes about 30 minutes from prep to serving.
cac_buoc: Peel and slice the eggplant, slice the cured pork, and set aside
In a bowl, combine 250g rice flour, 50g all-purpose flour, and 1 egg

While stirring with chopsticks, gradually add water (**water is used to adjust consistency**) until the batter can coat the eggplant and meat slices without falling off. Stop adding water, then add all slices to the batter and coat them thoroughly
Add **10-30ml** of oil to a flat pan and turn on low heat

Use chopsticks or a spoon to place the coated eggplant and meat slices into the pan. Fry until both sides are golden, then continue frying for **3-6 minutes** (**add more oil if the pan becomes dry during frying**)
Sprinkle with salt, toss evenly, and remove from the pan to serve
Use low heat for frying

mon_an.ten: Scallion Oil Noodles (Cong You Ban Mian)
mon_an.mo_ta: Scallion oil noodles are a classic Shanghai home-style dish, famous for their unique scallion aroma and quick, simple preparation. Rich in starch and healthy fats, they provide a quick energy boost. Beginners can usually finish this in 20 minutes, making it an ideal daily quick dinner.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The scallion oil sauce can be made in large batches and used over time. Below is the base amount for the sauce and the amount needed per serving of noodles.
Base scallion oil sauce (enough for 3-4 servings):
Dried noodles 80 g (equivalent to about 150 g fresh noodles)
cac_buoc: Prepare the scallion oil sauce
Wash the scallions and cut them into sections (about 5-7 cm). Separate the white stalks from the green leaves.
Pour 100 ml of cooking oil into a pan and heat over medium heat. Add the white scallion stalks first and fry until slightly golden.
Add the green scallion leaves, turn the heat to low, and continue to fry.
Keep the heat low and patiently fry for **15-20 minutes** until the scallions turn golden brown and crispy.
Remove the browned scallions (keep the scallion oil in the pan).

Add 60 ml light soy sauce, 20 ml dark soy sauce, and 15 g white sugar to the scallion oil in the pan. Stir over low heat for about **1 minute** until the sugar dissolves and the sauce is well combined. Turn off the heat immediately. Pour the prepared scallion oil sauce into a container, let it cool, and seal for storage. Cook the noodles (per serving)
Take 80 g of dried noodles.
Pour 1000 ml of water into a pot and bring to a boil over high heat.
Add the noodles and cook according to the package instructions (usually **3-8 minutes**; follow the package guide).
Remove the cooked noodles, drain well, and place in a bowl. Mix the noodles (per serving)
Add 15 ml of the prepared scallion oil sauce to the bowl of noodles.
You can add the previously fried scallion sections (optional).
Quickly toss with chopsticks until evenly coated and serve.
When frying the scallion oil, the heat must be low and you must be patient to fully extract the scallion aroma.
The prepared scallion oil sauce can be refrigerated for a period; simply use it directly the next time you have noodles.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is a classic home-style noodle dish from Southern Henan (Yunan), featuring a balanced combination of meat and vegetables. The noodles fully absorb the savory sauce, resulting in a soft yet chewy texture. Pork belly provides quality protein and fat, while celery is rich in fiber. The method is simple to learn even for beginners, taking about one hour in total.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients
Remove the skin from the pork and cut into thin slices `2 cm * 6 cm * 0.5 cm`, then set aside.
Remove the celery leaves, trim 2cm off the base, split down the middle, and cut into 2cm sections; set aside.
Peel and mince the garlic; slice the scallion into 0.2cm thin rounds; julienne the ginger. Have everything ready.
Heat a wok until smoking, swirl with 3ml of oil to coat, then pour out the excess.
Add fresh oil, then add the pork slices, scallion, ginger, garlic, and dried red chilies. Stir-fry for 1 minute, making sure to stir constantly.
Add cooking wine, light soy sauce, and dark soy sauce, then stir-fry for another 1 minute.
Add 500ml of hot water. Cover and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the celery and green chilies to the pan, season with salt and five-spice powder, cover and continue to simmer for 3 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Pour 1000ml of water into a steamer and bring to a boil. Spread the noodles evenly in the steamer basket, place in the pot, and steam for 15 minutes.
Remove the steamed noodles, use chopsticks and your hands to fluff them up on a cutting board, and let them cool at room temperature. Final processing
Add the noodles to the pan with the vegetables and sauce. Mix by using chopsticks in one hand and a spatula in the other to fold the vegetables over the noodles until the noodles are evenly colored.
Place the mixed noodles back into the steamer basket and steam one more time for 10 minutes, then turn off the heat.
Technical Summary
You can ask the butcher to slice the pork for you.
For your first time, prepare all ingredients beforehand to avoid rushing; once proficient, you can multitask.
Try to fluff the noodles during both steaming stages to prevent them from clumping. If the noodles are too long, you can break them for easier mixing and serving.
When removing the steamed noodles, be gentle to avoid tipping the basket and getting the noodles wet.
This dish pairs perfectly with beer!

mon_an.mo_ta: A classic Japanese home-style dish featuring a smooth, soft egg omelet wrapping tomato-sauce fried rice. It has a rich texture and an appetizing sweet and sour flavor. High in protein, starch, and various vitamins for balanced nutrition. Wrapping the omelet requires some technique, but the overall difficulty is moderate. It takes about 25 minutes from prep to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is suitable for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Finely dice the onion, carrot, and sausage or chicken breast; set aside.
Heat the pan, add 10ml of oil, and wait 10 seconds for it to get hot.
First, add the diced onion and sauté for 1 minute. Once fragrant, add the carrots, corn, and peas and continue to sauté for 2 minutes.
Add the diced sausage or chicken breast and stir-fry until the color changes.
Add the rice and stir-fry until the grains are separate, then add 20ml of ketchup. Mix well until the fried rice is finished, then remove and set aside.
Whisk the eggs and stir in 10ml of milk until well combined.
Add 5ml of oil to the pan, pour in the egg mixture, and gently swirl the pan to spread the egg evenly across the surface.
Cook over low heat. When the surface of the egg is half-cooked, place the fried rice in the center of the egg.
Use a spatula to fold the edges of the omelet over the rice, creating an oval shape.
Gently slide it onto a plate, adjust the shape, and squeeze a bit of ketchup on top for decoration.
Using overnight rice for fried rice prevents it from sticking to the pan and makes it tastier.
Adding milk to the eggs makes the omelet softer and smoother.
Keep the heat low when working with the egg to avoid burning the bottom.
If you are not confident in wrapping the rice, you can also spread the fried rice on a plate and simply drape the omelet over it.

mon_an.mo_ta: A home-style egg fried rice where golden egg strands coat separate grains of rice, combined with ham, carrots, and cucumber for a rich, savory texture. Eggs provide quality protein, carrots add vitamins, and the starch provides plenty of energy. While there are several steps, beginners can succeed by following the process. The entire process takes about 25 minutes.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 1-2 people.
Salt (number of servings * 4g - number of servings * 6g)
Calculate the ingredient proportions based on the conditions above.
cac_buoc: Use a spatula to break the rice into small clumps first.
Slice or dice the ham, carrots, cucumber, etc., as desired.
If you have pre-cooked meat at home, it will enhance the flavor.
Separate the egg whites and yolks into two large bowls and whisk each separately. Note: do not add salt at this stage.
Heat the wok over high heat. When it starts to smoke, add oil and pour in the egg whites. Once the main part has set, remove and set aside.
If there is enough oil, add the yolks directly; if not, add more oil and wait for it to heat up over high heat.
Once the yolks have set, turn the heat to medium-low. Add the ham, cooked meat, carrots, cucumber, and other prepared ingredients. Sauté for 10 seconds (until fragrant).
Add the egg whites back in, sauté for 5 seconds, then quickly add the rice and stir-fry over high heat so that every grain is coated with egg.
Break up any rice clumps while stir-frying. This step takes some time; continue until all the rice is separated and evenly mixed.
Turn the heat to low and add salt, pepper powder, and light soy sauce.
Continue to stir-fry evenly. When you see some rice grains "jumping" in the pan, it is almost done.
Finally, add the scallions and stir-fry for another 10 seconds.
Turn off the heat and serve in a bowl.
Technical Summary
Using overnight cold rice is best. If you don't have any, you can cook fresh rice (and cool it immediately in the fridge), but you will need to stir-fry longer to achieve separate grains.
The key to "separate grains" is stir-frying the rice until dry. Overnight rice is preferred because it has already lost some moisture.

mon_an.mo_ta: Luosifen is a specialty snack from Liuzhou, Guangxi, featuring a fresh, bold broth that is refreshingly sour and spicy, with soft yet chewy rice noodles. The flavor profile combines the fresh sweetness of snail broth, the unique fermented aroma of sour bamboo shoots, and the kick of chili oil in distinct layers. As a main dish, the noodles provide starch, while the snail meat and ingredients provide protein, and the sour bamboo shoots help stimulate digestion. The preparation is simple: just cook the noodles and add seasonings in order, making it very beginner-friendly. It takes about ten minutes from boiling the water to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Based on personal experience, one bag of instant Luosifen is enough for one person for one meal (even though it looks very large).
cac_buoc: Add water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the rice noodles and cook for 3-5 minutes, stirring with chopsticks to prevent sticking.
Add the broth packet, adjusting the amount to your taste.
Add the first set of ingredient packets, such as wood ear mushrooms, peanuts, and snails (these need to cook for a bit to absorb the flavor).
Add the seasoning packet, adjusting to your taste.
Stir and then remove from the pot into a bowl.
Add the remaining ingredient packets, such as sour bamboo shoots and yuba (these ingredients should not be soaked in the broth for too long).
Enjoy your meal.
If you prefer chewier noodles, shorten the cooking time in step two.
If you want to add a fried egg to your Luosifen, please refer to the fried egg instructions.
Choose additional side ingredients according to your personal preference.

mon_an.mo_ta: Tomato and egg dried noodles are a quick home-style meal that is sweet, sour, savory, and fresh. With a rich sauce and chewy noodles, this is a daily staple with Northern Chinese flavors. Eggs provide quality protein, tomatoes are rich in lycopene and vitamins, and the noodles provide balanced nutrition. The operation is simple with clear steps, making it beginner-friendly. It takes about 20 minutes from prep to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. The following amount is for 1 person.
cac_buoc: Pre-process the ingredients
Pre-processing is very important; no matter what you cook, preparing first prevents rushing, making cooking an enjoyable process.
Wash and finely chop the scallions.
Cut the tomato into chunks; if you are not good at cutting, it is recommended to look up a guide first!
Cut the green chili into diamond-shaped pieces.
Crack the eggs into a small bowl and whisk. If the eggs smell slightly fishy, you can add 2g of white vinegar to deodorize. Pre-cook the eggs
Heat the pan and pour in 15-20g of cooking oil. To make soft, fluffy eggs, you need a bit more oil, while leaving some in the pan for the tomatoes later.
When the oil is about 70% hot (hold your hand 10cm above and feel the heat), pour in the whisked eggs and quickly scramble them.
Once the eggs have set but are still smooth with no liquid left, remove them to a small bowl and set aside. Keep some oil in the pan. Make the tomato and egg sauce
Keep the residual oil in the pan and first sauté the white scallion stalks and minced garlic until fragrant.
Add the tomato chunks and green chili, and wait for the tomatoes to release some juice.
Quickly add 5g of soy sauce and 2g of white sugar.
Sauté for about ten seconds, then add a bowl of fresh water (just enough to almost cover the tomatoes).
After it boils, add the fried eggs and 5g of oyster sauce or 2g of chicken powder to enhance the freshness.

Reduce the sauce over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally to prevent sticking. Once reduced to the desired consistency, add the remaining chopped scallion greens and sesame oil (optional). The sauce is finished. Finally, cook the noodles
You don't need to wash the pan; add 500ml of fresh water directly.
Bring to a boil and add the dried noodles. Once the noodles soften, add 100ml of fresh water.
After it boils again, if the noodles float, add another 100ml of fresh water.
After it boils once more, check if the sides of the noodles are translucent; if so, they are cooked.
Transfer the noodles into the bowl with the sauce and toss to combine.
Adding 2g of black pepper to the whisked eggs makes them tastier.
When simmering the sauce, you can add 2g of white pepper powder to increase the aromatic spice.
You can cook the noodles all at once, but adding water multiple times makes them chewier and prevents sticking. The technique is to add cold water whenever it boils, repeating two or three times.

mon_an.ten: Braised Noodles with Yardlong Beans (Dou Jiao Mian)
mon_an.mo_ta: Braised noodles with yardlong beans is a Northern Chinese home-style dish where the noodles soak up the broth, resulting in a soft, chewy, and savory texture. It features the fresh taste of yardlong beans and the richness of sliced pork. Pork belly provides protein and fat, while yardlong beans are rich in fiber and vitamins. The operation is not difficult but requires attention to the heat and the timing of adding the broth. It is suitable for those with some cooking experience and takes about 30 minutes to serve.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: The following amount is for 1 person for one main meal! Please adjust ingredients according to actual needs!
Calculate the ingredient proportions based on the conditions above.
cac_buoc: Preparation
Cut the yardlong beans into 5cm - 6cm sections.
Cut the scallion into 1cm - 2cm pieces.
Julienne the ginger into 1mm x 1mm x 3cm strips.
Crush the garlic on a cutting board and mince into 1mm pieces.
Slice the pork belly into 2mm thick pieces.
First, heat the pan to evaporate all moisture. Hold your hand 10cm above the bottom and feel the distinct heat.

Add the measured cooking oil. Hold the handle, lift the pan 5cm above the stove, and swirl so the oil coats two-thirds of the pan (from the bottom up). > ps: skip this for non-stick pans; just wait 3-5 seconds for the oil to heat.
Add all the ginger and scallion pieces and sauté for 5 seconds until fragrant (Caution! Risk of oil splashing; gloves or protection recommended).
Add all the pork slices. Do not stir immediately; let them sit for 5 seconds, then toss so all the meat is coated in oil.
Continuously stir-fry the pork slices. Once they have all changed color, drizzle the light soy sauce evenly along the edge of the pan and stir well.
Add the salt, dark soy sauce, oyster sauce, thirteen-spice powder, chicken powder, and all the yardlong beans. Sauté for 2 minutes.
Pour in the prepared hot water.
When the water boils, use a ladle to scoop out half of the broth from the pan (Note! Do not scoop out the vegetables).
Spread all the noodles evenly over the vegetables.
Cover and braise over medium heat for 5 minutes.
Open the lid and use a spoon to drizzle the reserved broth evenly over the noodles, one spoonful at a time.
Cover and braise over medium heat for another 3 minutes.
Open the lid and sprinkle in all the garlic and MSG. > ps: there may still be some water in the pan; turn off the heat if you prefer them wetter, otherwise keep it on.
Use chopsticks to continuously toss and mix the vegetables and meat with the noodles.
Turn off the heat.
Distinguishing noodle thickness
Hair-thin (Mao xi: as the name suggests, like hair; similar to thin vermicelli)
Thin (Xi: slightly thicker than hair-thin, like incense sticks)
Medium-thin (Er xi: similar to regular stir-fry noodles)
Medium-thick (San xi: slightly thicker, like thick rice noodles; very chewy if hand-pulled)
Flat (Leek-leaf: shaped like a flat leek leaf)
Extra wide (Da kuan: like the wide noodles used in spicy hot pot)

mon_an.mo_ta: Mixed buckwheat noodles are a delicious, refreshing, and smooth sweet and sour dish. This is a simple and quick home-style mixed noodle recipe. Buckwheat noodles are rich in fiber and protein, and when combined with cucumber and carrots, they add freshness and vitamins for balanced nutrition. Just cook the noodles, cut the vegetables, and mix with Lao Gan Ma. It is very beginner-friendly and usually takes about 20 minutes. It tastes even better when chilled.
cac_buoc: Add the buckwheat noodles to cold water and cook until done (8-10 minutes), then remove and drain; set aside.
Cut the cucumber and carrot into small matchsticks.
Place the buckwheat noodles, cucumber, and carrot on a plate, top with Lao Gan Ma, and toss.
Buckwheat noodles taste better if refrigerated after draining.
You can choose additional ingredients according to your preference, such as peeled shrimp or minced meat.
You can choose other sauces according to your preference, such as peanut butter or sesame sauce.
The calorie count of buckwheat noodles is nearly the same as other noodles, so they are not necessarily a low-fat staple.

mon_an.ten: Hot and Sour Fern Root Noodles
mon_an.mo_ta: Hot and sour fern root noodles (juegen fen) have a smooth and chewy texture. This appetizing sour and spicy dish is a classic home-style cold appetizer but can also serve as a main dish. Fern root noodles are rich in starch and fiber, providing energy. The method is exceptionally simple and beginner-friendly, taking only 10 minutes from prep to finish.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Soy sauce : Vinegar : Chili oil (You Ba La Zi) = 3 : 2 : 2 (the specific amount of sauce depends on the amount of noodles; this ratio ensures the flavor is correct)
If the sauce tastes too light, you can add 2 to 5 grams of salt.
If you want a fresher taste, you can add 2 grams of sugar.
cac_buoc: Cook the fern root noodles
Fill a pot about 3/5 full with water and bring to a boil.
Once the water boils, add the fern root noodles and cook over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Remove from the pot. Prepare the sauce
Combine the soy sauce, vinegar, and chili oil according to the ratio.
Use a chopstick to dip and taste a bit.
If the soy sauce flavor is too strong, add the prepared salt.
If it is not fresh enough, add the prepared sugar.
Stir thoroughly until most of the granular seasonings have dissolved. Plate and finish
Take a bowl.
Pour the sauce prepared in the previous step into the bowl.
Rinse the fern root noodles under cold water, then add them to the sauce.
Mix thoroughly.
Finely mince the prepared scallion, garlic, and bird's eye chili and sprinkle over the noodles.
All done! (｡･∀･)ﾉﾞ
Scallion, ginger, and garlic are optional aromatics; they add flavor but can be omitted.
Sugar and salt are to taste; adjust the specific amounts as needed.
It is recommended to use a bowl for serving, as eating these noodles from a plate can be difficult.
The overall flavor is spicy; if you cannot eat spicy food, please reduce the chili oil and omit the bird's eye chili.

mon_an.ten: Fermented Rice Soup with Mini Tangyuan
mon_an.mo_ta: Fermented rice soup with mini tangyuan is a traditional Chinese dessert that is sweet, fragrant, soft, and chewy. The slight acidity of the fermented rice blends with the smooth texture of the glutinous rice balls for a comforting, warming treat. Rich in starch and some B vitamins, it provides a quick energy boost and helps promote blood circulation. There are no barriers to making this, making it especially beginner-friendly. It takes only about 15 minutes from boiling the water to serving, making it an easy home-style dessert to prepare anytime.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine how many servings you intend to make before starting. One portion is enough for 1-2 people.
Mini tangyuan (glutinous rice balls) 250 g * number of servings
Fermented rice (laotao) 50 g * number of servings
Goji berries 5 pieces * number of servings
cac_buoc: Add water to the pot and bring to a boil.
Add the mini tangyuan and cook for 8 minutes.
Add the fermented rice and goji berries and cook for another 2 minutes.
Ladle into a bowl, add white sugar to taste, and stir well.
Serve.
The amount of white sugar varies according to personal taste.
If you prefer a thicker texture, you can reduce the water by 100 ml.
If you like softer goji berries, you can cook them at the same time as the mini tangyuan.

mon_an.mo_ta: This traditional Northwest noodle dish is famous for its chewy hand-pulled noodles and the spicy aroma of hot oil sizzled over the top. It is a well-known daily staple in Shaanxi. Rich in starch and combined with green vegetables and bean sprouts, it provides a quick energy boost and a balanced meal. The entire process is simple and beginner-friendly, taking only about 30 minutes from preparation to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Usually 4 noodles for men and 3 for women is enough; adjust for larger appetites
cac_buoc: Prepare the ingredients
If pulling the noodles, use a rolling pin (or your hands if unavailable) to press lightly on the top and bottom edges, hold both ends with your hands, and gently pull them out
Finely chop the green onion and mince the garlic; set aside
Wash the green vegetables and bean sprouts; set aside (if using). Cook the noodles and season
Fill a pot with enough water and bring to a boil over high heat, then add 1g of salt
Add the noodles and stir gently with chopsticks to prevent sticking; cook until the noodles float, then cook for another 1-2 minutes
In the final minute of cooking the noodles, add the green vegetables and bean sprouts to blanch
Remove the cooked noodles, vegetables, and bean sprouts; drain well and place in a bowl
Top the noodles with light soy sauce, aromatic vinegar, chopped green onion, minced garlic, and dried chili flakes; you can also add some sesame seeds. Sizzle the oil
Add cooking oil to a pan and add Sichuan peppercorns, star anise, cinnamon stick, and bay leaves (if using); fry over low heat until fragrant, then remove the spices
Wait until the oil temperature is about 70% hot (slightly smoking), then quickly pour it evenly over the chili flakes in the bowl until you hear a "sizzling" sound
Use chopsticks to toss the noodles with all the seasonings and serve
Technical Summary
Choosing the right chili flakes is crucial; Shaanxi Qin Jiao chili flakes are recommended for their fragrance without being overly spicy
The temperature of the oil is the key to success; if it's too low, the chili won't be fragrant; if it's too high, it will burn easily
Meat lovers can add minced meat to make Oil-Sprinkled Noodles with Meat Sauce
Traditional Shaanxi Oil-Sprinkled Noodles emphasize "one green, two white, three red, four green," referring to the color combination of the noodles, minced garlic, chili, and green onions

mon_an.mo_ta: Bibimbap is a vibrant Korean home-cooked dish with rich textures. A sweet and spicy sauce coats the rice, vegetables, beef, and a sunny-side-up egg. One bite of the well-mixed bowl is incredibly satisfying. Various vegetables provide vitamins and fiber, while beef and eggs add high-quality protein for a balanced meal. It is simple to make, though preparation steps are slightly numerous; beginners can easily complete it in about 45 minutes from prep to table.
cac_buoc: Wash and julienne the vegetables, then stir-fry in a pan until softened and remove
Boil water and blanch the beef slices for about three minutes until just cooked, then remove
Fry the egg sunny-side up
Pack the rice into a small bowl and invert it into a larger serving bowl
Arrange the prepared vegetables and beef slices in a circle around the rice, then place the fried egg in the center

Prepare the sauce: mix 10ml Gochujang (sweet and spicy) + 5ml light soy sauce + two caps of Sprite (use sugar-free Sprite if dieting) + 10g sesame seeds + 5ml sesame oil; stir well and add more light soy sauce or salt if needed
Drizzle the prepared sauce over the arranged bowl
This is a very simple dish; though the process is a bit tedious, it is very satisfying when the vegetables, meat, rice, and sauce are mixed together
For a better presentation, you can use a stone pot instead of a regular bowl

mon_an.ten: Fried Chive Pockets (Jiu Cai He Zi)
mon_an.mo_ta: Fried Chive Pockets are a traditional Chinese pastry with a golden, crispy exterior and a fresh, juicy filling. The combination of chives, shrimp, and eggs is rich in vitamins and high-quality protein. The method is simple and very easy for beginners; it takes about 2.5 hours from kneading the dough to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2 people.
cac_buoc: Place the flour in a large bowl, add water, and stir into a smooth dough; let it rest for 30 minutes.
Wash and finely chop the chives, then add the beaten eggs and 5g of salt; stir well.
Divide the dough into small balls, roll them into thin circles, and wrap the chive, shrimp, and egg mixture inside.
Heat a pan with cooking oil, add the chive pockets, and fry until both sides are golden brown, about 3-4 minutes.
Serve on a plate and let cool slightly before enjoying.
You can add dried tofu or other ingredients according to your taste.
Watch the heat while frying to avoid burning the outside while the inside remains raw.

mon_an.mo_ta: This is an exquisite Jiangnan-style dim sum with paper-thin wrappers and a plump, juicy filling. Upon biting, the flavors of meat, fresh bamboo shoots, and the melted broth from the pork skin jelly (aspic) blend into a savory-sweet, tender, and chewy texture. Pork and shrimp provide high-quality protein, while winter bamboo shoots and shiitake mushrooms add fiber and micronutrients; the low-fat version further reduces saturated fat. Although the wrapping technique requires some patience, the overall steps are clear and can be mastered with practice. It takes about one hour from mixing the filling to serving.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2-3 people.
Shumai wrappers 240-465 g (about 24-31 sheets; 10g per sheet is recommended, 30 sheets)
Ground pork 300 g (for low-fat version, use 280 g pork tenderloin or shoulder)
Salt 3-5 g (reduce by 3 g if using bouillon cubes)
Concentrated bouillon cube 6 g (Knorr brand recommended, about 1/8 cube)
Shiitake mushrooms 75 g (or 30 g dried shiitake, soaked)
cac_buoc: (Low-fat version) Take 10 mL of cold water, add the food-grade thickener, and mix into a paste
(Low-fat version) Add 25 mL of boiling water and stir until it becomes a semi-transparent gel
(Low-fat version) Once cooled, mix with 280 g pure lean ground pork + 15 g melted lard (or chicken fat)
Mix the ground pork with minced ginger and green onion, then add light soy sauce, cooking wine, salt, sugar, and white pepper; stir in one direction until the mixture becomes elastic
If using a bouillon cube, dissolve it in 15 mL of hot water, stir until fully emulsified, then add 15 mL of room temperature water
Slowly add the water or broth while continuing to stir until the filling absorbs the liquid and becomes thick; if the meat seems too dry, add another 5 mL of water and continue stirring
Add optional ingredients (winter bamboo shoots, pork skin jelly, shiitake mushrooms), then drizzle with sesame oil and mix well. Refrigerate for 30 minutes to let the flavors meld
Take a shumai wrapper and place about 20-25 g of filling in the center (do not overfill, or it will be hard to wrap)
Use the curve of your thumb and index finger to gently gather the edges of the wrapper, creating a "vase" shape with an open top
Gently press the bottom with your fingers to ensure it stands upright
If using shrimp, place one peeled shrimp on top
Repeat the wrapping steps until all shumai are finished
Place in a steamer, spacing them apart to prevent sticking
Steam over high heat for 8-10 minutes
The fat in shumai mainly comes from fatty pork; in the low-fat version, a small amount of animal fat is used to compensate for the flavor after removing the fatty meat
If shumai wrappers are unavailable, you can use large wonton wrappers or thinly rolled dumpling wrappers
The wrapper diameter should be about 8-10 cm, weighing 10-15g each; maintain a wrapper-to-filling ratio of 1:2 to 1:2.5
It is recommended to use a medium setting on the meat grinder so the pork is neither too fine (pasty) nor too coarse (chunky), maintaining a good texture and bite
Using 5g ginger and 10g green onion won't overpower the fresh meat flavor; 10g ginger and 20g green onion will taste more like dumpling filling
Apply a little oil to your hand while wrapping to prevent the dough from sticking
Wait for the water to boil before placing the steamer in the pot so the wrappers don't collapse
Large batches can be frozen at -18°C; frozen shumai need to be steamed for 12-15 minutes
Best served with rose rice vinegar; can also be paired with chili sauce, chili oil (youbo lazi), light soy sauce, or ginger slivers according to taste

mon_an.ten: Seaweed and Bonito Flake Corn Rice
mon_an.mo_ta: This is a simple, fresh, and delicious Japanese-style dish. The rice grains are fluffy and infused with the savory taste of bonito flakes, the crispiness of seaweed, and the sweet crunch of corn. Bonito flakes are rich in high-quality protein and DHA, combined with minerals from seaweed and fiber from corn for a balanced meal. The method is extremely simple and easy for beginners; actual hands-on time is only 5 minutes, with a total time of about 40 minutes including rice cooking.
cac_buoc: Fluff the rice, add the corn kernels, and mix well
Add the seaweed and bonito flake mix
If using a Mi Jia mini rice cooker to cook Northeast rice, the water should be 3 millimeters above the rice; too much water will make the rice mushy instead of fluffy

mon_an.ten: Chole Bhature (Chickpea Curry with Fried Bread)
mon_an.mo_ta: Chickpea curry served with fried leavened bread is a classic North Indian street food. The bread is soft and fluffy, paired with richly spiced chickpeas for a complex texture that is sour, spicy, salty, and fragrant. Chickpeas are rich in plant protein and fiber, making this a filling and nutritious meal. While there are several steps, following the process is not difficult, making it suitable for home cooks with some experience. It takes about 50 minutes (chickpeas require 8 hours of pre-soaking).
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Determine the number of servings before starting. One portion is enough for 2-3 people.
cac_buoc: Preparation (8 hours prior)
Soak the dry chickpeas in clean water overnight (at least 8 hours); they will double in volume. Cook the chickpeas
Drain the soaked chickpeas
Place in a pot with 500ml water and 1 black tea bag (for color)
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to medium and **cook for 25-30 minutes** until the *chickpeas can be easily mashed with your fingers*
Remove the tea bag and keep the cooking water; set aside. Sauté the curry base
Heat 30ml of oil in a pan over medium heat
Add the chopped onions and sauté until *golden brown* (about 6-8 minutes)
Add the grated ginger and garlic; sauté for 1 minute
Add the chopped tomatoes and sauté until *tomatoes are completely soft and the oil separates* (about 5 minutes)
Add 3g turmeric, 5g red chili powder, 8g coriander powder, 5g cumin powder, and 6g salt
Sauté for 2 minutes to let the spices release their aroma
Pour the cooked chickpeas and their cooking water into the pan
Add the green chilies and stir well
Bring to a boil over high heat, then reduce to low and **simmer for 15-20 minutes**; occasionally mash some chickpeas with the back of the spatula to thicken the sauce
Add 5g garam masala and 3g pomegranate powder (or 15ml lemon juice)
Stir well and turn off the heat; set aside. Make the bread dough
In a large bowl, mix 250g all-purpose flour, 2g baking soda, and 3g salt
Add 60ml yogurt and 15ml cooking oil
Slowly add warm water while kneading into a *smooth, soft* dough (the dough should be slightly softer than regular dough)
Cover the dough with a damp cloth and let it rest for **30 minutes**. Fry the bread
Divide the dough into 8 equal small balls
Take a ball, grease your hands with a little oil, and roll it into a circle about 15cm in diameter and 3mm thick
Heat 500ml of oil in a deep pot over medium-high heat until it reaches about 180°C
Gently drop the bread into the hot oil and use a slotted spoon to lightly press it so it *puffs up*
**Fry for 1-2 minutes**, flipping once until *both sides are golden brown*
Remove and drain on paper towels. Serve
Reheat the chickpea curry
Serve the fried bread while hot with the chickpea curry
Can be served with sliced onions, green chilies, and lemon wedges
Soaking the chickpeas is mandatory; they will not soften otherwise. If short on time, you can pressure cook unsoaked chickpeas for 20 minutes.
The black tea bag is used to color the chickpeas, giving them a deep brown hue. This is an Indian restaurant secret.
The yogurt and baking soda in the dough are the keys to making the bread soft and puffy. The dough should not be too stiff.

This dish is a national breakfast-brunch staple in India, sold everywhere from street stalls to high-end restaurants. In Indian restaurants in China, it is often called "chickpea curry with fried bread".

mon_an.mo_ta: With a rich sesame oil aroma and simple seasoning of dark soy sauce and pepper, these savory noodles are a time-saving and budget-friendly home-cooked meal. The noodles provide sufficient starch, while sesame oil contains unsaturated fatty acids and vitamin E to boost energy. It is effortless to make, even for kitchen novices; it takes only about ten minutes from boiling the water to finishing the toss.
nguyen_lieu_dung_cu: Salt 30g (optional; this salt will not be fully consumed)
cac_buoc: Bring water to a boil in a pot (if you like chewy noodles, add 30g of salt to the water; noodles cooked in salt water are firmer)
Add the instant noodles to the pot for 3 minutes (or refer to the cooking time on the package)
When the noodles begin to loosen, start stirring so they heat evenly
Drain the water and transfer the noodles to a bowl
Add the measured sesame oil, dark soy sauce, pepper powder, and light soy sauce (optional)
Toss well with chopsticks
The simple and economical "lazy" sesame oil tossed noodles are ready

mon_an.mo_ta: A spicy mala broth combined with a hotpot base, peanut butter, and milk creates a rich, smooth, and distinctly spicy flavor. Paired with high-fiber buckwheat noodles and fresh vegetables, it is low-calorie and filling, perfect for those in a fat-loss phase. It is very easy to make with no cooking experience required; the whole process takes about 20 minutes before you can serve it directly in the pot.
cac_buoc: Wash the baby napa cabbage and lettuce; set aside
Add 500ml of water to a pot, turn on high heat, add the buckwheat noodles and baby napa cabbage, and wait for the water to boil
Once boiling, turn the heat to low and add the hotpot base, peanut butter, milk, light soy sauce, and chili oil; cook for 5 minutes after it returns to a boil
Add the lettuce and cook for another 2 minutes
Add the vinegar and Sichuan peppercorn oil, turn off the heat, and serve directly in the small pot.
Be sure to choose semi-dry buckwheat noodles for the best texture
Feel free to add other items like hotpot meatballs or egg rolls
The hotpot base, peanut butter, and milk are essential; they are the three "pillars" of the flavor
If you don't like sour flavors, you can omit the vinegar
